origins.en: Landscape and portrait painter (1620-1691). The street was laid out after the filling in of the Zaagmolensloot. Until the second half of the nineteenth century, a number of sawmills stood here. In 2005, the Albert Cuypmarkt, which is held on this street, celebrated its centenary.

origins.name: Albert Hahnplantsoen
origins.en: Political cartoonist (1877-1918), mainly caricatures. The park was previously called Willem Witsenpark.

origins.name: Albert Luthulistraat
origins.en: The South African Albert John Luthuli (1898-1967), former president of the African National Congress (ANC), until the 1950s the main spokesman for the nonviolent resistance against apartheid. In 1960 he received the Nobel Peace Prize.

origins.name: Albert Molhof
origins.en: Albert Mol (Amsterdam, January 3, 1917 - Laren (Gelderland), March 9, 2004) was a Dutch actor, dancer, cabaret performer and writer.

origins.name: Albert Neuhuysstraat
origins.en: Painter (1844-1914), best known for his Larense interior houses, among other things.

origins.name: Albert Schultenshof
origins.en: Linguist (1666-1750), professor at Franeker and Leiden. Discovered the meaning of Arabic for the study of Hebrew.

origins.name: Albert Verweystraat
origins.en: Poet and critic (1865-1937), professor at Leiden from 1924 to 1935. Co-founder of 'De Nieuwe Gids', later founder and editor of the literary magazine 'De Beweging'. His collected criticisms and essays have been published in ten volumes. Had an important influence on the young poets of his time.

origins.name: Albert Wittenbergplein
origins.en: During World War II, the Wittenberg family lived at President Brandstraat 32 II. The family consisted of Albert and Janna, the parents, and their two children, Albert and Tine. Albert Wittenberg, a Surinamese man from Paramaribo, who was also in the resistance. From the end of February 1943 to September 1945, they lovingly took in a Jewish girl who was 6 weeks old at the time, into their family. Albert Wittenberg was arrested by a Dutch policeman in 1944. After the detention center on the Weteringschans, the camps Vught and (probably) Dora-Mittelbau followed. As the Americans approached, thousands of prisoners were transported to Neuengamme camp.

origins.name: Albertus Magnushof
origins.en: German theologian and philosopher (1193-1280). One of the founders of scholasticism: the pursuit of wisdom, which tries to make the teaching of the church understandable to the mind. Magnus was the teacher of Thomas Aquinas.

origins.name: Alblasstraat
origins.en: River in the Alblasserwaard.

origins.name: Albrecht Dürerstraat
origins.en: German painter (1471-1528) also renowned engraver and woodcarver.

origins.name: Albrecht Rodenbachhof
origins.en: Flemish poet (1856-1880), soul of the Flemish student movement.

origins.name: Alcantarastraat
origins.en: More in Spain, Embalse Alcantara, located in the province of Extremadura near the border with Portugal.

origins.name: Aldebaranplein
origins.en: Star in the zodiac sign of Taurus.

origins.name: Aldebaranstraat
origins.en: Star in the zodiac sign of Taurus.

origins.name: Aldendriel
origins.en: Restored castle from the seventeenth century, located under Mill (North Brabant), originally from around 1500.

origins.name: Aldengoor
origins.en: Aldengoor or Aldenghoir, castle under Haelen near Roermond (Limburg).

origins.name: Aletta Jacobslaan
origins.en: Doctor (1854-1929), who settled in our country as the first female doctor in 1879. Fighter for the emancipation of the woman.

origins.name: Alexander Boersstraat
origins.en: Alexander Boers (1842-1890), mayor of Nieuwer-Amstel from 1885 to 1890. The street belonged to that municipality until May 1, 1896.

origins.name: Alexander Dumaslaan
origins.en: Named after two French novelists, namely the father, pseudonym of Davy de la Pailleterie (1802-1870), writer of 'The Three Musketeers', among others, and the son (1824-1875), writer of 'La dame aux camélias', among others.

origins.name: Alexanderkade
origins.en: Prince William Alexander Karel Hendrik Frederik (1851-1884), youngest son of King William III. Due to his early death, Princess Wilhelmina became heir to the throne.

origins.name: Alexanderplein
origins.en: Prince William Alexander Karel Hendrik Frederik (1851-1884), youngest son of King William III. Due to his early death, Princess Wilhelmina became heir to the throne.

origins.name: Alexandrine Tinnehof
origins.en: Alexandrine Pieternella Francoise Tinne (1835-1869), traveler and pioneer in photography. Traveled with her mother and aunt through North Africa and visited places that were not yet on the map. Took photos of her birthplace The Hague in the 1860s-'61.

origins.name: Alfred Döblinstraat
origins.en: German writer and doctor (1878-1957) went abroad in 1933, where he continued to publish. One of his best-known novels is 'Berlin Alexanderplatz'.

origins.name: Algolstraat
origins.en: Double star in the constellation Perseus.

origins.name: Alhambralaan
origins.en: Palace and fortress of the Moorish princes in Granada. Literally: the red castle, so named because the palace is made of red brick. Grand monument of Islamic secular architecture, mainly built between 1238 and 1358.

origins.name: Alida van den Bosstraat
origins.en: Alida Johanna van den Bos (1902-2003), Amsterdam gymnast. Won gold with the gymnastics team at the 1928 Olympic Games in Amsterdam and was thus one of the first Dutch female Olympic champions.

origins.name: Alkmaarstraat
origins.en: The city in North Holland.

origins.name: Allard Piersonstraat
origins.en: Walloon preacher (in Liège and Rotterdam), philosopher and aesthetician (1831-1896). From 1877 professor of art history, first in Heidelberg, then in Amsterdam. His major work has been: 'Our spiritual ancestors'. He worked tirelessly for the public school.

origins.name: Allen Ginsbergstraat
origins.en: Irwin Allen Ginsberg (1926-1997) was a Jewish-American poet.

origins.name: Allenstraat
origins.en: The lake, Loch Allen, located in county Leitrim, Northern Ireland.

origins.name: Alma Tademastraat
origins.en: Sir Laurens Alma Tadema (1836-1912), Dutch-English painter of historical subjects. Worked much in England. Buried in St. Paul's Cathedral in London.

origins.name: Almstraat
origins.en: The Alm river in the land of Altena (North Brabant).

origins.name: Alpert van Metzhof
origins.en: Also known as Alpertus. Lived around 1000. He is considered the first North Dutch historian.

origins.name: Aluminiumbrug
origins.en: This lifting bridge is named so because in 1956 the fall (bridge deck) of this bridge (as the first in the Netherlands) was made of aluminum. Another name was Dwingerbrug, after the adjacent fortification 'Swijght Utrecht'.

origins.name: Amaliastraat
origins.en: Amalia van Solms (1602-1675), spouse of stadholder Frederick Henry.

origins.name: Amandelstraat
origins.en: Fruit of the almond tree.

origins.name: Amazonenstraat
origins.en: The female soldiers from Greek mythology.

origins.name: Ambonplein
origins.en: Island in Indonesia, belonging to the Moluccas.

origins.name: Ambonstraat
origins.en: Island in Indonesia, belonging to the Moluccas.

origins.name: Amelandstraat
origins.en: Wadden island (North Holland).

origins.name: Amerbos
origins.en: The small nature reserve under Amen near Rolde (Drenthe).

origins.name: Amerikahavenweg
origins.en: The world region.

origins.name: Amoebastraat
origins.en: Microscopically small aquatic creature.

origins.name: Ampèrestraat
origins.en: André Marie Ampère (1775-1836), French mathematician and physicist. His name is now an international designation of the unit of electrical current strength.

origins.name: Amstel
origins.en: The river to which Amsterdam owes its name and origin.

origins.name: Amstelbestpad
origins.en: Historic farm or country house along the Amstel, near the current Weesperzijde.

origins.name: Amstelbeststraat
origins.en: Historic farm or country house along the Amstel, near the current Weesperzijde.

origins.name: Amstelboulevard
origins.en: Boulevard perpendicular to the Amstel.

origins.name: Amsteldijk
origins.en: Channel, dug around 1920 as part of Berlage's Plan Zuid. Connects the river of the same name with a five-way junction of canals, including the Boerenwetering, the Noorder and the Zuider Amstel Canal.

origins.name: Amstelkade
origins.en: Channel, dug around 1920 as part of Berlage's Plan Zuid. Connects the river of the same name with a five-way junction of canals, including the Boerenwetering, the Noorder and the Zuider Amstel Canal.

origins.name: Amstelpark
origins.en: City park near the Amstel.

origins.name: Amstelplein
origins.en: Channel, dug around 1920 as part of Berlage's Plan Zuid. Connects the river of the same name with a five-way junction of canals, including the Boerenwetering, the Noorder and the Zuider Amstel Canal.

origins.name: Amstelstraat
origins.en: The river.

origins.name: Amstelstroomlaan
origins.en: Former country house on the Amsteldijk, demolished in 1916. There was already a house here in 1583, which was sold in 1806 by Agatha Clara Crol under the name Amstelstroom. Earlier it was called Borssenburg.

origins.name: Amstelveenseweg
origins.en: Village. Before January 1, 1964, the municipality was called Nieuwer-Amstel. The section of the road along Vondelpark to the Overtoom was called Dubbele Buurt before the widening in 1898.

origins.name: Amstelveld
origins.en: The river.

origins.name: Amstelvlietstraat
origins.en: Historic country house on the Amsteldijk. Built after 1721 by Gerrit Nieuwenhuizen, who initially called it Meerhuizen. Since 1784 it has been known under the name Amstelvliet. Demolished in or after 1916.

origins.name: Amsterdam Rijnkanaalkade
origins.en: Pressurized canal with a length of 72 kilometers, connecting the IJ via Utrecht with the Waal near Tiel. Part of an important connection with the Ruhr area.

origins.name: Amundsenweg
origins.en: Roald Amundsen (1872-1928), Norwegian polar explorer. Discovered the northwest passage in 1903. Lost his life during the rescue attempt of the crew of the airship Italia.

origins.name: Analoogstraat
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Anatole Francesingel
origins.en: Pseudonym of Jacques Anatole Francois Thibault (1844-1924), French novelist and essayist. Received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1921.

origins.name: Anderiesenstraat
origins.en: Willem Gerardus Anderiesen (1903-1944), Amsterdam footballer. Played 309 league matches for Ajax between 1925 and 1940 and scored 20 goals. Played in 46 international matches, an Ajax record that was only broken in 1979 by Ruud Krol.

origins.name: Anderlechtlaan
origins.en: Belgian city, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Andersensingel
origins.en: Hans Christian Andersen (1805-1875), Danish writer of novels, poems and travel descriptions. He became best known for his fairy tales.

origins.name: Andijkstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland, located east of Medemblik.

origins.name: Andoornstraat
origins.en: Plant, belonging to the family of lamiaceae.

origins.name: Andreas Bonnstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam professor of surgery. Lived from 1738 to 1817.

origins.name: Andreas Schelfhoutstraat
origins.en: Painter (1787-1870) of landscapes and winter scenes. The street came under the name Bosboomstraat (council decision of Sloten, 1905) within the boundaries of Amsterdam, but this name was changed to avoid confusion with the Bosboom-Toussaintstraat named after his wife.

origins.name: Andreasplein
origins.en: Former hospital, which stood on this site since the 1970s of the twentieth century. It was opened in 1891 on the Keizersgracht as the Dutch Reformed Sisters' Institution. In 1996 it merged with the Sint Lucas Hospital and later moved to that location.

origins.name: Andrej Sacharovstraat
origins.en: Russian physicist (1921-1989) and activist for human rights. Opponent of nuclear weapons and a vocal critic of the Soviet regime. In 1975 he received the Nobel Peace Prize. In 1980 he was arrested and exiled to Gorky.

origins.name: Andries Copierstraat
origins.en: Andries Dirk Copier (1901-1991), glass artist, designer and ceramicist. Designed various tableware and glasses, such as the popular wine glass Gilde.

origins.name: Andries Snoekstraat
origins.en: Actor (1766-1829). In the heyday of Dutch theater until 1820, a dominant figure, together with Majofski and Wattier.

origins.name: Andries Vierlinghstraat
origins.en: Hydrologist (1507-1579) particularly known for the construction of dikes, including at Steenbergen.

origins.name: Andromedastraat
origins.en: Constellation and star nebula, located far outside our Milky Way galaxy.

origins.name: Anemoonstraat
origins.en: Plant, belonging to the family of ranunculus.

origins.name: Anfieldroad
origins.en: Stadium in Liverpool. Ajax played in this stadium on December 14, 1966 in the eighth final of the European Cup for Champions, Liverpool FC-Ajax (2-2).

origins.name: Anielewiczsingel
origins.en: Mordechai Anielewicz, one of the Polish Jews who organized the uprising in the Warsaw ghetto in 1943. Killed on May 7 of that year.

origins.name: Anjeliersstraat
origins.en: Flower, belonging to the rose family.

origins.name: Ank van der Moerstraat
origins.en: Anna Maria van der Moer (1912-1983), actress, played with various companies, including from 1950 to 1972 with the Dutch Comedy. She also worked as a director and actress on radio and television programs.

origins.name: Ankerweg
origins.en: Named after the anchor, a ship part.

origins.name: Anna Bijnsstraat
origins.en: South Dutch poet (1494-1575). Vigorously opposed Luther's teachings.

origins.name: Anna Blamansingel
origins.en: Pseudonym of Johanna Petronella Vrugt (1905-1960), writer. She describes the modern life problems. Her worldview shows similarities to that of French existentialism. In 1957 she received the P.C. Hooft Prize.

origins.name: Anna Pavlovastraat
origins.en: Anna Pavlova was a Russian ballet dancer, choreographer, producer and teacher. She became famous for her interpretation of The Dying Swan.

origins.name: Anna Spenglerstraat
origins.en: Elisabeth Catharina (also known as Anna) Spengler (1842- ca.1905), nurse who worked with Johanna Reynvaan for a few years on the reorganization of nursing at the Wilhelmina Hospital. Originally erroneously named Anna Sprenglerstraat (council decision, 1985).

origins.name: Anna van Burenstraat
origins.en: First wife of Prince William of Orange (1533-1558).

origins.name: Anna van den Vondelstraat
origins.en: Daughter of Joost van den Vondel (1620-1675), who cared for her father for many years. Originally named Anna Vondelstraat, later (council decision, 1986) changed due to confusion with the Vondelstraat.

origins.name: Anna Vockstraat
origins.en: Anna Vock (1884-1962), founded the Swiss gay and lesbian association Schweizerisches Freundschafts Verband in 1933 and was its president for the first few years. The club emerged from the women's club Amicitia and the club for gay men Excentric.

origins.name: Annabellaweg
origins.en: Juicy, sweet cherry from a white-flowering cherry tree.

origins.name: Anne Frankstraat
origins.en: Anne Frank, born in 1929 to Jewish parents, was hiding with her parents and other family members in the building Prinsengracht 263 from 1942 to 1944, where she kept a diary. In 1944, the family was found and deported by the German occupiers. Anne Frank died in the Bergen-Belsen extermination camp in 1945 from illness and exhaustion.

origins.name: Anne Kooistrahof
origins.en: Anne Hendrik Kooistra (1919-1942), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, killed in the Gross Rosen concentration camp. He was one of the pioneers among the illegal workers in the Netherlands, helped organize the illegal press and was also active in the financial support of the victims of the February Strike. He was also associated with the illegal newspaper 'Vrij Nederland'.

origins.name: Annie Boshof
origins.en: Actress (1886-1975). Played many (main) roles in the films of Hollandia in the 1910s of the 20th century, the film company of director Maurits Binger. Belonged to the permanent core of actors around Maurits Binger, and was a real film diva at the time.

origins.name: Annie M.G. Schmidtstraat
origins.en: Anna Maria Geertruida Schmidt (1911-1995), writer of poems, songs, children's books, theater, musicals, cabaret texts and radio and television programs. Worked for a long time as a journalist for 'Het Parool'. Her children's books, including 'Pluk van de Petteflet' and the series 'Jip en Janneke', are enormously popular.

origins.name: Annie Romeinplein
origins.en: Annie Romein-Verschoor (1895-1978), writer and historian. Married to the historian Jan Romein with whom she wrote several history books. In the 1950s she challenged the prevailing view of the position of the woman. In 1970-1971 her autobiography 'Omzien in verwondering' appeared, in which she emerges as a sharp-witted and critical woman.

origins.name: Anselmushof
origins.en: Anselmus, Archbishop of Canterbury (1033-1109), is called the father of scholastic philosophy.

origins.name: Anske Lammingastraat
origins.en: Hydrologist (1855-1920). Founder of irrigation technology in the then Dutch East Indies.

origins.name: Antarusstraat
origins.en: Name of a star.

origins.name: Anthonie van Akenstraat
origins.en: Tennis star (1876-1966). Was Dutch champion three times at the beginning of the twentieth century. Played under the pseudonym A.N. Thonie for a while because otherwise she would tarnish the good name of the family. As the first woman in the Netherlands, she dared to serve forehand, although the racket regularly got stuck behind the hat she had to wear on the court.

origins.name: Anthonie van Dijckstraat
origins.en: Flemish painter (1599-1641), pupil of Rubens, court painter of Charles I of England. In his time the greatest portrait painter.

origins.name: Anthony Fokkerweg
origins.en: Aircraft builder (1890-1939). Started in a workshop in Berlin, he later moved his company to Amsterdam. The Dutch Fokker factory supplied aircraft all over the world. In 1996, the N.V. Koninklijke Nederlandse Vliegtuigenfabriek was declared bankrupt.

origins.name: Anthony Spatzierhof
origins.en: Actor (1718-1777), also theater director. Performed abroad several times.

origins.name: Antillenstraat
origins.en: Island group in the Caribbean Sea, in particular the six islands that together form the Dutch Antilles.

origins.name: Anton Constandsestraat
origins.en: Anton Levien Constandse (1899-1985), political publicist. After the war, he was editor of foreign affairs for twenty years at the 'Algemeen Handelsblad'. Especially known as the author of numerous books, brochures and political commentaries, in which he expressed his anarchism-inspired views.

origins.name: Anton de Komplein
origins.en: Surinamese advocate for human rights (1898-1945), fought for the democratic rights of the population and advocated for the independence of the country. Arrested and deported to the Netherlands in 1933, where he fought against unemployment and the emerging fascism in 1944, he was arrested again by the Germans, died in the concentration camp Neuengamme.

origins.name: Anton Hölzelsingel
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1909-1945), was involved in many illegal activities.

origins.name: Anton Jolingbrug
origins.en: Antonius Jacobus Joling (1857-1934), architect. Learned the trade from Pierre Cuypers (1827-1921), and began working for himself around 1887. Designed mainly public buildings such as offices, hospitals and schools. The building of Peek & Cloppenburg on the Dam is by Joling.

origins.name: Anton Petershof
origins.en: Actor (1812-1872), very popular with the Amsterdam audience in the middle of the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Anton Schleperspad
origins.en: Lived from 1945 to 1993. He made a special effort to preserve the area through which the path named after him runs: the Oeverlanden. He was co-founder of the association 'De Oeverlanden blijven'.

origins.name: Anton Struikstraat
origins.en: Thomas Antonie Struik (1897-1945), resistance fighter, born in Rotterdam, killed in Lübeck (Germany).

origins.name: Anton Verheijstraat
origins.en: Musician (1871-1924), pianist, organist and conductor. Composed mainly music for men's choirs.

origins.name: Anton Waldorpstraat
origins.en: Painter (1803-1866), representative of the realist school. Painted landscapes, interiors and portraits.

origins.name: Antonie Heinsiusstraat
origins.en: Pensionary of Delft, later council pensionary (1641-1720). Great support from Prince William III during his stadtholdership.

origins.name: Antonio Vivaldistraat
origins.en: Italian composer (1678-1741), from 1703 to 1740 associated with the Conservatorio dell'Ospedale della Pietà, one of the four famous music schools in Venice. The great importance of Vivaldi as a composer lies in the development of the violin concerto. His most famous work is the 'Le quattro stagioni' (The four seasons), published in Amsterdam in 1725.

origins.name: Antony Moddermanstraat
origins.en: Lawyer (1838-1885), professor in Amsterdam and Leiden, Minister of Justice.

origins.name: Antoon Keldermansstraat
origins.en: Flemish architect (1450-1512). Built, among other things, the town halls of Middelburg and Veere.

origins.name: Antwerpenbaan
origins.en: Belgian city, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Apollolaan
origins.en: Apollo was one of the main gods of Greek mythology: god of the sun, music and poetry, leader of the muses. The wider part of this avenue, near the Minervalaan, was called August Allebéplein until 1958.

origins.name: Appelweg
origins.en: The fruit of the apple tree.

origins.name: Aragohof
origins.en: Dominique F.J. Arago (1786-1853), French natural and astronomer, discoverer of electromagnetism.

origins.name: Arcadia
origins.en: Region on the Greek peninsula of the Peloponnese. The area inspired the Greek-Roman ideal image of an unspoiled, beauty and nature-oriented society.

origins.name: Arcellastraat
origins.en: A microscopically small aquatic creature surrounded by a scale.

origins.name: Archangelkade
origins.en: The Russian port city on the Barents Sea (North Sea), export port of wood. The city was already regularly visited by Amsterdam merchants around 1600.

origins.name: Archangelweg
origins.en: The Russian port city on the Barents Sea (North Sea), export port of wood. The city was already regularly visited by Amsterdam merchants around 1600.

origins.name: Archimedeslaan
origins.en: Famous Greek mathematician and physicist (287-212 BC), known for the Law of Archimedes, which states that "The upward force experienced by a body in a fluid is equal to the weight of the displaced fluid". .The Archimedesweg was incorporated under the name Langeweg when the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was abolished (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1901).

origins.name: Archimedesplantsoen
origins.en: Famous Greek mathematician and physicist (287-212 BC), known for the Law of Archimedes, which states that "The upward force experienced by a body in a fluid is equal to the weight of the displaced fluid". .The Archimedesweg was incorporated under the name Langeweg when the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was abolished (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1901).

origins.name: Archimedesweg
origins.en: Famous Greek mathematician and physicist (287-212 BC), known for the Law of Archimedes, which states that "The upward force experienced by a body in a fluid is equal to the weight of the displaced fluid". .The Archimedesweg was transferred under the name Langeweg when the municipality of Watergraafsmeer was abolished (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1901).

origins.name: Ardennenlaan
origins.en: Hilly area in Belgium.

origins.name: Arenborg
origins.en: A seventeenth-century manor house near Venlo (Limburg).

origins.name: Arend Bontekoeplantsoen
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1895-1945), born in Naarden, killed in the Sachsenhausen concentration camp (Germany).

origins.name: Arendonksingel
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Arènpalmstraat
origins.en: Palm species. The areca palm or sugar palm is common in the Indonesian archipelago. The palm species produces palm wine, sugar and flour.

origins.name: Arent Janszoon Ernststraat
origins.en: Arent Janszoon Ernst van Bassen Bailiff of Amstelland from 1569 to 1573

origins.name: Argonautenstraat
origins.en: Greek sea heroes who perform on the ship Argo to retrieve the Golden Fleece.

origins.name: Argostraat
origins.en: Former constellation, now divided into three smaller constellations.

origins.name: Ariana Nozemanstraat
origins.en: Ariana Nozeman, born v.d. Bergh (died 1661), actress. In 1655 the first woman to perform at the Amsterdam Schouwburg.

origins.name: Arie Biemondstraat
origins.en: Neurologist (1902-1973), affiliated with the Wilhelminagasthuis. From 1947 to 1970 professor at the University of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Arij Prinsstraat
origins.en: Industrialist and writer (1860-1922), initially published under the pseudonym Cooplandt. Wrote naturalist sketches, later medieval fantasies.

origins.name: Aristotelesstraat
origins.en: Greatest Greek philosopher of antiquity (384-322 BC). Had a great influence on the development of thought.

origins.name: Arlandaweg
origins.en: Name of Stockholm airport.

origins.name: Armbrug
origins.en: The seventh bridge over the Oudezijls Voorburgwal. The middle section of this wooden bridge in front of the O.Z. Armsteeg was removable, it was rebuilt in 1882 and renewed in 1906

origins.name: Armeensebrug
origins.en: Named after nearby former Armenian church

origins.name: Arnold Geulincxpad
origins.en: South Dutch philosopher (1626-1669).

origins.name: Arnold Ingwersenpad
origins.en: Architect (1882-1959), among other things, designed in 1918-1919 together with T. Kuipers the area around Zwanenplein and Koekoeksplein in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Arnold Schönberglaan
origins.en: American composer of Austrian descent (1874-1951). Broke with his atonal compositions with traditional harmony and its application. Formed with his students Alban Berg and Anton Webern the so-called Second Vienna School, which represents a turning point in music history.

origins.name: Arondeusstraat
origins.en: Willem Arondeus (1894-1943), painter and graphic artist. Active in the resistance during the German occupation, executed in Haarlem. He had a major role in the organization of the robbery of the Population Register in 1943, among other things.

origins.name: Artemisstraat
origins.en: Goddess from Greek mythology, daughter of the supreme god Zeus and twin sister of Apollo. The Latin name of Artemis is Diana.

origins.name: Arthur van Schendelstraat
origins.en: Novelist (1874-1946). Originally a neoromanticist, later dealt with simple Dutch themes.

origins.name: Arubastraat
origins.en: Until January 1, 1986 part of the Netherlands Antilles. Since then autonomous country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands (satus aparte).

origins.name: Asingaborg
origins.en: Seventeenth-century castle near Middelstum (Groningen), restored in 1926.

origins.name: Assendelftstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland. The street was originally named Tweede Spaarndammerdwarsstraat (council decision, 1881). From 2-9-1913 to 6-6-1917, there was a Assendelftstraat in the name on another location in this neighborhood, but it was never built. In 1978, the street changed its course completely due to a change in the street pattern.

origins.name: Assumburg
origins.en: Castle near Heemskerk (North Holland), built in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, restored in the seventeenth century and in 1911.

origins.name: Asta Elstakstraat
origins.en: The Surinamese Asta Elstak (1917-1994) has meant a lot for both Suriname and the Surinamese community in the Netherlands. She was, among other things, a board member of the National Organization of Surinamese Elders.

origins.name: Astasiastraat
origins.en: A microscopically small aquatic creature.

origins.name: Asterdwarsweg
origins.en: A microscopically small aquatic creature.

origins.name: Asterweg
origins.en: Ornamental plant, belongs to the composite family.

origins.name: Atatürk
origins.en: Named after the first Turkish housing complex on site. Mustafa Kemal (1881-1938), Turkish military and statesman, founder and first president of the Republic of Turkey. Carried out a radical reform of old Turkey into a Western European model. He received the name Atatürk (= father of the Turks) in 1934 with the introduction of surnames.

origins.name: Atje Keulen-Deelstrastraat
origins.en: Speed skater (1938-2013). One of the greatest Dutch skaters of all time. Her palmares include four world titles, three European titles and three medals at the Sapporo Olympic Games in 1972. She also won 61 skating marathons.

origins.name: Atlantisplein
origins.en: Mythical island, already mentioned by Plato, with paradisiacal living conditions and a high civilization, destroyed by a catastrophe. Possible locations include the Atlantic Ocean and the Greek island of Santorini.

origins.name: Atlas Maiorbrug
origins.en: Named after the Atlas Maior made by Joan Blaeu in 1662 on the Bloemgracht. In 1672 this workshop completely burned down

origins.name: Atochabrug
origins.en: Station in Madrid

origins.name: August Allebéplein
origins.en: Painter and draftsman (1846-1927), director of the Academy of Fine Arts. In contrast to the lyrical character of the Hague School, he placed a moderate realism.

origins.name: August Vermeylenstraat
origins.en: Flemish literary scholar (1872-1945), professor in Ghent and founder of the monthly magazine 'Van nu en straks'. Wrote 'Overview of the new Flemish literatures'.

origins.name: Aurikelstraat
origins.en: Ornamental plant, a primula species.

origins.name: Australiëhavenweg
origins.en: The world region.

origins.name: Avalon
origins.en: Mythical island in the British waters, where King Arthur is said to have sailed to recover from injuries sustained in a battle.

origins.name: Avenhornstraat
origins.en: The village of Avenhorn, north of the Beemster.

origins.name: Avercampstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Avercamp (1585-1634), painter, mainly of winter scenes. Avercamp, living in Kampen from 1613, was born deaf and dumb and therefore had the nickname: the mute of Kampen.

origins.name: Avogadrostraat
origins.en: Italian physicist (1776-1856). Known for the Law of Avogadro of 1814: 'equal volumes of different gases and vapors contain the same number of molecules at the same pressure and temperature'.

origins.name: Azaleastraat
origins.en: Small shrub, garden and houseplant.

origins.name: Azartplein
origins.en: Since 1992, this has been the unofficial name of the place on the island, where the first new inhabitants of the area met the already present sailors and artists. 'Azart' is Russian for inspiration.

origins.name: Aziëhavenweg
origins.en: The largest of the world regions.

origins.name: B. Merkelbachsingel
origins.en: Benjamin Merkelbach (1901-1961), Amsterdam architect. Follower of the New Building who was responsible for residential blocks in the West and commercial buildings in Nieuwendam, among other things. Became urban planner in 1956.

origins.name: Baanakkerspad
origins.en: Small natural monument in the pond area of Jisp and Wormer (North Holland).

origins.name: Baanbrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after the Lijnbaansgracht, which was formerly called Baangracht

origins.name: Baarsjesweg
origins.en: The former inn 'De Drie Baarsjes', located at the Kostverlorenvaart at the time.

origins.name: Baarsstraat
origins.en: Freshwater fish.

origins.name: Baas Gansendonckstraat
origins.en: Main character from the novella of the same name by the Flemish writer Hendrik Conscience (1812-1883).

origins.name: Bachplein
origins.en: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685-1750), German composer. The most important member of the German Bach family, which produced many composers. Wrote oratorios (Matthäus Passion) among other things and more than four hundred cantatas. Last and most universal representative of the Baroque.

origins.name: Bachstraat
origins.en: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685-1750), German composer. The most important member of the German Bach family, which produced many composers. Wrote oratorios (Matthäus Passion) among other things and more than four hundred cantatas. Last and most universal representative of the Baroque.

origins.name: Back-upstraat
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Backershagen
origins.en: An 18th-century country house in Wassenaar (South Holland). The name is derived from the Backer and Hagen families.

origins.name: Baden Powellweg
origins.en: Lord Robert Baden PoweIl (1857-1941). English general in the Boer War. Founded the Boy Scouts movement in 1908, of which he was the international leader until his death.

origins.name: Badhuiskade
origins.en: Former bath facility Obelt, built in 1914 and demolished around 1927. The road is no longer a public road today and is entirely on the grounds of the Shell laboratory.

origins.name: Badrianhof
origins.en: Gerhard Joseph Badrian (1906-1944), born in Upper Silesia (Germany), executed by firing squad in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Baetostraat
origins.en: A tragic play by P.C. Hooft (1581-1647).

origins.name: Baffinstraat
origins.en: William Baffin (1584-1622), English sailor, discovered in 1616 in search of the northwest passage the Baffin Bay and Baffinland named after him.

origins.name: Baionen
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the French port city of Bayonne, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Bakhuizen van den Brinkhof
origins.en: Reinier C. Bakhuizen van den Brink (1810-1865), literary scholar and historian. Editorial member of 'De Gids'. State Archivist in 1854.

origins.name: Bakhuys Roozeboomstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Willem Bakhuys Roozeboom (1854-1907) was a chemist. Amsterdam professor from 1896.

origins.name: Bakkersbrug
origins.en: The name of this pickup bridge is derived from the bakery, which was located in the adjacent Plantage Middenlaan until the early 1960s

origins.name: Bakkersstraat
origins.en: This street, which was first called this in 1604, owes its name to the 'Backhuis', which stood here from around 1595 to 1603. Here the ship shelters for the VOC were baked.

origins.name: Bakkerswaal
origins.en: Nature monument on the Lek near Lekkerkerk.

origins.name: Bakkumstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland.

origins.name: Balatonmeerlaan
origins.en: More, located in the west of Hungary.

origins.name: Balboaplein
origins.en: Vasco Nunez de Balboa (1475-1517), Spanish explorer. Discovered the South Pacific Ocean in 1513.

origins.name: Balboastraat
origins.en: Vasco Nunez de Balboa (1475-1517), Spanish explorer. Discovered the South Pacific Ocean in 1513.

origins.name: Baldermoer
origins.en: The place Baltimore, port city on the Irish south coast. Written according to a spelling as that found on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Baldwinstraat
origins.en: James Baldwin (1924-1987), American writer. Racism and homosexuality are the main themes in his work. Together with Martin Luther King, among others, he campaigned for civil rights.

origins.name: Balearenlaan
origins.en: Spanish island group in the Mediterranean Sea. The most famous islands of the group are Majorca, Menorca, Ibiza and Formentera.

origins.name: Balgzandstraat
origins.en: The sandbank in the Wadden Sea, near Den Helder.

origins.name: Balistraat
origins.en: The island east of Java, in Indonesia. Known for the Hindu artworks.

origins.name: Balthasar Floriszstraat
origins.en: Balthasar Florisz van Berkenrode (1591-1644), cartographer and surveyor. Made large, very accurately drawn plans of Amsterdam in 1625 and 1644.

origins.name: Bamberghof
origins.en: The artist family Bamberg, whose fame was acquired by David Bamberg (1787-1858) as a popular magician, and Eduard Bamberg (1816-1900) as an actor and director of the 'Salon des Variétés' in the Amstelstraat.

origins.name: Bananenstraat
origins.en: Named after the banana, a fruit.

origins.name: Bandijkstraat
origins.en: Heavy river embankment that serves to divert the water at high river levels. The word 'ban' means jurisdiction or legal authority and refers in this case to the administration under which such an embankment falls.

origins.name: Bankastraat
origins.en: The island east of Sumatra in Indonesia, known for its tin mining.

origins.name: Bankwerkerij
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the different workshops were used for the naming.

origins.name: Banne Buikslootlaan
origins.en: Until 1921, Buiksloot was an independent municipality, after which it merged into Amsterdam. 'Ban' means both jurisdiction and legal authority. The Banne Buiksloot was traditionally one of the six bans (jurisdictions) into which the bailiwick of Waterland was divided. After the Batavian Revolution of 1795, the word continued to exist, but then only referred to the polder. It was not until 1936 that the Waterland bans were lifted.

origins.name: Banneplein
origins.en: This square is located in the center of the Buiksloot district, historically the Banne Buiksloot. A ban or banne was in earlier centuries an administrative area. The bans together formed the bailiwick.

origins.name: Banstraat
origins.en: Joan Albert Ban (1597-1644), priest and composer. Composed among other things on texts by Vondel and Tesselschade.

origins.name: Bantammerbrug
origins.en: The name of this permanent bridge evokes memories of the sixteenth century, when Dutchmen brought the products from Bantam (Dutch East Indies) to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Banterij
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the Irish port town of Bantry, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries

origins.name: Barajasweg
origins.en: Name of the Madrid airport.

origins.name: Barbara Strozzilaan
origins.en: Italian composer (1619-1677), adopted daughter of the poet Giulio Strozzi, studied music with Francesco Cavalli, the opera composer of his time. Wrote more than a hundred vocal works, including madrigals, cantatas, arias and duets.

origins.name: Barbara van Meertenstraat
origins.en: Anna Barbara van Meerten-Schilperoort (1778-1853), educator and writer. Published about and advocated for the education of girls, care for the poor and prisoners.

origins.name: Barbusselaan
origins.en: Henri Barbusse (1873-1933), French novelist.

origins.name: Barcelonaplein
origins.en: Port city on the east coast of Spain, where the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a passenger service.

origins.name: Barentszplein
origins.en: Willem Barentszoon, the famous captain, who together with Jacob van Heemskerck tried to reach India in 1596 via the North Sea. He spent the winter on Nova Zembla, but died on the return trip in 1597.

origins.name: Barentszstraat
origins.en: Willem Barentszoon, the famous captain, who together with Jacob van Heemskerck tried to reach India in 1596 via the North Sea. He spent the winter on Nova Zembla, but died on the return trip in 1597.

origins.name: Barkasstraat
origins.en: Originally the largest sloop on board a warship. Today, the barge is a popular sturdy motorboat with an open cabin.

origins.name: Barkentijnkade
origins.en: Ship, crossing between a schooner, bark and brig. Also known as barkschooner or schoonerbark.

origins.name: Barkpad
origins.en: A bark is a three-masted sailing ship, which is rigged longitudinally.

origins.name: Barndesteeg
origins.en: The name is derived from barnen, obsolete form of fires. It is likely that the alley was completely or partially destroyed by fire in earlier years. As an old spelling for this alley, Brandesteeg, Bernendesteeg and Verbemdesteeg are also used.

origins.name: Barnevelderstraat
origins.en: The chicken breed, bred in Barneveld and surroundings. The street was laid on the site, on which the Sluis company used to stand, which produced chicken feed and birdseed.

origins.name: Baron de Coubertinlaan
origins.en: Pierre F. Baron de Coubertin (1863-1937), Frenchman. Initiator and first organizer of the modern Olympic Games.

origins.name: Baron G.A. Tindalplein
origins.en: George August Tindal (1839-1921), director and commissioner of several Amsterdam steamship companies, including the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland', from 1872 to 1874 alderman of Amsterdam and later chamberlain of William III.

origins.name: Baron G.A. Tindalstraat
origins.en: George August Tindal (1839-1921), director and commissioner of several Amsterdam steamship companies, including the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland', from 1872 to 1874 alderman of Amsterdam and later chamberlain of William III.

origins.name: Baron Schimmelpenninck van der Oyeweg
origins.en: Alphert baron Schimmelpenninck van der Oye (1880-1943), chairman of the Dutch Olympic Committee for many years. Shot dead by the Germans in 1943.

origins.name: Baroniepad
origins.en: The Barony of Breda, region between Bergen op Zoom and 's-Hertogenbosch (North Brabant).

origins.name: Baroniestraat
origins.en: The Barony of Breda, region between Bergen op Zoom and 's-Hertogenbosch (North Brabant).

origins.name: Baronstraat
origins.en: One of the leaders of the uprising of the enslaved Surinamese. The runaway enslaved people, also known as marrons, waged a guerrilla war against their oppressors. They plundered the plantations and thus inflicted heavy blows on the economy.

origins.name: Bart de Ligtstraat
origins.en: Theologian (1883-1938), Christian socialist, later anarchist, anti-militarist. From 1910 to 1915 pastor of the Dutch Reformed Church.

origins.name: Bart Poesiatstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam brewer's servant (1831-1898), co-founder of 'Patrimonium' and of the Christian Workers' Union.

origins.name: Bart van der Leckplantsoen
origins.en: Painter and designer (1876-1958), known for his figurative style. Worked with geometric shapes and primary colors. Was briefly affiliated with De Stijl.

origins.name: Bart van Hovestraat
origins.en: Sculptor (1854-1914), produced sculptural groups for the Sint Nicolaaskerk, the Sint Bernardus institution and the Barlaeus Gymnasium.

origins.name: Bartholomeus Diazstraat
origins.en: Portuguese explorer (1450-1500). He was the first European to sail around the Cape of Good Hope in 1486.

origins.name: Bartholomeus Drijfhoutstraat
origins.en: Seventeenth-century architect (born 1605) from the school of Jacob van Campen. Built the Lakenhal in Leiden in 1640 and the Oosterkerk in Middelburg in 1647.

origins.name: Bartholomeus Ruloffsstraat
origins.en: Conductor (1740-1801), organist of the Westerkerk and director of the orchestras of the Stadsschouwburg and Felix Meritis. He wrote music for Van Alphen's children's songs.

origins.name: Bartholt Enthesstraat
origins.en: Member of the Confederation of the Nobles (1540-1580), vice-admiral of the Geuzen under Lumey during the capture of Den Briel. In the same year, he made an attempt to conquer Amsterdam on behalf of Lumey.

origins.name: Basisweg
origins.en: When the port was being built in the western port area, a basic canal was originally designed, from which the large inlet harbors would emerge. The road designed along this canal was therefore named Basisweg. The basic canal was not built, the road was. As a result of the construction of the Hemspoorweg, the Basisweg was shortened in 1978 and the western part was renamed Noordzeeweg.

origins.name: Bastenakenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Luxembourg. Flemish name for Bastogne.

origins.name: Bastiaan Plooijstraat
origins.en: Bastiaan Plooijst (1890-1967) is best known for his designs for Reformed and Reformed churches. He built about thirty of them in his lifetime, including Maranathakerk

origins.name: Bastingstraat
origins.en: het Mosplein. For this neighborhood, the category names of Dutch architects who have been involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-North have been chosen.

origins.name: Bataviastraat
origins.en: City on Java, capital of the former Dutch East Indies. The city is now called Jakarta.

origins.name: Batjanstraat
origins.en: Island in Indonesia, belonging to the Moluccas.

origins.name: Batteryparkstraat
origins.en: Waterfront development at the southern tip of Manhattan (New York City), a park named after the battery cannons that were placed there in the 17th century by Dutch colonists, partly built using enslaved people. In the 19th century, the area transformed into a public city park and at the end of the 20th century into an example of urban redevelopment.

origins.name: Bauduinlaan
origins.en: Mr. D. Bauduin from The Hague became the first dike governor of the Houtrakpolder in 1876.

origins.name: Bavinkhof
origins.en: Roman character of the writer Nescio. Nescio (Latin = 'I don't know') is the pseudonym of Jan Hendrik Frederik Grönloh (1882-1961). His most famous works include 'De uitvreter' and 'Titaantjes'.

origins.name: Baweanstraat
origins.en: Indonesian island in the Java Sea, north of Surabaya.

origins.name: Becquerelstraat
origins.en: Antonie Henri Becquerel (1852-1908), French physicist. Discovered that the salts of uranium emit a type of x-rays. In 1903 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

origins.name: Beeckenstein
origins.en: Old outside near Velsen (North Holland) from the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Beek en Hoff
origins.en: Former farmhouse on the Haarlemmerweg, opposite the village of Sloterdijk.

origins.name: Beemdgrasstraat
origins.en: Native plant genus of about five hundred species from the grass family.

origins.name: Beemsterstraat
origins.en: The Beemster polder, a reclaimed lake between 1608 and 1612 northwest of Purmerend.

origins.name: Beethovenplein
origins.en: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), German composer, master of instrumental music. Composed among other things 9 symphonies, 32 piano sonatas, 11 overtures and 17 string quartets.

origins.name: Beethovenstraat
origins.en: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827), German composer, master of instrumental music. Composed among other things 9 symphonies, 32 piano sonatas, 11 overtures and 17 string quartets.

origins.name: Begijnensteeg
origins.en: The court, founded in the fourteenth century, was intended for the accommodation of beguines (lay sisters). The Begijnhof was originally, together with the St. Lucia's monastery, completely surrounded by water. Behind the houses of Kalverstraat was a ditch, the Beguin's ditch, which ran from the still undammed Spui to the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. This canal was neglected and therefore the rest was filled in in 1865. It was named Filled in Begijnhof Canal, which name was legalized by a council decision in 1914.

origins.name: Begoniastraat
origins.en: Named after the begonia, a plant.

origins.name: Beijerlandstraat
origins.en: Western part of the island of de Hoeksche Waard (South Holland).

origins.name: Beiraweg
origins.en: African port city, located in Mozambique. The street is located near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

origins.name: Beitelkade
origins.en: Carpentry tools.

origins.name: Belgiëplein
origins.en: The country.

origins.name: Bella Vistastraat
origins.en: Former country house on the Amstel.

origins.name: Bellamydwarsstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Bellamy (1757-1786), poet, originally baker's apprentice. A part of the street and the cross street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 under the names Nieuwe Weteringstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1888) and Nieuwe Weteringdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1891).

origins.name: Bellamyplein
origins.en: Jacobus Bellamy (1757-1786), poet, originally baker's apprentice. A part of the street and the cross street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 under the names Nieuwe Weteringstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1888) and Nieuwe Weteringdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1891).

origins.name: Bellamystraat
origins.en: Jacobus Bellamy (1757-1786), poet, originally baker's apprentice. A part of the street and the cross street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 under the names Nieuwe Weteringstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1888) and Nieuwe Weteringdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1891).

origins.name: Bellefleurhof
origins.en: Brabant apple variety from the nineteenth century with large, fresh greenish-red apples.

origins.name: Belmermeer
origins.en: Drying plant southeast of Broek in Waterland and located for half in that municipality. Belmermeer means connecting lake. The Amsterdam part belonged to the then abolished municipalities of Nieuwendam and Ransdorp before 1921.

origins.name: Beloegastraat
origins.en: Also known as the white dolphin, it can grow up to ten to twelve meters long, weigh up to 1400 kilograms and live for at least one hundred years. Lives in the Caspian and Black Seas.

origins.name: Beltbrug
origins.en: Reminiscent of the municipal landfill, which served there until 1888.

origins.name: Belvedereweg
origins.en: Former manor house, stood on the west side of the old Schagerlaan. The manor house was also known under the name 'Mijn lust is rust'.

origins.name: Ben Brilstraat
origins.en: Barend (Ben) Bril (1912-2003), amateur boxer, represented the Netherlands at the Olympic Summer Games in 1928 at the age of fifteen, in the flyweight division (up to 50.8 kg). He won the Dutch title eight times in his weight class.

origins.name: Ben Hope
origins.en: Mountain peak in Scotland, 927 meters high.

origins.name: Ben van Meerendonkstraat
origins.en: Ben van Meerendonk (1913-2008) was a Dutch photojournalist.

origins.name: Ben Viljoenstraat
origins.en: South African Boer Commander, who repelled an English invasion in 1896. Participated in the Second Boer War in 1899. Born 1868, died in America (year of death unknown).

origins.name: Ben Websterstraat
origins.en: Benjamin Francis Webster (1909-1973), American jazz tenor saxophonist, emigrated to Europe in 1964. Known as a performer of fast, intense tempos with a raw tone and as a creator of sensitive ballads.

origins.name: Benit
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the French port town of Binic, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Benjamin Brittenstraat
origins.en: Lord Edward Benjamin Britten (1913-1976), English composer and pianist. One of the most important classical composers of the twentieth century. Composed, among other things, the opera 'Peter Grimes' and the 'War Requiem'.

origins.name: Benkoelenstraat
origins.en: City on the west coast of the island of Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Bennebroekstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland.

origins.name: Benno Stokvisstraat
origins.en: Benno Jules Stokvis (1901-1977), lawyer and politician. Became known for his defense in 1933 of Henk Sneevliet during his trial following the mutiny on the naval ship De Zeven Provinciën. Publicist, literary critic and advocate for full rights for homosexuals. Antifascist and after the war a fierce critic of Stalinism.

origins.name: Bentinckstraat
origins.en: Barend Hendrik baron Bentinck tot Buckhorst (1753-1830), governor of Overijssel. Had to leave the country due to sympathy for Stadhouder Willem V. Played an important role in the establishment of the Kingdom in 1813.

origins.name: Benzolweg
origins.en: Mixture of hydrocarbons. A petroleum derivative.

origins.name: Bep Bakhuysstraat
origins.en: Elisa Hendrik Bakhuys (1909-1982), footballer. Played a leading role in the successes of the Dutch national team in the 1930s.

origins.name: Berberisstraat
origins.en: Named after the barberry, a shrub.

origins.name: Berceusestraat
origins.en: French for 'crib song' or 'lullaby'. Title of a poem by the Flemish modernist Paul van Ostaijen (1896-1928).

origins.name: Berchvliet
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the French port city of Barfleur, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Bercylaan
origins.en: Neighborhood along the Seine in Southeast Paris, where many wine warehouses stood along the Seine. In the late twentieth century, large-scale renovation took place.

origins.name: Berend Boeijingastraat
origins.en: Urban planner and architect (1886-1969), among others in service of the Municipal Housing Service. Designed the former laboratory of the Vrije Universiteit. Built Disteldorp, Tuindorp Oostzaan and Tuindorp Nieuwendam.

origins.name: Berensluis
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after Berenstraat, to which it is adjacent. In the adjacent part of the current Jordaan, in the seventeenth century, the tanneries and the leather trade were located

origins.name: Berenstraat
origins.en: In the adjacent part of the current Jordaan, in the seventeenth century, the tanneries and the fur trade were located. These also included bear skins.

origins.name: Bergmolen
origins.en: A mountain or bell mill is named after the hill that is raised around the mill when the mill is ready, as an alternative to a tower. A mountain mill is usually a grain mill.

origins.name: Bergstraat
origins.en: The street already existed under this name, before it came within the walls during the enlargement of 1593. From 1633 it is known that there was a house with a facade stone, on which the mountain of Sinai. Whether such a building existed before that and whether that is the name giver of the street is not known.

origins.name: Beringenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Berkelstraat
origins.en: The small river, which flows into the IJssel near Zutphen.

origins.name: Berkhouthof
origins.en: Village in North Holland (near Hoorn).

origins.name: Berlaarstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Berlagebrug
origins.en: Hendrik Petrus Berlage (1856-1934), architect. Chief architect of the Koopmansbeurs on the Damrak, among other things. Designer of the expansion plan-Zuid and the Mercatorplein and surroundings. His last creation was the Berlagebrug (1932). In 1966, Hildo Krop made a statue of him, which was placed on the Victorieplein.

origins.name: Berlagehof
origins.en: Hendrik Petrus Berlage (1856-1934), architect. Chief architect of the Koopmansbeurs on the Damrak, among other things. Designer of the expansion plan-Zuid and the Mercatorplein and surroundings. His last creation was the Berlage Bridge (1932). In 1966, Hildo Krop made a statue of him, which was placed on the Victorieplein.

origins.name: Bernard Kochstraat
origins.en: Musician (1791-1858), conductor of the Italian Opera in Amsterdam, composed among other things the opera 'Mother Goose'.

origins.name: Bernard Loderstraat
origins.en: Lawyer (1849-1935), great expert in international law, president of the Permanent Court of International Justice.

origins.name: Bernard Shawsingel
origins.en: George Bernard Shaw (1856-1950), British (Irish) playwright and novelist of 'Pygmalion' among others.

origins.name: Bernard Zweerskade
origins.en: Composer and conductor (1854-1924). Professor at the Amsterdam Conservatory. He chose exclusively Dutch texts from, for example, Boutens and Verweij for his songs and choral works.

origins.name: Bernissestraat
origins.en: In the Middle Ages a wide water, now still a small bay between Voorne and Putten (South Holland).

origins.name: Bert Haanstrakade
origins.en: Film director (1916-1997), became famous with films such as 'Fanfare', 'Zoo', 'Alleman' and 'Bij de beesten af', in which he humorously examined Dutch society. For his films and documentaries he received 78 awards, including in 1958 an Oscar for his documentary 'Glas'.

origins.name: Bertelmanplein
origins.en: Jan Georg Bertelman (1782-1854), composer of cantatas and a requiem.

origins.name: Bertelmanstraat
origins.en: Jan Georg Bertelman (1782-1854), composer of cantatas and a requiem.

origins.name: Bertha von Suttnerstraat
origins.en: Austrian writer (1848-1914). In 1891 she founded the Österreichische Gesellschaft der Friedensfreunde (since 1964 Suttner-Gesellschaft). Her book 'Die Waffen nieder' has become world famous for its pacifist tendency and moving style. She inspired Alfred Nobel to establish the Nobel Prizes. In 1905 she received the Nobel Peace Prize.

origins.name: Berthelotstraat
origins.en: Pierre Eugène Marcellin Berthelot (Paris, October 29, 1827 - there, March 18, 1907) was a French chemist and politician. In his chemical work he discovered the synthesis routes for many hydrocarbons, fats, sugars, and thus proved that organic chemical compounds can be prepared using the same chemical techniques as inorganic compounds.

origins.name: Berthold Brechtstraat
origins.en: Eugen Berthold Friedrich Brecht (1898-1956), also known as Bertolt Brecht. There is disagreement about the correct spelling. German theater and prose writer. Belonged to the so-called exile writers. In 1933 he left Nazi Germany and came to the United States of North America via France. In 1947 he returned to his homeland.

origins.name: Bertrand Russellstraat
origins.en: Bertrand Arthur William Russell (1872-1970), British philosopher and publicist. In his work as a writer, teacher, speaker and activist, four areas can be distinguished: philosophy of mathematics and logic, epistemology, ethics and education, and finally pacifism. In 1950 he received the Nobel Prize for Literature.

origins.name: Bertus van Grouwstraat
origins.en: Gijsbertus Ludovicus van Grouw (1907-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, killed in concentration camp Neuengamme.

origins.name: Berzeliusstraat
origins.en: Johannes Jacob Berzelius (1779-1848), Swedish chemist. Founder of modern analysis.

origins.name: Bessemerstraat
origins.en: Henry Bessemer (1813-1898), English engineer. Inventor of a method for rolling glass and preparing molten metal. The street has been renamed Ringlaan from the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Bessenpad
origins.en: The fruits.

origins.name: Bestevâerstraat
origins.en: Erenaam, given by the sea people to Maarten Harpertsz. Tromp, and later to Michiel Adriaansz. de Ruyter. Literally: best father. The name of the street was originally established by the municipality of Sloten as Wilhelminastraat (council decision of Sloten, 1911).

origins.name: Bet van Beerenbrug
origins.en: Elizabeth Maria van Beeren (1902-1967) was the owner of the nearby café 't Mandje on Zeedijk 63. She was called the Queen of Zeedijk. She was openly lesbian and her café became a refuge for homosexuals in the 1950s, which made her a pioneer in their emancipation.

origins.name: Betelgeuzestraat
origins.en: Star in the constellation Orion.

origins.name: Bethaniëndwarsstraat
origins.en: The monastery of St. Mary Magdalene in Bethany, which stood here from around 1450 to 1589. The street was laid out in 1506 along the southern wall of the monastery.

origins.name: Bethaniënstraat
origins.en: The monastery of St. Mary Magdalene in Bethany, which stood here from around 1450 to 1589. The street was laid out in 1506 along the southern wall of the monastery.

origins.name: Betuwestraat
origins.en: The region in Gelderland, between the Rhine and the Waal.

origins.name: Beukenplein
origins.en: Named after the beech, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Beukenweg
origins.en: Named after the beech, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Beulingstraat
origins.en: One of the residents, Gerrit Jansz Beulinck, who lived here around 1660. He may have made this known with a signboard. In the sixteenth century, the names Leertouwers- and also Huidevettersstraat and -sloot appear here.

origins.name: Beursplein
origins.en: The Koopmansbeurs of Berlage, built in 1903. The street and square were created after the filling in of part of Damrak. The name Beurspassage was created after the former Baafjessteeg was rebuilt by new construction in 1903.

origins.name: Beursstraat
origins.en: The Koopmansbeurs of Berlage, built in 1903. The street and square were created after the filling in of part of Damrak. The name Beurspassage was created after the former Baafjessteeg was rebuilt by new construction in 1903.

origins.name: Beverenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of West Flanders.

origins.name: Beverwijkstraat
origins.en: City in North Holland, at the foot of the dune area.

origins.name: Beysterveld
origins.en: The castle Oud Beysterveld near Oirschot (North Brabant), built in 1775 on the foundations of a seventeenth-century castle, later used as a monastery.

origins.name: Bezaanjachtplein
origins.en: Type sailing ship, usually with three masts. The rear mast is called the mainmast, to which a jib sail is attached.

origins.name: Bickersgracht
origins.en: These streets are located on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr. Johan Bicker (1591-1653), shipbuilder and merchant, ships and mayor of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets that were later laid out on this island automatically took the name of the founder.

origins.name: Bickerswerf
origins.en: These streets are located on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr. Johan Bicker (1591-1653), shipbuilder and merchant, ships and mayor of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets that were later laid out on this island automatically took the name of the founder.

origins.name: Bierens de Haanstraat
origins.en: Johannes D. Bierens de Haan (1866-1943), philosopher. Dedicated a study among other things to Spinoza.

origins.name: Biesboschstraat
origins.en: The area of islands, peatlands and creeks, now partially covered, between the Bergsche Maas and Merwede. Before the implementation of the Delta works subject to tides.

origins.name: Bieslookpad
origins.en: Plant, belonging to the genus allium, used as a spice.

origins.name: Bijdorpstraat
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Bijlmerdreef
origins.en: Named after the polder, created by the draining of the Bijlmermeer in 1626. The polder became an independent municipality in 1817 and in 1846 was merged with Weesperkarspel. When the municipality of Weesperkarspel was abolished in 1966, a part was added to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Bijlmerplein
origins.en: Named after the polder, created by the draining of the Bijlmermeer in 1626. The polder became an independent municipality in 1817 and in 1846 was merged with Weesperkarspel. When the municipality of Weesperkarspel was abolished in 1966, a part was added to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Bijlmerpleinpad
origins.en: Name of underlying square

origins.name: Bijlmerringsloot
origins.en: Named after the polder, created by the draining of the Bijlmermeer in 1626. The polder became an independent municipality in 1817 and in 1846 was merged with Weesperkarspel. When the municipality of Weesperkarspel was abolished in 1966, a part was added to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Bijltjespad
origins.en: The Bijltjes, name for the Kattenburgers (shipwrights) in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Known for the struggle around the Kattenburgerbrug between Patriots and Bijltjes, who were royalists.

origins.name: Bilderdijkkade
origins.en: Willem Bilderdijk (1756-1831), poet and historian. Bilderdijk went against the complacent spirit of his time and was therefore a much-controversial figure. The name Bilderdijkstraat originally extended to Vondelstraat. (That part, from Jacob van Lennepkade, is now called Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat. (council decision, 1894.) The Bilderdijkpark (park and street) was laid out on the grounds of the cemetery of the former Roman Catholic church 'De Liefde'.

origins.name: Bilderdijkpark
origins.en: Willem Bilderdijk (1756-1831), poet and historian. Bilderdijk went against the complacent spirit of his time and was therefore a much-controversial figure. The name Bilderdijkstraat originally extended to Vondelstraat. (That part, from Jacob van Lennepkade, is now called Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat. (council decision, 1894.) The Bilderdijkpark (park and street) was laid out on the grounds of the cemetery of the former Roman Catholic church 'De Liefde'.

origins.name: Bilderdijkstraat
origins.en: Willem Bilderdijk (1756-1831), poet and historian. Bilderdijk went against the complacent spirit of his time and was therefore a much-controversial figure. The name Bilderdijkstraat originally extended to Vondelstraat. (That part, from Jacob van Lennepkade, is now called Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat. (council decision, 1894.) The Bilderdijkpark (park and street) was laid out on the grounds of the cemetery of the former Roman Catholic church 'De Liefde'.

origins.name: Billie Holidaystraat
origins.en: Eleanora Gough McKay (1915-1959), artist name Billie Holiday, American singer, debuted in 1929 and made her first recording in 1933. Known for her timbre and nonchalant phrasing.

origins.name: Billitonstraat
origins.en: Island in Indonesia between Sumatra and Kalimantan (Borneo). Important due to tin mining.

origins.name: Binairstraat
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Binnen Bantammerstraat
origins.en: The name evokes memories of the sixteenth century, when the Dutch brought the products to Amsterdam from Bantam (Dutch East Indies). In 1597, Houtman's ships were unloaded in the Waal. The Binnen Bantammerstraat was originally called Bantammerstraat. The bridge over the Geldersekade already bore the name Bantamsbrug around 1600. The houses located on the street were then described as lying outside the Bantamspoort. In 1644 the Nieuwe Waalseiland was created. The Bantammerstraat then received the addition Binnen, and the extension, over the Oude Waal, became Buiten Bantammerstraat.

origins.name: Binnen Brouwersstraat
origins.en: To the many breweries that could be found in this neighborhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The designation Binnen and Buiten is related to the location relative to the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Binnen Dommersstraat
origins.en: The owner of the land on which the street was laid out was lJsbrand Jansz. Dommer. He was a surveyor and councilman, appointed in 1579 as a councillor of the city. Binnen and Buiten indicate the location, inside and outside the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Binnen Oranjestraat
origins.en: The origin of the name is uncertain. It may refer to the house 'de Prins van Oranje', which used to stand here close to the Haarlemmerdijk. The division into Binnen and Buiten Oranjestraat indicates the location: inside and outside the dike (Haarlemmerdijk).

origins.name: Binnen Vissersstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the many fishermen who originally lived here - originally outside the gate. The first street was within the dike, the second was on the IJ side, so outside the dike.

origins.name: Binnen Wieringerstraat
origins.en: Albert Pietersz van Wieringen is the namesake here. According to old documents from 1610 and 1624, he had a house and some land in ownership here. At that time, the street is already referred to as Wieringerstraat. The separation of the two parts comes into use in the eighteenth century, namely inside and outside the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Binnendraaierij
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the different workshops were used for the naming. Because the street is divided into two parts by a square, there is a Binnendraaierij and a Buitendraaierij.

origins.name: Binnenhofstraat
origins.en: The name indicates the location: the courtyard in a multi-story complex. The 'Binnenhof' (where the Binnenhofstraat runs around) is no longer a public road. This name was abolished by council decision in 1949 after the renovation of the complex.

origins.name: Binnenkadijk
origins.en: When a lot of land had been silted up outside the old sea wall (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike or canal was built. Originally, the new sea wall was spoken of, but that later fell out of use. With further raising of this new dike, the Lowness and Height of the Canal were spoken of. The Between Canals was called Korte Kerkstraat until 1943. This is indeed in the extension of the Plantage Kerklaan, but has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Binnenkant
origins.en: The Walloon Island (see below Walloon) created by dredging in 1644 was named Binnenkant on the city side and Buitenkant on the IJ side. The latter name was changed to Prins Hendrikkade in 1879.

origins.name: Binnenpolderringdijk Noord
origins.en: Refers to the ring dike of the Osdorper Binnenpolder

origins.name: Binnenvaart
origins.en: Shipping on the inland waterways.

origins.name: Binnenzagerij
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the different workshops were used for the naming. Because the street is divided into two parts by a square, there is a Binnenzagerij and a Buitenzagerij.

origins.name: Biothof
origins.en: Jean-Baptiste Biot (1774-1862), French physicist and astronomer. Made the first scientific balloon flight in 1804. Worked on electromagnetism, among other things.

origins.name: Bitterzoetstraat
origins.en: Plant, belonging to the nightshade family.

origins.name: Blancefloorstraat
origins.en: Figure from the medieval knight's romance 'Floris ende Blancefloor'.

origins.name: Blankenbergestraat
origins.en: Belgian coastal town, located in the province of West Flanders.

origins.name: Blankenstraat
origins.en: Jan Blanken (1755-1838), civil engineer and fort builder. The North Holland Canal was dug according to his design in the years 1818 to 1824.

origins.name: Blasiusstraat
origins.en: Gerardus Blasius (1625-1693), professor of medicine in Amsterdam. The street was originally named Vierde Boerhaavestraat (council decision, 1882).

origins.name: Blauwbrug
origins.en: The name of this permanent bridge recalls an earlier version of it, which was painted blue in the color of Nassau after the alteration of Amsterdam in 1578. The current bridge dates from 1884. The architects B. de Greef and W. Springer were inspired by a Seine Bridge. Another name for this bridge was Sophiabrug, despite all changes the name Blauwbrug was maintained. This was once another name, for the Blauwbrug, which was never adopted, just like Sophiaplein in front of Muntplein. Sophia of Württemberg (1817-1877) was the first wife of King William III, who opened this renovated bridge in 1839.

origins.name: Blauwburgwal
origins.en: Probably named after the Blue Bridge. The canal was dug at the end of the sixteenth century. The current name first appears from 1614. Previously, the canal was referred to as the Blue Bridge canal outside Jan Roonpoort, or as the perpendicular city wall near the Blue Bridge. Most bridges were painted red at that time.

origins.name: Blauwdasstraat
origins.en: The singing bird. Colorful bird the size of a sparrow, is kept in aviaries a lot. Found in Suriname, Guyana, Venezuela and northern Brazil.

origins.name: Blauwezandbrug
origins.en: Garden village Buiksloot was formerly called the Blue Sand because of the bluish color of the sprayed soil on which this village was built

origins.name: Blauwhoedenveem
origins.en: A veem is a company responsible for storing and delivering goods in and out of its warehouses. The veems each had their own license plate, after which they were named. These could be different colors and models of hats (e.g. Blue hats, Clogs). They also derived their name from the origin of the workers (e.g. Friese Veem, Zeeuwse Veem).

origins.name: Blauwpijpstraat
origins.en: Named after the ships - blue pipes named because of the blue stripe on the chimney - of the former Dutch Steam Navigation Company Oceaan NV, which was based on Borneokade.

origins.name: Blauwvoetstraat
origins.en: A poem by the Flemish poet Albrecht Rodenbach. (Blue Footing is a Flemish student movement around 1875, as a resistance to the Frenchification of lectures.)

origins.name: Blazerpad
origins.en: Small fishing vessel, similar to a barge.

origins.name: Bleijenbeek
origins.en: Seventeenth-century castle near the village of Afferden (Limburg) completely burned down in 1944, now a ruin.

origins.name: Bloedstraat
origins.en: For the construction of the street, this was the blood chamber of the Brothers of Mercy monastery. This was the operating room, but may have served as a torture chamber. According to the historian Melchior Fokkens (1661), Alva allegedly kept his 'bloodline' here.

origins.name: Bloemendalergouw
origins.en: Bloemendaal was one of the quarters of the former Banne Ransdorp. The county (Waterland name for village road) ran in the eighteenth century from Ransdorp to the Zeedijk. The last part was washed away by the water of the Kinselmeer in the following centuries. The second part of the current road (in the direction of Holysloot) was originally called Kanaalweg.

origins.name: Bloemgracht
origins.en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion from 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which the canal is named. On the fort stood the mill 'De Blom' from 1614 to 1878, which was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

origins.name: Bloemstraat
origins.en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion from 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which the canal is named. On the fort stood the mill 'De Blom' from 1614 to 1878, which was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

origins.name: Blokkerstraat
origins.en: The North Holland villages of Wester- and Oosterblokker, near Hoorn.

origins.name: Blokmakerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name from shipbuilding. The name recalls the many shipyards that were located along Grote Bickersstraat in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Blomwijckerpad
origins.en: A road that disappeared due to the urban expansion in the old Sloten.

origins.name: Bloys van Treslongstraat
origins.en: Willem Bloys of Treslong (1529-1594), Dutch admiral, leader of the Geuzen during the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Blusséstraat
origins.en: Jan Jacob Blussé (1870-1931), well-known skiff rower. Did much for rowing in the Netherlands. From 1898 to 1931 chairman of rowing club 'De Hoop'.

origins.name: Boas en Judelshof
origins.en: Israel Boas (1811-1886) and Nathan Judels (1815-1903), both cabaret performers. Directors of the 'Salon des Variétés' in the Amstelstraat.

origins.name: Bob Haarmslaan
origins.en: Bob Haarms was a former player of AFC Ajax and later a (rehabilitation) coach for many years. He was very popular with the club and the supporters.

origins.name: Bocholtstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Bodenseehof
origins.en: The lake, the Bodensee, located on the border between Germany and Switzerland.

origins.name: Boeckenburg
origins.en: Later name of the castle Boechorst, which was located in the Boekhorstpolder near Voorhout (South Holland).

origins.name: Boeierspad
origins.en: A schooner is a sailing yacht with a flat bottom.

origins.name: Boeierstraat
origins.en: Boat, small flat bottom, mainly used by the middle class for comfortable business trips

origins.name: Boeninlaan
origins.en: Ivan Aleksejevitsj Boenin (1870-1953), Russian writer from the early twentieth century. Living in France since the Russian Revolution. He received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1933.

origins.name: Boerenweteringpad
origins.en: The name of the water, which originally ran from Kalfjeslaan to the current Koningsplein. Also formerly called Oude Wetering, in contrast to the Nieuwe Wetering (Kostverlorenvaart). The Weteringbuurt and the Weteringschans derive their name from this water.

origins.name: Boerhaaveplein
origins.en: Hermannus Boerhaave (1668-1738), professor of medicine in Leiden. Gained international fame. The street name Boerhaavestraat (first to fourth) has been changed quite often: established as Boerhaavestraat on 15-11-1876, changed to Eerste Boerhaavestraat on 15-11-1882. This change lapses again on 10-12-1884. On 13-10-1897 the street is extended with the same name and finally on 19-2-1908 the division into the current Eerste and Tweede Boerhaavestraat follows. For the Second, Third and Fourth Boerhaavestraat appointed in 1882, the names Deymanstraat, Ruyschstraat and Blasiusstraat were replaced.

origins.name: Boeroestraat
origins.en: Island in Indonesia, belonging to the Ambon Islands (Moluccas).

origins.name: Boetonstraat
origins.en: Island in Indonesia, located south of Sulawesi (Celebes).

origins.name: Bogortuin
origins.en: The Indonesian city of Bogor, the former Buitenzorg, is sixty kilometers south of Jakarta and is especially famous for its botanical garden. The garden, which was established in 1817, houses more than ten thousand species of tropical plants from all over the world.

origins.name: Bok de Korverweg
origins.en: Johannes Marius de Korver (1883-1957), footballer. Was a key player and captain of the Dutch national team many times, including in the match at Houtrust (1913), in which England was defeated by the Netherlands for the first time.

origins.name: Bokkinghangen
origins.en: A bokkinghang is a shed, where herring is hung to be smoked. Smoked herring is called bokking. By decree of 1652, this part was designated at Barentszplein for these smokehouses.

origins.name: Bolensteinpad
origins.en: The naming of Nigtevechtpad will be changed to Bolensteinpad because there is already an existing street in Weesp with the name Nigtevechtsepad. This could cause confusion. The name Bolenstein fits within the theme of "castles and country estates along the Vecht". This name was submitted by a resident. Bolenstein is a knighthood town in Maarssen and built in the 14th century.

origins.name: Bolestein
origins.en: Castle-like house on the Vecht near Maarssen (Utrecht), originally fourteenth-century, significantly renovated in the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries.

origins.name: Bolkstraat
origins.en: Louis Bolk (1866-1930), professor of anatomy in Amsterdam. Known in the field of evolutionary theory.

origins.name: Bolstoen
origins.en: The English port city of Boston, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Bombraak
origins.en: Named after a small wheel behind the Oostzanerdijk, near Buitendijk. A wheel is a pond that has formed after a dike breach or has remained after a flood. Braak is a North Holland word for wheel.

origins.name: Bonaireplein
origins.en: Island belonging to the Dutch Antilles.

origins.name: Bonairestraat
origins.en: Island belonging to the Dutch Antilles.

origins.name: Bongart
origins.en: Sixteenth-century castle near Bocholtz (Limburg). Today, only two wing buildings and a round corner tower remain of it.

origins.name: Bongerdbrug
origins.en: Bongerd is another word for 'tree orchard'. In addition, Bongerd is the name of the neighborhood where the bridge was located.

origins.name: Bongerdkade
