origins.en: Another word for 'tree garden'. In addition, De Bongerd is the name of the neighborhood in which the quay is located.

origins.name: Bonhoeffersingel
origins.en: Dietrich Bonhoeffer (1906-1945), German theologian and writer. As a preacher, he openly showed his aversion to the Nazi regime and from 1940 he actively participated in the resistance. In 1943 he was taken prisoner. From prison he wrote his world-famous letters. Shortly before the end of the war, he was executed.

origins.name: Boniplein
origins.en: An area on the southwestern peninsula of Sulawesi (Indonesia).

origins.name: Bonistraat
origins.en: An area on the southwestern peninsula of Sulawesi (Indonesia).

origins.name: Bonnefantenstraat
origins.en: The Bonnefanten Museum in Maastricht. Provincial museum in Limburg for fine arts and archaeology. The collection consists of ancient archaeological finds, medieval sculpture, early Italian painting, painting from the Southern Netherlands and a department of contemporary art. In 1995, the new museum building, by the Italian architect Aldo Rossi, was opened.

origins.name: Bontekoestraat
origins.en: Willem lJsbrantsz Bontekoe (1587-1618), sailor, known for his travel descriptions.

origins.name: Boomgaardlaan
origins.en: Street located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd. The word bongerd means orchard. The streets in the neighborhood are named after fruit varieties.

origins.name: Boomklokstraat
origins.en: Until 1863, the city of the IJ was separated by a long stretch of palisade. In that palisade were a number of openings, so-called 'trees', for the benefit of shipping. When opening and closing the 'trees', the tree bell was sounded. One of the openings was located near the place where the Boomklokstraat is now.

origins.name: Boomsteeg
origins.en: The alley is named after the former corner house on the Zeedijk, then called 'in de lyndeboom'.

origins.name: Boomstraat
origins.en: In this part of the Jordaan, streets are named after flowers, shrubs and trees. The street was also called Lindeboomstraat in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Boorderstraat
origins.en: Metalworker. Someone who works with the metal drill. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Boorstraat
origins.en: Named after the drill, a tool.

origins.name: Bootstraat
origins.en: Reminiscent of the former seventeenth-century shipbuilding yard 'De Boot'.

origins.name: Borgerstraat
origins.en: Elias Anne Borger (1784-1820), Leiden professor of theology and classical history and literature. Poet and orator.

origins.name: Borggraaf
origins.en: Miniature castle near Lottum/Grubbenvorst (Limburg), built in the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Borgloonstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Boris Pasternakstraat
origins.en: Boris Leonidovitsj Pasternak (1890-1960), Russian poet and prose writer. His best-known work is 'Doctor Zhivago'.

origins.name: Borneokade
origins.en: The largest island in Indonesia. Borneo belongs to the Republic of Indonesia, with the exception of the northwestern part, which belongs to Malaysia. Now called Kalimantan.

origins.name: Borneolaan
origins.en: The largest island in Indonesia. Borneo belongs to the Republic of Indonesia, with the exception of the northwestern part, which belongs to Malaysia. Now called Kalimantan.

origins.name: Borneostraat
origins.en: The largest island in Indonesia. Borneo belongs to the Republic of Indonesia, with the exception of the northwestern part, which belongs to Malaysia. Now called Kalimantan.

origins.name: Bornhout
origins.en: The English port town of Burnham (near Bristol), according to a spelling as that found on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Borrendammehof
origins.en: In the sixteenth century, land near Zierikzee (Zeeland) drowned.

origins.name: Borssenburgplein
origins.en: Former country house on the Amsteldijk, demolished in 1886. Around 1583 this was the country residence of Jacob Frans Oetgens, who was married to Lysbeth Bors, after whom he named the country house.

origins.name: Borssenburgstraat
origins.en: Former country house on the Amsteldijk, demolished in 1886. Around 1583 this was the country residence of Jacob Frans Oetgens, who was married to Lysbeth Bors, after whom he named the country house.

origins.name: Bos en Lommerplantsoen
origins.en: Named after a farmhouse on the former Sloterdijkermeerweg (no. 60), originally from the eighteenth century, rebuilt in 1886 and demolished in 1940. The oldest part of the road originally called Joos Banckersstraat (council decision, 1922 and 27-4-1933). On the site of Bos en Lommerplantsoen, before the construction of the GAK building, there were Adindastraat and Saidjastraat (council decision, 1939).

origins.name: Bos en Lommerplein
origins.en: Named after a farmhouse on the former Sloterdijkermeerweg (no. 60), originally from the eighteenth century, rebuilt in 1886 and demolished in 1940. The oldest part of the road originally called Joos Banckersstraat (council decision, 1922 and 27-4-1933). On the site of the Bos en Lommerplantsoen, before the construction of the GAK building, there were Adindastraat and Saidjastraat (council decision, 1939).

origins.name: Bos en Lommerweg
origins.en: Named after a farmhouse on the former Sloterdijkermeerweg (no. 60), originally from the eighteenth century, rebuilt in 1886 and demolished in 1940. The oldest part of the road originally called Joos Banckersstraat (council decision, 1922 and 27-4-1933). On the site of the Bos en Lommerplantsoen, before the construction of the GAK building, there were Adindastraat and Saidjastraat (council decision, 1939).

origins.name: Bosboom Toussaintstraat
origins.en: Anna Louisa Geertruide Toussaint (1812-1886), married in 1851 to the painter Jan Bosboom. Author of a large number of, mostly historical, novels. The street was named in honor of the writer during her lifetime, which was an exception and is still an exception to the rule of not naming living persons.

origins.name: Bosbraakhof
origins.en: Historical name from Rhineland, to which the Sloterpolders belong (map of Rhineland from 1614). Braak refers to dyke breach and means the same as break or wheel (= pond that has arisen after a dyke breach).

origins.name: Bosch van Drakesteinpad
origins.en: Baron Gérard Dagobert Henri Bosch van Drakestein (1887-1972), cyclist. Won seventeen national championships and two Olympic medals (in 1924 and 1928).

origins.name: Bosplaat
origins.en: Eastern part of Terschelling. Nature reserve with dunes, beaches and channels.

origins.name: Bosrankstraat
origins.en: Perennial climbing plant from the ranunculus family. Found in calcareous soil in forests and creeping wood.

origins.name: Boterbloemstraat
origins.en: Plant genus from the ranunculus family of about four hundred species, with usually yellow or white flower petals.

origins.name: Boterdiepstraat
origins.en: Channel in the province of Groningen.

origins.name: Boterkersstraat
origins.en: Yellow to light pink cherry variety with pronounced flavor, a nineteenth-century variety from England.

origins.name: Bottelarijstraat
origins.en: Reference to the wine trade Roders that was located on the Cruquiusterrein between 1965 and 2010. Wine was brought in by ship and stored in five silos. After payment of import duties, the wine was bottled and sold. When the rules were tightened and wine had to be bottled in the country of origin from now on, this came to an end.

origins.name: Botterstraat
origins.en: Fisherman's vessel with bun, in which the fish is preserved alive.

origins.name: Botteskerksingel
origins.en: During the St. Elisabethsvloed of 1421, the village south of the Merwede drowned.

origins.name: Botticellistraat
origins.en: Sandro Botticelli (1447-1510), Italian painter of allegorical figures and portraits.

origins.name: Boulevardpad
origins.en: With the name Boulevard, the neighborhood - which proposed this name - thought of the Eilandenboulevard, a local name for the Kattenburger-, the Wittenburger- and the Oostenburgergracht, which was converted into a wide traffic road by widening and reshaping around 1960.

origins.name: Boutenburg
origins.en: Former farmhouse on the Haarlemmerweg, near the Vredenhofweg.

origins.name: Boutensstraat
origins.en: Pieter Cornelis Boutens (1870-1943), poet. As a teacher of classical languages, also a translator of ancient Greek authors.

origins.name: Bouvigne
origins.en: Castle near Ginneken (North Brabant) owned by the House of Orange from 1614 to 1775. During the siege of Breda (1637) it was the headquarters of Frederick Henry. Building embankment

origins.name: Bouwen Ewoutszstraat
origins.en: Guerrilla captain from the Eighty Years' War. Forced the Spanish to surrender the city of Middelburg in 1574.

origins.name: Bovenover
origins.en: In this building, two streets run over each other, one on the ground floor, 'alongside' the facade, the other street on the third floor, which is why it was named Bovenover.

origins.name: Boy Edgarstraat
origins.en: George Willem Fred (Boy) Edgar (1915-1980), composer and arranger of entertainment music, originally a doctor. With his compositions, he contributed greatly to the repertoire of light music.

origins.name: Boylestraat
origins.en: Robert Boyle (1627-1691), English physicist. Boyle's Law: at constant temperature, the volume of a gas is inversely proportional to the pressure exerted on it.

origins.name: Boymansweg
origins.en: The Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam. Frans Jacob Otto Boijmans (1767-1847), judge in Utrecht, bequeathed his art collection to the city of Rotterdam. In 1849, the Museum Boijmans was founded. The addition Van Beuningen dates back to 1958, when the collection was expanded with the collection of the Rotterdam collector and patron D.G. van Beuningen (1877-1955).

origins.name: Braak en Bosch
origins.en: Former farmer's estate on the Haarlemmerweg, demolished for the construction of garden city Geuzenveld.

origins.name: Brachthuijzerstraat
origins.en: Daniël Brachthuijzer (1779-1832), organist of the Nieuwe Kerk and bellringer of the Munttoren. Interpreter of Bach and Handel.

origins.name: Braeburnstraat
origins.en: Apple variety from New Zealand with firm fruit. Probably a cross between Granny Smith and Lady Hamilton.

origins.name: Brahmsstraat
origins.en: Johannes Brahms (1833-1897), German composer. Master of chamber music. Composed among other things four symphonies, a violin concerto, two piano concertos and about three hundred songs.

origins.name: Bramzeil
origins.en: One of the sails of a ship.

origins.name: Bramzeilhof
origins.en: One of the sails of a ship.

origins.name: Brand Dirk Ochsepark
origins.en: Brand Dirk Ochse (1892-1958), director of the film studio Polygoon based in Haarlem, which became known for the cinema newsreel.

origins.name: Brandewijnsteeg
origins.en: The alley ran behind the brewery 'Den Witten Haen', which used to stand on the Geldersekade. The name is probably therefore derived from this.

origins.name: Brandslangstraat
origins.en: Refers to a company that used to be located here and made fire fighting materials

origins.name: Brandts Buysstraat
origins.en: Jan Willem Frans Brandts Buys (1868-1939). Musician, who settled in Austria in 1893. Composed operas, piano concertos and orchestral music.

origins.name: Brandweerbrug
origins.en: Named after the adjacent fire brigade barracks

origins.name: Brantasgracht
origins.en: River in Indonesia, East Java, 257 km long.

origins.name: Brede Kerkepad
origins.en: The Kerkepad is named after its location and function: the path of the dike village Nieuwendam to the village church.

origins.name: Brede Vogelstraat
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Brederodestraat
origins.en: Gerhard A. Bredero (1585-1618), poet and playwright. Wrote among other things 'De Spaanse Brabander'.

origins.name: Bredeweg
origins.en: Named after the size relative to the surrounding streets.

origins.name: Brediusstraat
origins.en: Willem Elias Bredius (1860-1930). Pioneer of swimming in the Netherlands. Chairman of the Dutch Swimming Federation from 1900 to 1929.

origins.name: Breedveld
origins.en: These names have been given to convey the meaning of the word, as a counterpart to Het Hoogt and Het Laagt.

origins.name: Breezandpad
origins.en: Village in North Holland, falls under the municipality of Anna Paulowna.

origins.name: Breitnerstraat
origins.en: George Hendrik Breitner (1857-1923), impressionist painter, especially of Amsterdam cityscapes. The street was initially named Dijsselhofstraat (council decision, 1925).

origins.name: Bremstraat
origins.en: Heather, belonging to the daisy family.

origins.name: Brenner
origins.en: Mountain pass, located between Austria and Italy, 1374 meters high.

origins.name: Brentanostraat
origins.en: Clemens Brentano (1778-1842), German novelist and Bernard von Brentano (1901-1964), German novelist, who belonged to the so-called exile writers.

origins.name: Brettenpad
origins.en: De Bretten is the name of a former country house annex farm, which was located on the old Spaarnwouderdijk.

origins.name: Breughelstraat
origins.en: Southern Dutch painter family from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Known are: Pieter de Oude, 'the Farmer Breughel' (1525-1569), Pieter de Jonge, 'the Helsche Breughel' (1564-1638) and Jan de Oude, nicknamed 'the Velvet Breughel' (1568-1625).

origins.name: Brienzerstraat
origins.en: The lake, the Brienzersee, located in the middle of Switzerland.

origins.name: Brigantijnkade
origins.en: Sailboat with two masts, also called schooner.

origins.name: Brink
origins.en: Brink means edge. The brink (plaza or plain) is usually located a little beside the settlement. Occurs in villages on sandy soils, higher clayey formations and in villages on a mixture of both soil types. Brinkhof,

origins.name: Brinkiepad
origins.en: To the adjacent children's farm with the same name.

origins.name: Brinkstraat
origins.en: A brink is an open space in a settlement. Nowadays, many brinks have been transformed into a square in a village.

origins.name: Brisselkerkstraat
origins.en: A church village on the island of Schouwen, swallowed by the sea in 1554.

origins.name: Bristou
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the French port city of Brest, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Brittenburg
origins.en: Sunk Roman fortress at the old Rhine mouth near Katwijk (South Holland). In 1520 and also after that, the foundations on the beach became visible during heavy storms.

origins.name: Broekergouw
origins.en: The county runs to the village of Broek in Waterland. The word county is a Waterland term for village road.

origins.name: Broekzijdschepad
origins.en: Seventeenth-century polder south of Gaasperdam, near Abcoude.

origins.name: Bromostraat
origins.en: Volcano on the Indonesian island of Java. Bromo is part of the Tengger massif in East Java.

origins.name: Bronckhorststraat
origins.en: Johannes G. Bronckhorst (1603-1662), painter and stained glass artist of historical scenes (windows Nieuwe Kerk and Palace on the Dam).

origins.name: Brouwersgracht
origins.en: To the many breweries that could be found in this neighborhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The designation Binnen and Buiten is related to the location relative to the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Bruins Slotstraat
origins.en: Jan Albertus Hendrik Johan Bruins Slot (1906-1972), politician. From 1933 to 1942 mayor of Adorp, co-founder of the illegal resistance newspaper 'Trouw'. After World War II, he became a member of the House of Representatives for the Anti-Revolutionary Party and ten years later he was a faction leader. He combined this position with the editorial leadership of 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Bruinvisstraat
origins.en: Whale-like and fish-eating mammal that never grows longer than two meters.

origins.name: Brusselsingel
origins.en: Capital of Belgium, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Bufferstraat
origins.en: A disc on a steel spring between two train carriages, which serves to break the impact when colliding with each other.

origins.name: Buiksloterbreek
origins.en: Until 1921, Buiksloot was an independent municipality, after which it merged into Amsterdam. 'Ban' means both jurisdiction and legal authority. The Banne Buiksloot was traditionally one of the six bans (jurisdictions) into which the bailiwick of Waterland was divided. After the Batavian Revolution of 1795, the word continued to exist, but then only referred to the polder. It was not until 1936 that the Waterland bans were lifted.

origins.name: Buiksloterdijk
origins.en: Waterlandse Zeedijk, as far as it lies in the former municipality of Buiksloot. The section along the extension of Meeuwenlaan was later renamed Leeuwarderweg (council decision, 1936), while by council decision in 1974 the last section of the dike was added to the Landsmeerderdijk.

origins.name: Buiksloterkerkpad
origins.en: Until 1921, Buiksloot was an independent municipality, after which it merged into Amsterdam. 'Ban' means both jurisdiction and legal authority. The Banne Buiksloot was traditionally one of the six bans (jurisdictions) into which the bailiwick of Waterland was divided. After the Batavian Revolution of 1795, the word continued to exist, but then only referred to the polder. It was not until 1936 that the Waterland bans were lifted.

origins.name: Buikslotermeerdijk
origins.en: The Buikslotermeerpolder, a lake drained in 1628. Originally pastureland, between 1965 and 1974 largely built up with urban development, in addition there is a recreational purpose. The dike came under Amsterdam in 1921 under the name Meerdijk.

origins.name: Buikslotermeerplein
origins.en: The Buikslotermeerpolder, a lake drained in 1628. Originally pastureland, between 1965 and 1974 largely built up with urban development, in addition there is a recreational purpose. The dike came under Amsterdam in 1921 under the name Meerdijk.

origins.name: Buiksloterweg
origins.en: The road to the village of Buiksloot from the Toll House. The road has been in Amsterdam since 1877.

origins.name: Buiten Bantammerstraat
origins.en: The name evokes memories of the sixteenth century, when the Dutch brought the products to Amsterdam from Bantam (Dutch East Indies). In 1597, Houtman's ships were unloaded in the Waal. Binnen Bantammerstraat was originally called Bantammerstraat. The bridge over the Geldersekade already bore the name Bantamsbrug around 1600. The houses located on the street were then described as lying outside the Bantamspoort. In 1644 the Nieuwe Waalseiland was created. The Bantammerstraat then received the addition Binnen, and the extension, over the Oude Waal, became Buiten Bantammerstraat.

origins.name: Buiten Brouwersstraat
origins.en: To the many breweries that could be found in this neighborhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The designation Binnen and Buiten is related to the location relative to the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Buiten Dommersstraat
origins.en: The owner of the land on which the street was laid out was lJsbrand Jansz. Dommer. He was a surveyor and councilman, appointed in 1579 as a councillor of the city. Binnen and Buiten indicate the location, inside and outside the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Buiten Kadijken
origins.en: When a lot of land had been silted up outside the old sea wall (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike or canal was built. Originally, the new sea wall was spoken of, but that later fell out of use. With further raising of this new dike, the Lowness and the Height of the Canal were spoken of. The Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat until 1943. This is indeed in the extension of the Plantage Kerklaan, but has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Buiten Oranjestraat
origins.en: The origin of the name is uncertain. It may refer to the house 'de Prins van Oranje', which used to stand here close to the Haarlemmerdijk. The division into Binnen and Buiten Oranjestraat indicates the location: inside and outside the dike (Haarlemmerdijk).

origins.name: Buiten Vissersstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the many fishermen who originally lived here - originally outside the gate. The first street was within the dike, the second was on the IJ side, so outside the dike.

origins.name: Buiten Wieringerstraat
origins.en: Albert Pietersz van Wieringen is the namesake here. According to old documents from 1610 and 1624, he had a house and some land in ownership here. At that time, the street is already referred to as Wieringerstraat. The separation of the two parts comes into use in the eighteenth century, namely inside and outside the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Buitendijk
origins.en: Named after the hinterland of the Oostzanerdijk at the site of the Melkweg sports park and the Coentunnel.

origins.name: Buitendraaierij
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the various workshops were used for the naming, in this case the shipbuilding yard's foundry.

origins.name: Buitengouw
origins.en: Historical name of a connection between Zunderdorpergouw and Buikslotermeer.

origins.name: Buitenkerkerweg
origins.en: Named after Buitenkerk, one of the four quarters in which Diemen was formerly divided. On the other side of the canal, in Diemen, is the Buitenkerkerlaan.

origins.name: Buitenrustpad
origins.en: Former country house on Kruislaan opposite the current cemetery built before 1725.

origins.name: Buitenveldertselaan
origins.en: Named after the Binnendijksche Buitenveldersche polder, originally an area of meadows and gardens.

origins.name: Buitenzagerij
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the various workshops were used for the naming, in this case the sawmill of the shipyard.

origins.name: Bulgerstein
origins.en: Former castle on the Maas in Schieland, according to tradition built in the eleventh century.

origins.name: Bullebak
origins.en: The bull's head was a mythical water ghost, which not only roamed around the old sluice gate near the Haarlemmerplein, but also under the stone vault that connected the Bloemgracht with the Buitensingel (bridge 160). According to tradition, the monster lay there waiting to pull passersby who dared to venture too close to the water into the water.

origins.name: Bullepad
origins.en: Named after a side road that disappeared due to the urban expansion of the Haarlemmerweg, near the Vredenhofweg. Presumably, this was where the bull, or the local stud, roamed.

origins.name: Bullewijkpad
origins.en: River, formed by the confluence of the Waver and the Holendrecht, which flows into the Amstel near Ouderkerk.

origins.name: Bultrugpad
origins.en: Whale-like, black with a white belly side and peculiar bumps on the body, especially on the head, occurs all over the world.

origins.name: Bundlaan
origins.en: Important street in Shanghai along the Huangpu River, which has been extensively revitalized since the 1980s of the twentieth century.

origins.name: Bunsenstraat
origins.en: Robert Wilhelm Bunsen (1811-1899), German chemist, discoverer of spectral analysis. Also inventor of the Bunsen burner named after him, a gas burner in which the gas is mixed with air before igniting.

origins.name: Burgemeester Bletzstraat
origins.en: Jan Christiaan Bletz (1865-1956). Mayor of Weesperkarspel from 1895 to 1931. The street was named shortly after his resignation as mayor.

origins.name: Burgemeester Cramergracht
origins.en: Willem Daniël Cramer (1788-1856), mayor of Amsterdam from 1836 to 1841.

origins.name: Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan
origins.en: Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan Willem de Vlugt (1872-1945) was the mayor of Amsterdam between 1921 and 1941. He was a carpenter's son from Kattenburg who had an early career as a builder and contractor. In that capacity, he was involved in the construction of De Bijenkorf, among other things. The mayoralty of De Vlugt has been somewhat forgotten, partly due to the popularity and influence of his aldermen Floor Wibaut and Solomon de Miranda. De Vlugt earned good money in construction but had no connections with the business, scientific or cultural elite of the city. He was convinced anti-revolutionary: a conservative Christian as mayor of an Amsterdam that was mainly left-wing at the time.

origins.name: Burgemeester Eliasstraat
origins.en: Mr. David Willem Elias (1758-1828). Member of the municipal council 1781-1795 and mayor of Amsterdam from 1813 to 1828. In 1814 co-founder of the Dutch Bible Society.

origins.name: Burgemeester Fockstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Fock (1828-1910), mayor of Amsterdam from 1866 to 1868, then commissioner of the King for South Holland.

origins.name: Burgemeester Hogguerstraat
origins.en: Mr. Paul Iwan Hogguer (1760-1816), member of the Municipal Council from 1791 to 1795, mayor of Amsterdam from 1813 to 1816 and president of the Nederlandsche Bank.

origins.name: Burgemeester Kasteleinstraat
origins.en: Dirk Daniel Willem Kastelein, born 1916, mayor of the former municipality of Weesperkarspel from 1956 until the abolition of that municipality in 1966. The street name was established at the last council meeting of that municipality. Previously, the street was called Gaaspstraat (council decision of Weesperkarspel, 1957).

origins.name: Burgemeester Mulstraat
origins.en: Aart Willem Mul (born 1887), mayor of the municipality of Weesperkarspel, then acting mayor for several years.

origins.name: Burgemeester Rendorpstraat
origins.en: Joachim Rendorp (1728-1792), several times mayor of Amsterdam between 1781 and 1792.

origins.name: Burgemeester Röellstraat
origins.en: Mr. Antonie baron Röell (1864-1940), from 1910 to 1915 mayor of Amsterdam, then commissioner of the Queen for North Holland.

origins.name: Burgemeester Stramanweg
origins.en: Josephus Anthonius A. Straman (1890-1938), from 1920 mayor of Ouder-Amstel.

origins.name: Burgemeester Tellegenstraat
origins.en: Jan Willem Cornelis Tellegen (1859-1921), civil engineer. Mayor of Amsterdam from 1915 to 1921, before that director of the Building and Housing Inspection Service.

origins.name: Burgemeester van de Pollstraat
origins.en: Mr. Frederik van de Poll (1780-1853), mayor of Amsterdam from 1828 to 1835, resigned in connection with the tax riot.

origins.name: Burgemeester Van Leeuwenlaan
origins.en: Wilhelmus Frederik van Leeuwen (1860-1930), successively alderman (1895-1901) and mayor of Amsterdam (1901-1910), commissioner of the Queen for North Holland (1910-1915) and vice-president of the Council of State. During his mayoralty, the municipal companies for water, gas and transport were established.

origins.name: Burgemeester van Tienhovengracht
origins.en: Gijsbert van Tienhoven (1841-1914), alderman from 1874 to 1880 and mayor of Amsterdam from 1880 to 1891, then minister.

origins.name: Burgemeester Vening Meineszlaan
origins.en: Sjoerd Anne Vening Meinesz (1833-1909), alderman of Amsterdam (1869-1872), mayor of Rotterdam (1881-1891) and mayor of Amsterdam (1891-1901).

origins.name: Burgersdijkstraat
origins.en: Leendert A.J. Burgersdijk (1828-1900), naturalist and literary scholar. Translated Shakespeare's complete works into Dutch.

origins.name: Burgersweerhof
origins.en: Burgersweer was formerly a settlement south of and on the Lutkemeer (map by Gerrit Drogeham circa 1650).

origins.name: Burgerweeshuispad
origins.en: Named after the Burgerweeshuis, which was located in the buildings of the current Amsterdam Historical Museum on Kalverstraat from 1580 to 1960, after which it moved to the IJsbaanpad. The orphanage got its name from the fact that only those children were admitted whose parents could be shown to have been officially citizens of the city.

origins.name: Burmandwarsstraat
origins.en: Johannes Burman (1706-1779), professor of botany in Amsterdam. When the street was laid out, it first took the name Oetgensstraat (council decision, 1881).

origins.name: Burmanstraat
origins.en: Johannes Burman (1706-1779), professor of botany in Amsterdam. When the street was laid out, it first took the name Oetgensstraat (council decision, 1881).

origins.name: Busken Huetstraat
origins.en: Coenraad Busken Huet (1826-1886), Walloon preacher, who devoted himself to journalism and literature from 1862. Member of the editorial board of 'De Nieuwe Gids'.

origins.name: Buskenblaserstraat
origins.en: One of the sotternies from the fourteenth century.

origins.name: Bussumstraat
origins.en: Location in the Gooi (North Holland).

origins.name: Butaanweg
origins.en: Colorless and odorless, flammable gas.

origins.name: Butskopweg
origins.en: Dolphin-like with a clear snout and a very stubby, high forehead. Can reach a length of between seven and ten meters. Found in the Atlantic and in the southern Indian Ocean.

origins.name: Buys Ballotstraat
origins.en: Christoforus Henricius Buys Ballot (1817-1890), meteorologist, founder of the meteorological institute. (Buys Ballot Law).

origins.name: Buyskade
origins.en: Johan Theodoor Buys (1828-1893), Leiden professor of political science. Wrote, among other things, 'The Constitution', a three-part standard work, published 1883-1888.

origins.name: Buyspad
origins.en: Johan Theodoor Buys (1828-1893), Leiden professor of political science. Wrote, among other things, 'The Constitution', a three-part standard work published between 1883 and 1888.

origins.name: Buziaustraat
origins.en: Johannes Fr. Buziau (1877-1958). Revue artist. For many years associated with the Ter Hall revue.

origins.name: C. Kruyswijkstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Kruyswijk (1884-1935), architect. Of his hand are fourteen Amsterdam primary schools and several churches, such as the current Apostolic Church on Clematisstraat.

origins.name: C. van Eesterenlaan
origins.en: Cornelis van Eesteren (1897-1988), architect and urban planner. From 1929 to 1959 he was head of the Urban Development Department of the Department of Public Works of the municipality of Amsterdam. Designer of the General Expansion Plan Amsterdam. He had a very important role in the planning of the post-war neighborhoods Slotermeer, Slotervaart, Osdorp and the Bijlmermeer.

origins.name: C.J.K. van Aalststraat
origins.en: Cornelis Johannes Karel van Aalst (1866-1939), banker. President of the Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij and later director of the Nederlandsche Overzee Trust Maatschappij. One of the initiators of the establishment of the Koninklijke Hollandsche Lloyd and the Nederlandsche Scheepvaart Unie.

origins.name: C.K. Eloutstraat
origins.en: Cornelis K. Elout (1870-1947), journalist, for many years a parliamentary reporter and correspondent affiliated with the Algemeen Handelsblad.

origins.name: C.P.M. Rommeplantsoen
origins.en: Carl Paul Maria Romme (1896-1980), statesman. Member of the House of Representatives for the Roman Catholic State Party (1933-1937), Minister of Social Affairs under Colijn (1937-1939) and alderman of the municipality of Amsterdam. From 1946 to 1961 he was the leader of the KVP faction and from 1945 to 1953 editor-in-chief of 'deVolkskrant'. In 1971 he became Minister of State.

origins.name: Cabotstraat
origins.en: Father Giovanni Cabot (1425-1498) and son Sebastiano Cabot (1472-1557), Italian explorers. Giovanni discovered Labrador among other things, Sebastiano explored the east coast of South America and discovered Newfoundland.

origins.name: Cabralstraat
origins.en: Pedro Alvarez Cabral (1460-1520). Portuguese sailor, who discovered Brazil on his journey to India in 1500.

origins.name: Cacaoweg
origins.en: The tropical product, raw material for chocolate, that is transhipped in the Amsterdam port.

origins.name: Callantsoogstraat
origins.en: Village in the North Holland dune strip.

origins.name: Camera Obscurabrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after the book Camera Obscura, which was published in 1839 by Hildebrand, a pseudonym of Nicolaas Beets (1814-1903).

origins.name: Camille Balystraat
origins.en: Camille E. Baly (St. Maarten, 1936 - St. Maarten, 2012) was a poet, writer and lecturer. In his work he made extensive use of the oral history of the Bovenwindse islands of the former Dutch Antilles. He wrote mainly in English, but also gave lectures in Dutch. He served for many years as the head of the Culture and Education Department of the island of Sint Maarten

origins.name: Campanulapad
origins.en: Named after the plant.

origins.name: Campanulastraat
origins.en: Named after the plant.

origins.name: Camperstraat
origins.en: Petrus Camper (1722-1789), professor of medicine and surgery in Amsterdam and Groningen.

origins.name: Cannenburg
origins.en: Castle near Vaassen (Gelderland) from the fourteenth century, subsequently repeatedly renovated.

origins.name: Capriweg
origins.en: Italian island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Carillonstraat
origins.en: Clock game consisting of a number of cast bells.

origins.name: Carnapstraat
origins.en: Rudolf Carnap (1891-1970), German-American philosopher. From 1931 to 1935 professor in Prague. The task of philosophy for Carnap consisted mainly in the logical and epistemological analysis of the language of science.

origins.name: Carolina MacGillavrylaan
origins.en: Carolina Henriëtte MacGillavry (1904-1993), professor of chemistry at the University of Amsterdam. She was the first woman to join the Royal Academy of Sciences (KNWA) (in 1950).

origins.name: Carrascoplein
origins.en: Name of the airport in Montevideo, Uruguay.

origins.name: Carry Pothuis-Smitstraat
origins.en: Wilhelmina Carolina Benjamina Smit (1872-1951), a feminist from the first hour and a leading figure in the social democratic women's organizations. From 1919 to 1924, she was a member of the Amsterdam city council. In 1920, she became the first female member of the House of Representatives.

origins.name: Carry van Bruggenstraat
origins.en: Carry de Haan (1881-1932), writer, wife of the writer Kees van Bruggen.

origins.name: Cas Oorthuyskade
origins.en: Photographer (1908-1975). Became a member of the Association of Workers Photographers in the 1930s. During World War II, he was part of the photography group, which later became known as De Ondergedoken Camera. He captured the hunger winter of 1944 in photographs. Even after the liberation, social commitment remained central to Oorthuys' photography for a long time.

origins.name: Casablancaweg
origins.en: Port city in Morocco. The street is located near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

origins.name: Castorplein
origins.en: Star in the zodiac sign Gemini.

origins.name: Castorstraat
origins.en: Star in the zodiac sign Gemini.

origins.name: Catharina Boudewijnshof
origins.en: Catharina Boudewijns (ca. 1520-after 1603), South Dutch poet, representative of the specifically Catholic literature in the second half of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Catharina van Rennesstraat
origins.en: Composer, singer and pedagogue (1858-1940). Her great merit lies in the field of children's songs. She composed much music to texts by Guido Gezelle and wrote the music for 'Three little kindergarteners' and 'Children of a Father' among other things. Founded singing schools in various places.

origins.name: Catharina van Tussenbroekstraat
origins.en: Doctor (1852-1925), graduated in 1887 and therefore belongs to the three female doctors who graduated before 1898. At the National Exhibition of Women's Work in 1898, she made a plea for good vocational training for women. Member of the Association of women with an academic title. In 1919 she ended her career as a midwife.

origins.name: Ceintuurbaan
origins.en: At the end of the nineteenth century, a beltway or belt was laid around a large part of the city, which later took the name Ceintuurbaan as far as this road was between the Boerenwetering and the Amstel. The other parts later received other names, because a middle section was not yet in Amsterdam at that time.

origins.name: Ceintuurbrug
origins.en: At the end of the nineteenth century, a beltway or belt was laid around a large part of the city, which later took the name Ceintuurbaan as far as this road was between the Boerenwetering and the Amstel. The other parts later received other names, because a middle section was not yet in Amsterdam at that time.

origins.name: Celebesstraat
origins.en: Island in Indonesia. Now called Sulawesi.

origins.name: Celsiusstraat
origins.en: Anders Celsius (1701-1744), Swedish physicist and astronomer. In 1742 he introduced a temperature scale from zero to one hundred degrees, known as the Celsius scale. The street was originally named Steinstraat by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1891).

origins.name: Centaurusstraat
origins.en: Constellation above the southern hemisphere.

origins.name: Centavoshof
origins.en: The centavo has the value of 1/100 of the standard coin of Portugal (the escudo).

origins.name: Centimehof
origins.en: The cent has the value of 1/100 of the standard coin of France (the French franc).

origins.name: Centrale Groothandelsmarkt
origins.en: References the Centrale Market Halls

origins.name: Céramiquelaan
origins.en: Wijk aan de Maas in Maastricht, which derives its name from the demolished pottery factory Société Céramique. In 1987, the current buildings were developed by architects such as Aldo Rossi and Jo Coenen.

origins.name: Ceramplein
origins.en: Island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Chaloen
origins.en: The castle, also known as Schaloen, located near Valkenburg (Limburg), built in the seventeenth century, restored and modified in 1894.

origins.name: Changiweg
origins.en: Name of Singapore's airport.

origins.name: Charles Boissevainstraat
origins.en: Journalist (1842-1929). For many years editor-in-chief of the Algemeen Handelsblad. Known for his writings in the section 'From day to day'.

origins.name: Charles Leickertstraat
origins.en: Painter (1818-1907), mainly painted cityscapes.

origins.name: Charlie Parkerstraat
origins.en: American jazz alto saxophonist (1920-1955), nicknamed Bird. Improvisational musician and composer. One of the most important figures in the history of jazz music.

origins.name: Charlotte Brontéstraat
origins.en: English novelist (1816-1855), sister of the writers Anne and Emily Brontë. The correct spelling is by the way Brontë. Her most famous book is 'Jane Eyre'.

origins.name: Charlotte de Bourbonstraat
origins.en: The third wife of Prince William of Orange (1546-1582).

origins.name: Chasséstraat
origins.en: David Henderikus Chassé (1765-1849), officer. In 1815 general in the battle of Waterloo, defended the Citadel of Antwerp in 1832. The street was named Van Rijnstraat (council decision of Sloten, 1910) when it was built.

origins.name: Chestertonlaan
origins.en: Gilbert Keith Chesteron (1874-1936), English novelist, poet and essayist. His lasting fame is due to the stories about the priest-detective Father Brown.

origins.name: Chet Bakerstraat
origins.en: Chesney Henry Baker (1929-1988), American singer and trumpeter. Known for his restrained trumpet solos and his fragile singing. In the 1980s he worked mainly in Europe. Died in Amsterdam from a fall from the window of a hotel on Prins Hendrikkade.

origins.name: Chico Mendesstraat
origins.en: Brazilian rubber tapper (1944-1988) from the Amazon region, prominent activist for the conservation of the rainforests and against land theft by large landowners.

origins.name: Chopinstraat
origins.en: Frederic Chopin (1810-1849), Polish composer and pianist, settled in Paris in 1831.

origins.name: Chris Lebeaustraat
origins.en: Visual artist (1878-1945), important representative of Dutch Art Nouveau and Art Deco. He was active in the resistance during World War II. In 1943 he was arrested and two years later died in the Dachau concentration camp.

origins.name: Christiaan Brüningsstraat
origins.en: Hydrologist (1736-1805). Strived for centralization of water management.

origins.name: Christiaan de Wetstraat
origins.en: One of the farmer generals of the Orange Free State (1854-1922). He caused the English a number of defeats. Even after the peace of 1902, he remained anti-English. He was still named after him during his lifetime. The street was first named De Wetstraat in 1904. The shape of the street was changed several times by council decision in 1920, 26-7-1923 and 7-5-1929.

origins.name: Christiaan Huygensplein
origins.en: Mathematician and physicist (1629-1695), inventor of the pendulum clock works and designer of the theory of light waves.

origins.name: Christian Neefestraat
origins.en: Christian Gottlob Neefe (1748-1798), German opera composer and conductor. Court organist in Bonn and from 1779 teacher of Ludwig van Beethoven.

origins.name: Christine Poolmanhof
origins.en: Actress (1850-1930), for many years associated with the Royal Association Het Nederlands Toneel under Willem Royaards.

origins.name: Christine Stoetzhof
origins.en: Actress (1829-1897), she excelled in comedic roles and succeeded Mrs. Kleine as a teacher at the Drama School. She was a granddaughter of Majofski, mother of Marie van Westerhoven and grandmother of Louis Chrispijn.

origins.name: Christoffel Plantijngracht
origins.en: South Dutch printer and lexicographer (1514-1589). His printing house and publishing house in Antwerp developed into one of the most famous in Europe (now a museum).

origins.name: Christoffel Plantijnpad
origins.en: South Dutch printer and lexicographer (1514-1589). His printing house and publishing house in Antwerp developed into one of the most famous in Europe (now a museum).

origins.name: Christoffelkruidstraat
origins.en: In South Limburg, ornamental plant from the ranunculus family with white flowers and poisonous, black berries.

origins.name: Chrysantenstraat
origins.en: Plant.

origins.name: Churchill-laan
origins.en: Sir Winston L.S. Churchill (1874-1965), English statesman, leader of the British war cabinet in the 1940s-45s. One of the great three - alongside Roosevelt and Stalin -, thanks to whom we owe our liberation. Received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1953. Churchill is one of the few people who were honored with street naming during their lifetime. Before 1946, the street was called Noorder Amstellaan (council decision, 1922).

origins.name: Cilliersstraat
origins.en: Sarel Cilliers, South African, leader of the Great Trek of the Boers in 1836 from the Cape Colony to the later Transvaal.

origins.name: Circusplein
origins.en: Attractions in a tent, including animal training, acrobatics and clown shows. The name is related to the caravan world and refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Cissy van Marxveldtstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Sietske Beek-de Haan (1889-1948), children's book writer. Especially known for her four-part Joop ter Heul series.

origins.name: Citroenenstraat
origins.en: Citrus fruit.

origins.name: Clara Bartonstraat
origins.en: Nurse (1821-1912). Known as the 'Florence Nightingale' from the American Civil War. One of the pioneers of the Red Cross.

origins.name: Clara Meyer-Wichmannstraat
origins.en: Clara Gertrud Meyer-Wichmann (1885-1922), lawyer and publicist. Involved in the founding of a local branch of the Dutch Federation for Women's Suffrage. From 1911 to 1916, she published extensively on women's suffrage. The national support point for the government's emancipation policy in the field of law, the Clara Wichmann Foundation, is named after her.

origins.name: Clara Schumannstraat
origins.en: Clara Schuman (1819 - 1896) German composer and pianist

origins.name: Clara Zetkinstraat
origins.en: German advocate of women's emancipation (1857-1933), active from 1878 for the then illegal German Social Democratic Party. At the beginning of this century she headed the German women's movement. From 1920 to 1933 she was a member of the Reichstag, which she chaired in 1933.

origins.name: Claude Debussylaan
origins.en: Claude Achille Debussy (1862-1918), French composer. Innovator within classical music. Was inspired by his travels to Beirut and by Javanese music. With his own separate sound combinations and harmonies, he wrote numerous works for piano, orchestra, chamber music and vocal music.

origins.name: Claus van Amsbergstraat
origins.en: Claus George Willem Otto Frederik Geert van Amsberg (1926-2002), Prince of the Netherlands, Viscount van Amsberg, husband of Queen Beatrix of the Netherlands. Prince Claus was committed to peace and human rights. He was appointed, among other things, as a member of the National Advisory Council for Development Cooperation, chairman of the National Commission for Development Strategy and as chairman of the Dutch Volunteer Foundation.

origins.name: Clauskindereweg
origins.en: In 1511 drowned village on Schouwen-Duiveland (Zeeland) by a storm surge.

origins.name: Clematisstraat
origins.en: Climbing plant.

origins.name: Cliffordstraat
origins.en: Mr. George Gerard Clifford (1779-1847). Thesaurus of Amsterdam, Minister of Colonies, Minister of State.

origins.name: Cliostraat
origins.en: The muse of history (Greek mythology).

origins.name: Coenhavenweg
origins.en: Jan Pieterszn Coen (1587-1629). Governor-General of Dutch East Indies (1619-1623 and 1627-1629), founded Batavia that after the transfer of sovereignty regained its old name

origins.name: Coentunnelcircuit
origins.en: Jan Pieterszn Coen (1587-1629). Governor-General of Dutch East Indies (1619-1623 and 1627-1629), founded Batavia that after the transfer of sovereignty regained its old name

origins.name: Coentunnelweg
origins.en: Jan Pieterszn Coen (1587-1629). Governor-General of Dutch East Indies (1619-1623 and 1627-1629), founded Batavia that after the transfer of sovereignty regained its old name

origins.name: Coffijboomstraat
origins.en: Named after the historic ship the Coffijboom, with which enslaved people were transported in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Cola Debrotstraat
origins.en: Cola Debrot (Bonaire, 1902 - Amsterdam, 1981) left at the age of fourteen to study in the Netherlands. He studied law in Utrecht for a while, but left for Paris in 1928. From 1931 he studied medicine in the Netherlands and he settled in Amsterdam as a doctor in 1942. During that study, Debrot debuted with a long novella My sister the black woman (1935) and in 1940 he was co-founder of the magazine Criterium. In 1948 Debrot returned to the Antilles and settled in Willemstad, where he was active in the cultural field, especially for the Cultural Center of Curaçao. In 1952 he was appointed minister of the Dutch Antilles and in 1962 governor.

origins.name: Colenbranderhof
origins.en: Herman Theodoor Colenbrander (1871-1945), historian. Editorial secretary of 'De Gids', writer of several historical works including 'De Patriottentijd', 'De Belgische Omwenteling', and 'Koloniale Geschiedenis'.

origins.name: Colensostraat
origins.en: Place in Natal (South Africa), where the Boer general, Botha, defeated the English in 1899.

origins.name: Colimastraat
origins.en: Volcano in Mexico, with two peaks.

origins.name: Colnot en Poonshof
origins.en: The cabaret performers Gustaaf Jacobus Marinus Colnot (1863-1951) and Salomon Poons (1853-1925), operators of the Plantage-Schouwburg on the current Henri Polaklaan.

origins.name: Columbusplein
origins.en: Christopher Columbus (1446-1506), sailor from Genoa. In his attempt to reach China via the west, he discovered the Antilles in 1492 and on three subsequent voyages Central and South America.

origins.name: Columbusstraat
origins.en: Christopher Columbus (1446-1506), sailor from Genoa. In his attempt to reach China via the west, he discovered the Antilles in 1492 and on three subsequent voyages Central and South America.

origins.name: Comeniusstraat
origins.en: Jan Amos Komenski (1592-1670), calling himself Comenius. Founder of pedagogy, from Moravia (Czech Republic). Settled in Amsterdam in 1657, lived for a long time with mayor De Geer at Keizersgracht 123 (the 'House with the Heads'. Buried in Naarden, where his mausoleum is now part of the Comenius Museum.

origins.name: Commelinstraat
origins.en: Caspar Commelin (1636-1693), historian of Amsterdam. Provided the updated and new edition in 1691 of 'De beschrijvinghe van Amsterdam'.

origins.name: Compagniestraat
origins.en: Named after the United East India Company, which had its arsenal, shipyard and canal line built here on Oostenburg from 1661. The building Oostenburgergracht 79 still reminds us of this. The street was laid out on the former Oostenburgermiddenstraat, which has since fallen into disrepair.

origins.name: Computerweg
origins.en: As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Conakryweg
origins.en: African port city, capital of Guinea. The street is located near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

origins.name: Concertgebouwplein
origins.en: The concert hall, built between 1882 and 1888 by A.L. van Gendt. Shortly after opening, the Concertgebouw Orchestra was founded. On the occasion of the 100th anniversary of the Concertgebouw, the square was given this name. Previously Jan Willem Brouwersplein (council decision, 1912).

origins.name: Condensatorweg
origins.en: Part of electrical appliances or independent element, that can contain electrical charge.

origins.name: Confuciusplein
origins.en: Correct spelling is Confucius. Chinese philosopher (551-478 BC), founder of the ancient Chinese state religion, in which personal morality is subject to that of the state.

origins.name: Conny Stuartstraat
origins.en: Conny Stuart (Wijhe, September 5, 1913 - Amsterdam, August 22, 2010), pseudonym of Cornelia van Meijgaard, was a Dutch singer, actress, cabaret performer and musical star

origins.name: Conradstraat
origins.en: Frederik Willem Conrad (1800-1876), civil engineer. Designer of several civil engineering works in the Netherlands and of the plans for the dredging of the Suez Canal. Also of the first railway station near the Haarlemmerpoort (1839).

origins.name: Contactweg
origins.en: Electrical connection.

origins.name: Coöperatiehof
origins.en: The form of cooperation that made housing construction in this district possible after World War I.

origins.name: Coornhertstraat
origins.en: Dirk Volkertsz Coornhert (1522-1590), writer, humanist and philosopher. Fought against the abuses in the Roman Catholic Church.

origins.name: Copernicusstraat
origins.en: Nicolaus Copernicus (1473-1543), Polish physician and astronomer. Learned that the sun is the center of our solar system. This in contrast to the doctrine of Ptolemy, who assumed the earth as the center.

origins.name: Coppelstockstraat
origins.en: Jan Pieterszn Coppelstock, the ferryman who helped the water gunners take Den Briel on April 1, 1572.

origins.name: Cor Hermusstraat
origins.en: Actor and director (1889-1953). As a gifted teacher, he had an influence on the younger generation.

origins.name: Cor Ruyshof
origins.en: Actor (1890-1952), excellent in the comedic genre. Performed with his own company for many years.

origins.name: Cor van der Hartbrug
origins.en: Cornelis van der Hart (1928-2006) was a Dutch stopper, who began his football career at Ajax in 1947, where he was also assistant coach from 1984 to 1987. He played 44 times for the Dutch national team between 1955 and 1961.

origins.name: Corantijnstraat
origins.en: River in Suriname, on the border of Guyana.

origins.name: Corellistraat
origins.en: Arcangelo Corelli (1653-1713), Italian composer and violinist.

origins.name: Cornelis Aarnoutsstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Aarnouts or Aernouts (1914-1943), resistance fighter. Organized the distribution apparatus of the illegal newspaper 'De Waarheid'. Gunned down in Scheveningen on August 10, 1943.

origins.name: Cornelis Anthoniszstraat
origins.en: Painter, engraver and cartographer (1500-after 1559). Known for his plans of Amsterdam. In 1536 he made a painted map, his extensive woodcut dates from 1544.

origins.name: Cornelis Dijksterhuisstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1921-1944), involved in the organization of the illegal newspaper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Cornelis Dirkszstraat
origins.en: Mayor of Monnickendam, later admiral of North Holland (1542-1583). One of the leaders of the Watergeuzen. Defeated the Spanish on the Zuiderzee in 1573.

origins.name: Cornelis Dopperkade
origins.en: Composer (1870-1939), opera conductor, later second conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra. Composed eight symphonies and several operas.

origins.name: Cornelis Douwesweg
origins.en: Maritime, scientific and astronomical (1712-1773). Director of the Amsterdam Maritime School.

origins.name: Cornelis Drebbelstraat
origins.en: Mechanical engineer, physicist and versatile inventor (1572-1631), Dutch by birth, working at the imperial court in Prague (1610-1613), later in England. Designed the first submarine and improved the microscope. The street was acquired in 1921 under the name Kerklaan from the municipality of Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Cornelis Krusemanstraat
origins.en: Painter (1797-1857), painted historical and biblical scenes.

origins.name: Cornelis Lelylaan
origins.en: Hydrologist and statesman (1854-1929), minister of Water Works several times. He designed the plan for the closure and partial drying of the Zuiderzee. His statue, made by Man Andriessen, stands at the beginning of the Afsluitdijk. The town of Lelystad, capital of the province of Flevoland, is named after him.

origins.name: Cornelis Lelyplein
origins.en: Hydrologist and statesman (1854-1929), minister of Water Works several times. He designed the plan for the closure and partial drying of the Zuiderzee. His statue, made by Man Andriessen, stands at the beginning of the Afsluitdijk. The town of Lelystad, capital of the province of Flevoland, is named after him.

origins.name: Cornelis Outshoornstraat
origins.en: Architect (1812-1875). Among his works are the Palace of Public Industry (1859-1864) and the Amstel Hotel (1864).

origins.name: Cornelis Roobolstraat
origins.en: Captain of the Gueux. Captured by the Spanish in 1572 in Haarlem and executed.

origins.name: Cornelis Roosstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Jansz. Roos (1692-1757), mayor of Oostzaan and shipowner in the whaling trade in 1724 and 1725. He owned a dozen warehouses on the Twiske in which there were distillation plants. (His gravestone can be found in the Reformed Church in Oostzaan.)

origins.name: Cornelis Schuurmanhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1915-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Scheveningen. Schuurman was a member of the illegal newspaper 'De Waarheid'.

origins.name: Cornelis Schuytstraat
origins.en: Composer and organist (1557-1616). Gained fame mainly as an organist.

origins.name: Cornelis Sorgdragerstraat
origins.en: Commander of whaling (first voyage 1690). Distinguished himself by recording the experiences of whaling in his 'Blooming rise of the ancient and contemporary Greenland fishing'.

origins.name: Cornelis Springerstraat
origins.en: Painter (1817-1891). Painted cityscapes, including those of Haarlem and Den Briel.

origins.name: Cornelis Troostplein
origins.en: Pastel and genre painter (1697-1750). Gained fame with his group portrait 'Inspectors of the Collegium Medicum'.

origins.name: Cornelis Trooststraat
origins.en: Pastel and genre painter (1697-1750). Gained fame with his group portrait 'Inspectors of the Collegium Medicum'.

origins.name: Cornelis van Alkemadestraat
origins.en: Historian (1654-1737). Wrote about old monasteries and noble houses.

origins.name: Cornelis van der Lindenstraat
origins.en: Conductor and composer (1839-1918), composed operas, cantatas and overtures. From 1886 to 1903 conductor of the Dutch Opera.

origins.name: Cornelis van Rijplantsoen
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1896-1958), fought in 1940 near the Grebbeberg. After his demobilization, he founded a resistance group and was also editor of 'Vrij Nederland'. In 1941 arrested for espionage and possession of illegal weapons, sentenced to death in 1942. This sentence was later converted into fifteen years of prison. He was imprisoned until the liberation in 1945.

origins.name: Cornelis van Vollenhovenstraat
origins.en: Jurist (1874-1933), professor at Leiden from 1901 to 1933. Expert in Indian law and international law.

origins.name: Cornelis Vermuydenstraat
origins.en: Hydrologist (1590-1677). Took his knowledge of Zeelandic embankments with him to England in 1619. Was involved in the draining of the large fenland area The Fens in East Anglia. Was raised to the English nobility in 1629, but later imprisoned for debt due to failed projects. Some of his plans were still carried out posthumously.

origins.name: Cornelis Vriendtstraat
origins.en: Flemish builder and sculptor (1518-1575). Built the Antwerp town hall among other things.

origins.name: Cornelis Zillesenlaan
origins.en: Tax collector (1736-1828) and member of the Dutch Society of Sciences. He made two discoveries related to the improvement of means for navigation determination. However, the intended improvements were not achieved.

origins.name: Coronelstraat
origins.en: Pierre Antoine Coronel (1914-1945) resistance fighter. Born in Ouder-Amstel, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Corsgenbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after timber merchant Corsgen Jacobsz, who in the fifteenth century had an orchard on the Singel, just outside the city. The bridge over the Singel therefore got its name and then also the alley on the other side of the Singel. This bridge was also known as Korsjesbrug or Korsjespoort.

origins.name: Corsicaweg
origins.en: Island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Cort van der Lindenkade
origins.en: Pieter W.A. Cort van der Linden (1846-1935), liberal statesman. Professor in Groningen and Amsterdam, Minister of Justice (1897-1901) and Prime Minister (1913-1918). Brought about universal suffrage and financial equality between public and private education.

origins.name: Cortenbach
origins.en: The original fifteenth-century castle, now a mansion mainly from 1776, located under Voerendaal (South Limburg).

origins.name: Corversbosstraat
origins.en: Nature monument west of Hilversum. The Corversbos originally belonged to the country house Gooilust and was owned for a while by the Amsterdam regent family Corver.

origins.name: Cosmariumstraat
origins.en: A microscopic aquatic plant, algae, consisting of two congruent halves.

origins.name: Couhornerhoek
origins.en: Named after the almost perpendicular bend in the Oostzanerdijk between Plejadenplein and Molenwijk. Lying completely free in the IJ.

origins.name: Count Basiestraat
origins.en: William (Count) Basie (1904-1984), American jazz pianist, composer and bandleader.

origins.name: Courbetstraat
origins.en: Gustave Courbet (1819-1877), French painter of realism. Painted mainly hunting and portrait works.

origins.name: Crabschuytstraat
origins.en: Small fishing boat, which appears at the beginning of the seventeenth century in a description by shipbuilder Cornelis van Yk.

origins.name: Crack-State
origins.en: Impressive state in Heerenveen (Friesland), probably built in 1608 by Hypolitus Crack.

origins.name: Cromme Camp
origins.en: Historical name in the former municipality of Sloten: a piece of land.

origins.name: Cronenburg
origins.en: Former castle under Loenen aan de Vecht. Built in 1122 and destroyed in 1296, rebuilt in 1354 and demolished in 1837. Today only the outlines of the foundations remain.

origins.name: Cronjéstraat
origins.en: Pieter Arnoldus Cronjé (1835-1911), South African general of the Boers, who had to surrender to the English at Paardenburg in 1900.

origins.name: Cruquiuskade
origins.en: Nicolaas Samuel Cruquius (or Kruik) (1678-1754), civil engineer. Designer of a plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Cruquiusstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Samuel Cruquius (or Kruik) (1678-1754), civil engineer. Designer of a plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Cruquiusweg
origins.en: Nicolaas Samuel Cruquius (or Kruik) (1678-1754), civil engineer. Designer of a plan to drain the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Cruuskerkstraat
origins.en: During the St. Elisabethsvloed of 1421, the church village, which is located on the site of the present-day Dubbeldam (South Holland), drowned.

origins.name: Crynssenstraat
origins.en: Abraham Crynssen, Zeelandish admiral. Conquered Suriname in 1667, fought in the Battle of Duins and against the Algerians. Died in 1669.

origins.name: Cullinanplein
origins.en: Culinan is the largest South African diamond

origins.name: Curaçaostraat
origins.en: Island belonging to the Dutch Antilles.

origins.name: Curiestraat
origins.en: The French couple Pierre Curie (1859-1906) and Marie Curie-Sklodowska (1867-1934), discoverers of radium. Received the Nobel Prize in Physics together in 1903. Madame Curie again in 1911 for chemistry.

origins.name: Cuyperspassage
origins.en: Petrus J. Cuypers (1827-1921), architect, creator of Dutch neo-Gothic. Built among other things the Rijksmuseum (1885), the Central Station (1889) and the Vondelkerk (1878).

origins.name: Cycladenlaan
origins.en: Greek island group in the Aegean Sea. All the islands of the Cyclades are located in a circle (ancient Greek: kyklos) around Delos, an important Greek sanctuary in antiquity.

origins.name: Cyclamenstraat
origins.en: Houseplant.

origins.name: Czaar Peterstraat
origins.en: Peter I, emperor of Russia (1672-1725), who spent about half a year in the Netherlands in 1697, first in Amsterdam, then in Zaandam. Worked on the shipyard of the Dutch East India Company to learn shipbuilding.

origins.name: D.L. Hudigstraat
origins.en: Dirk Louis Jacobszoon Hudig (1876-1973), from 1917 to 1947 director of the Royal Dutch Steam Boat Company, had as such a prominent position in the Dutch and international shipping world. Numerous subsidiary positions, including president commissioner of the N.V. Nederlandse Telegraaf Maatschappij.

origins.name: Da Costakade
origins.en: Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860), Amsterdam lawyer, poet and prose writer of Portuguese-Jewish descent, who converted to Christianity.

origins.name: Da Costaplein
origins.en: Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860), Amsterdam lawyer, poet and prose writer of Portuguese-Jewish descent, who converted to Christianity.

origins.name: Da Costastraat
origins.en: Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860), Amsterdam lawyer, poet and prose writer of Portuguese-Jewish descent, who converted to Christianity.

origins.name: Daalwijk
origins.en: Name of a manor house in Markelo (Overijssel) and a patrician house under Zuilen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Daalwijkdreef
origins.en: Name of a manor house in Markelo (Overijssel) and a patrician house under Zuilen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Daam van Harenstraat
origins.en: Captain of the Geuzen fleet during the conquest of Den Briel.

origins.name: Daan Roodenburghplein
origins.en: Architect (1885-1972), designed the Ajax stadium 'De Meer' on the Middenweg that was demolished in 1996. Also designed much in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Dachstein
origins.en: Mountain peak in Austria, 1995 meters high.

origins.name: Dadelpalmstraat
origins.en: Palm species. The date palm has been planted on a large scale for thousands of years due to the edible fruits of the tree, the dates

origins.name: Dadelstraat
origins.en: The fruit of the date palm.

origins.name: Daelenbroek
origins.en: Eighteenth-century castle under Herkenbos (Limburg). Today, only one wing remains, in use as a residence.

origins.name: Dageraadsbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the former, nearby shipyard 'De Dageraad'.

origins.name: Daguerrestraat
origins.en: Louis-Jacques Mandé Daguerre (1787-1851), French photographer. Inventor in 1837 of the daguerreotype, a method (photographic image on a silvered plate) for which photographs could be developed on a large scale, and thus one of the founders of photography

origins.name: Dalsteindreef
origins.en: Men's house under Rheden (Gelderland).

origins.name: Daltonstraat
origins.en: John Dalton (1766-1844), English chemist and physicist. Founder of the theory of atoms.

origins.name: Dam
origins.en: The dam that was built between 1204 and 1275 here in the Amstel River and to which Amsterdam owes its name. Originally there were two squares. The actual dam was called Middeldam. The western part (on the side of the Palace) was called the Plaetse until the sixteenth century. Already in the seventeenth century both squares are considered as one and referred to by the name Dam. In 1795 the name was changed to Revolutieplein and during Napoleon's time to Napoleonplein. After 1813 the name Dam comes back. A part of the Dam on the side of the Bijenkorf had the name Vissersdam (after the Fish Market), and on the side of the Rokin was then the Vijgendam.

origins.name: Damloperspad
origins.en: Freighter with side swords, similar to a schooner.

origins.name: Damrak
origins.en: Rak is the old name for a straight stretch of navigable water. Here is therefore the rak or the waterway to the Dam. Over the course of the eighteenth century, it narrowed on the west side. The name of the water was passed on to it when the road or quay was built (in 1526). The houses on Warmoesstraat between Nieuwebrugsteeg and the Beurs are still called the houses 'aan 't Water'.

origins.name: Damstraat
origins.en: The street that leads to the Dam. The name was given to the Halsteeg, after the widening of this street was ready. The name halsteeg reminds us of the Meat Hall, which stood on the corner of the Nes in the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Danie Theronstraat
origins.en: Military commander (1869-1900) under General De Wet in the Boer War of 1899-1902. Killed by a bomb.

origins.name: Daniël de Langestraat
origins.en: Performing artist (1841-1918), composed symphonies and cantatas. One of the founders and director of the Amsterdam Conservatory.

origins.name: Daniël Defoelaan
origins.en: British novelist and satirist (1660-1731). His most famous book is still 'Robinson Crusoe'.

origins.name: Daniël Goedkoopstraat
origins.en: First director of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (1850-1929).

origins.name: Daniël Stalpertstraat
origins.en: Daniël Stalpaert (1615-1684), architect and draughtsman. Completed the town hall designed by Jacob van Campen on the Dam. As a city architect, he also designed, among other things, the Admiralty Building in Kattenburg (now the Maritime Museum), the Oosterkerk, the church on the Amstelveld, the Synagogue at the corner of the Nieuwe Amstelstraat and the Huiszittenweduwenhof. As a surveyor, he made a plan of the fourth enlargement of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Dantestraat
origins.en: Dante Alighieri (1265-1321), Italian poet and writer of 'La Divina Commedia', among other works, which is still considered a masterpiece today.

origins.name: Danzigerbocht
origins.en: The city of Gdańsk (now Gdansk), an important timber port on the Baltic Sea. Originally a so-called Free City, later German and since 1945 a Polish city.

origins.name: Danzigerkade
origins.en: The city of Gdańsk (now Gdansk), an important timber port on the Baltic Sea. Originally a so-called Free City, later German and since 1945 a Polish city.

origins.name: Dapperplein
origins.en: Olfert Dapper (1636-1689), physician in Amsterdam. In 1663 provided a historical description of the city of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Dapperstraat
origins.en: Olfert Dapper (1636-1689), physician in Amsterdam. In 1663 provided a historical description of the city of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Darlingstraat
origins.en: River in South Australia, named after a 19th-century governor of New South Wales, Sir Ralph Darling.

origins.name: Darwinplantsoen
origins.en: Charles Darwin (1809-1882), English natural researcher, known for his descent and evolution theory.

origins.name: Daveren
origins.en: The English port town of Dover, according to a spelling as that found on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: David Blesstraat
origins.en: Painter and engraver (1821-1899), painted mainly scenes from domestic life.

origins.name: David Humehof
origins.en: English philosopher (1711-1776), precursor of Kant. Also known as a historian.

origins.name: David Kouwenaarstraat
origins.en: Journalist (1876-1957), editor of the 'Nieuwe Rotterdamse Courant' and chairman of the 'Amsterdamse Pers'. Author of 'Amsterdam, crown jewel of Europe' and of 'Between Dam and Muntplein'.

origins.name: David Ricardostraat
origins.en: British economist (1772-1823), of Dutch origin, known for his theories relating to the determination of wages and value.

origins.name: David Vosstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1899-1944), born in Amsterdam, killed in Auschwitz (Poland).

origins.name: David Wijnkoopstraat
origins.en: Politician (1876-1941) of Jewish descent. He played an important role in the railway strike in 1903. Originally a member of the SDAP, he founded the Social Democratic Party (later the Communist Party) in 1909. From 1919 to 1940 he was a member of the municipal council, in addition from 1918 to 1925 and from 1929 to 1940 a member of the House of Representatives. He died at his hiding address.

origins.name: Davisstraat
origins.en: John Davis (1550-1605), English sailor. Discovered the east coast of Greenland in 1585 and the Davis Strait named after him.

origins.name: De Alpen
origins.en: The mountain, located in France, Germany, Switzerland, Austria and Italy.

origins.name: De Arendbrug
origins.en: One of the two locomotives that pulled the opening train on September 25, 1839, on the first railway line in the Netherlands. The departure point was in the current Westerpark; the final stop was Haarlem. The Arend was taken out of service and demolished after 1857; in 1938 a replica was built that is now in the Railway Museum in Utrecht.

origins.name: De Bazelhof
origins.en: Karel P.C. de Bazel (1869-1923), architect, pupil of Pierre Cuypers. Built, among other things, the building of the Dutch Trading Company in the Vijzelstraat and the (former) Maritime Museum in the Cornelis Schuytstraat. Pioneer of mass housing construction.

origins.name: De Biezenhof
origins.en: Historical name, found on a map from the seventeenth century of Sloten/Osdorp.

origins.name: De Bleeckster
origins.en: Whale hunter from the late seventeenth century and early eighteenth century, who operated from Oostzanerwerf.

origins.name: De Boelelaan
origins.en: Gerrit de Boele, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland (1354/55).

origins.name: De Borcht
origins.en: The sixteenth-century castle near Baarlo (Limburg), with fifteenth-century remains. In 1473 the castle was conquered by Charles the Bold.

origins.name: De Breekstraat
origins.en: To the adjacent pond, the Schellingwouder Breek, was formed after a breach of the Waterlandse sea wall. Breek means the same as barren (= pond that has formed after a breach of the sea wall).

origins.name: De Clercqstraat
origins.en: Willem de Clercq (1795-1844), literary figure. One of the leading figures of the 'Reveil'. In addition, director of the Nederlandsche Handel Maatschappij. The road was laid on the former Bleekerssloot.

origins.name: De corridor
origins.en: A corridor is literally a strip of land between two areas. The road forms a connection between the shopping area around the Arena and the Bijlmer station.

origins.name: De Cuserstraat
origins.en: Willem de Cuser, bailiff of Amstelland, Waterland and Rhineland 1326/1327. Killed in 1392 by the Herculean nobles.

origins.name: De Duikerstraat
origins.en: In general, a hydrological name for a pipe for the passage of water under a road or dam. On an old map of Rhineland, the name 'den Duycker' appears in the area of the old Sloten/Osdorp.

origins.name: De Egmondenstraat
origins.en: The North Holland towns of Egmond-Binnen, Egmond aan Zee, and Egmond aan den Hoef.

origins.name: De entree
origins.en: The street leads to the nearby Amsterdam ArenA (see Arena Boulevard).

origins.name: De Genestetstraat
origins.en: Petrus Augustus de Genestet (1829-1861), Reformed preacher and poet. Especially known for his 'Leaked Poems'.

origins.name: De Groene Zoom
origins.en: Named after the layout, a park strip with paths.

origins.name: De Heusweg
origins.en: Probably named after the millers family De Heus who later founded the animal feed company.

origins.name: De Kempenaerstraat
origins.en: Jacob Mattheus de Kempenaer (1793-1870), liberal statesman. Minister of the Interior (1848-1849). Worked on the constitution, which was adopted in 1848.

origins.name: De Klencke
origins.en: Fortified country house dating from around 1740, located in Oosterhesselen (Drenthe). Previously there was another manor house here, of which only a number of foundations remain from 1670 and a tombstone from 1635.

origins.name: De Kluftstraat
origins.en: Name of the café that stood in this location between 1857-1965. 'Kluft' is a North Holland term for an exit or entrance from a dike.

origins.name: De la Reijstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Hercules de la Reij (1847-1914), called Uncle Koos. Farmer general in the Boer War of Independence against the English. Opposed Louis Botha's politics in 1914 and was shot dead in Johannesburg during a police operation.

origins.name: De la Sallestraat
origins.en: Jean Baptiste de la Salle (1651-1719), Frenchman, founder of the congregation 'brothers of the Christian schools'.

origins.name: De Lairessestraat
origins.en: Gerard de Lairesse (1641-1711), painter of allegories, wall and ceiling paintings. He came to Amsterdam from Liège in 1667. In 1707 his 'Great Painter's Book' appeared.

origins.name: De Leeuw van Vlaanderenstraat
origins.en: Based on the novel of the same name by the Flemish writer Hendrik Conscience (1838).

origins.name: De Leggende Osstraat
origins.en: Historical stopping farm along the Kadoelenweg. Rebuilt in 1983. 'Laying' is here slang for lying down.

origins.name: De Lierhof
origins.en: Together with the municipalities of 's-Gravenzande, Heenweg, Honselersdijk, Kwintsheul, Maasdijk, Monster, Naaldwijk, Ter Heijde and Wateringen, De Lier is part of the municipality of Westland formed on January 1, 2004 in South Holland.

origins.name: De loper
origins.en: A narrow and long carpet that is laid out to welcome someone. The street leads to the nearby Amsterdam ArenA (see Arena Boulevard).

origins.name: De Mirandalaan
origins.en: Salomon (Monne) Rodriques de Miranda (1875-1942), a council member for the SDAP for 28 years, of which sixteen years as a member of the Amsterdam city council, among others for housing. Murdered by the occupiers in a concentration camp.

origins.name: De passage
origins.en: The street leads to the nearby Amsterdam ArenA (see Arena Boulevard).

origins.name: De Peerelstraat
origins.en: Former manor house in the Watergraafsmeer. Located next to Zorgwijk on the Oosterringdijk

origins.name: De Rijpgracht
origins.en: Jan Cornelisz de Rijp (1570-1630), seafarer, sailed simultaneously with Heemskerk and Barentsz in search of a northern passage, but did not overwinter on Nova Zembla because he followed a route around Spitzbergen. When the street was built, it was named Willem Barentsstraat by the municipal council of the former municipality of Sloten (council decision, 1910).

origins.name: De Rijpstraat
origins.en: Jan Cornelisz de Rijp (1570-1630), seafarer, sailed simultaneously with Heemskerk and Barentsz in search of a northern passage, but did not overwinter on Nova Zembla because he followed a route around Spitzbergen. When the street was built, it was named Willem Barentsstraat by the municipal council of the former municipality of Sloten (council decision, 1910).

origins.name: De Roos van Dekamaweg
origins.en: Historical novel by Jacob van Lennep from 1836, set in the fourteenth century.

origins.name: De Ruijterkade
origins.en: Michiel Adriaansz. de Ruyter (1607-1676), the famous admiral of Holland and West Friesland. Born in Vlissingen. In Amsterdam he lived on the current Prins Hendrikkade.

origins.name: De Savornin Lohmanstraat
origins.en: Alexander F. de Savornin Lohman (1837-1924), lawyer and statesman, initially anti-revolutionary, after a conflict with Abraham Kuyper Christian-historical. Professor at the Vrije Universiteit and from 1890 to 1895 Minister of the Interior.

origins.name: De Schaapherderstraat
origins.en: Historical novel from 1838 by J.F. Oltmans, which tells the story of the Utrecht War 1481-1483.

origins.name: De Schorrenstraat
origins.en: Nature reserve on the eastern side of Texel, where bird species breed such as spoonbill, mallard and oystercatcher. Marshes are located offshore, eroded pieces of land with vegetation, which are no longer submerged at normal high tide.

origins.name: De Sitterstraat
origins.en: Willem de Sitter (1872-1934), astronomer. Professor at Leiden and director of the Leiden Observatory. Wrote a study on the expanding universe.

origins.name: De Tourton Bruynsstraat
origins.en: Titus Willem de Tourton Bruyns (1898-1943), resistance fighter, born in Teteringe, killed in the German extermination camp Buchenwald.

origins.name: De Wieden
origins.en: The Beulaker and the Belter Wiede, the wetland area in Northwest Overijssel between Giethoorn and Vollenhove.

origins.name: De Wittenkade
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis de Witt (1623-1672), mayor of Dordrecht, and Johan de Witt (1625-1672), council pensionary of Holland, both murdered by the people in The Hague on false charges. One side of the quay first bore the name Maljapenkade.

origins.name: De Wittenstraat
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis de Witt (1623-1672), mayor of Dordrecht, and Johan de Witt (1625-1672), council pensionary of Holland, both murdered by the people in The Hague on false charges. One side of the quay first bore the name Maljapenkade.

origins.name: De-Grote-Geusplein
origins.en: Nickname for Count Hendrik van Brederode (1531-1568). Leader of the procession of the Nobles in 1566. One of the first leaders in the Eighty Years' War against Spain.

origins.name: Deccaweg
origins.en: The decca system is a navigation aid, used in maritime and aviation. It is based on measuring the time difference in receiving radio signals, which are simultaneously transmitted by two stations.

origins.name: Dekschuitstraat
origins.en: Flat-bottomed vessel, with only cargo space on the deck.

origins.name: Del Court van Krimpenstraat
origins.en: Golf player (1889-1944). Founder of the game of golf in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Delflandlaan
origins.en: High Council in South Holland, bordering Rhineland and Schieland.

origins.name: Delflandplein
origins.en: High Council in South Holland, bordering Rhineland and Schieland.

origins.name: Delistraat
origins.en: Landscape on Sumatra's east coast (Indonesia), formerly known for tobacco culture. Capital is Medan.

origins.name: Deltastraat
origins.en: Delta is the name of the country at the mouth of rivers, when they flow into the sea in two or more branches. The word has its origin in the Greek letter delta, which has the shape of a triangle.

origins.name: Demerarastraat
