origins.en: River in South America, along which the Dutch colony of the same name was founded early in the seventeenth century. In 1814 the area became part of the United Kingdom and in 1831 it became part of British Guiana.

origins.name: Demerhof
origins.en: River in Belgium.

origins.name: Den Brielstraat
origins.en: Den Briel was the first city to be conquered by the Gueux on the Spaniards in 1572.

origins.name: Den Burgstraat
origins.en: Capital of the Wadden Sea island of Texel.

origins.name: Den Helderstraat
origins.en: The city on the northern tip of North Holland.

origins.name: Den Texstraat
origins.en: Mr. Cornelis Jacob Arnold den Tex (1824-1882), mayor of Amsterdam from 1868 to 1879.

origins.name: Denderhof
origins.en: River in Belgium.

origins.name: Dennenhof
origins.en: Coniferous tree. The native European spruce is by far the most common species in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Dennenrodepad
origins.en: Farm under Grubbenvorst (Limburg). Red is an old term for forest clearing, compare it to the still existing verb rake.

origins.name: Derde Egelantiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the eglantine (sweet briar), a shrub.

origins.name: Derde Goudsbloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: The flower, belonging to the family of the composites.

origins.name: Derde Helmersstraat
origins.en: Jan Frederik Helmers (1767-1813), Amsterdam broker who devoted himself to the arts, wrote, among other things, 'De Hollandse Natie' (1813). The second part of the Eerste Helmersstraat was in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 and was then called Hofdijkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890). The beginning of this street was originally a short side street of the Nassau quay and was called Sophiapark.

origins.name: Derde Hugo de Grootstraat
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of International Law. Became involved in church disputes as leader of the Remonstrants and was imprisoned at Loevestein at the request of Prince Maurice. From there, he managed to escape in 1621 through a bookcase.

origins.name: Derde Kostverlorenkade
origins.en: To the Kostverloren Wetering, dug in 1413 to obtain a shorter waterway to the Haarlemmer and Leidse lakes. According to some, a reason for the name Kostverloren would be that this waterway, which has been a source of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609, has cost a lot of money in proceedings. The name Kostverloren occurs in various places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Derde Leliedwarsstraat
origins.en: The namesake of all these streets is the oldest, namely the Oude Leliestraat, which is already mentioned in 1560. This derives its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Tower lock). The name passed on after 1612 to the canal dug along its extension and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets located in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Derde Looiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the leather trade, to which these and the nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal belt are named, were first located outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came within the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after those long-established businesses, starting with the Runstraat and the Huidenstraat. After 1658, the tanneries expanded to areas east of the Vijzelgracht, where we now find the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat. The Derde Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision, 1898) for filling in. For the Drowned Nieuwe Looierssloot,

origins.name: Derde Marnixdwarsstraat
origins.en: Philip of Marnix, lord of Sint Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and advisor of Prince William of Orange, author of the Union of the Nobles (1568) possibly poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was laid out after 1850 on the site where the city walls used to be, which were demolished between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Derde Oosterparkstraat
origins.en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark and originally (council decision, 1882) named as Eerste, Tweede and Derde Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat previously bore the name Oetgenspad after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a 16th-century mayor whose land a number of paths were laid out. The street name applied until 1895 until Linnaeusstraat. In the latter year, the street section along the park was named after the park.

origins.name: Derde Schinkelstraat
origins.en: A swing bridge is a short connecting piece between two canals. In this case Nieuwe Meer and Overtoom. It is assumed that the connecting piece owes its name to its shape: 'swing bridge' is synonymous with 'shin', the lower leg between the foot and the knee. The quay was previously called Nieuwer-Amstel Visserkade. The streets were respectively named Visserstraat, Alexanderstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1882) and Willemsparkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1883) by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, but were changed due to confusion with names already existing in Amsterdam in 1896.

origins.name: Derde Vogelstraat
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Derde Weteringdwarsstraat
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed out of the Spui from the outside. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this here. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Parts have been transformed into walking places (First and Second Wetering Plantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat.

origins.name: Derde Wittenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (next to Kattenburg and Oostenburg), built in the second half of the seventeenth century, from the beginning built with shipyards and houses. One of the first shipyards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. Very likely we must look here for the origin of the name Wittenburg.

origins.name: Derkinderenstraat
origins.en: Antonius Johannes Derkinderen (1859-1925), painter. Known for his murals (town hall in Den Bosch) and book illustrations. Director of the Royal Academy of Fine Arts.

origins.name: Des Présstraat
origins.en: Josquin des Prés or Després (1450-1521), French composer and chapel master (masses and chansons).

origins.name: Descartespad
origins.en: Rene Descartes (1596-1650), also called Cartesius. French philosopher, natural scientist and mathematician. Founder of modern philosophy. He lived from 1629 to 1649 at the Westermarkt (no. 6).

origins.name: Descartesstraat
origins.en: Rene Descartes (1596-1650), also called Cartesius. French philosopher, natural scientist and mathematician. Founder of modern philosophy. He lived from 1629 to 1649 at the Westermarkt (no. 6).

origins.name: Desselstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Deurloostraat
origins.en: One of the Zeeuwse sea gulfs, at the mouth of the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Develstein
origins.en: Name of a townhouse in Heerjansdam (South Holland).

origins.name: Dever
origins.en: Castle dating from around 1400 near Lisse (South Holland), of which only the ruins of a large semicircular tower remain today. A manor house was built against it in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Deymanstraat
origins.en: Jan Deyman (1620-1666), professor of anatomy in Amsterdam. The street was previously called Tweede Boerhaavestraat (council decision, 1882).

origins.name: Diaconessenbrug
origins.en: Near this bridge stood a hospital, the LDI: The Lutheran Sisters Institution, from 1884 for more than 100 years. The Sisters, who were responsible for "nursing care", also lived mostly in the building at Koninginneweg 1.

origins.name: Diamantstraat
origins.en: Hardest and most precious gemstone. The reason why this and other gemstones are named after it is unknown. It is assumed that this happened in connection with the diamond cutting workshop of Asscher, which has been located in Tolstraat since 1907. The street has been transferred under the name Eerste De Ruyterdwarsstraat from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890).

origins.name: Diatomastraat
origins.en: Microscopically small aquatic creature. One of the diatoms, a diatom.

origins.name: Dichtershofje
origins.en: Reference to the overarching theme of the street names in the neighborhood. In the immediate vicinity of this courtyard, many eighteenth and nineteenth-century poets and writers are named.

origins.name: Dick Greinerstraat
origins.en: Architect (1891-1964), among other things, built the center of Betonstad in Amsterdam Watergraafsmeer in the 1920s. After the war, he contributed to the development of Middelburg and Ierseke.

origins.name: Dick Hilleniuspad
origins.en: Biologist, essayist and poet (1927-1987). In his versatile work, these three aspects are always recognizable. He wrote about travel and art, among other things.

origins.name: Dickenslaan
origins.en: Charles John Huffham Dickens (1812-1870), English novelist. In his work he exposes social injustices, for example in 'Oliver Twist'. Author of the famous Christmas story 'A Christmas Carol'.

origins.name: Diderotstraat
origins.en: Denis Diderot (1713-1784), French philosopher, who, among other things, together with d'Alembert compiled an encyclopedia of 35 volumes in 1749.

origins.name: Diemerbospad
origins.en: The Diemerbospad is a cycling path between the Brasapark in Amsterdam Zuidoost and the Diemerbos in the municipality of Diemen.

origins.name: Diemerparklaan
origins.en: Named after the village of Diemen. The park is ecologically managed and acts as a link between the nature reserves on the south and north sides of the IJmeer.

origins.name: Diemerzeedijk
origins.en: This dike, only partially in Amsterdam, runs from Zeeburg along the village of Diemen to Muiderberg. The dike was already built in the fourteenth century to divert the water of the Zuiderzee. Before the draining of the Watergraafs- or Diemermeer, the dike was the only connection from Amsterdam to Muiden and surrounding areas.

origins.name: Diepen
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the French port city of Dieppe, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Diepenbeekplantsoen
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Diepenbrockstraat
origins.en: Alphonsus Joannes Marie Diepenbrock (1862-1921), composer of international level. Mainly wrote church music.

origins.name: Dierenriem
origins.en: The belt of sun and planets on the firmament. In ancient times, the zodiac was captured with twelve signs (constellations) at equal distances.

origins.name: Diezestraat
origins.en: River in North Brabant, formed by the confluence of the Dommel and the Aa.

origins.name: Digitaalstraat
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Dijkbraak
origins.en: Named after the wheel (= puddle formed after a dike breach or remaining after a flood) within the Oostzanerdijk west of the Zuideinde to Oostzaan. Braak is a North Holland word for wheel.

origins.name: Dijkdwarsstraat
origins.en: The street was built at the end of the sixteenth century as a dike, after which the surrounding area (formerly a swamp) was drained.

origins.name: Dijkgraafplein
origins.en: A dike reeve is the chairman of the dike or water board.

origins.name: Dijkmanshuizenstraat
origins.en: Polder on the Wadden Sea island of Texel, north of Oudeschild, nature reserve.

origins.name: Dijkmeerlaan
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Dijkmeerstraat
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Dijksgracht
origins.en: Named after the water of the same name, which runs on the inside of the railway embankment located here. This embankment originally closed the Oosterdok off from the then still open IJ.

origins.name: Dijkstraat
origins.en: The street was built at the end of the sixteenth century as a dike, after which the surrounding area (formerly a swamp) was drained.

origins.name: Dijkwater
origins.en: Nature reserve between Duiveland and Dreischor (Zeeland). Closed creek with riparian lands.

origins.name: Dijkwegpad
origins.en: Old local name from this part of Rhineland.

origins.name: Dijlehof
origins.en: River in Belgium.

origins.name: Dijsselhofplantsoen
origins.en: Gerrit Willem Dijsselhof (1866-1924), painter of impressionism. The park was first called Breitnerpark for a few years (council decision, 1925).

origins.name: Dikninge
origins.en: Originally this was an old abbey (1325-1602), now a late-empire country house on the Reest near De Wijk (Drenthe). Fence posts from 1817.

origins.name: Dilbeekpad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Dillestraat
origins.en: Plant from the aster family, which is often used as a kitchen herb in the northern half of Europe.

origins.name: Dilsenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Dina Appeldoornstraat
origins.en: Christina Adriana Arendina Koudijs, born Van Appeldoorn (1884-1938), composer of chamber music and symphonic poems. Also composed Dutch dances and a suite for orchestra.

origins.name: Dinarpromenade
origins.en: Currency from the Arab world and the Balkans

origins.name: Dintelstraat
origins.en: River in North Brabant. Flows into the Volkerak near Dinteloord.

origins.name: Diopter
origins.en: Pseudonym of Arie Keppler (1876-1941). Literally: wastrel, also known as lookout. The first director of the Amsterdam Municipal Housing Service (1915-1936). Great advocate and promoter of social housing. Under his leadership, among other things, the garden towns in the north were built.

origins.name: Diponegorostraat
origins.en: Diponegoro (Jakarta, Java 1785 - Makassar, 1855). The aristocrat Diponegoro, 'prince' of a Javanese principality, led the Javanese uprising against Dutch colonial rule in the Java War (1825-1830). Dutch authority wavered, but still achieved victory. The battle may have cost more than 200,000 deaths. Diponegoro was exiled to Celebes. Diponegoro is one of the greatest 'national heroes' of Indonesia.

origins.name: Dirhampad
origins.en: In the Valutabuurt of Nieuw-West, parallel to the Guldenpromenade, there is an unnamed bicycle path. This bicycle path is named after the Moroccan currency unit the Dirham, with which this important bicycle path gets the name Dirhampad.

origins.name: Dirk Bonsstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1897-1945), born in Brandwijk, executed by firing squad in Zijpersluis.

origins.name: Dirk Deutekompad
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1895-1945), member of the illegal CPN. Arrested in July 1944 for his help to Jews and transported to Neuengamme/Buchenwald camp, where he died on April 20, 1945. In the camp he cared for a group of Jewish children, all of whom were hanged by the camp authorities.

origins.name: Dirk Hartoghstraat
origins.en: Sailor, who discovered the west coast of Australia in 1616.

origins.name: Dirk Schäferstraat
origins.en: Composer and pianist (1873-1931). Great interpreter of Chopin.

origins.name: Dirk Sonoystraat
origins.en: Diederick van Sonoy. Leader of the Watergeuzen (1529-1597), a nobleman who fled Germany, who sided with Prince William of Orange and was appointed governor of West Friesland. During the reign of Prince Maurice, he fell out of favor.

origins.name: Dirk van Hasseltssteeg
origins.en: the Jordaan and he received several medals from the city of Amsterdam for humanity. In the immediate vicinity of this bridge are three courtyards named after men, who also saved many drowning people, namely Doris Rijkers, Jan Cupido and Frans Naerebout.

origins.name: Dirk Vreekenstraat
origins.en: Participant in February strike 1941.

origins.name: Dirk Wittehof
origins.en: By profession a trader (1884-1932), in his spare time a songwriter of folk songs, which were sung with great success by Pisuisse.

origins.name: Dirkshornplantsoen
origins.en: Village south of Schagen (North Holland).

origins.name: Discusstraat
origins.en: Discus, used in discus throwing during the Greek and Roman camp games.

origins.name: Disketteweg
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Displaystraat
origins.en: As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Distelachterstraat
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Distelkade
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Distelkruisstraat
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Distelplein
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Distelvoorstraat
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Distelweg
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Ditlaar
origins.en: The former manor house of dam lord Ellard Ditelaar, which stood in the eighteenth century between the village of Sloten and the Slotermeer.

origins.name: Djakartaterras
origins.en: Also known as: Jakarta (formerly Batavia). The capital of the Republic of Indonesia. The street section was created by a breakthrough in the facade wall.

origins.name: Djambistraat
origins.en: City and old residence on Sumatra's eastern art (Indonesia).

origins.name: Doblijn
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the Irish port city and capital Dublin, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Docklandsweg
origins.en: Former port industry area on the Thames in Southeast London, which has been redeveloped since the 1980s into a residential and working area. Also a district in Dublin where large-scale renovation projects have been started.

origins.name: Doddendaal
origins.en: Castle located under Ewijk (Gelderland), probably founded in the eleventh or twelfth century. The name Doddendaal dates from 1379. The building has been renovated repeatedly. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, the cellar served as a church for the Roman Catholics.

origins.name: Doggersbankstraat
origins.en: Shallow in the North Sea, where in 1781 the Dutch admiral Zoutman gave the English fleet a defeat.

origins.name: Doggerstraat
origins.en: Ship, derives its name from the place where this vessel sailed for fishing, namely the Dogger Bank. The Dogger fished for herring and cod, among other things.

origins.name: Dokter Meurerlaan
origins.en: Rudolf J.Th. Meurer (1866-1950), Amsterdam doctor, very well-known rowing official and coach of 'Nereus' for many years. He is the promoter of the Bosbaan and founder of the Amsterdam Medical Sports Accreditation Bureau. m

origins.name: Dolfijnhof
origins.en: Constellation.

origins.name: Dolhaantjestraat
origins.en: Nickname of Adrianus van Berques, Walloon nobleman, who served as admiral of the Water Geuzen. Died in Hainaut in 1572.

origins.name: Dolingadreef
origins.en: A stae in Grouw (Friesland). State is a Frisian term for farmer's farmstead.

origins.name: Dollardpad
origins.en: Nature reserve in the arm of the Wadden Sea between Groningen and Germany. The area was formed in the Middle Ages.

origins.name: Dom H. van der Laanstraat
origins.en: Dom van der Laan (1904-1991), architect and Benedictine monk. In 1925, he founded the 'BouwkundigeStudiekring' with fellow students at the Delft Technical University, which often met at the home of Granpré Molière - the founder of the Delft School.

origins.name: Domela Nieuwenhuisstraat
origins.en: Ferdinand Domela Nieuwenhuis (1846-1919), Luther's pastor, who left the church in 1879. Dutch folk leader, pioneer of socialism in the Netherlands, founder of the Social Democratic Union. Member of the House of Representatives from 1888-1891. Became a socialist anarchist, which led to a break with Troelstra et al. The park was laid out on the site of the Maria Magdalene Church, which was demolished in 1968. Nearby, on Nassauplein, stands his statue, made by the sculptor Johan Polet in 1931.

origins.name: Domenico Scarlattilaan
origins.en: Italian composer (1685-1757), chapel master in Rome, cimbalist at the Spanish court, composed more than five hundred works for keyboard.

origins.name: Domselaerstraat
origins.en: Tobias van Domselaer (1611-1685), historian. His 'Description of Amsterdam', which he published in 1665, was compiled from notes by Cornelis Dapper and Pontanus.

origins.name: Don Boscostraat
origins.en: Italian priest (1815-1888). Dedicated his entire life to the upbringing of neglected youth.

origins.name: Donarstraat
origins.en: German god of thunder.

origins.name: Donauweg
origins.en: The second longest river in Europe. Originates in the Black Forest and flows into the Black Sea.

origins.name: Dongestraat
origins.en: River in North Brabant.

origins.name: Donker Curtiusstraat
origins.en: Dirk Donker Curtius (1792-1864), liberal statesman, initially a journalist. Fought for constitutional revision. Later minister of Justice. The law on ministerial responsibility and the right of association is named after him.

origins.name: Doornburg
origins.en: The Doornenburgh, seventeenth-century house on the Vecht near Maarssen. Renovated in 1721 and later in the twentieth century. (Not to be confused with castle de Doornenburg in the Betuwe.)

origins.name: Dora Tamanaplein
origins.en: South African resistance fighter (1901-1983), very active in the women's movement. Member of the women's wing of the African National Congress (ANC) and one of the leading figures of the Federation of South African Women.

origins.name: Doris Lessingstraat
origins.en: Doris Lessing (1919-2013) was a British writer.

origins.name: Dorpsstraat Holysloot
origins.en: Village, since 1921 part of Amsterdam. The origin of the name is unknown, the village already appears under the name Hoolesloot in 1288.

origins.name: Dorpsweg Ransdorp
origins.en: The village of Ransdorp was a separate municipality until 1-1-1921. Then the municipality, together with the associated villages of Durgerdam, Holysloot and Schellingwoude, was merged with Amsterdam.

origins.name: Dortmuiden
origins.en: This is the English port city of Dartmouth, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Dorus Rijkershof
origins.en: Captain of the rescue boat in Den Helder (1847-1928). Saved hundreds of shipwrecked people from death. In his honor, the Dorus Rijkersfonds was named, which supports the deceased relationships of rescuers.

origins.name: Dostojevskisingel
origins.en: Fyodor Mikhailovich Dostoevsky (1821-1881), one of the most famous Russian writers of the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Dotterbloemstraat
origins.en: The wildflower, belonging to the buttercup family.

origins.name: Douwes Dekkerstraat
origins.en: Eduard Douwes Dekker (1820-1887), pseudonym Multatuli. An Amsterdammer who moved to the East in 1838 where he became a civil servant, resigned due to a conflict, and then devoted himself to literature. Precursor of the Eighties. He wrote, among other things, 'Max Havelaar' and 'Woutertje Pieterse'. The Multatuli Museum is housed in his birthplace on Korsjespoortsteeg.

origins.name: Dovenetelstraat
origins.en: Plant genus, belonging to the family of the lamiaceae.

origins.name: Dr. C.W. Ittmannpad
origins.en: Cesar Willem Ittmann (1914-1945), surgical assistant at the Internal Hospital. Was affiliated with the Group of Identity Documents Central and the Student Resistance. Provided care for sick and wounded resistance fighters. Participated in sabotage and was executed on the former Rozenoord airfield, located on the Amstel.

origins.name: Dr. E. Boekmanstraat
origins.en: Emanuel Boekman (1889-1940). Prominent socialist democrat, municipal council member for the SDAP. From 1931 to 1940, alderman for Education and the Arts. With his dissertation 'Government and art policy' from 1938, he laid the foundation for post-war art policy.

origins.name: Dr. J.A. Ringersstraat
origins.en: Johannes Aleidis Ringers (1885-1965), civil engineer, director of Rijkswaterstaat and then manager of the Indian railways. Was interned by the Germans during the war. After the war Minister of Public Works and Reconstruction in the Schermerhorn and Beel cabinets.

origins.name: Dr. Jan van Breemenstraat
origins.en: Jan Frans Leonard van Breemen (1874-1961). Pioneer in the field of rheumatism control. The Rheumatology Center was built along this street in 1965.

origins.name: Draaierweg
origins.en: Occupational name of a metal and woodworker.

origins.name: Drachmesingel
origins.en: The currency of Greece.

origins.name: Drakenstein
origins.en: Ridderhofstede near Lage Vuursche (Utrecht) from 1640.

origins.name: Drie Burgpad
origins.en: Former country house on the ringdijk of the Watergraafsmeer, now Weesperzijde.

origins.name: Driebanstraat
origins.en: Polder in West Friesland.

origins.name: Driedistelstraat
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Drieharingenbrug
origins.en: This pickup bridge gets its name from the three hake above the door of the house 'De Drie Haringen' in Vierwindendwarsstraat no.1.

origins.name: Driehoekstraat
origins.en: Built in the middle of the seventeenth century. The name is derived from the shape of the street.

origins.name: Driekoningenstraat
origins.en: Named after a signboard of the corner building on the Singel. The name is already mentioned in 1608. Before that, the street was called Lijnbaanstraat.

origins.name: Driemondweg
origins.en: To the village of Driemond. After the dissolution of the municipality of Weesperkarspel on 1-8-1966 added to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Drontermeerpad
origins.en: One of the Veluwe edge lakes

origins.name: Droogbak
origins.en: The name already appears in the first half of the seventeenth century and probably originated due to the drying of the sheets of the sheet weavers.

origins.name: Drostenburg
origins.en: Farm south of Borculo (Gelderland).

origins.name: Druivenbrug
origins.en: The fruits, grown in the Netherlands for table grapes, in Germany, France, Spain and Italy for wine production and in Greece, the Balkans and California for raisins.

origins.name: Druivenstraat
origins.en: The fruits, grown in the Netherlands for table grapes, in Germany, France, Spain and Italy for wine production and in Greece, the Balkans and California for raisins.

origins.name: Drusiushof
origins.en: Joannes van den Driesse or Drusius (1550-1600), orientalist. Professor in the Netherlands and England.

origins.name: Du Perronstraat
origins.en: Charles Edgar du Perron (1899-1940), poet, writer and critic. He wrote among other things 'Land of origin'.

origins.name: Duarte Pachecostraat
origins.en: Portuguese sailor (died in 1533), contemporary of Columbus and Bartholomew Dias. In 1488 he joined the latter on the island of Principe in the Atlantic Ocean when he returned from his exploration of the route to India around the Cape.

origins.name: Dubbele Buurt
origins.en: Originally located entirely in the municipality of Haarlemmerliede and Spaarnwoude, since 1963 a border correction has brought it to a part of Amsterdam's territory.

origins.name: Dubbelink
origins.en: Farm north of Delden (Overijssel).

origins.name: Dubbelinkdreef
origins.en: Farm north of Delden (Overijssel).

origins.name: Dubbelmondehof
origins.en: During the St. Elisabeth flood of 1421, the church village drowned in the former Zuidhollandschewaard.

origins.name: Dudok de Withof
origins.en: Corneille Abraham Adrien (Bram) Dudok de Wit (1841-1911), advocate for sports. He had the nickname of 'sports minister' and served as a competition commissioner at all kinds of competitions. At the exhibition competitions in Paris in 1900 (the second Olympic Games), he was the general delegate for the Netherlands. His brother L.C. Dudok de Wit (1843-1913), better known as Kees de Tippelaar, has become a symbol of hiking.

origins.name: Dufaystraat
origins.en: Guillaume Dufay (1400-1474), musician from Hainaut. Famous composer of the fifteenth century, mainly of masses.

origins.name: Duffelhof
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Duinbeek
origins.en: The shrub.

origins.name: Duindoornplein
origins.en: Named after the sea buckthorn, a shrub.

origins.name: Duindoornstraat
origins.en: Named after the sea buckthorn, a shrub.

origins.name: Duinluststraat
origins.en: Nature monument near Overveen/Bloemendaal, consisting of forest and dune area.

origins.name: Duivelandstraat
origins.en: Southern part of the Zeelandic island of Schouwen-Duiveland.

origins.name: Duivendrechtsekade
origins.en: The village of Duivendrecht in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. Duivendrecht comes from Doeve (a first name) and drecht (place where the ships are pulled overland). When Watergraafsmeer was still a lake, a ferry was maintained from where the village now lies, across to the other side, towards Oetewaal.

origins.name: Duivendrechtselaan
origins.en: The village of Duivendrecht in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. Duivendrecht comes from Doeve (a first name) and drecht (place where the ships are pulled overland). When Watergraafsmeer was still a lake, a ferry was maintained from where the village now lies, across to the other side, towards Oetewaal.

origins.name: Duizendschoonstraat
origins.en: Named after the sweet william, an ornamental plant.

origins.name: Dukdalfweg
origins.en: Named after the wooden palisade construction, consisting of a straight pole in the middle and about four buttresses, which must prevent ships from hitting the sidewall. The word is derived from Duc d'Alve, the indomitable Duke of Alva.

origins.name: Duke Ellingtonstraat
origins.en: Edward Kennedy (Duke) Ellington (1899-1974), American jazz composer, pianist, bandleader and arranger. Known for his various styles, including jungle and mood.

origins.name: Dulcie Septemberpad
origins.en: Representative of the African National Congress (ANC) in France and Switzerland. In April 1988 she was murdered in Paris for her struggle against apartheid.

origins.name: Dulongstraat
origins.en: Pierre Dulong (1785-1838), French natural and chemist. He discovered that of all solid elements, the atomic temperature is the same.

origins.name: Durbanweg
origins.en: Port city in South Africa. The street is located near the Afrikahaven in the western port area.

origins.name: Durgerdammerdijk
origins.en: Named after the village that belonged to the then abolished municipality of Ransdorp until 1921. The name was created by distortion of the oldest name: IJdoringherdam = dam located at the corner of the IJ. (The outlying polder located here on the outside of the dike has retained the name IJdoorn.) The Durgerdammerdijk is the part of Waterlands sea wall to which Durgerdam is located.

origins.name: Durgerdammergouw
origins.en: Named after the village that belonged to the then abolished municipality of Ransdorp until 1921. The name was created by distortion of the oldest name: IJdoringherdam = dam located at the corner of the IJ. (The outlying polder located here on the outside of the dike has retained the name IJdoorn.) The Durgerdammerdijk is the part of Waterlands sea wall to which Durgerdam is located.

origins.name: Dusartstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Dusart (1660-1704), painter and engraver, pupil of Van Ostade.

origins.name: Dwars Spinhuissteeg
origins.en: To the nearby Spinhuis, a women's prison founded in 1596. From 1833 to 1941, the main police headquarters was located in this building.

origins.name: Dwarswatering
origins.en: Former watercourse near the current Sportpark De Eendracht.

origins.name: Dwergpalmstraat
origins.en: Palm species, belonging to the umbrella palms. Also grows as one of the few palm species in Europe.

origins.name: Dwergplanetenbaan
origins.en: Planetary-like celestial bodies, larger than asteroids but smaller than planets. Unlike the latter group, they have not cleared their orbit of other objects. In our solar system, Pluto, Eris, Makemake, Haumea and Ceres fall under the category of dwarf planets.

origins.name: Dwergvinvisstraat
origins.en: Whale-like.

origins.name: Dynamostraat
origins.en: Device that converts mechanical force into electrical force.

origins.name: Eastonstraat
origins.en: Charles Easton (1864-1920), journalist and astronomer. Editor-in-chief of 'Het Nieuws van den Dag'. Wrote several meteorological studies.

origins.name: Echtenstein
origins.en: Men's house in Emmen (Drenthe).

origins.name: Eckeharthof
origins.en: Meister E.J. Eckehart (1260-1329), German mystic. Dominican monk whose teachings were condemned after his death.

origins.name: Eclipshof
origins.en: An eclipse is the darkening of a celestial body, because it is hidden behind another or comes into its shadow.

origins.name: Ecuplein
origins.en: The European Currency Unit (ecu), currency unit for the European Community. Also used as a standalone currency.

origins.name: Edammerpad
origins.en: Named after the North Holland town.

origins.name: Edammerstraat
origins.en: Named after the North Holland town.

origins.name: Edenburg
origins.en: South African geographical name.

origins.name: Edenville
origins.en: City in South Africa. Small agricultural town, located in the north of the Free State province.

origins.name: Edisonstraat
origins.en: Thomas Alva Edison (1847-1931), North American inventor of the microphone, the megaphone, the phonograph and the electric light bulb.

origins.name: Edith Magnusstraat
origins.en: Edith Magnus (1925-1993), was part of the women's core of the Dutch Association for the Integration of Homosexuality, the current COC, in the 1960s. Organized the first women's national congresses, which were of great significance for the lesbian woman.

origins.name: Edmond Halleylaan
origins.en: English astronomer (1656-1742), member of the Royal Society and in 1731 appointed 'Astronomer Royal'. Wrote about magnetism and published a map of the Atlantic Ocean and a world map, on which he made improvements to courses. A comet and an observatory are named after him.

origins.name: Edmond Halleysteiger
origins.en: English astronomer (1656-1742), member of the Royal Society and in 1731 appointed 'Astronomer Royal'. Wrote about magnetism and published a map of the Atlantic Ocean and a world map, on which he made improvements to courses. A comet and an observatory are named after him.

origins.name: Edmund Gunterstraat
origins.en: English astronomer (1581-1626). Inventor of the quadrant, a kind of ruler with logarithmic distributions. Worked in the scientific field on navigation and navigation problems.

origins.name: Eduard Hellendoornstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1912-1941), involved in the February Strike of 1941. One of the '18 deaths of the Waalsdorpervlakte'.

origins.name: Eduard Jacobshof
origins.en: Amsterdam cabaret artist (1868-1914), introduced the life song in our country.

origins.name: Eduard Meijerstraat
origins.en: Water polo and swimming champion (1878-1929).

origins.name: Eduard van Beinumstraat
origins.en: Eduard A. van Beinum (1901-1959), from 1945 until his death conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra, from 1949 to 1952 also conductor of the London Philharmonic Orchestra.

origins.name: Eduard Vetermanstraat
origins.en: Literary, playwright and director (1901-1946). He adapted some books by Timmermans for the stage.

origins.name: Edumbe
origins.en: City in South Africa, located in the province of KwaZulu-Natal.

origins.name: Edward Masseystraat
origins.en: English scholar, in 1802 he developed the mechanical log, a device that indicates the speed of a ship. Between 1802 and 1848 he obtained six patents on various mechanical nautical measuring instruments.

origins.name: Edward Wrightstraat
origins.en: English scholar (died in 1615), his findings have been particularly important for shipping. Published in 1599 'Certaine errors in navigation'.

origins.name: Eef Kamerbeekstraat
origins.en: Evert Kamerbeek (1934-2008), athlete. As a decathlete, eleven-time Dutch Champion since 1954.

origins.name: Eemlandstraat
origins.en: Region in the northeast of the province of Utrecht, located in the watershed of the Eem River.

origins.name: Eemsstraat
origins.en: Sea gap between Delfzijl and Germany (mouth of the Eems River).

origins.name: Eendenstraat
origins.en: Named after the duck, a water bird.

origins.name: Eendrachtstraat
origins.en: Water between Tholen and North Brabant.

origins.name: Eenhoornhof
origins.en: Constellation.

origins.name: Eensgevonden
origins.en: South African geographical name.

origins.name: Eerste Amstelvlietpad
origins.en: Historic country house on the Amsteldijk. Built after 1721 by Gerrit Nieuwenhuizen, who initially called it Meerhuizen. Since 1784 it has been known under the name Amstelvliet. Demolished in or after 1916.

origins.name: Eerste Anjeliersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Flower, belonging to the rose family.

origins.name: Eerste Atjehstraat
origins.en: The northern part of the Indonesian island of Sumatra. Especially known for the Atjeh War (1873-1904), to which the name of General Van Heutsz is associated.

origins.name: Eerste Bloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion from 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which the canal is named. On the fort stood the mill 'De Blom' from 1614 to 1878, which was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

origins.name: Eerste Boerhaavestraat
origins.en: Hermannus Boerhaave (1668-1738), professor of medicine in Leiden. Gained international fame. The street name Boerhaavestraat (first to fourth) has been changed quite often: established as Boerhaavestraat on 15-11-1876, changed to Eerste Boerhaavestraat on 15-11-1882, this change expired again on 10-12-1884. On 13-10-1897 the street is extended with the same name and finally on 19-2-1908 the division into the current Eerste and Tweede Boerhaavestraat follows. For the Second, Third and Fourth Boerhaavestraat appointed in 1882, the names Deymanstraat, Ruyschstraat and Blasiusstraat were replaced.

origins.name: Eerste Boomdwarsstraat
origins.en: In this part of the Jordaan, streets are named after flowers, shrubs and trees. The street was also called Lindeboomstraat in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Eerste Breeuwersstraat
origins.en: Occupational name. A brewer sealed the seams between the planks in a ship's wall. In the Eerste Breeuwersstraat (formerly Breeuwersstraat), many brewers lived in the seventeenth century, who worked at the shipyards on the Prinsen- and Realeneiland. In 1895, the street running parallel to it was given the same name, making the addition Eerste and Tweede necessary.

origins.name: Eerste Ceramstraat
origins.en: Island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Eerste Coehoornstraat
origins.en: Menno baron van Coehoorn (1641-1704) fortification builder, general engineer of the fortifications.

origins.name: Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat
origins.en: Poet and prose writer (1596-1687), wrote among other things 'Hofwijck' and short poems. He was secretary of several successive stadholders. Before 1894 parts of these streets were called Eerste and Tweede Bilderdijkstraat (council decision, 1878 and 19-12-1883).

origins.name: Eerste Disteldwarsstraat
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after the Eerste World War.

origins.name: Eerste Egelantiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the eglantine (sweet briar), a shrub.

origins.name: Eerste Goudsbloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: The flower, belonging to the family of the composites.

origins.name: Eerste Helmersstraat
origins.en: Jan Frederik Helmers (1767-1813), Amsterdam broker, who devoted himself to the arts. Wrote, among other things, 'De Hollandse Natie' (1813). The second part of the Eerste Helmersstraat was in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 and was then called Hofdijkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890). The beginning of this street was originally a short side street of the Nassau quay and was called Sophiapark.

origins.name: Eerste Hugo de Grootstraat
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of International Law. Became involved in church disputes as leader of the Remonstrants and was imprisoned at Loevestein at the request of Prince Maurice. From there, he managed to escape in 1621 through a bookcase.

origins.name: Eerste Jacob van Campenstraat
origins.en: Master builder (1595-1659). Designer of the town hall on the Dam, now a royal palace, however, was not allowed to complete the work. Van Campen also built the Heiligewegse gate in 1636 and a palace for Prince Frederick Henry in 1657 in Rijswijk. The split into Eerste and Tweede took place after the intervening part of the street was sold in 1930 to Heineken Brewery.

origins.name: Eerste Jan Steenstraat
origins.en: Painter (1626-1679), often painted domestic scenes: cheerful and cluttered interiors. This is how the expression 'a household of Jan Steen' was born.

origins.name: Eerste Jan van der Heijdenstraat
origins.en: Painter and technician (1637-1712), inventor of the snake fire hose and of a new model street lamp. Painter of portraits and cityscapes.

origins.name: Eerste Keucheniusstraat
origins.en: Levinus W.C. Keuchenius (1822-1893), anti-revolutionary statesman. Fierce opponent of the public school. From 1888 to 1890 Minister of Colonies.

origins.name: Eerste Kostverlorenkade
origins.en: To the Kostverloren Wetering, dug in 1413 to obtain a shorter waterway to the Haarlemmer and Leidse lakes. According to some, a reason for the name Kostverloren would be that this waterway, which has been a source of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609, has cost a lot of money in proceedings. The name Kostverloren occurs in various places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Eerste Laurierdwarsstraat
origins.en: The South European ornamental tree

origins.name: Eerste Leeghwaterstraat
origins.en: Jan Adriaansz Leeghwater (1575-1650), civil engineer. Worked as a supervisor and millwright on many drainage works, including the Beemster. Designer of the first plan for draining the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Eerste Leliedwarsstraat
origins.en: The namesake of all these streets is the oldest, namely the Oude Leliestraat, which is already mentioned in 1560. This derives its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Tower lock). The name passed on after 1612 to the canal dug along its extension and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets located in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Eerste Lindendwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the linden (lime tree), a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Eerste Looiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the leather trade, to which these and the nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal belt are named, were first located outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came within the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after those long-established businesses, starting with the Runstraat and the Huidenstraat. After 1658, the tanneries spread out to areas east of the Vijzelgracht, where we now find the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat. The Third Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision, 1898) for filling in. For the Drowned Nieuwe Looierssloot

origins.name: Eerste Marnixdwarsstraat
origins.en: Philip of Marnix, lord of Sint Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and advisor of Prince William of Orange, author of the Union of the Nobles (1568). Possibly poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, formerly called Schans, was laid out after 1850 on the site where the city walls used to be, which were demolished between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Eerste Marnixplantsoen
origins.en: Philip of Marnix, lord of Sint Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and advisor of Prince William of Orange, author of the Union of the Nobles (1568). Possibly poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, formerly called Schans, was laid out after 1850 on the site where the city walls used to be, which were demolished between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Eerste Nassaustraat
origins.en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. The quay was referred to as Buitensingel before the naming in 1879.

origins.name: Eerste Oosterparkstraat
origins.en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark and originally (council decision, 1882) named First, Second and Third Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat previously bore the name Oetgenspad after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a 16th-century mayor whose land a number of paths were laid out. The street name applied until 1895 until Linnaeusstraat. In the latter year, the street section along the park was named after the park.

origins.name: Eerste Passeerdersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Passing was the preparation and processing of Spanish leather. When this type of leather processing was banned in Amsterdam-Centrum in 1631, this passership settled here next to the already existing leather tanneries.

origins.name: Eerste Ringdijkstraat
origins.en: Regarding its location relative to the Watergraafsmeer. The Ooster Ringdijk was called Noorder- and Zuider-Ringdijk before the annexation of the municipality of Watergraafsmeer. The Eerste Ringdijkstraat was then called Schoollaan, while even earlier the name Dielemanstraat seems to have appeared. A Tweede Ringdijkstraat (formerly Dijklaan) has now completely disappeared due to demolition.

origins.name: Eerste Rozendwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the rose, a flower.

origins.name: Eerste Schinkelstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the old amusement park Schinkelhaven. The street was part of the Schinkelkade before 1922.

origins.name: Eerste Sweelinckstraat
origins.en: Jan Pietersz Sweelinck (1562-1621), musician of great fame. Organist of the Old church. Wrote many compositions for the psalms and the love songs. Part of the Tweede Sweelinckstraat was in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1896 as Tweede Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890).

origins.name: Eerste Tuindwarsstraat
origins.en: Garden here has the meaning of shipyard or enclosed space. The street name is derived from the Stadstimmertuin (the City Shipyard), which was located here from 1612 to 1660 (near the Lijnbaansgracht) and where the street ran along.

origins.name: Eerste Van der Helststraat
origins.en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of civic guard and regents' group portraits.

origins.name: Eerste Van Swindenstraat
origins.en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor in Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He was part of the Commission to determine the meter, after which he developed the metric system, which was introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

origins.name: Eerste Vogelstraat
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Eerste Weteringdwarsstraat
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed out of the Spui from the outside. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this here. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Sections have been transformed into walking areas (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat.

origins.name: Eerste Weteringplantsoen
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed out of the Spui from the outside. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this here. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Sections have been transformed into walking paths (Eerste and Tweede Weteringplantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat.

origins.name: Eerstegeluk
origins.en: South African geographical name.

origins.name: Eeuwige Jeugdlaan
origins.en: Probably named after the legendary water source 'Fontein der Eeuwige Jeugd'. The legend states that whoever drank from the fountain would gain a youthful appearance. The lane also borders the Jeugdland district, which was built between 1995 and 1998. The name can also be derived from here.

origins.name: Efua Sutherlandstraat
origins.en: Efua Theodora Sutherland-Morgue (1924-1996), Ghanaian writer, actress and social worker. Head of the Ghanaian Experimental Theater. In 1961 she founded the literary magazine 'Okyeame' and was affiliated with the University Institute for African Studies in Ghana as a researcher. She has made an important contribution to raising awareness of Ghanaian culture.

origins.name: Egelantiersgracht
origins.en: Named after the eglantine (sweet briar), a shrub.

origins.name: Egelantiersstraat
origins.en: Named after the eglantine (sweet briar), a shrub.

origins.name: Egeldonk
origins.en: Farm in Zundert (North Brabant). In North Brabant, the addition Donk is often used and means: small height.

origins.name: Egelenburg
origins.en: Formerly outside southeast of Heiloo (North Holland). Built by the gentlemen of Warmenhuysen.

origins.name: Egellelie
origins.en: The egellelie is a plant that originally occurs along the cape in South Africa.

origins.name: Egelskopstraat
origins.en: Swamp plant, grows well in small ponds.

origins.name: Eggertstraat
origins.en: Willem Eggert, lord of Purmerland and Ilpendam (1340-1417). Very wealthy Amsterdammer, alderman of the city and one of the founders of the Nieuwe Kerk. Before 1865 the street was called Ellendigesteeg.

origins.name: Egidiusstraat
origins.en: The person addressed in an anonymous medieval lament.

origins.name: EGoli
origins.en: EGoli is the Zulu name of Johannesburg, the largest city in South Africa, located in the province of Gauteng. Literally: city of gold. Forty percent of the world's gold has been found in or around this city.

origins.name: Egstraat
origins.en: The agricultural machinery. The street was part of the Zaaiersweg (council decision, 1924) when it was first laid.

origins.name: Ehrlichstraat
origins.en: Paul Ehrlich (1854-1915), German doctor who discovered salversan in 1910, an arsenic preparation against syphilis. In 1908 he received the Nobel Prize in Medicine.

origins.name: Eierlandstraat
origins.en: Northern part of Texel, originally a separate dune island, later connected to Texel by a sand dune wall, after which the Eierlandse polder was formed by the reclamation of the Wadden Sea. Both on the sea side and on the Wadden Sea side are extensive nature reserves. The Eierlandse gap (between Texel and Vlieland) is a seal reserve.

origins.name: Eiger
origins.en: Mountain peak in Switzerland, 3970 meters high.

origins.name: Eijkmanstraat
origins.en: Christiaan Eijkman (1858-1930), physician and bacteriologist, professor at the University of Utrecht. Discovered the cause of beriberi. In 1929 he received the Nobel Prize in Medicine.

origins.name: Eikenplein
origins.en: Named after the oak, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Eikenweg
origins.en: Named after the oak, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Einthovenstraat
origins.en: Willem Einthoven (1860-1927), Leiden professor of physiology, heart specialist. Inventor of the string galvanometer. Received the Nobel Prize in 1924.

origins.name: Eisdenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Eisingastraat
origins.en: Eise Eisinga (1744-1828), Frisian amateur astronomer. Built a planetarium, which still exists today in Franeker.

origins.name: Ekangala
origins.en: Village in South Africa, located in the Kwandebele area (formerly Transvaal) in the province of Mpumalanga.

origins.name: EKapa
origins.en: South African designation for Cape Town (dialect).

origins.name: Ekingenstraat
origins.en: In 1532, the church village on North Beveland (Zeeland) drowned.

origins.name: Eksteenfontein
origins.en: South African geographical name.

origins.name: Eksterstraat
origins.en: the bird

origins.name: Elandsgracht
origins.en: In this district there used to be many tanneries, where the hides of elk, deer, bears, etc. were processed.

origins.name: Elandsstraat
origins.en: In this district there used to be many tanneries, where the hides of elk, deer, bears, etc. were processed.

origins.name: Elbaweg
origins.en: Italian island in the Mediterranean Sea. In 1814 Napoleon was exiled to Elba.

origins.name: Elberveld
origins.en: South African geographical name.

origins.name: Elckerlijcstraat
origins.en: Morality from the fifteenth century, attributed to Petrus van Diest. The full title is: 'The mirror of the Salicheyt of Elckerlijc'.

origins.name: Eldorado
origins.en: Spanish for 'the gilded', from a myth about an initiation ritual among the Colombian Muisca Indians, in which a new tribal leader was covered completely with gold dust and swam in a mythical lake. The legend slowly changed from a person to a gold country, which has been sought after for centuries by conquistadors, French, English and Dutch.

origins.name: Elegaststraat
origins.en: Character from the Middle Dutch knightly romance 'Carel and the Elegant'.

origins.name: Elektronstraat
origins.en: The smallest amount of negative electricity, one of the building blocks of the atom.

origins.name: Elementenstraat
origins.en: The unit in a galvanic battery.

origins.name: Elfendansstraat
origins.en: The name refers to the poem 'Elvendans' by Jacqueline E. van der Waals (1868-1922), which is included in the collection 'New Verses' (1909).

origins.name: Elim
origins.en: to Park Frankendael

origins.name: Elisabeth Adriaansestraat
origins.en: Elisabeth (Betsy) Adriaanse (Roermond, 1906- Chur, 1939) pioneered as a lawyer and advocate for women's suffrage.

origins.name: Elisabeth Boddaertstraat
origins.en: Mrs. Elisabeth Boddaert (1867-1948), founded homes for neglected youth in our country.

origins.name: Elisabeth Samsonstraat
origins.en: Surinamese businesswoman (1715-1771), belonged to the class of reasonably well-off free mulattoes (half-blood). Unlike many whites in the colony, she could read and write. She lived on an equal basis with the white Carl Otto Creutz. In the slave society, she managed to occupy an important position despite racist opposition.

origins.name: Elisabeth van Dorpstraat
origins.en: Elisabeth (Lizzy) van Dorp (Arnhem, September 5, 1872-Banyubiru, September 6, 1945) was a pioneer as a lawyer, economist, politician and advocate for women's suffrage.

origins.name: Elisabeth Wolffstraat
origins.en: Elisabeth Wolff born Bekker (Betje Wolff) (1738-1804), writer. Wrote together with Aagje Deken among others 'Sara Burgerhart' and 'Willem Leevend'.

origins.name: Eliza van Calcarstraat
origins.en: Eliza Carolina Ferdinanda van Calcar-Schiotling (1822-1904), educator and writer. Argued in 'The double calling of the woman' for education for women.

origins.name: Elizabeth Anscombestraat
origins.en: Elizabeth Anscombe (1919 – 2001) was a British analytical philosopher.

origins.name: Elizabeth Cady Stantonplein
origins.en: American activist (1815-1902), advocate for women's suffrage in the United States. Also expanded her activism to Europe, and was at the forefront of the International Women's Council in 1888.

origins.name: Ella Fitzgeraldstraat
origins.en: Ella Jane Fitzgerald (1917-1996). Considered one of the most important American jazz singers in history. Typical of her were, among others, her range of four octaves, her clear pronunciation and her talent for scat singing.

origins.name: Ellert Vlieropstraat
origins.en: Captain of the Geuzen fleet, fought during the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Elpermeer
origins.en: Nature reserve in the Grollo forest ranger station (Drenthe).

origins.name: Elpermeerpad
origins.en: Nature reserve in the Grollo forest ranger station (Drenthe).

origins.name: Elsrijkdreef
origins.en: A former farm in Amstelveen.

origins.name: Elstarstraat
origins.en: Dutch apple variety, yellow-green with red blush. Originates from a cross between Golden Delicious and Ingrid Marie.

origins.name: Elzenhagensingel
origins.en: Name of a demolished farm on the Buikslotermeerdijk (demolished in 1964).

origins.name: Elzenstraat
origins.en: Named after the alder, a tree.

origins.name: Emanuel van Meterenstraat
origins.en: South Dutch merchant and historian (1535-1612), wrote among other things 'Historie der Nederlandse oorlogen'.

origins.name: Emanzana
origins.en: Nature reserve in South Africa, east of Johannesburg. Known for its sulfur spring, which was named Emanzana by the first inhabitants in the area. The Zulu name Emanzana means 'healing water'.

origins.name: Emfuleni
origins.en: Municipality in South Africa, located in the province of Gauteng. The Zulu name means 'place where there are many rivers'. The municipality got this name because of its location next to the Vaal River.

origins.name: Emilie Knappertstraat
origins.en: Founder of social work in the Netherlands (1860-1952).

origins.name: Emmalaan
origins.en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934). Second wife of King William III, regent queen from 1890 to 1898, mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

origins.name: Emmaplein
origins.en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934). Second wife of King William III, regent queen from 1890 to 1898, mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

origins.name: Emmastraat
origins.en: Adelheid Emma Wilhelmina Theresia of Waldeck-Pyrmont (1858-1934). Second wife of King William III, regent queen from 1890 to 1898, mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

origins.name: Emmeline Pankhurststraat
origins.en: English advocate for women's suffrage (1858-1928), among other things head of the English Association for Women's Suffrage. In London she gave public lectures and organized protest marches. She was arrested several times for her militant attitude. In 1928, the year when women in Great Britain gained the right to vote, Pankhurst died.

origins.name: Emmikhovenstraat
origins.en: During the St. Elizabeth flood, land in the Land of Altena (North Brabant) was drowned.

origins.name: Emmy Andriessestraat
origins.en: Photographer (1914-1953), joined a group of photographers during World War II who later became known as 'De Ondergedoken Camera', and made a photo report of the hunger winter in Amsterdam. After the war, she mainly devoted herself to portrait photography.

origins.name: Empangeni
origins.en: City in South Africa, located in the province of KwaZulu-Natal.

origins.name: Endumeni
origins.en: City in South Africa, the former Dundee, located in the province of KwaZulu-Natal. The Zulu name means 'place of thunderstorm', lightning often strikes the Endumeni hill.

origins.name: Engcobo
origins.en: City in South Africa, located in the Eastern Cape province.

origins.name: Enge Kerksteeg
origins.en: To the Old Church, where the steps lead up from Warmoesstraat, which was originally called Kerkstraat for part of it.

origins.name: Enge Lombardsteeg
origins.en: To the nearby Lommerd or Bank van Lening, founded in the year 1614.

origins.name: Engelsesteeg
origins.en: The alley was already called that in the sixteenth century. There used to be many inns here, which shows that it was a sought-after neighborhood, perhaps especially for English sailors.

origins.name: Enkeldoorn
origins.en: South African geographical name.

origins.name: Enkhuizerplein
origins.en: The North Holland town of Enkhuizen.

origins.name: Enkhuizerstraat
origins.en: The North Holland town of Enkhuizen.

origins.name: Ennemaborg
origins.en: A Groninger manor house from the late Middle Ages near Midwolde (Groningen), restored around 1700. In its current form a stately country house.

origins.name: Enny Vredestraat
origins.en: He was a member of the CDA city council in Amsterdam from 1978 to 1986. After that, he first became state secretary for Foreign Trade and later for Housing. From 1994 to 1997, he was the parliamentary leader of the CDA in the House of Representatives.

origins.name: Entabeni
origins.en: Wildlife reserve in South Africa, located in the Limpopo province. The name means 'the place of the mountain', after its location in the mountainous Waterberg region. The area is part of the World Heritage Site.

origins.name: Entrepotdok
origins.en: Named after the function. The dock was built in 1827, imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid. The warehouses have lost their function as a transhipment point, the upper floors of some have now been converted into houses (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Entrepothof
origins.en: Named after the function. The dock was built in 1827, imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid. The warehouses have lost their function as a transhipment point, the upper floors of some have now been converted into houses (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Entrepotkade
origins.en: Named after the function. The dock was built in 1827, imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid. The warehouses have lost their function as a transhipment point, the upper floors of some have now been converted into houses (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Eosstraat
origins.en: Figure from Greek mythology, also known as Aurore or Aurora. Goddess of sunrise and dawn.

origins.name: Epicurusstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher (341-270 BC). His philosophy was that only insight and moral life lead to happiness.

origins.name: Erasmusgracht
origins.en: Desiderius Erasmus (1467-1536), humanist. Made fierce attacks on the abuses in the Roman Catholic Church. His best-known work is 'Praise of Folly'.

origins.name: Ereprijsstraat
origins.en: Named after the speedwell, a plant.

origins.name: Erich Salomonstraat
origins.en: German-Jewish photojournalist (1886-1944), pioneer in the field of candid photography, where people are photographed unnoticed. Grandmaster of political documentary photography and society photography.

origins.name: Erik de Roodestraat
origins.en: Also known as Eric the Red. Norwegian seafarer, who settled in Iceland in 960 and from there discovered Greenland in 985.

origins.name: Ernest Staesplein
origins.en: Title of a collection of prose from 1874 by the Flemish writer Anton Bergman (1835-1874).

origins.name: Ernest Staesstraat
origins.en: Title of a collection of prose from 1874 by the Flemish writer Anton Bergman (1835-1874).

origins.name: Ernst Cahn en Alfred Kohnbrug
origins.en: Ernst Cahn was the man with whom Alfred Kohn (died in 1941) ran the ice cream parlors Koco, the home of Jewish fighting groups during World War II.

origins.name: Ernst Cahnsingel
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1889-1941), owner of ice cream parlor 'Koco' in Van Woustraat, from which resistance against anti-Jewish riots was organized in 1941.

origins.name: Ertskade
origins.en: The ore boats used to be unloaded at the quay.

origins.name: Escudolaan
origins.en: The escudo is the currency of Portugal.

origins.name: Eshowe
origins.en: Eshowe is a place in South Africa, inspired by the sound of the wind blowing through the indigenous Dlinza forest.

origins.name: Esmoreitstraat
origins.en: Fourteenth-century Flemish abel game.

origins.name: Esplanade de Meer
origins.en: Former Ajax stadium De Meer.

origins.name: Esther de Boer-van Rijkstraat
origins.en: Actress (1854-1937). Played the role of Kniertje more than a thousand times in Herman Heijermans' 'On Hope of Blessing'.

origins.name: Ethekwini
origins.en: Port city in South Africa, the former Durban, located in the province of KwaZulu-Natal. The Zulu name means 'place where the ocean and the earth meet'.

origins.name: Etnastraat
origins.en: Volcano on the Italian island of Sicily. Highest and most active volcano in Europe.

origins.name: Eudorinastraat
origins.en: Microscopically small aquatic animal ciliate. Able to assimilate carbon dioxide due to presence of chlorophyll.

origins.name: Eurokade
origins.en: Name of the future European currency.

origins.name: Europaboulevard
origins.en: Named after the continent. The naming is in response to the resolution of the Advisory Assembly of the Council of Europe dated 29-12-1957, in which it is called on every municipality in Europe to give a square or street the name Europe, in order to help promote the idea of European unity. With this naming, the name Westerscheldeplein (council decision, 1935) and the name Scheldestraat for part of that street (council decision, 1927) abolished.

origins.name: Europaplein
origins.en: Named after the continent. The naming is in response to the resolution of the Advisory Assembly of the Council of Europe dated 29-12-1957, in which it is called on every municipality in Europe to give a square or street the name Europe, in order to help promote the idea of European unity. With this naming, the name Westerscheldeplein (council decision, 1935) and the name Scheldestraat for part of that street (council decision, 1927) abolished.

origins.name: Eva Besnyöstraat
origins.en: Hungarian-Dutch photographer (1910-2003), born in Budapest, came to the Netherlands in the early 1930s. Known for her socially engaged reports, architecture photography and portraits.

origins.name: Eva Schalkbrug
origins.en: Eva Schalk (1890-1978) was the first woman on a water board. She was the head country of the polder Buik Slotermeer for 27 years and the head country of the High Authority for Waters for 21 years.

origins.name: Everard van Reijdhof
origins.en: Historian (1550-1602), councilor of the Frisian stadholder William Louis. Writer, among other things, of 'Historie der Nederlandse oorlogen', an important source for knowledge of the Dutch Revolt.

origins.name: Eversdal
origins.en: South African geographical name.

origins.name: Evert Cornelisstraat
origins.en: Conductor and pianist (1884-1931). From 1910 to 1919 second conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra, then conductor of the Utrecht City Orchestra.

origins.name: Evert van der Wallbrug
origins.en: Evert van der Wall (1944-2003) was from 1979 to 1983 a member of parliament for the PVDA as a councillor for Education and Youth Affairs in Amsterdam. In 2002 he became chairman of the Oost-Watergraafsmeer district. He worked for the development of Oostpoort with a central district hall and a large school, and that is why this bridge is named after him.

origins.name: Evertsweertplantsoen
origins.en: In 1530, a village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland (Zeeland) drowned.

origins.name: Evertsweertstraat
origins.en: In 1530, a village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland (Zeeland) drowned.

origins.name: Ewoud Worststraat
origins.en: Guzen Admiral (died 1574), participated in the uprising in Vlissingen in 1572 and the siege of Middelburg in 1573.

origins.name: Ezelsbrug
origins.en: The name of this bridge recalls the difficult struggle that the residents had to fight against the car lobby, which preferred to see bridges for normal traffic realized here. They often felt like donkeys who had to bump into the same stone over and over again. The name is also a reference to the tool, which is called the donkey bridge. The bridge was officially opened on March 14, 1987 by letting a donkey walk over it.

origins.name: F.C. Dondersstraat
origins.en: Franciscus Cornelis Donders (1818-1889), world-famous ophthalmologist.

origins.name: Faas Wilkesstraat
origins.en: Servaas Wilkes (1923-2006), footballer. Was Johan Cruijff's great example with his elegant play. Played as the first Dutchman for a foreign top club. Until 1998 record holder for Oranje with 35 goals from 38 international matches.

origins.name: Fagelstraat
origins.en: Caspar Fagel (1629-1688), in 1672 he succeeds Johan de Witt as council pensionary of Holland.

origins.name: Fahrenheitsingel
origins.en: Gabriel Daniel Fahrenheit (1686-1736), German by birth, who settled in the Netherlands as a physicist. In 1715 he set the freezing point of the thermometer at 32 degrees and the boiling point at 212 degrees. The Fahrenheitstraat was originally called De Wetstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1901).

origins.name: Fahrenheitstraat
origins.en: Gabriel Daniel Fahrenheit (1686-1736), German by birth, who settled in the Netherlands as a physicist. In 1715 he set the freezing point of the thermometer at 32 degrees and the boiling point at 212 degrees. The Fahrenheitstraat was originally called De Wetstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1901).

origins.name: Falckstraat
origins.en: Anton Reinhard Falck (1777-1843), statesman and lawyer. One of the leaders of the 1813 revolution. Minister of Education, Industry and Colonies under King William I. Founder of the Reading Museum. The street was laid out on a subdued section of the Achtergracht.

origins.name: Fannius Scholtenstraat
origins.en: Cornelis A. Fannius Scholten (1767-1832), lawyer in The Hague. During the 1813 revolution together with Melchior Kemper commissioner of the General Administration in Amsterdam. Subsequently state councillor in extraordinary service.

origins.name: Fanny Blankers-Koenlaan
origins.en: Francina Elsje Blankers-Koen (1918 -2004), athlete. Won four gold medals in 1948 during the Olympic Games in London. In 1999, the International Athletics Federation (IAAF) named her 'Athlete of the Century'.

origins.name: Fanny Durackstraat
origins.en: Australian swimmer, won gold in the 100-meter freestyle at the 1912 Olympic Games in Stockholm. First woman to win Olympic swimming gold.

origins.name: Fanny Mendelssohnstraat
origins.en: Fanny Mendelssohn was a German composer and pianist

origins.name: Faradaystraat
origins.en: Michael Faraday (1791-1867), English natural and chemist. Founder of the electromagnetic light theory.

origins.name: Fazantenweg
origins.en: Named after the pheasant, a fowl.

origins.name: Februariplein
origins.en: To the February strike on February 25 and 26, 1941. Protest strike against the first raids in the Jewish quarter.

origins.name: Feike de Boerlaan
origins.en: Feike de Boer (1892-1976), director of the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland' from 1934 to 1946. Numerous subsidiary positions, including commissioner of the N.V. Ned. Ind. Steenkolen Handel Maatschappij and of the N.V. Nederlandse Dok Maatschappij. From 1945 to 1946, exactly three hundred days, mayor of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Ferdinand Bolstraat
origins.en: Painter (1616-1680), pupil of Rembrandt, painted portraits and regency portraits among other things. (By council decision in 1921, the boundary with Gerard Doustraat was more precisely determined.)

origins.name: Ferdinand Huyckstraat
origins.en: Historical novel by Jacob van Lennep, dealing with life in Amsterdam in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Ferguutstraat
origins.en: Celtic knight novel from the thirteenth century.

origins.name: Ferrarisstraat
origins.en: Giorgi Ferraris (1847-1897), Italian mathematician and physicist, discoverer of the principle of alternating current.

origins.name: Ferry Ploegerstraat
origins.en: Ferdinand Ploeger (1915-1944), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Bloemendaal.

origins.name: Fibigerstraat
origins.en: Johannes Andrea Grib Fibiger (1867-1928), Danish physician. Well-known scholar in the field of cancer research. Received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1926.

origins.name: Fijnje van Salverdastraat
origins.en: Johannes Gerardus Wijbo Fijnje van Salverda (1796-1889), waterworks and railway engineer and inventor. As chief engineer of Waterstaat, he was responsible for the implementation of the improvement of the Nieuwe Waterweg.

origins.name: Filips van Almondestraat
origins.en: Sea hero (1646-1711), admiral during the nine-year war against France from 1688 to 1697.

origins.name: Finsenstraat
origins.en: Niels Finsen (1860-1904), Danish physician. Inventor of the Finnes lamp for electrical radiation, named after him. Received the Nobel Prize in 1903. The street was part of Bunsenstraat from 26-7-1939 until this naming.

origins.name: Firststraat
origins.en: Ruth First (1925-1982), journalist. Daughter of Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe who came to South Africa. Wrote about the deplorable consequences of Apartheid. After several arrests, she fled to England where she continued to work for the anti-apartheid movement. In 1982, she was murdered by the South African secret service.

origins.name: Fizeaustraat
origins.en: Armand Hyppolyte Fizeau (1819-1896), French physicist. Inventor of a method for measuring the speed of light.

origins.name: Flamingostraat
origins.en: Bird. Found in subtropical areas, also sporadically appears in temperate air masses.

origins.name: Flammarionstraat
origins.en: Camillo Flammarion (1842-1925), French astronomer, writer of many popular works on astronomy and geology.

origins.name: Fleerde
origins.en: Name of a participating house in Bergharen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Flevopark
origins.en: Named after the Flevian Lake, from which the North Sea originated.

origins.name: Flevoparkweg
origins.en: Named after the Flevian Lake, from which the North Sea (now IJsselmeer) originated.

origins.name: Flierbosdreef
origins.en: Name of some farms, including in Wouw (North Brabant) and Stedium (Groningen).

origins.name: Florapad
origins.en: The collective name of the plant world. Originally the Roman goddess of spring and flowers.

origins.name: Floraparkweg
origins.en: The collective name of the plant world. Originally the Roman goddess of spring and flowers.

origins.name: Floraweg
origins.en: The collective name of the plant world. Originally the Roman goddess of spring and flowers.

origins.name: Florence Nightingalestraat
origins.en: British nurse (1820-1910), nicknamed the lady with the lamp, known for the Crimean War of 1854. She became the pioneer of modern nursing and was the precursor of the Red Cross.

origins.name: Florijn
origins.en: Name of farms in Groenlo (Gelderland) and Wassenaar (South Holland). In Eibergen (Gelderland) it is the name of a hamlet.

origins.name: Floris van der Laakenstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1945), born in Amsterdam, executed at Hattem. He was commander of the radio service of the Council of Resistance.

origins.name: Floris Versterstraat
origins.en: Painter (1861-1927), student of Breitner, initially an impressionist. Painted still lifes, portraits and landscapes.

origins.name: Fluessenlaan
origins.en: More, located in southern Friesland.

origins.name: Fluitschipstraat
origins.en: Seventeenth-century cargo ship, a three-masted ship with a curved hull.

origins.name: Foekje Dillemastraat
origins.en: Athlete (1926-2007). Rival of Fanny Blankers-Koen in the 200 meters. Was suspended for life after a mandatory sex test in 1950, because she was not fully female. The standards were later changed and after her death, her honor was restored.

origins.name: Foeliedwarsstraat
origins.en: One of the - at the time important - products that were imported from East India and stored here in the warehouses of the Dutch East India Company.

origins.name: Foeliestraat
origins.en: One of the - at the time important - products that were imported from East India and stored here in the warehouses of the Dutch East India Company.

origins.name: Foersterhof
origins.en: Friedrich Wilhelm Foerster (1869-1959), founder of the modern vocational school.

origins.name: Fogostraat
origins.en: Volcano in Cape Verde. The volcano is still active.

origins.name: Fokke Simonszstraat
origins.en: Arent Fokke Simonsz (1755-1812), Amsterdam bookseller, poet and prose writer, who lived on the Looierssloot. Fokke was in charge of the care of the archives and antiquities for a while, of which he left descriptions. The street was laid out on the Nieuwe Looierssloot, which was filled in in 1873.

origins.name: Fokkemast
origins.en: One of the masts (the front) of a ship.

origins.name: Fokkezeil
origins.en: One of the sails of a ship.

origins.name: Fonteinkruidstraat
origins.en: The name comes from the fountain herb genus in the family of the same name, the leaves lie on the water surface or float underwater, the flowers are located in green spikes

origins.name: Foppingadreef
origins.en: A state of farmstead near Dronrijp (Friesland).

origins.name: Forintplantsoen
origins.en: The currency of Hungary.

origins.name: Formosastraat
origins.en: The island of Formosa or Taiwan off the coast of China, occupied by Japan until 1945, then Chinese. Taiwan is now in fact an independent state, although China considers the island a Chinese province. The name is Portuguese by the way: 'ilha formosa' means 'the beautiful island'.

origins.name: Fortuinstraat
origins.en: Named after shipyard Het Fortuin, which was located on the island of Wittenburg in the second half of the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Fosfaatweg
origins.en: Named after the Phosphate Factory, where this road and quay lead to. Before 1949, the road was part of the Ringweg in the Amsterdammer Polder.

origins.name: Foucaultstraat
origins.en: Jean B.L. Foucault (1819-1868), French physicist. Showed the rotation of the earth using a pendulum hung in the Pantheon in Paris. Discoverer of the induction currents named after him.

origins.name: Fraijlemaborg
