origins.en: Name of a country estate in Slochteren. A castle is originally a stone fortification. The province of Groningen used to have many castles. The Fraeylemaborg is now used as a museum with style rooms.

origins.name: Frambozenstraat
origins.en: The fruit of the raspberry bush.

origins.name: Frances Harperstraat
origins.en: Frances Ellen Watkins Harper (1825-1911) was an African American poet and writer.

origins.name: Francisco Faleirostraat
origins.en: Banned Portuguese scholar, entered Spanish government service. Worked in the scientific field on navigation and navigation problems. Provided support to Ferdinand Magellan in finding the route to South America.

origins.name: Franciscus Claessenstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1894-1945), born in Helden, killed in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

origins.name: Frank Martinus Arionstraat
origins.en: Frank Martinus Arion, pen name of Frank Efraim Martinus (Curaçao, 1936 - Curaçao, 2015), was a writer, poet and linguist. He worked in the Netherlands, Suriname and the Dutch Antilles and wrote in Dutch and Papiaments. In 1955 Martinus Arion left for the Netherlands to study Dutch language and literature at the University of Leiden. He came into contact with Cola Debrot. Together with him, he published his first poetry collection in 1957. After that, he founded an Antillean magazine, Encuentro Antilliano, with others. His debut novel Double Play (1973) was his greatest success. In 1975, he taught at the Institute for Teacher Training in Paramaribo.

origins.name: Frank van der Goesstraat
origins.en: Publicist and writer (1859-1939), well-known socialist theoretician. Co-founder of 'De Nieuwe Gids'. Founder of the SDAP in 1894, foreign correspondent of 'Het Volk'.

origins.name: Frankemaheerdpad
origins.en: Named after a farm in Warffum (Groningen).

origins.name: Frankenstraat
origins.en: The franc is the currency of France, Belgium, Luxembourg and Switzerland.

origins.name: Frans Bastiaansestraat
origins.en: W.A.F. Bastiaanse (1868-1947), poet and writer. He wrote the History of Dutch Literature (1927).

origins.name: Frans de Wollantstraat
origins.en: Eighteenth-century Dutch genius officer, made a name for himself in Russia under Catherine the Great as a designer of hydraulic works and the construction of the city of Odessa.

origins.name: Frans Duwaerstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1911-1944), born in Amsterdam, also executed there.

origins.name: Frans Halsstraat
origins.en: Painter (1580-1666). Painted portraits and civic guard portraits.

origins.name: Frans Naerebouthof
origins.en: Vlissinger dockyard, known as a sea rescuer (1748-1818). He gained particular fame with the shipwreck of the Woestduin in 1779.

origins.name: Frans van Mierisstraat
origins.en: Frans van Mieris de Oude (1635-1681), painter. Painted genre and historical works. His father and his son were also known painters.

origins.name: Franz Kafkastraat
origins.en: Franz Kafka (1883-1924) was a German writer who is considered one of the most important authors of the 20th century.

origins.name: Franz Zieglerstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1893-1939), photographed members of the royal family and the Hague society. From 1929 official court photographer.

origins.name: Fraunhoferstraat
origins.en: Joseph Fraunhofer (1787-1826), German physicist. Improved many optical instruments. Discovered the lines in the solar spectrum (the lines of Fraunhofer).

origins.name: Fred Petterbaan
origins.en: Frederik Hermanus Petter was a trade unionist and one of the leaders of the 1903 Railway Strike.

origins.name: Fred. Roeskestraat
origins.en: Frederik J. Roeske (1868-1961), from 1891 to 1953 conductor of the Royal Men's Singing Association Apollo. In addition, composer of music for a large number of songs. The street was part of Prinses Irenestraat for this naming.

origins.name: Fred. Thomasstraat
origins.en: Fredericus F.X.M.D. Thomas (1906-1959), journalist. Editor of the daily newspaper 'De Tijd' and writer of 'Amsterdam, city of my heart'.

origins.name: Frederik Hendrikplantsoen
origins.en: Prince Frederick Henry (1584-1647), son of the fourth marriage of Prince William of Orange, half-brother of Prince Maurice, stadtholder from 1625. His successful performance as army commander earned him the name 'town builder'. The Frederik Hendrikplantsoen was first called Frederik Hendrikplein for a few years (council decision, 1886).

origins.name: Frederik Hendrikstraat
origins.en: Prince Frederik Hendrik (1584-1647), son of the fourth marriage of Prince William of Orange, half-brother of Prince Maurice, stadtholder from 1625. His successful performance as army commander earned him the name 'town builder'. The Frederik Hendrikplein was first called Frederik Hendrikplein for a few years (council decision, 1886).

origins.name: Frederik van Dorpstraat
origins.en: Member of the Union of the Nobles, of East Frisian origin (1547-1612). Fought at Heiligerlee and participated in the conquest of Den Briel and the liberation of Leiden.

origins.name: Frederik van Eedenstraat
origins.en: Writer and psychiatrist (1860-1932). Co-founder of the literary magazine 'De Nieuwe Gids'. From 1894 went his own way and founded a cooperative commune in Bussum. Wrote among other things 'Van de koele meren des doods'.

origins.name: Frederiksplein
origins.en: Prince Frederick William Karel (1798-1881), second son of King William I. Thanks in part to his support, the construction of the Palace of Public Industry was promoted (opened 1864, burned down 1929).

origins.name: Frederiksstraat
origins.en: Frederik Schröder granted a construction loan around 1880 for the construction along this street to be built, which is why the street was named after him. The street was taken over by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under this name.

origins.name: Freek Oxstraat
origins.en: Frederik Johannes Marius Ox (1920-1944), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died in a firefight with Germans in Euterpestraat (now Gerrit van der Veenstraat) on June 15, 1944.

origins.name: Fregatstraat
origins.en: Fast sailing three-masted ship.

origins.name: Fregelaan
origins.en: Gottlob Frege (1848-1925), German mathematician and philosopher, professor in Jena. First gave a consistently developed derivation of mathematics to logic. Designer of the Begriffsschrift, a symbolic writing system for logic.

origins.name: Fresiastraat
origins.en: Named after the freesia, a plant.

origins.name: Freule Wttewaalpad
origins.en: Freule Christine Wilhelmine Isabelle Wttewaal van Stoetwegen (1901-1986), politician. From 1945 to 1971 member of the House of Representatives for the Christian-Historical Union. She was part of the parliamentary inquiry committee (1949-1956), which investigated the policy of the Dutch government in London during World War II.

origins.name: Frida Katzstraat
origins.en: Frida Mackay-Katz (Amsterdam, July 29, 1885 - Aerdenhout, March 30, 1963) was a pioneer as a lawyer, municipal, national and local politician and advocate for women's suffrage.

origins.name: Frieslandstraat
origins.en: The province. In the vicinity, a number of streets are named after Frisian castles.

origins.name: Frissenstein
origins.en: Name of a mansion in Deil (Gelderland).

origins.name: Frissensteinpad
origins.en: Name of a mansion in Deil (Gelderland).

origins.name: Frits Rotganshof
origins.en: Photographer (1912-1978). Master of the panoramic photo. During World War II, he illegally photographed the German occupation. After the war, he photographed the activities in the ports of Rotterdam and Amsterdam. In the 1960s, Rotgans was involved in aviation photography and photo montages.

origins.name: Fritz Conijnstraat
origins.en: Fritz Gerhard Marie Conijn (1923-1944), resistance fighter and student, born in Alkmaar, executed by firing squad in Vught.

origins.name: Fritz Dietrich Kahlenbergstraat
origins.en: Filmer (1916-1995). During World War II, he also took many photographs. In 1944, he brought together the Amsterdam photography group, with the aim of capturing the last year of the occupation. Later, the group became known as 'The Hidden Camera'.

origins.name: Fröbelstraat
origins.en: Friedrich Wilhelm August Fröbel (1782-1852), German pedagogue. Founder of the first kindergarten in 1827.

origins.name: Funenkade
origins.en: The strip of land, on which among other things the Czaar Peterstraat was built, came within the city at the expansion of 1658 and was then called Funen. This was thought of as the Danish island of Funen, where Admiral De Ruyter achieved victory in a naval battle against the Swedes in 1659.

origins.name: Funenpark
origins.en: The strip of land, on which among other things the Czaar Peterstraat was built, came within the city at the expansion of 1658 and was then called Funen. This was thought of as the Danish island of Funen, where Admiral De Ruyter achieved victory in a naval battle against the Swedes in 1659.

origins.name: Funke Küpperstraat
origins.en: Albert Funke Küpper (1894-1934), illustrator and caricaturist. Associated with the political satirical weekly magazine 'De Notekraker'.

origins.name: G.J. Scheurleerpad
origins.en: Gerardus Jacobus Scheurleer (1886-1948), tennis player. Many times champion of the Netherlands in doubles together with Diemer Kool, among others.

origins.name: G.J. Scheurleerweg
origins.en: Gerardus Jacobus Scheurleer (1886-1948), tennis player. Many times champion of the Netherlands in doubles together with Diemer Kool, among others.

origins.name: G.J.M. Sarlemijnstraat
origins.en: Gerardus Josephus Maria Sarlemijn (1909-1993), Amsterdam architect. With Adriaan Evers he designed in a conservative Bossche style. Received the Golden Pin of the municipality of Amsterdam for the inventorying of monuments in the city.

origins.name: G.T. Ketjenweg
origins.en: Gerard Tileman Chain, trader in dry cleaners and paint stores, and original founder of AKZO Nobel. In 1935 he founded the sulfuric acid factory Chain on the current Marnixstraat. From 1916 production was centralized in Amsterdam-Noord. In 1969 the factory of Chain merged with the company AKU to form AKZO.

origins.name: Gaandeweg
origins.en: The name falls under the theme 'Social and satisfied living' for the G-neighbourhood Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

origins.name: Gaasperdammerpad
origins.en: The name comes from the Gaasp river

origins.name: Gaasperdammerweg
origins.en: To the neighborhood of the same name on the Gaasp river.

origins.name: Gaasperparkpad
origins.en: The name comes from the Gaasp river

origins.name: Gaasperplaspad
origins.en: The name comes from the Gaasp stream. The Gaasperplas itself is an artificial lake up to 35 meters deep, created by sand mining for the construction of the Bijlmermeer.

origins.name: Gaasperzoompad
origins.en: The name comes from the Gaasp river

origins.name: Gaaspstraat
origins.en: The Gaasp stream, the unexcavated part of the Weespertrekvaart.

origins.name: Gaasterlandpad
origins.en: Southern part of Friesland, between Stavoren and Lemmer. This is where the only places where the Frisian coast does not need to be secured by dike construction are located.

origins.name: Gaasterlandstraat
origins.en: Southern part of Friesland, between Stavoren and Lemmer. This is where the only places where the Frisian coast does not need to be secured by dike construction are located.

origins.name: Gabriël Metsustraat
origins.en: Painter (1629-1667), mainly of genre pieces. He was a pupil of Gerard Dou. As early as 6-10-1880, a street was named Metsu, but that name was changed to Paulus Potterstraat in 1893.

origins.name: Gabriela Mistralstraat
origins.en: Gabriela Mistral (1889-1957) was a Chilean poet. She was the first Latin American person to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

origins.name: Gaffelaarspad
origins.en: Ship with flat bottom and round bow, is mainly used for inland navigation.

origins.name: Gaffelstraat
origins.en: Agricultural machinery, with which the hay is stacked.

origins.name: Galantstraat
origins.en: The name falls under the theme 'Social and satisfied living' for the G-neighbourhood Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

origins.name: Galastraat
origins.en: Sweet, juicy apple from New Zealand, developed as a variety in the first half of the twentieth century.

origins.name: Galgenbrug
origins.en: The name refers to the view from this bridge of the gallows of the Volewijk, which stood here until 1795

origins.name: Galgenstraat
origins.en: The view from this street of the gallows of the Volewijk is the origin of this name. In 1662, the municipal council decided to change the name to Prinsendwarsstraat, but that name never came into effect.

origins.name: Galggouw
origins.en: This province, located in the municipality of Broek in Waterland, gets its name from an old gallows field.

origins.name: Galileïplantsoen
origins.en: Galileo Galilei (1564-1642), Italian mathematician, professor in Pisa and Padua. Discoverer of the laws of fall and pendulum. Constructed the first telescope and discovered many celestial bodies.

origins.name: Galjoenstraat
origins.en: Heavy and log sailing ship from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, with three or four masts and high fore- and aft castle.

origins.name: Galjootstraat
origins.en: Ship. Flat-bottomed merchant ship with side swords for coastal shipping.

origins.name: Galvanistraat
origins.en: Luigi Galvani (1737-1798), Italian physicist. Discovered the electricity generated by chemical action.

origins.name: Galwin
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the Irish port city of Galway, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Gamerenstraat
origins.en: Gamerenstraat (formerly Van Gamerenstraat) is named after Virginie Gameren (Curaçao, March 19, 1833 - date and place of death unknown) Virginie was a woman who was enslaved who fought for her freedom by initiating a legal procedure against her owner. She won this procedure and thus forced her freedom from the Ministry of Colonies. She took the surname Gameren, which gave her and her children autonomy.

origins.name: Ganzebloemstraat
origins.en: The flower, belonging to the family of the composites.

origins.name: Ganzenhoefpad
origins.en: Name of a farm on the Vecht near Maarseveen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Ganzenveldstraat
origins.en: Het Ganzenveld is part of the Schoorlse dunes (North Holland).

origins.name: Ganzenweg
origins.en: Named after the goose, a water bird.

origins.name: Garcia Lorcastraat
origins.en: Federico Garcia Lorca (1898-1936) was a Spanish progressive poet and playwright.

origins.name: Gare du Nord
origins.en: Important train station in the north of Paris, opened in 1864.

origins.name: Garstkamp
origins.en: Name of a farm near Beesd (Gelderland).

origins.name: Gasthuismolensteeg
origins.en: On the city wall (the Singel), where the current alley is located, was the mill of the Sint Elisabethsgasthuis (fifteenth and sixteenth centuries). The Sint Elisabethsgasthuis was the oldest hospital in the city, founded in the fourteenth century. In 1492, the building was attached to the town hall. Both buildings were later demolished for the construction of the new town hall (now palace). Before 1913, this was the Wijde Gasthuismolensteeg. Even earlier, the names Molensteeg and Benninghstraat appear.

origins.name: Gatwickstraat
origins.en: Name of one of London's airports.

origins.name: Gebroeders A. en B. Wolfswinkelweg
origins.en: The brothers Antoon (1919-1942) and Bertus (1921-1942) Wolfswinkel, resistance fighters. They distributed illegal material, raised money for the resistance and were part of a sabotage group at the Fokker factory in Amsterdam-Noord, where they worked. They actively participated in the February Strike in 1941. On November 19, 1942, both were executed in Soesterberg.

origins.name: Gedempt Hamerkanaal
origins.en: Refers to the former Hamerkanaal

origins.name: Gedempte Begijnensloot
origins.en: The court, founded in the fourteenth century, was intended for the accommodation of beguines (lay sisters). The Begijnhof was originally, together with the St. Lucia's monastery, completely surrounded by water. Behind the houses of Kalverstraat was a ditch, the Beguin's ditch, which ran from the still undammed Spui to the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. This canal was neglected and therefore the rest was filled in in 1865. It was named Gedempte Begijnensloot, a name that was legalized by a council decision in 1914.

origins.name: Gedempte Insteekhaven
origins.en: The docking port referred to here has been part of the shipyard, the Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). Some floating dry docks were located in this port. The port has been leveled for residential construction on this site.

origins.name: Geduld
origins.en: The ability to be able to wait long when reaching a goal.

origins.name: Geelbekstraat
origins.en: The songbird, belonging to the finch family.

origins.name: Geelvinckssteeg
origins.en: At the corner of this alley stood two warehouses in the past, which bore the name De Geelvinck. The name first appears in the last years of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Geer Ban
origins.en: The Geer Ban or Free Geer was one of the four parts into which the municipality of Sloten existed in earlier centuries. See also Free Geer. A ban was an administrative area in ancient times. A number of bans together formed a bailiwick.

origins.name: Geerdinkhof
origins.en: Very old name of a property in Vasse near Tubbergen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Geerdinkhofpad
origins.en: Very old name of a property in Vasse near Tubbergen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Geerdinkhofweg
origins.en: Very old name of a property in Vasse near Tubbergen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Geert Grootestraat
origins.en: Philosopher (1340-1384), founder of the Brotherhood of the Common Life. Vigorously opposed abuses in the church, but also against heretics. He was the founder of the religious renewal known as Modern Devotion.

origins.name: Geertje Wielemaplein
origins.en: Swimmer (1934-2009). Won a silver medal in the 100-meter backstroke at the 1952 Olympic Games in Helsinki. Became the first Sportswoman of the Year in the Netherlands in 1954.

origins.name: Geertruida van Lierstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1915-1969), involved in many illegal activities and member of the Amsterdam resistance group CS-6.

origins.name: Geervliet
origins.en: Old town (city rights 1381) on the Brielse Maas and the now silted Bernisse (South Holland).

origins.name: Geldersekade
origins.en: In the second expansion of the city on the east side, the current Geldersekade was the city moat. The inner wall (on the side of the Zeedijk) is therefore the oldest. Built around 1500. The other side was outside the city until 1585. In the seventeenth century, that old side was partly called Cologne quay and further Gelderse kaai, also briefly London quay or English quay. The names originated because there were jetties here where ships docked that sailed to the Gelderland cities, to Cologne, London and other English harbors.

origins.name: Geldershoofd
origins.en: Name of a country house near Brummen (Gelderland). The buildings Geldershoofd and Gravestein together formed the building Gliphoeve before the renovation in 1983.

origins.name: Geleenstraat
origins.en: River in South Limburg, flows into the Maas at Stevensweerdt.

origins.name: Geleyn Bouwenszstraat
origins.en: Captain with the Watergeuzen during the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Gelrestraat
origins.en: The old name of Gelderland. Also a county (1046-1339) and then until 1795 a duchy, which roughly corresponded to the current Gelderland, plus a part of Limburg and Germany.

origins.name: Generaal Vetterstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Augustinus Vetter (1837-1907), military supreme commander of the expedition to Lombok (1894) and Aceh (1896).

origins.name: Generatorstraat
origins.en: The device for generating electricity.

origins.name: Genhoes
origins.en: Castle Genhoes or Oud-Valkenburg, near Valkenburg (Limburg), built around 1500. Late Gothic main building of limestone, renovated and expanded in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Restored in 1962 and in the following years.

origins.name: Gentiaanplein
origins.en: Named after the gentian, a plant.

origins.name: Gentiaanstraat
origins.en: Named after the gentian, a plant.

origins.name: George Balanchinestraat
origins.en: George Balanchine was an American choreographer of Georgian descent. He is considered one of the most important choreographers of the classical ballet of the twentieth century.

origins.name: George Gershwinlaan
origins.en: American composer and pianist (1898-1990). Incorporated jazz elements into classical music. Wrote the opera 'Porgy and Bess' and numerous musicals. Also composed piano works, orchestral works and concerts.

origins.name: George Gershwinplein
origins.en: American composer and pianist (1898-1990). Incorporated jazz elements into classical music. Wrote the opera 'Porgy and Bess' and numerous musicals. Also composed piano works, orchestral works and concerts.

origins.name: George Sandstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Aurore Dupin, baroness Dudevant (1804-1876), French novelist. She advocated for the unrestrained development of the woman through her free way of life and in her work. She is considered the first truly emancipated woman of the New Age.

origins.name: George Sliekerkade
origins.en: George Christiaan Slieker (1861-1945), the first Dutch film exhibitor, traveled with his traveling cinema along fairs and annual markets.

origins.name: George Westinghousestraat
origins.en: American engineer (1846-1914), who invented the Westinghouse brake named after him: an air pressure brake, in particular in use on railways.

origins.name: Geraardsbergenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of East Flanders.

origins.name: Geraniumweg
origins.en: The garden and houseplant.

origins.name: Gerard Borstkade
origins.en: Jacobus Gerardus Gerbrant Borst (1902-1975), internist, 35 years professor at the University of Amsterdam and head of the internal clinic in the Internal Hospital. During the war years, among other things, member of the leadership of the medical resistance. Founder of modern blood transfusion therapy.

origins.name: Gerard Brandtstraat
origins.en: Remonstrant theologian (1626-1685). Initially wrote church history, later poetry. Until 1896 the street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel and was called H.G. Kosterstraat, after a construction company (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1880).

origins.name: Gerard Callenburgstraat
origins.en: Admiral (1642-1722). Captain of the admiral's ship of Admiral De Ruyter. Participated in the naval battles at Solebay (1672), at Etna (1676) and in the conquest of Gibraltar (1704).

origins.name: Gerard Douplein
origins.en: Painter (1613-1675). Representative of the Leiden school. Student of Rembrandt and teacher of Metsu and Van Mieris, among others.

origins.name: Gerard Doustraat
origins.en: Painter (1613-1675). Representative of the Leiden school. Student of Rembrandt and teacher of Metsu and Van Mieris, among others.

origins.name: Gerard Hulst van Keulenstraat
origins.en: Gerard Hulst of Cologne (1733-1801) led the famous Van Keulen company from 1756, which was based in Amsterdam at the corner of Nieuwebrugsteeg and Prins Hendrikkade for two centuries (approx. 1680-1885). The company was specialized in making and selling sea maps and nautical instruments and acted as publisher and seller of books, especially in the nautical field.

origins.name: Gerard Revebrug
origins.en: Gerard Kornelis van het Reve (1923-2006), writer and poet. Formed the Great Three of postwar literature together with Harry Mulisch (1927-2010) and Willem Frederik Hermans (1921-1995). Wrote among other things 'The evenings' (1947), 'Werther Nieland' (1949) and 'Closer to You' (1966). Received the P.C. Hooft Prize (1968) and the Prize of the Dutch Letters (2001).

origins.name: Gerard Ruttenhof
origins.en: Film director (1902-1982), made two important Dutch feature films from the 1930s of the twentieth century with the films 'Dood water' (1934), about the construction of the Afsluitdijk, and 'Rubber' (1935), about a plantation woman in Suriname.

origins.name: Gerard Schaepstraat
origins.en: Council and aldermen of Amsterdam (1594-1666), ambassador at the English and Danish courts.

origins.name: Gerard Terborgstraat
origins.en: Painter (1617-1681), of portrait and genre pieces.

origins.name: Gerardus van der Groeplaan
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1922-1945), worked at the Fokker factory in Amsterdam-North and was part of a sabotage group within this company. Distributed 'The Truth' and raised money for the resistance. Sentenced to death in 1942, but this sentence was converted into a life sentence in prison. Freed by the French. Died on July 16, 1945.

origins.name: Gerda Brautigamstraat
origins.en: Gerarda Brautigam (1913-1982), politician and journalist. From 1945 to 1967 editor of Het Vrije Volk and from 1963 to 1972 member of the House of Representatives for the Labour Party. She was mainly concerned with consumer affairs, which made her very well known.

origins.name: Gerrie Knetemannlaan
origins.en: Cyclist (1951-2004), nickname 'de Kneet'. His greatest success came in 1978 with the world championship on the road.

origins.name: Gerrit Bronkepad
origins.en: Gerrit Bronke (19th century) designed the church in Holysloot (National Monument) in 1846. For this neighborhood, the category names of Dutch architects who have been involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-North have been chosen.

origins.name: Gerrit Mannourystraat
origins.en: Mathematician and philosopher (1867-1956), professor at the University of Amsterdam and one of the most important Dutch mathematicians of this century.

origins.name: Gerrit Stuyverstraat
origins.en: Watergeus, fought during the liberation of Haarlem in 1572.

origins.name: Gerrit van den Boschpad
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1911-1944). He had an important role in the spread of the illegal newspaper 'De Waarheid'. Killed in the Dachau concentration camp.

origins.name: Gerrit van der Puijstraat
origins.en: A resident of Sloten (1915-1988), he has been committed to the Slotense community for many years.

origins.name: Gerrit van der Veenstraat
origins.en: Gerrit Jan van der Veen (1902-1944), resistance fighter, by profession sculptor. For his sculptural work he won the Prix de Rome. He actively participated in the resistance. Van der Veen was one of the initiators of the robbery of the Population Register (March 27, 1943) and was executed in the dunes near Overveen. The street was previously called Euterpestraat, after the muse of music and poetry, and was very notorious during the occupation years 1940-1945 due to the establishment of the German Security Service (S.D.) in the Meisjes-HBS.

origins.name: Gerrit van Erkelstraat
origins.en: Gerrit van Erkel (1860-1937) leader of the radical socialist trade union movement.

origins.name: Gerrit Versteegstraat
origins.en: Architect (1873-1938), built part of Tuindorp Watergraafsmeer, worked with Hendrik Berlage on the western part of the Transvaalbuurt and designed the building blocks on Koekoekstraat in the north.

origins.name: Geschutswerf
origins.en: Gun is the collective name for cannons and heavy machine guns. Located on the site where the Geschutswerf of the Admiralty of Amsterdam was located. In the eighteenth century, gunpowder was manufactured here.

origins.name: Geulstraat
origins.en: River in South Limburg, tributary of the Maas. The Geuldal forms part of the border with Belgium.

origins.name: Geurt Brinkgrevebrug
origins.en: Mumentenbeschermer, sculptor and publicist (1917-2005). Advocate for the preservation of the historic city center, which ultimately led to a turnaround in thinking about the old cultural heritage. Also played a major role in the preservation of the old street structure in the Nieuwmarkt neighborhood. Received the Silver Pen in 1982.

origins.name: Geuzenkade
origins.en: Initially intended as a slur, but considered a name of honor by the allied nobles in the struggle against Spain. Later the battle name for all opponents of Spain in the Eighty Years' War. The Short Geuzenstraat previously belonged to the Geuzenstraat.

origins.name: Geuzenstraat
origins.en: Initially intended as a slur, but considered a name of honor by the allied nobles in the struggle against Spain. Later the battle name for all opponents of Spain in the Eighty Years' War. The Short Geuzenstraat was previously part of the Geuzenstraat.

origins.name: Gevlebrug
origins.en: The Swedish port city of Gävle on the Gulf of Bothnia, an important export port for wood. Now one of the largest oil ports in Sweden.

origins.name: Gibraltarstraat
origins.en: The southernmost point of Spain, named here in connection with the naval battle against the Spaniards in 1607, in which Jacob van Heemskerck died.

origins.name: Giessenburg
origins.en: Lost castle in Giessen-Oudkerk of which only some remains have survived today.

origins.name: Gieterij
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the various workshops were used for the naming, in this case the foundry of the shipyard.

origins.name: Gietersstraat
origins.en: Named after 't Giethuis, the city's gunpowder and bell foundry, which stood here from 1614 to 1821. The street name first appeared in use in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Gijsbrecht van Aemstelstraat
origins.en: To Gijsbrecht IV (circa 1235-1303), the last lord of Aemstel who was Lord of Amsterdam, bailiff of Amstelland. Became famous through Vondel's tragedy.

origins.name: Gijsbrecht van IJselsteinstraat
origins.en: Governor of Amstelland and Waterland from 1358 to 1361.

origins.name: Gillis Steltmanstraat
origins.en: Watergeus, became known during the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Gillis van Ledenberchstraat
origins.en: Treasurer of the States of Utrecht (1550-1618), supporter of Van Oldenbarneveldt and imprisoned by Prince Maurice. The street previously bore the name Tweede Hugo de Grootdwarsstraat (council decision, 1897 and 1-9-1908).

origins.name: Glauberweg
origins.en: Johannes Rudolf Glauber (1604-1670), German chemist and physician. Discovered the laxative effect of the Glauber's Salt named after him, used against gallstones.

origins.name: Glitterstraat
origins.en: The name falls under the theme 'Social and satisfied living' for the G-neighbourhood Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

origins.name: Gloriantstraat
origins.en: An abel game from the fourteenth century.

origins.name: Goed Geluimd hof
origins.en: The name falls under the theme 'Social and satisfied living' for the G-neighbourhood Grunder/Grubbehoeve.

origins.name: Goeman Borgesiusstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Goeman Borgesius (1847-1917), liberal statesman, Minister of the Interior from 1897 to 1901 (Compulsory Education Act, Housing Act, Accident Act).

origins.name: Goereestraat
origins.en: Part of the South Holland island of Goeree-Overflakkee.

origins.name: Golfbaanpad
origins.en: Path at Golf Course De Hoge Dijk.

origins.name: Gooiluststraat
origins.en: Country estate in 's-Graveland, of which the Corversbos was originally also part. 's Graveland is a peninsula of a piece of Gooise heath. After the removal of the sand, Amsterdam regents in the seventeenth century built country houses and nurseries here.

origins.name: Gooioord
origins.en: Name of a townhouse in Bussum (North Holland).

origins.name: Gooise Kant
origins.en: Neighbourhood bypass road, exits and connects to the K-neighbourhood and the Gooiseweg.

origins.name: Gooiseweg
origins.en: The road leads in the direction of the Gooi.

origins.name: Gordijnensteeg
origins.en: Named after the sixteenth and seventeenth-century residents Willem and Samuel du Gardijn. The alley was also known as Bloeddwarsstraat at that time.

origins.name: Gorontalostraat
origins.en: Location on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes) in Indonesia.

origins.name: Gorsstraat
origins.en: In South Holland, the name used for land located offshore, covered with vegetation, that is only flooded during high tide (elsewhere called a sandbank or marsh).

origins.name: Gosschalklaan
origins.en: Isaac Gosschalk (1838-1907), architect. One of the most important Dutch architects of the nineteenth century. In 1885 Gosschalk was commissioned by the Imperial Continental Gaz-Association to design the buildings of the Westergasfabriek.

origins.name: Goudbalpad
origins.en: Old Dutch pear variety. The street is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Gouden Leeuw
origins.en: Name of a farm in the Haarlemmermeer (The name also appears in Hummelo and Leiden).

origins.name: Goudestein
origins.en: Castle under Maarsen on the Vecht, dating from 1754, built at the behest of the Amsterdam mayor Huydecoper.

origins.name: Goudreinetstraat
origins.en: The fruit, a type of apple.

origins.name: Goudriaanstraat
origins.en: Bernardus Hermanus Goudriaan (1796-1842), chief engineer of Rijkswaterstaat. Was appointed by the government to assess the first railway plans.

origins.name: Goudsbloemstraat
origins.en: The flower, belonging to the family of the composites.

origins.name: Gouwenaarssteeg
origins.en: Named after the broker Willem Jac. Gouwenaar, who lived around 1600 on the corner of the Stromarkt.

origins.name: Govert Flinckstraat
origins.en: Painter (1615-1660), pupil of Rembrandt. Especially known for his civic guard portraits and portraits.

origins.name: Gowin Knightstraat
origins.en: English physician (1713-1772), published in the eighteenth century on magnetic experiments related to the compass used by sailors.

origins.name: Graaf Florisstraat
origins.en: Floris V (1254-1296), count of Holland, murdered by the nobles. Graaf Floris is the donor of the oldest known privilege to Amsterdam, which in 1275 granted toll-free passage to 'den luden bij Amstelredam'. This is also the oldest dated document in which the name Amsterdam appears.

origins.name: Graafschapstraat
origins.en: A commonly used name for part of the Gelderse Achterhoek. Originally the old county of Zutphen. A part of the street was renamed Jacob Soetendorpstraat in 1978.

origins.name: Graanstraat
origins.en: Collective name of the agricultural products, insofar as they belong to the family of grasses.

origins.name: Graftdijkerstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland, located between the Beemster and the Schermer.

origins.name: Graham Bellstraat
origins.en: Alexander Graham BelI (1847-1922), Scottish physicist. Constructed the first useful telephone.

origins.name: Gran Paradiso
origins.en: Highest mountain in Italy, 4061 meters.

origins.name: Granaatstraat
origins.en: A semi-precious stone.

origins.name: Granidastraat
origins.en: Tragic play by P.C. Hooft (1602-1605).

origins.name: Grasrijk
origins.en: Former farm on the Uitweg, demolished for the construction of garden city Osdorp.

origins.name: Grasweg
origins.en: The most common and largest plant family.

origins.name: Gravenstraat
origins.en: The graves from the House of Hainaut (1299-1345). When they were in Amsterdam, they stayed in a inn located here at the time. The alley already appears in the early fifteenth century under the name of 's-Gravenstraat.

origins.name: Gravestein
origins.en: Named after a Surinamese plantation. The buildings Gravestein and Geldershoofd together formed the building called Gliphoeve before the renovation in 1983.

origins.name: Grensstraat
origins.en: Before 1896, the street formed the border between Amsterdam and Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Grevelingenstraat
origins.en: Sea current between the islands of Goeree and Schouwen. Now closed off from the open sea by the Grevelingendam.

origins.name: Grianestraat
origins.en: Tragicomedy by Brederode from the year 1612.

origins.name: Griendstraat
origins.en: Collective name for a vegetation of woody crops (mostly willows), which are regularly cut down. Griend or gravel soils are located in or along the water.

origins.name: Griftstraat
origins.en: Excavated drainage ditch on the Veluwe, flows into the IJssel near Hattem.

origins.name: Grimbergenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Grimburgwal
origins.en: To the water the Grim, which from 1342 to around 1400 formed the southern boundary of the city (grim = muddy ditch).

origins.name: Griseldestraat
origins.en: Sproke from 1393. A sproke is a medieval rhymed story, similar to a farmer's tale or farce.

origins.name: Groen van Prinstererstraat
origins.en: Guillaume Groen van Prinsterer (1801-1876), statesman and historian. Leader of the Antirevolutionaries from 1849 to 1866. Fierce opponent of liberals and Roman Catholics.

origins.name: Groenburgwal
origins.en: The land between Kloveniersburgwal and Zwanenburgwal, where the linen windows stood and which was annexed to the city in 1593, was then the place of the dyeing houses. This canal was therefore originally called Verwersgracht. At the beginning of the seventeenth century, the name Groenburgwal was created, because there were special green dyeing houses here.

origins.name: Groene Ridderhof
origins.en: To Jan Claesz. Groene Ridder, actually Backer (1588-?). Was the owner of the ship De Groene Ridder, but decided around 1631 to run a ship's inn near the Kadoelenbreek. Around 1538 he sold it again. Since then, there has always been a restaurant at this location, at Landsmeerderdijk 195.

origins.name: Groene Ridderpad
origins.en: To Jan Claesz. Groene Ridder, actually Backer (1588-?). Was the owner of the ship De Groene Ridder, but decided around 1631 to run a ship's inn near the Kadoelenbreek. Around 1538 he sold it again. Since then, there has always been a restaurant at this location, at Landsmeerderdijk 195.

origins.name: Groenehuyzen
origins.en: Former farm in the former municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Groenendaalstraat
origins.en: Country estate near Heemstede (North Holland).

origins.name: Groeneveen
origins.en: Old patrician house in Velsen from the sixteenth century (also called Papenburg).

origins.name: Groenhoedenveem
origins.en: A veem is a company responsible for storing and delivering goods in and out of its warehouses. The veems each had their own license plate, after which they were named. These could be different colors and models of hats (e.g. Green Hats, Cloche Hats). They also derived their name from the origin of the workers (e.g. Friese Veem, Zeeuwse Veem).

origins.name: Groenhoven
origins.en: Name of different farms (Leiden, Loosduinen, Wassenaar and Kerkwijk).

origins.name: Groenlandia
origins.en: Whaling ship that sailed around 1759 from Oostzanerwerf, owned by shipowner Aard Speciaal (1717-1760).

origins.name: Groenlandstraat
origins.en: Island in the Atlantic Ocean, northeast of Canada. Greenland is part of the Kingdom of Denmark and is the largest island in the world.

origins.name: Groenlust
origins.en: Farm on the Noorderweg, opposite the Enge Wormer, in the Wijde Wormer.

origins.name: Groenmarktkade
origins.en: Groenmarkt is a shortening of Groentemarkt, held here from 1896 to 1934. In 1934, the Central Market Halls were built on Jan van Galenstraat, after which this vegetable market was abolished.

origins.name: Groenpad
origins.en: Former dirt road in the old municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Groesbeekdreef
origins.en: Name of the upper driveway

origins.name: Groetstraat
origins.en: The North Holland village on the dune edge.

origins.name: Groezestraat
origins.en: Sedimented, offshore land with light vegetation, also known as marsh, bog, shallows or shoal.

origins.name: Groningenstraat
origins.en: The province. The adjacent streets are named after Groninger castles (castles).

origins.name: Groot Blankenberg
origins.en: Former castle, destroyed in 1381. This place now houses the Blankenberg house, built as a monastery in 1825, located under Cadier and Keer (Limburg).

origins.name: Groot-Essenburg
origins.en: Building from 1652 near Hierden on the Veluwe, built on the foundations of a thirteenth-century castle. Restored in 1929.

origins.name: Grootslagstraat
origins.en: Large polder west of Enkhuizen.

origins.name: Grootzeil
origins.en: One of the sails of a ship.

origins.name: Grootzeilhof
origins.en: One of the sails of a ship.

origins.name: Grossglockner
origins.en: Highest mountain in Austria, 3787 meters.

origins.name: Grote Beerstraat
origins.en: The constellation.

origins.name: Grote Bickersstraat
origins.en: These streets are located on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr. Johan Bicker (1591-1653), shipbuilder and merchant, ships and mayor of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets that were later laid out on this island automatically took the name of the founder.

origins.name: Grote Diestraat
origins.en: Literally: 'Big water', to distinguish it from the Kleine Die further along. The quay was at the level of the Nieuwendijk.

origins.name: Grote Ruwenberg
origins.en: Only a tower with shooting holes remains of this castle under St. Michielsgestel (North Brabant). The rest has been converted and expanded into a boarding school.

origins.name: Grote Wittenburgerstraat
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (next to Kattenburg and Oostenburg), built in the second half of the seventeenth century, from the beginning built with shipyards and houses. One of the first shipyards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. Very likely we must look here for the origin of the name Wittenburg.

origins.name: Grubbehoeve
origins.en: Farm near Albergen under Tubbergen (Overijssel). The farm is named after the Grubbe family, who is already mentioned in 1394.

origins.name: Guggenheimlaan
origins.en: Museum Solomon R. Guggenheim in New York, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, built in 1956. Known for the spiral-running gallery around the central hall. The basis of the modern art collection was collected by multimillionaire Solomon Guggenheim.

origins.name: Guido Gezellestraat
origins.en: Flemish priest and poet (1830-1899). Has a very extensive oeuvre. Above all a natural poet.

origins.name: Guldehandsteeg
origins.en: The signboard of the inn 'In de gulde Hant' is the name giver here. The inn stood in the sixteenth century on the corner with Warmoesstraat. The alley ends with a water curb on the water of the Damrak, which is why the name Watersteeg also appears in the Middle Ages. The current name was re-registered in the street register around 1980 after having been omitted for about a hundred years.

origins.name: Gulden Kruis
origins.en: Name of a patrician house in Beverwijk (North Holland).

origins.name: Gulden Kruispad
origins.en: Name of a patrician house in Beverwijk (North Holland).

origins.name: Gulden Winckelplantsoen
origins.en: To a poem by Vondel from 1613.

origins.name: Gulden Winckelstraat
origins.en: To a poem by Vondel from 1613.

origins.name: Guldenpromenade
origins.en: The guilder was the Dutch currency until the introduction of the euro on January 1, 2002.

origins.name: Gunterstein
origins.en: Castle on the right bank of the Vecht near Breukelen, built in the thirteenth century, inhabited from 1611 to 1619 by Johan van Oldenbarneveldt. The current building was built after the destruction by the French in 1672.

origins.name: Gustav Mahlerlaan
origins.en: Austrian composer and conductor (1860-1911). One of the most important conductors of his time. He linked his compositions with the late romanticism and the modern period of classical music. Mahler had a special bond with Amsterdam, the city he first visited in 1903 at the invitation of Willem Mengelberg, the conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra. This visit became the beginning of a close bond between the orchestra and the composer.

origins.name: Gustav Mahlerplein
origins.en: Austrian composer and conductor (1860-1911). One of the most important conductors of his time. He linked his compositions with the late romanticism and the modern period of classical music. Mahler had a special bond with Amsterdam, the city he first visited in 1903 at the invitation of Willem Mengelberg, the conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra. This visit became the beginning of a close bond between the orchestra and the composer.

origins.name: Gutserstraat
origins.en: Someone who sticks out with a gut (wedge with hollow beak), for example wood. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Guus Trestorffstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1905-1944), born in Amsterdam and executed there.

origins.name: Gyroscoopweg
origins.en: Rapidly rotating body, symmetrically built around a rotational axis. Used for ship compasses. The instrument was invented by Foucault.

origins.name: H. Cleyndertweg
origins.en: Hendrik Cleyndert A.zn (1881-1958). Originally a grain trader in Nieuwendam. Founder of government care for landscape and recreation. Member of the Association for the Preservation of Nature Monuments in the Netherlands, Bond Heemschut and Association Hendrick de Keyser.

origins.name: H. Diesveldsingel
origins.en: The name is misspelled. Johannes Henricus (Harry) Diesveldt (1918-1944), resistance fighter and Englishman. Returned from England as a secret agent-telegramist. He was arrested in Amsterdam and executed in Vught.

origins.name: H. Gerhardstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Gerhard (1829-1886), Amsterdam tailor, one of the socialist pioneers, co-founder of De Dageraad in 1856. Represented in our country the 'First Socialist International' founded in 1864.

origins.name: H. Stolleplantsoen
origins.en: Heinrich Wilhelm Christian Stolle (1924-2006), architect and furniture designer. Was part of a partnership with Frans van Gool and Arnold Oyevaar, which designed 1100 houses in the Buikslotermeer.

origins.name: H.A.J. Baanderskade
origins.en: Herman Ambrosius Jan Baanders (1876-1953), architect of the Amsterdam school. Designed, among other things, the Amsterdam Lyceum on Valeriusplein and housing in Rooseveltlaan and Uiterwaardenstraat.

origins.name: H.J. Algrastraat
origins.en: Hendrik Algra (1896-1982), journalist and anti-revolutionary politician. Chief editor of the 'Friesch Dagblad'. From 1946 to 1969 he served in the House of Representatives for the Anti-Revolutionary Party, with areas of focus on defense, foreign affairs and education.

origins.name: H.J.E. Wenckebachweg
origins.en: Henri Johan Eduard Wenckebach (1861-1924), founder and director of the Royal Dutch Highovens and Steelworks. The first name of the street (Industrieweg council decision, 1963) was withdrawn at the request of the municipality of Ouder-Amstel, because an Industrieweg already existed in Duivendrecht.

origins.name: H.J.M. Walenkampstraat
origins.en: Hermanus Johannes Maria Walenkamp (1871-1933), architect and graphic designer. He interned at P.J.H. Cuypers. Among his works are residential buildings Zaanhof in the Spaarndammerbuurt.

origins.name: H.M. Kraaijvangerstraat
origins.en: Herman Kraaijvanger (1903-1981), architect. Founded an architectural firm together with his brother. The pre-war work of the firm falls within the tradition of Dutch brick architecture, almost exclusively realized for Catholic clients.

origins.name: H.T. Zwiersplantsoen
origins.en: Henri Tino Zwiers (1900-1992), architect, born in Amsterdam. Pioneer in the Netherlands in the field of building with prefabricated elements, such as in Terrasdorp. Was a professor in Delft from 1938.

origins.name: Haag en Veld
origins.en: Patrician house in Velsen (North Holland), first mentioned in 1671.

origins.name: Haaksbergweg
origins.en: Name of a mountain near Haaksbergen.

origins.name: Haardstee
origins.en: Name of a farm near Steenderen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Haarlemmer Houttuinen
origins.en: To expand the existing wood storage sites, after 1612 some areas were designated for wood stacking. Due to their location parallel to Haarlemmerstraat and dike, they received this name. The character of a street emerged when the quay was widened in the nineteenth century and built with houses, and the railway dike was laid. Around 1970, that character changed again due to the demolition of most of the buildings and the construction of a wide traffic road, to relieve traffic through the Haarlemmerdijk and -straat. This widening also disappeared Westerdokstraat, Korte Westerdokstraat and Teerplein.

origins.name: Haarlemmerdijk
origins.en: The city of Haarlem. Before the city expansion of 1593, the Haarlemmerpoort was at the end of the Nieuwendijk. The Haarlemmerdijk was therefore outside the city. In 1593, the section up to the Korte Prinsengracht was brought within the city and was renamed Haarlemmerstraat. A few years later (1612), the next section became urban area, but retained the name Haarlemmerdijk. The Haarlemmerpoort (by Hendrik de Keyser) stood on the Haarlemmerplein from approximately 1615. In 1837, that gate was demolished and rebuilt, and renamed Willemspoort during the entrance of King William II in 1840.

origins.name: Haarlemmermeerstraat
origins.en: The municipality of that name, created after the reclamation in 1852.

origins.name: Haarlemmerplein
origins.en: The city of Haarlem. Before the city expansion of 1593, the Haarlemmerpoort was located at the end of the Nieuwendijk. The Haarlemmerdijk was therefore outside the city. In 1593, the section up to the Korte Prinsengracht was brought within the city and was renamed Haarlemmerstraat. A few years later (1612), the next section became urban area, but retained the name Haarlemmerdijk. From around 1615, the Haarlemmerpoort (by Hendrik de Keyser) stood on the Haarlemmerplein. In 1837, that gate was demolished and rebuilt, and renamed Willemspoort when King William II entered in 1840.

origins.name: Haarlemmersluis
origins.en: This bridge is named after the Haarlemmerstraat, which is the main road from Amsterdam to Haarlem

origins.name: Haarlemmerstraat
origins.en: The city of Haarlem. Before the city expansion of 1593, the Haarlemmerpoort was located at the end of the Nieuwendijk. The Haarlemmerdijk was therefore outside the city. In 1593, the section up to the Korte Prinsengracht was drawn into the city and was renamed Haarlemmerstraat. A few years later (1612), the next section became urban area, but retained the name Haarlemmerdijk. The Haarlemmerpoort (by Hendrik de Keyser) stood on the Haarlemmerplein from approximately 1615. In 1837, that gate was demolished and rebuilt, and renamed Willemspoort during the entrance of King William II in 1840.

origins.name: Haarlemmerweg
origins.en: The traffic road to Haarlem.

origins.name: Haarlerbergpad
origins.en: Name of a hill near Haarle (Overijssel), a height in the loess mound from the penultimate ice age (200,000-130,000 years ago).

origins.name: Haarlerbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Haarle (Overijssel), a height in the loess mound from the penultimate ice age (200,000-130,000 years ago).

origins.name: Hacquartstraat
origins.en: Carolus Hacquart (1640-1730), musician. Wrote pieces for the viola da gamba. Was associated with the Court of the Oranjes as a gamba player.

origins.name: Hagedoornplein
origins.en: Named after the hawthorn, a shrub.

origins.name: Hagedoornweg
origins.en: The shrub. A part of the square was named Plein Spanje '36-'39 in 1986.

origins.name: Hageland
origins.en: Region in Belgium, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Hagenau
origins.en: The Hagenau estate on the Veluwe, originally owned by stadtholder William II.

origins.name: Hajo Brugmanshof
origins.en: Historian (1868-1939). He wrote, among other things, a history of Amsterdam in eight volumes (1933).

origins.name: Hakfort
origins.en: Castle from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, renovated in 1788 and located under Vorden (Gelderland). It is named after knight Bemt van Hackfort (died 1559).

origins.name: Halmaheirastraat
origins.en: One of the islands belonging to the Moluccas (Indonesia).

origins.name: Halteriastraat
origins.en: Microscopic aquatic creature: trilobite. Large stiff hairs cause a jumping movement. Smaller hairs provide a flowing movement in the water, causing food to be swept inside.

origins.name: Halvemaansbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge derives its name from Halvemaansteeg. The origin of this name may be found on the facade of Halvemaanssteeg No. 18, with the indication 'Van Ouds de Halve Maan'

origins.name: Halvemaansteeg
origins.en: The origin of this name may be found in the facade of No. 18, with the indication 'van ouds de Halve Maan'. It is also possible that the bridge is the namesake: the Halvemaansbrug received a semi-curved shape in 1626 (now straight). The name of the alley is already mentioned at the beginning of the seventeenth century and would therefore be older than the bridge.

origins.name: Hamerstraat
origins.en: During the German occupation, he saved many adults and children from the Hollandse Schouwburg and the crèche opposite it, among others, Lau Mazirel and Walter Süskind. He was also one of the founders of the nearby Kriterion cinema, which is operated by students of the University of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Hammarbystraat
origins.en: Waterfront district in southern Stockholm, which has been renovated and redeveloped since the 1990s of the twentieth century.

origins.name: Hamontstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Han Hollanderlaan
origins.en: Hartog Hollander (1886-1943), legendary radio reporter. Made a great contribution to the popularization of the sport in the Netherlands through his reports. Killed in the Sobibor extermination camp.

origins.name: Handbalstraat
origins.en: Refers to the handball club that was here

origins.name: Handboogstraat
origins.en: In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, the Archery and Crossbow Targets were built on the Singel. Both had a shooting range, which extended behind the houses on Kalverstraat. In 1649, two streets were laid out on the grounds of these orchards, which were named Handboogstraat and Voetboogstraat.

origins.name: Händelstraat
origins.en: Georg Friedrich Händel (1685-1759), German-English composer. In addition to operas, he composed 32 oratorios, six concerti grossi, twenty organ concertos, chamber music, songs and festive music.

origins.name: Hanedastraat
origins.en: Name of one of Tokyo's airports.

origins.name: Hannie Dankbaarpassage
origins.en: Henriëtte Christine Jaqueline Dankbaar (1952-2007), politician. First GroenLinks borough chairwoman of Amsterdam (Oud-West, 1990-2002). Originating from the PSP. Becomes popular for her great social involvement.

origins.name: Hans Katanhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1943), student, born in Hilversum, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Hans Meerum Terwogtweg
origins.en: Albert Hendrik Magdalus Meerum Terwogt (1883-1960), elder statesman of the sports journalists. He was sports editor of the 'Nieuwe Rotterdamse Courant' for forty years.

origins.name: Hans Onversaagdstraat
origins.en: Guzen captain during the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Haparandadam
origins.en: Swedish port town on the Gulf of Bothnia. Shipyard.

origins.name: Haparandaweg
origins.en: Swedish port town on the Gulf of Bothnia. Shipyard.

origins.name: Hardwareweg
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Haringbuisdijk
origins.en: Ship, used for herring fishing.

origins.name: Haringvlietstraat
origins.en: Sea current from the Hellegatsplein to the North Sea (between Voorne and Zuid-Beveland). Is now closed off from the open sea by a dam.

origins.name: Harkstraat
origins.en: The gardening tools.

origins.name: Harmoniehof
origins.en: Basic concept from music theory.

origins.name: Haroekoestraat
origins.en: Island, belonging to the Moluccas (Indonesia).

origins.name: Harriet Freezerstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Harriët Wilhelmina Vriesendorp-Eybergen (1911-1971), literary critic and journalist. Wrote for 'De Groene Amsterdammer' and 'Het Parool', editor of the monthly magazine 'Opzij' and involved in the founding of Man Vrouw Maatschappij. She gave many popular lectures, which she made an important contribution to the improvement of the position of the woman.

origins.name: Harry Banninkstraat
origins.en: Composer (1929-1999), arranger and pianist. He wrote music for the musicals of Annie M.G. Schmidt, among others, including 'Heerlijk duurt het langst' and 'Ja zuster, Nee zuster'.

origins.name: Harry Koningsbergerstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1924-1945), born in Blokzijl, executed by firing squad in Zeist.

origins.name: Hart Nibbrigstraat
origins.en: Ferdinand Hart Nibbrig (1866-1915), painter and lithographer, painted portraits and landscapes. Representative of neo-impressionism.

origins.name: Hartelstein
origins.en: Former castle under Itteren (South Limburg), of which remain a fortified farmstead with 17th century remains.

origins.name: Hartenstraat
origins.en: Reminds me of the tanneries and the fur trade, which used to be located in this neighborhood. Heart is an old-fashioned form of deer.

origins.name: Hasebroekstraat
origins.en: Johannes Petrus Hasebroek (1812-1896), preacher and writer. Wrote under the pseudonym Jonathan, among other things, 'Truth and dreams'.

origins.name: Haspelsstraat
origins.en: Abraham Haspels (1893-1942), resistance fighter, born in the municipality of Haarlemmermeer, executed by firing squad in Amersfoort. He was involved in the February Strike in 1941, among other things.

origins.name: Hasselaerssteeg
origins.en: Pieter Dircks Hasselaer (1554-1616), merchant and regent. He bought the brewery 'De Witte Arent' on the corner of the alley and the Prins Hendrikkade in 1587. Before settling in Amsterdam, he had earned much fame as a sharpshooter during the siege of Haarlem. The alley was previously called Trouweloossteegje, which recalls the former St. Jacobskapel, where the divorces were announced.

origins.name: Hatostraat
origins.en: Name of the airport in Willemstad, Curaçao.

origins.name: Havankbrug
origins.en: Havank, pseudonym of Hendrikus Frederikus (Hans) van der Kallen (Leeuwarden, February 19, 1904 - there, June 22, 1964), was a Dutch writer. Havank began his career as a writer of detective novels in Amsterdam. He wrote his first two novels in Amsterdam. He is best known for his 'Shadow series'.

origins.name: Havenstraat
origins.en: Berth for ships.

origins.name: Havikshorst
origins.en: Old manor house (now country house) from 1753, surrounded by a wide moat. Located under De Wijk (Drenthe).

origins.name: Havikslaan
origins.en: Named after the goshawk, a bird of prey.

origins.name: Haya van Someren-Downerstraat
origins.en: Haya Victoria van Someren-Downer (1926-1980), politician, member of the VVD. From 1959 to 1968 she served in the House of Representatives, where she was mainly concerned with education, media and traffic and water affairs. From 1974 to 1980 member of the House of Lords where she campaigned for education and royal affairs.

origins.name: Hazelaarstraat
origins.en: The deciduous tree, which produces hazelnuts.

origins.name: Hazenstraat
origins.en: The rodent the rabbit. The name is given because of the fur of this animal. The street is located near the old tanneries and the fur trade.

origins.name: Heathrowstraat
origins.en: Name of one of London's airports.

origins.name: Hebridenlaan
origins.en: Scottish island group. The group consists of about five hundred islands of which about one hundred are inhabited. The main islands are Lewis and Skye.

origins.name: Hecht en Sterkhof
origins.en: Hecht and Sterk, also known as Storkoe, was a coffee plantation on the Commewijnerivier in the Commewijne district in Suriname. At its peak in 1819, the plantation consisted of more than 1000 acres. After emancipation in 1863, the plantation did not recruit contractors and was probably put out of production shortly after emancipation. In 1910, the plantation was purchased by the Government to make it, together with Frederiksburg, a government plantation. It was set up for the issuance of land to contract workers.

origins.name: Hechtelstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Hectorstraat
origins.en: Figure from Greek mythology: army commander, son of the king of Troy.

origins.name: Hederabrug
origins.en: The scientific name for climbing ivy is hedera. Waterland

origins.name: Heemstedestraat
origins.en: Location in North Holland, growing together with Haarlem.

origins.name: Heer Halewijnstraat
origins.en: Medieval song about a female murderer who is herself murdered by a princess.

origins.name: Heermoesstraat
origins.en: Plant from the horsetail family, which can store substances such as heavy metals from the environment in its own cells. Wild horsetail has been used for centuries for many ailments, including as a diuretic, for joint pain and to strengthen the skeleton and connective tissue.

origins.name: Heesterveld
origins.en: Name of a farm near Nuland (North Brabant).

origins.name: Hegelhof
origins.en: Georg W.F. Hegel (1841-1926), German philosopher. Has had a great influence on the development of philosophy. Was a professor in Berlin. One of his followers in the Netherlands was Bolland.

origins.name: Hegeraatstraat
origins.en: H.J. Hegeraat (1874-1919), teacher, later associated with the daily newspaper 'Het Volk' as a journalist. Writer of several socialist battle songs.

origins.name: Heggerankweg
origins.en: The climbing plant occurs in hedges and creeping wood.

origins.name: Heibrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the Heisteeg, to which it is located. The Heisteeg derives its name from a corner house that was called 't Hayblok. This house is already mentioned at the beginning of the sixteenth century. An unofficial name for this bridge was Strontenburgerbrug until 1606. It was named so because of the environmental nuisance, caused by two nearby shipyards.

origins.name: Heidotistraat
origins.en: Heidoti is a village in the jurisdiction of Upper Saramacca in the northern part of Suriname. In the village live Maroons of the Kwinti people.

origins.name: Heiligeweg
origins.en: After the Miracle of Amsterdam, the chapel 'Ter Heilige Stede' was founded between Rokin and Kalverstraat (later Nieuwezijds Kapel). For the benefit of the pilgrims, a road was then laid alongside the Heiligewegsevaart (later Overtoom) from Sloten to Kalverstraat, which was called the Heiligeweg. Our street is the remainder of that pilgrimage route. In old documents, Leidsestraat is also called Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Heiligewegsluis
origins.en: After the Miracle of Amsterdam, the chapel 'Ter Heilige Stede' was founded between Rokin and Kalverstraat (later Nieuwezijds Kapel). For the benefit of the pilgrims, a road was then laid alongside the Heiligewegsevaart (later Overtoom) from Sloten to Kalverstraat, which was called the Heiligeweg. Our street is the remainder of that pilgrimage route. In old documents, Leidsestraat is also called Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Heimansweg
origins.en: Eduard (Eli) Heimans (1861-1914), natural researcher. Amsterdam teacher, who together with J.P. Thijsse wrote a series of booklets about birds and flowers. Together they founded the Dutch Natural History Society and the magazine 'De Levende Natuur'. Heimans died during a geological excursion.

origins.name: Hein Donnerbrug
origins.en: Jan Hein Donner (1927-1988) was a chess grandmaster, who became champion of the Netherlands several times. He was also a polemicist and columnist for the NRC-Handelsblad.

origins.name: Heining
origins.en: Named after an offshore polder in the former IJ, after the construction of the Grote IJ polders, a separate irrigation area in those polders. The name indicates land that produces little hay. Came to Amsterdam due to the border arrangement with Haarlemmerliede and Spaamwoude in 1963.

origins.name: Heinzestraat
origins.en: Gustav Adolph Heinze (1820-1904), German by birth, conductor in Amsterdam of the German Opera, the Liedertafel Euterpe and the Vincentius concerts. From 1862 to 1885 director of the music school of Toonkunst. Composed cantatas and oratorios.

origins.name: Hekelveld
origins.en: It is likely that this was where the flax was bleached, which had to be processed into rope on the neighboring railway lines, when these lands were still outside the walls. In 1604, there are still two houses that remember this craft by their facade stones. The Hekelveld was originally a canal and was filled in around 1865.

origins.name: Hekla
origins.en: Volcano in Iceland, 1491 meters high.

origins.name: Helena Kuipers-Rietberghof
origins.en: Helena Theodora Kuipers-Rietberg (1893-1944), resistance fighter, born in Winterswijk, died in the Ravensbrück concentration camp. She was known as the mother of the 'National Organization for Aid to Undergrounders' (the L.O.). In addition, she had a stake in the distribution of the illegal newspaper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Helena Mercierstraat
origins.en: Pioneer of the women's movement in Amsterdam (1839-1910), writer on social issues.

origins.name: Helene Madisonstraat
origins.en: American swimmer, won gold in the 100-meter freestyle at the 1932 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

origins.name: Hélène Swarthstraat
origins.en: Hélène Lapidoth born Swarth (1859-1941), poet of love poetry. For a time highly regarded by many, in later years became an forgotten figure.

origins.name: Helicopterstraat
origins.en: Elevator aircraft, which can rise and fall vertically, was constructed in 1933 by the aircraft builder J. Sikorsky, American of Russian birth.

origins.name: Heliotroopstraat
origins.en: Ornamental shrub, originally from South America.

origins.name: Hella Haasseplein
origins.en: Hélène Serafia Haasse (1918-2011). Writer of novels, essays, poetry and plays. Received the P.C. Hooft Prize in 1983 and the Prize of the Dutch Letters in 2004. Wrote the record number of 3 Book Week gifts, including 'Oeroeg' (1948), possibly her most famous work. Belongs to the most widely read Dutch authors abroad.

origins.name: Hellenburg
origins.en: Lost castle in the vicinity of Goes, whose foundations have now been exposed.

origins.name: Hellingstraat
origins.en: The name refers to the two concrete ship slips on the NDSM site, which were used to launch ships.

origins.name: Helmgrasstraat
origins.en: Permanent native pioneer plant from the grass family. Important in dune formation.

origins.name: Helmholtzstraat
origins.en: Hermann von Helmholtz (1821-1894), German physician and physicist. Inventor of the ophthalmoscope.

origins.name: Helsingforsbrug
origins.en: Helsingfors is the Swedish name for Helsinki, the capital of Finland. The names in the Ports of the North are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Hembrugstraat
origins.en: To the former railway bridge over the North Sea Canal, which was a hindrance to the Amsterdam harbor. The bridge was demolished after the opening of the railway tunnel (the Hemtunnel).

origins.name: Hemonylaan
origins.en: The brothers Frans Hemony (1609-1667) and Pieter Hemony (1619-1680) Bellfounders of the carillons in the Old Church, the Zuiderkerk, the Westerkerk and the Mint Tower.

origins.name: Hemonystraat
origins.en: The brothers Frans Hemony (1609-1667) and Pieter Hemony (1619-1680) Bellfounders of the carillons in the Old Church, the Zuiderkerk, the Westerkerk and the Mint Tower.

origins.name: Hemsterhuisstraat
origins.en: Tiberius Hemsterhuis (1685-1766), classical philologist. Professor in Amsterdam (wisdom), later in Franeker and Leiden (Greek and national history).

origins.name: Hemweg
origins.en: To a former island called the Hem in the former IJ. The Hem was initially a spit of land that only later became an island due to a river bend. The word is the same as 'ham', which is only known as 'inham' anymore. There is now only one last piece of the Hemweg left, originally this road began in the Spaarndammerbuurt.

origins.name: Hendrik Bulthuisstraat
origins.en: Barber (1892-1948), from the Frisian village of Bergum. Designer of the B.M. sailboat, pioneer of sailing as a folk sport.

origins.name: Hendrik de Bruynstraat
origins.en: Hydrologist (1815-1885). Known for the waterworks he built in Surabaya (Dutch East Indies).

origins.name: Hendrik Dienskestraat
origins.en: Resistance hero, office worker, born in Schiedam 1907 and killed in Helenstedt (Germany) in 1945.

origins.name: Hendrik Godfroidhof
origins.en: Hendrikus Godfroid (1899-1943), resistance fighter, born in Arnhem, died in the prison of Scheveningen. He was a member of the illegal newspaper 'De Waarheid'.

origins.name: Hendrik Hosstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Pieter Hos (1906-1944), resistance fighter, born in Haarlem and executed in Scheveningen. He was in charge of the national apparatus of the illegal newspaper 'Vrij Nederland'.

origins.name: Hendrik Jacobszstraat
origins.en: Violin maker. Manufactured violins between 1690 and 1740 in the style of the Italian Amati.

origins.name: Hendrik Jonkerplein
origins.en: Amsterdam industrialist (1778-1843), who founded the steam and other machinery factory that was previously located here in 1806. Before 1956, this was Bickersplein. The naming was made following a request from the N.V. Hk. Jonker and Zn, which had existed for 150 years that year.

origins.name: Hendrik Soeteboomstraat
origins.en: Historian (1616-1678). Wrote several books about Waterland, including 'De historie van Waterland' and 'De Waterlanders' (1660).

origins.name: Hendrik van Wijnstraat
origins.en: Historian (1740-1831), founder of the General State Archives (1802). Wrote appendices and annotations to the 'Fatherland History' of the historian Jan Wagenaar.

origins.name: Hendrik Veldhuishof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1922-1944), established a printing house in Blaricum for the illegal newspaper 'Trouw', where other illegal printing was also produced. In June 1944 he was arrested and shortly thereafter executed in Vught.

origins.name: Hendrik Werkmanstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Nicolaas Werkman (1882-1945), artist, printer and resistance fighter. Printer at collective 'De Blauwe Schuit' that published critical articles about the German occupation. Shot dead in 1945.

origins.name: Hendrikje Stoffelsstraat
origins.en: Life partner of Rembrandt van Rijn (1626-1663). Entered his household around 1647 as a maid and soon lived with the painter. Probably modeled for several works. Was buried in the Westerkerk.

origins.name: Hendrikus Rempestraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1903-1944), born in Amsterdam, killed in Bruttig (Germany).

origins.name: Henegouwenstraat
origins.en: Province in the south of Belgium.

origins.name: Henk Curièrekade
origins.en: Peter Heinrich Curière (1911-1981), legendary figure in the Spaarndammer neighborhood due to his positive and active involvement in urban renewal in this neighborhood and as chairman of the Neighborhood Improvement Committee.

origins.name: Henk Gortzakstraat
origins.en: Hendricus Gortzak (1909-1989), politician. Member of the Communist Party of Holland. Involved in the activities of the illegally established Communist Party of the Netherlands during the occupation. In 1948 he entered the House of Representatives for the CPN and from 1952 to 1958 he was faction chairman. In 1958 Gortzak was expelled from the party due to a conflict with the party leadership.

origins.name: Henk Henriëtstraat
origins.en: Painter and graphic artist (1903-1945).

origins.name: Henk Hienschstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Jan Hiensch (1912-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, killed in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

origins.name: Henk Sneevlietpad
origins.en: Hendricus J.F.M. Sneevliet (1883-1942), politician and active figure in the trade union movement in the Netherlands and in the former Dutch East Indies. Internationally known as a communist due to his contacts with China and Russia. As a resistance fighter, he was executed by the Germans.

origins.name: Henk Sneevlietweg
origins.en: Hendricus J.F.M. Sneevliet (1883-1942), politician and active figure in the trade union movement in the Netherlands and in the former Dutch East Indies. Internationally known as a communist due to his contacts with China and Russia. As a resistance fighter, he was executed by the Germans.

origins.name: Henkenshage
origins.en: Castle in St. Oedenrode, founded in the fifteenth century and partly in the seventeenth century, renovated in the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Henri Bergsonstraat
origins.en: French philosopher and physicist (1859-1941), author of 'Creative evolution' (1907). Received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1927.

origins.name: Henri Berssenbruggehof
origins.en: Photographer (1873-1959). Photographed street life, the ordinary (craftsman) man and portrayed the cultural elite of the Netherlands. Known for his harmonious compositions, contrasting light-dark ratios and perfected printing methods.

origins.name: Henri Borelstraat
origins.en: Prose writer and playwright (1869-1933). Writer of Indian stories and Hague novels.

origins.name: Henri Dunantstraat
origins.en: Jean Henri Dunant (1828-1910), Swiss writer and philanthropist. Founded the International Red Cross in 1864. In 1901 he received the first Nobel Peace Prize.

origins.name: Henri Polaklaan
origins.en: Trade union leader and politician (1868-1943), co-founder of the SDAP in 1894 and the first socialist-democratic member of the Amsterdam municipal council. In 1894 he founded the Algemene Nederlandsche Diamantbewerkersbond, which later took the initiative for the founding of the NVV. Due to this naming in 1945, the name PIantage Franselaan expired. At the beginning of the eighteenth century, it was said of the Achterlaan.

origins.name: Henri Zagwijnstraat
origins.en: Composer (1878-1954), wrote chamber music and choral works.

origins.name: Henric van Veldekehof
origins.en: Flemish poet (second half of the twelfth century), among other things of 'The Legend of Saint Servatius' and of a large number of 'Ode to Love'.

origins.name: Henrick de Keijserplein
origins.en: City architect and sculptor (1565-1621), built in Amsterdam the first Stock Exchange, the Wester-, the Zuider- and the Noorderkerk, the Montelbaans- and the Munttoren. In Delft you will find the grave monument of William of Orange.

origins.name: Henrick de Keijserstraat
origins.en: City architect and sculptor (1565-1621), built in Amsterdam the first Stock Exchange, the Wester-, the Zuider- and the Noorderkerk, the Montelbaans- and the Munttoren. In Delft you will find the grave monument of William of Orange.

origins.name: Henriëtte Bosmansstraat
origins.en: Pianist and composer (1895-1952) Composed songs mostly on French texts. Performed as a pianist both in the Netherlands and abroad.

origins.name: Henriëtte Roland Holststraat
origins.en: Henriëtte Roland Holst born Van der Schalk (1869-1952), poet. For many years militant socialist, also in her poems and verse dramas.

origins.name: Henriëtte Ronnerplein
origins.en: Henriëtte Ronner born Knip (1821-1909), painter, especially of dogs and cats.

origins.name: Henriëtte Ronnerstraat
origins.en: Henriëtte Ronner born Knip (1821-1909), painter, especially of dogs and cats.

origins.name: Hensbroekerstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland, between Alkmaar and Hoorn.

origins.name: Herbert Spencerhof
origins.en: English philosopher and sociologist (1820-1903), follower of Rousseau.

origins.name: Hercules Seghersstraat
origins.en: Hercules Pietersz Seghers (1589-1638), engraver and landscape painter. Influences of Seghers are noticeable in the works of Rembrandt and Ruysdael. It was only in the twentieth century that his style of painting found great appreciation.

origins.name: Herculesstraat
origins.en: Hercules is the strong hero in Greek mythology. He is the son of the supreme god Zeus.

origins.name: Herderhof
origins.en: Johann Gottfried Herder (1744-1803), German philosopher and writer. Had a great influence on Goethe.

origins.name: Herengracht
origins.en: To the Lords Regulators of the city (The city was not previously governed, but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch, when it was widened in 1612 to the current canal, as the first of the three main canals. The part beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658. The Nieuwe Herengracht also belongs to that expansion.

origins.name: Herenmarkt
origins.en: To the Lords Regents of the city (The city was not previously governed, but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch, when it was widened in 1612 to the current canal, as the first of the three main canals. The part beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658. The Nieuwe Herengracht also belongs to that expansion.

origins.name: Herenstraat
origins.en: To the Lords Regents of the city (The city was not previously governed, but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch, when it was widened in 1612 to the current canal, as the first of the three main canals. The part beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658. The Nieuwe Herengracht also belongs to that expansion.

origins.name: Herentalsstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Herfststraat
origins.en: The autumn season. In 1966, the street was transferred from the abolished municipality of Weesperkarspel under the name Vechtstraat (council decision of weesperkarspel, 1957), but that name could not be maintained due to confusion with the existing Vechtstraat.

origins.name: Herikerbergweg
origins.en: Hill near the hamlet of Herike, municipality of Markelo (Overijssel).

origins.name: Heringa-State
origins.en: Castle in Marssum near Leeuwarden, also called Poptaslot, built in the sixteenth century, restored in 1908.

origins.name: Herinkhave
origins.en: Originally a fourteenth-century house located near Tubbergen (Overijssel), now a simple fortified manor house from 1723.

origins.name: Herman Bonpad
origins.en: Hermanus J. Bon (1873-1945), known as Pa Bon in casual conversation. Advocate and for many years leader of the school football matches in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Herman de Manstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of the Jewish novelist Salomon Hamburger (1898-1946). Converted to Roman Catholicism. He wrote the novel 'The flowing water' among others.

origins.name: Herman Gorterstraat
origins.en: Poet (1864-1927). Made his name especially with his great nature poem 'May' (1889). Wrote 'Critique of the Literary Movement of the Eighties' and was a militant Marxist socialist for many years.

origins.name: Herman Heijermansweg
origins.en: Journalist, novelist and playwright (1864-1924). Wrote many novels set in Amsterdam, also under the pseudonym Samuel Falkland. His great success was the play 'In the hope of blessing'.

origins.name: Herman Hellingplantsoen
origins.en: Guzen captain who served under governor Diederik Sonoy, during the Siege of Amsterdam (1572-1578). Helling died in 1577 together with hopman Nicolaas Ruychaver during a failed attempt to take over the town hall on the Dam.

origins.name: Herman Poortstraat
origins.en: Poet and writer (1886-1933). Gained particular fame as a teacher of literary subjects for the Volksuniversiteit and as a theater critic. Among other things, he wrote a study on Brederode.

origins.name: Herman Robbersstraat
origins.en: Literary (1868-1937), writer of novellas and novels. In addition, editor-in-chief of Elsevier and critic.
