origins.name: Hermanus Coenradistraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1909-1941), electrician. Born in Amsterdam, executed in The Hague.

origins.name: Hermietenstraat
origins.en: To a house, which stood at the corner of the Rokin at the beginning of the seventeenth century and was called 'De Heremyt'. Until 1912 this was Hermietensteeg. In that year the alley was widened to six meters: the addition of the alley was changed into a street. Hermit is derived from the word hermit, which means recluse.

origins.name: Hermitagelaan
origins.en: Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg, one of the largest museum complexes in the world. The origin of the collection is the precious imperial private collection of paintings. Famous for the work of Titian, Rubens and especially Rembrandt.

origins.name: Herschelstraat
origins.en: Friedrich W. Herschel (1738-1822), English astronomer. Made mirror reflectors and discovered the planet Uranus.

origins.name: Hertingenstraat
origins.en: Around 1500, a church village drowned in Zeelandic Flanders.

origins.name: Hertspieghelweg
origins.en: Learned poem by Spieghel (1549-1612), merchant and literary scholar.

origins.name: Hertzogstraat
origins.en: James B.M. Hertzog (1866-1942), South African statesman, general in the Boer War from 1899 to 1902. Served as minister on several occasions and in 1924 as prime minister of the Republic of South Africa.

origins.name: Hertzstraat
origins.en: Heinrich Rudolf Hertz (1857-1894), German physicist, founder of radio telegraphy. The unit of frequency is named after him.

origins.name: Herwijk
origins.en: The English port city of Harwich, according to a spelling as that found on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Hessenbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill east of Heerlerheide (Limburg).

origins.name: Hestiastraat
origins.en: Figure from Greek mythology. Oldest daughter of Chronos and Rhea and sister of Zeus. Goddess of the hearth fire and hospitality.

origins.name: Het Breed
origins.en: These names have been given to convey the meaning of the word, as a counterpart to Het Hoogt and Het Laagt.

origins.name: Het Dok
origins.en: The street was laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company, by the staff in the area nicknamed Het Dok.

origins.name: Het Hoogt
origins.en: Named after the location.

origins.name: Het Laagt
origins.en: The name has been given to the path that has been laid out at street level, and therefore reflects the location. The residential street above, at the height of the third living floor, has been named Het Hoogt.

origins.name: Hettenheuvelweg
origins.en: Hill near Bergh in Montferland (Gelderland).

origins.name: Heusdenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Heverleestraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Hexaanweg
origins.en: Tropical product, a component of gasoline, that is being dumped in the Amsterdam port.

origins.name: Hilbert van Dijkhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1944), by profession milk slicer, born in Kampen, executed in Bloemendaal.

origins.name: Hildebrandstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Nicolaas Beets.

origins.name: Hildegard von Bingenstraat
origins.en: Hildegard von Bingen was a German composer, but also a scientist (cosmology, botany), abbess and philosopher

origins.name: Hildo Kropplein
origins.en: Hildebrand Lucien Krop (1884-1970), urban sculptor and painter. He produced, among other things, the Berlage Monument in Amsterdam. Through his decorations and sculptures on Amsterdam bridges and buildings, he has been of great significance to the 'Amsterdam School'.

origins.name: Hildsven
origins.en: The pond, located on the west side of the municipality of Moergestel in the province of North Brabant, is a natural monument.

origins.name: Hillegomstraat
origins.en: Location in South Holland, on the border of North Holland.

origins.name: Hillenraadt
origins.en: A noble house surrounded by canals in Swalmen (Limburg) from the sixteenth century, renovated and enlarged in later centuries.

origins.name: Hilverbeekstraat
origins.en: Country estate under 's-Graveland, founded in the seventeenth century by Amsterdam patricians.

origins.name: Hilversumstraat
origins.en: City in the Gooi.

origins.name: Hiridostraat
origins.en: Mountain in Somalia

origins.name: Hirschpassage
origins.en: Named after the former fashion store Hirsch and Cie, which opened in 1882 at the corner of Leidseplein and Weteringschans. The management had completed its training at Hirsch in Brussels, which itself was a branch of the entire French fashion-oriented German Hirsch Group.

origins.name: Hobaostraat
origins.en: Mountain top on Bonaire

origins.name: Hobbemakade
origins.en: Meindert Hobbema (1638-1709), landscape painter, pupil of Ruysdael.

origins.name: Hobbemastraat
origins.en: Meindert Hobbema (1638-1709), landscape painter, pupil of Ruysdael.

origins.name: Hodenpijlkade
origins.en: Village under Schipluiden in the Westland.

origins.name: Hoek van Hollandstraat
origins.en: Village at the mouth of the Nieuwe Waterweg, since 1914 belonging to the municipality of Rotterdam.

origins.name: Hoekenes
origins.en: Island in the former IJ. The word nes means spit of land.

origins.name: Hoekenespad
origins.en: Island in the former IJ. The word nes means spit of land.

origins.name: Hoekenesplantsoen
origins.en: Island in the former IJ. The word nes means spit of land.

origins.name: Hoekenrode
origins.en: Name of an old farm in De Bilt (Utrecht).

origins.name: Hoekenrodepad
origins.en: Name of an old farm in De Bilt (Utrecht).

origins.name: Hoekschewaardplein
origins.en: The South Holland island.

origins.name: Hoekschewaardweg
origins.en: The South Holland island.

origins.name: Hoekslootstraat
origins.en: The name Hoeksloot appears on maps of Rhineland and the surrounding area from the eighteenth century. After around 1800, the ditch is called Hoornsloot. It still runs along Amstelveenseweg and in Amstelveen along the Emmakade.

origins.name: Hoendiepstraat
origins.en: Channel in the province of Groningen.

origins.name: Hof van Eden
origins.en: According to the Hebrew Bible, the Hof van Eden or Garden of Eden was a garden in or equal to the perfect and beautiful Paradise where Adam and Eve lived.

origins.name: Hof van Groenen
origins.en: This is probably an earlier name of the seventeenth-century knightly court town and craft lordship in Delfland, which appears under the name Groeneveld in 1771.

origins.name: Hof van Versailles
origins.en: Palace of Versailles, southwest of Paris. One of the most impressive baroque buildings in Europe, built for Louis XIV. Largely completed between 1661 and 1690.

origins.name: Hofgeest
origins.en: Name of a patrician house in Velsen (North Holland).

origins.name: Hofmeesterstraat
origins.en: Someone who takes care of passengers on passenger boats for the meals and the service of the buffet.

origins.name: Hofmeyrstraat
origins.en: Jan Hendrik Hofmeyr (1845-1912), South African statesman. Fought for the enforcement of Dutch in South Africa.

origins.name: Hofwijckstraat
origins.en: Autobiographical work by Constantijn Huygens, from 1651. It was also the name of his house outside Voorburg, which still exists.

origins.name: Hogeboomspad
origins.en: Name of a path, which used to lie north of Leimuiden and was swallowed up by the Haarlemmermeer. A high tree is a high-altitude footbridge, in principle consisting of only one tree or beam.

origins.name: Hogehilweg
origins.en: De Hoge Hil, a hill near Domburg (Zeeland).

origins.name: Hogelandplein
origins.en: The Hogeland (also written as Hoogeland) is the region in the province of Groningen north of the Reitdiep and the Damsterdiep. The name refers to the relatively high elevation of the ground, caused by the siltation of the sea. The soil therefore consists of sea clay.

origins.name: Hogendijk
origins.en: Area in Groningen, north of the Reitdiep and the Damsterdiep. The name refers to the high elevation of the seabed relative to the peatlands south of the area.

origins.name: Hogevecht
origins.en: Patrician house on the Vecht between Loenen and Breukelen.

origins.name: Hogeweg
origins.en: Named so by the municipal council of the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer, because the road is at the front of the polder.

origins.name: Hogewerf
origins.en: A former knightly manor (now farm) near Oud Beijerland, named after the former owner Lord Hubrecht Hoogewerff.

origins.name: Holbeinstraat
origins.en: Hans Holbein the Younger (1497-1543), German painter and engraver.

origins.name: Holendrechtdreef
origins.en: Water flow on the border of North Holland and Utrecht.

origins.name: Holendrechterweg
origins.en: Water flow on the border of North Holland and Utrecht.

origins.name: Holendrechtplein
origins.en: Water flow on the border of North Holland and Utrecht.

origins.name: Holendrechtstraat
origins.en: Water flow on the border of North Holland and Utrecht. The Holendrechterweg runs along this water and was previously entirely in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. With the annexation of 1966, part of this road came onto Amsterdam's territory.

origins.name: Hollandia Kattenburgpad
origins.en: Raincoat factory, which stood here until the end of the 1960s of the twentieth century. On this path a monument has been erected in memory of the tragic event of November 11, 1942, when 367 Jewish staff members of the raincoat factory Hollandia Kattenburg were arrested by the Germans and deported to the concentration camps with their family members who had been taken from their homes. Only eight staff members survived the camps.

origins.name: Hollandse Tuin
origins.en: Name of one of the many shipyards, which were located here in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries along Grote Bickersstraat.

origins.name: Hollemanstraat
origins.en: Arnold F. Holleman (1859-1953), chemist, professor in Amsterdam from 1905 to 1926. His textbooks on chemistry have been translated into many languages.

origins.name: Holterbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Holten (Overijssel).

origins.name: Holtmeulen
origins.en: Castle in Tegelen. Headquarters of Frederick Henry during the siege of Venlo in 1646.

origins.name: Holwerdahof
origins.en: Jan Hendrik Holwerda (1873-1951), archaeologist and historian, director of the Rijksmuseum van Oudheden in Leiden. Wrote among other things 'Dutch earliest civilization' (1925).

origins.name: Holy
origins.en: Former knightly court town north of Vlaardingen (South Holland).

origins.name: Homme Hettingastraat
origins.en: Friesian greaveman, member of the Confederation of the Nobles (1566), joined the army of Louis of Nassau in 1568.

origins.name: Hondecoeterstraat
origins.en: Melchior d'Hondecoeter (1636-1695), painter of animals and still lifes.

origins.name: Hondiusstraat
origins.en: Jodocus de Hondt or Hondius (1563-1612), a cartographer, engraver and publisher from Ghent in Amsterdam, especially of maps and atlases (including the Mercator atlas).

origins.name: Hondsrugweg
origins.en: Hillside in Drenthe.

origins.name: Honingen
origins.en: Originally a thirteenth-century water castle of the lords of Kralingen, east of Rotterdam. In 1573 Lumey was imprisoned here.

origins.name: Honselersdijkstraat
origins.en: Village under Naaldwijk, in the Westland.

origins.name: Honthorststraat
origins.en: Gerard van Honthorst (1590-1656), painter of portraits and night scenes. Court painter of Frederick Henry.

origins.name: Hoofddorpplein
origins.en: Village, capital of the municipality of Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Hoofddorpweg
origins.en: Village, capital of the municipality of Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Hoofdweg
origins.en: The name was given by the former municipality of Sloten for the function: a wide central traffic road. After the annexation in 1921, the road was extended in a northerly direction to the Bos en Lommerplein.

origins.name: Hooge Venne
origins.en: Former farm in the old municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Hoogheemraadweg
origins.en: A high commissioner is a member of the board of directors of a high commissionerate, a water board to which several water boards and polders fall under. Amsterdam includes parts of the high commissionerates of Amstelland, Rhine-Land and Waterland. The high commissionerates of Amstelland and Waterland have now merged into a larger whole.

origins.name: Hoogoorddreef
origins.en: Men's house under Hilversum, built around 1900 (North Holland).

origins.name: Hoogoordplein
origins.en: Men's house under Hilversum, built around 1900 (North Holland).

origins.name: Hoogte Kadijk
origins.en: When a lot of land had been silted up outside the old sea wall (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike or canal was built. Originally, it was called the new sea wall, but that later fell out of use. With further raising of this new dike, it was called the Laagte and the Hoogte of the Kadijk. The Between Dikes was called Korte Kerkstraat until 1943. This is indeed in the extension of the Plantage Kerklaan, but has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Hoogwoudstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland.

origins.name: Hooistraat
origins.en: Mowed and dried grass (and some other crops), used as feed in livestock farming.

origins.name: Hooivletstraat
origins.en: Ship (flat-bottomed), which was used for transporting hay.

origins.name: Hoopende Swaen
origins.en: Whale hunter of the Oostzaanse shipowner Pieter Swan. Fished in the seas east of Greenland between 1759 and 1775.

origins.name: Hoorneboeg
origins.en: Country estate under Hilversum (North Holland).

origins.name: Hoornsestraat
origins.en: To the North Holland town of Hoorn. Once an important Zuiderzee city, which can still be seen from numerous monumental buildings.

origins.name: Hoptille
origins.en: Neighborhood with a bridge of the same name west of Hijlaard (Friesland).

origins.name: Hoptillepad
origins.en: Neighborhood with a bridge of the same name west of Hijlaard (Friesland).

origins.name: Hornweg
origins.en: Former island De Hoorn or Horn in the former IJ. After the construction of the North Sea Canal, the island could still be clearly recognized in the landscape in the Great IJpolder. Due to the extension of the Westhaven (around 1960), it was completely buried. 'Horn' means corner and was given to similar coastal formations as 'nes' and 'ham'. The full name of this horn was Zaanderhorn. It was a peninsula that belonged to the western part of Zaanden, the predecessor of Zaandam.

origins.name: Hortensiastraat
origins.en: Ornamental shrub.

origins.name: Hortusplantsoen
origins.en: To the opposite Hortus Botanicus. The quay used to be called Muidergracht, but due to the confusion with the Plantage Muidergracht, this name was established in 1911.

origins.name: Houdringe
origins.en: Nature reserve in De Bilt (Utrecht).

origins.name: Houthalenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Houthavenkade
origins.en: Transportation goods that were and are shipped through the Amsterdam port.

origins.name: Houthavenweg
origins.en: Transportation goods that were and are shipped through the Amsterdam port.

origins.name: Houtkopersburgwal
origins.en: Named after the many wood merchants and their storage facilities, who settled along this water in the seventeenth century. Until 1878, the cross street was called Vlooienburgsteeg.

origins.name: Houtkopersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the many wood merchants and their storage facilities, who settled along this water in the seventeenth century. Until 1878, the cross street was called Vlooienburgsteeg.

origins.name: Houtmandwarsstraat
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis (circa 1540-1599) and Frederik Houtman (died 1625), who made the first voyage under the Dutch flag to East India in 1595/1597 on behalf of Amsterdam merchants. Cornelis made a second voyage and was governor of Ambon for six years, Frederik became governor of the Moluccas.

origins.name: Houtmankade
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis (circa 1540-1599) and Frederik Houtman (died 1625), who made the first voyage under the Dutch flag to East India in 1595/1597 on behalf of Amsterdam merchants. Cornelis made a second voyage and was governor of Ambon for six years, Frederik became governor of the Moluccas.

origins.name: Houtmanstraat
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis (circa 1540-1599) and Frederik Houtman (died 1625), who made the first voyage under the Dutch flag to East India in 1595/1597 on behalf of Amsterdam merchants. Cornelis made a second voyage and was governor of Ambon for six years, Frederik became governor of the Moluccas.

origins.name: Houtrijkstraat
origins.en: To the former village of Houtrijk and Polanen, now Halfweg. Previously, the name of this street was Tweede Spaamdammerstraat (council decision, 1881). In 1978, due to the change of the street pattern, a part of the street was renamed and joined to the Assendelftstraat.

origins.name: Hoyerpad
origins.en: Roman character of the writer Nescio. Nescio (Latin: 'I don't know') is the pseudonym of Jan Hendrik Frederik Grönloh (1882-1961), who became especially known with his stories 'De uitvreter' and 'Titaantjes'.

origins.name: Huddekade
origins.en: Johannes Hudde (1628-1704), mayor of Amsterdam from 1672 to 1704, expert in the field of water management. The former Hoogesluis (built 1662, demolished 1883) was made according to his design.

origins.name: Huddestraat
origins.en: Johannes Hudde (1628-1704), mayor of Amsterdam from 1672 to 1704, expert in the field of water management. The former Hoogesluis (built 1662, demolished 1883) was made according to his design.

origins.name: Hudsonhof
origins.en: Henry Hudson (1550-1611), English sailor in service of the United East India Company. Discovered the Hudson Bay named after him between Labrador and Canada (1610).

origins.name: Hudsonstraat
origins.en: Henry Hudson (1550-1611), English sailor in service of the United East India Company. Discovered the Hudson Bay named after him between Labrador and Canada (1610).

origins.name: Hugo de Grootkade
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of International Law. Became involved in church disputes as leader of the Remonstrants and was imprisoned at Loevestein at the request of Prince Maurice. From there, he managed to escape in 1621 through a bookcase.

origins.name: Hugo de Grootplein
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of International Law. Became involved in church disputes as leader of the Remonstrants and was imprisoned at Loevestein at the request of Prince Maurice. From there, he managed to escape in 1621 through a bookcase.

origins.name: Hugo de Vrieslaan
origins.en: Botanist (1848-1935), professor at the University of Amsterdam 1880-1918. He developed the mutation theory, which assumes sudden change of characteristics. The theory applies to all living organisms, so not only to plants.

origins.name: Hugo Floris Ruysstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1924-1943), born in Bussum, executed in Haarlem.

origins.name: Hugo Verriesthof
origins.en: Flemish priest and literary scholar (1840-1922). Member of the literary organization 'Van nu en straks'. Author of 'Twenty Flemish Headlines', among other works.

origins.name: Huidekoperstraat
origins.en: Pieter Huidekoper (1798-1852), mayor of Amsterdam from 1842 to 1849. He was passionate about better public housing. The text on a plaque for him reads: 'He was good to the city, he did well to the poor'.

origins.name: Huidenstraat
origins.en: To the fur trade that was concentrated here in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Huifkarpad
origins.en: The type of caravan that was in use around 1900. The street name refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Huigenbos
origins.en: Names of farms in Scherpenzeel (Gelderland) and Egmond Binnen (North Holland).

origins.name: Huismanshof
origins.en: A householder is the main occupant of a house in the countryside.

origins.name: Huiswoudhof
origins.en: Otto Huiswoud (Paramaribo, 1893 - Amsterdam, 1961) and Hermina (given name Dumont. 1905, British Guiana - Amsterdam, 1998). In New York, Otto Huiswoud became involved in social and political issues and in 1914 he became a member of the socialist party. In 1919 he was a co-founder of the Communist Party of the United States. In 1926 he married Hermina. She was also involved in the international communist movement: she worked as a translator for the Communist International (Komintern) and wrote for the monthly magazine The Negro Worker. After World War II, the couple moved to Amsterdam where Otto Huiswoud was president of the Association Ons Suriname from 1954 to 1961.

origins.name: Huiswoudstraat
origins.en: Otto Huiswoud (Paramaribo, 1893 - Amsterdam, 1961) and Hermina (given name Dumont. 1905, British Guiana - Amsterdam, 1998). In New York, Otto Huiswoud became involved in social and political issues and in 1914 he became a member of the socialist party. In 1919 he was a co-founder of the Communist Party of the United States. In 1926 he married Hermina. She was also involved in the international communist movement: she worked as a translator for the Communist International (Komintern) and wrote for the monthly magazine The Negro Worker. After World War II, the couple moved to Amsterdam where Otto Huiswoud was president of the Association Ons Suriname from 1954 to 1961.

origins.name: Hullenbergweg
origins.en: The name of a hill near Bennekom (Gelderland).

origins.name: Hulstweg
origins.en: The shrub with hard, thorny leaves and red berries.

origins.name: Humberto Delgadoplein
origins.en: Portuguese general (1906-1965). Was the opposition candidate during the presidential elections of 1958 of the official candidate of dictator Salazar. He lost due to massive electoral fraud and terror by the secret service. In 1965 he was murdered by the secret services of Spain and Portugal.

origins.name: Humberweg
origins.en: The wide mouth of the English rivers the Trent and the Ouse. The name is well known in the coal trade, because English coal is brought in from the adjacent areas.

origins.name: Huntum
origins.en: Patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

origins.name: Huntumdreef
origins.en: Patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

origins.name: Huntumpad
origins.en: Patrician house on the Vecht, south of Vreeland.

origins.name: Hunzestraat
origins.en: River, which springs in Drenthe and widens at the border of the province of Groningen to the Zuidlaardermeer.

origins.name: Hygiëaplein
origins.en: Health goddess from Greek mythology.

origins.name: Hygiëastraat
origins.en: Health goddess from Greek mythology.

origins.name: Ibizastraat
origins.en: Spanish island in the Mediterranean Sea. The island is part of the Balearic Islands archipelago.

origins.name: Iepenplein
origins.en: Named after the elm, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Iepenweg
origins.en: Named after the elm, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: IJ-tunnel
origins.en: The road through the tunnel under the IJ, put into use on 30-10-1968.

origins.name: IJburglaan
origins.en: The name fits into the Amsterdam tradition, in which artificial islands and peninsulas have a name that ends in -burg. The name IJburg makes it clear that the location is located in the IJmeer.

origins.name: IJdok
origins.en: Part of the Westerdokseiland.

origins.name: IJdoornlaan
origins.en: The off-dike polder, just east of the village of Durgerdam. Nature reserve, consisting of hay and reedlands.

origins.name: IJplein
origins.en: After the demolition of the sheds of the Amsterdam Dry Dock Company, a square was planned at the beginning of Meeuwenlaan. In advance, this was already called the IJpIein by the planners. The name IJplein was chosen, but no square was created, but three parallel streets, which now bear the same name: an example of incorrect naming.

origins.name: IJpromenade
origins.en: The IJ was formerly a branch of the North Sea. In the years 1865 to 1872 it was reclaimed by the construction of the North Sea Canal and in 1872 closed off from the North Sea by the IJdijk and the Orange Locks.

origins.name: IJsbaanpad
origins.en: Named after the ice rink on the IJsclubterrein, where the road leads to it.

origins.name: IJselmondestraat
origins.en: One of the South Holland islands.

origins.name: IJselstraat
origins.en: The IJssel River, a branch of the Rhine, runs from Westervoort to the IJsselmeer.

origins.name: IJslandtpad
origins.en: The eighteenth-century manor house on the Middenweg, later annexed to the still existing Frankendael. Demolished at the beginning of the nineteenth century.

origins.name: IJsselmeerstraat
origins.en: Named after the IJsselmeer

origins.name: IJzerhof
origins.en: River in Belgium.

origins.name: IJzerwerkerstraat
origins.en: Craftsman, iron and steel processor. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Ilpendammerstraat
origins.en: Village in Waterland on the North Holland Canal.

origins.name: Ilperveldstraat
origins.en: Nature reserve in the municipalities of Landsmeer and Waterland, a brackish water bog area.

origins.name: Imbos
origins.en: A hilltop between Arnhem and Laag Soeren, a natural monument since 1937, is part of the Veluwezoom National Park.

origins.name: Immanuel Kanthof
origins.en: German philosopher (1724-1804), professor at Königsberg (Germany), one of the greatest thinkers of his time. Wrote among other things 'Critique of Pure Reason'.

origins.name: Imogirituin
origins.en: The Indonesian city of Imogiri, located on a hill, seventeen kilometers southeast of Yogyakarta. The city is famous for its princely cemetery from the seventeenth century. In 1646, Sultan Agung was buried here for the first time.

origins.name: Imstenrade
origins.en: Old country house near Heerlen (Limburg).

origins.name: Inaristraat
origins.en: The Inari Lake, located in northern Finland against the Russian border.

origins.name: Ingelandenweg
origins.en: These are the landowners in the polder, who are elected to represent them in the polder council and vote on polder charges.

origins.name: Ingenhouszhof
origins.en: Jan lngenhousz (1730-1799), physicist, discoverer of the respiration of plants.

origins.name: Ingogostraat
origins.en: Place in Natal (South Africa) where the Boer general Joubert defeated the English in 1881 (First Boer War).

origins.name: Inlaagstraat
origins.en: A fill embankment is a embankment that has been built up because the original embankment is threatened by erosion from the waves and must be abandoned as the main water barrier. In this case, it refers to an earlier strip of land northwest of Sloterdijk.

origins.name: Insulindeweg
origins.en: The name given by Multatuli to the then Dutch East Indies, derived from the Latin 'insula' = island.

origins.name: Internetstraat
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Inzet
origins.en: Inzet, in the meaning of dedication.

origins.name: Ir. B. Bijvoetbrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after the architect Bernard Bijvoet (1889-1979), a representative of the 'New Building'. He designed, among other things, the Sanatorium Zonnestraal and the Hotel Gooiland in Hilversum. He was strongly involved in the construction of the nearby Muziektheater aan het Waterlooplein.

origins.name: Ir. Jakoba Mulderplein
origins.en: Jakoba Mulder (1900-1988), chief architect at the Urban Expansion Department and later head of the Urban Development Department of the Public Works Department in Amsterdam. Her most important work was the design of the Amsterdamse Bos.

origins.name: Irawan Soejonostraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1945), member of an Indonesian resistance group later named after him in Leiden.

origins.name: Isaäc Asscherpad
origins.en: Founder of the diamond cutting company Asscher in Tolstraat. He lived from 1843 to 1902.

origins.name: Isaac Gogelweg
origins.en: Isaac Jan Alexander Gogel (1765-1821), statesman and patriot. Founder of various types of taxes. In 1814 King William I consulted Gogel for his financial affairs.

origins.name: Isaac Titsinghkade
origins.en: Lawyer (1744-1812), envoy in China and Japan, also doctor, merchant, diplomat, philosopher and collector of Japonica. He worked for 32 years in the service of the VOC.

origins.name: Isaak Gosseshof
origins.en: Historian (1873-1940), professor in Groningen. Co-authored with N. Japikse the 'Handbook of the Political History of the Netherlands'.

origins.name: Isabella Richaardsstraat
origins.en: Isabella Johanna Alyda Richaards (1904-1985), first female parliamentarian (1963-1969) since the introduction of universal suffrage in Suriname in 1948. The Surinamese Women's Day falls on the date of her entry into parliament: May 14.

origins.name: Isarweg
origins.en: Side river of the Danube, flows along the German city of Munich.

origins.name: Iseoplantsoen
origins.en: The lake, Lago d'Iseo, located in the province of Lombardy in northern Italy.

origins.name: Isolatorweg
origins.en: Insulating material or insulating body, on which the electrical conductors rest.

origins.name: Israël Queridostraat
origins.en: Writer (1872-1932), originally diamond cutter. Many years literary contributor to the 'Algemeen Handelsblad'. Wrote several novels about Amsterdamian folk life.

origins.name: Ite Boeremastraat
origins.en: Ite Boerema (1902-1980), surgeon, from 1946 to 1973 professor of surgery at the University of Amsterdam. Built the hyperpressure tank in the Wilhelminagasthuis.

origins.name: Iwan Kantemanplein
origins.en: Iwan Hugo Kanteman (1908-1945), resistance fighter, born in Suriname. From 1940 until his arrest in 1944, worked for the air defense service in Amsterdam. From 1943, worked in an illegal association for the CPN and ensured the spread of the 'Truth'. After his arrest, transferred to various concentration camps. Died in Buchenwald from illness and exhaustion.

origins.name: J. Calsstraat
origins.en: Jozef Maria Laurens Theo Cals (1914-1971), politician, member of the KVP. Among other things, from 1952 to 1963 Minister of Education, Arts and Sciences. Was especially the man of the Mammoth Law, a law to regulate the entire primary education system. In 1965 he became prime minister. The cabinet he led fell in the 'night of Schmelzer' (November 22, 1966).

origins.name: J. de Koostraat
origins.en: Jan de Koo (1841-1909), initially a preacher, later an influential journalist. Founder of 'De Groene Amsterdammer'.

origins.name: J. Drijverweg
origins.en: Jan Drijver (1896-1963). Chief Director/Secretary of the Association for the Preservation of Nature Monuments and Secretary of the Dutch Association for the Protection of Birds.

origins.name: J. Dunnebierstraat
origins.en: Jacob Dunnebier (1904-1988), architect. Was responsible with architect Cees Ronstadt for the renovation of various buildings in the Old Town.

origins.name: J.A. dèr Mouwstraat
origins.en: Johan Andreas dèr Mouw (1862-1919), literary scholar and doctor of classical literature. Wrote under the pseudonym Adwaita. His poetry contains eastern mysticism in western forms.

origins.name: J.C. Breenstraat
origins.en: Johannes C. Breen (1865-1927), historian. City archivist of Amsterdam.

origins.name: J.C. Schröderstraat
origins.en: Jan Christiaan Schröder (1871-1938), journalist. For many years editor-in-chief of the daily newspaper 'De Telegraaf', he wrote, among other things, the column: Diary of an Amsterdammer.

origins.name: J.C. van Epenstraat
origins.en: Johannes Christiaan van Epen (1880-1960), architect of the Amsterdam school. Designed housing development on the Amsteldijk, Saffierstraat and Harmoniehof, among other things.

origins.name: J.F. Ankersmitstraat
origins.en: Johan Frederik Ankersmit (1871-1942), journalist. He debuted at 'De Telegraaf' and was associated with the daily newspaper 'Het Volk' from its founding in 1900 until 1937.

origins.name: J.F. Berghoefplantsoen
origins.en: Johannes Franciscus Berghoef (1903-1994), architect. From 1947 to 1969 professor at the Technical University in Delft. One of the most important representatives of the Delft School. Won the Amsterdam Town Hall Prize in 1939 in collaboration with J.J.M. Vegter.

origins.name: J.F. van Hengelstraat
origins.en: Johannes Frederik van Hengel (1887-1975), director of the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland' from 1919 to 1946. Numerous ancillary functions, including commissioner of the Amsterdam Harbor Company and member of the board of directors of the Amsterdam Maritime Museum.

origins.name: J.G. Suurhoffstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Gerardus Suurhoff (1905-1967), politician. He was, with the exception of the war years and a few months in 1946, a member of the Second Chamber of Representatives for the SDAP and later the PvdA from 1939 to 1952 and from 1959 to 1961. From 1949 to 1952 he was second chairman of the Dutch Federation of Trade Unions (NVV). Minister of Social Affairs (1952-1958) and Minister of Transport and Water Affairs (1965-1966).

origins.name: J.H. Hisgenpad
origins.en: Julius Heinrich Hisgen (1875-1957), well-known cricket player from the Dutch cricket team. One of the pioneers of Dutch cricket.

origins.name: J.H. van Heekpad
origins.en: Jan Herman van Heek (1873-1957), Twente textile manufacturer, who has made great contributions to the field of nature conservation and the protection of medieval buildings, especially in Gelderland and Utrecht.

origins.name: J.H. van Heekweg
origins.en: Jan Herman van Heek (1873-1957), Twente textile manufacturer, who has made great contributions to the field of nature conservation and the protection of medieval buildings, especially in Gelderland and Utrecht.

origins.name: J.J. Cremerplein
origins.en: Jacobus Johannes Cremer (1827-1880), literary scholar. Author of 'Factory Children' (a plea for child protection) and 'Overbetuwse Novels', among others.

origins.name: J.J. Cremerstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Johannes Cremer (1827-1880), literary scholar. Author of 'Factory Children' (a plea for child protection) and 'Overbetuwse Novels', among others.

origins.name: J.J. Viottastraat
origins.en: Joannes Josephus Viotta (1814-1859), physician in Amsterdam, of Italian origin, also composer of church music and folk songs on the texts of J.P. Heije.

origins.name: J.J.M. Vegterstraat
origins.en: Architect (1906-1982). One of the most important representatives of the Delft School won the competition for the Amsterdam town hall in 1939 in collaboration with J.F. Berghoef.

origins.name: J.M. den Uylstraat
origins.en: Johannes Marten (Joop) den Uyl (1919-1987), social democratic statesman. He was, among other things, alderman for Economic Affairs of Amsterdam, Minister of Economic Affairs in the Cals cabinet (1965-1966) and from 1967 parliamentary leader of the Labour Party in the House of Representatives, before becoming prime minister in 1973. From 1977 to 1981 he led his party in opposition. In the second Van Agt cabinet (1981-1982), he was Minister of Social Affairs and Employment.

origins.name: J.M. van der Meylaan
origins.en: Johan Melchior van der Mey (1878-1949), architect of the Amsterdam School. One of the founders of expressionism in architecture. Designed the Scheepvaarthuis among other things.

origins.name: J.P. Kloosstraat
origins.en: Jan Piet Kloos (1905-2001), architect. Designed many schools, hospitals and parent centers, such as on Schoenerstraat in Noord. Worked uncompromisingly in the spirit of New Building and functionalism.

origins.name: J.S. Ruppertstraat
origins.en: Johan Stephaan Ruppert (1877-1934), one of the leaders of the Amsterdam Christian Councils Federation and the Christian trade union movement.

origins.name: J.W. Siebbeleshof
origins.en: Lived from 1904 to 1985. He worked for many years to protect the interests of older residents in the Nieuwmarkt neighborhood. The arrival of the Center for the Elderly for people from the neighborhood is largely due to him.

origins.name: Jaagpad
origins.en: The name recalls the time of the tugboat, when the ship hunter pulled the ships through the water with his horse. Many waterways (tugways) had a tow path.

origins.name: Jaap Edenstraat
origins.en: Athlete (1873-1925). In 1894 and 1895 he was world champion cyclist. From 1896 to 1914 world champion speed skater in the 5000 m.

origins.name: Jaap Kunstbrug
origins.en: Jaap Kunst, (August 12, 1891 Groningen - died December 7, 1960, Amsterdam), Dutch ethnomusicologist, who was one of the founders of the modern age. Kunst began studying the violin at an early age and became seriously interested in the folk culture of the Netherlands. After obtaining a diploma in 1917 from the Rijksuniversiteit Groningen, he joined a string trio that toured through Dutch East Indies. Art continued to work for the government in Java (Indonesia) until the mid-1930s. There he collected and studied the indigenous music, especially that of the Javanese gamelan.

origins.name: Jaap Nunes Vazstraat
origins.en: In 1930, his growing reputation as an authority on Indonesian music brought him to be a musicologist for the Dutch government. He began making extensive excursions, collecting many musical instruments, recordings, books and photographs. In 1934, Kunst returned to the Netherlands and in 1936 he became curator of the Royal Institute of the Tropics in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Jaap Speyerstraat
origins.en: And began with one of the largest musicological collections in Europe.

origins.name: Jaargetijden
origins.en: The seasons. Nearby are the Winter, Spring, Summer and Autumn Streets. The street was previously named Schoolstraat by the municipality of Weesperkarspel. After the dissolution of that municipality, the name of the street had to be changed, because Amsterdam already had a Schoolstraat.

origins.name: Jac. P. Thijsseplein
origins.en: Jacobus P. Thijsse (1865-1945), teacher, later teacher. Known plant and animal scientist. Founded the Dutch Natural History Society together with Eli Heimans. Co-founder and secretary of the Association for the Preservation of Natural Monuments in the Netherlands. Also known as a publicist for 'Illustrated Flora of the Netherlands' and the Verkade albums.

origins.name: Jachthavenweg
origins.en: The road runs along the yacht harbors on the Nieuwe Meer.

origins.name: Jacob Bontiusplaats
origins.en: Physician in service of the VOC (1592-1631). Studied the flora and fauna in the area around Batavia (now Jakarta), the administrative Amsterdam-Centrum of the former colony of Dutch East Indies.

origins.name: Jacob Burggraafstraat
origins.en: Companion of shipbuilder Jan Witheyn, to whom the first shipyard was rented on the island of Wittenburg in 1656.

origins.name: Jacob Cabeliaustraat
origins.en: Watergeus from the Eighty Years' War. Fought for the capture of Den Briel (1572) and the defense of Alkmaar (1573).

origins.name: Jacob Catskade
origins.en: Jacob Cats (1577-1660), also known as Father Cats, poet and statesman, among other things, council pensionary of Holland and West Friesland under Frederick Henry. Gained great popularity with his didactic poetry.

origins.name: Jacob de Rijkhof
origins.en: Amsterdam grain merchant (1541-1584), who joined the Watergeuzen and participated in the capture of Den Briel in 1572. After that, he became commander of Veere.

origins.name: Jacob Frankhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), merchant traveler, born in Amsterdam, killed in Sobibor (Poland).

origins.name: Jacob Geelstraat
origins.en: Literary and philologist (1789-1862). Argued against the outdated art forms.

origins.name: Jacob Groenplantsoen
origins.en: Jacob Andries Groen jr. (1925-1987), historian. Wrote a lot about the history of Amsterdam, especially about Amsterdam-North. Known among other things for his book 'Rondom Volewijck en Tolhuis' and for his journalistic work for the daily newspaper 'De Noord-Amsterdammer'.

origins.name: Jacob Honigstraat
origins.en: Mayor of Zaandijk, founder of the Archaeological Society for the Zaanstreek. Before 1930, the name of this street was Meijerstraat. Since 1-8-1966, the street falls under Amsterdam.

origins.name: Jacob Husleystraat
origins.en: Jacob Otten Husley (1730-1795), member of an Amsterdam architectural family. Built Felix Meritis among other things.

origins.name: Jacob Krausstraat
origins.en: Hydrologist (1861-1951), minister of Waterstaat in 1905 and 1908. Led the implementation of port works in Chile.

origins.name: Jacob Krüsestraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1905-1944), born in Amsterdam, killed in the Oranienburg concentration camp. Krüse was affiliated with the illegal newspaper 'Trouw' and with the 'National Organization for Aid to Undergrounders' (the L.O.).

origins.name: Jacob Marisplein
origins.en: Painter (1837-1899), mainly painted landscapes and Amsterdam street scenes.

origins.name: Jacob Marisstraat
origins.en: Painter (1837-1899), mainly painted landscapes and Amsterdam street scenes.

origins.name: Jacob Melkmanstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1902-1943), by profession merchant traveler, born in Amsterdam, executed on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Jacob Obrechtplein
origins.en: Composer (1430-1505), worked abroad for many years, among other things as choir conductor. He composed a large number of masses and motets.

origins.name: Jacob Obrechtstraat
origins.en: Composer (1430-1505), worked abroad for many years, among other things as choir conductor. He composed a large number of masses and motets.

origins.name: Jacob Paffstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1915-1966), participated in the robbery of the Detention Center at the Amsterdam Weteringschans on April 30, 1944.

origins.name: Jacob Tilstraat
origins.en: Geuzen captains (1544-1584). Distinguished themselves in particular in the battle on the Zuiderzee in 1573 against Bossu.

origins.name: Jacob van Arteveldestraat
origins.en: Novel by the Flemish writer Hendrik Conscience (1812-1883). Jacob van Artevelde lived from around 1290 to 1345 and was a Flemish folk leader.

origins.name: Jacob van Lennepkade
origins.en: Prose writer (1802-1868), mainly of historical novels, including 'The Rose of Dekama' and 'Ferdinand Huyck'.

origins.name: Jacob van Lennepstraat
origins.en: Prose writer (1802-1868), mainly of historical novels, including 'The Rose of Dekama' and 'Ferdinand Huyck'.

origins.name: Jacob van Maerlantstraat
origins.en: Flemish priest (ca. 1235-ca. 1300), from the village of Maerlant near Den Briel, later municipal secretary of Damme. Main figure of the German poets of the thirteenth century. Especially his learned poems are known.

origins.name: Jacob van Wassenaar Obdamstraat
origins.en: Jacob baron of Wassenaar, lord of Obdam (1610-1665). Dutch lieutenant general, who flew his ship into the air in the Battle of Lowestoft during the Second English War.

origins.name: Jacob van Weesenbekestraat
origins.en: Secretary of William of Orange (1524-1575).

origins.name: Jacoba Mosselhof
origins.en: Jacoba Mossel sparked the discussion in the Dutch Protestant Union about the possibility of working as a religious teacher and as a preacher as a woman. She asked the executive board to allow women to enter the training as a religious teacher and this was allowed.

origins.name: Jacobus van Looystraat
origins.en: Literary and painter (1855-1930), known for his autobiographical novel cycle 'Jaapje-Jaap-Jacob'. He was a member of the editorial board of 'De Nieuwe Gids' for several years.

origins.name: Jacques Oppenheimstraat
origins.en: Jurist (1849-1924), professor at Groningen and Leiden in state and administrative law, later also in international law. In 1913 he was chairman of the State Commission for Equal Representation.

origins.name: Jacques Veltmanstraat
origins.en: Louis Jacques Veltman (1817-1907), actor. In addition to the popular 'marqué', the villain in the melodramas, he was also a talented actor in the classical genre.

origins.name: Jaddanbaikade
origins.en: Jaddanbai was an Indian classical composer who, in addition to composing, also had talent for singing, dancing, acting and film production.

origins.name: James Bradleystraat
origins.en: English astronomer (1693-1762). Member of the Royal Society, appointed in 1721 as 'Savilian professor of Astronomy' at Oxford and later as 'Astronomer Royal'. In 1728 he determined the speed of light at 301,000 km/sec, which was in the interest of shipping.

origins.name: James Cookstraat
origins.en: English explorer (1728-1779), among other things, discovered the east coast of Australia.

origins.name: James Rosskade
origins.en: James Clarke Ross (1800-1862), English polar explorer. Led the South Pole Expedition 1839-1843.

origins.name: James Wattstraat
origins.en: English physicist (1736-1819), inventor of the steam engine. The working capacity of an electrical current unit is named after him. The street previously bore the name Hans Lipperheijstraat (council decision, 1923).

origins.name: Jan Abelszstraat
origins.en: Guerrilla captain from the Eighty Years' War. Became famous for the battle for the Eems in 1568, he participated in the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Jan Beijerpad
origins.en: Jan (Johannes Hendrikus) Beijer (1944-1994), birdwatcher who often visited the Diemerzeedijk.

origins.name: Jan Bernardusstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a former resident or landowner. Before the annexation of 1896, the street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the same name.

origins.name: Jan Bongastraat
origins.en: Frisian grietman, member of the Union of the Nobles in 1566. Captain under Louis of Nassau. Died in 1580 against Rennenberg.

origins.name: Jan Boterenbroodstraat
origins.en: Architect (1886-1936) of the Amsterdam school. Designed, among other things, Huize Lydia on Roelof Hartplein and housing in Tuindorp Nieuwendam.

origins.name: Jan Bottemastraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1908-1944), played an important role in the care of undergrounders. Was commander of the strike team (K.P.) Amsterdam-North. Shot dead in Wormerveer.

origins.name: Jan C. de Voshof
origins.en: Jan Cornelis de Vos (1855-1931) actor and director, known by his colleagues as Jan C. For many years associated with the Association Het Nederlands Toneel. He was a leader for many young actors and actresses.

origins.name: Jan Celestraat
origins.en: Johannes Cele (1347-1417), educational figure and school organizer. Rector of the famous Zwolle city school, which, together with that of Deventer, laid the foundation for early Dutch humanism.

origins.name: Jan Cupidohof
origins.en: The captain of the rescue boat Brandaris (1869-1938). Under his leadership, 261 shipwrecked people were saved.

origins.name: Jan de Greefstraat
origins.en: Architect (1784-1834), among others of the warehouses on the Entrepotdok.

origins.name: Jan de Jonghkade
origins.en: Gerrit Jan de Jongh (1845-1917), director of Municipal Works Rotterdam. One of the founders of modern Rotterdam. Under his leadership, an electricity network, a water supply and a modern sewerage system were built. He became especially well-known for his involvement in urban development and the expansion of the Rotterdam harbors.

origins.name: Jan de Jonghstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1912-1945), born in Amsterdam, shot dead there.

origins.name: Jan de Louterpad
origins.en: Jurist (1847-1932), professor in Amsterdam and Utrecht. Taught international law and public law.

origins.name: Jan de Louterstraat
origins.en: Jurist (1847-1932), professor in Amsterdam and Utrecht. Taught international law and public law.

origins.name: Jan den Haenstraat
origins.en: One of the sea heroes in the Battle of Solebay in 1672. Died in 1676 in Palermo against the French.

origins.name: Jan Eisenloeffelstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Johannes Wigbold (1876-1957), goldsmith, established his own workshop in 1911. Representative of Dutch Art Nouveau and Art Deco.

origins.name: Jan Evertsenstraat
origins.en: Johan Evertsen (1600-1666), belonging to a Zeelandish family of sea heroes. Participated as an admiral in several naval battles, including the Battle of Duins (1639). Killed in the Second English War.

origins.name: Jan Goeverneurhof
origins.en: Literary (1809-1889), best known as a children's poet. Wrote under the pseudonym Jan de Rijmer. Founder and editor of the family publication 'De Huisvriend' for many years.

origins.name: Jan Goldschmedingstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1921-1944), involved in the organization of the illegal newspaper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Jan Hanzenstraat
origins.en: A landowner, who bought a piece of land in 1564 on the condition that a path along it be maintained, and that is why it was called the Jan Hanzenpad. The path was partly in Nieuwer-Amstel and ran from the Singel to the Kostverlorenwetering. Later, the remains bore the names Jan Hanzenstraat and Jan Hanzenkade. The quay was renamed Agatha Dekenstraat in 1904.

origins.name: Jan Haringstraat
origins.en: Watergeus from Hoorn. Defended the Diemerzeedijk between IJ and Diemermeer (Watergraafsmeer) for a while in 1573 only against the Spanish.

origins.name: Jan Janzenstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed in The Hague.

origins.name: Jan Kiststraat
origins.en: Captain (died in 1740), sailed on a transport ship in service of the Dutch East India Company (VOC).

origins.name: Jan Lelimanhof
origins.en: Architect (1829-1910), architect of among others 'Arti et Amicitiae', the Prinsengracht hospital, several bakeries and a number of workers' housing (including in the Valckenierstraat).

origins.name: Jan Lievensstraat
origins.en: Painter (1607-1674), pupil of Rembrandt. He provided wall paintings in the town hall on the Dam, among other things.

origins.name: Jan Ligthartstraat
origins.en: Gerard Jan Ligthart (1859-1916), educator. Together with H. Scheepstra, he wrote the previously very well-known reading books for schoolchildren, 'Ot and Sien'.

origins.name: Jan Luijkenstraat
origins.en: Poet and graphic artist (1649-1712), especially popular through 'Het menselijk bedrijf', which he made together with his brother Caspar. By council decision in 1895 the street name was extended a little, which however was repealed again by council decision in 1912.

origins.name: Jan Maijenstraat
origins.en: The Dutch sea captain Jan Cornelisz May, who discovered the Jan Mayeneiland, named after him, between Spitsbergen and Iceland in 1611.

origins.name: Jan Mankesstraat
origins.en: Painter and engraver (1889-1920), mainly of animals.

origins.name: Jan Mensplein
origins.en: Jan Mens (Amsterdam, September 18, 1897 – Amsterdam, October 31, 1967) was a Dutch writer. In 1935 he came into contact with former schoolteacher Theo Thijssen who provided him with recommendations and feedback. In 1938 he won the Komso First Prize for his manuscript People Without Money with which he broke through. In the early sixties he was the best-selling writer in the Netherlands, known for the work The little truth. This work gives an image of the life of the 'ordinary' Amsterdammer.

origins.name: Jan Moretuspad
origins.en: Jan Moretus (1543-1610) was the son-in-law of Christoffel Plantijn and worked with him in his bookstore for a long period of time. After the death of Christoffel Plantijn, Jan Moretus continued the bookstore and associated printing house until his death in 1610.

origins.name: Jan Muschstraat
origins.en: Johannes Petrus Musch (1875-1960), actor, brilliant Shakespeare and Vondel interpreter. Played a long series of major roles (Lucifer, The Wise Cat, Nathan the Wise, Molière's The Cheat). Celebrated his 60th theater anniversary in 1952.

origins.name: Jan Nautahof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1917-1944), born in Almelo, killed in Camp Vught. Nauta worked for the illegal newspaper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Jan Olphert Vaillantlaan
origins.en: Navy officer (1751-1800) in service of the Admiralty of Amsterdam. Expert in the field of length determination at sea through lunar distances. In 1784, he published 'Treatise on the Art of Navigation'.

origins.name: Jan Oudegeeststraat
origins.en: One of the founders of the Dutch trade union movement (1870-1950). from 1909 to 1919 chairman of the NVV and from 1919 to 1926 secretary of the International Federation of Trade Unions. Also a member of the Amsterdam municipal council and of the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors.

origins.name: Jan Peppinkstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1942), was involved in many illegal activities. Led the espionage group 'Nederland Vrij'.

origins.name: Jan Pieter Heijestraat
origins.en: Amsterdam physician and poet (1809-1876). Founded the Association for Nursing in 1844. He was also director of Toonkunst for thirty years and promoted folk singing. He wrote the popular children's songs 'De Zilvervloot', 'Kabels los' and 'Vlaggelied'.

origins.name: Jan Postmahof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1895-1944), active in the labor movement. Born in Amsterdam and executed as a leader of the illegal communist party in Vught.

origins.name: Jan Poytstraat
origins.en: Jan Poyt (birth and death year unknown), designer in the 16th century) is the designer of the distinctive tower of Ransdorp. This tower dates back to the early sixteenth century Simon van Woerden (1902-1998) designed the Bethel Church around 1958. For this neighborhood, the category names of Dutch architects who have been involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-North have been chosen.

origins.name: Jan Puntstraat
origins.en: Actor from the eighteenth century, highly valued at the time, later fiercely criticized. Point was also a skilled engraver.

origins.name: Jan Rebelstraat
origins.en: Jan Rebel was an island in the former IJ. The name appears on old maps. How the island got its name is unknown.

origins.name: Jan Ringelstraat
origins.en: The water gush from Oostzaan that in 1576 sailed through the chain in the port of Muiden, so that Sonoy could enter with his fleet.

origins.name: Jan Schaeferbrug
origins.en: Johannes Lodewijk Nicolaas Schaefer (1940-1994), politician for the Labour Party. He was a member of the House of Representatives from 1971, was state secretary for urban renewal at the Ministry of Housing and Spatial Planning in the Den Uyl Cabinet from 1973 to 1977, and was a city councillor (housing affairs, urban renewal, building and housing supervision, land management) in Amsterdam from 1978 to 1986. From him come the winged words: "You can't live in nonsense." Provided a huge impetus to urban renewal and housing production in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Jan Schaeferpad
origins.en: Johannes Lodewijk Nicolaas Schaefer (1940-1994), politician for the Labour Party. Served in the House of Representatives from 1971. Was state secretary for urban renewal at the Ministry of Housing and Spatial Planning in the Den Uyl Cabinet from 1973 to 1977, and from 1978 to 1986 alderman (housing affairs, urban renewal, building and housing supervision, land management) in Amsterdam. From him come the winged words: "You can't live in nonsense." Provided a huge impetus to urban renewal and housing production in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Jan Sluijtersstraat
origins.en: Painter (1881-1957), developed a completely unique style in his portraits, still lifes and genre pieces.

origins.name: Jan Smitstraat
origins.en: Johannes Wilhelmus Smit (1851-1940), founder of the Roman Catholic People's Federation. Worked mainly among the workers on the Eastern Islands.

origins.name: Jan Somerhof
origins.en: Jan Egbert W.H. Somer (1905-1945), resistance fighter, by profession printer. He printed the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool' for a long time. Born in Hoorn and executed on April 13, 1945 in Zutphen.

origins.name: Jan Springerhof
origins.en: Jan L. Springer (1850-1915), architect, who built the Stadsschouwburg together with J.B. Springer and A.L. van Gendt (completed 1894). He was also director of the Hague Academy of Fine Arts.

origins.name: Jan Swammerdambrug
origins.en: Jan Swammerdam (1637-1680), anatomist and physicist. Conducted important microscopic research, preserved in his 'Bible of Nature'.

origins.name: Jan Theuniszhof
origins.en: Language scholar (1569-1638), specializing in Arabic.

origins.name: Jan Thoméepad
origins.en: Doctor and football pioneer known far beyond the border (1886-1954). Until his death, medical caregiver of the Dutch national football team.

origins.name: Jan Tooropstraat
origins.en: Painter and draftsman (1858-1928). Developed a completely unique style with a lot of symbolism, later filled with religious mood. Fresco in the Beurs aan het Damrak.

origins.name: Jan van Beersstraat
origins.en: Flemish literary figure (1821-1888), poet of Flemish folk life.

origins.name: Jan van Boendalestraat
origins.en: Flemish poet (circa 1280-circa 1365). City secretary of Antwerp. Famous learned poet.

origins.name: Jan van der Neuthof
origins.en: Jan Tijmen van der Neut (1921-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, killed in the prison camp Siegburg (Germany). In 1941 he was arrested by the occupiers for distributing the illegal newspaper 'Vrij Nederland'.

origins.name: Jan van Duivenvoordestraat
origins.en: Lord of Warmond (1547-1610), fought on the side of the Water Geuzen, defeated the Spanish in the port of Cadiz (1596).

origins.name: Jan van Eijckstraat
origins.en: South Dutch painter (1386-1440). Court painter of Jan van Beyeren, later of Philip of Burgundy. He applied oil paint in a completely new way for that time.

origins.name: Jan van Galenstraat
origins.en: Admiral (1604-1653). Died in the battle of Livorno against the English.

origins.name: Jan van Goyenkade
origins.en: Painter (1595-1635), mainly landscape painter.

origins.name: Jan van Houthof
origins.en: Literary (1542-1609), first scientific archivist. Wrote the first Dutch alexandrines.

origins.name: Jan van Riebeekstraat
origins.en: Jan Anthonie van Riebeeck or Riebeek (1618-1708), founded the Cape Colony at Cape de Goede Hoop in 1652, when he was in service of the Dutch East India Company.

origins.name: Jan van Schaffelaarplantsoen
origins.en: Rider chief in the battle between Hoeksen and Kabeljauwen, jumped from the tower of Barneveld for the survival of his men. Main character from 'De Schaapherder', a historical novel by J.F. Oltmans.

origins.name: Jan van Zutphenplantsoen
origins.en: Amsterdam diamond cutter (1863-1958), founded in 1894 with Henri Polak the General Dutch Diamond Cutters' Association (ANDB). Later carried out important work in the field of social humanitarianism.

origins.name: Jan van Zutphenstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam diamond cutter (1863-1958), founded in 1894 with Henri Polak the General Dutch Diamond Cutters' Association (ANDB). Later carried out important work in the field of social humanitarianism.

origins.name: Jan Vethstraat
origins.en: Painter and draftsman (1864-1925), also art historian. Worked to preserve the beauty of the Amsterdam cityscape.

origins.name: Jan Voermanstraat
origins.en: Painter of landscapes and flowers (1857-1944). Managed many Verkade albums.

origins.name: Jan Vrijmanstraat
origins.en: Jan Hulsebos (1925-1997), journalist and filmmaker. Changed his name to Jan Vrijman during World War II. Involved in the illegal newspaper 'De Waarheid'. Co-founder and director of the International Documentary Festival Amsterdam (IDFA).

origins.name: Jan Vroegopsingel
origins.en: Amsterdam chief police officer (1877-1946), co-founder and from 1917 to 1946 chairman of the Federation of Allotment Gardeners.

origins.name: Jan Willem Brouwersstraat
origins.en: Joannes Wilhelmus Brouwers (1831-1893), Roman Catholic clergyman, publicist and writer. From 1863-1870 co-editor of the daily newspaper 'De Tijd', from 1870 pastor at Bovenkerk.

origins.name: Jan Wilsbrug
origins.en: is named after Jan Wils (1891-1972). He was the architect of the Olympic Stadium and the two Citroën buildings on Stadionplein. He also designed the Citytheater on Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen

origins.name: Jan Witheijnstraat
origins.en: Shipbuilder (1610-1662). In 1656 he was the first to be leased a shipyard on the island of Wittenburg.

origins.name: Jan Zijvertszstraat
origins.en: Guzen captain, known for the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Jan Zwanenburghof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1921-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Janna van der Weglaan
origins.en: Janna Rinske van der Weg (1893-1974), skater. Was the first woman ever to ride the Elfstedentocht in 1917, and the second in the history of the event to participate. In her daily life, she was a maid.

origins.name: Janusz Korczakstraat
origins.en: Polish-Jewish doctor (1878-1942), pedagogue, children's book writer and director of an orphanage. On August 6, 1942, he was deported with two hundred children from the orphanage to the Treblinka extermination camp and there murdered together with the children.

origins.name: Jarasingel
origins.en: Victor Jara (1938-1973), Chilean singer. On international tours he represented the voice of the opposition. For Chilean television he made programs about the horrors of the civil war and fascism. In 1973 he was murdered by the junta.

origins.name: Jarmuiden
origins.en: The English port town of Yarmouth, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Jasmijnstraat
origins.en: Named after the jasmine, a shrub.

origins.name: Jasonstraat
origins.en: Figure from Greek mythology, leader of the Argonauts around 1350 BC.

origins.name: Jasper Leijnsenstraat
origins.en: The heroic sailor during a naval battle against the Spanish at Reimerswaal in 1574.

origins.name: Jasper Warnerstraat
origins.en: Pioneer of the sport of football (1870-1924), became president of the Dutch Football Association in 1897 as successor to Pim Mulier.

origins.name: Javakade
origins.en: The island, one of the large Sunda islands (Indonesia). For years, the establishments of the Dutch Shipping Company were located on the quay, which had a large share of sea transport to the former Dutch East Indies in its hands.

origins.name: Javaplantsoen
origins.en: The island, one of the large Sunda islands (Indonesia). For years, the establishments of the Dutch Shipping Company were located on the quay, which had a large share of sea transport to the former Dutch East Indies in its hands.

origins.name: Javaplein
origins.en: The island, one of the large Sunda islands (Indonesia). For years, the establishments of the Dutch Shipping Company were located on the quay, which had a large share of sea transport to the former Dutch East Indies in its hands.

origins.name: Javastraat
origins.en: The island, one of the large Sunda islands (Indonesia). For years, the establishments of the Dutch Shipping Company were located on the quay, which had a large share of sea transport to the former Dutch East Indies in its hands.

origins.name: Jean Desmetstraat
origins.en: Film distributor and cinema owner (1875-1956). Began as a fair and travel cinema operator. By bringing foreign film productions to be screened in the Netherlands, he made a substantial contribution to the radical changes that took place in the film industry between 1907 and 1916.

origins.name: Jekerstraat
origins.en: River, which flows into the Maas near Maastricht.

origins.name: Jelle Posthumapad
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed in 1943 in Scheveningen. He was active in the distribution of the illegal newspaper 'De Waarheid'.

origins.name: Jeltje de Bosch Kemperpad
origins.en: Freule de Bosch Kemper (1836 to 1916). She was the driving force behind several associations that organized nursing courses. Co-founder of the Tesselschade Association. She promoted, among other things, the establishment of the Amsterdam Housekeeping School and the drawing school for girls.

origins.name: Jennerstraat
origins.en: Edward Jenner (1749-1823), English physician. Improved the possibility of smallpox vaccination as a means of combating smallpox so that it became mass-useable. The name of the street was previously established as Emmalaan (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1904).

origins.name: Jephtastraat
origins.en: Dramatic play by Vondel, dating from 1659. By council decision in 1948, the street name was extended in a southerly direction, but that part was added to Gulden Winckelplantsoen on 18-2-1970.

origins.name: Jeroenensteeg
origins.en: Probably named after the former Sint Jeroenentoren, one of the small towers on the city wall of the fifteenth century, where the street led. Jeroen was pastor of Noordwijk and was killed by the Normans in the ninth century. Later he was canonized.

origins.name: Jisperveldstraat
origins.en: Nature reserve near the North Holland town of Jisp. Botanically important bog area.

origins.name: Joan Melchior Kemperstraat
origins.en: Jurist (1776-1824), professor in Amsterdam and Leiden. Argued against the regency and advocated for a constitutional form of government.

origins.name: Joan Muyskenweg
origins.en: Amsterdam industrial magnate (1866-1928), director of Werkspoor. Had an important stake in the development of this company.

origins.name: Joannes de Swaefhof
origins.en: Seventeenth-century schoolmaster from Middelburg. His 'treatise on education' is considered the first complete pedagogy published in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Joannes Reddingiusstraat
origins.en: Poet (1873-1944), belonged to the flowering of the Eighties.

origins.name: Jodenbreestraat
origins.en: This street, built on part of the Sint Antoniesdijk, was part of the Sint Antoniesbreestraat until the second half of the seventeenth century. At that time, the Jewish population began to increase significantly and this part of the Breestraat became the main street of the 'Jewish Quarter'. Since then, the name Jodenbreestraat has become popular. After the Jewish inhabitants were deported by the occupiers during the war years 1940-1945 and a large part of the buildings on the uneven side were demolished (and set on fire in the fireplaces), the rest of that street facade was moved in the 1960s.

origins.name: Joes Kloppenburgbrug
origins.en: Joes Kloppenburg (1970- 1996) was killed on August 17, 1996 by Richard L., when he intervened in a street fight in the Voetboogsteeg with the words 'Cut it out!'. This bridge is relatively close to the place where he died and is intended as a symbol against senseless violence.

origins.name: Joh.M. Coenenstraat
origins.en: Johannes Meinardus Coenen (1825-1899), visual artist. Composed choral works, ballets and operas. Conducted concerts at Felix Meritis and at the Palace of Public Enterprise.

origins.name: Johan Braakensiekhof
origins.en: Illustrator and caricaturist (1858-1940). Provided a weekly illustration in the 'Groene Amsterdammer' for many years. Also illustrator of children's books.

origins.name: Johan Broedeletstraat
origins.en: Novel and playwright (1877-1947). Also reviewer of 'De Haagse Post'.

origins.name: Johan Coltermanpad
origins.en: Guerrilla captain from the Eighty Years' War, representative of the Prince of Orange. Fought at Enkhuizen and Haarlem in 1572.

origins.name: Johan Cruijff Boulevard
origins.en: Johan Cruijff born April 25, 1947 in Amsterdam / died March 24, 2016 in Barcelona. Striker Ajax 1964-1973

origins.name: Johan de Meesterstraat
origins.en: Literary (1860-1931), novelist, editor of 'De Nieuwe Gids' and contributor to the 'Nieuwe Rotterdamse Courant'.

origins.name: Johan Greivestraat
origins.en: Johan Conrad Greive (Amsterdam, April 2, 1837 - there, May 14, 1891) was a Dutch visual artist, best known for his landscapes in a realistic style. During his career, he was a member of the artists' association Arti et Amicitiae and taught at the Rijksakademie. Works by him can be seen, among other things, in the Rijksmuseum and Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Johan Herman Doornstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1910-1944), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Ede.

origins.name: Johan Hofmanstraat
origins.en: Probably named after J. Hofman, he was chairman of the Nederlandsche Christelijke Typografen Bond (NCTB). In addition, he was editor of the organ of the NCTB. He wrote several articles in Eltheto and Stemmen des Tijds. In addition, the Memorial Book for the anniversary of the NCTB was written by him. In 1945, Hofman became second chairman of the reorganized CNV board.

origins.name: Johan Huijsenstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1877-1959), versatile portrait photographer, also made cityscapes.

origins.name: Johan Huizingalaan
origins.en: Historian (1874-1945), professor at Groningen and Leiden. Has many publications to his name, including 'Autumn of the Middle Ages'.

origins.name: Johan Jongkindstraat
origins.en: Landscape painter and engraver (1819-1891), lived most of his life in France. Representative of Impressionism.

origins.name: Johan Kernstraat
origins.en: Linguist (1833-1917), professor at Leiden in Sanskrit. Expert in Indian and Malay-Polynesian languages and literature.

origins.name: Johan Limpersstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1915-1944), by profession sculptor (Prix de Rôme 1940), born in Haarlem, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Johan Lulofsstraat
origins.en: Professor of astronomy, mathematics and philosophy at Leiden (1711-1768). Expert in the field of the timekeeping method and as such advisor of the States of Holland and the General States. In 1750 his 'Introduction to a natural and mathematical view of the earth's orbit' appeared.

origins.name: Johan Ramaerstraat
origins.en: Hydrologist (1852-1932), builder of the Merwedekanaal.

origins.name: Johan Rijnjastraat
origins.en: Architect (1870-1941), designed, among other things, the first buildings in Noord between 1911 and 1915.

origins.name: Johan Schamppad
origins.en: Johan Frederik Jeremias Schamp (1899-1943), resistance fighter. He was active in the distribution of the illegal newspaper 'Vrij Nederland'. Died after being abused by the occupiers in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Johan Schippersplantsoen
origins.en: Johan Godefridus Schippers (1923-1945), resistance fighter, born and executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Johan van der Keukenstraat
origins.en: Photographer and filmmaker (1938-2001), followed a film course in Paris and gained great fame in the Netherlands at a young age with his photo book 'We are 17'. From the 1960s onwards, he mainly developed as a filmmaker. He made dozens of short and longer films for which he received many awards, nationally and internationally.

origins.name: Johan van Hasseltkade
origins.en: Lived from 1850 to 1916, was director of Public Works 1900-1907, before that director of the Waterworks.

origins.name: Johan van Hasseltweg
origins.en: Lived from 1850 to 1916, was director of Public Works 1900-1907, before that director of the Waterworks.

origins.name: Johan van Kuyckstraat
origins.en: Guzen captain, who fought the Spanish in Vlissingen in 1572.

origins.name: Johann Keplerstraat
origins.en: Bohemian astronomer (1571-1630), one of the founders of modern astronomy. He discovered the laws that determine the movement of the planets. Predecessor of Newton.

origins.name: Johann Siegerstraat
origins.en: Johann Gerhard Wilhelm Sieger (1856-1942), founder of the Amsterdam Chinine Factory.

origins.name: Johanna Naberstraat
origins.en: Feminist (1859-1941), co-founder of the International Archive for the Women's Movement. Secretary of the Association for Women's Suffrage, board member of the World Federation for Women's Suffrage and member of the Amsterdam municipal council. In addition to studies on feminism, she wrote historical publications.

origins.name: Johanna Schouten-Elsenhoutstraat
origins.en: Johanna Isidoro Eugenia Schouten-Elsenhout (1910-1992) was a Surinamese poet.

origins.name: Johanna Westerdijkstraat
origins.en: Botanist (1883-1961), since 1906 director of the phytopathological laboratory Willie Commelin Scholten in Amsterdam. In 1917 she was appointed professor, as the first woman in the Netherlands. The universities of Uppsala and Giessen conferred honorary doctorates on her.

origins.name: Johannes de Bekahof
origins.en: A chronicler from the fourteenth century, wrote among other things the 'Great Bishop's Chronicle of Utrecht'.

origins.name: Johannes Hilverdinkstraat
origins.en: Painter (1813-1902). Painted mainly landscapes.

origins.name: Johannes J. Glasweg
origins.en: Johannes Jacob Glas (1917-1942), resistance fighter. Maintained the connection between the Truth resistance groups in companies in Amsterdam-North, manufactured explosives and had a stake in the February Strike (1941). He was arrested in 1941 and executed on November 19, 1942 in Soesterberg.

origins.name: Johannes Jelgerhuishof
origins.en: Actor, cartoonist and painter (1770-1836). Made a name for himself as a character actor.

origins.name: Johannes Meewisstraat
origins.en: Johannes Adriaan Meewis (1905-1948), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died as a result of imprisonment in Davos.

origins.name: Johannes Poststraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1944), by profession farmer, born in Hoogeveen. Played a leading role in the resistance, especially in the national strike groups. Was executed in Bloemendaal in 1944 after a failed robbery of the Prison House in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Johannes van der Steurstraat
origins.en: Philanthropist (1865-1945), leader of an orphanage for children in Magelang (Indonesia) and fighter for child protection in former Dutch East Indies. Generally known as 'Pa van der Steur'.

origins.name: Johannes van der Waalsstraat
origins.en: Previously Van der Waalsstraat. Physicist (1837-1923), professor in Amsterdam. Specialized in the properties of gases. Improved the Law of Boyle-Gay-Lussac. In 1910 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics. The name change occurred in 1955 due to confusion with the Waalstraat in the Rivierenbuurt.

origins.name: Johannes van Meurshof
origins.en: Historian (1579-1639), professor of history and Greek at Leiden. Wrote important historical works about the Netherlands and Denmark.

origins.name: Johannes Verhulststraat
origins.en: Composer and conductor (1816-1891), wrote masses, overtures and songs. Conductor of the Caecilea concerts and of Felix Meritis. Around 1870 the undisputed leader of the music scene in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Johannes Vermeerplein
origins.en: Painter (1632-1675), mainly painted landscapes and interiors.

origins.name: Johannes Vermeerstraat
origins.en: Painter (1632-1675), mainly painted landscapes and interiors.

origins.name: Johannes Worpstraat
origins.en: Organist and composer (1821-1891), author of the study work 'Music Theory'.

origins.name: Johannis de Rijkestraat
origins.en: Hydrologist (1842-1913). Worked in 1865 as an overseer during the construction of the Oranjesluizen near Schellingwoude, and went to Japan in 1872. Improved harbors and large waterworks in the national service there. Was a kind of state secretary at the Japanese Ministry of Transport and Water Works from 1891-1903. Was knighted for his work in the Netherlands and Japan.

origins.name: John Blankensteinstraat
origins.en: Football referee (1949-2006). Was one of the few openly gay people in the football world and fought for gay emancipation.

origins.name: John Campbellstraat
origins.en: Eighteenth-century English captain, commander of the ship Chatham. Designed the sextant in 1757, a geometric instrument for determining position at sea.

origins.name: John Coltranestraat
origins.en: William John Coltrane (1926-1967), American jazz saxophonist. Inspired by Indian and Arabic music.

origins.name: John Fernhouthof
origins.en: Photographer, cameraman and director (1913-1987), trained by cineaste Joris Ivens. Like Ivens, he also made a number of left-wing engaged films. His most famous film is 'Sky over Holland' (1967), in which he shows the relationship between Dutch art and the Dutch landscape.

origins.name: John Franklinstraat
origins.en: English naval officer (1786-1847). He investigated the northwest passage, but the expedition sank in the polar ice.

origins.name: John Hadleystraat
origins.en: English natural and mathematical (1682-1744). Inventor of the angle measuring instrument the octant, with which the location on the sea could be determined.

origins.name: John Lockehof
origins.en: English philosopher (1632-1704), founder of a new pedagogy. He was a precursor of Kant.

origins.name: John M. Keynesplein
origins.en: John Maynard Keynes (1883-1946), British economist. Known for his book 'The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money', in which he argues that the government should have an active role in the economy and should counteract economic stagnation through investments. His book is often seen as the foundation of contemporary macroeconomics.

origins.name: John Motleyhof
origins.en: John Lothrop Motley (1814-1877), American historian of the Netherlands, wrote among other things 'The rise of the Dutch Republic' (1856) and 'Life and death of John of Barneveld' (1875).

origins.name: John Napierstraat
origins.en: Scottish scholar (1550-1617), inventor of the principle of calculating with logarithms and thus paving the way for modern astronomy. His invention was of great importance to shipping.

origins.name: Joke Smitstraat
origins.en: Advocate of the women's emancipation movement (1933-1981), reviewer and publicist. Founder of the movement 'Man Woman Society' and member of the Emancipation Commission. From 1970 to 1971 she served on the Amsterdam municipal council for the PvdA. Upper idea for her own political party for women.

origins.name: Jolicoeurstraat
origins.en: One of the leaders of the uprising of the enslaved Surinamese. The runaway enslaved people, also known as marrons, waged a guerrilla war against their oppressors. They plundered the plantations and thus inflicted heavy blows on the economy

origins.name: Jollenpad
origins.en: A jol is a small keelboat.

origins.name: Jonagoldstraat
origins.en: Apple variety from the United States, known for its good taste and similar storage possibilities.

origins.name: Jonas Daniël Meijerplein
origins.en: Secretary of the Commission for the Composition of the Constitution of 1813 (1780-1834). The square was created by filling in parts of the Houtgracht and the Muidergracht. The name was given to this square between the synagogues, because J.D. Meijer was the designer of the concordat between the two Jewish communities as a peace founder in 1810.

origins.name: Jonathanhof
origins.en: Apple, also known as the Ulster Seedling. Is the progenitor of the Jonagold and originates from the United States.

origins.name: Joop Eijlstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1896-1941), by profession warehouse clerk, born in Amsterdam, executed in The Hague.

origins.name: Joop Gerritzestraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1913-1942), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Soest.

origins.name: Joop IJisbergstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1900-1942), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Soest.

origins.name: Joop van Weezelhof
origins.en: Joseph Jacques van Weezel, Resistance fighter (1909-1945), active in the CPN from 1930. In 1941 he was arrested by the Nazis on suspicion of organizing the February Uprising. In 1945 he died in concentration camp Dachau.

origins.name: Joos Banckersplantsoen
origins.en: Admiral of the Fleet (1599-1647). Had a share in the conquest of the Silver Fleet under Piet Hein and in the battle of Duins under Cornelis Tromp.

origins.name: Joos Banckersweg
