origins.en: Admiral of the Fleet (1599-1647). Had a share in the conquest of the Silver Fleet under Piet Hein and in the battle of Duins under Cornelis Tromp.

origins.name: Joos de Moorstraat
origins.en: Vice-admiral of Zeeland (1548-1618), known from the Eighty Years' War. He fought against the Dunkirk corsairs.

origins.name: Joost Bilhamerstraat
origins.en: Master builder (1541-1590), also land surveyor and cartographer. Among other things, he is the architect of the tower of the Old Church. His map of 1575 is one of the oldest known maps of Holland.

origins.name: Joris Ivensplein
origins.en: Filmmaker (1898-1989), one of the most important documentary filmmakers in film history. He became known for avant-garde documentaries such as 'The Bridge' (1928) and 'Rain' (1929), in which he experimented with movement and rhythm. Later, he became increasingly interested in social issues and became a convinced communist. He made films commissioned by various communist regimes. Due to his films about the police actions in Indonesia, he was persona non grata in the Netherlands. He received numerous awards for his films.

origins.name: Joris Ivensstraat
origins.en: Filmmaker (1898-1989), one of the most important documentary filmmakers in film history. He became known for avant-garde documentaries such as 'The Bridge' (1928) and 'Rain' (1929), in which he experimented with movement and rhythm. Later, he became increasingly interested in social issues and became a convinced communist. He made films commissioned by various communist regimes. Due to his films about the police actions in Indonesia, he was persona non grata in the Netherlands. He received numerous awards for his films.

origins.name: Joris van Andringastraat
origins.en: Seventeenth-century naval commander, died in 1676. Secretary of Admiral Michiel de Ruijter.

origins.name: Joris van den Berghweg
origins.en: Sports journalist (1882-1953), in particular in the field of cycling.

origins.name: Joseph Haydnpad
origins.en: Joseph Haydn (1732 - 1809) Austrian composer

origins.name: Joseph Scaligerstraat
origins.en: Joseph Justus Scaliger (1540-1609), classical philologist and professor in Geneva. Fled as a Huguenot after the Night of the Barbeque to Holland, then became a professor in Leiden. Master of Hugo de Groot. Founder of the Leiden philological school.

origins.name: Joseph Schumpeterstraat
origins.en: Joseph Alois Schumpeter (1883-1950), Austrian economist. Fled to America due to the rise of the Nazis. Known for his theory of 'creative destruction': old ways of working and old structures are constantly replaced by new ones.

origins.name: Josephus Jittastraat
origins.en: Abraham Carel Josephus Jitta (1887-1958) was a Dutch jurist and professor at Delft University of Applied Sciences.

origins.name: Joubertstraat
origins.en: Petrus Joubert (1831-1900), supreme commander of the Farmers in the Transvaal Freedom Wars.

origins.name: Jouke Zietsmastraat
origins.en: Jouke Zietsma (1893-1962) was involved with Tuindorp Nieuwendam. This garden village is a highlight of the rural variant of the Amsterdam School. For this neighborhood, the category names of Dutch architects who have been involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-North have been chosen.

origins.name: Jozef Israëlskade
origins.en: Painter (1824-1911), student of J.W. Pieneman and J.H. Kruseman. Became known for his socially concerned scenes, including those from the lives of poor fishermen.

origins.name: Juliana van Stolbergstraat
origins.en: Wife of Willem van Nassau (1506-1580), mother of Prince Willem of Orange. Princess Juliana is named after her.

origins.name: Julianaplein
origins.en: Juliana Louise Emma Marie Wilhelmina, born April 30, 1909, married in 1937 to Prince Bernhard von Lippe-Biesterfeld, from 1948 to 1980 queen of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

origins.name: Julius Pergerstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1840-1924), contemporary of Pieter Oosterhuis. Photographed engineering works, including bridges and railways, just like Oosterhuis.

origins.name: Jungfrau
origins.en: Mountain peak in Switzerland, 4158 meters high.

origins.name: Jupiterstraat
origins.en: The largest planet in our solar system.

origins.name: Justus Halbertsmastraat
origins.en: Frisian writer, philologist and historian (1789-1869).

origins.name: Justus Lipsiusstraat
origins.en: Language scholar (1547-1606), professor at Leiden and later at Leuven.

origins.name: Justus van Maurikstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam cigar manufacturer (1846-1904), who gained great popularity as a writer of Amsterdam folk life. He was co-editor of 'De Groene Amsterdammer'.

origins.name: Juttepeerpad
origins.en: Old Dutch pear variety. The street is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Kaapstadweg
origins.en: Together with Bloemfontein and Pretoria, one of the capitals of South Africa.

origins.name: Kaasjeskruidstraat
origins.en: Plant family that owes its name to the somewhat cheesy fruit shape. The also found in the Netherlands great cheese herb was used in classical antiquity against all kinds of ailments: from intestinal and uterine problems to wasp and scorpion stings.

origins.name: Kabelgaststraat
origins.en: Occupational name: someone responsible for splitting and welding cables. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Kabelweg
origins.en: The insulated cable bundle for the conduction of electricity underwater or underground. The route follows the terrain area along which the high-voltage cables were laid around 1950 from the Centrale Hemweg to the then under construction western garden towns, to supply them with electricity.

origins.name: Kadijksplein
origins.en: When a lot of land had been silted up outside the old sea wall (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike or canal was built. Originally, the new sea wall was spoken of, but that later fell out of use. With further raising of this new dike, the Lowness and Height of the Canal were spoken of. The Between Canals was called Korte Kerkstraat until 1943. This is indeed in the extension of the Plantage Kerklaan, but has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Kadoelenbrug
origins.en: Name for the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was annexed to Amsterdam on August 1, 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) already appears in 1375. In 1429, there is talk of the lordship of Landsmeer and the lordship of Quadolen, which then had one lord together. Old maps indicate Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterlandse zeedijk (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1-8-1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed due to confusion with the Zuideinde (former Oostzaan).

origins.name: Kadoelenpad
origins.en: Name for the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was annexed to Amsterdam on August 1, 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) already appears in 1375. origins.name: Kagelinkkade
origins.en: Name of an old farm east of Diepenheim (Overijssel) near the Kagelink forest.

origins.name: Kajuitpad
origins.en: Ship part.

origins.name: Kajuitweg
origins.en: Ship part.

origins.name: Kalfjeslaan
origins.en: The former inn on the Amsteldijk from the eighteenth century (demolished 1967), later café-restaurant Het Kalfje.

origins.name: Kalkmarkt
origins.en: On this quay, the lime market was held from around 1663 until the end of the eighteenth century. The quay was created by the construction of the New Walloon Island in 1644.

origins.name: Kalkoenstraat
origins.en: Named after the turkey, a fowl.

origins.name: Kalmoesstraat
origins.en: Aquatic plant.

origins.name: Kalverstraat
origins.en: To the calf market, which was held here until the seventeenth century. The name already appears as such in 1393. However, no evidence has been found that a livestock market was actually held here. However, that in 1586 calf market was on the Dam. The part between Spui and Munt was called, when it came to lie within the city, Byndewyck, that is Binnenwijk. This southern part had the livestock market from 1486 to 1629 and was also called Ossemarkt. After that, the name Kalverstraat spread throughout the entire street.

origins.name: Kamerlingh Onneslaan
origins.en: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes (1853-1926), physicist, professor at Leiden and made helium liquid. In 1913 he won the Nobel Prize in Physics.

origins.name: Kamerpalmhof
origins.en: Palm species, related to the succulent. The leaves are thick and leathery.

origins.name: Kamillestraat
origins.en: Strongly scented meadow plant, belonging to the composites. In addition to meadows, it is also common on wasteland.

origins.name: Kamperfoelieweg
origins.en: Named after the honeysuckle, a climbing shrub.

origins.name: Kampervenuspad
origins.en: Old Dutch pear variety. The street is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Kampina
origins.en: Nature monument located east of Oisterwijk (North Brabant). It consists of marshes, the Kapinaseheide and the valley of the Beerse stream.

origins.name: Kanaaldijk West
origins.en: Named after the Kanaaldijk. Western side of the dike.

origins.name: Kanaalpost
origins.en: is named after the Canal Dyke

origins.name: Kanaalstraat
origins.en: With canal, this refers to the nearby Jacob van Lennepkanaal.

origins.name: Kanariestraat
origins.en: Named after the canary, a singing bird.

origins.name: Kaneelappelstraat
origins.en: Tropical fruit, originally from South America. The skin is usually green and the very soft flesh is white, with a sweet, aromatic taste.

origins.name: Kanteel
origins.en: The rising part of a crenellated defensive wall with shooting slits. Due to the rectangular shape of a parapet, the name refers to the adjacent buildings.

origins.name: Kantershof
origins.en: Name of a farm in Bunde (Limburg).

origins.name: Kantershofpad
origins.en: Name of a farm in Bunde (Limburg).

origins.name: Kantershofstraat
origins.en: Name of a farm in Bunde (Limburg).

origins.name: Kapkarpad
origins.en: The very first type of caravan. The street name refers to the caravan park on site.

origins.name: Kapoeasweg
origins.en: Navigable river in Indonesia, on Kalimantan (Borneo).

origins.name: Kapteynstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Cornelis Kapteyn (1851-1922), astronomer, professor at Groningen. Known for his research in the field of stellar streams. Also gave lectures in the United States and South Africa.

origins.name: Karel Doormanstraat
origins.en: Karel Willem Frederik Marie Doorman (1889-1942), naval officer. During World War II, he was rear admiral in Dutch East Indies. In 1942, he was given the impossible task of preventing the landing of the Japanese on Java. Doorman died in this famous battle in the Java Sea. The street came under the name Houtmanstraat in Amsterdam's territory in 1921 (council decision of Sloten, 1910) and was renamed Zeven Provinciënstraat by council decision in 1922, after the naval ship of Admiral De Ruyter. After some changes in the boundary of the street (council decision, 1933 and 10-6-1936), the current name was established in 1946.

origins.name: Karel du Jardinstraat
origins.en: Landscape and animal painter (1622-1678).

origins.name: Karel Klinkenbergstraat
origins.en: Painter of cityscapes (1852-1924).

origins.name: Karel van de Woestijnestraat
origins.en: Flemish literary scholar (1878-1929), professor at Ghent from 1921. One of the greatest Flemish poets after Guido Gezelle. Also known as a critic.

origins.name: Karel van het Revebrug
origins.en: Karel van het Reve (1921-1999) was a professor of Russian literature and writer. He is generally considered one of the most important nonfiction writers in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Karimatastraat
origins.en: Indonesian island group, located off the west coast of Kalimantan (Borneo).

origins.name: Karl Grögersingel
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), one of the nine people involved in the attack on the Amsterdam Population Register on March 27, 1943. Also involved in the attack on the railway at Sloterdijk and in the establishment of the inciting magazine 'Rattenkruid'.

origins.name: Karl Marxpad
origins.en: Karl Heinrich Marx (1818-1883), German philosopher and economist, believed that capitalism would inevitably perish due to its own development. Founder of Marxism, which focuses on class struggle and the overthrow of the ruling class.

origins.name: Karlskrona-eiland
origins.en: Swedish port city on the Baltic Sea from which a lot of ash, wood and iron used to be transported to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Karnstraat
origins.en: Dairy tool for the preparation of butter from milk.

origins.name: Karpatastraat
origins.en: Karpata, nicknamed Bastian, one of the leaders of the slave uprising that broke out in Curaçao in August 1795. In September of that year he was captured and tried.

origins.name: Karperstraat
origins.en: Named after the carp, a freshwater fish.

origins.name: Karperweg
origins.en: Named after the carp, a freshwater fish.

origins.name: Karspeldreef
origins.en: The name recalls the former municipality of Weesperkarspel. Karspel or kerspel is an old term for a rural municipality, even earlier for a church village or parish.

origins.name: Karthuizersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The streets were laid out on the site where the monastery of 'Carthuysers ter saliger havene' was located from 1394 to 1578. The cross street was called Blindemansteeg until 1892, but that name was changed because there was confusion with the other Blindemansteeg. The path and playground are the grounds of the former cemetery of the monastery. The garden was therefore called the Carthusian Cemetery until 1889.

origins.name: Karthuizersplantsoen
origins.en: The streets were laid out on the site where the monastery of 'Carthuysers ter saliger havene' was located from 1394 to 1578. The cross street was called Blindemansteeg until 1892, but that name was changed because there was confusion with the other Blindemansteeg. The path and playground are the grounds of the former cemetery of the monastery. The garden was therefore called the Carthusian Cemetery until 1889.

origins.name: Karveelstraat
origins.en: Nineteenth-century sailing ship, a fast sailor with predominantly large sails.

origins.name: Kastanjeplein
origins.en: Named after the chestnut, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Kastanjeweg
origins.en: Named after the chestnut, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Kastelenstraat
origins.en: The name was given because the street runs through the district with castle names. The last part of the Kastelenstraat was named in Zwaansvliet on 3-2-1965.

origins.name: Kasterleepark
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Kastrupstraat
origins.en: Name of Copenhagen airport.

origins.name: Katrijpstraat
origins.en: Village, also known as Catrijp, at the foot of the dunes near Schoorl (North Holland).

origins.name: Kattenburgergracht
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands, next to Wittenburg and Oostenburg. is already referred to by the name Kattenburg for the paving and construction in the second half of the seventeenth century. A reason for this name has not been found to date. However, there was a house with the name 'de Cat', but that name is only mentioned in the eighteenth century. After many buildings had already been demolished during the occupation years, the rest was demolished in the years 1965 to 1968. After that, construction began again according to a new street pattern. Kattenburgerplein is the only one that still reminds you of the old buildings.
