origins.name: Kattengat
origins.en: Originally this was a narrow canal, which ran from the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal (now Spuistraat) to the Singel. There is no consensus on the origin of the name. A narrow passage was formerly called a cat's throat = a hole so narrow that no cat could pass through. The name may also be named after the former soil conditions: marshy land, where catnip grows. In the second half of the nineteenth century, the canal was filled in. Part of it is now called Koggestraat. The remaining alley was significantly widened by demolition in 1936.

origins.name: Kattenlaan
origins.en: The origin of the name and the age are unknown. The street was transferred from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the same name in 1896.

origins.name: Katwijkstraat
origins.en: The South Holland fishing and seaside resort.

origins.name: Kazernestraat
origins.en: To the Oranje-Nassau barracks built in 1811.

origins.name: Kea Boumanstraat
origins.en: Kornelia Bouman (1903-1998), tennis star. Was the only Dutch Grand Slam winner until 1996 (Open French Championships, 1927). Won bronze in the mixed doubles at the 1924 Olympic Games.

origins.name: Keerpunt
origins.en: The name came from conversations with neighbors: a turning point in the vision of the municipal government to build houses instead of office buildings, the result of the input of the neighborhood.

origins.name: Keerwal
origins.en: Place where you can't go any further and have to turn around again. The buildings on Keerwal form a screening building for the houses on the railway in the Funenpark.

origins.name: Kees Abspoelstraat
origins.en: Kees Abspoel (1899-1970) was Shell's house architect and designed, in that capacity, the Shell Great Laboratory in Amsterdam Noord on the Overhoeks site in Noord.

origins.name: Kees Boekestraat
origins.en: For this neighborhood, the category names of Dutch architects who have been involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-North have been chosen.

origins.name: Kees Broekmanstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Broekman (1927-1992), skater. In 1952, he was the first Dutchman to win a medal at the Winter Olympics, namely silver in the 5000 meters. He also finished second in the 10 kilometers.

origins.name: Kees Fensbrug
origins.en: Kees Fens (1929 -2008) was an Amsterdam literary critic, essayist and literary scholar. In 1990 he received the P.C. Hooft Prize and in 2004 he received an honorary doctorate from the University of Amsterdam. From his house he had a view of this bridge and in 2008 he published the book 'The happiness of the bridge'.

origins.name: Kees Schererhof
origins.en: Christoffel Johannes Scherer (1920-1993), photographer. Continued with reports on, among other things, the 1953 Watersnoodramp. Two years later, he was co-founder of World Press Photo. Captured Amsterdam in a poetic way.

origins.name: Keienbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill in Gelderland, between Velp and Beekhuizen.

origins.name: Keizersbrug
origins.en: It derives its name from the nearby Keizersstraat

origins.name: Keizersgracht
origins.en: Named after Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms in 1489.

origins.name: Keizersstraat
origins.en: Located on the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Kelbergen
origins.en: Name of a townhouse in Brummen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kelbergenpad
origins.en: Name of a townhouse in Brummen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kemangiestraat
origins.en: Herb, also known as lemon basil or Thai basil.

origins.name: Kemiriestraat
origins.en: Note. A kemirie is a kind of almond with a very strong taste.

origins.name: Kemminkhorstweg
origins.en: Named after the old Kemminckhorst farm near Dalfsen (Overijssel).

origins.name: Kempenlaan
origins.en: The border area of Belgian and Dutch Brabant.

origins.name: Kempering
origins.en: Name of a farm in Reutum near Tubbergen (Overijssel).

origins.name: Ken Saro-Wiwastraat
origins.en: Nigerian writer (1941-1995), politician and businessman. As leader of the MOSOP, the movement for the survival of the Ogoniv people founded in 1990, he campaigned for more autonomy for the Ogoni. In 1995, he was sentenced to death by the dictatorial regime after a sham trial. On November 10, 1995, he was hanged together with eight other Ogoni activists.

origins.name: Kennemerduinstraat
origins.en: The national park de Kennemerduinen, a nature reserve north of the Bloemendaalse Zeeweg.

origins.name: Keratellastraat
origins.en: Microscopically small aquatic creature with two rapidly rotating cilia rings. In possession of sturdy chewing apparatus to grind the food finely. The keratella inhabits a house characterized by thorns.

origins.name: Kerdijkhof
origins.en: Arnoldus Polak Kerdijk (1846-1905), politician and journalist. As a progressive liberal, he fought hard for the emancipation of the worker. He was also director of the Rijkspostspaarbank.

origins.name: Kerkepad
origins.en: The Kerkepad is named after its location and function: the path of the dike village Nieuwendam to the village church.

origins.name: Kerklaan Zunderdorp
origins.en: The main street of Zunderdorp, leading towards the village church.

origins.name: Kerkstraat
origins.en: The Kerkstraat was built in 1665 and was named so because the plan was to connect four churches with this street, namely the Amstel Church, the Oosterkerk and two others that were never built, namely one near Molenpad and a second near Weesperstraat. Later on, the street received several names: Kerkstraat (up to the Amstel), Nieuwe Kerkstraat (up to the Roetersstraat), Plantage Kerklaan (in the Plantage) and Korte Kerkstraat, which was renamed Tussen Kadijken in 1943.

origins.name: Kermispad
origins.en: The folk festival with attractions. The name is related to the caravan world and refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Kerriestraat
origins.en: Herb mixture, originally from India, where the word 'kari' means sauce. The English simplified the word 'kari' to 'curry'. Through Indonesia, the use of curry came to the Netherlands.

origins.name: Kersenstraat
origins.en: The fruits of the cherry tree.

origins.name: Kerstomaatplantsoen
origins.en: Type of tomato, also known as cocktail or cherry tomato.

origins.name: Kervelplantsoen
origins.en: Herb. In the Middle Ages, the plant was very common in monastery gardens.

origins.name: Ketelhuisplein
origins.en: The very distinctive boiler house of the former Wilhelmina Gasthuis.

origins.name: Ketelmakerij
origins.en: The street is located on the premises of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company. Ketelmakerij refers to one of the workplaces that were located here.

origins.name: Ketelmakerstraat
origins.en: This occupational name recalls the old boilerworks, which were located here.

origins.name: Ketelstraat
origins.en: The machine component the steam boiler, a closed tank in which water is heated to steam.

origins.name: Keurenplein
origins.en: Councils were the ordinances of each public authority before 1795. The name is related to the verb 'to approve' in the sense of 'choose', originally it referred to the rules that had to be observed or established on the day on which new administrators were elected.

origins.name: Keverberg
origins.en: Castle in Kessel (Limburg), also known as Castle Kessel, built on the foundations of an eleventh-century castle, and destroyed by the German troops in 1944.

origins.name: Kiefskamp
origins.en: One of the best preserved eighteenth-century country houses from around 1770, located near Vorden (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kiekstraat
origins.en: Israel David Kiek (1811-1899), photo pioneer. His surname has become synonymous in the Netherlands with the pretentious, candid photo: the snapshot. He had a photo studio in Leiden and was a photographer of Leiden student life.

origins.name: Kierkegaardstraat
origins.en: Søren Kierkegaard (1813-1855), Danish preacher and philosopher, in his work the emphasis is on his personal worldview. He rejects the state church and ecclesiastical Christianity.

origins.name: Kievitstraat
origins.en: Named after the lapwing, a meadow bird.

origins.name: Kijkduinstraat
origins.en: The former fort south of Huisduinen near Den Helder, known for the naval battle in 1673 when Admiral De Ruyter defeated the united English-French fleet.

origins.name: Kikkenstein
origins.en: Name of a patrician house in Loenen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kikkensteinhof
origins.en: Name of a patrician house in Loenen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kikkensteinstraat
origins.en: Name of a patrician house in Loenen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kimpoweg
origins.en: Name of the airport in Seoul, South Korea.

origins.name: Kinderdijkstraat
origins.en: The riverbank along the North, in the Alblasserwaard (South Holland).

origins.name: King's Cross
origins.en: Large railway station in Northern London

origins.name: Kingsfordweg
origins.en: Name of the airport in Sydney, Australia.

origins.name: Kinkerstraat
origins.en: He translated works by Shakespeare and Schiller...

origins.name: Kinrooistraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Klaas Geertsplantsoen
origins.en: Klaas Geerts (1932-2002) was the founder of architectural firm lnbo. He played an important role in the reconstruction of the Netherlands and designed the Molenwijk. For this neighborhood, the category names of Dutch architects who have been involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-North have been chosen.

origins.name: Klaas Katerstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam bricklayer (1833-1906), founded in 1876 in Amsterdam the Christian Association Patrimonium, of which he was president until 1899. From 1880 to 1900 he was leader of the Christian Workers' Union.

origins.name: Klaas Wannen
origins.en: Named after the ditch between the Twiske and the Gouw, probably after a farmer. Disappeared due to the flooding of the Twiske and the conversion into a forest area.

origins.name: Klapmutsenveem
origins.en: A veem is a company responsible for storing and delivering goods in and out of its warehouses. The veems each had their own license plate, after which they were named. These could be different colors and models of hats (e.g. Cloche hats, Blue hats). They also derived their name from the origin of the workers (e.g. Friese veem, Zeeuwse veem).

origins.name: Klaprozenweg
origins.en: The poppy, name of a plant belonging to the poppy family.

origins.name: Klarenburg
origins.en: The former Karenburg farm on the Uitweg, demolished for the construction of garden town Osdorp. The l in the street name is therefore abusive, but the mayor and aldermen later did not consider this deviation to be significant enough to change the council decision.

origins.name: Klaroenstraat
origins.en: Leafy vegetable with red-flamed leaves, also known as amaranth or Chinese spinach.

origins.name: Klaverbladstraat
origins.en: The name refers to the leaf of the native edible plant species from the daisy family.

origins.name: Kleefkruidstraat
origins.en: Edible plant from the asteraceae family, which owes its hairy characteristic to the many hooks that cover it.

origins.name: Kleiburg
origins.en: Former farm in the Bijlmermeer, on the Weespertrekvaart.

origins.name: Kleine Beerstraat
origins.en: Constellation.

origins.name: Kleine Bickersstraat
origins.en: These streets are located on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr. Johan Bicker (1591-1653), shipbuilder and merchant, ships and mayor of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets that were later laid out on this island automatically took the name of the founder.

origins.name: Kleine Diestraat
origins.en: The nearby water the Kleine Die and the Grote Die. 'Die' is a contraction of 'de' and 'ie'. 'Ie' in turn is again a North Holland variant of 'aa', which means water and is written as 'ee' in Frisian-speaking areas. The spelling 'IJ' is actually incorrect.

origins.name: Kleine Houtstraat
origins.en: Reminds of the timber trade that used to be concentrated around the Haarlemmer Houttuinen. (The Grote Houtstraat fell into disrepair in 1973.)

origins.name: Kleine Pimpernelstraat
origins.en: Perennial plant with edible leaves. There are greenish-purple flowers on the bulbous flower head.

origins.name: Kleine Wittenburgerstraat
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (next to Kattenburg and Oostenburg), built in the second half of the seventeenth century, from the beginning built with shipyards and houses. One of the first shipyards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. Very likely we must look here for the origin of the name Wittenburg.

origins.name: Kleine Zonneplein
origins.en: The central body in the planetary system to which Earth belongs.

origins.name: Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen
origins.en: Maria Johanna Kleine born Gartman (1818-1885), actress. As the first teacher at the Drama School, she formed many actors and leaders. Before the naming in 1915, the square was part of the Lijnbaansgracht and the Weteringschans.

origins.name: Klieverink
origins.en: The Klieverink or Klievering, name of a farm in Losser (Overijssel).

origins.name: Klieverinkweg
origins.en: The Klieverink or Klievering, name of a farm in Losser (Overijssel).

origins.name: Klimopbrug
origins.en: Named after the ivy, a climbing shrub.

origins.name: Klimopstraatje
origins.en: Named after the ivy, a climbing shrub.

origins.name: Klimopweg
origins.en: Named after the ivy, a climbing shrub.

origins.name: Klinkerweg
origins.en: Metalworker, who assembles iron parts together using rivets. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Klipperstraat
origins.en: Long, narrow, fast-sailing triple-masted ship.

origins.name: Kloekhorststraat
origins.en: Name of an old farm in the hamlet of Klein Dochteren under Lochem (Gelderland).

origins.name: Klokkenbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Nijmegen.

origins.name: Klönne plein
origins.en: The company August Klönne, specialized in gas holders, was responsible for the construction of the new telescopic gas holder of the Westergasfabiek in 1902. The gas holder is the landmark of the former factory site.

origins.name: Kloveniersburgwal
origins.en: The Kloveniersburgwal owes its name to a company of the civic guard called the kloveniers, after the firearm its men carried, the klover or culverin.

origins.name: Klovenierssteeg
origins.en: To the Kloveniersdoelen, the place of gathering of the old shooting club. At that place is now the Doelenhotel. The old shooting club originally used the crossbow, but in 1522 the shooters received rifles or crossbows and were then called kloveniers. This city wall was until the end of the sixteenth century the outer city canal. Before 1909 the alley was called Watersteeg, but this caused confusion with the Watersteeg on the Rokin.

origins.name: Kneppelhoutstraat
origins.en: Johannes Kneppelhout (1814-1885), pseudonym Klikspaan, writer of realistic-humorous sketches and stories.

origins.name: Kneppelweg
origins.en: Name of an old farm near Eefde (Gelderland).

origins.name: Knokkestraat
origins.en: Belgian coastal town, located in the province of West Flanders.

origins.name: Knollendamstraat
origins.en: Village in the Zaanstreek. The street was originally named as Derde Spaarndammerdwarsstraat (council decision, 1881).

origins.name: KNSM-laan
origins.en: The Royal Dutch Steam Boat Company, founded in 1856, one of the largest Dutch shipping companies. It operated scheduled services to West Indies, Central America, the west and north coast of South America, the Levant and European ports. It also operated between North and South America. In 1981, the KNSM merged into the Royal NedLloyd group.

origins.name: Koekoeksplein
origins.en: Named after the cuckoo, a singing bird.

origins.name: Koekoeksstraat
origins.en: Named after the cuckoo, a singing bird.

origins.name: Koen Limpergstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1908-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Haarlem.

origins.name: Koenenkade
origins.en: To a former resident.

origins.name: Koerierstersplein
origins.en: Girls who were active in the resistance during World War II. They distributed bonka cards, fake papers and money and accompanied Jewish children by bicycle or train. The street name is also a tribute to the couriers Miep Gies and Elly Voskuijl who cared for the undergrounders in the Achterhuis, including Anne Frank.

origins.name: Koestraat
origins.en: The street ran along the stable of the former Bethany monastery, which stretched between this street and Bethaniënstraat.

origins.name: Koffieweg
origins.en: The ground powder of roasted coffee beans. Coffee is dumped in the Amsterdam harbor.

origins.name: Kofschipstraat
origins.en: Circular two-masted boat with wide stern, a slow sailor.

origins.name: Kogeldistelstraat
origins.en: Named after the globe thistle, a thistle.

origins.name: Koggestraat
origins.en: Old ship type, after which the traditional Amsterdam Koggeschip is named. For the filling in in the nineteenth century, the water belonged to the Kattengat.

origins.name: Koivistokade
origins.en: Large Russian oil port on the Baltic Sea, now known as Primorsk. Koivisto, Finnish for birch grove, belonged to Finland between 1918-1944.

origins.name: Kokmeeuwpad
origins.en: Bird, belonging to the family of gulls.

origins.name: Kokospalmhof
origins.en: Palm species. The inside of the fruit of this palm resembles the face of an ape, which is called 'coco' in Portuguese.

origins.name: Kolbergbrug
origins.en: Kolberg was the German name for the Polish port city of Kolobrzeg on the Baltic Sea. The names in the Houthavens are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Kolfschotenstraat
origins.en: Country estate with house in Scherpenzeel (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kolibristraat
origins.en: Very small tropical bird.

origins.name: Kolksluis
origins.en: Bridge 302 is located in the Zeedijk over the Oudezijdskolk. A pool of a sluice lock is the space between both pairs of sluice doors. This was the drainage of the Oudezijds Voor- and Achterburgwal into the IJ. The lock dates back to the beginning of the fifteenth century.

origins.name: Kolksteeg
origins.en: This was the drainage of the Oudezijds Voor- and Achterburgwal into the IJ. The sluice dates back to the beginning of the fifteenth century.

origins.name: Kollenbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill east of Sittard (Limburg).

origins.name: Kölpinstraat
origins.en: The lake, the Kölpinsee, located in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, North Germany.

origins.name: Kombuisweg
origins.en: A galley is a kitchen on a ship.

origins.name: Kometensingel
origins.en: Small celestial bodies consisting of ice, gas and dust..

origins.name: Komijnstraat
origins.en: Kitchen herb from the nightshade family, native to the Middle East and India.

origins.name: Kompasweg
origins.en: Named after the navigation instrument.

origins.name: Konijnenstraat
origins.en: Rodent. The name originated under the influence of the fur trade, which was practiced in this part of the city.

origins.name: Koningin Wilhelminaplein
origins.en: Wilhelmina Helena Paulina Maria princess of Orange Nassau (1880-1962), daughter of King William III and Queen Emma. Koningin of the Netherlands from 1898 to 1948.

origins.name: Koninginneweg
origins.en: Named after the then-queen Emma (see Emmalaan).

origins.name: Koningsbergenbrug
origins.en: Koningsbergen was the German name for the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad on the Baltic Sea. The names in the Houthavens are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Koningslaan
origins.en: To the kings from the House of Orange-Nassau.

origins.name: Koningspalmplein
origins.en: Palm species. Considered by many to be the most beautiful palm in the world, hence the name king palm.

origins.name: Koningsplein
origins.en: In the first years of the seventeenth century, part of the Singel Koningsgracht was named in honor of the ally King Henry IV of France. The square on this Koningsgracht therefore took the name Koningsplein. The name Koningsgracht did not last, but the name of the square has been preserved.

origins.name: Koningsstraat
origins.en: The streets are located on the old Lastage and were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Koogstraat
origins.en: The village of Koog aan de Zaan (North Holland).

origins.name: Koolpalmhof
origins.en: Tree, also known as cabbage tree or grass palm. Although its shape resembles a palm tree, the cabbage palm does not belong to that family of trees. The young, soft leaves were eaten instead of cabbage.

origins.name: Koolrabistraat
origins.en: Vegetable presumably originating from Northern Europe, the thickened stem of which is eaten.

origins.name: Koopvaardersplantsoen
origins.en: Collective name for former merchant ships.

origins.name: Koornhorst
origins.en: Name of a farm in Bergh-Montferland (Gelderland).

origins.name: Koos Vorrinkweg
origins.en: Jacobus Jan. Vorrink (1891-1955), teacher and politician, founder and leader of the AJC, chairman of the SDAP and member of parliament. Had an active role in the founding of the Labour Party.

origins.name: Koperslagerij
origins.en: The street is located on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company. Koperslagerij refers to one of the workshops that were located here.

origins.name: Kopjachtplein
origins.en: Sailboat with high bow.

origins.name: Koppelingpad
origins.en: Machine part.

origins.name: Koppenburglaan
origins.en: Name of an old farm in Lathum, municipality of Angerloo (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kopraweg
origins.en: Kopra is the dried flesh of the coconut. Making kopra was once done by traders who traveled from port to port in the Pacific Ocean.

origins.name: Korenbloemstraat
origins.en: The plant, belonging to the family of composites.

origins.name: Korfbalstraat
origins.en: Named after the korfball that was played here at the former sports park

origins.name: Korianderstraat
origins.en: Plant from the screenflower family, also known as ketoembar. Originating from the Mediterranean region and the Middle East.

origins.name: Kormelinkweg
origins.en: Old farm southwest of Eibergen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Korrelbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the Korrel family, who had a milk shop in Eerste Jan Steenstraat 4 from 1947 to 1985. This bridge is also intended as a tribute to the many disappeared small middlemen from the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s; a time when you could still puff up.

origins.name: Korsjespoortsteeg
origins.en: To the wood buyer Corsgen Jacobszoon, who in the fifteenth century had an orchard on the Singel, outside the city. The bridge over the Singel therefore got the name Korsjesbrug. Later the name passed on to the gate and the street leading to it. In the sixteenth century a new longer alley was built along the extension of the first alley. Both had the name Korsjespoortsteeg at the time, but the oldest was given the addition 'Short'.

origins.name: Korte 's-Gravesandestraat
origins.en: Willem Jan van 's-Gravesande (1688-1742), Leiden professor of mathematics and astronomy. In the Netherlands the first follower of Newton.

origins.name: Korte Amstelstraat
origins.en: The Korte Amstelstraat was created by partial filling in of the Nieuwe Achtergracht around 1670. In the middle of the Amstelveld, a church was planned. Therefore, in 1669, the auxiliary church was built in a corner. The church was never built, the auxiliary church still stands there.

origins.name: Korte Blekersstraat
origins.en: Before 1911 called Korte Blekerspad, after the bleachworks located there in the eighteenth century, along the Blekerssloot.

origins.name: Korte De Wittenstraat
origins.en: The brothers Cornelis de Witt (1623-1672), mayor of Dordrecht, and Johan de Witt (1625-1672), council pensionary of Holland, both murdered by the people in The Hague on false charges. One side of the quay first bore the name Maljapenkade.

origins.name: Korte Dijkstraat
origins.en: The street was built at the end of the sixteenth century as a dike, after which the surrounding area (formerly a swamp) was drained.

origins.name: Korte Distelstraat
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Korte Geuzenstraat
origins.en: Initially intended as a slur, but considered a name of honor by the allied nobles in the struggle against Spain. Later the battle name for all opponents of Spain in the Eighty Years' War. The Korte Geuzenstraat previously belonged to the Geuzenstraat.

origins.name: Korte Keizersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Located on the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Korte Keizersstraat
origins.en: Located on the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Korte Kolksteeg
origins.en: Originally, the water that came from the underlying peatland area through the now filled in Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal flowed through this pool to the Damrak. Around 1350, the Martelaarsgracht was dug and this drainage ceased. By the end of the fifteenth century, the pool had been filled in.

origins.name: Korte Koningsdwarsstraat
origins.en: Located on the Lastage. The streets were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Korte Koningsstraat
origins.en: The streets are located on the old Lastage and were laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Korte Korsjespoortsteeg
origins.en: To the wood buyer Corsgen Jacobszoon, who in the fifteenth century had an orchard on the Singel, outside the city. The bridge over the Singel therefore got the name Korsjesbrug. Later the name passed on to the gate and the street leading to it. In the sixteenth century a new longer alley was built along the extension of the first alley. Both had the name Korsjespoortsteeg at the time, but the oldest was given the addition 'Korte'.

origins.name: Korte Leidsedwarsstraat
origins.en: The city of Leiden.

origins.name: Korte Lijnbaanssteeg
origins.en: The ropewalks of the rope-making works. The Lijnbaanssteeg dates back to the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outer canal. The rope-making works needed a fairly large area for the exercise of its business. This could only be found on the outside of the city. The ropewalks were on the city side of the canal, so within the rampart. The Linebaansgracht ran around the entire city. It is now filled in in a number of places and has been given other names there, such as Leidseplein, Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen, Frederiksplein, Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat, Valckenierstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

origins.name: Korte Marnixkade
origins.en: Philip of Marnix, lord of Sint Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and advisor of Prince William of Orange, author of the Union of the Nobles (1568). Possibly poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, formerly called Schans, was laid out after 1850 on the site where the city walls used to be, which were demolished between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Korte Marnixstraat
origins.en: Philip of Marnix, lord of Sint Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and advisor of Prince William of Orange, compiler of the Union of the Nobles (1568). Possibly poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was built after 1850 on the site where the city walls used to be, which were demolished between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Korte Meerhuizenstraat
origins.en: Former country house on the Amstel near the site where the Amstelkade now meets the Amsteldijk, demolished around 1914. In the seventeenth century, the poet Hendrik Laurens Spieghel lived here.

origins.name: Korte Niezel
origins.en: The name is a corruption of liesdel = del or valley in which lies (lissen) grows. It was a swampy land north of the higher ground, on which the Old Church was built. In the second half of the fourteenth century, this low area was raised and built up. In one of the streets, the old name Liesdel remained alive. In the following centuries, this name became Niesdel and in the eighteenth century officially Niezel. In the sixteenth century, a street is extended in the direction of the existing one, which after several other names finally gets the name Korte Niezel, while the oldest part gets the addition Lange.

origins.name: Korte Ouderkerkerbrug
origins.en: Named after the village of Ouderkerk aan de Amstel, where these roads lead to it. The addition Korte dates from 1956, after the dike was dug through for the industrial area.

origins.name: Korte Ouderkerkerdijk
origins.en: Name of the dike in which this bridge is located

origins.name: Korte Papaverweg
origins.en: The plant, wild and cultivated. is also called buttercup.

origins.name: Korte Prinsengracht
origins.en: To 'the princely title', which refers to that of the princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and in terms of the nature of the buildings, the simplest. During the enlargement of 1612, it was dug and built from Brouwersgracht to Leidsegracht. With the enlargement of 1658, this canal is also extended across the Amstel (up to the Entrepotdok). For the part on the Plantage, see also Plantage Westermanlaan - formerly Plantage Prinsenlaan. The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for the current Noordermarkt did not find favor with the bourgeoisie.

origins.name: Korte Reguliersdwarsstraat
origins.en: All these names remind us of the Reguliersklooster, which stood outside the then-city gate from 1394 to 1532, on the site where Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now intersect. The city gate, whose Mint Tower is a remnant, was formerly called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht ended at that gate at that time. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, parts of it were demolished. Before 1909, Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Korte Schimmelstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Jan Schimmel (1825-1906), bank director, known as a novelist and playwright. He was also editor of 'De Gids'. These streets came into Amsterdam in 1896 with the names Van Speyckstraat and Van Speyckdwarsstraat established by Nieuwer-Amstel, but were renamed in 1922, after another Van Speyckstraat came within the municipal boundary due to the annexation of Sloten.

origins.name: Korte Spinhuissteeg
origins.en: To the nearby Spinhuis, a women's prison founded in 1596. From 1833 to 1941, the main police headquarters was located in this building.

origins.name: Korte Stormsteeg
origins.en: Because this part of the city was on the outermost edge until the sixteenth century, people here were hit hard by storms. It is likely that the name of the alley was therefore created.

origins.name: Korte Tolstraat
origins.en: To the toll booth at the corner of the current Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was collected since around 1780 until the annexation of this area in 1896. The toll was intended for the maintenance of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation, the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1886).

origins.name: Korte van Eeghenstraat
origins.en: Named after Isabelle Henriette van Eeghen (1913-1996), archivist and historian. The name of the street was established by the municipality of Nieuwer Amstel on 7-2-1896 as Heemskerkstraat (after minister J. Heemskerk Az.). After the annexation of 1896, the name was changed to Van Eeghendwarsstraat because there already existed a Van Heemskerckstraat in Amsterdam (council decision, 1896). However, the residents and owners requested to change the name. Dwarsstraat in their opinion fell short of prosperity. The municipal council then decided on the current name.

origins.name: Korte Vogelstraat
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Korte Water
origins.en: Historical name from the old Sloten/Osdorp. According to the map by Jan Dou from 1687, Korte Water was located south of the Ookmeertje.

origins.name: Korte Zoutkeetsgracht
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, the salt chain stood on both sides of this canal. These were warehouses where coarse salt was processed for household use.

origins.name: Kortenaerstraat
origins.en: Egbert M. Kortenaer, vice admiral. Participated in the naval battles at Terheide (1653) and in the Sont (1658). Died in 1665 in the battle of Lowestoft against the English.

origins.name: Kortenakenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Korteweghof
origins.en: Diederik Johannes Korteweg (1848-1941), mathematician and astronomer, professor in Amsterdam. Provided the publication of the complete works of Christiaan Huygens.

origins.name: Kortrijk
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of West Flanders.

origins.name: Kortvoort
origins.en: Neighbourhood and house under Oss (North Brabant). A ford is a passable place.

origins.name: Kortwoudepad
origins.en: Kortwoude is a hamlet in the Dutch province of Friesland, in the municipality of Achtkarspelen.

origins.name: Kostverlorenstraat
origins.en: To the Kostverloren Wetering, dug in 1413 to obtain a shorter waterway to the Haarlemmer and Leidse lakes. According to some, a reason for the name Kostverloren would be that this waterway, which has been a source of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609, has cost a lot of money in proceedings. The name Kostverloren occurs in various places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Kotteraarstraat
origins.en: The metalworker, who works with the lathe, a tool for clearing and cylindricalizing holes. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Kotterspad
origins.en: Fast-sailing ship, used among other things for coastal shipping and fishing. Derived from the English to cut (cut).

origins.name: Kousenbandstraat
origins.en: Pod up to 90 centimeters long, presumably from tropical Africa. Grown in South America and the Asian tropics.

origins.name: Kouterstraat
origins.en: A kouter is the blade of a plow.

origins.name: Kouwenoord
origins.en: Name of various farms, including in Kesteren (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kouwenoordweg
origins.en: Name of various farms, including in Kesteren (Gelderland).

origins.name: Koxhorn
origins.en: Old country house in Wassenaar (South Holland).

origins.name: Kraaiennest
origins.en: Name of a house and fort in Breukelen-Sint Pieter (Utrecht) and of a farm in Harmelen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kraaiennestpad
origins.en: Name of a house and fort in Breukelen-Sint Pieter (Utrecht) and of a farm in Harmelen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kraaienplein
origins.en: Named after the crow, a bird.

origins.name: Kraailookstraat
origins.en: Plant, rare wild leek species.

origins.name: Kraaipanstraat
origins.en: The place in Transvaal (South Africa) where the Boer War (1899-1902) was fought against the English.

origins.name: Kraandrijverstraat
origins.en: The crane driver or crane operator operates the lifting crane, with which loads can be moved horizontally and vertically. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Kraansluis
origins.en: The name of this permanent bridge recalls the Great Crane, which stood on the IJ from 1643 to 1841 and was used to set masts in ships and to unload stone blocks and artillery

origins.name: Kraanspoor
origins.en: The name comes from the concrete structure from 1952 on which the offices are built. In the past, there were two large cranes here that hoisted cargo from the land onto the ships.

origins.name: Krabbendamstraat
origins.en: Village in the Kop of North Holland.

origins.name: Kraijenhoffstraat
origins.en: Cornelis R.Th. baron van Kraijenhoff (1758-1840), civil engineer, minister of War under King Louis Napoleon. Strengthened the fortifications around the city in 1815.

origins.name: Kramatplantsoen
origins.en: A suburb of Batavia (now Jakarta). Kramat is an Islamic concept for something that is sacred (grave, animal or object) and to which a miraculous power is attributed.

origins.name: Kramatweg
origins.en: A suburb of Batavia (now Jakarta). Kramat is an Islamic concept for something that is sacred (grave, animal or object) and to which a miraculous power is attributed.

origins.name: Krammerstraat
origins.en: The waterway between Overflakkee and St. Philipsland.

origins.name: Kranenburg
origins.en: Former knight's manor on the Rottemeren near Bleiswijk.

origins.name: Krasseurstraat
origins.en: Worker in a construction workshop scratching the working drawings on metal plates. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Kratontuin
origins.en: To the fortified and walled palace of Javanese rulers - the center of political power and culture - which often formed a city within a city. Each dynasty founded a new kraton, in which sometimes a few thousand people lived. The most famous kraton in Java is that of Yogyakarta, founded in 1757.

origins.name: Kreeftstraat
origins.en: Constellation, also sign of the Zodiac.

origins.name: Krelis Louwenstraat
origins.en: Happy play by Pieter Langendijk, often performed successfully.

origins.name: Kretaweg
origins.en: Greek island.

origins.name: Kribbestraat
origins.en: Stone weirs installed in rivers to direct the flow of water.

origins.name: Krijn Breurstraat
origins.en: Krijn Martinus Breur (1917-1943), resistance fighter, born in Dordrecht, executed by firing squad in Leusden.

origins.name: Krijn Taconiskade
origins.en: Photojournalist (1918-1979), joined the photo group 'De Ondergedoken Camera' during World War II, which illegally photographed during the hunger winter. Worked after the liberation for international photojournalism, made a report on a famine in Haiti, among other things. Was a member of the famous photography collective Magnum.

origins.name: Krimpertplein
origins.en: Name of a farm on the Verwolde estate near Laren (Gelderland).

origins.name: Krom Boomssloot
origins.en: Crossing of the Recht Boomsloot, hence preposition curved.

origins.name: Krombekstraat
origins.en: One of the few remaining varieties of the Dutch white bean.

origins.name: Kromme Distelstraat
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Kromme Leimuidenstraat
origins.en: Village between the Westeinder Plassen and the Braassemermeer in South Holland. The addition Kromme indicates the shape of the street.

origins.name: Kromme Palmstraat
origins.en: The tree. The Palmgracht was filled in in 1895.

origins.name: Kromme Waal
origins.en: The quays were ancient harbors of the IJ on the old side (Oude Waal) and on the new side (Nieuwe Waal), where the sea ships were moored in winter. The Oude Waal was made too shallow by siltation. On top of that, the Waalseiland was dredged in 1646. The quay on the city side retained the names Oude Waal and Kromme Waal (after the shape), on the Waalseiland the names Binnenkant and Buitenkant (now Prins Hendrikkade) came. The Nieuwe Waal disappeared due to the construction of the Western Entrepot Dock. The Waalsteeg was called Schippersstraatje before 1912. The name was changed due to confusion with the Schippersstraat.

origins.name: Kromme-Mijdrechtstraat
origins.en: The water in South Holland. From the confluence with the Drecht, the Amstel is formed. That the street has a curved shape is a coincidence or a joke by the namesake.

origins.name: Krommehoekstraat
origins.en: Curved corner name of disappeared farm

origins.name: Krommeniestraat
origins.en: The village in the Zaanstreek. As a result of construction and demolition, the street was shortened in 1978 and a section was moved to the Spaarndammerplantsoen.

origins.name: Krommertstraat
origins.en: The winding waterway the Krommert, already partially filled in before 1930. The rest was filled in in the 1950s.

origins.name: Kromwijkdreef
origins.en: Name of various patrician houses, including in Tienhoven (Utrecht) and Maarsseveen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Kronstadtbrug
origins.en: Kronstadt is a Russian port city on the Gulf of Finland near St. Petersburg. The names in the Houthavens are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Kroonweg
origins.en: The currency of Sweden, Denmark, Norway and the Czech Republic.

origins.name: Krooswijkhof
origins.en: Krooswijk or Crooswijk is a former 16th-century country house on the Rotte, now a Rotterdam neighborhood near the Crooswijk cemetery. This palace was laid out with other streets on the previously planned route of the Rotterdamseweg.

origins.name: Krootstraat
origins.en: The beetroot or red beet is a root crop and belongs to the family to which the sugar beet also belongs.

origins.name: Kropaarstraat
origins.en: Grass species, which occurs in Europe, Asia and North Africa.

origins.name: Krugerplein
origins.en: Johannes Stephanus Paul Kruger, better known as Paul Kruger (1825-1904), president of the Transvaal from 1883. Tried unsuccessfully to gain support for his country in Europe in the struggle against British domination (died in Switzerland).

origins.name: Krugerstraat
origins.en: Johannes Stephanus Paul Kruger, better known as Paul Kruger (1825-1904), president of the Transvaal from 1883. Tried unsuccessfully to gain support for his country in Europe in the struggle against British domination (died in Switzerland).

origins.name: Kruisbessenstraat
origins.en: Fruits of the shrub of the same name.

origins.name: Kruisherenpad
origins.en: In the early period of the garden city (circa 1955), the path was the regular route of the priests of the Roman Catholic Church to their parish church. Those priests belonged to the Order of the Knights of St. George, so the path soon took this name.

origins.name: Kruislaan
origins.en: Regarding the location: the road crosses the Middenweg.

origins.name: Kruitberg
origins.en: Old patrician house under Santpoort (North Holland), which belonged to stadtholder William III in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Kruitberghof
origins.en: Old patrician house under Santpoort (North Holland), which belonged to stadtholder William III in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Kruitbergstraat
origins.en: Old patrician house under Santpoort (North Holland), which belonged to stadtholder William III in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Kruithuisstraat
origins.en: In the seventeenth century, a gunpowder magazine was built on this site. After having been in use for several decades, it was demolished due to the encroaching development.

origins.name: Kruldistelstraat
origins.en: Named after the welted thistle, a thistle.

origins.name: Krulslaplantsoen
origins.en: Variation of the ordinary leaf lettuce with a slightly curly leaf.

origins.name: Kruysweerstraat
origins.en: Formerly outside on the Amstel.

origins.name: ks. Ibisplantsoen
origins.en: The crane ship Ibis, built in 1982 at the shipyard of the NSM (the successor of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij). This crane ship, with a lifting capacity of 1600 tons, has been used for hydraulic works in the Persian Gulf.

origins.name: ks. Ibisweg
origins.en: The crane ship Ibis, built in 1982 at the shipyard of the NSM (the successor of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij) for Ballast-Nedam. This crane ship, with a lifting capacity of 1600 tons, is used for hydraulic works in the Persian Gulf.

origins.name: Kuilsenhofweg
origins.en: Name of a farm in Beek near Nijmegen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Kuinderstraat
origins.en: River in Friesland. Used to flow into the IJsselmeer near the town of Kuinre.

origins.name: Kuiperbergweg
origins.en: Hill near Ootmarsum, top of the eastern escarpment of Overijssel.

origins.name: Kuiperssteeg
origins.en: To the cooperage established here in the seventeenth century. Before that, the alley is known as St. Clarensteeg under the name of the former monastery St. Claren.

origins.name: Kuipersstraat
origins.en: Named after the former Kuiperspad, which already existed in the seventeenth century and on which the street was laid out. Until 1896, the street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the same name.

origins.name: Kurk
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the Irish port city of Cork, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Kustvaarderstraat
origins.en: Ship specially for coastal shipping, usually of a maximum of 500 tons. More commonly known as a coaster.

origins.name: Kwadijkerstraat
origins.en: The village of Kwadijk, located north of Purmerend.

origins.name: Kwadrantweg
origins.en: Instrument for measuring the altitude of celestial bodies, used in navigation.

origins.name: Kwakersplein
origins.en: To the former Kwakerspoel and the Quaker Island. These names are first mentioned here around 1680. The name is probably derived from the sect of the Quakers (Quakers). The followers of this sect, whose principles were first preached in Amsterdam around 1656, were expelled from the city so that they could gather in this remote place outside the city limits. In 1674, they were allowed to gather in a house on the Keizersgracht. The name de Bijkerk of one of the mills that stood here also advocates for this name. Another explanation is the old spelling 'kwakel', which was the name of a high narrow wooden bridge and still occurs in North Holland to this day.

origins.name: Kwakersstraat
origins.en: To the former Kwakerspoel and the Quaker Island. These names are first mentioned here around 1680. The name is probably derived from the sect of the Quakers (Quakers). The followers of this sect, whose principles were first preached in Amsterdam around 1656, were expelled from the city so that they could gather in this remote place outside the city limits. In 1674, they were allowed to gather in a house on the Keizersgracht. The name de Bijkerk of one of the mills that stood here also advocates for this name. Another explanation is the old spelling 'kwakel', which was the name of a high narrow wooden bridge and still occurs in North Holland to this day.

origins.name: Kwartelstraat
origins.en: Bird, belonging to the chickens.

origins.name: Kwartiermeesterstraat
origins.en: Officer who takes care of the quarters and the intendancy.

origins.name: Kwekerijlaan
origins.en: Place where vegetables are grown. The street is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Kwelderweg
origins.en: Extensive land reclamation with vegetation, which usually no longer occurs during high water.

origins.name: Kwintsheulstraat
origins.en: Village in the Westland (South Holland).

origins.name: L. van Sonsbeeckstraat
origins.en: Louis Hendrik van Sonsbeeck (1831-1903), mayor of Sloten from 1864 to 1868, then of Vlagtwedde.

origins.name: L.J.M. Beelstraat
origins.en: Louis Jozef Maria Beel (1902-1977), statesman, member of the KVP. In 1945 he became Minister of the Interior and in 1946 Prime Minister. From 1951 to 1956 he was again Minister of the Interior and then again Prime Minister in the period 1958-1959. In addition, among other things, Minister of State.

origins.name: La Guardiaweg
origins.en: Name of one of the airports in New York.

origins.name: La Meye
origins.en: Mountain peak in France, 3987 meters high.

origins.name: Laagte Kadijk
origins.en: When a lot of land had been silted up outside the old sea wall (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike or canal was built. Originally, it was called the new sea wall, but that later fell out of use. With further raising of this new dike, it was called the Laagte and the Height of the Kadijk. The Between Dikes was called Korte Kerkstraat until 1943. This is indeed in the extension of the Plantage Kerklaan, but has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Laan der Hesperiden
origins.en: Figures from Greek mythology. Seven nymphs, who guard the tree with the golden apples in the land of Hesperia.

origins.name: Laan van Spartaan
origins.en: This lane is home to the accommodation of the Amsterdam football club VVA/Spartaan, founded in 1901.

origins.name: Laan van Vlaanderen
origins.en: The usual name for the Dutch-speaking region of Belgium, north of the language border. Named after the former county, which derives its name from a Carolingian province, pagus Flandrensis.

origins.name: Laanweg
origins.en: Originally this was a road with trees. When the Buiksloterham was drained in 1851, three roads came here: the 'road' (along the canal), the 'dike' (former Zeedijk) and this 'lane'. The Laanweg disappeared around 1970 due to demolition of the buildings and by raising this polder. The old name is now given to a section of ventweg from Ranonkelkade and Meidoornweg.

origins.name: Laarderhoogtweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Laren (North Holland).

origins.name: Laboratoriumstraat
origins.en: To the nearby Aviation Laboratory, where scientific experiments and observations are carried out for the benefit of aviation.

origins.name: Ladogameerhof
origins.en: The Ladagomeer (Ladozskojemeer), located in northern Russia near the border with Finland.

origins.name: Laing's Nekstraat
origins.en: Mountain pass in South Africa, also known as Langenek, known for Joubert's victory over the English in the First Boer War. The oldest part of the street (near the Ringvaart) has had several names over the years. Before 1896, that was Tweede Ringkadedwarsstraat, established by Nieuwer-Amstel. By council decision in 1901 that name was changed to Meerstraat and in 1912 this piece of street was pulled up near the Laing's Nekstraat.

origins.name: Lakenhalstraat
origins.en: The Stedelijk Museum De Lakenhal in Leiden, located in a building from 1640 by the city architect Arent van 's Gravesande. It was opened as a museum in 1874. Known for its historic collection of silver, glass, tin, tiles and paintings by famous Leideners.

origins.name: Lamarckhof
origins.en: Jean de Monet de Lamarck (1744-1827), French biologist who formulated the first modern theory of descent. Precursor of Darwin.

origins.name: Lambert Rimastraat
origins.en: Lambert Gregoire Rima (1907-1943), resistance fighter, born in The Hague, executed in Leusden. Rima was affiliated with the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Lamonggracht
origins.en: River on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Lampenistenstraat
origins.en: Occupational name: someone responsible for lighting and maintaining lamps, for example on board a ship or at a station.

origins.name: Lampongstraat
origins.en: During the period of Dutch administration over Indonesia, this was a residence in the south of Sumatra.

origins.name: Land van Cocagneplein
origins.en: Luilekkerland; Medieval legend about a land with food and drink in abundance, where you don't have to work.

origins.name: Landbouwstraat
origins.en: Cultivation of plant products for human and animal use.

origins.name: Landskroon
origins.en: Formerly outside with hunting lodge and falconry farm, from the seventeenth century, located on the Vecht under Muiden. Long ago demolished. Nowadays there is a farm with the same name on that site.

origins.name: Landsmeerderdijk
origins.en: To the village of Landsmeer. Until 1966, this part of the Waterland sea wall belonged to the municipality of Landsmeer.

origins.name: Landsteinerstraat
origins.en: Karl Landsteiner (1868-1943), Austrian - later American - pathologist. Discovered the blood groups and the rhesus factor, which made blood transfusion possible. Won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1930.

origins.name: Langbroekdreef
origins.en: Village in the province of Utrecht.

origins.name: Langbroekpad
origins.en: Village in the province of Utrecht.

origins.name: Lange Distelstraat
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Lange Leidsedwarsstraat
origins.en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date back to the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got this name because it led to the Leidsepoort. It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Lange Niezel
origins.en: The name is a corruption of liesdel = del or valley in which lies (lissen) grow. It was a swampy land north of the higher ground, on which the Old Church was built. In the second half of the fourteenth century, this low area was raised and built up. In one of the streets, the old name Liesdel remained alive. In the following centuries, this name became Niesdel and in the eighteenth century officially Niezel. In the sixteenth century, a street is extended in the direction of the old town, which after several other names finally takes the name Korte Niezel, while the oldest part takes the addition Lange.

origins.name: Lange Stammerdijk
origins.en: The road has been passed on under this name from the municipality of Weesperkarspel.

origins.name: Lange Vogelstraat
origins.en: The streets are located in the city district where the streets are named after birds. The neighborhood where these twelve streets are located is sometimes called the Bird Village.

origins.name: Lange Vonder
origins.en: Named after a long wooden bridge near Broek in Waterland over the outcrop of the Kerk Ee river into the Havenrak. A viaduct is a narrow wooden connection over a body of water.

origins.name: Langebrugsteeg
origins.en: Compared to the other streets that were laid out here between the canals, this street was exceptionally long

origins.name: Langestraat
origins.en: Compared to the other streets that were laid out here between the canals, this street was exceptionally long

origins.name: Langkatstraat
origins.en: Landscape on the east coast of the island of Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Langsom
origins.en: Name of a former mill water level in the Riekerpolder.

origins.name: Langswater
origins.en: Old Rhine-German name, occurring on the map of Floris Balthasar van Berkenrode from 1610. Langswater was a moat of the old Osdorp to the IJ, near Spieringhorn.

origins.name: Lanseloetstraat
origins.en: One of the main characters from the Abel play 'Lanseloet ende Sanderijn' (from around 1400).

origins.name: Lanzarotestraat
origins.en: Spanish island off the northwest coast of Africa, one of the Canary Islands.

origins.name: Laplacestraat
origins.en: Pierre Simon Marquis de Laplace (1749-1827), French mathematician and astronomer. Formulated the hypothesis that the solar system originated from a rotating gas ball.

origins.name: Larikslaan
origins.en: Tree of the coniferous family, which sheds its needles in winter. In the Netherlands, the Japanese variant is mainly found.

origins.name: Lascarpad
origins.en: The Lascar is the most active stratovolcano in the Andes (in Chile), with a height of 5,592 m

origins.name: Lassusstraat
origins.en: Orlando di Lasso (1532-1594), French spelling Roland de Lassus, born in Hainaut, chapel master in Rome, Antwerp and Munich. Wrote church and secular music. He is called the prince of music.

origins.name: Lastageweg
origins.en: The Lastage was originally land silted up by the sea outside the sea dyke, stretching between the Nieuwmarkt and the later Oudeschans. The name appears as early as 1342 and stayed in use into the eighteenth century. At first shipyards, warehouses and ropewalks settled here, and everything needed for ballasting, unloading and loading ships was made here. In the second half of the sixteenth century houses were built and streets laid out; in 1593 the area officially came within the city. The Lastageweg was named in 1931, after the clearance of the Jonker- and Ridderbuurt, and was made by widening the Tweede Jonker- and Tweede Ridderdwarsstraat.

origins.name: Latexweg
origins.en: Tropical product, raw material of rubber, that was dumped in the Amsterdam harbor.

origins.name: Latherusstraat
origins.en: The climbing plant, also called lathyrus, belonging to the family of the leguminous plants.

origins.name: Lau Mazirelstraat
origins.en: Laura Carola Mazirel (1907-1974), lawyer and prosecutor in Amsterdam. She campaigned for groups of people who were isolated in society. Before World War II, these were German refugees, after the war gypsies and homosexuals. During World War II, she was involved in both the children's daycare center of the Hollandse Schouwburg, where the Jewish population was concentrated for their deportation, and the resistance group around Gerrit van der Veen.

origins.name: Lauernessestraat
origins.en: Based on the novel by Bosboom-Toussaint from 1840, 'Het huis Lauernesse'.

origins.name: Lauriergracht
origins.en: The South European ornamental tree

origins.name: Laurierstraat
origins.en: The South European ornamental tree. (The canal was dug on the site of the old Kaatsbaanpad.)

origins.name: Lavendelstraat
origins.en: Halfheester, a balmaceous herb used in the perfumery industry.

origins.name: Lavoisierstraat
origins.en: Antoine L. Lavoisier (1743-1794), French chemist and one of the founders of modern chemistry.

origins.name: Le Mairekade
origins.en: Jacob le Maire (1585-1616), explorer. Discovered the sea route named after him at the southern tip of South America and the cape, which he called Cape Horn, to his hometown Hoorn. The Le Maire Street was projected and named in a different place on 20-11-1878, but that council decision was withdrawn on 19-8-1905.

origins.name: Le Mairestraat
origins.en: Jacob le Maire (1585-1616), explorer. Discovered the sea route named after him at the southern tip of South America and the cape, which he named Cape Horn, to his hometown Hoorn. The Le Mairestraat was projected and named at a different location on 20-11-1878, but that decision was withdrawn on 19-8-1905.

origins.name: Le Tourmalet
origins.en: Mountain peak in France, 2114 meters high.

origins.name: Lederambachtstraat
origins.en: As a result of the Saint Elizabeth flood in 1421, land near the Biesbosch drowned.

origins.name: Leen Jongewaardkade
origins.en: Leendert (Leen) Jongewaard (Amsterdam, March 30, 1927 - Nice, June 4, 1996) was a Dutch actor and singer who gained fame especially through his performances in the television series Ja zuster, nee zuster, 't Schaep met de 5 pooten and Citroentje met suiker and through his interpretations of songs such as In een rijtuigje, Op een mooie Pinksterdag and M'n opa

origins.name: Leendert Schijveschuurderstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1917-1941), involved in many illegal activities and participant in the February Strike in 1941.

origins.name: Leendert Valstarhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1896-1942), born in Delft, killed in concentration camp Buchenwald (Germany).

origins.name: Leenhofstraat
origins.en: Ferdinand Leenhoff (1841-1914), sculptor. Made, among other things, the statue of Thorbecke (1876) on Thorbeckeplein and that of Jan Pzn. Coen in Hoorn. He spent most of his life in France, where much of his sculpture can be found.

origins.name: Leerdamhof
origins.en: Place aan de Linge in South Holland, especially known for the glass industry.

origins.name: Leeuwarderweg
origins.en: The main road to the north, which leads via the Afsluitdijk to Leeuwarden. The Leeuwarderweg was part of the Buiksloterdijk before 1936. The Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg was built with the completion of the IJ tunnel.

origins.name: Leeuwendalersweg
origins.en: Country play by Vondel, written in honor of the Peace with Spain, and performed in the Amsterdam Schouwburg in 1648.

origins.name: Leeuwenhoekstraat
origins.en: Anthonie van Leeuwenhoek (1632-1723), correspondent of the Royal Society and inventor of the microscope. Saw bacteria for the first time.

origins.name: Leeuwenwerf
origins.en: The former shipyard 'De Gouden Leeuw', which used to be located here along the canal.

origins.name: Leeuwerikstraat
origins.en: Named after the skylark, a singing bird.

origins.name: Leghornstraat
origins.en: White chicken breed, which makes up a large part of the Dutch chicken flock. Leghorn is the English name for Livorno, so this chicken breed is of Italian origin.

origins.name: Legmeerplein
origins.en: A former peat bog, now a polder between Aalsmeer and Amstelveen, drained in 1874.

origins.name: Legmeerstraat
origins.en: A former peat bog, now a polder between Aalsmeer and Amstelveen, drained in 1874.

origins.name: Leibnizstraat
origins.en: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibnitz (1646-1716), German philosopher and statesman. Important thinker of the seventeenth century. Tried to bring the scholars of all countries into contact with each other. As a physicist, he independently developed calculus, independent of Newton.

origins.name: Leidekkerssteeg
origins.en: Named after a former resident Heinrich de Leydecker, who lived here in 1550. Previously, the alley is known as Graefmakerssteeg, which suggests that there may have once lived a grave digger.

origins.name: Leidsegracht
origins.en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date back to the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got this name because it led to the Leidsepoort. It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Leidsekade
origins.en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date back to the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got this name because it led to the Leidsepoort. It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Leidsekruisstraat
origins.en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date back to the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got this name because it led to the Leidsepoort. It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Leidseplein
origins.en: The city of Leiden.

origins.name: Leidsestraat
origins.en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date back to the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got this name because it ran up to the Leidsepoort. It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Leiduinstraat
origins.en: Country estate near Heemstede (North Holland).

origins.name: Leimuidenstraat
origins.en: Village between the Westeinder Plassen and the Braassemermeer in South Holland. The addition Kromme indicates the shape of the street.

origins.name: Lekkeresluis
origins.en: In the past, there were stalls at this fixed bridge, where among other things a 'pancake from the Lekkeresluis' was baked

origins.name: Leksmondhof
origins.en: The village of Lexmond or Leksmond aan de Lek (South Holland) is already mentioned in the twelfth century.

origins.name: Lekstraat
origins.en: Part of the Rhine between Wijk bij Duurstede and Krimpen.

origins.name: Leliegracht
origins.en: The namesake of all these streets is the oldest, namely the Oude Leliestraat, which is already mentioned in 1560. This derives its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Tower lock). The name passed on after 1612 to the canal dug along its extension and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets located in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Leliendaalstraat
origins.en: Named after the historic ship the Leliëndaal, with which enslaved people were transported in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Leliesluis
origins.en: The name of this permanent bridge is derived from the canal to which it is located. This canal in turn is named after the Old Leliestraat, which is already mentioned in 1560. This derived its name from the house 'In de Witte Lelye' on the Singel near the Tower Lock..

origins.name: Lemelerbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Lemele (Overijssel).

origins.name: Lemoenpad
origins.en: The equipment with which a horse was harnessed for a caravan. The street name refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Lentestraat
origins.en: The spring season. The street came in 1966, under the name Merwedestraat, from the then dissolved municipality of Weesperkarspel (council decision of Weesperkarspel, 1957).

origins.name: Leo Frijdahof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1923-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Bloemendaal.

origins.name: Leo Heijdenrijkstraat
origins.en: Leonardus Justinus Heijdenrijk (1932-1999) was a Dutch architect.

origins.name: Leo Hornstraat
origins.en: Leopold Silvain Horn (1916-1995), football referee. Played internationally between 1951 and 1966. Horn was Jewish and resistance fighter in World War II. Later successful businessman.

origins.name: Leo Smitstraat
origins.en: Dutch composer of Portuguese-Jewish descent (1900-1943). Studied at the Amsterdam Conservatory. He left a small but rich oeuvre, influenced by Ravel and Stravinsky. On April 27, 1943, he was transported to the Sobibor extermination camp, where he was killed on April 30.

origins.name: Leonard Bernsteinstraat
origins.en: American conductor and composer (1917-1989). Gained great fame with his musicals, including 'West Side Story'. Also composed operas, symphonies and concerts. Worked as conductor with all the major orchestras in the world.

origins.name: Leonard Springerbrug
origins.en: Leonard Antonij Springer (Amsterdam January 24, 1855 - Haarlem September 28, 1940) was a landscape architect who designed and landscaped more than 600 small and large gardens, city parks, country estates and cemeteries. In Amsterdam, among others, the Oosterpark, part of Frankendeal Park and the Nieuwe Ooster Cemetery.

origins.name: Leonardostraat
origins.en: Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519), Italian painter, sculptor and architect. Artist with great genius. The 'Last Supper' and the 'Mona Lisa' are by his hand.

origins.name: Leopoldstraat
origins.en: Jan Hendrik Leopold (1865-1925), poet and writer of literary studies. His verses testify to great loneliness.

origins.name: Lepelkruisstraat
origins.en: Nothing can be said with certainty about the origin of the name. It is likely that the name is derived from a facade stone. Lepelstraat was originally a short side street of Weesperstraat and until the middle of the eighteenth century officially Weesperdwarsstraat. At the end of the nineteenth century, Lepelstraat was extended in both directions on the grounds of the Veemarkt and the Stadswerf. Due to new construction along Weesperstraat, only the western part remains. The eastern part was renamed Lepelkruisstraat and Korte Lepelstraat in 1980.

origins.name: Lepelstraat
origins.en: Nothing can be said with certainty about the origin of the name. It is likely that the name is derived from a facade stone. The Lepelstraat was originally a short side street of the Weesperstraat and until the middle of the eighteenth century officially the Weesperdwarsstraat. At the end of the nineteenth century, the Lepelstraat was extended in both directions on the grounds of the Veemarkt and the Stadswerf. Due to new construction along Weesperstraat, only the western part remains. The eastern part was renamed Lepelkruisstraat and Korte Lepelstraat in 1980.

origins.name: Lesbosstraat
origins.en: Greek island in the Aegean Sea, off the coast of Turkey.

origins.name: Letelierstraat
origins.en: Orlando Letelier (1932-1976), Chilean Minister of Foreign Affairs under President Allende. He was arrested during Pinochet's coup d'état in 1973. After his release, he became the leader of the Chilean exiles. Through his contact with influential politicians in the United States, he posed a threat to the regime. Assassinated by the Chilean secret police.

origins.name: Leusdenhof
origins.en: Municipality in the province of Utrecht, known for the estate De Treek and the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Leuvenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Levantkade
origins.en: To the area of the Levant (the coasts of the Eastern Mediterranean, Syria, Egypt, Lebanon and Israel), on which the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a line service.

origins.name: Levantplein
origins.en: To the area of the Levant (the coasts of the Eastern Mediterranean, Syria, Egypt, Lebanon and Israel), on which the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a line service.

origins.name: Lex Althoffstraat
origins.en: Resistance hero and journalist (1904-1941), born in Haarlem, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Lia Doranastraat
origins.en: Lia Dorana, pseudonym of Beppy van Werven (1918 - 2010), was a Dutch cabaret performer, singer and actress

origins.name: Libau-eiland
origins.en: Old German name for Liepaja, now a Latvian port city. From here a lot of wood was shipped to Amsterdam in the past.

origins.name: Lichterstraat
origins.en: Inland waterway ship without its own propulsion, used for cargo transport.

origins.name: Lidewijdepad
origins.en: Novel by Busken Huet from 1868.

origins.name: Lidostraat
origins.en: Long island in the lagoon of Venice where large-scale renovation took place around 2012.

origins.name: Liendenhof
origins.en: Named after the village near Elst in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Liergouw
origins.en: The name de Liere already appears here in the seventeenth century according to a map by Gerrit Drogeham. Lier is a water name and also occurs in the Westland and south of Zwolle, among other places. The exact meaning of the name is unknown.

origins.name: Lies Bakhuyzenlaan
origins.en: Lies Bakhuyzen (1923-1997), secretary of the Sloten-Oud Osdorp Village Council, was committed to the Dutch Reformed Church and was a member of the Johanniter Order for almost twenty years, an organization that provides spiritual assistance to people in need. The lane, which runs from the Sloterweg to the Ringvaartdijk, is located near the former home of Lies Bakhuyzen.

origins.name: Liesdelsluis
origins.en: The Liesdel in the name of this permanent bridge means 'a low land covered with linden trees'

origins.name: Lieven de Keystraat
origins.en: Flemish builder (1560-1627), since 1591 in Haarlem. He built, among other things, the Meat Hall and the Waag in Haarlem.

origins.name: Lieven Keersemakerstraat
origins.en: Leader of the Geuzen (1528-1613) in the uprising against Spanish rule in Veere.

origins.name: Ligusterhof
origins.en: Plant genus from the olive family, widely used in hedges. The wild ligustrum is native to the Netherlands.

origins.name: Lijnbaansbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the Lijnbaanssteeg, in which it lies. This alley dates back to the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outer canal and the lineways of the rope-making works were located here on a kind of industrial site.

origins.name: Lijnbaansgracht
origins.en: The ropewalks of the rope-making works. The Linebaansteeg dates back to the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outer canal. The rope-making works needed a fairly large area for the exercise of its business. That could only be found on the outside of the city. The Linebaan lay on the city side of the canal, so within the rampart. The Lijnbaansgracht walked around the entire city. It is now filled in in a number of places and has been given other names there, such as Leidseplein, Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen, Frederiksplein, Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat, Valckenierstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

origins.name: Lijnbaanssteeg
origins.en: The ropewalks of the rope-making works. The Lijnbaanssteeg dates back to the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outer canal. The rope-making works needed a fairly large area for the exercise of its business. This could only be found on the outside of the city. The ropewalks were on the city side of the canal, so within the rampart. The Linebaansgracht ran around the entire city. It is now filled in in a number of places and has been given other names there, such as Leidseplein, Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen, Frederiksplein, Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat, Valckenierstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

origins.name: Lijndenstraat
origins.en: Frederik baron van Lijnden van Hemmen (1761-1845), fortification and hydraulic engineer and member of parliament. Wrote a treatise (in 1821) on the draining of the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Lijnoliestraat
origins.en: Reference to the Vettewinkel paint factory, later Sigma, which was located on the Cruquiusterrein from 1934 to 2008. Linseed oil, shortly before linseed oil, is a component of paints and a basis for varnish.

origins.name: Lijsterweg
origins.en: Named after the thrush, a singing bird.

origins.name: Lijzijde
origins.en: Ship's side, the side of the ship facing away from the wind.

origins.name: Limburghof
origins.en: The province. The nearby streets are named after Limburg castles.

origins.name: Limmenstraat
origins.en: Village in the North Holland region of Noord-Kennermerland.

origins.name: Limmerick
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the Irish port city Limerick, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Lindekersstraat
origins.en: Old cherry variety, also known as Early Rivers. Blooms early.

origins.name: Lindengracht
origins.en: Named after the linden (lime tree), a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Lindenhoevestraat
origins.en: Former eighteenth-century country house near the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, which was located approximately at this location.

origins.name: Lindenhoeveweg
origins.en: Former eighteenth-century country house near the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, which was located approximately at this location.

origins.name: Lindenstraat
origins.en: Named after the linden (lime tree), a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Linnaeusdwarsstraat
origins.en: Carl Linnaeus or Linnaeus (1707-1778), Swedish botanist, obtained his doctorate in 1735 from the University of Harderwijk. He was one of the first to design a systematics of the plant and animal world. Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg until 1878 (see under Oetewalerstraat). Even earlier, there was talk of Geldeloze pad. The Linnaeusdwarsstraat was still called Ipsenstraat in 1886, after J. Ipsen who had the first house built in this alley.

origins.en: Carl Linnaeus or Linnaeus (1707-1778), Swedish botanist, obtained his doctorate in 1735 from the University of Harderwijk. Even earlier, there was talk of Geldeloze pad. The Linnaeusdwarsstraat was still called Ipsenstraat in 1886, after J. Ipsen who had the first house built in this alley.

origins.en: Carl Linnaeus or Linnaeus (1707-1778), Swedish botanist, obtained his doctorate in 1735 at the University of Harderwijk. He was one of the first to design a systematics of the plant and animal world. The Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg until 1878 (see at Oetewalerstraat). Even earlier, there was talk of Geldeloze pad. The Linnaeusdwarsstraat was still called Ipsenstraat in 1886, after J. Ipsen who had the first house built in this alley.

origins.name: Linterhof
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Lipariweg
origins.en: Volcanic island northeast of Sicily, namesake of the island group in which Stromboli is located among others.

origins.name: Lippijnstraat
origins.en: Sotternie from the Middle Ages.

origins.name: Lirestraat
origins.en: The currency of Italy.

origins.name: Lisdoddelaan
origins.en: Aquatic plant, grows along the banks of streams, lakes and ponds.

origins.name: Lise Meitnerpad
origins.en: Elise Meitner (1878-1968), Austrian-Swedish physicist. Her specialties were radioactivity and nuclear physics. Led an investigation into nuclear fusion in uranium with the German chemist Otto Hahn (1879-1968) for which Meitner provided the justification in 1939. Hahn received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1944; Meitner's contribution was not recognized. Later rehabilitation followed, among other things, with the naming of the chemical element 109, discovered in 1982, as meitnerium.

origins.name: Litasweg
origins.en: The currency of Lithuania.

origins.name: Livornostraat
origins.en: The Italian city where the Dutch naval officer Jan van Galen defeated the English fleet in a naval battle in 1653.

origins.name: Lizzy Ansinghstraat
origins.en: Maria Elisabeth Georgine (Lizzy) Ansingh (1875-1959), painter. Especially known for her puppet plays. She belonged to the 'Amsterdam jesters'. Anslijnstraat, Nicolaas Osdorp council decision, 1959 14: l 6 Education reformer (1778-1838). Writer of school books, including 'De brave Hendrik'.

origins.name: Lloydplein
origins.en: Refers to the newly opened Llyod Hotel.

origins.name: Lobo-Braakensiekstraat
origins.en: Greta Lobo-Braakensiek, (1882-1926) and David Jessurun Lobo, (1884-1926) were famous theater actors. In addition, David was a director and translated some plays. The couple died in a train accident near Leiden.

origins.name: Locomotiefstraat
origins.en: In this area from 1913 to 2002 was the company Orenstein & Koppel that produced Railway Equipment. A locomotive is used to drive trains or rolling stock. In pulled trains, the locomotive pulls the train and can also push it

origins.name: Lodewijk Boisotstraat
origins.en: Admiral van Zeeland (1530-1576), served under William of Orange. Freed Leiden from the Spanish siege in 1572. Drowned in an attempt to free Zierikzee.

origins.name: Lodewijk Tripstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam merchant (1605-1684), several times mayor of Amsterdam. In 1665, together with his brother Hendrik, he had the 'Trippenhuis' built on the Kloveniersburgwal.

origins.name: Lodewijk van Duurenstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1917-1944), involved in the organization of the illegal newspaper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Loefzijde
origins.en: Ship's term, the side of the ship where the wind is blowing.

origins.name: Loenendreef
origins.en: The village on the Vecht (Utrecht).

origins.name: Loenermark
origins.en: Together with the Loenense Bos, an extensive nature reserve on the Veluwe.

origins.name: Loenermarkbrug
origins.en: Together with the Loenense Bos, an extensive nature reserve on the Veluwe.

origins.name: Loet C. Barnstijnstraat
origins.en: Born Lodewijk Cohen (1880-1953). Called himself Loet C. Barnstijn after his mother to distinguish himself from others with the name Cohen. Film distributor and producer. Started a cinema in The Hague in 1912. Founder of the famous Filmstad studios.

origins.name: Loevestein
origins.en: Old castle on the junction of Maas and Waal in Poederooien (Gelderland), founded by Dirckhoef. It has never been inhabited by a noble family. In the seventeenth century it was a prison where many famous figures had been imprisoned, including Hugo de Groot. The castle therefore had the nickname: the Dutch Tower.

origins.name: Loggerhof
origins.en: Fast-sailing fishing vessel with sharp bow.

origins.name: Lohuis
origins.en: Nature monument located southeast of Aalten (Gelderland), consisting of forests with heathland.

origins.name: Lokerenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of East Flanders.

origins.name: Lomanstraat
origins.en: Abraham Dirk Loman (1823-1897), theologian and writer. Edited the Old Dutch songs, collected by Valerius.

origins.name: Lombokstraat
origins.en: One of the small Sunda islands (Indonesia).

origins.name: Lommelstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Lomondlaan
