origins.en: The lake, Loch Lomond, located on the border of Central and Strathclyde region in western Scotland.

origins.name: Lontarpalmstraat
origins.en: Palm species. Lontar comes from 'rontal', a combination of two old Javanese words, ron (leaf) and tal (tree). Due to the shape of the leaves, spread out like a fan, the rontal tree is also called fan palm.

origins.name: Loodskotterhof
origins.en: Coastal vessel that brings and retrieves the dock from and to the ships.

origins.name: Looiersgracht
origins.en: The tanneries and the leather trade, to which these and the nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal belt are named, were first located outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came within the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after those long-established businesses, starting with the Runstraat and the Huidenstraat. After 1658, the tanneries spread out to areas east of the Vijzelgracht, where we now find the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat. The Third Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision, 1898) for filling in. For the Drowned Nieuwe Looierssloot,

origins.name: Loosdrechtdreef
origins.en: The villages of Oud- and Nieuw-Loosdrecht (Utrecht).

origins.name: Loosduinenstraat
origins.en: Village in South Holland, south of The Hague and annexed to The Hague in 1923.

origins.name: Lootsstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Loots (1765-1834), Amsterdam broker, who devoted himself to poetry. His poems were collected and published after his death.

origins.name: Loowaard
origins.en: Country house near Duiven (Gelderland), dating from around 1550.

origins.name: Lopikhof
origins.en: Village in the Lopikerwaard (Utrecht) between Lek and Hollandse IJssel. It derives its name from a bog stream, which originally was called Lobeke.

origins.name: Lord Kelvinstraat
origins.en: Sir William Thomson alias Lord Kelvin (1824-1907), English physicist, founder of thermodynamics. Designed many electrical measuring instruments and discovered the element argon.

origins.name: Lorentzlaan
origins.en: Hendrik Anton Lorentz (1853-1928), physicist. Founder of the electron theory. Received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1902.

origins.name: Lorreinenstraat
origins.en: Frankish knightly novel from the twelfth or thirteenth century: rhymed story about the time of Charlemagne.

origins.name: Lou Jansenplein
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1900-1943), by profession office clerk, born in Amsterdam, executed in The Hague.

origins.name: Louis Apolstraat
origins.en: Painter (1850-1936), known for his winter scenes.

origins.name: Louis Armstrongstraat
origins.en: Louis Daniel Armstrong (1900-1971), American trumpeter, singer and jazz orchestra conductor. One of the most important figures in the history of jazz music.

origins.name: Louis Bouwmeesterstraat
origins.en: Louis Frederik Johannes Bouwmeester (1841-1925), actor. Worked for many years at the Vereeniging Het Nederlandsch Toneel and founded the Haarlemsch Toneel in 1903. Specialized mainly in the classical genre.

origins.name: Louis Chrispijnstraat
origins.en: Father Louis Chrispijn sr. (1854-1926), gifted actor and director and son Louis Chrispijn jr. (1878-1931), actor who excelled especially in the comedic genre.

origins.name: Louis Couperusstraat
origins.en: Louis Marie Anne Couperus (1863-1923), literary critic. Wrote numerous psychological and historical novels and a large number of essays, letters and journalistic work. Known for his dandyism, aesthetics and fatalism.

origins.name: Louis Davidsstraat
origins.en: Artist name of Simon David (1883-1939), revue artist and chansonnier. Known for his life songs. Also wrote revues, in which his sister Henriëtte Davids (deceased 1975) performed.

origins.name: Louis de Visserstraat
origins.en: Louis Leonardus Hendrikus de Visser (1878-1945), politician, originally a member of the SDAP, later a communist. He was chairman of the Communist Party from 1925 to 1935 and a member of the House of Representatives from 1925 to 1940. In 1941 he was arrested and deported to the Neuengamme concentration camp, where he died shortly before the liberation.

origins.name: Louis J. Welterbrug
origins.en: Mr. Louis J. Welter (1910 - 1943) was active under the alias 'Kriek' in the Javanese resistance during the Japanese occupation of Dutch East Indies (1942 - 1945). He compiled a report with military information, which could have accelerated an Allied invasion. He also helped build an illegal transmitter near Bandung. This was almost operational when he was arrested in September 1942. In May 1943, he was sentenced to death and beheaded.

origins.name: Louis Moorhof
origins.en: Louis Barth. Joh. Moor (1856-1937), actor, who mainly played in the French Comedy. He also gained fame as a director and translator of foreign plays.

origins.name: Louis Naarstigstraat
origins.en: AIoysius Christiaan Naarstig (1895-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Louis Raemaekersstraat
origins.en: Drawer of political cartoons (1869-1956), for many years permanent illustrator of the daily newspaper 'De Telegraaf'.

origins.name: Louis Schottingstraat
origins.en: Journalist (1870-1957), as a reporter affiliated with the 'Algemeen Handelsblad'. He was for many years the elder statesman of the council reporters of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Louise de Colignystraat
origins.en: Fourth wife of Prince William of Orange (1555-1620). Mother of Prince Frederick Henry.

origins.name: Louise Marie Loeberplantsoen
origins.en: Painter (1894-1983). Visited the Rijksakademie in Amsterdam, her birthplace, between 1915 and 1918. Worked in an abstract-figurative and non-figurative style.

origins.name: Louise Wentstraat
origins.en: Louise Went (1865-1951), one of the founders of the Amsterdam Building Fund Association. In 1895 she conducted an investigation into the living conditions in the Jordaan for the Jordaan Construction Company.

origins.name: Louvrelaan
origins.en: Palais, later Musée du Louvre in Paris. Construction, begun in the sixteenth century, has been worked on for centuries by various architects. The origin of the collection is the art treasures of Louis XV. The royal collection was greatly expanded by Napoleon. Most important museum in France.

origins.name: Louweshoek
origins.en: Stefan Louwes (1889-1953), agricultural consultant. Head of food supply during World War II. By council decision in 1960, the road has been shortened a lot.

origins.name: Louwesweg
origins.en: Stefan Louwes (1889-1953), agricultural consultant. Head of food supply during World War II. By council decision in 1960, the road has been shortened a lot.

origins.name: Lübeckbrug
origins.en: Lübeck is a Hanseatic city in the German state of Schleswig-Holstein. The names in the Harbors are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries

origins.name: Lucellestraat
origins.en: Play by Brederode from 1616, dedicated to Maria Tesselschade.

origins.name: Luchtvaartstraat
origins.en: The traffic with means of transport by air. The name was given in connection with the nearby Aviation Laboratory.

origins.name: Lucien Gaudinstraat
origins.en: French fencer, won a gold medal at the Olympic Games in Paris in 1924.

origins.name: Ludovicus Imminkpad
origins.en: Ludovicus lmmink (1822-1869) mainly designed for the Zaanstreek but is known in Amsterdam for the Nieuwendammerkerk. For this neighborhood, the category names of Dutch architects who have been involved in housing projects in Amsterdam-North were chosen.

origins.name: Luiksingel
origins.en: Belgian city, located in the province of Liège.

origins.name: Lumeijstraat
origins.en: Willem van Lumey (1542-1576), leader of the Water Geuzen for Den Briel in 1572. Then appointed lieutenant and governor of Holland by William of Orange. Finally dismissed for his atrocities. The street was renamed Emmastraat by the municipality of Sloten (council decision of Sloten, 1911), but these and other names were changed after the annexation of 1921, because they already existed elsewhere in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Lumièrestraat
origins.en: Auguste Marie Louis Nicholas Lumière (1862-1954) and Louis Jean Lumière (1864-1948), French film pioneers. With the invention of the cinematograph, an apparatus that combined film camera and film projector, the Lumière brothers are among the founders of cinematography.

origins.name: Lupineplein
origins.en: The plant, used as an ornamental plant and grown as fertilizer for sandy soil due to the nitrogen nodules.

origins.name: Lupinestraat
origins.en: The plant, used as an ornamental plant and grown as fertilizer for sandy soil due to the nitrogen nodules.

origins.name: Luthuliplein
origins.en: The South African Albert John Luthuli (1898-1967), former president of the African National Congress (ANC), until the 1950s the main spokesman for the nonviolent resistance against apartheid. In 1960 he received the Nobel Peace Prize.

origins.name: Lutkemeerweg
origins.en: Named after the Lutkemeer, which was dried up here in 1865 (Lutke = small).

origins.name: Lutmastraat
origins.en: Janus Lutma (1588-1669), gold and silversmith. Part of this street was transferred from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel in 1896 as the Ruyterstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890), while another part bore the name Lutmaplein until 1924 (council decision, 1917).

origins.name: Luttenbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Raalte (Overijssel).

origins.name: Luvernes
origins.en: The Scottish port city of Inverness, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Luyendijkje
origins.en: The path was laid out on a low summer dike, which had this name for centuries and runs through the municipality of Landsmeer under the same name. The name 'luyendijk' is the same as 'looidijk' and was given to a rear embankment, which had to prevent water from the adjacent area from entering. In this case, it is a embankment along the border with Oostzaan, laid out at the end of the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Luzacstraat
origins.en: Louis Caspar Luzac (1786-1861), statesman. Minister of the Interior, who helped prepare the 1848 constitutional revision.

origins.name: Lyceumbrug
origins.en: The name of this bridge refers to the nearby Amsterdam Lyceum

origins.name: M. Berdenis van Berlekomstraat
origins.en: Mathilde Wibaut-Berdenis of Berlekom (1862-1952), socialist and feminist. Founded a branch of the Association for Women's Suffrage in Middelburg in 1895. Advocate for universal women's suffrage. Married to alderman F.M. Wibaut, with whom she wrote the book 'Becoming marriage'.

origins.name: M. Gandhilaan
origins.en: Mohandas (Mahatma) Karamchand Gandhi (1869-1948), leader of the nonviolent resistance in India that led to the country's independence in 1947. In addition to opposing the British ruler, he advocated a boycott of imported goods. Often he was arrested for his actions and murdered shortly after independence.

origins.name: M. Hanenbergstraat
origins.en: Matthijs Abel Joannes Hanenberg (1781-1838), from 1815 first sheriff, then until 1837 mayor of the municipalities of Sloten, Sloterdijk, Osdorp and the Vrije Geer.

origins.name: M.C. Addicksstraat
origins.en: Martinus Casimir Addicks (1887-1941), born in Amersfoort. One of the first victims of the resistance during the German occupation, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: M.J. Granpré Molièreplein
origins.en: Marinus Jan Granpré Molière (1883-1972), architect. Founder of the 'Delft School', which wanted to establish a connection between traditional and modern architecture. He designed expansion plans for many Dutch cities, built, among other things, the town halls of Naaldwijk, Zwijndrecht and Uithoorn. Also designer of the church located on the square.

origins.name: M.J.E. Lippitsstraat
origins.en: Meinardus Johannes Elias Lippits (1869-1941), architect. Designed housing blocks in Amsterdam-North according to the garden city layout. Was also involved in the construction of the Schiller Hotel on Rembrandtplein.

origins.name: Ma Braunpad
origins.en: Mrs. M.J. Braun-Voorwinde (1883-1956), Rotterdam swimming instructor, who continues to live on as Ma Braun as one of the pioneers of swimming in our country. She trained the first Dutch women who successfully participated in the Olympic Games from 1924 onwards.

origins.name: Maagdenpalmstraat
origins.en: Plant family in particularly warm, but sometimes also temperate regions. The pink maiden palm contains substances that are processed into cancer drugs. The extract of the small maiden palm native to the Netherlands can be used as a gargling drink and as a remedy for diarrhea.

origins.name: Maanhof
origins.en: The celestial body, which moves in an elliptical orbit around the earth.

origins.name: Maanstraat
origins.en: The celestial body, which moves in an elliptical orbit around the earth.

origins.name: Maarkedalpad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Maarsenhof
origins.en: Village on the Vecht (Utrecht).

origins.name: Maarten Harpertszoon Trompstraat
origins.en: Dutch admiral (1597-1653), who defeated the Spanish fleet at Duins in 1639. He died in the naval battle at Terheide against the English.

origins.name: Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat
origins.en: Lived from around 1520 to 1592. From 1567 to 1576 physician to the king of Denmark and Norway, Frederick II. In 1578 one of the main figures of the Alteration (the silent revolution in Amsterdam in which the Spanish-minded mayors were removed outside the city walls). From that year on, Koster was mayor of Amsterdam several times, during which periods he continued to practice his medical practice. He gave the first public anatomy lessons. The street was called Amstelgrachtje before 1872, renamed in 1866. Even earlier it was part of the Lijnbaansgracht.

origins.name: Maasdrielhof
origins.en: Village on the Maas in Gelderland.

origins.name: Maaseikpad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Maaseikstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Maaslandstraat
origins.en: South Holland village in the municipality of Midden-Delfland.

origins.name: Maassluisstraat
origins.en: City on the Nieuwe Waterweg (South Holland).

origins.name: Maasstraat
origins.en: The river, which springs up in France and flows through our country from Maastricht.

origins.name: Madelievenstraat
origins.en: The meadow flower, belonging to the family of composites.

origins.name: Madurastraat
origins.en: Island located north of Java (Indonesia).

origins.name: Magalhaensplein
origins.en: Fernando de Magalhaens or Magalhaes (1480-1521) Portuguese sailor. Discovered the sea route named after him between South America and Tierra del Fuego in 1520 and crossed the Pacific Ocean to the Philippines first from there.

origins.name: Magalhaensstraat
origins.en: Fernando de Magalhaens or Magalhaes (1480-1521) Portuguese sailor. Discovered the sea route named after him between South America and Tierra del Fuego in 1520 and crossed the Pacific Ocean to the Philippines first from there.

origins.name: Magersfonteinstraat
origins.en: Place in South Africa (Orange Free State), known for the victory of the Boers over the English in the Boer War (1899-1902).

origins.name: Magneetstraat
origins.en: The electro-magnet is meant: an not entirely closed iron circuit, on which coils are attached and where direct current is passed through.

origins.name: Magnoliastraat
origins.en: A ornamental tree, which blooms before the leaves appear.

origins.name: Mainhavenweg
origins.en: Side river of the Rhine, to which the city of Mainz is located.

origins.name: Majanggracht
origins.en: River on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Majoie Hajarystraat
origins.en: Majoie Hajary (August 16, 1921 Paramaribo - August 25, 2017 Neuilly-sur-Seine) was a composer from a multicultural family. She gained fame with her musical work with which she conveyed, among other things, the value of a diverse society.

origins.name: Majoor Bosshardtbrug
origins.en: Alida Margaretha Bosshardt (1913-2007) became known for her work for the Salvation Army, which took place largely in the immediate vicinity of this bridge. She also founded the Goodwill Center here in the Wallows. In 2009, she was elected as the 'Greatest Amsterdammer of all time'. The 'major' (who was actually a lieutenant colonel) was a real bridge builder between various groups and that is why a bridge name naming was preferred over a street name naming

origins.name: Majoor Fransweg
origins.en: Name of the 1874 epistolary novel by Bosboom-Toussaint.

origins.name: Majubastraat
origins.en: Amajuba or Majuba, a Zulu word for pigeon hill, was a mountain peak on the border of Transvaal and Orange Free State, known from the First Boer War (1880-1881).

origins.name: Makassarplein
origins.en: Indonesian port city, located on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes). Now called Ujung Pandang.

origins.name: Makassarstraat
origins.en: Indonesian port city, located on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes). Now called Ujung Pandang.

origins.name: Makersstraat
origins.en: Refers to an area within Strandeiland where many creative companies in the manufacturing industry can establish themselves.

origins.name: Maldenhof
origins.en: The village on the Maas-Waal canal (Gelderland).

origins.name: Maliebaan
origins.en: The name recalls the 'Maliebaen', which used to be located near the Schagerlaan in the past. A maliebaan is a playground for a game that resembles a plunger and was played with a kind of long iron hammers and wooden balls.

origins.name: Maltaweg
origins.en: Island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Malvastraat
origins.en: Plant genus, more commonly known as cheese herb.

origins.name: Mandarijnenstraat
origins.en: Named after the mandarin, a fruit.

origins.name: Mandenmakerspad
origins.en: Originally a typical traveling profession. The name is related to the caravan world and refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Manegestraat
origins.en: To the French riding school, which stood here from 1761 to 1881.

origins.name: Manenburgstraat
origins.en: A former eighteenth-century country house on Kruislaan on the site of the current Nieuwe Ooster Cemetery.

origins.name: Manna de Wijs-Moutonhof
origins.en: Writer of cabaret songs (1873-1947). Also performed herself in the cabaret, bringing her own songs.

origins.name: Maputoweg
origins.en: Port city, capital of Mozambique. The street is located near the Africa Harbor in the Western Harbor Area.

origins.name: Marathonweg
origins.en: Originally a village on the east coast of Attica (Greece), where the Persians were defeated in 490 BC. Diomedon brought this news to Athens (42 km) in a short time. This event is named the Marathon race.

origins.name: Marcantilaan
origins.en: Marcanti is the former name of the congress center 'De Hoeksteen' next to the entrance of the Centrale Markt and located opposite this alley. Marcanti is a contraction of MarktCantine, the original function of the building dating back to 1933.

origins.name: Marcellus Emantsstraat
origins.en: Poet, novelist and playwright (1848-1923). Precursor of the Eighties. His work is strongly somber in tone.

origins.name: Marchanthof
origins.en: Hendrik Pieter (Henri) Marchant (1869-1956), statesman. One of the founders of the Free Democratic Union and, among other things, Minister of Education, Arts and Sciences under Prime Minister Colijn. The New Spelling of 1933 is named after him.

origins.name: Marco Polostraat
origins.en: Venetian world traveler (1254-1323). Lived for a quarter of a century among the Chinese, known for his travel stories.

origins.name: Marconistraat
origins.en: The Italian engineer Guilielmo Marconi (1874-1937), who invented wireless telegraphy in 1896. In 1909 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

origins.name: Marcusstraat
origins.en: Balthazar Jan Fred. Marcus (1806-1865), mayor of the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, to which this street belonged until 1896.

origins.name: Marga Klompélaan
origins.en: Margaretha Albertina Maria Klompé (1912-1986), politician, member of the KVP. She was the first female minister in the Netherlands, when she became Minister of Social Work in 1956. With a three-year break, she remained so until 1971. That year she was appointed Minister of State.

origins.name: Marguerite Yourcenarstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of the Frenchwoman Marguerite Cleenewerck de Crayencour (1903-1987), writer. Taught French literature in the US from 1942 to 1950 and from 1952 to 1953, where she finally settled. Yourcenar practiced all literary genres and was also an excellent translator.

origins.name: Maria Austriastraat
origins.en: Artist name of the Czech-Jewish photographer Marie Karoline Oestreicher (1915-1975), who settled in Amsterdam before the war. Was active in the resistance during the war. In 1945 co-founder of photo agency Particam (Partisans Camera). Her theater photos and portraits of musicians, actors, dancers, directors and writers are well known.

origins.name: Maria Beshof
origins.en: Maria Elisabeth Bes was the first female student at the Polytechnic School in Delft (now TU Delft) and the first female chemical engineer.

origins.name: Maria Montessoristraat
origins.en: Italian doctor (1870-1952), who gained great fame as an educator due to her teaching method, based on the free individual development of the child.

origins.name: Maria Snelplantsoen
origins.en: Maria Dina Snel (1890-1941), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, died in the prison of Scheveningen. She had a share in the distribution of the illegal newspaper 'Vrij Nederland'.

origins.name: Maria Ulfahstraat
origins.en: Maria Ulfah Santoso (Serang 1911 - Jakarta 1988), after the execution of her husband by Dutch troops in February 1949 remarried and known as Maria Ulfah Soebadio. Maria Ulfah, of aristocratic family, was the first Indonesian woman to complete her law studies in the Netherlands (1929-1933). She campaigned for the emancipation of Indonesian women in various boards, among other things as president of the Indonesian Women's Federation Kowani. She was the first woman to hold a ministerial position - of social affairs in the second and third Sjahrir cabinet (1946-1947)

origins.name: Mariadistelkade
origins.en: The milk thistle (Silybum marianum) is a one- or two-year plant that belongs to the composite family (Asteraceae).

origins.name: Marianellastraat
origins.en: Marianella Garcia Villas (1949-1983), chairwoman of the Commission for Human Rights in El Salvador since its establishment in 1973. The government saw her as a terrorist, forcing her to leave the country. From Mexico, she continued her work. Taken prisoner and murdered by the army in 1983.

origins.name: Marianne Hilaridesplantsoen
origins.en: Marianne Hilarides was a Dutch ballet dancer. She was a student of Sonia Gaskell and made her debut at the Ballet Recital in 1950, where she was given solo roles to dance, including the pas de deux in Le Cygne Noir.

origins.name: Marianne Philipsstraat
origins.en: Marianne Goudeket born Philips (1866-1950), novelist. She wrote, among other things, 'Wedding in Europe' and 'The Confession'.

origins.name: Marie Altelaarplein
origins.en: Neighborhood activist, feminist and communist (1917-2005), nicknamed Aunt Marie. Driving force behind a fifteen-year campaign against high rent prices on the Eastern Islands in the 1970s and 1980s of the previous century.

origins.name: Marie Baronlaan
origins.en: Marie Baron participated in the 1924 modern Olympic Games in Paris as a swimmer at the age of 16.

origins.name: Marie Heinekenplein
origins.en: Painteress (1844-1930), she mainly painted flowers and still lifes. Between 1883 and 1899 she had several exhibitions in Amsterdam. She was a member of the Amsterdam artist society 'Arti et Amicitiae'.

origins.name: Marie van Westerhovenstraat
origins.en: Actress (1857-1946), married to Louis Chrispijn. She has been on stage for more than sixty years. Also performed in operette for many years.

origins.name: Marieken van Nimwegenstraat
origins.en: Name of a miracle play from the fifteenth century.

origins.name: Mariëndaal
origins.en: Country estate, consisting of a 19th-century country house with nature reserve, located between Arnhem and Oosterbeek.

origins.name: Marifoonweg
origins.en: Mobile phone for use in water.

origins.name: Marinierskade
origins.en: To the nearby Marine Barracks.

origins.name: Mariotteplein
origins.en: Edme Mariotte (1620-1684), French physicist. Discovered the colored rings around the sun and moon and the blind spot in the eye.

origins.name: Mariottestraat
origins.en: Edme Mariotte (1620-1684), French physicist. Discovered the colored rings around the sun and moon and the blind spot in the eye.

origins.name: Maritzstraat
origins.en: Gerrit Maritz (1797-1839), one of the leaders of the Great Trek of the Boers in South Africa in 1835 and the following years. Defeated the Matabele in 1937. The boys' book Pieter Maritz and the place name Pieter Maritzburg have nothing to do with a historical figure with that name. It is a contraction of the two pioneers Gerrit Maritz and Pieter Retief.

origins.name: Marius Bauerplantsoen
origins.en: Marius A.J. Bauer (1867-1932), painter and engraver. Due to his many Eastern travels, his engravings are marked by oriental fantasy.

origins.name: Marius Bauerstraat
origins.en: Marius A.J. Bauer (1867-1932), painter and engraver. Due to his many Eastern travels, his engravings are marked by oriental fantasy.

origins.name: Marius Meijboomstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1911-1998), had a famous photo studio in Amsterdam and mainly made portraits, fashion and advertising photos. Known for his photos of the Royal family. During the war he was part of the photography group, which later became known as 'De Ondergedoken Camera'.

origins.name: Marius van Bouwdijk Bastiaansestraat
origins.en: Marius A. van Bouwdijk Bastiaanse (1886-1964), gynecologist affiliated with the Wilhelminagasthuis and professor at the University of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Marjoleinstraat
origins.en: The shrub, which is used as a herb.

origins.name: Markelerbergpad
origins.en: Markelergberpad, Refers to the Markelerberg, a hill of 66 meters located in the municipality of Hof van Twente.

origins.name: Markengouw
origins.en: The village and the former island of that name (North Holland).

origins.name: Markerveld
origins.en: Polder near Uitgeest (North Holland), created in 1637.

origins.name: Markiespad
origins.en: The fabric canopy above the entrance of a caravan. The street name refers to the caravan park on site.

origins.name: Markonstraat
origins.en: This was probably a former country house on the Amstel

origins.name: Marksingel
origins.en: The currency of Germany and Finland.

origins.name: Marmolada
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3354 meters high.

origins.name: Marnixkade
origins.en: Philip of Marnix, lord of Sint Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and advisor of Prince William of Orange, author of the Union of the Nobles (1568). Possibly poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, formerly called Schans, was laid out after 1850 on the site where the city walls used to be, which were demolished between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Marnixplein
origins.en: Philip of Marnix, lord of Sint Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and advisor of Prince William of Orange, author of the Union of the Nobles (1568). Possibly poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, formerly called Schans, was laid out after 1850 on the site where the city walls used to be, which were demolished between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Marnixstraat
origins.en: Philip of Marnix, lord of Sint Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and advisor of Prince William of Orange, compiler of the Union of the Nobles (1568). Possibly poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, previously called Schans, was built after 1850 on the site where the city walls used to be, which were demolished between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Maroastraat
origins.en: Volcano in New Zealand

origins.name: Marowijnestraat
origins.en: River in Suriname, on the border of French Guiana.

origins.name: Marquette
origins.en: Castle in Heemskerk, so named since 1612 after Daniel de Hortaing, lord of Marquette. The castle dates back to the fourteenth century and was at the time a strong stronghold of the Kabeljauwen. The current form dates largely from 1741.

origins.name: Marskramerstraat
origins.en: Originally a typical traveling profession. Street vendor who carries his goods in a basket on his back. The name is related to the caravan world and refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Marsmanstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Marsman (1899-1940), poet. In 1940 he fled to England, but the ship ran aground on a mine. Marsman was one of the victims.

origins.name: Marsstraat
origins.en: The planet.

origins.name: Martelaarsgracht
origins.en: Probably named after a house, where the 'martyr' was hanged. Before the filling in, the water from the Nieuwezijds Voor- and Achterburgwal flowed here in the IJ. Only on the even side was there a quay at that time. The bridge in the Nieuwendijk over this canal was called the Martelaarsbrug.

origins.name: Marten Corverhof
origins.en: Actor and theater reformer (1727-1794).

origins.name: Marten Toonderbrug
origins.en: Marten Toonder (Rotterdam, May 2, 1912 – Laren, July 27, 2005) was a Dutch comic book writer. In addition to his great role in literature, Toonder also used his talents during World War II.

origins.name: Martien Coppenshof
origins.en: Martinus Franciscus Josephus Coppens (1908-1986), photographer. Mainly known for his photos of Brabant farmer families. In addition to people, he also photographed churches, cathedrals and landscapes.

origins.name: Martin Cortesstraat
origins.en: Spanish master navigator (1532-1589). In 1551 he wrote the navigation handbook 'Breve Compendio de la Sphera y de la Arte de Navegar', which appeared in English in 1561 as 'The Arte of Navigation' and became popular among English sailors.

origins.name: Martin Ennalsplein
origins.en: Defender of human rights (1927-1991). In the 1970s, secretary-general of Amnesty International and involved in the founding of many other human rights organizations. Under his leadership, Amnesty's field of work was expanded with campaigns against torture, the death penalty, extrajudicial executions and disappearances.

origins.name: Martin Ennalsstraat
origins.en: Defender of human rights (1927-1991). In the 1970s, secretary-general of Amnesty International and involved in the founding of many other human rights organizations. Under his leadership, Amnesty's field of work was expanded with campaigns against torture, the death penalty, extrajudicial executions and disappearances.

origins.name: Martin Luther Kingpark
origins.en: American preacher (1929-1968), internationally known for his fight against poverty and discrimination, was murdered on April 4, 1968 in Memphis (U.S.A.). Before 1968, the park was called Amstelpark (council decision, 1949), which name was later given to another park. The name change took place at the request of the Pacifist Socialist Party (PSP).

origins.name: Martin Niemöllerstraat
origins.en: German pastor (1892-1984) and peace activist. The 'Confessing Church' he founded openly opposed Hitler. Was arrested in 1937 and held in concentration camps as 'personal prisoner' of Hitler until 1945. After the war he advocated for international reconciliation and against armament.

origins.name: Martin Vlaarkade
origins.en: Martinus Vlaar (1904-1975), one of the organizers of the February Strike in 1941, was arrested shortly after and liberated by American troops in 1945. After that, he was very active in the Spaarndammer neighborhood.

origins.name: Martini van Geffenstraat
origins.en: Mr. Frans Willem H.P.J. Martini van Geffen (1832-1883), mayor of the municipality of Sloten from 1881 to 1883.

origins.name: Martinus Jan Langeveldstraat
origins.en: Pedagogue (1905-1989), student of Philip Kohnstamm among others. Langeveld is considered one of the most important educators of the second half of the twentieth century.

origins.name: Martinus Nijhoffstraat
origins.en: Poet and essayist (1894-1953). Known critic and editor of 'De Gids'. Belonged to the greats of his contemporaries.

origins.name: Mary van der Sluisstraat
origins.en: Mary Meijer-van der Sluis (1917-1994), fencer. Dutch champion in 1937 and 1947 and participant in the Olympic Games in 1948. Had to temporarily suspend her sports career during the war due to her Jewish heritage.

origins.name: Mary Zeldenruststraat
origins.en: Mary Zeldenrust-Noordanus (1928-1984), psychologist. She was committed to sexual emancipation and women's emancipation. Founder of the Institute for Psychological Market Research.

origins.name: Mastbos
origins.en: A natural monument near Breda.

origins.name: Masthof
origins.en: The ship part.

origins.name: Mata Harihof
origins.en: Artist name of the Frisian Margaretha Geertruida Zelle (1876-1917). Mata Hari is Malay for 'eye of the day'. Oriental dancer, among others in Paris, and spy during World War I. Due to her espionage activities directed against the Germans, she was sentenced to death and executed in 1917. Five films were made about her life in different countries.

origins.name: Mataramstraat
origins.en: Province on the island of Java (Indonesia) during the Dutch administration. Originally it was a separate kingdom on Java. It has also been the name of a principality that existed until 1894 on the island of Lombok.

origins.name: Matenesse-hof
origins.en: A thirteenth-century castle on the Schie in the old craft of Mathenesse. Today it is a Rotterdam neighborhood.

origins.name: Mathurastraat
origins.en: One of the three main fighters, who resisted the repressive system on the plantations in Suriname through the so-called 'Fonale Sankties'.

origins.name: Matrozenhof
origins.en: References the nearby maritime training institute.

origins.name: Mattenbiesstraat
origins.en: Reed species, grows on the banks of sweet and brackish waters.

origins.name: Matterhorn
origins.en: Mountain, located in Switzerland and Italy, 4477 meters high.

origins.name: Mattheus Sladushof
origins.en: Language scholar (1569-1629), specializing in Hebrew and Arabic.

origins.name: Maurice Peeterspad
origins.en: Mauritius Prosper Peeters (1882-1957), cyclist. Became the Netherlands' first Olympic cycling champion by winning the sprint event in Antwerp in 1920. Four years later, he won bronze in the tandem in Paris.

origins.name: Maurice Ravellaan
origins.en: Joseph Maurice Ravel (1875-1937), French composer, conductor and pianist of Swiss and Basque descent. Considered with contemporary Claude Debussy (1862-1918) as the main impressionist component. His most famous work is the ballet 'Boléro' (1928).

origins.name: Maurits Kannstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1894-1942), by profession lawyer, born in The Hague, killed in the Sachsenhausen concentration camp.

origins.name: Maurits Sabbehof
origins.en: Flemish literary writer (1873-1938), writer of novels, literary reviews and plays. In 1923 professor in Brussels and curator of the Plantin Museum in Antwerp.

origins.name: Mauritskade
origins.en: Maurits, Prince of Orange (1567-1625), from 1585 stadtholder of Holland and Zeeland, later of all seven provinces. The quay originally formed part of the Buitensingel.

origins.name: Mauritsstraat
origins.en: In the past, there was also a Mauritsstraat (council decision, 1880) here. It ran through to the Rhijnspoorplein (Weesperpoort station) at that time. Added to Swammerdamstraat in 1970, the old name is now back again. For explanation of the name,

origins.name: Mauvestraat
origins.en: Anton Mauve (1838-1888), landscape painter.

origins.name: Max de Haasstraat
origins.en: Max de Haas (1898-1983) journalist, director and screenwriter. When the Germans invade the Netherlands in May 1940, De Haas, who as a politically conscious Jew has few illusions about the plans of the Nazis, flees to England with his wife Gretl, who is from Vienna.

origins.name: Max Euweplein
origins.en: Machgielis Euwe (1901-1981), mathematician, chess grandmaster and theorist. From 1921 to 1958 he was virtually unbroken Dutch champion and in 1935 he won the world title. In 1981 he was awarded the Silver Medal of the City of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Max Planckstraat
origins.en: German physicist (1858-1947), professor in Berlin and Vienna. Received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1918.

origins.name: Maxwellstraat
origins.en: The English physicist James Clerk Maxwell (1831-1879), inventor of the electromagnetic light theory.

origins.name: Maya Angeloustraat
origins.en: Maya Angelou (1928-2014), actually Margueritte Johnson, was an American writer and poet.

origins.name: Mechelensingel
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Medemblikstraat
origins.en: Place in North Holland, formerly an important Zuiderzee city.

origins.name: Meentstraat
origins.en: Meent is an Old Dutch word for common grazing land. This naming is a historical Rhine-Lander name: land that disappeared due to flooding east of Heemstede.

origins.name: Meer en Vaart
origins.en: Former manor house on the Sloterdijkermeerweg near the Haarlemmerweg, demolished for the construction of Bos en Lommer. It was the official residence of the mayor of the municipality of Sloten, which was abolished in 1921.

origins.name: Meerhuizenplein
origins.en: Former country house on the Amstel near the site where the Amstelkade now meets the Amsteldijk, demolished around 1914. In the seventeenth century, the poet Hendrik Laurens Spieghel lived here.

origins.name: Meerhuizenstraat
origins.en: Former country house on the Amstel near the site where the Amstelkade now meets the Amsteldijk, demolished around 1914. In the seventeenth century, the poet Hendrik Laurens Spieghel lived here.

origins.name: Meerkerkdreef
origins.en: The place Meerkerk on the Merwedekanaal (South Holland), between Vianen and Gorinchem.

origins.name: Meerluchtlaan
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Meermontkade
origins.en: Former country house on the Amstel.

origins.name: Meernhof
origins.en: Village west of Utrecht.

origins.name: Meerpad
origins.en: This refers to the former Buikslotermeer, where the path led out.

origins.name: Meeuwenlaan
origins.en: Named after the gull, a bird.

origins.name: Meeuwenplein
origins.en: Named after the gull, a bird.

origins.name: Meibergdreef
origins.en: Hill south of Berg en Dal/Groesbeek (Gelderland).

origins.name: Meibergpad
origins.en: Hill south of Berg en Dal/Groesbeek (Gelderland).

origins.name: Meidoornplein
origins.en: The tree or shrub from the apple family.

origins.name: Meidoornweg
origins.en: The tree or shrub from the apple family.

origins.name: Meimorgenstraat
origins.en: Poem of the same name by Jacqueline E. van der Waals (1868-1922), which is included in the collection 'New Verses' (1909).

origins.name: Mekongweg
origins.en: River with a length of more than four thousand kilometers, running through China, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.

origins.name: Melis Stokehof
origins.en: Dutch poet from the thirteenth century, known for his 'Rijmkroniek'. Considered a follower of Jacob van Maerlant.

origins.name: Melkdistelstraat
origins.en: Named after the sow thistle, a thistle.

origins.name: Melkweg
origins.en: The Milky Way is the faintly glowing band in the sky, caused by the light of the millions of stars in the galaxy to which our sun belongs. The road was previously known as the Ringway.

origins.name: Meloenenstraat
origins.en: Named after the melon, a fruit.

origins.name: Melsbroekhof
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Memeleiland
origins.en: Old Prussian city, since 1945 called Klaipeda and part of Lithuania. In the second half of the eighteenth century important for the supply of wood to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Memlingstraat
origins.en: Hans Memling (1430-1494), South Dutch painter of altarpieces and portraits. A number of his works have been brought together in Bruges.

origins.name: Menadostraat
origins.en: Location on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi (Celebes).

origins.name: Mendelhof
origins.en: Gregor Mendel (1822-1884), Austrian biologist who discovered inheritance in plants.

origins.name: Mendes da Costahof
origins.en: Jozef Mendes da Costa (1863-1939), sculptor. His work can be found in the boardroom of the Stock Exchange, among other places.

origins.name: Menno ter Braakstraat
origins.en: Essayist and critic (1902-1940). Vigorously opposed the emerging nationalism.

origins.name: Mensinge
origins.en: Old Drenthe farmstead, partly surrounded by water, near Roden. Originally from 1381, renovated in 1728.

origins.name: Mercatorplein
origins.en: Flemish geographer and cartographer, whose real name was Gerard Kremer (1512-1594). Drawn the first world map in cylindrical projection.

origins.name: Mercatorstraat
origins.en: Flemish geographer and cartographer, whose real name was Gerard Kremer (1512-1594). Drawn the first world map in cylindrical projection.

origins.name: Merckenburg
origins.en: Eighteenth-century building in Heukelom (South Holland), with a fourteenth-century square tower in the middle of the front facade, as a remnant of the original castle.

origins.name: Mercuriusplein
origins.en: The smallest planet. It is closest to the sun.

origins.name: Mercuriusstraat
origins.en: The smallest planet. It is closest to the sun.

origins.name: Merdekagracht
origins.en: Merdeka means free or independent and already formed the forbidden battle cry of the nationalist movement during the colonial period. After the Proclamation of the Republic of Indonesia on August 17, 1945, it became the characteristic battle cry of the independence fighters.

origins.name: Merelstraat
origins.en: The singing bird (black thrush).

origins.name: Merenburgstraat
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Merlijnstraat
origins.en: Name of a Celtic novel, edited in 1260 by Jacob van Maerlant.

origins.name: Merwedeplein
origins.en: The stream, formed by the confluence of Maas and Waal.

origins.name: Mesdagstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Mesdag (1831-1915), painter of seascapes.

origins.name: Messchaertstraat
origins.en: Johannes Martinus Messchaert (1857-1922), baritone singer. In 1884 he founded the Amsterdam Conservatory, together with Daniël de Lange, Frans Coenen and Julius Röntgen.

origins.name: Messinastraat
origins.en: Italian port city on Sicily, where the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a passenger service.

origins.name: Metaalbewerkerweg
origins.en: The profession, a collective term for the workers in the metal industry.

origins.name: Meteorensingel
origins.en: Meteors are 'falling stars', presumably fragments of former comets.

origins.name: Meteorenweg
origins.en: Meteors are 'falling stars', presumably fragments of former comets.

origins.name: Methaanweg
origins.en: The gas, a colorless and odorless mine gas and swamp gas.

origins.name: Metselstraat
origins.en: Reference to the concrete company Albeton that was located on the Cruquiusterrein between 1977 and 2014.

origins.name: Mezenstraat
origins.en: Named after the tit, a singing bird.

origins.name: Mezquitalaan
origins.en: Islamic building in Córdoba, resembling a fortress, founded in 785 by emir Abdar-Rahman. Over the centuries supplemented with Christian elements, the sixteenth-century cathedral in the center of the complex being the most important.

origins.name: Michel de Klerkhof
origins.en: Architect (1884-1923). Built several residential complexes in Amsterdam, including in the Spaarndammerbuurt (Amsterdam School style).

origins.name: Michelangelostraat
origins.en: Michelangelo Buonarroti (1475-1564), Italian sculptor, painter, architect and poet. The greatest visual artist of his time. (Dome of St. Peter's Basilica and paintings in the Sistine Chapel in Rome.)

origins.name: Michiel de Ruijtertunnel
origins.en: Michiel Adriaansz. de Ruyter (1607-1676), the famous admiral of Holland and West Friesland. Born in Vlissingen. In Amsterdam he lived on the current Prins Hendrikkade.

origins.name: Middelhoffstraat
origins.en: A former amusement park that was located on the east side of the Schagerlaan.

origins.name: Middeliestraat
origins.en: Village northwest of Edam (North Holland).

origins.name: Middelveldstraat
origins.en: To the Middelveldsche Akerpolder, where this neighborhood is located.

origins.name: Middenlaan Zunderdorp
origins.en: The street was officially named this way in 1953, following the local name that has always been in use here. The street does not run through the middle of the village, but is the main road relative to the village and the nearby hamlets.

origins.name: Middenmeerpad
origins.en: To the former manor house Midden-Meer, which stood on the corner of Middenweg and Kruislaan until 1809.

origins.name: Middenweg
origins.en: Named after the location. The road is laid across (middle) through the dried-up Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Midscheeps
origins.en: Term for everything located in the middle of a ship.

origins.name: Midwoudpad
origins.en: Village in North Holland, in the West Friesland region.

origins.name: Mien Labbertonstraat
origins.en: Youth book writer (1883-1966), published among other things 'Young Hearts' (1938) and 'Spring Blossoms' (poems, 1926).

origins.name: Mijehof
origins.en: Village on the river of the same name in South Holland, which flows into the Oude Rijn near Zwammerdam.

origins.name: Mijndenhof
origins.en: The village on the Vecht, located opposite Loenen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Milletstraat
origins.en: Jean François Millet (1815-1875), French landscape painter.

origins.name: Millingenhof
origins.en: The village on the Rhine (Gelderland).

origins.name: Milovan Djilasplein
origins.en: Yugoslav politician and human rights activist (1911-1995). Was co-founder of the partisan army in 1941 and became vice prime minister in 1946 under Marshal Tito. Fell out of favor due to his struggle for more democracy.

origins.name: Milovan Djilasstraat
origins.en: Yugoslav writer and human rights activist (1911-1997), one of Josip Tito's closest associates, secretary-general of the Yugoslav Communist Party. He openly expressed his disappointment with communism. He broke away from Tito and was imprisoned several times.

origins.name: Minahassastraat
origins.en: Region on the island of Sulawesi (Indonesia).

origins.name: Minckelersstraat
origins.en: Jan Pieter Minckelers (1748-1824), physicist. Discovered the usefulness of coal gas for lighting purposes.

origins.name: Minervahavenweg
origins.en: In Roman mythology the goddess of wisdom.

origins.name: Minervalaan
origins.en: In Roman mythology the goddess of wisdom.

origins.name: Minervaplein
origins.en: In Roman mythology the goddess of wisdom.

origins.name: Minnemoersstraat
origins.en: The name originated at the end of the seventeenth century and is probably derived from a facade stone or signboard. Before that, the street was known as Bickersdwarsstraat. A nurse or nurse was a woman who took care of a baby with maternal care, breastfed and/or fed the baby.

origins.name: Miraplein
origins.en: Star in the constellation Whale.

origins.name: Modelmakerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name: someone who makes models, for example for casting molds. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Modemstraat
origins.en: Device to convert computer signals on the telephone network. As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Moeder Alacoquebrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after Moeder Alacoque (1892 - 1956), a Dutch nun who helped many prisoners during the Japanese occupation of Dutch East Indies ('42 - '45. She was mother superior of the Charitas Hospital in Palembang on Sumatra. Among the patients were several people involved in the spread of war news and the smuggling of money and drugs to prisoner camps in Palembang.

origins.name: Moederkruidstraat
origins.en: Medicinal plant

origins.name: Moerbeienstraat
origins.en: The fruit of the mulberry tree. The leaves of the tree are used for the cultivation of silkworms.

origins.name: Moerdijkstraat
origins.en: Place at the Hollandsch Diep, where Jan Willem Friso drowned in 1711. Between 1868 and 1872, the Moerdijk Bridge (rail bridge 2530 m) was built here and in 1936 the traffic bridge.

origins.name: Moermanskkade
origins.en: Russian port city and naval base on the Barents Sea, founded in 1915.

origins.name: Moermond
origins.en: Picturesque castle in Renesse (Zeeland), severely damaged by water during the storm disaster of 1953. During the restoration, the foundations of a large castle from the early Middle Ages were uncovered.

origins.name: Moestuinlaan
origins.en: Vegetable garden. The street is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Moezelhavenweg
origins.en: Side river that flows into the Rhine near Koblenz (Germany). Important river for the industries and mines in the Saar region.

origins.name: Mokerstraat
origins.en: A heavy blacksmith or breaking hammer.

origins.name: Molen 't Haasjepad
origins.en: Poldermolen, octagonal ground sluice gate. Kept the Wilmkebreek dry from the reclamation in 1633. The mill was seriously damaged during the 1916 flood disaster, and was subsequently replaced by an electric pumping station. Demolished in 1924.

origins.name: Molenaarsweg
origins.en: The miller is someone who operates a mill. The road runs along the Molenwijk park (see there). Before 1976, the road was part of the Stellingweg.

origins.name: Molenbeekstraat
origins.en: Name of various Dutch waterways, including in Limburg and along the Veluwezoom.

origins.name: Molengouw
origins.en: To the mill that stood near the current Nibbixwoudstraat, and where this street used to lead as a path to it.

origins.name: Molenpad
origins.en: This path was outside the city in the sixteenth century and led to a mill near the current Raamplein (Raamstraat was also called Molenpad until the seventeenth century). By the way, Molenpad is the only one of the many outer paths that retained the name path when it came to lie within the walls after 1612.

origins.name: Molenslootpad
origins.en: Name for a main waterway that leads to the polder mill.

origins.name: Molensteeg
origins.en: The alley dates back to the beginning of the fourteenth century, when the count of Holland had a mill built on the Zeedijk. This mill had disappeared by 1357, but the alley has retained its name to this day. In the sixteenth century, the alley was also called Minderbroederssteeg.

origins.name: Molenwerf
origins.en: This name was established in 1956, but already existed for a long time. The millyard is the piece of land on which a mill stands. In this case, the site where the mill stood in the old village of Sloterdijk.

origins.name: Molenwijk
origins.en: This is the name of a park. The residential buildings established in this park form a number of mill districts on the map and bear names of mill types.

origins.name: Molsteeg
origins.en: The name of this alley first appears in 1557 and refers to the house 'De Mol', which was already mentioned in 1533 and stood on the land where this alley is now located.

origins.name: Molukkenstraat
origins.en: Island group in Indonesia, located between Sulawesi and New Guinea, to which among others the islands of Ambon, Ceram and Halmaheira belong. (Indonesian name = Maluku).

origins.name: Mondlanestraat
origins.en: Eduardo Mondlane (1920-1969), leader of the liberation movement Frelimo in Mozambique. He was assassinated in 1969. It took until 1975 for Mozambique to become independent from Portugal.

origins.name: Monitorstraat
origins.en: Screen. As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Monnikendammerplantsoen
origins.en: The place in North Holland, once a thriving Zuiderzee city.

origins.name: Monnikendammerweg
origins.en: The place in North Holland, once a thriving Zuiderzee city.

origins.name: Monnikendwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the Brothers of the Poor or Grey Monks monastery, founded in 1464, destroyed in 1578. The oldest name of the street is Grauwemonnikenstraat (1581).

origins.name: Monnikenstraat
origins.en: Named after the Brothers of the Poor or Grey Monks monastery, founded in 1464, destroyed in 1578. The oldest name of the street is Grauwemonnikenstraat (1581).

origins.name: Monnikskapstraat
origins.en: Plant genus from the ranunculus family. Blooms yellow, purple, blue, pink or white. The name is derived from the strikingly shaped upper petal. The monk cap mainly grows on alpine meadows on the northern hemisphere. Of the more than 250 species, only the yellow monk cap is native to the Netherlands.

origins.name: Monte Adi
origins.en: Mountain peak in Spain, 1453 meters high.

origins.name: Monte Perdido
origins.en: Mountain peak in Spain, 3355 meters high.

origins.name: Monte Viso
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3841 meters high.

origins.name: Montelbaanstraat
origins.en: Named after the Montelbaan Tower, built in the sixteenth century. The street was laid out after the renovation of the Jonker- and Ridderbuurt around 1930. As for the origin of the name Montelbaan, we are in the dark.

origins.name: Montferlandstraat
origins.en: The hilly landscape near 's-Heerenberg and Zeddam (Gelderland).

origins.name: Montfoorthof
origins.en: The place on the Hollandsche IJssel (Utrecht).

origins.name: Moreelsestraat
origins.en: Paulus Moreelse (1571-1638), painter, influenced by Titian. He painted, among other things, the archers of the Kloveniersdoelen.

origins.name: Morellenstraat
origins.en: The fruit, a kind of cherry.

origins.name: Morsestraat
origins.en: The North American Samuel Morse (1791-1872). Formed a system of symbols from a combination of dots and lines (Morse code).

origins.name: Mortelstraat
origins.en: Reference to the concrete company Albeton that was located on the Cruquiusterrein between 1977 and 2014.

origins.name: Mosplein
origins.en: The plants, spore plants, that are spread all over the world.

origins.name: Mosstraat
origins.en: The plants, spore plants, that are spread all over the world.

origins.name: Mosveld
origins.en: The plants, spore plants, that are spread all over the world.

origins.name: Motorkade
origins.en: A motor is a power machine, which provides moving force. Powered by electricity, gases or heat.

origins.name: Motorwal
origins.en: A motor is a power machine, which provides moving force. Powered by electricity, gases or heat.

origins.name: Mozartkade
origins.en: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756-1791), Austrian composer of church music, operas, symphonies, piano concertos, songs and chamber music. The greatest composer of the classical period.

origins.name: Mozes en Aäronstraat
origins.en: To the two Old Testament figures Mozes, leader during the exodus from Egypt, and Aaron, head of the priesthood. The street runs between the former town hall (worldly authority, Mozes) and the Nieuwe Kerk (spiritual authority, Aaron).

origins.name: Mr. P.N. Arntzeniusweg
origins.en: Pieter N. Arntzenius (1745-1799), lawyer and poet. Secretary of the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: ms. Oslofjordweg
origins.en: The motor ship Oslofjord. A passenger ship built at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM) for a Norwegian shipping company and intended for the voyage between Norway and North America. At the christening in 1948, the ship was christened by the queen of Norway.

origins.name: ms. Tarnweg
origins.en: Motor ship (ms) Tarn, built at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (later NDSM).

origins.name: ms. van Riemsdijkweg
origins.en: The motor ship Van Riemsdijk. A cargo and passenger ship, built in 1939 at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (later NDSM) for the Koninklijke Pakketvaart Maatschappij (KPM) for use in Indonesia. When the war broke out in May 1940, the ship had not yet been completed. By the end of the war, the ship was sunk by the occupiers in the North Sea Canal and after the war was salvaged and dismantled.

origins.name: mt. Lincolnweg
origins.en: The turbinetanker Esso Lincoln was built in 1961 at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM) on behalf of Esso. It was the hundredth ship to be launched after 1945, on December 15, 1962.

origins.name: mt. Ondinaweg
origins.en: Motor tanker, 6341 tons, built in 1939 at the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (later NDSM) on behalf of Anglo Saxon Petroleum Co.

origins.name: Muiderbergbrug
origins.en: To the town of Muiderberg

origins.name: Muiderlaan
origins.en: Runs in the direction of Muiden, just like Muiderstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

origins.name: Muiderstraat
origins.en: The street runs in the direction of the city of Muiden (as well as the Plantage Muidergracht). The north side of this street was largely demolished during the hunger winter of 1944-45 and for the rest in the following years. After that, the street width was increased to 37 meters.

origins.name: Muntbergweg
origins.en: A hill west of Groesbeek (Gelderland).

origins.name: Muntendamstraat
origins.en: Pieter Muntendam (1901-1986), from 1953 professor of social medicine at Leiden. He has been intensively involved in public health in the Netherlands for sixty years, among other things as director-general and as state secretary. He had a forward-looking position on euthanasia and abortion. One of his many functions was that of chairman of the State Commission for Alternative Medicines.

origins.name: Muntplein
origins.en: The Amsterdammers simply call it the Mint. In the building next to the Mint Tower (remnant of the Regulierspoort), coins were minted for a period of time in the seventeenth century. Since then, the name Mint has remained associated with it. The official name Muntplein dates back to 1917. From 1-25-1877 to 1917, the square was called Sophiaplein (see at Sophialaan), and until 1877 Schapenplein.

origins.name: Murdoch Mackenziestraat
origins.en: Scottish cartographer (1712-1797), made maps of the Orkney Islands among other things. The sea book of the Orkney Islands that was given to her ships by the VOC after 1753 was a translation of Mackenzie's work.

origins.name: Murillostraat
origins.en: Bartholome Esteban Murillo (1618-1682), Spanish Baroque painter (Madonnas and saints).

origins.name: Museumbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the nearby Rijksmuseum, which was built in 1883 by Pierre Cuypers

origins.name: Museumplein
origins.en: To the nearby Rijksmuseum, built in 1883 by Pierre Cuypers. In 1883, 1887 and 1895 large exhibitions were held at the Museumplein, after which it was an ice club field until around 1940.

origins.name: Museumstraat
origins.en: To the nearby Rijksmuseum, built in 1883 by Pierre Cuypers. In 1883, 1887 and 1895 large exhibitions were held on Museumplein, after which it was an ice club field until around 1940.

origins.name: Mussenstraat
origins.en: The birds belonging to the finches.

origins.name: Muurbloemstraat
origins.en: The plant, family of the cruciferous vegetables.

origins.name: Muzenplein
origins.en: In Greek mythology, the muses (daughters of Zeus) are the goddesses of the arts and sciences.

origins.name: N. Lansdorpstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Lansdorp (1885-1968), architect. Designer of the church on Mosstraat. In Amsterdam he built 2000 houses and 160 schools, such as the Vossiusgymnasium.

origins.name: Na Druk Gelukbrug
origins.en: is named after Dirk Beukeboom's farm on the then-current Brug is named after Dirk Beukeboom's farm on the then-current Oude Amstelveenseweg 255, which had to make way for the construction of the Olympic Stadium and the Olympic neighborhood The name of this farm refers to

origins.name: Naaldwijkstraat
origins.en: Name of a village in the Westland (South Holland).

origins.name: Naardermeerstraat
origins.en: The nature monument west of Naarden. In 1905, the municipality of Amsterdam's plan to purchase the area for landfill was rejected by the municipal council. This was the impetus for the establishment of the Association for the Preservation of Nature Monuments in the Netherlands, which purchased the Naardermeer in 1906.

origins.name: Nachtegaalstraat
origins.en: Named after the nightingale, a singing bird.

origins.name: Nachtwachtlaan
origins.en: The famous painting by Rembrandt, depicting the corps of Captain Frans Banning Cock (1642). The name Night Watch was erroneously given to the painting by the fading of the paint.

origins.name: Nadezjda Mandelstamstraat
origins.en: Wife of the dissident Russian writer Osip Mandelstam. Nadezjda Mandelstam (1899-1980) risked her own life to promote the publication of poetry collections by her husband, who died during his internment in 1938.

origins.name: Nadia en Lili Boulangerplantsoen
origins.en: Nadia (Paris, September 16, 1887 - there, October 22, 1979) and Lili (Paris, 1893 - Mézy-sur-Seine, 1918) Boulanger were sisters and both composers. They meant a lot to classical music at the beginning of the 20th century. They were especially known in their native France but eventually also gained fame abroad. Nadia Boulanger's musical activity is closely linked to that of the American Fontainebleau Conservatory. She conducted here from 1949 until the end of her life and trained more than 600 students. Lili Boulanger was the first woman to win the Prix de Rome. After that, she was constantly ill and died at the age of only 24.

origins.name: Nadirstraat
origins.en: A concept in astronomy: the imaginary point on the celestial sphere, located perpendicular to the observer (opposite of zenith).

origins.name: Nadorststeeg
origins.en: According to old registers, in 1557 there was a inn on the corner of the Nes and this alley, where the 'Nadorst' was located.

origins.name: Nageljongenstraat
origins.en: Occupational name: young worker who makes the rivets glowing hot and indicates the rivet for sounding. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Namenhof
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Namur.

origins.name: Nannie van Wehlstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Susanne J.A. Reys (1880-1944), children's book writer. Not only wrote girls' books but also essays on pedagogical and feminist issues.

origins.name: Nannoplein
origins.en: Name of an idyll by the writer Carel Vosmaer (1882).

origins.name: Naritaweg
origins.en: Name of one of Tokyo's airports.

origins.name: Narva-eiland
origins.en: City in Estonia near the border with Russia, as a historic export port of wood of importance to Amsterdam.

origins.name: Narwalstraat
origins.en: Whale-like, gray with brown spots on the upper side, only a few teeth in the upper jaw, does not grow longer than five meters. Found in the Arctic region.

origins.name: Nassaukade
origins.en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. The quay was referred to as Buitensingel before the naming in 1879.

origins.name: Nassauplein
origins.en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. The quay was referred to as Buitensingel before the naming in 1879.

origins.name: Nathan F. Israëlweg
origins.en: Nathan Frederik Israël (1904-1944), resistance fighter. Was involved in the preparation of the February Strike in 1941, participated in the armed resistance and produced the illegal newspaper 'De Waarheid' in Amsterdam Noord. Died in a firefight on August 15, 1944.

origins.name: Navigatiepad
origins.en: Location determination at sea. The streets in the area relate to shipping and seamanship.

origins.name: NDSM-kade
origins.en: Nederlandse Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, was founded in 1946 from a merger of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). Located along the northern IJ coast and built cargo ships, among other things, and carried out repairs and ship modifications. The new shipyard closed in 1979; the repair part (a second NSM) went bankrupt in 1984.

origins.name: NDSM-pier
origins.en: Nederlands Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, was founded in 1946 from a merger of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). Lived along the northern IJ coast and built cargo ships among other things and carried out repairs and ship modifications. The new shipyard closed in 1979

origins.name: NDSM-plein
origins.en: Nederlands Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, was founded in 1946 from a merger of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). Lived along the northern IJ coast and built cargo ships among other things and carried out repairs and ship modifications. The new shipyard closed in 1979

origins.name: NDSM-straat
origins.en: Nederlands Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij, was founded in 1946 from a merger of the Nederlandsche Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NSM) and the Nederlandsche Dok Maatschappij (NDM). Lived along the northern IJ coast and built cargo ships among other things and carried out repairs and ship modifications. The new shipyard closed in 1979

origins.name: Nederhoven
origins.en: Castle surrounded by a moat in Beegden (Limburg), with a date of construction 1614.

origins.name: Nedersticht
origins.en: Old name for the current province of Utrecht. Opposite Oversticht, which included the current provinces of Overijssel and Drenthe as well as Oost- and Weststellingwerf and the city of Groningen.

origins.name: Neerkanne
origins.en: Originally a medieval castle, near Canne near Maastricht, repeatedly destroyed. The current form dates from 1700, restored in 1955. It is also called Castle Agimont.

origins.name: Neerlandiaplein
origins.en: Name of the building built in 1888 by the Deaconry of the Reformed Church. It served as a home for married elderly people, and was part of the Amstelhoven complex where needy elderly people lived. Today it forms part of the Hermitage.

origins.name: Nellesteinpad
origins.en: Name of a house in Maarn (Utrecht). The name Nellestein has been used since 1976 for a residential area near the Gaasperplas Metro station.

origins.name: Nellie Bodenheimstraat
origins.en: Children's book writer (1874-1951), became especially known for the illustrations she made for children's books.

origins.name: Nelson Mandelapark
origins.en: Nelson Rolihlahla 'Madiba' Mandela (1918-2013). South African anti-apartheid fighter and politician, who is seen as the Father of the Fatherland in his home country. He was sentenced to life imprisonment in 1963 as leader of the military branch of the ANC, but was released in 1990. Received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993 with President F.W. de Klerk for their efforts to end the apartheid regime. Elected president in the first free elections of 1994, an office he held for 5 years.

origins.name: Neptunusplein
origins.en: Planet in our solar system.

origins.name: Neptunusstraat
origins.en: Planet in our solar system.

origins.name: Nepveustraat
origins.en: Jan Nepveu (1719-1779), governor of Suriname.

origins.name: Nes
origins.en: The toponym nes is an indication for a low-lying spit of land along a water. The name Nes, originally Nesse, indicates that there used to be swampy land here. Until the seventeenth century, the northern part was still called Gansoord. The word oord means roughly the same as nes, but is mainly found along the larger rivers.

origins.name: Nesciobrug
origins.en: Nescio was the pseudonym of the Amsterdam writer J.H.F. Grönloh, known for novellas such as De Uitvreter and Titaantjes. He enjoyed walking in the area around the neighboring Diemerzeedijk and the Buiten-IJ.

origins.name: Nesserhoek
origins.en: Named after the right-angle bend in the Waterlandse Zeedijk, now Buiksloterdijk, located freely in the IJ, strongly attacked by westerly wind and waves.

origins.name: Nesserland
origins.en: Named after the promontory, Nes, extending freely into the IJ from the Buiksloter Sea Wall.

origins.name: Nesserton
origins.en: Named after the end of the Nes, a spit in the IJ, on the northwest side of the Buiksloterham, marked with a ton on a stake, that disappeared due to the construction of the North Sea Canal.

origins.name: Netwerkweg
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Newtonstraat
origins.en: Isaac Newton (1642-1727), English mathematician and physicist. He discovered important laws in the field of gravity.

origins.name: Niasstraat
origins.en: Island group on the west coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Nibbixwoudstraat
origins.en: Village between Hoorn and Medemblik (North Holland).

origins.name: Nic. de Roeverstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas de Roever (1850-1893), Amsterdam city archivist and historian. Author of 'In de oude Amstelstad'.

origins.name: Nickeriestraat
origins.en: River in Suriname.

origins.name: Nico Broekhuysenweg
origins.en: Nicolaas Broekhuysen (1876-1958). Initiator and pioneer of basketball in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Nico Jessekade
origins.en: Photographer (1911-1976), started as a doctor with his own general practice. Known for his loose way of photographing, characterized by blurriness, and the use of flash. His most famous book is 'Women of Paris', which has appeared in several countries

origins.name: Nico Snijdersstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Nico van Suchtelenhof
origins.en: Literary (1878-1949), initially wrote poetry, later novels. Director of the World Library in Amsterdam for many years.

origins.name: Nicolaas Anslijnstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Anslijn education reformer (1778-1838) Writer of school reading books, including 'The Brave Hendrik' Born in Leiden, died in Alkmaar.

origins.name: Nicolaas Beetsplantsoen
origins.en: Literary and writer (1814-1903). As a student, he wrote the famous 'Camera Obscura' under the pseudonym Hildebrand.

origins.name: Nicolaas Beetsstraat
origins.en: Literary and writer (1814-1903). As a student, he wrote the famous 'Camera Obscura' under the pseudonym Hildebrand.

origins.name: Nicolaas Berchemstraat
origins.en: Painter (1620-1683), especially of landscapes.

origins.name: Nicolaas Hennemanhof
origins.en: Photographer (1813-1898). Settled in London around 1847. Was assistant to the famous English photographer William Henry Fox Talbot for many years, and was appointed court photographer at the court of Queen Victoria.

origins.name: Nicolaas Japiksestraat
origins.en: Historian (1872-1944), director of the royal house archive of the queen. He wrote historical studies, including 'History of the House of Orange-Nassau'.

origins.name: Nicolaas Maesstraat
origins.en: Painter (1632-1693), painted historical pieces and portraits. He was a pupil of Rembrandt.

origins.name: Nicolaas Ruychaverstraat
origins.en: Guerrilla captain during the capture of Den Briel and the siege of Alkmaar. Died in 1577 in a failed raid on Amsterdam, to get the city on the side of the Prince.

origins.name: Nicolaas Tetterodestraat
origins.en: Amsterdam industrialist (1816-1894), founder of the letter foundry 'Amsterdam'.

origins.name: Nicolaas Witsenkade
origins.en: Shipbuilder, cartographer, writer. Lived from 1641 to 1717. Studied law in Leiden and was an advisor to Tsar Peter the Great. His book on shipping from 1671 is one of the important sources on Dutch shipbuilding in the seventeenth century. He was Mayor of Amsterdam many times between 1682 and 1705.

origins.name: Nicolaas Witsenstraat
origins.en: Shipbuilder, cartographer, writer. Lived from 1641 to 1717. Studied law in Leiden and was an advisor to Tsar Peter the Great. His book on shipping from 1671 is one of the important sources on Dutch shipbuilding in the seventeenth century. He was mayor of Amsterdam many times between 1682 and 1705.

origins.name: Nida Senffstraat
origins.en: Dina Willemina Jacoba Senff (1920-1995), swimmer. Won gold in the 100-meter backstroke during the 1936 Berlin Olympic Games. First forgot to touch at the turn, swam back and still won.

origins.name: Niek Engelschmanbrug
origins.en: This permanent bridge is named after Niek Engelschman (1914-1988), who was also known as Bob Angelo. He was very active in the struggle for the emancipation of homosexuals and was the founder of the COC.

origins.name: Nienke van Hichtumstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Sjoukje Maria Diederika Troelstra-Bokma de Boer (1860-1939), wife of SDAP politician P.J. Troelstra. Juvenile book writer, became especially well known with 'Afke's dozen', in which she described the poverty and social abuses around the turn of the century.

origins.name: Nierkerkestraat
origins.en: A village that drowned in 1530 near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland.

origins.name: Niersstraat
origins.en: River in Limburg, which flows into the Maas near Gennep.

origins.name: Nieuw Herlaer
origins.en: Former castle in St. Michielsgestel. Later, a monastery with that name was built here. Of the original castle, only a tower with a spire remains.

origins.name: Nieuw-Zeelandweg
origins.en: Located east of the Australiëweg. Geographically, Nieuw-Zeeland is located east of Australia.

origins.name: Nieuwe Achtergracht
origins.en: Excavated at the same time as the Achtergracht, but on the other (new) side of the Amstel. Around 1670, a section was filled in, creating the Korte Amstelstraat. Also

origins.name: Nieuwe Akerweg
origins.en: Named after the Akerpolder in the former municipality of Sloten. The names Aker and Akerwatering are historical names, which already appear on a map of Rhineland from 1687 by Jan Dou.

origins.name: Nieuwe Amstelbrug
origins.en: At the delivery in 1903 of this, partly designed by Berlage, double bascule bridge, this was the latest bridge over the Amstel. The High Lock was also known as the Amstel Bridge, but this bridge was newer, hence the Nieuwe Amstelbrug

origins.name: Nieuwe Amstelstraat
origins.en: The river.

origins.name: Nieuwe Batavierstraat
origins.en: It is believed that the origin of the name must be sought at a facade stone or signboard in the former Batavierstraat. Batavier is most likely a corruption of Batavia. The Nieuwe Batavierstraat was created by reconstruction of the island of Uilenburg.

origins.name: Nieuwe Doelenstraat
origins.en: The targets were the places where the shooting guilds gathered and where they practiced shooting at a target. The Old Doelenstraat was laid out on the site of the oldest targets, which date back to the fifteenth century. The Nieuwe Doelenstraat derives its name from the Kloveniersdoelen, which stood on the site of the current Doelenhotel from 1522.

origins.name: Nieuwe Egelantiersstraat
origins.en: Named after the eglantine (sweet briar), a shrub.

origins.name: Nieuwe Foeliestraat
origins.en: One of the - at the time important - products that were imported from East India and stored here in the warehouses of the Dutch East India Company.

origins.name: Nieuwe Gietersstraat
origins.en: Named after 't Giethuis, the city's gunpowder and bell foundry, which stood here from 1614 to 1821. The street name first appeared in use in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Nieuwe Gouw
origins.en: Gouw is a Waterland term for road. The addition Nieuwe indicates that this road is slightly younger than the other Waterland roads. However, the road already appears on the map of Amstellandt and the surroundings of Covens from 1749. In 1957, the name was officially established again.

origins.name: Nieuwe Haagseweg
origins.en: The traffic road to The Hague. The old Haagseweg now has a secondary function.

origins.name: Nieuwe Hemweg
origins.en: To a former island called the Hem in the former IJ. The Hem was initially a spit of land that was only later made into an island by a breakwater. The word is the same as 'ham', which is now only known as 'inham'. There is now only one last stretch of the Hemweg, originally this road began in the Spaarndammerbuurt. Due to the construction of some harbors, the road was dug through in 1947. Parts are now called Coenhavenweg and Archangelweg. The Nieuwe Hemweg was built to replace the Hemweg.

origins.name: Nieuwe Herengracht
origins.en: To the Lords Regulators of the city (The city was not previously governed, but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch, when it was widened in 1612 to the current canal, as the first of the three main canals. The part beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658. The Nieuwe Herengracht also belongs to that expansion.

origins.name: Nieuwe Hoogstraat
origins.en: These streets are slightly higher than those in the immediate vicinity. The Oude Hoogstraat was laid out around 1490, the Nieuwe Hoogstraat a century later.

origins.name: Nieuwe Jonkerstraat
origins.en: The Jonker-, Ridder-, Koning- and Keizersstraten were laid out in the second half of the sixteenth century on originally reclaimed land outside the Zeedijk, officially drawn within the city in 1593 (see Lastage). Although the origin of the name is unknown, it is obvious to assume that the four groups of names were determined by the then municipal government. The Jonker- and Ridderbuurt was renovated in 1928. The Lastageweg was also built at that time. The Nieuwe Jonkerstraat is a remnant of the former Jonkerstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Keizersgracht
origins.en: Named after Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms in 1489.

origins.name: Nieuwe Kerkstraat
origins.en: The Kerkstraat was laid out in 1665 and was named so to connect the plan with this street to four churches, namely the Amstelkerk, the Oosterkerk and two others that were never built, namely one near Molenpad and a second near Weesperstraat. Later the street received several names: Kerkstraat (up to the Amstel), Nieuwe Kerkstraat (up to the Roetersstraat), Plantage Kerklaan (in the Plantage) and Korte Kerkstraat, which was renamed Tussen Kadijken in 1943.

origins.name: Nieuwe Laan
origins.en: Former road in the Sloter Middelveldsche Polder, connecting road between Uitweg and Sloterdijkermeerweg. On a map of 1650 that old road is called Nieuwelaan, on later maps the name Malleweg appears. The current Nieuwe Laan was given the name Malleweg when it was built in 1958 (council decision, 1958), but due to objections the name was changed to Nieuwe Laan in 1967.

origins.name: Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg
origins.en: The main road to the north, which leads via the Afsluitdijk to Leeuwarden. The Leeuwarderweg was part of the Buiksloterdijk before 1936. The Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg was built with the completion of the IJ tunnel.

origins.name: Nieuwe Leliestraat
origins.en: The namesake of all these streets is the oldest, namely the Oude Leliestraat, which is already mentioned in 1560. This derives its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Tower lock).
