The name passed on after 1612 to the canal dug along its extension and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets located in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Nieuwe Looiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the leather trade, to which these and the nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal belt are named, were first located outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came within the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after those long-established businesses, starting with the Runstraat and the Huidenstraat. After 1658, the tanneries expanded to areas east of the Vijzelgracht, where we now find the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and cross street. The Third Looiersdwarsstraat was the Old Tanneries Canal (council decision, 1898) for filling in. For the Drowned Nieuwe Tanneries Canal,

origins.name: Nieuwe Looiersstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the leather trade, to which these and the nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal belt are named, were first located outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came within the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after those long-established businesses, starting with the Runstraat and the Huidenstraat. After 1658, the tanneries spread out to areas east of the Vijzelgracht, where we now find the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and cross street. The Third Tanner Cross Street was the Old Tanner Slough (council decision, 1898) for filling in. For the Drowned New Tanner Slough,

origins.name: Nieuwe Maanstraat
origins.en: The celestial body, which moves in an elliptical orbit around the earth.

origins.name: Nieuwe Meerpad
origins.en: The water surface was given this name to distinguish it from the Old Lake (see there). The Nieuwe Lake has been enlarged since the 1950s with part of the Riekerpolder and pumped to a depth of thirty meters for sand mining for the western garden towns.

origins.name: Nieuwe Nieuwstraat
origins.en: In a maternity resolution of 1550, it was decided to build a new street near the Korsjespoort, this street was simply called 'new street'. Thirty years later, the Sint Geertruidenklooster and the Lieve Vrouwengasthuis were demolished that stood between the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and the Nieuwendijk. Again, one of the newly built streets was named after the 'new street'. To distinguish the two new streets, the names in the first half of the seventeenth century were given the addition 'Old' and 'New', and they have retained these names to this day. The Nieuwe Nieuwstraat was initially also called Nieuwe Herenstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Oostenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. The demolition of the streets and buildings began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was removed from public transport in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and declared abandoned in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abandoned in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Nieuwe Oostenburgerstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the easternmost of the three islands (with Kattenburg and Wittenburg) brought within the city by the expansion of 1658. Laying out streets and building began in 1664. At first three streets ran from the canal, named for their position Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was closed to traffic for the growing Werkspoor works and abolished in 1957; the Oostenburgermiddenstraat followed in 1985, where the Compagniestraat now runs. Land freed by the disappearance of some shipyards took the Nieuwe Oostenburgerstraat and -dwarsstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Osdorpergracht
origins.en: To the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. The Osdorperweg used to bear the names Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

origins.name: Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat
origins.en: Passing was the preparation and processing of Spanish leather. When this type of leather processing was banned in Amsterdam-Centrum in 1631, this passership settled here next to the already existing leather tanneries.

origins.name: Nieuwe Prinsengracht
origins.en: To 'the princely title', which refers to that of the princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and in terms of the nature of the buildings, the simplest. During the enlargement of 1612, it was dug and built from Brouwersgracht to Leidsegracht. With the enlargement of 1658, this canal is also extended across the Amstel (up to the Entrepotdok). For the part on the Plantage, see also Plantage Westermanlaan - formerly Plantage Prinsenlaan. The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for the current Noordermarkt did not find favor with the bourgeoisie.

origins.name: Nieuwe Purmerweg
origins.en: The polder, created by the draining of the lake between 1618 and 1622 near Purmerend.

origins.name: Nieuwe Ridderstraat
origins.en: The Jonker-, Ridder-, Koning- and Keizersstraten were laid out in the second half of the sixteenth century on originally reclaimed land outside the Zeedijk, officially drawn within the city in 1593 (see Lastage). Although the origin of the name is unknown, it is obvious to assume that the four groups of names were determined by the then municipal government. The Jonker- and Ridderbuurt was renovated in 1928. The Lastageweg was also built at that time. The Nieuwe Jonkerstraat is a remnant of the former Jonkerstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Schermerstraat
origins.en: Between 1631 and 1635 more were drained in North Holland.

origins.name: Nieuwe Spiegelstraat
origins.en: To a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers, who had soap factories. In 1564 Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' lived in the corner building of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel and in 1608 Pieter Lourens Spiegel. The intended house is still called Hertspiegel in 1738. Construction of the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat begins in 1665. Again, it is likely that a resident from the Spiegel family was the namesake.

origins.name: Nieuwe Teertuinen
origins.en: When the old oil gardens (now Prins Hendrikkade) were moved to the Sloterdijksgracht and thus became the staging ground for the oil buyers there, the name of the quay there soon changed to Nieuwe Teertuinen.

origins.name: Nieuwe Tuinstraat
origins.en: Garden here has the meaning of shipyard or enclosed space. The street name is derived from the Stadstimmertuin (the City Shipyard), which was located here from 1612 to 1660 (near the Lijnbaansgracht) and where the street ran along.

origins.name: Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat
origins.en: The island of Uilenburg, which together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken came to lie within the city in 1593. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known with certainty, but it is likely that the name comes from the marshland here, which was called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was formed by the merger of the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Utrechtseweg
origins.en: To the city of Utrecht. The street leads to the Frederiksplein, where the Utrechtsepoort used to stand (demolished in 1860). The Nieuwe Utrechtseweg is the new route to Utrecht. The old road ran via Duivendrecht and Abcoude.

origins.name: Nieuwe Vijzelstraat
origins.en: The name is probably derived from the former inhabitants Cornelis Arents Vijselaar (around 1600) and Jan Vijselaar (around 1632). Vijzelstraat was then a short street and ran to the current Reguliersdwarsstraat. When the street was extended, the name also passed on to this extension. Until the eighteenth century, people spoke of Oude and Nieuwe Vijzelstraat. The Vijzelgracht, dug between 1660 and 1670, was filled in 1934.

origins.name: Nieuwe Wagenstraat
origins.en: There was also a car park at the Haarlemmerpoort, and a Wagenstraat also came there. Due to confusion, the latter was changed to Nieuwe Wagenstraat in 1909. At the same time and for the same reason, the Schapensteeg was then changed to Korte Wagenstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwe Westerdokstraat
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was built and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Nieuwe Weteringstraat
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed out of the Spui from the outside. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Parts have been recreated in promenades (First and Second Weteringplantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name of Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was built on the site that became available due to the demolition of the Flour and Bread Factory.

origins.name: Nieuwe Willemsstraat
origins.en: This is the extension of the Willemsstraat (see there). This name was also originally determined with one s.

origins.name: Nieuwe Zonneweg
origins.en: The central body in the planetary system to which Earth belongs.

origins.name: Nieuwe-Wercksbrug
origins.en: Named after the original name for the current Jordaan.

origins.name: Nieuwebrugsteeg
origins.en: To the bridge where the alley leads. The first wooden bridge over the northern part of the Damrak was built between 1402 and 1421. When it was later replaced by a stone bridge, it was renamed Nieuwebrug. In old documents we also find the name Uiterstebrug.

origins.name: Nieuwegeinlaan
origins.en: Village south of Utrecht.

origins.name: Nieuwegrachtje
origins.en: At the beginning of the nineteenth century, an open street was laid out on the former wooden wall along the Rapenburgergracht, which was named 't Nieuwe grachtje.

origins.name: Nieuwendammer Sluispad
origins.en: Named after the nearby sluice gate. An old local name has thus been officially made.

origins.name: Nieuwendammerdijk
origins.en: The part of the Waterland sea wall that was in the former municipality of Nieuwendam until 1-1-1921. The name Nieuwendam originated when a new sea wall or dam was built here in 1516 after a break in the sea wall. That name was passed on to the later formed sea wall village.

origins.name: Nieuwendammerkade
origins.en: It is likely that the Nieuwendijk owes its name to a partial fortification along the Amstelmouth, in which the Amsteldam mentioned in 1275 also played a role.

origins.name: Nieuwendammerstraat
origins.en: To the former village of Nieuwendam. The first part of the street came under the name Nieuwstraat on Amsterdam's territory with the annexation of 1-1-1921.

origins.name: Nieuwendijk
origins.en: It is likely that the Nieuwendijk owes its name to a partial fortification along the Amstelmouth, in which the Amsteldam mentioned in 1275 also played a role.

origins.name: Nieuwenhuysenstraat
origins.en: Frederik Nieuwenhuysen (1905-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed in Haarlem.

origins.name: Nieuwerhoek
origins.en: Country house from the seventeenth century near Loenen aan de Vecht. One of the three corner houses (Ouder-, Middel- and Nieuwerhoek), founded by the Amsterdam family Van Hoek. Ouderhoek was demolished in 1838.

origins.name: Nieuwersluishof
origins.en: Village on the Vecht (Utrecht).

origins.name: Nieuwevaart
origins.en: To the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to connect the IJ and the Oosterdok along the shortest possible route with the IJ mouth at Zeeburg.

origins.name: Nieuwevaartkade
origins.en: To the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to connect the IJ and the Oosterdok along the shortest possible route with the IJ mouth at Zeeburg.

origins.name: Nieuwevaartweg
origins.en: To the Nieuwe Vaart, dug around 1650 to connect the IJ and the Oosterdok along the shortest possible route with the IJ mouth at Zeeburg.

origins.name: Nieuwezijds Armsteeg
origins.en: Arm has the meaning of bend here. The alley leads to the bend of Warmoesstraat.

origins.name: Nieuwezijds Kolk
origins.en: Originally, the water that came from the underlying peatland area through the now filled in Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal flowed through this pool to the Damrak. Around 1350, the Martelaarsgracht was dug and this drainage ceased. By the end of the fifteenth century, the pool had been filled in.

origins.name: Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal
origins.en: For the origin of the name, see Oudezijds Voorburgwal. The Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal was filled in in 1884. Before the filling in, some sections had unofficial names of the markets held on site: Pijpenmarkt, Boommarkt, Bloemmarkt and Postzegelmarkt.

origins.name: Nieuwlandhof
origins.en: Name of the village in the Lower Betuwe, west of Leerdam (South Holland).

origins.name: Nieuwmarkt
origins.en: Created in 1614 by filling in and vaulting over a part of the Kloveniersburgwal. The new square that arose around the Waag as a result was initially called Sint Antoniesmarkt, later called Nieuwmarkt.

origins.name: Nieuwpoortkade
origins.en: The place in Belgium where Prince Maurice defeated the Spanish in 1600.

origins.name: Nieuwpoortstraat
origins.en: The place in Belgium where Prince Maurice defeated the Spanish in 1600.

origins.name: Niftrikhof
origins.en: To the village of the same name in the Land of Maas and Waal (Gelderland).

origins.name: Nigellestraat
origins.en: A garden plant, belonging to the ranunculus family, more commonly known as lady in green.

origins.name: Nigtevechthof
origins.en: The village south of Weesp, between the Vecht and the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal (Utrecht).

origins.name: Nijenburg
origins.en: One of the five thirteenth-century castles with which Floris V wanted to subdue the West Frisians. The castle destroyed in 1491, whose foundations can still be seen, is just east of Alkmaar near Oudorp (North Holland).

origins.name: Nijlpaardenbrug
origins.en: Refers to hippos in Artis

origins.name: Nilda Pintostraat
origins.en: Nilda Maria Geerding Jessurun Pinto (1918-1954), Curaçao writer. Especially known for the vivid way in which she recorded Curaçaoan folk tales in Papiamento.

origins.name: Nirwana
origins.en: In Buddhism, the highest spiritual state that a person can achieve, in which the soul has been freed from desire, aversion and delusion and he has come to rest as it were.

origins.name: Nisserstraat
origins.en: The Nissermeer, located in Telemark, southern Norway.

origins.name: Nobelweg
origins.en: Alfred Nobel (1833-1896), Swedish industrialist and chemist, inventor of dynamite and nitroglycerine. After his death, he bequeathed his fortune to a fund, from which six Nobel Prizes have been awarded annually since 1901 to those who make exceptional contributions to the following disciplines: physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, peace and economics.

origins.name: Nolensstraat
origins.en: Willem Hubertus Nolens (1860-1931) Roman Catholic clergyman and politician, after the death of Schaepman for many years the leader of the Roman Catholic State Party and member of parliament. From 1909 professor in Amsterdam in labor law.

origins.name: Nooit Dorstraat
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Noord-Bevelandstraat
origins.en: Zeeuwse island.

origins.name: Noordbrabantstraat
origins.en: The province. The street is located in the middle of streets named after castles in this province.

origins.name: Noorder IJdijk
origins.en: North side of the IJ

origins.name: Noorder Valdeur
origins.en: Named after the drainage ditch between the Twiske and the Haal, which was presumably equipped with a wooden sluice gate. The sluices were raised with a rope, which hung over a block in a portal. Disappeared due to the flooding of the Twiske.

origins.name: Noorderakerweg
origins.en: The Akerpolder, where the road runs through, is the name giver here. The addition Noorder serves to distinguish it from the other, the Zuiderakerweg. The road came under the name Noorderakerweg in 1921 from the then dissolved municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Noorderbreedte
origins.en: The distance in degrees of a place north of the equator.

origins.name: Noorderdwarsstraat
origins.en: The names are derived from the North Sea Forest, in the seventeenth century a neighborhood of gardens, cut through by paths and canals, which stretched from the Reguliersgracht to the Spiegelgracht. The land was ceded by the city in 1670 to three charitable institutions, which built houses on it.

origins.name: Noorderhaakspad
origins.en: Sandbank near Texel, the western part of which serves as a resting area for birds and seals. Also known as Furious Ball.

origins.name: Noorderkerkstraat
origins.en: The Noorderkerk, a Protestant cruciform church, built in 1623 by Cornelis Danckertsz.

origins.name: Noorderkroonstraat
origins.en: Named after the Northern Crown (Corona Borealis), a constellation.

origins.name: Noordermarkt
origins.en: To the Noorderkerk (see at Noorderkerkstraat). Until 1655, the square was largely occupied by the cemetery attached to the church. In that year and the following year, the cemeteries were moved to a place outside the city. Officially, the market square first received the name Prinsenmarkt (after the Prinsengracht), but that name could not be maintained.

origins.name: Noorderpark
origins.en: It was created in 2014 by merging the Florapark and the Volewijkspark, two green areas on either side of the North Holland Canal. The park owes its name to its location in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Noorderstraat
origins.en: The names are derived from the North Sea Forest, in the seventeenth century a neighborhood of gardens, cut through by paths and canals, which stretched from the Reguliersgracht to the Spiegelgracht. The land was ceded by the city in 1670 to three charitable institutions, which built houses on it.

origins.name: Noordhollandschkanaaldijk
origins.en: The canal between Amsterdam and Den Helder, dug in the years 1818-1824 according to the design of Jan Blanken, because the port of Amsterdam became inaccessible due to the sandbanks at the mouth of the IJ. (The Willemssluizen are named after King William I, who stimulated the construction of the canal.)

origins.name: Noordhollandstraat
origins.en: The province. The surrounding streets are named after castles in this province.

origins.name: Noordkaapstraat
origins.en: The high rock formation, known as the northernmost point of Norway and Europe.

origins.name: Noordkaperweg
origins.en: Whale, black, sometimes with a white belly. Can reach a length of 15 meters. It lives in the temperate regions of the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans and around the Southern Ocean.

origins.name: Noordplein
origins.en: The area around Noord metro station forms the high urban center of Amsterdam Noord. The name Noordplein tells about the geographical location in the city. The square forms the heart of Noord and connects Noord with Zuid via the metro line and the Zuidplein there.

origins.name: Noordsche Compagniebrug
origins.en: Named after the Noordsche or Greenland Company, which had its warehouses at Keizersgracht 40-44 in the so-called Greenland warehouses.

origins.name: Noordwal
origins.en: To the location, namely the north bank of the IJ.

origins.name: Noordzeekanaalweg
origins.en: Road named after the North Sea.

origins.name: Noordzeeweg
origins.en: Marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean

origins.name: Noordzijde
origins.en: Named after its location relative to the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Notarisappelstraat
origins.en: Apple variety that was first grown in 1890 by notary J.H.Th.W. van den Ham in Lunteren.

origins.name: Notenstraat
origins.en: The fruits of the nut tree.

origins.name: Notweg
origins.en: A former road between the Sloterdijkermeerweg and the Haarlemmerweg, disappeared before the construction of the Bos and Lommerbuurt. A notweg is a country road, intended for the transport of the harvest from the field. The Frisian word 'not' means 'harvest'. The term occurs frequently in North Holland above the IJ, also as a notsloot for a waterway with the same function.

origins.name: Nova Zemblastraat
origins.en: Island in the North Sea. Barentsz and Heemskerk overwintered there from 1596 to 1597 during their unsuccessful attempt to reach India via the northern route. This street first belonged to the Roggeveenstraat (council decision, 1878).

origins.name: Nuldernauwpad
origins.en: Veluwe border lake between Gelderland and Flevoland.

origins.name: Nydia Ecuryhof
origins.en: Nydia Maria Enrica Ecury (Oranjestad, 1926 - Willemstad, 2012) was a teacher, writer, translator and actress. Ecury studied English and journalism in Canada. In 1957 she settled in Curaçao where she taught at the Martinus-Mavo and at the Nilda Pinto-Household School. She also taught Papiaments privately. In 1967 Ecury was one of the founders of the theater group Thalia. In 1972 she debuted as a poet, after which she published several poetry collections. Ecury also played a role in the film Almacita di desolato in 1986. In 1995 she received the Pierre Lauffer Prize and in 2007 the Cola Debrot Prize.

origins.name: Nydia Ecurystraat
origins.en: Nydia Maria Enrica Ecury (Oranjestad, 1926 - Willemstad, 2012) was a teacher, writer, translator and actress. Ecury studied English and journalism in Canada. In 1957 she settled in Curaçao where she taught at the Martinus-Mavo and at the Nilda Pinto-Household School. She also taught Papiaments privately. In 1967 Ecury was one of the founders of the theater group Thalia. In 1972 she debuted as a poet, after which she published several poetry collections. Ecury also played a role in the film Almacita di desolato in 1986. In 1995 she received the Pierre Lauffer Prize and in 2007 the Cola Debrot Prize.

origins.name: Obiplein
origins.en: Island group in Indonesia, belonging to the Moluccas. The square was built in 1980 on the site of the former Obistraat (council decision, 1923).

origins.name: Oceanenweg
origins.en: The major world oceans: the Atlantic, the Indian and the Pacific.

origins.name: Ochtenhof
origins.en: Village on the Waal in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Octaanweg
origins.en: Carbon monoxide, a petroleum derivative.

origins.name: Oderweg
origins.en: The river on the border of Poland and Germany.

origins.name: Oermilla Tewariestraat
origins.en: Oermilla S. Radjaram Tewarie-Manichand (1922-1990), first Hindu female president of the women's organization of the Sanatan Dharm, an important religious movement of the Hindu Surinamese. Between 1944 and 1968 she gave several religious-cultural lectures in Suriname.

origins.name: Oesjesduiker
origins.en: The name of this diver comes from the signboard 't Osje, which was formerly attached to a butcher on the corner of the Oostenburgergracht

origins.name: Oetewalerpad
origins.en: The village of Oetewaal or Outewaal or Houtewaal, formerly located on the Zeedijk near the current Muiderpoort. The village, which is already mentioned in 1387, was burned down by the Spanish in 1575 and devastated by a storm surge in 1651, but was rebuilt again and again. In 1658 it was annexed by Amsterdam to the fourth extension. Before 1878, Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg and was the road from Oetewaal to the Diemermeer (Watergraafsmeer). The current Oetewalerstraat came under the name Noordstraat (council decision of Nieuwe-Amstel, 1884) after the annexation of 1896.

origins.name: Oetewalerstraat
origins.en: The village of Oetewaal or Outewaal or Houtewaal, formerly located on the Zeedijk near the current Muiderpoort. The village, which is already mentioned in 1387, was burned down by the Spanish in 1575 and devastated by a storm surge in 1651, but was rebuilt again and again. In 1658 it was annexed by Amsterdam to the fourth extension. Before 1878, Linnaeusstraat was called Oetewalerweg and was the road from Oetewaal to the Diemermeer (Watergraafsmeer). The current Oetewalerstraat came under the name Noordstraat (council decision of Nieuwe-Amstel, 1884) after the annexation of 1896.

origins.name: Oetgensdwarsstraat
origins.en: Frans Hendriks Oetgens (1559-1625), city factory master and mayor of Amsterdam on several occasions, was the owner of the land located here around 1600. The former street names Oetgenspad (now Eerste Oosterparkstraat) and Oetgensachterpad also remind us of this. The streets newly built in 1980 were laid out on the site where in 1864 the King. Beiersche Bierbrouwerij was built, in operation until 1927. Part of the stables still functioned as business spaces until around 1955.

origins.name: Oetgensstraat
origins.en: Frans Hendriks Oetgens (1559-1625), city factory master and mayor of Amsterdam on several occasions, was the owner of the land located here around 1600. The former street names Oetgenspad (now Eerste Oosterparkstraat) and Oetgensachterpad also remind us of this. The streets newly built in 1980 were laid out on the site where in 1864 the King. Beiersche Bierbrouwerij was built, in operation until 1927. Part of the stables still functioned as business spaces until around 1955.

origins.name: Oeverlandenweg
origins.en: A citizen has proposed naming an unnamed space Oeverlandenweg. The Oeverlandenweg runs from Adam Smithplein to the Oeverlanden and is therefore seen as an appropriate name for this public space.

origins.name: Oeverpad
origins.en: To the location: along and towards the bank of the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Oeverparklaan
origins.en: Refers to the Oeverpark where this lane runs along the entire length.

origins.name: Oeverzeggestraat
origins.en: Reed species, grows at the water edge of ponds and in slow-flowing waters.

origins.name: Ogentrooststraat
origins.en: Plant, belonging to the mint family.

origins.name: Ohmstraat
origins.en: Georg S. Ohm (1787-1854), German physicist, who formulated the law of the strength of electric current (an ohm is a unit of electrical resistance).

origins.name: Okeghemstraat
origins.en: Johannes van Okeghem (1430-1495), Flemish composer, is considered the master of the Dutch School. He wrote masses, motets and chansons and was the teacher of Dufay and Obrecht.

origins.name: Oldambtstraat
origins.en: The eastern part of the province of Groningen. 'Old' is the North and East Dutch form for 'old'. The word 'ambt' or 'ambacht' means administrative district.

origins.name: Oldenaller
origins.en: Country house under Nijkerk (Gelderland), built in 1655 probably according to a design by Jacob van Campen, on the site of an earlier castle. The house was renovated around 1850 by K.G. Zocher.

origins.name: Oldengaarde
origins.en: Drenthe country house under Dwingelo from 1717.

origins.name: Oleanderstraat
origins.en: Named after the oleander, an ornamental shrub.

origins.name: Olga de Haasstraat
origins.en: Olga de Haas was a Dutch ballet dancer.

origins.name: Oliepalmstraat
origins.en: Palm species. The oil palm produces palm oil, which is used among other things in margarine, soap, biscuits and as fuel.

origins.name: Olifantswerf
origins.en: To the former shipbuilding yard 'De Olyphant' which was located here in Kattenburg.

origins.name: Olmenweg
origins.en: The deciduous tree, more commonly known as the elm.

origins.name: Olof Palmeplein
origins.en: Sven Olof Joachim Palme (1927-1986), Swedish politician of international allure. Founder and chairman of the Palme Commission for Disarmament and Security. He fought against the apartheid regime in South Africa. In the 1960s and 1970s, he campaigned with others against the U.S. actions in Vietnam. In 1986, he was murdered.

origins.name: Oltmansstraat
origins.en: Jan Frederik Oltmans (1806-1854), writer. Wrote historical novels, including 'The Shepherd'.

origins.name: Olympiakade
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Olympiaplein
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Olympiastraat
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Olympiaweg
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Olympisch Stadion
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Ombilinstraat
origins.en: River in Central Sumatra, Indonesia.

origins.name: Ommerenhof
origins.en: Location in the Neder-Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Omval
origins.en: Landtong between the Amstel and the ring canal of the Watergraafsmeer. Since the seventeenth century or earlier so named after a 'wreck' located there, that is, a construction site or ruin. The name has been passed down with the transition on 1-1-1921 of this part of the municipality of Ouder-Amstel.

origins.name: Onbekendegracht
origins.en: The canal was dug as a diversion of the Nieuwe Achtergracht (see there). The name is said to have originated because, due to this diversion, the Nieuwe Achtergracht was no longer visible from the Amstel. In 1948, one of the residents made a request to the mayor and aldermen to change this name, because they found it a somewhat strange name. Fortunately, this request was not accepted.

origins.name: Onderlangs
origins.en: Named after its location relative to the ring road of the Watergraafsmeer (here Gooiseweg).

origins.name: Onkelboerensteeg
origins.en: Named after a resident from the seventeenth century, Dirk Honckelboer. The oldest spelling is therefore Onckelboerssteegje. Previously, the alley was called Pleytstraat and Kijffstraat.

origins.name: Onsenoort
origins.en: Castle from the fourteenth century in Nieuwkuyk near Vlijmen (North Brabant), of which only a heavy rectangular tower remains.

origins.name: Onstein
origins.en: A 1711 moat-surrounded country house, located near Vorden (Gelderland).

origins.name: Oogststraat
origins.en: The yield of the field crops.

origins.name: Ooievaarsweg
origins.en: Named after the stork, a bird.

origins.name: Ookmeerweg
origins.en: To the former polder, a dry-milled pond north of the hamlet of Osdorp.

origins.name: Oossaander Hoop
origins.en: Ship of the Oostzaanse shipowner Pieter Swan. Was engaged in whaling under the command of his brother Cornelis from 1769 to 1775.

origins.name: Oost-Indische Huisbrug
origins.en: Named after the nearby Oost-Indische House on the Kloveniersburgwal corner of Oude Hoogstraat

origins.name: Oostakkerstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of East Flanders.

origins.name: Oosteinde
origins.en: The name indicates the location relative to the Utrechtsepoort. That gate stood in the middle of the Frederiksplein, where later the Palace of Public Enterprise would stand. The street ran along the east side and at the end of the city (outside the gate, inside the city moat). The street on the other side was then given the name Westeinde.

origins.name: Oostelijke Handelskade
origins.en: The eastern harbor basin owes its origin to trade. The road was laid in 1875-1883. In 1919, a section was named Piet Heinkade (council decision, 1919). The reason why the word Oostelijke was added to the name is not clear from the correspondence that led to the naming. The road was already called Handelskade in 1883 for the naming. Originally it was a quay along the closure dike of the Oosterdok.

origins.name: Oostenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. The demolition of the streets and buildings began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was removed from public transport in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and declared abandoned in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abandoned in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgergracht
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. The demolition of the streets and buildings began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was removed from public transport in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and declared abandoned in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abandoned in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgermiddenstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. The demolition of the streets and buildings began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was removed from public transport in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and declared abandoned in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abandoned in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgerpark
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. The demolition of the streets and buildings began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was removed from public transport in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and declared abandoned in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abandoned in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgervoorstraat
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. The demolition of the streets and buildings began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middle street and -back street according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was removed from public transport in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and declared abandoned in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abandoned in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Ooster Ringdijk
origins.en: Regarding its location relative to the Watergraafsmeer. The Ooster Ringdijk was named Noorder- and Zuider-Ringdijk before the annexation of the Watergraafsmeer municipality. The Eerste Ringdijkstraat was then called Schoollaan, while even earlier the name Dielemanstraat seems to have appeared. A Tweede Ringdijkstraat (formerly Dijklaan) has now completely disappeared due to demolition.

origins.name: Oosterdok
origins.en: The Oosterdok was created by a seawall completed in 1832 on the east side of the city. The quay on and along this dyke was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

origins.name: Oosterdoksdraaibrug
origins.en: This revolving bridge is located near the Oosterdok, hence the name.

origins.name: Oosterdokskade
origins.en: The Oosterdok was created by a seawall completed in 1832 on the east side of the city. The quay on and along this dyke was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

origins.name: Oosterdoksstraat
origins.en: The Oosterdok was created by a seawall completed in 1832 on the east side of the city. The quay on and along this dyke was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

origins.name: Oosterendstraat
origins.en: Village on the island of Texel.

origins.name: Oosterlengte
origins.en: The distance of a place in degrees east of the meridian, which was first assumed.

origins.name: Oostermeerstraat
origins.en: Formerly outside on the Amstel.

origins.name: Oosterpark
origins.en: Towards the location in the eastern part of the city. The name first only applied to the park, built in 1887 and in the following years. The road along the park was first named in 1895 and previously called Eerste Parkstraat (see Eerste Oosterparkstraat).

origins.name: Oostersekade
origins.en: The origin of this name is unknown. Since the description East Side of the Oudeschans also occurs, the explanation may be that Eastern was used for Eastern. (The Oosterkerk was also known as the Eastern church.) Another assumption for the origin of the name is that this may have been a docking place for ships for the Eastern trade (compare Texelse kade and Gelderse kade).

origins.name: Oosterspoorplein
origins.en: The Eastern Railway, the railway from Amsterdam to Amersfoort, opened in 1874 and extended in 1876 to Zutphen, thus creating the connection to North Germany.

origins.name: Oostertoegang
origins.en: Eastern access from the Oosterdok to the IJ

origins.name: Oosthuizenstraat
origins.en: Village northeast of the Beemster (North Holland).

origins.name: Oostoever
origins.en: Regarding the location relative to the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Oostzaanstraat
origins.en: The village of Oostzaan, located east of the Zaan.

origins.name: Oostzanerdijk
origins.en: The part of the Waterlandse sea wall that originally belonged to the municipality of Oostzaan.

origins.name: Opdijkstraat
origins.en: A dike that has been built 'higher up' as a kind of second defensive line against the water.

origins.name: Openhartsteeg
origins.en: Named after a facade stone, an open heart with orange apple. Already in the sixteenth century this was a sign of Orange sympathies. The alley was also formerly known as Pottenbakkerssteeg.

origins.name: Ophemerthof
origins.en: Village on the Waal, southwest of Tiel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Opheusdenhof
origins.en: Village in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Opijnenhof
origins.en: Village in the Tielerwaard on the Waal, northwest of Zaltbommel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Opmerkzaam
origins.en: The group of women, who regularly holds her silent march on Meiplein in Buenos Aires (Argentina). They want to know the truth about the fate of their men and children, who have disappeared under the general regime. In contrast to the weapons of violence and empty talk, they show in their collectivity and their persistence their struggle for truth, freedom and justice. Around this square, a number of streets are named after the virtues they represent.

origins.name: Opveld
origins.en: Castle in Heer (Limburg).

origins.name: Oranje Nassaulaan
origins.en: The House Oranje-Nassau is a branch of the House of Nassau.

origins.name: Oranje-Vrijstaatkade
origins.en: The Farmers' Republic, founded in 1842, which joined forces with the Transvaal in 1899 in the struggle against the English. Today, Oranje Free State is a province of the Republic of South Africa.

origins.name: Oranje-Vrijstaatplein
origins.en: The Farmers' Republic, founded in 1842, which joined forces with the Transvaal in 1899 in the struggle against the English. Today, Oranje Free State is a province of the Republic of South Africa.

origins.name: Oranjebrug
origins.en: This pick-up bridge derives its name from the street in which it lies. The origin of this street name is uncertain. It may refer to the house 'de Prins van Oranje', which used to stand here close to the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Orcastraat
origins.en: Also known as swordfish, black, with a white underside. Can grow six meters long and its dorsal fin is two meters long.

origins.name: Örehof
origins.en: The öre has the value of 1/100 of the standard coin of Sweden, Norway and Denmark (the crown).

origins.name: Orgeldraaierspad
origins.en: Originally a typical traveling profession. The name is related to the caravan world and refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Orionplantsoen
origins.en: Orion is a striking constellation on the ecliptic. In Greek mythology, Orion was a hunter who pursued the Pleiades, was accidentally killed by Artemis and then was elevated to a constellation.

origins.name: Orionstraat
origins.en: Constellation.

origins.name: Orlyplein
origins.en: Name of the airport in Paris.

origins.name: Ornsteinstraat
origins.en: Leonard Salomon Ornstein (1880-1941), physicist, professor at Utrecht from 1915.

origins.name: Orteliuskade
origins.en: Abraham Ortelius (1527-1598), Flemish geographer, creator of a famous atlas.

origins.name: Orteliuspad
origins.en: Abraham Ortelius (1527-1598), Flemish geographer, creator of a famous atlas.

origins.name: Orteliusstraat
origins.en: Abraham Ortelius (1527-1598), Flemish geographer, creator of a famous atlas.

origins.name: Ortler
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3899 meters high

origins.name: Osdorper Ban
origins.en: To the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. A ban is another word for governor.

origins.name: Osdorperweg
origins.en: To the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. The Osdorperweg has always borne the names Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

origins.name: Osdorpplein
origins.en: To the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. The Osdorperweg used to bear the names Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

origins.name: Ostwaldstraat
origins.en: Wilhelm Ostwald (1853-1932), German chemist. Made important inventions in the field of color theory. In 1909 he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

origins.name: Oterleekstraat
origins.en: Village east of Alkmaar (North Holland).

origins.name: Otopeniweg
origins.en: Name of Bucharest airport.

origins.name: Ottho Heldringstraat
origins.en: Preacher (1804-1876), founder of an asylum for fallen women and founder of the homes for neglected youth named after him.

origins.name: Oturia
origins.en: Mountain peak in Spain, 1920 meters high.

origins.name: Ouborg
origins.en: Fourteenth-century castle on the Swalm near Swalmen (Limburg), of which only a ruin of a heavy octagonal tower remains today.

origins.name: Oud-Ehrenstein
origins.en: Once a strong castle, of which medieval parts still exist, located on the road Heerlen-Kerkrade (Limburg). Before 1363, this stein (fortified stone house) came into the possession of the noble family of Ederen. The name passed on to the castle and was shortened to Ehrenstein.

origins.name: Oudaen
origins.en: Ridderhofstad under Breukelen, on the right bank of the Vecht, partially still medieval, rebuilt in the seventeenth century. It is one of the few castles that escaped the arson by the French troops in 1672.

origins.name: Oude Doelenstraat
origins.en: The targets were the places where the shooting guilds gathered and where they practiced shooting at a target. The Oude Doelenstraat was built on the site of the oldest targets, which date back to the fifteenth century. The Nieuwe Doelenstraat takes its name from the Kloveniersdoelen, which stood on the site of the current Doelenhotel from 1522.

origins.name: Oude Haagseweg
origins.en: The traffic road to The Hague. The old Haagseweg now has a secondary function.

origins.name: Oude Hoogstraat
origins.en: These streets are slightly higher than those in the immediate vicinity. The Oude Hoogstraat was built around 1490, the Nieuwe Hoogstraat a century later.

origins.name: Oude Kinkerbrug
origins.en: Johannes Kinker (1764-1845) was a Dutch poet, philosopher and lawyer

origins.name: Oude Leliestraat
origins.en: The namesake of all these streets is the oldest, namely the Oude Leliestraat, which is already mentioned in 1560. This derives its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Tower lock). The name passed on after 1612 to the canal dug along its extension and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets located in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Oude Looiersstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the leather trade, to which these and the nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal belt are named, were first located outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came within the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after those long-established businesses, starting with the Runstraat and the Huidenstraat. After 1658, the tanneries expanded to areas east of the Vijzelgracht, where we now find the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat. The Third Tanneriesdwarsstraat was for the filling in the Oude Tanneriesdijk (council decision, 1898). For the Drowned Nieuwe Tanneriesdijk

origins.name: Oude Meerhof
origins.en: Named after the former Oude Lake that lay along the extension of the still existing New Lake.

origins.name: Oude Nieuwstraat
origins.en: In a maternity resolution of 1550, it was decided to build a new street near the Korsjespoort. This street was simply called 'new street'. Thirty years later, the Sint Geertruidenklooster and the Lieve Vrouwengasthuis were demolished that stood between the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and the Nieuwendijk. Again, one of the newly built streets was named after the 'new street'. To distinguish the two new streets, the names were given the addition 'Oude' and 'Nieuwe' in the first half of the seventeenth century, and they have retained these names to this day. The Nieuwe Nieuwstraat was initially also called Nieuwe Herenstraat.

origins.name: Oude Spiegelstraat
origins.en: To a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers, who had soap factories. In 1564 Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' lived in the corner building of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel and in 1608 Pieter Lourens Spiegel. The intended house is still called Hertspiegel in 1738. The construction of the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat began in 1665. Again, it is likely that a resident from the Spiegel family was the name giver here.

origins.name: Oude Turfmarkt
origins.en: The peat market, which was held from 1564 to 1642 on this part of the former Amsteloever. In 1913 the name was declared obsolete and the quay near the Rokin was pulled back. In 1946 the quay regained its historic name.

origins.name: Oude Waal
origins.en: The quays were ancient harbors of the IJ on the old side (Oude Waal) and on the new side (Nieuwe Waal), where the sea ships were moored in winter. The Oude Waal was made shallow by dredging. On top of that, the Waalseiland was built in 1646. The quay on the city side retained the names Oude Waal and Kromme Waal (after the shape) on the Waalseiland the names Binnenkant and Buitenkant (now Prins Hendrikkade) came. The Nieuwe Waal disappeared due to the construction of the Western Entrepot Dock. The Waalsteeg was called Schippersstraatje before 1912. The name was changed due to confusion with the Schippersstraat.

origins.name: Oude-IJselstraat
origins.en: The Oude IJssel is a tributary of the IJssel River.

origins.name: Oudebrugsteeg
origins.en: The alley led to the oldest bridge that was built over the Damrak at the beginning of the fourteenth century as a connection between the old and the new side. The bridge deteriorated when this part of the Damrak was filled in. The two alleys still indicate the location of that old bridge.

origins.name: Oudekennissteeg
origins.en: Since the older spelling Oudekerksteeg is used, it is clear that there is a name alteration here, which dates back to the eighteenth century. The alley is named after the nearby Oude Kerk. Originally, the alley was called Barvoetsbroeders-, Minderbroeders- or Grauwmonnikensteeg.

origins.name: Oudekerksbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the nearby Old Church, the oldest church in Amsterdam. This church dates back to 1306 and is dedicated to Saint Nicholas.

origins.name: Oudekerksplein
origins.en: To the Old Church located here. The square largely originated from the clearing of the cemetery surrounding the church, which was replaced in 1655 by a cemetery outside the city walls. The Old Church is the oldest church in Amsterdam, probably dating from 1306, and dedicated to Saint Nicholas. The current tower dates from 1566, built by Joost Bilhamer.

origins.name: Oudemanshof
origins.en: Corneille A.J.A. Oudemans (1825-1906), botanist, professor in Amsterdam from 1859. Wrote, among other things, the 'Flora of the Netherlands'.

origins.name: Oudenaardeplantsoen
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of East Flanders.

origins.name: Oudenrijnlaan
origins.en: Village west of Utrecht.

origins.name: Ouderkerkerdijk
origins.en: Named after the village of Ouderkerk aan de Amstel, where these roads lead to it. The addition Korte dates from 1956, after the dike was dug through for the industrial area.

origins.name: Oudeschans
origins.en: A bastion is an earthen wall and as such the Oudeschans was built around 1516 for defense against the Gelders. The concept of bastion has long since been lost here, but water and quay have retained the name. The addition 'Old' will have been given, when in the next century a new bastion was built around the enlarged city.

origins.name: Oudezijds Achterburgwal
origins.en: The canal behind the Foreburgwal on the old side. See further Oudezijds Foreburgwal. The square in front of the Old Wall Church, which until then was part of this city wall, was named Walenpleintje on 22-3-1978.

origins.name: Oudezijds Armsteeg
origins.en: Arm has the meaning of bend here. The alley leads to the bend of Warmoesstraat.

origins.name: Oudorperstraat
origins.en: The North Holland village of Oudorp.

origins.name: Ouwerdingenpad
origins.en: In 1532, land on South Beveland drowned.

origins.name: Overamstelstraat
origins.en: Named after the Overamstelsche Polder, which was located in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896. Compared to the center of that municipality, the polder was located on the other side of the Amstel. The street originally ran through to Linnaeusstraat and was called Korte en Lange Overamstelstraat. When, after the construction of the Transvaalbuurt, only Korte Overamstelstraat remained, the addition 'Korte' was declared obsolete in 1913.

origins.name: Overbrakerpad
origins.en: Named after the Overbraker Binnenpolder. From 1943 to around 1960 there was also an Overbrakerweg (in the Overbraker Buitenpolder), but that disappeared due to the construction of the Sloterdijk industrial area.

origins.name: Overdam
origins.en: Once a noble house, later a farm, located on the Vecht between Weesp and Nigtevecht (Utrecht).

origins.name: Overflakkeestraat
origins.en: Part of the South Holland island of Goeree-Overflakkee.

origins.name: Overhaalsgang
origins.en: Originally a lane (waaigat) on the Hoogte Kadijk, which provided access to the crossing over the Nieuwe Vaart in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, demolished around 1877 in connection with the construction of a railway line along the Wittenburgergracht. On the site of that old crossing is now a permanent embankment connection.

origins.name: Overhaalstraat
origins.en: A transfer spring is a traffic technical term for a passing.

origins.name: Overhoeksparklaan
origins.en: On this site stands the eponymous high office tower designed by Arthur Staal for Shell in 1966. The term 'overhead', or 'diagonally placed', refers to the orientation of the building relative to the city and water.

origins.name: Overhoeksplein
origins.en: On this site stands the eponymous high office tower designed by Arthur Staal for Shell in 1966. The term 'overhead', or 'diagonally placed', refers to the orientation of the building relative to the city and water.

origins.name: Overijsselweg
origins.en: The province. In the vicinity, several streets are named after castles from Overijssel.

origins.name: Overleg
origins.en: Overleg with parties inside and outside the collective.

origins.name: Overpeltstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Overschiestraat
origins.en: The former village in South Holland, part of Rotterdam since 1941.

origins.name: Overslag
origins.en: Loading goods from sea vessels onto inland vessels and vice versa.

origins.name: Overslaghof
origins.en: Loading goods from sea vessels onto inland vessels and vice versa.

origins.name: Overtoom
origins.en: Named after the overtoom (a dam over which ships were pulled) that was built in the fourteenth century in the Schinkel. The Overtoom was a waterway before the filling in in 1904, the Heiligewegse- or Overtoomsevaart. The southern quay was called, as far as it was in Amsterdam, Vondelkade (council decision, 1875). The north side (the quiet side) has always had the name Overtoom.

origins.name: Overveenstraat
origins.en: Village near Haarlem (North Holland).

origins.name: Overvoorde
origins.en: Old noble house, located under Rijswijk (South Holland).

origins.name: Overzichtweg
origins.en: A former country house on the Schagerlaan, built around 1701 by Jacob Pauw, who gave it the name Groenhoven. A subsequent owner changed the name to Oversicht. The outside was demolished in 1804. The former Pauwenlaan, located west of the Schagerlaan, was named after the Jacob Pauw mentioned here.

origins.name: P. Dijkstraplein
origins.en: P. Dijkstra (1891-1957), director of the Royal Dutch Steam Boat Company from 1945 to 1955 director of the Holland Afrikalijn.

origins.name: P. Hans Frankfurthersingel
origins.en: P. Hans Frankfurther (1932-1996) has been committed to the village of Sloten and the Sloten-Oud Osdorp village council for more than thirty years. The Mill of Sloten returned to the district thanks in part to his efforts in 1991. In 1994 and 1995, he successfully coordinated the campaign around the referendum on the preservation of the Vrije Geer meadow.

origins.name: P. Lieftinckstraat
origins.en: Pieter Lieftinck (1902-1987), economist and politician, member of the Labour Party. Minister of Finance from 1945 to 1952. Famous for his money laundering in the summer of 1945. Initially erroneously named P. Lieftingstraat. By council decision in 1990 the error was corrected.

origins.name: P.E. Tegelbergplein
origins.en: Petrus Emelius Tegelberg (1838-1917), appointed co-director of the N.V. Stoomvaart Maatschappij 'Nederland' in 1873. Board member of the Amsterdamse Droogdokmaatschappij and treasurer of the Amsterdamse Kamer van Koophandel.

origins.name: P.J. Oudstraat
origins.en: Pieter Jacob Oud (1886-1968), liberal statesman. Minister of Finance in the extraparliamentary crisis cabinets of Colijn, known for his austerity policy. In 1948 co-founder of the VVD, chairman of the House of Representatives faction. In the period 1938-1941 and 1945-1952 he was mayor of Rotterdam.

origins.name: P.L. Marnettestraat
origins.en: Pieter Lucas Marnette (1888-1948), Amsterdam architect. Much of his work, such as the school building on Schermerstraat, can be considered part of the Amsterdam School. At the Department of Public Works, he designed street furniture.

origins.name: Paalbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill between Ermelo and Speulde (Gelderland).

origins.name: Paardekraalstraat
origins.en: Location in Transvaal (South Africa), where in 1880 the Transvaal Farmers' National Council met and where it was decided to resist the impending English domination. The section between Transvaalkade and -straat was designated by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel as Eerste Ringkadedwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890), changed to Polderstraat on 16-10-1901, and moved to Paardekraalstraat in 1912.

origins.name: Paardenstraat
origins.en: This street and the nearby Wagenstraat were the home of draggers, stablekeepers and carriage drivers in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. They are located near Rembrandtplein, where markets used to be held, while earlier in the neighborhood near the Regulierspoort (Muntplein) there was a carriage square.

origins.name: Paasbergpad
origins.en: Refers to the Easter Mountain, a hill 80 meters high in the Twente municipality of Losser

origins.name: Paasheuvelweg
origins.en: Hill near Vierhouten (Gelderland).

origins.name: Pablo Nerudalaan
origins.en: Chilean poet (1904-1973). In 1971 he received the Nobel Prize for Literature.

origins.name: Pacayastraat
origins.en: Mountain in Guatemala

origins.name: Padangstraat
origins.en: Port city on the west coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Paerlduiker
origins.en: derives its name from the brewery 'De Paerl', which was built in Wittenburg in the middle of the seventeenth century by Reinst and Grootenhuizen

origins.name: Pakingehof
origins.en: In 1377, the church village in the Braakman drowned, a now again reclaimed bay of the Westerschelde (Zeeuws-Vlaanderen).

origins.name: Paladruhof
origins.en: The lake, Lac de Paladru, located in southeastern France in the province of Isère.

origins.name: Palamedesstraat
origins.en: 'Palamedes or the murdered senselessness' a tragedy by Vondel, written in 1626 after the death of Maurits about Van Oldenbarneveldt. The part of the Overtoom, where this street is a side street, used to be called Vondelkade. Until 1890, the Palamedesstraat was a private street. The name was given by the construction company. With the takeover by the municipality, the name was also retained.

origins.name: Paleisstraat
origins.en: The name derives from the Town Hall, built in 1648, since 1808 Royal Palace. Before 1875 the street was called Gasthuisstraat, after the oldest hospital in the city, dating back to the fourteenth century, and Stilsteeg (no explanation can be given for this latter name). Another part was called Korte Gasthuismolensteeg before 1875.

origins.name: Palembangstraat
origins.en: City on Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Palestrinastraat
origins.en: Giovanni Palestrina (1525-1594), Italian composer of sacred music, organist and chapel master.

origins.name: Paletstraat
origins.en: Painter's tools, namely the board on which the painter mixes his colors.

origins.name: Palmdwarsstraat
origins.en: Refer to Palm Tree

origins.name: Palmgracht
origins.en: Refer to Palm Tree

origins.name: Palmstraat
origins.en: Refer to Palm Tree

origins.name: Pamirstraat
origins.en: Mountain in Tajikistan/Afghanistan

origins.name: Pampuslaan
origins.en: Name of an artificial island in the IJsselmeer east of Amsterdam. At low tide, ships often had to wait for a long time until the water was high enough to pass over the sandbank to Amsterdam. The expression 'lying before Pampus' comes from here.

origins.name: Panamakade
origins.en: To the Panama Canal, which was dug between 1900 and 1914 by the Isthmus of Panama (Central America).

origins.name: Panamalaan
origins.en: To the Panama Canal, which was dug between 1900 and 1914 by the Isthmus of Panama (Central America).

origins.name: Panchulisteeg
origins.en: Panchuli is a mountain in the Himalayas

origins.name: Pancrasstraat
origins.en: Gerbrand Claesz Pancras (1591-1649), Amsterdam soap maker, who was mayor of the city from 1639 to 1649. The name was established as Pancraskade during the construction (council decision, 1876). After the filling in in 1908, the name was changed.

origins.name: Pandimsteeg
origins.en: Pandim is a mountain in India

origins.name: Pandorinastraat
origins.en: Microscopically small aquatic plant. Colony-forming green seaweed, surrounded by yellowish sheath. Able to assimilate carbon dioxide due to the presence of chlorophyll.

origins.name: Pannerdenstraat
origins.en: Village on the Rhine (Gelderland).

origins.name: Papa Koendersstraat
origins.en: Julius Gustaaf Arnout Koenders, better known as Papa Koenders (Paramaribo, 1886 - Paramaribo 1957) was a teacher and an activist for the Sranantongo. In his own words, he was 'great-grandson of grandparents who were slaves'. With his association Pohama founded in 1944, he promoted Sranan and Creole culture. In addition, he founded the monthly magazine Foetoe-boi, which appeared from 1946 to 1956.

origins.name: Papaverhoek
origins.en: The plant, wild and cultivated. is also called buttercup.

origins.name: Papaverweg
origins.en: The plant, wild and cultivated. is also called buttercup.

origins.name: Papenbrugsteeg
origins.en: To the Papenbrug, which was here over the Damrak before the partial filling in and was built shortly before 1475. According to a sixteenth-century story, there was an old dilapidated bridge over the Damrak here, which was set on fire by some clergy on a Good Friday. As a result, the restored or renewed bridge was named Papenbrug.

origins.name: Papendrechtstraat
origins.en: Village on the Beneden-Merwede, opposite Dordrecht (South Holland).

origins.name: Papiermolensluis
origins.en: The name of this permanent bridge is derived from the signboard 'De Papiermolen' on the corner house, where a paper seller lived.

origins.name: Papierweg
origins.en: The product, which is transhipped in the Amsterdam port.

origins.name: Paradijsappelstraat
origins.en: Very old apple from North Holland. The color is predominantly red.

origins.name: Paradijsplein
origins.en: The word, of Old Persian origin, means 'surrounded by a wall'. Often it refers to a garden, but above all it is a world where existence is peaceful and timeless.

origins.name: Paramariboplein
origins.en: The capital of Suriname.

origins.name: Paramaribostraat
origins.en: The capital of Suriname.

origins.name: Parelstraat
origins.en: Named after the former Pearl Bridge between Kattenburger- and Wittenburgergracht, and after the seventeenth-century brewery De Parel.

origins.name: Parkhof
origins.en: The green area in the vicinity of the palace.

origins.name: Parlevinker
origins.en: A parlevinker is a retail trader who sells with a small boat along the ships.

origins.name: Parlevinkerpad
origins.en: A parlevinker is a retail trader who sells with a small boat along the ships.

origins.name: Parmenidesstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher (540-460 BC), the main of the school of the Eleates, who taught the unity of all nature.

origins.name: Parnassusweg
origins.en: Mountain in Greece, in Greek mythology the residence of Apollo and the muses. Today figuratively used: the realm of poetic art.

origins.name: Parosstraat
origins.en: Greek island in the Aegean Sea, part of the Cycladic island group. All the islands of the Cyclades are located in a circle (ancient Greek: kyklos) around Delos, an important Greek sanctuary in antiquity.

origins.name: Parthenonhof
origins.en: The large Doric temple on the Acropolis of Athens, built from 447-432 BC in honor of the city goddess Athena. High point of Greek architecture, due to its unrivaled harmonious proportions.

origins.name: Pascalstraat
origins.en: Blaise Pascal (1623-1662), French philosopher and physicist. The hydraulic system is based on Pascal's Law.

origins.name: Passeerdersgracht
origins.en: Passing was the preparation and processing of Spanish leather. When this type of leather processing was banned in Amsterdam-Centrum in 1631, this passership settled here next to the already existing leather tanneries.

origins.name: Passeerdersstraat
origins.en: Passing was the preparation and processing of Spanish leather. When this type of leather processing was banned in Amsterdam-Centrum in 1631, this passership settled here next to the already existing leather tanneries.

origins.name: Passtukkenpad
origins.en: Probably named after the passtuk used to fill or measure spaces between objects.

origins.name: Pastelstraat
origins.en: A colored pencil. The name is also given to the final product, the chalk drawing.

origins.name: Pasteurstraat
origins.en: Louis Pasteur (1822-1895), French chemist. Proved that various diseases are caused by bacteria. Found a serum against rabies and a method to kill bacteria (pasteurization). Before 1922, this was Prins Hendrikstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1902).

origins.name: Pasubio
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 2236 meters high.

origins.name: Paterslaan
origins.en: According to old deeds of sale, the name of a meadow along the Wijkergouw under Schellingwoude.

origins.name: Patrice Lumumbastraat
origins.en: First prime minister of Congo, took office on June 23, 1960. Just a week later, the former Belgian colony was an independent republic. Lumumba was hated in Belgium and Congo for his fiery speech about the injustices of colonial rule. Lumumba only served his office until September 5, 1960. On January 17, 1961, he was murdered.

origins.name: Patroclosstraat
origins.en: Greek hero in the Trojan War, sung by Homer.

origins.name: Paul Christiaan Fluhof
origins.en: Paul Christiaan Flu (Paramaribo, 1884 - Leiden 1945) was a doctor, professor of tropical hygiene and rector magnificus of the University of Leiden. The very talented Flu obtained his medical degree at the Medical School in Paramaribo at the age of twenty, after which he left for the Netherlands to further his studies. He worked in Suriname, the Netherlands and Indonesia. He also achieved a lot in Suriname: he was the founder of the water supply network and helped many through his extensive knowledge of various tropical diseases. Flu's groundbreaking work was noticed: in 1911 he was appointed Knight of the Order of Orange Nassau.

origins.name: Paul Christiaan Flustraat
origins.en: Paul Christiaan Flu (Paramaribo, 1884 - Leiden 1945) was a doctor, professor of tropical hygiene and rector magnificus of the University of Leiden. The very talented Flu obtained his medical degree at the Medical School in Paramaribo at the age of twenty, after which he left for the Netherlands to further his studies. He worked in Suriname, the Netherlands and Indonesia. He also achieved a lot in Suriname: he was the founder of the water supply network and helped many through his extensive knowledge of various tropical diseases. Flu's groundbreaking work was noticed: in 1911 he was appointed Knight of the Order of Orange Nassau.

origins.name: Paul Hufkade
origins.en: Photographer (1924-2002), famous for his staged studio images, glamour portraits, advertising campaigns and glossy fashion reports.

origins.name: Paul Scholtenstraat
origins.en: Jurist (1875-1946), professor at the University of Amsterdam from 1907. Known for his edition of the Civil Law and the Commercial Law.

origins.name: Paul Schuitemahof
origins.en: Graphic designer and photographer (1897-1973). Known for his powerful typographic designs. After 1926 he introduced photographic elements into his designs. He was one of the first designers to use photo montage for industrial design. Representative of New Photography.

origins.name: Paul van Vlissingenstraat
origins.en: Paul Fentener van Vlissingen was a Dutch entrepreneur, columnist, publicist, conservationist and philanthropist. He was a member of the Van Vlissingen patrician family.

origins.name: Paulus Potterstraat
origins.en: Painter (1625-1654), mainly of landscapes and animals.

origins.name: Paulus van Hemertstraat
origins.en: Theologian and philosopher (1756-1825). Due to objections to the doctrine of predestination, he resigned as a preacher, after which he mainly dealt with Kant's philosophy.

origins.name: Pauwels-van Bienestraat
origins.en: The artist couple Désiré Pauwels (1861-1942) and Sophie van Biene (1854-1907). Pauwels was a famous singer, first at the French Opera in The Hague, later at the Dutch Opera. Sophie van Biene was associated with the Dutch Theater as an actress.

origins.name: Pauwenpad
origins.en: About this place used to run Pauwenlaan, named after Jacob Pauw who built a country house nearby around 1701. Pauwenlaan disappeared due to the construction of the railway line to Utrecht.

origins.name: Pazzanistraat
origins.en: Julius Pazzani, engineer. Director of the Imperial Continental Gaz-Association. Responsible for the technical design of the buildings of the Westergasfabriek. The street is located on the grounds of this former factory.

origins.name: Pedro de Medinalaan
origins.en: Spanish cosmographer (1493-1567). Published in 1545 the book 'Arte de Navegar'. In 1580 the Dutch translation appeared under the title 'De zeevaert oft conste van ter zee te varen'.

origins.name: Pedro Nunesstraat
origins.en: Portuguese mathematician (1502-1578), from 1529 royal cosmographer. Published on the degree arc. His findings were practically useful in navigation.

origins.name: Peelstraat
origins.en: Area on the border of North Brabant and Limburg, originally a poor area of heath and bog, now completely cultivated. The last remnant of Peel has been preserved as a nature reserve under the name Grote Peel.

origins.name: Pegasusstraat
origins.en: Constellation.

origins.name: Pekelharingstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Adrianus Pekelharing (1848-1922), physician, professor at Utrecht from 1881, best known for his Beri-beri research.

origins.name: Pekkendam
origins.en: Former estate under Diepenheim (Overijssel).

origins.name: Pelerin
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the French port city of Le Pellerin, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Pelikaanbrug
origins.en: Given the proximity of the d'Peliekaan warehouse at Hoogte Kadijk 51

origins.name: Pelikaanstraat
origins.en: Named after the pelican, a bird.

origins.name: Pelistersteeg
origins.en: Pelister is a mountain in North Macedonia

origins.name: Penninkshof
origins.en: Historical name from Rhineland. The name can still be found in Penningsveer aan de Liede (between Haarlem and Spaarnwoude).

origins.name: Pennyhof
origins.en: The penny has the value of 1/100 of the standard coin of Great Britain (the pound sterling).

origins.name: Penseelstraat
origins.en: Painting and drawing tools, a thin brush.

origins.name: Peperstraat
origins.en: To the Pepper Yard, which was located on the site of the current Peperstraat and belonged to the warehouses of the Dutch East India Company, where, among other things, the spices mentioned were stored.

origins.name: Perenpad
origins.en: The fruits of the pear tree.

origins.name: Pernaubrug
origins.en: Pernau was the German name for the Estonian port city of Pärnu on the Gulf of Riga. The names in the Shipyards are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Perseusstraat
origins.en: Constellation in the northern Milky Way.

origins.name: Persijn
origins.en: Castle from the sixteenth century, demolished in the eighteenth century, which was located under Wassenaar (South Holland). It was named after the Hague branch of the Persijns.

origins.name: Persstraat
origins.en: Reference to the paper recycling company that was located on the Cruquiusterrein until the redevelopment of the area in the twenty-first century.

origins.name: Perzikstraat
origins.en: The fruit of the peach tree.

origins.name: Pesetalaan
origins.en: The currency of Spain.

origins.name: Pestalozzihof
origins.en: Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi (1746-1827), Swiss pedagogue influenced by Rousseau. Innovator of methods for popular education.

origins.name: Pesthuysbrug
origins.en: Named after the old plague house, built in 1635 in the Stads- or Godshuispolder, initially only for plague sufferers, later also used for the care of dysentery and typhoid patients and the insane. In 1891, after various new and renovations, it became the Wilhelminagasthuis. In 1925, the last part of the old plague house was demolished.

origins.name: Petemayenbrug
origins.en: The name of this double lift bridge is probably a bastardization of Petemoeienbrug. A petemoei is a (godmother) aunt and was also used in the past as a term for an old woman.

origins.name: Peter Martensstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1937-1992). As a socially engaged photojournalist, he mainly photographed human suffering, where the form was subordinate to the content. A photo had to shock.

origins.name: Peter Schatstraat
origins.en: Composer (1935-2003), of operas, orchestral and choral works. He was considered the greatest talent of his generation for the development of Dutch tonal art. In 1973 he received the prestigious Matthijs Vermeulen Prize.

origins.name: Peter van Anrooystraat
origins.en: Conductor and composer (1879-1954). Was conductor of several orchestras, known as a composer for his Piet Hein rhapsody. Pioneer in the field of youth concerts.

origins.name: Peter Wotkehof
origins.en: Austrian photographer (1800-1870), settled in Rotterdam in 1854, made daguerreotypes as one of the first practitioners in the Netherlands, especially of musicians and panoramas of Rotterdam.

origins.name: Petroleumhavenweg
origins.en: To the port located here for unloading oil tankers and the areas for storing petroleum products. The port was put into use in 1888. The first part of the road was previously named Vlothavenweg (council decision, 1953).

origins.name: Petrus Blokhof
origins.en: Historian (1855-1929), Leiden professor, writer of 'History of the Dutch people' and of the 'Social history of Leiden'.

origins.name: Pettenstraat
origins.en: Village at the northern end of the Hondsbossche Zeewering (North Holland).

origins.name: Peursumstraat
origins.en: Village in the Alblasserwaard near the river Giessen (South Holland).

origins.name: Philip Vingboonsstraat
origins.en: Master builder (1613-1678), who applied the raised gable and pilasters. He built, among other things, the Trippenhuis and many beautiful canal houses on Herengracht and Keizersgracht, Rokin and Singel.

origins.name: Piarcoplein
origins.en: Name of the Port of Spain, Trinidad airport.

origins.name: Pienemanstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Pieneman (1810-1860), history and portrait painter. President of the association of visual artists and art-loving members "Maatschappij Arti et Amicitiae", founded in 1839, as successor to his father J.W. Pieneman.

origins.name: Pier Afrika
origins.en: The world region.

origins.name: Pier Azië
origins.en: The largest of the world regions.

origins.name: Pier Europa
origins.en: The world region.

origins.name: Pier Panderstraat
origins.en: Frisian sculptor (1864-1919). A part of his work is collected in the Pier Pandertempel in Leeuwarden.

origins.name: Pierre Cuypershof
origins.en: Petrus J. Cuypers (1827-1921), architect, creator of Dutch neo-Gothic. Built among other things the Rijksmuseum (1885), the Central Station (1889) and the Vondelkerk (1878).

origins.name: Pierre Lallementstraat
origins.en: French mechanical engineer (1843-1891). Lallement, a stroller builder, saw a passing tricycle in 1862 and came up with the idea of adding pedals to the front wheel, a discovery that he patented four years later. Thus, he is considered the inventor of the bicycle with pedals.

origins.name: Pierre Laufferstraat
origins.en: Pierre A. Lauffer (Curaçao, 1920 - Curaçao, 1981) was a writer, poet and cultural activist for the preservation of his mother tongue, Papiaments. Lauffer wrote stories at a young age and remained active as an author. In 1944 his first poetry collection appeared, entirely in Papiaments, Patria (fatherland). In language and subject it represents a turning point in literature. Lauffer is indeed called the national poet of Curaçao, because he strongly advocated for the preservation of folklore and the history of his island. He considered Papiaments to be a carrier of culture with a fundamental role in Curaçao's quest for autonomy.

origins.name: Piet Dickentmanbrug
origins.en: Pieter Casper Johan Dickentman (1879-1950) was an Amsterdam cyclist. He was the first professional stayer in the Netherlands and became world champion in 1903

origins.name: Piet Gijzenbrugstraat
origins.en: Bridge over the Leiden Canal under Noordwijkerhout. The name Piet Gijzenbrug has been passed on to the neighborhood around that bridge.

origins.name: Piet Heinkade
origins.en: Pieter Pierszn Heijn (1577-1629), vice-admiral in service of the West Indian Company. Known for the conquest in 1628 of the Spanish silver fleet in the bay of Matanzas (Central America).

origins.name: Piet Heintunnel
origins.en: Pieter Pierszn Heijn (1577-1629), vice-admiral in service of the West Indian Company. Known for the conquest in 1628 of the Spanish silver fleet in the bay of Matanzas (Central America).

origins.name: Piet Kranenbergpad
origins.en: Ajax 1961 - 1974 365 matches in Eredivisie (146 goals) 6 x national champion / 5 winner KNVB Cup / 3 x winner European Cup for national champions / 2 x winner European Supercup/ 1 x winner Intertoto cup / 1 winner world cup. Piet Keizer played 34 international matches and never played for a club other than Ajax. In 1969, Ajax became the first Dutch club to reach the final in the prestigious Europa Cup for Landskampioenen. Today, that tournament continues under the name 'Champions League'. Ajax lost that final but two years later, in 1971, Ajax still won the most important football prize.

origins.name: Piet Meerburgbrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after Piet Meerburg, who was born in De Bilt in 1919 and died in Amsterdam in 2010. He was involved in saving Jewish children during World War II, for which he received the Yad Vashem award. One of those children was the later mayor Ed van Thijn. He was also a prominent theater entrepreneur in Amsterdam. For example, he was director of the Nieuwe de la Mar theater for many years and produced the musical My Fair Lady.

origins.name: Piet Moeskopspad
origins.en: Pieter Daniel Moeskops (1893-1964), cyclist. In the 1920s, he was a five-time world sprint champion.

origins.name: Piet Mondriaanplein
origins.en: Painter (1872-1944), living in the United States after 1940. Pioneer in the field of abstract art, leader of neoplasticism.

origins.name: Piet Mondriaanstraat
origins.en: Painter (1872-1944), living in the United States after 1940. Pioneer in the field of abstract art, leader of neoplasticism.

origins.name: Piet Nakstraat
origins.en: Pieter Frederik Willem Nak (1906-1996), working at City Cleaning, central figure within the illegal communist party. Together with colleague Willem Kraan initiator of the February Strike in 1941. In the 1960s he managed to broaden the Vietnamese movement, which led to general rejection of the American actions there.

origins.name: Piet Peelenbrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after Piet Peelen (1922-1978), who worked at the Bridges Department. He made efforts to promote livability in Osdorp, especially in the field of traffic.

origins.name: Piet Wiedijkstraat
origins.en: especially in the field of traffic.
