origins.name: Piet Zwarthof
origins.en: Photographer, typographer and industrial designer (1885-1977). Pioneer of 'New Photography' and modern typography. He rejected traditional typographic rules. Instead, he used the basic principles of constructivism. His work is recognizable by the primary colors, geometric shapes, repeated word patterns, tight diagonally placed lettering and an early use of photo montage.

origins.name: Pieter A. van Heijningestraat
origins.en: Pieter Adrianus van Heijninge (1903-1942), resistance fighter. Distributed illegal material, raised money for the illegality and instigated the February Strike in 1941. Was arrested in 1941 and executed on October 16, 1942 in Woudenberg.

origins.name: Pieter Aertszstraat
origins.en: Painter (1508-1575), painted genre pieces and church interiors. Before 1919 the street was called Nieuwe Tolstraat.

origins.name: Pieter Baststraat
origins.en: Pieter Bast (ca. 1550-1605) Dutch engraver and painter. Child of the famous printing family Plantijn.

origins.name: Pieter Boorsmapad
origins.en: Amateur historian (1871-1951), interested in the history of the Zaanstreek. Laid the foundation for the systematic study of the Zaanse mill history.

origins.name: Pieter Borstraat
origins.en: Pieter Christiaan Bor (1559-1635), historian and Governor of Holland. Author of 'The Dutch Wars'.

origins.name: Pieter Buyskensstraat
origins.en: Gueux captain during the uprising in Enkhuizen (1534-1606).

origins.name: Pieter Calandlaan
origins.en: Water engineer (1826-1902). His name is mainly associated with the construction of the New Waterway from Rotterdam to Hoek van Holland (1866-1872).

origins.name: Pieter Cornelisz. Hooftstraat
origins.en: One of the great writers of the seventeenth century (1581-1647). He wrote poetry and plays, including 'Granida' and 'Warenar'. Prince Maurice appointed him Drost of Muiden. The Muiderslot was then the gathering place of intellectuals for many years.

origins.name: Pieter de Hoochstraat
origins.en: Painter (1639-1684), especially of interior scenes.

origins.name: Pieter Goosstraat
origins.en: Mapmaker (ca. 1616-1675) in service of the VOC. Made small-scale postage stamps, among other things, from which the course towards the Dutch East Indies could be plotted.

origins.name: Pieter Holmplein
origins.en: Swedish sailor (ca. 1686-1776), and master in the art of seamanship. Settled in Amsterdam, first in the Korsjespoortsteeg and later in the Kattegat. He was an expert in the field of course and navigation calculation. In 1748 he published his famous 'Seaman's sextant'.

origins.name: Pieter Holmstraat
origins.en: Swedish sailor (ca. 1686-1776), and master in the art of seamanship. Settled in Amsterdam, first in the Korsjespoortsteeg and later in the Kattegat. He was an expert in the field of course and navigation calculation. In 1748 he published his famous 'Seaman's sextant'.

origins.name: Pieter Jacobszdwarsstraat
origins.en: A landowner who lived here at the end of the fourteenth century, beginning of the fifteenth century. The alley was then called Gasthuissteeg, but was later named after him.

origins.name: Pieter Jacobszstraat
origins.en: A landowner who lived here at the end of the fourteenth century, beginning of the fifteenth century. The alley was then called Gasthuissteeg, but was later named after him.

origins.name: Pieter Langendijkstraat
origins.en: Literary and playwright (1683-1756). Writer of 'The mutual marriage fraud' and 'Krelis Louwen' among others. The street was first named without the addition of the first name (1900), but this was sometimes corrupted to Lange Dijkstraat.

origins.name: Pieter Lastmankade
origins.en: Amsterdam painter (1583-1633), among other things of biblical scenes, teacher of Rembrandt. By council decision of 10-1-1923, a part is named after him in Jan van Goyenkade.

origins.name: Pieter Lodewijk Takstraat
origins.en: Journalist and politician (1848-1907), one of the leaders of the SDAP, editor-in-chief of Het Volk. He was one of the founders of the General Workers' Cooperative De Dageraad.

origins.name: Pieter Nieuwlandstraat
origins.en: Poet, historian and astronomer (1764-1794), professor in Amsterdam and Leiden in astronomy and nautical science. At the age of 19, he had already been recommended for a professorship in Latin. This street was initially named Derde Van Swindenstraat (council decision, 1882).

origins.name: Pieter Oosterhuisstraat
origins.en: Photographer (1816-1885), originally a painter. Began with a portrait studio. Later made stereoscopic photographs and cartes-de-visite of cityscapes, which he sold in large quantities. Known for his industrial photographs, which recorded the construction of railway lines, bridges, harbors and canals.

origins.name: Pieter Oosterleehof
origins.en: Pedagogue and publicist (1863-1930), director of the Christian training school De Klokkenberg in Nijmegen. A well-known personality in the education world. He wrote, among other things, 'The History of Christian Education'.

origins.name: Pieter Pauwstraat
origins.en: Pieter Adriaensz Pauw (1552-1611), councilor and alderman of Amsterdam. His brother Reynier Pauw was mayor.

origins.name: Pieter Postpad
origins.en: Master builder (1608-1669), had a share in the construction of the town hall on the Dam. Other buildings: Mauritshuis and Huis ten Bosch in The Hague, town hall in Maastricht.

origins.name: Pieter Postsingel
origins.en: Master builder (1608-1669), had a share in the construction of the town hall on the Dam. Other buildings: Mauritshuis and Huis ten Bosch in The Hague, town hall in Maastricht.

origins.name: Pieter van den Heuvelpad
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1915-1942), distributed illegal material, was involved in the preparation of the February Strike in 1941 and was part of a sabotage group within the Fokker factory in Amsterdam-North, where he worked. On November 19, 1942, he was executed in Soesterberg.

origins.name: Pieter van der Doesstraat
origins.en: Commander of the Dutch fleet in the struggle against the Spanish (1562-1599).

origins.name: Pieter van der Meulenhof
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1912-1944), born 1912 in The Hague, killed in prison in Scheveningen. Van der Meulen was active as a printer in the production of the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Pieter van der Werfstraat
origins.en: Mayor of Leiden, who distinguished himself particularly during the siege of Leiden in 1572 by his perseverance.

origins.name: Pieter Vlamingstraat
origins.en: Historian (1686-1733). He wrote a 'Description of Amsterdam' that remained unfinished due to his sudden death and was later used by the historian Jan Wagenaar.

origins.name: Pieter Zeemanlaan
origins.en: Physicist (1865-1943), professor in Amsterdam. Especially known for his study of light (Zeeman effect). In 1902 he received the Nobel Prize in Physics.

origins.name: Pietersbergweg
origins.en: Named after the Sint-Pietersberg in Maastricht.

origins.name: Pigmentstraat
origins.en: Reference to the Vettewinkel paint factory, later Sigma, which was located on the Cruquiusterrein from 1934 to 2008.

origins.name: Pijlkruidstraat
origins.en: Aquatic plant. The name refers to the shape of the leaves.

origins.name: Pijnackerstraat
origins.en: Adam Pijnacker (1622-1673), painter, in particular of landscapes.

origins.name: Pikoletstraat
origins.en: Songbird, belonging to the finch family. Found in Suriname, among other places.

origins.name: Pilatus
origins.en: Mountain peak in Switzerland, 2129 meters high.

origins.name: Pilotenstraat
origins.en: A pilot is a captain. In this case, it refers to the aircraft pilot.

origins.name: Pina Bauschplein
origins.en: Pina Bausch was a German dancer and choreographer. One of the founders of neo-expressionist modern dance.

origins.name: Pinasstraat
origins.en: A seventeenth-century sailing ship with a square stern.

origins.name: Pinatuboplein
origins.en: Mountain in the Philippines

origins.name: Pindosweg
origins.en: Pindos is a mountain range in Greece

origins.name: Pinksterbloemstraat
origins.en: The meadow plant, belonging to the family of the cruciferous plants.

origins.name: Piraeusplein
origins.en: Greek port city, on which the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a scheduled service.

origins.name: Piri Reisplein
origins.en: Hadji Muhiddin Piri Ibn Hadji Mehmed, better known as Piri Reis ('Army Captain Piri'). Ottoman sailor, navigator and cartographer from the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Creator of the Piri Reis map, a detailed world map that appeared in 1513.

origins.name: Pirinsteeg
origins.en: Pirin is a mountain in Bulgaria

origins.name: Pirolastraat
origins.en: Plant, mainly found in dune area.

origins.name: Pisuissehof
origins.en: Jean Louis Pisuisse (1880-1927), cabaret artist. Great artist in the world of folk art.

origins.name: Plaatwerkerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name: someone who processes sheet metal. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Planciusstraat
origins.en: Petrus Plancius (1550-1622), preacher and navigator. Designer of many voyages of discovery.

origins.name: Planetenplein
origins.en: Celestial bodies, which move in elliptical orbits around the sun. The earth is also a planet.

origins.name: Planetenstraat
origins.en: Celestial bodies, which move in elliptical orbits around the sun. The earth is also a planet.

origins.name: Plantage Badlaan
origins.en: To the bathhouse, which stood here from 1797 to 1820.

origins.name: Plantage Doklaan
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that this new plantation cut through in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Plantage Kerklaan
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that this new plantation cut through in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Plantage Lepellaan
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that this new plantation cut through in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Plantage Middenlaan
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that cut through this new plantation in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross lanes were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Plantage Muidergracht
origins.en: The place Muiden. The former Muidergracht began at the Leprozengracht. Part of it was renamed Jonas Daniël Meijerplein after filling in, the second part was later renamed Hortusplantsoen. The part of the Plantage Muidergracht parallel to Sarphatistraat was called Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.

origins.name: Plantage Parklaan
origins.en: The avenue ran along the former 'Park', a wide strip of land along the Nieuwe Herengracht. The Wertheimpark is the remainder of that. Where the sports field is now located, there was a concert hall with winter garden from 1849 and from 1883 to 1912 the Parkschouwburg.

origins.name: Plantage Westermanlaan
origins.en: The Nieuwe Prinsengracht originally ran through to the Entrepotdok. In 1864 it was partially drawn into Artis (recognizable by the ponds). The rest was filled in and on 19-11-1879 was renamed Plantage Prinsenlaan by Rb. On the occasion of the zoo's 125th anniversary, that name was changed in 1963 to the current name, named after Gerardus Frederik Westerman (1807-1890), the founder of 'Artis'.

origins.name: Plantagekade
origins.en: In 1682, the city government decided to build a 'plantation' in this area, which came within the city in 1658: a promenade only built with summer cottages, gardens and a few inns. A straight layout was cut across the entire area of the site. The avenue that this new plantation cut through in length was named Middenweg or Middenlaan, and three cross avenues were created. The summer houses were gradually replaced by residential houses, so today only the Wertheimpark still recalls the former purpose.

origins.name: Platanenweg
origins.en: Named after the plane tree, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Platenwagenweg
origins.en: The type of caravan, which was in use around 1930. The street name refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Platostraat
origins.en: Athenian philosopher (427-347 BC), student of Socrates. One of the greatest thinkers in history. Founded a philosophical school in Athens.

origins.name: Pleimuiden
origins.en: The English port city of Plymouth, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Plein '40-'45
origins.en: Reminiscent of the years of German occupation (World War II). On the square stands the liberation carillon. The square is located on the edge of the resistance heroes' neighborhood.

origins.name: Plein Spanje '36-'39
origins.en: The name recalls the Spanish Civil War of 1936 to 1939, the futile struggle against Franco and his fascist regime. The name and the monument erected here are a tribute to a number of volunteers from the Netherlands who died in that struggle.

origins.name: Plejadenplein
origins.en: The star group, also known as the Seven Stars.

origins.name: Plejadenweg
origins.en: The star group, also known as the Seven Stars.

origins.name: Plesmanlaan
origins.en: Albert Plesman (1889-1953), aviation pioneer. Founded KLM in 1919, of which he was director until his death.

origins.name: Plesostraat
origins.en: Name of the airport in Zagreb, Croatia.

origins.name: Plimsollweg
origins.en: Plimsoll is the brand on the skin of a ship, which indicates up to what depth can be loaded under different conditions (named after the Englishman S. Plimsoll).

origins.name: Ploegstraat
origins.en: Agricultural machinery for loosening (plowing) the arable land.

origins.name: Plotterstraat
origins.en: Typewriter controlled by a computer. As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Plutarchusstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher and writer (50-120), wrote biographies (Vitae) of a number of famous Greeks and Romans and philosophical writings (Moralia).

origins.name: Plutostraat
origins.en: The planet that is farthest from the sun.

origins.name: Pluvierplein
origins.en: The bird. In the Netherlands, the beach plover is best known.

origins.name: Pluvierstraat
origins.en: The bird. In the Netherlands, the beach plover is best known.

origins.name: Poederooienstraat
origins.en: Village on the Maas in the Bommelerwaard.

origins.name: Poeldijkstraat
origins.en: Village in the Westland.

origins.name: Poggenbeekstraat
origins.en: Georg Jan Poggenbeek (1853-1903), painter, mainly of landscapes.

origins.name: Polanenstraat
origins.en: The former village of Houtrijk and Polanen, now called Halfweg.

origins.name: Polderweg
origins.en: Back to the former state. Until around 1940, there was a polder here with the community garden complex Tuinwijk.

origins.name: Polijsterweg
origins.en: Occupational name of the person who polishes, that is, smooths an uneven surface of, for example, metal or wood.

origins.name: Polluxplein
origins.en: The star that together with the star Castor forms the main stars of the constellation Gemini.

origins.name: Polluxstraat
origins.en: The star that together with the star Castor forms the main stars of the constellation Gemini.

origins.name: Polonceau-kade
origins.en: Camille Polonceau (1813-1859), French railway engineer. Became known for his designs for girders and beams. The so-called Polonceauspant is one of the most important features of the purification plant, the boiler house and the water gas factory of the Westergasfabriek.

origins.name: Polsbroekstraat
origins.en: The rural village in the Lopikerwaard (Utrecht).

origins.name: Polygoongracht
origins.en: Film factory, founded in 1919 in Haarlem. Producer of commissioned films, documentaries and weekly cinema news bulletins.

origins.name: Pomonastraat
origins.en: Roman goddess of the fruit trees

origins.name: Pompmanstraat
origins.en: Job title: someone who is responsible for the pumps in the machine room of a ship.

origins.name: Pond Sterlinglaan
origins.en: The currency of Great Britain.

origins.name: Ponserstraat
origins.en: Occupational name: someone who blows holes, presses holes into something with a machine, for example in metal. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Pontanusstraat
origins.en: Johannes Isaac Pontanus (1571-1639), historian in the service of the king of Denmark and the States of Gelderland. In 1611 a description of Amsterdam appeared from him.

origins.name: Pontplein
origins.en: This square owes its name to the IJplein ferry that docks there.

origins.name: Pontsteiger
origins.en: The departure point of the Distelweg ferry and the Houthaven ferry.

origins.name: Poolsterstraat
origins.en: The star that is exactly above the north and therefore remains unchanged in the same place for us.

origins.name: Poolstraat
origins.en: De Pool is the name of a former warehouse on Prins Hendrikkade, in which from 1719 until its demolition in 1878 the Roman Catholic secret church De Pool was located. In the later Roman Catholic Annakerk on Wittenburgergracht (now also demolished again), which became the successor of the secret church, the facade stone of that old warehouse was placed there, so that the name went with Wittenburg.

origins.name: Poortland
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the English port city of Portland, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Poppendammergouw
origins.en: One of the quarters of the former Banne Ransdorp. The other quarters were Bloemendaal, Holysloot, Ransdorp and Durgerdam. The road came through the annexation of the municipality of Ransdorp in 1921 on Amsterdam's territory.

origins.name: Populierenweg
origins.en: Named after the poplar, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Portengenstraat
origins.en: Village, west of Breukelen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Portsmuiden
origins.en: The English port city of Portsmouth, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Postjeskade
origins.en: To the former Postjeswetering. A postje is a freshwater fish.

origins.name: Postjesweg
origins.en: To the former Postjeswetering. A postje is a freshwater fish.

origins.name: Potgieterstraat
origins.en: Everardus Johannes Potgieter (1808-1875), merchant, writer, poet and critic, who became the center of a literary circle. Founded 'De Gids' in 1837, which he would edit for thirty years.

origins.name: Potvisstraat
origins.en: Whale-like, with a round, thick head and large teeth. The sperm whale lives scattered around the world.

origins.name: Pracanalaan
origins.en: The lake of Pracana, located in Portugal, in the province of Castelo Branco.

origins.name: Pradolaan
origins.en: Museo del Prado in Madrid, the national museum of Spain, opened in 1918. The foundation of the rich art collection was laid by the collection of Charles V, which was greatly expanded by Philip II and Philip IV. Famous for the paintings of Spanish, Italian and South Dutch artists.

origins.name: Pramenpad
origins.en: A flat-bottomed small inland vessel, is mainly used for the transport of livestock and manure.

origins.name: Praterlaan
origins.en: Stadion in Vienna. Ajax won the Champions League final against AC Milan (1-0) in this stadium on May 24, 1995.

origins.name: Preangerstraat
origins.en: Landscape near Bandung in western Java (Indonesia). Known for the cultivation of coffee, tea and tea plantations.

origins.name: Presanella
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3564 meters high.

origins.name: President Allendelaan
origins.en: Salvador Allende Gossens (1908-1973), president of the Republic of Chile from 1970, died during a coup. Allende brought a socialist government with a Marxist signature to the Chilean republic. The avenue was called West Shore before 1974 (council decision, 1948).

origins.name: President Brandstraat
origins.en: Jan Hendrik Brand (1823-1888), president of the Orange Free State (from 1864). His motto is well known: 'Everything will come right, if we all do our duty'.

origins.name: President Kennedylaan
origins.en: John Fitzgerald Kennedy (1917-1963), 35th president of the United States of North America from 1961, whose short reign was characterized by a firm approach, assassinated in Texas on November 22, 1963. Before 1964, the avenue was called Rivierenlaan.

origins.name: President Kennedyplantsoen
origins.en: John Fitzgerald Kennedy (1917-1963), 35th president of the United States of North America from 1961, whose short reign was characterized by a firm approach, assassinated in Texas on November 22, 1963. Before 1964, the avenue was called Rivierenlaan.

origins.name: President Steynplantsoen
origins.en: Martinus Theunis Steijn (1857-1916), president of Oranje Vrijstraat (1896-1902). Participated in the Second Boer War (1899-1902).

origins.name: President Steynstraat
origins.en: Martinus Theunis Steijn (1857-1916), president of Oranje Vrijstraat (1896-1902). Participated in the Second Boer War (1899-1902).

origins.name: Pretoriusstraat
origins.en: Andries Pretorius (1799-1853), one of the pioneers of the Transvaal Boers, defeated the Zulu king Dingaan in 1838. The city of Pretoria is named after him.

origins.name: Prins Bernhardplein
origins.en: Named after His Highness Prins Bernhard Lucas Emmanuel of Orange-Nassau, Van Vollenhoven (1969-).

origins.name: Prins Hendrikkade
origins.en: The youngest son of King William II, Prince William Frederick Hendrik (1820-1879), who had a warm interest in trade and shipping. The bust of the prince stands opposite the Shipping House and was made in 1885 by Professor F. Stracke. With the naming in 1879, a number of evocative names disappeared and with them a piece of memory of history. Calculated from the Singel, these were: the Herring Factory, derived from the herring trade established here in the late sixteenth century, on the site of the current Herring Factory Bridge stood the Herring Factory Tower.

origins.name: Prins Hendriklaan
origins.en: Hendrik, Duke of Mecklenburg-Schwerin, Prince of the Netherlands (1876-1934), married Queen Wilhelmina in 1901.

origins.name: Prinseneiland
origins.en: Probably named after the house 'The three Princes', which must have stood here in the seventeenth century. The house had busts of Prince William I, Prince Maurice and Prince Frederick Henry. However, it is not known where this house stood.

origins.name: Prinsengracht
origins.en: To 'the princely title', which refers to that of the princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and in terms of the nature of the buildings, the simplest. During the enlargement of 1612, it was dug and built from Brouwersgracht to Leidsegracht. With the enlargement of 1658, this canal is also extended across the Amstel (up to the Entrepotdok). For the part on the Plantage, see also Plantage Westermanlaan - formerly Plantage Prinsenlaan. The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for the current Noordermarkt did not find favor with the bourgeoisie.

origins.name: Prinsenhofssteeg
origins.en: The former St. Ceciliënsklooster was converted into a residence for royal persons visiting the city after 1578. This is why the building was named Prinsenhof. When the meetings of the Admiralty were later held here, in addition to the name Prinsenhof, the name Admiralty Hof was also created. In 1808, the town hall on the Dam was converted into a palace and the Prinsenhof became the town hall. This remained until 1988. In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries this was Ceciliënsteeg.

origins.name: Prinsensluis
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the street in which it is located and the canal over which it lies. Prince refers to the royal title here, which refers to that of the princes of Orange.

origins.name: Prinsenstraat
origins.en: To 'the princely title', which refers to that of the princes of Orange

origins.name: Prinses Amaliaplein
origins.en: Catharina-Amalia Beatrix Carmen Victoria of Orange-Nassau (December 7, 2003), heir princess of Orange, Prinses of the Netherlands, Prinses of Orange-Nassau, eldest daughter of Prince Willem-Alexander and Princess Máxima. Her nickname is Amalia.

origins.name: Prinses Irenestraat
origins.en: Irene Emma Elisabeth, second daughter of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard, born 5-8-1939. She married in 1964 in Rome to the French nobleman Prince Carel Hugo of Bourbon Parma. For technical reasons, the western part of the Prinses Irenestraat near Rb. was renamed Fred. Roeskestraat on 27-4-1977.

origins.name: Prinses Margrietstraat
origins.en: Margriet Francisca, princess of the Netherlands, born 1943 in Canada, third daughter of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard. In 1967 she married Pieter van Vollenhoven.

origins.name: Prinses Marijkestraat
origins.en: Maria Christina, princess of the Netherlands, born 1947. Fourth daughter of Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard. Was first called Princess Marijke, but has been calling herself Princess Christina since 1967.

origins.name: Printerstraat
origins.en: Device with which text and images, stored in a computer, can be printed. As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Processorstraat
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Prof. H. Bavinckstraat
origins.en: Herman Bavinck (1854-1921), professor of theology at the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam. Due to his work in the field of pedagogy, he had a great influence on Christian education.

origins.name: Prof. Ph. Kohnstammstraat
origins.en: Philippus Abraham Kohnstamm (1875-1951), professor of pedagogy in Amsterdam and Utrecht. Had a great influence on the field of pedagogy at home and abroad.

origins.name: Prof. R. Casimirstraat
origins.en: Rommert Casimir (1877-1957), pedagogue, professor at Leiden, publicist.

origins.name: Prof. Tulpplein
origins.en: Nicolaas Tulp (1593-1674), Amsterdam physician, professor at the Athenaeum Illustre for the surgical guild. Also several times mayor of the city. The title Professor was added to the street name in 1946, because many were inclined to look for the street in the flower district.

origins.name: Prof. Tulpstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Tulp (1593-1674), Amsterdam physician, professor at the Athenaeum Illustre for the surgical guild. Also several times mayor of the city. The title Professor was added to the street name in 1946, because many were inclined to look for the street in the flower district.

origins.name: Professor J.H. Gunningstraat
origins.en: Professor Johannes Hermanus Gunning (1859-1951), pedagogue. He was the first professor of pedagogy in government service and was the first in the Netherlands to advocate for the establishment of a high school.

origins.name: Profiltigracht
origins.en: Film factory, founded in 1929 in The Hague. Producer of (commissioned) films, documentaries and cinema newsreels. First counterpart, later partner of Polygoon.

origins.name: Programmeurstraat
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Propaanweg
origins.en: A petroleum derivative: gas used as motor fuel.

origins.name: Propellerstraat
origins.en: The common propulsion method for aircraft before the advent of jet engines.

origins.name: Provincialeweg
origins.en: Name determined by the municipality of Weesperkarspel for the road along the Weespertrekvaart and the Gaasp. Originally, the road was called the Weesperzandpad, built around 1640 by the cities of Amsterdam and Weesp. Until 1929, the road was managed by the Commissioners of the Zandpad. In 1929, management was taken over by the Province.

origins.name: Pruimenstraat
origins.en: The fruits of the plum tree.

origins.name: Ptolemaeusstraat
origins.en: Claudius Ptolemy (second century AD), Greek mathematician and astronomer. He first gave an overview of the geographical lengths and latitudes of the main cities of antiquity. Ptolemy's theorem: in a quadrilateral with coordinates, the product of the diagonals is equal to the sum of the products of the opposite sides.

origins.name: Puiflijkpad
origins.en: Village in the Land of Maas and Waal (Gelderland).

origins.name: Pumoriplein
origins.en: Pumori is a mountain in the Himalayas

origins.name: Punterspad
origins.en: An open boat with flat bottom, particularly in use in the area around Giethoorn.

origins.name: Purmerhof
origins.en: The polder, created by the draining of the lake between 1618 and 1622 near Purmerend.

origins.name: Purmerplein
origins.en: The polder, created by the draining of the lake between 1618 and 1622 near Purmerend.

origins.name: Purmerweg
origins.en: The polder, created by the draining of the lake between 1618 and 1622 near Purmerend.

origins.name: Purperhoedenveem
origins.en: A veem is a company responsible for storing and delivering goods in and out of its warehouses. The veems each had their own license plate, after which they were named. These could be different colors and models of hats (e.g. Puper hats, Clogs). They also derived their name from the origin of the workers (e.g. Vriesseveem, Zeeuwse Veem).

origins.name: Putterplantsoen
origins.en: Songbird, also known as thistle finch. Often kept as a cage bird.

origins.name: Putterstraat
origins.en: Songbird, also known as thistle finch. Often kept as a cage bird.

origins.name: Pybo Steenstrastraat
origins.en: Educator (died in 1788). Lecturer in mathematics, astronomy and nautical science at the Athenaeum Illustre in Amsterdam. Examiner of the sailors in service of the VOC in Amsterdam. He published among other things 'Fundamental principles of seamanship' (1766) and 'Public lessons on finding longitude at sea' (1770).

origins.name: Pyreneeën
origins.en: The mountain, located in France and Spain.

origins.name: Pythagorasstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher and mathematician (582-507 BC), best known for the theorem named after him: the square of the hypotenuse of a right triangle is equal to the sum of the squares of the two right sides. The street was called Mr. Cornelis van Lennepstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1904) before 1922.

origins.name: Quashibastraat
origins.en: Quashiba lived in slavery on Saint Martin. In 1835 she managed to escape in a small boat with a few fellow slaves, including her two children Sammy and Jane, to the nearby British island of Anguilla. Five years ago, her partner, Matthew Stancliff, dared to sail to Sint Maarten to pick up Quashiba's sister Minny and her children as well, so that they too could live freely. Quashiba and her family are therefore facing the struggle for freedom.

origins.name: Quellijnstraat
origins.en: Artus Quellijn or Quellinus (1609-1668), South Dutch sculptor. He made, among other things, the sculpture for the town hall on the Dam.

origins.name: Quinten Massijsstraat
origins.en: Flemish painter and goldsmith (1466-1530). The name is also written as Matsijs.

origins.name: R.J.H. Fortuynplein
origins.en: R.J.H. Fortuyn (born 1916) was appointed director of the Royal Dutch Lloyd in Amsterdam in 1956.

origins.name: R.J.H. Fortuynstraat
origins.en: R.J.H. Fortuyn (born 1916) was appointed director of the Royal Dutch Lloyd in Amsterdam in 1956.

origins.name: Raadhuisstraat
origins.en: To the town hall, designed in the seventeenth century by Jacob van Campen and built by Daniël Stalpaert. In 1808, ordered by King Louis Napoleon, it was evacuated and has since been used as a royal palace. The Raadhuisstraat was created in 1895 by widening the Huiszittensteeg and the Korte Huiszittensteeg, by filling in the Warmoesgracht and by a breakthrough of the canal wall.

origins.name: Raamdwarsstraat
origins.en: The linen windows, where the painted linen was hung to dry, had to be set up outside the city. When the Kloveniersburgwal was still the city moat, these windows could be found at the height of the current Raamgracht. The nearby Verversstraat also still reminds us of this old Amsterdam industry.

origins.name: Raamgracht
origins.en: The linen windows, where the painted linen was hung to dry, had to be set up outside the city. When the Kloveniersburgwal was still the city moat, these windows could be found at the height of the current Raamgracht. The nearby Verversstraat also still reminds us of this old Amsterdam industry.

origins.name: Raamplein
origins.en: The linen windows, which were moved here, were drawn into the city during the enlargements of the city in the sixteenth century when the area between Kloveniersburgwal and Zwanenburgwal was drawn into the city. The Raamplein was created by filling in a section of Lijnbaansgracht.

origins.name: Raampoort
origins.en: This bridge is named after the Raampoort, which was demolished in 1844

origins.name: Raamsteeg
origins.en: The linen windows that were found on the outside of the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. This is the oldest place whose name is remembered by the linen dyeing houses.

origins.name: Raamstraat
origins.en: The linen windows, which were moved here, when the city was expanded in the sixteenth century, the area between Kloveniersburgwal and Zwanenburgwal was drawn closer to the city. Raamplein was created by filling in a section of Lijnbaansgracht.

origins.name: Raasdorperweg
origins.en: The former hamlet of Raasdorp, which was located on the edge of the Lutkemeer.

origins.name: Rachel Ruyschbrug
origins.en: Rachel Ruysch (The Hague, 1664 - Amsterdam, 1750) was one of the most successful still life painters of the 17th and 18th centuries. She is world famous for her colorful and lifelike floral paintings. As a married woman and mother of ten children, she continued her brilliant career unabated.

origins.name: Radarweg
origins.en: The navigation aid for ships and aircraft in the dark and poor visibility. The system is based on the reflection of radio waves. Radar is the abbreviation of Radio Detection and Ranging. The road was initially named Gyroscope Road.

origins.name: Radboud
origins.en: Square castle with round corner towers founded around 1289 by Floris V in Medemblik (North Holland). Partially demolished in the seventeenth century and rebuilt in 1890.

origins.name: Rademakerstraat
origins.en: Abraham Rademaker (1675,76-1735) was a Dutch engraver and painter who became famous for his prints of castles, cities and country estates in the 17th and 18th centuries. He made dozens of images of existing country estates in the vicinity of Amsterdam, among other places.

origins.name: Raden Adjeng Kartinistraat
origins.en: Indonesian publicist and propagandist (1879-1904), advocate for human rights and pioneer of the Indonesian feminist movement. In 1903 her manifesto 'Give the Javanese education' appeared, followed in 1911 by her letters. In 1964 she was elevated to national heroine.

origins.name: Raderbootstraat
origins.en: Vehicle, which is propelled by means of propellers.

origins.name: Radioweg
origins.en: The transmission of sound and signals through electrical waves, discovered by Hertz in 1888 and first applied by Marconi in 1900. At the time of the establishment of this street name, radio was one of the most important discoveries, through the application via the broadcasting associations.

origins.name: Ramskooi
origins.en: No explanation can be found for the name of this alley, which already existed around 1450. Some historians think of the name of a Norwegian woodcutter, while another assumption is that Jan Ran had a duck pond here. In the sixteenth century, the alley appears under the name Jan Ranskoy. The alley originally ran through to Prins Hendrikkade, which until 1879 was called Texelse kade for that part, and even earlier Nieuwezijds Houttuinen.

origins.name: Randwijkhof
origins.en: Location in Gelderland, located between Wageningen and Arnhem.

origins.name: Rangeerderstraat
origins.en: Railway worker, who is responsible for connecting and disconnecting train carriages and maneuvering the trains to the different tracks.

origins.name: Ranonkelkade
origins.en: Named after the buttercup (ranunculus), a plant.

origins.name: Raoul Wallenberghofje
origins.en: Swedish diplomat (1912-unknown), he advocated for peace and human rights. During World War II, he saved tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews from deportation. In 1945, he was captured by Soviet troops. In 1947, according to the Soviets, he died of a heart attack in captivity, but his death has never been confirmed.

origins.name: Raoul Wallenbergstraat
origins.en: Swedish diplomat (1912-unknown), he advocated for peace and human rights. During World War II, he saved tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews from deportation. In 1945, he was captured by Soviet troops. In 1947, according to the Soviets, he died of a heart attack in captivity, but his death has never been confirmed.

origins.name: Rapenburg
origins.en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now Oosterdok), Oudeschans, Rapenburgwal and Schippersgrachtje. The main street has taken the name of the island. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

origins.name: Rapenburgerplein
origins.en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now Oosterdok), Oudeschans, Rapenburgwal and Schippersgrachtje. The main street has taken the name of the island. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

origins.name: Rapenburgerstraat
origins.en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now Oosterdok), Oudeschans, Rapenburgwal and Schippersgrachtje. The main street has taken the name of the island. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

origins.name: Raphael Lemkinstraat
origins.en: Polish-Jewish lawyer (1901-1959), fought in the Polish resistance in 1939, fled to Sweden and later to the US. In the Holocaust he lost 49 family members. In 1944 he introduced the term genocide and in 1948 he was the driving force behind the UN negotiations on the Genocide Convention.

origins.name: Raphaëlplein
origins.en: Raffaëllo di Senti (1483-1520), Italian painter, leading figure of the Renaissance. Painted numerous madonnas, frescoes and portraits. Also worked as an architect on St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.

origins.name: Raphaëlstraat
origins.en: Raffaëllo di Senti (1483-1520), Italian painter, leading figure of the Renaissance. Painted numerous madonnas, frescoes and portraits. Also worked as an architect on St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.

origins.name: Ravensteinplein
origins.en: Old fortified town on the Maas (North Brabant).

origins.name: Ravensteinstraat
origins.en: Old fortified town on the Maas (North Brabant).

origins.name: Ravenstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out on the grounds of the shipyard 'De Raven' that was demolished in 1887. Marten Willems Raven is listed as the owner of this shipyard in 1692.

origins.name: Ravenswaaipad
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Maurik in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Ravenwerf
origins.en: The shipbuilding yard 'De Zwarte Raaf', which used to be located here between Kattenburgerstraat and -gracht.

origins.name: Realengracht
origins.en: Reynier Reael, in 1633 alderman (schepen) of the city. He was the owner of the entire Realeneiland.

origins.name: Réaumurstraat
origins.en: René Antoine F. de Réaumur (1683-1757), French physicist. In 1730 he constructed the thermometer named after him with an eighty-part scale. The street name was previously established by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer as Bothastraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1891).

origins.name: Recht Boomssloot
origins.en: The 16th-century shipbuilder Cornelis Pietersz Boom. To connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the surrounding water, he had a canal and a cross-channel dug. These were then named after him.

origins.name: Reesluis
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the Reestraat, in which it lies.

origins.name: Reestraat
origins.en: Deer species. The name recalls the fur trade, which was concentrated before the construction of the street in this neighborhood, and later in the nearby southern part of the Jordaan.

origins.name: Reewijkplein
origins.en: The South Holland village of Reeuwijk.

origins.name: Reggestraat
origins.en: Side river of the Overijssel Vecht.

origins.name: Reguliersbreestraat
origins.en: All these names remind us of the Reguliersklooster, which stood outside the then-city gate from 1394 to 1532, on the site where Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now intersect. The city gate, whose Mint Tower is a remnant, was formerly called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht ended at that gate at that time. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, parts of it were demolished. Before 1909, Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Reguliersdwarsstraat
origins.en: All these names remind us of the Reguliersklooster, which stood outside the then-city gate from 1394 to 1532, on the site where Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now intersect. The city gate, whose Mint Tower is a remnant, was formerly called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht ended at that gate at that time. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, parts of it were demolished. Before 1909, Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Reguliersgracht
origins.en: All these names remind us of the Reguliersklooster, which stood outside the then-city gate from 1394 to 1532, on the site where Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now intersect. The city gate, whose Mint Tower is a remnant, was formerly called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht ended there at that gate. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, parts of it were demolished. Before 1909, Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Reigersbos
origins.en: Name of a farm that stood on Abcouderstraatweg near the former Zwetskade.

origins.name: Reigersbosachterom
origins.en: Name of a farm that stood on Abcouderstraatweg near the former Zwetskade.

origins.name: Reigersbosdreef
origins.en: Name of a farm that stood on Abcouderstraatweg near the former Zwetskade.

origins.name: Reigersbospad
origins.en: Name of a farm that stood on Abcouderstraatweg near the former Zwetskade.

origins.name: Reigerweg
origins.en: Named after the heron, a bird.

origins.name: Reijnier Vinkeleskade
origins.en: Etcher and draftsman (1741-1816), produced approximately three thousand prints, including many Amsterdam cityscapes. His work is therefore also important for topography.

origins.name: Reimersbeek
origins.en: Castle in Nuth (Limburg), founded in the sixteenth century, partially demolished and renovated in the eighteenth century. Today it is a rectangular house, consisting of three wings with a seventeenth-century gatehouse and accompanying farmhouse from 1705.

origins.name: Reimerswaalstraat
origins.en: Location on Zuid-Beveland near Yerseke. The land of Reimerswaal was completely swallowed up by a storm surge in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Reina Prinsen Geerligsstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1922-1943), born in Semarang (Indonesia), killed in the Oranienburg concentration camp (Germany).

origins.name: Reinaert de Vosstraat
origins.en: Medieval animal epic, probably of French origin, edited in Middle Dutch in 1260. Before 1939, this street was part of the Zeven Provinciënstraat (= Bestevâerstraat).

origins.name: Reinhard Dozyhof
origins.en: Historian (1820-1883), professor at Leiden. Famous orientalist.

origins.name: Reinier Claeszenplein
origins.en: Dutch vice-admiral. Was attacked by the Spanish fleet in 1606 at Cape St. Vincent (Portugal) and was flown into the air, instead of surrendering.

origins.name: Reinier Claeszenstraat
origins.en: Dutch vice-admiral. Was attacked by the Spanish fleet in 1606 at Cape St. Vincent (Portugal) and was flown into the air, instead of surrendering.

origins.name: Reinier Engelmanstraat
origins.en: Actor (1795-1845), pupil, later partner, of Andries Snoek.

origins.name: Reinveen
origins.en: Former farm on the Uitweg, demolished for the construction of garden city Osdorp.

origins.name: Reinwardtstraat
origins.en: Caspar G.C. Reinwardt (1773-1854), professor of chemistry and pharmacy in Amsterdam. Director of the Royal Cabinet of Natural History in Amsterdam. Organized the medical service in Java in 1817.

origins.name: Reitdiepstraat
origins.en: Channel between the city of Groningen and Zoutkamp.

origins.name: Reitzstraat
origins.en: Francis William Reitz (1844-1934), South African statesman and writer. President of Oranje Vrijstraat from 1889 to 1896. Participated in the Second Boer War (1899-1902).

origins.name: Reizigersweg
origins.en: Travelling people. The name refers to the caravan park on site.

origins.name: Reling
origins.en: The railing of the fence that surrounds the ship deck.

origins.name: Rembrandtpark
origins.en: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn (1606-1669), the greatest Dutch painter of the Golden Age. The placement of his statue, first on the side in 1852, in the middle in 1875, was the reason why the square was renamed Rembrandtplein in 1876. Previously, the square was called Botermarkt, while the corner at Amstelstraat was unofficially called Kippenhoek because of the poultry market.

origins.name: Rembrandtplein
origins.en: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn (1606-1669), the greatest Dutch painter of the Golden Age. In 1852, the cast iron Rembrandt Monument, which was made by Louis Royer, was unveiled by King William III. This was first placed on the side of the square. In 1875, the monument was moved to the center, which was the reason for changing the name of the square to Rembrandtplein. Before that, the square was called Botermarkt after the market that took place here every Monday morning since the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Remijden
origins.en: Historical name of a piece of land in the old Sloten.

origins.name: Remmerdenplein
origins.en: Neighborhood in the Gelderland municipality of Rheden.

origins.name: Rengerskerkestraat
origins.en: A village lost in a storm surge in the seventeenth century south of Schouwen (Zeeland).

origins.name: Renkumhof
origins.en: Place on the Rhine (Gelderland).

origins.name: Renooiplein
origins.en: Village on the Linge in the Betuwe.

origins.name: Renswoudestraat
origins.en: Village in the Gelderse valley, with a seventeenth-century castle of the same name (Utrecht).

origins.name: Resedastraat
origins.en: The garden plant. Found in the wild in dune area.

origins.name: Retiefstraat
origins.en: Pieter Retief (1788-1838), leader of the South African Boers during the Great Trek of 1835 and the following years.

origins.name: Retirobrug
origins.en: Station in Buenos Aires

origins.name: Revaleiland
origins.en: Nowadays Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. Amsterdam was the largest buyer of rye, grain and wood in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Reyer Anslostraat
origins.en: Poet (1625-1669), wrote among other things a laudatory poem on Amsterdam on the occasion of the laying of the first stone of the new town hall in 1648. Before 1896, this street was called Nieuwer-Amstel Parkstraat by the municipality.

origins.name: Rheastraat
origins.en: Figure from Greek mythology. One of the Titans, wife of Cronus, mother of Hestia, Hera, Demeter, Poseidon, Hades and Zeus.

origins.name: Rhenenhof
origins.en: City on the Rhine near the Grebbeberg (Utrecht).

origins.name: Rhijnestein
origins.en: Ridderhofstad in Cothen near Jutphaas on the Kromme Rijn, consisting of a residential tower and a gate from the sixteenth century. The second tower and the central part date from around 1850.

origins.name: Rhijnspoorplein
origins.en: To the former Rhijnspoorwegmaatschappij, which opened the Weesperpoort station here in 1843. The company was later incorporated into the Dutch Railways.

origins.name: Rhijnvis Feithstraat
origins.en: Poet (1753-1824). Both in his poetry and his plays he was a great innovator. Loved by many during his lifetime. His evangelical New Year's carol is well known: 'Hours days months years, flying like a shadow away'.

origins.name: Rhodosweg
origins.en: Greek island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Rhôneweg
origins.en: The river, which springs in Switzerland and flows through Lake Geneva and France near Marseille into the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Ribesstraat
origins.en: Named after the flowering currant (ribes), a shrub.

origins.name: Richard Holstraat
origins.en: Conductor, composer and pedagogue (1825-1904). Leader of the classical concerts in the Palace of Public Enterprise, teacher of Johan Wagenaar and Willem Mengelberg. Composed a number of symphonies.

origins.name: Richard Wagnerstraat
origins.en: German composer (1813-1883), creator of the nineteenth-century German musical drama ('Lohengrin', 'Tannhauser', 'Parsifal', 'Nibelungen').

origins.name: Ridderspoorweg
origins.en: Plant with purple, blue, red, yellow or white flowers. The scientific name, 'Delphinium', comes from the Latin word for dolphin, because the buds of the flower resemble a dolphin in some ways.

origins.name: Rie Mastenbroekstraat
origins.en: Hendrika Wilhelmina Kuypers-Mastenbroek (1919-2003), swimmer. Won three gold medals and one silver medal in 1936 during the Olympic Games, an unprecedented medal haul for a swimmer to date.

origins.name: Riekerweg
origins.en: To the Riekerpolder located here. The name comes from the former village of Rijk that was located south of the village of Sloten.

origins.name: Rietlandpark
origins.en: Until around 1880, an undeveloped, partly swampy and reed-covered area. After trade areas and sorting areas were built here at the end of the nineteenth century, the docks and roads were given their own names. The name Stads Rietlanden is still used today for the sorting area.

origins.name: Rietlandterras
origins.en: Until around 1880, an undeveloped, partly swampy and reed-covered area. After trade areas and sorting areas were built here at the end of the nineteenth century, the docks and roads were given their own names. The name Stads Rietlanden is still used today for the sorting area.

origins.name: Rietnesse
origins.en: The former castle of Costijn van Sirixe in Zierikzee on Schouwen-Duiveland (Zeeland).

origins.name: Rietveld Schröderpad
origins.en: The museum Het Rietveld Schröderhuis in Utrecht. The architect Gerrit Rietveld (1888-1964) designed the house for Truus Schröder-Schräder, whose contribution has been very decisive for the final result. The house, the interior and the furniture comply with the architectural principles of De Stijl. After the death of Truus Schröder in 1985, the house was opened to the public.

origins.name: Rietwijkerstraat
origins.en: A neighborhood that disappeared due to the construction of the Amsterdamse Bos under Amstelveen. Originally a village located further west, it was drowned in the Haarlemmermeer in the second half of the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Rietzangerweg
origins.en: Named after the sedge warbler, a singing bird.

origins.name: Rigakade
origins.en: Port and capital of Latvia.

origins.name: Rigelstraat
origins.en: Star in the constellation Orion.

origins.name: Rijgersborgh
origins.en: Farm (also called Reigersbosch) on the Uitweg, demolished for the construction of the Slotermeer district.

origins.name: Rijnlandlaan
origins.en: An area around the Old Rhine from Katwijk aan Zee to Utrecht, mostly in the current province of South Holland.

origins.name: Rijnsburgstraat
origins.en: Location in South Holland. The street originally made up part of the Sloterweg, but this section was renamed in 1973, because due to urban expansion the Sloterweg was divided into two parts.

origins.name: Rijnstraat
origins.en: The river that springs in Switzerland, which comes into our country near Lobith.

origins.name: Rijsbesstraat
origins.en: Blue-black currant from the heath family, slightly ovaler than the forest currant, rare in the Netherlands. Grows in peat-rich soil near forest ponds. Tastes slightly sweet and is used to make jam, jelly or juice.

origins.name: Rijsdrechthof
origins.en: Old Rhine-Landish name: a water north of Leimuiden, disappeared due to the draining of the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Rijssenburghof
origins.en: Drowned settlement between Leimuiden and Aalsmeer.

origins.name: Rijswijkstraat
origins.en: Village in South Holland, border municipality of The Hague.

origins.name: Rijtuigenhof
origins.en: This courtyard with the adjacent houses was laid out and built on a site that was occupied from 1910 until around 1980 by the company buildings of the Amsterdamse Rijtuig Maatschappij.

origins.name: Ringdijk
origins.en: Regarding its location relative to the Watergraafsmeer. The Ooster Ringdijk was named Noorder- and Zuider-Ringdijk before the annexation of the Watergraafsmeer municipality. The Eerste Ringdijkstraat was then called Schoollaan, while even earlier the name Dielemanstraat seems to have appeared. A Tweede Ringdijkstraat (formerly Dijklaan) has now completely disappeared due to demolition.

origins.name: Ringslangpad
origins.en: Harmless snake from the family of water snakes, native to Amsterdam. Can reach a length of up to one and a half meters. The color is brown to olive green, and the animal owes its name to the yellow neck spots that can merge into a ring.

origins.name: Ringvaartdijk
origins.en: The water along which the path runs. A canal is the bosom of a polder, into which excess water from the polder is discharged.

origins.name: Ringweg-Noord
origins.en: Named after the function of this national road (A 10), whose parts have been localized by adding the wind direction. The western part of this Ringweg was previously named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten IJ via a tunnel.

origins.name: Ringweg-Oost
origins.en: Named after the function of this national road (A 10), whose parts have been localized by adding the wind direction. The western part of this ring road was previously named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten IJ via a tunnel.

origins.name: Ringweg-West
origins.en: Named after the function of this national road (A 10), whose parts have been localized by adding the wind direction. The western part of this Ringweg was previously named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten IJ via a tunnel.

origins.name: Ringweg-Zuid
origins.en: Named after the function of this national road (A 10), whose parts have been localized by adding the wind direction. The western part of this Ringweg was previously named Einsteinweg, Coentunnelweg and Coentunnel. The Ringweg-Oost crosses the Buiten IJ via a tunnel.

origins.name: Rini Ottehof
origins.en: Sara Catharina Otte (1917-1991), film actress, made a sensation as a young girl in 1935 with her leading role in the film 'Young Hearts'. Especially her appearance and her unpolished way of acting stood out.

origins.name: Rinus Michelslaan
origins.en: Marinus Jacobus Hendricus Michels (1928-2005), footballer and coach of Ajax. In 1971 he won the European Cup I with Ajax. Then achieved great success as coach of Barcelona and as national coach of the Dutch national team, during the World Cup in 1974 (second) and the European Championship in 1988 (first). Gained the nickname 'the General'. Founder of 'total football'.

origins.name: Riouwstraat
origins.en: The Riouw Archipelago, a group of islands in Indonesia near the east coast of Sumatra.

origins.name: Rita Reysbrug
origins.en: Maria Everdina Reys (1924-2013) is the most famous jazz singer in the Netherlands and perhaps in Europe, as evidenced by her nickname 'Europe's First Lady of Jazz'. She was married to Wessel Ilcken, who has a street name near this bridge. In the Park Haagseweg, all the streets are named after famous jazz musicians.

origins.name: Ritzema Bosstraat
origins.en: Jan Ritzema Bos (1850-1928), botanist, professor at Wageningen. Founder of plant pathology and of state supervision of it in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Robbert Cijferstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1919-1945), born in Amsterdam, executed at the Zijpersluis (North Holland).

origins.name: Robert Doumastraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1918-1943), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Robert Fruinlaan
origins.en: Robert Jacobus Fruin (1823-1899), historian, professor at Leiden. Wrote a large number of historical studies, including 'Ten years from the Eighty Years' War'.

origins.name: Robert Kochplantsoen
origins.en: German bacteriologist (1843-1910), discoverer of the cholera bacterium (1883) and of the tuberculosis bacterium (1882). Won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1905. Part of the Robert Kochplantsoen was built on the former Meerlaan (council decision, 1923).

origins.name: Robert Scottstraat
origins.en: English South Pole traveler (1868-1912). Died during a second expedition, during which he reached the South Pole.

origins.name: Robijnstraat
origins.en: Hard, red gemstone. The municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel gave the street its name Tweede De when it was built.

origins.name: Rochussenstraat
origins.en: Jan Jacob Rochussen (1797-1871), statesman. successively Minister of Finance, Governor-General of Dutch East Indies and Minister of Colonies.

origins.name: Rocketstraat
origins.en: Name of the first English locomotive to run on a regular railway service.

origins.name: Rode Kruisstraat
origins.en: The street was thus named on the occasion of the centenary of the Dutch Rode Cross (founded in 1867). The adjacent streets are named after persons closely involved in this.

origins.name: Rodenrijsstraat
origins.en: Village north of Rotterdam.

origins.name: Roebelkade
origins.en: The currency of Russia.

origins.name: Roelantstraat
origins.en: To the Roelantslied. The epic from the thirteenth century that tells the story of Roelant, a knight of the Frankish prince Charlemagne. Before 1939, this street was part of the De Rijpstraat.

origins.name: Roelof Hartplein
origins.en: Amsterdam physician and philanthropist (1837-1892).

origins.name: Roelof Hartstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam physician and philanthropist (1837-1892).

origins.name: Roemer
origins.en: Named after a ditch between the Twiske and De Gouw. Disappeared due to the construction of the Twiske.

origins.name: Roemer Visscherstraat
origins.en: Amsterdam merchant and poet (1547-1620). Host for the artists Vondel, Hooft, Huygens and Brederode in his home on the Geldersekade.

origins.name: Roepie Kruizestraat
origins.en: Jan Hendrik Kruize (1925-1992), hockey player. Won bronze with his team at the 1948 Olympic Games in London and four years later in Helsinki silver.

origins.name: Roerdomppad
origins.en: Name of underlying path

origins.name: Roerstraat
origins.en: River that springs in the Eifel and flows into the Maas near Roermond.

origins.name: Roeselarestraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of West Flanders.

origins.name: Roesiel
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the French port city of La Rochelle, which appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Roetersstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Roeters (1617-1699), alderman of the city and owner of the land of the Roeterseiland named after him. The street was laid out on the Roetersburgwal, which was reclaimed in 1873.

origins.name: Roffart
origins.en: A seventeenth-century outdoor space with a gate from 1629 in Baarlo (Limburg).

origins.name: Roggeveenstraat
origins.en: Jacob Roggeveen (1659-1729), sailor, who made a trip to East India around South America in 1721/1723. He discovered on that trip, on Easter 1722, the island that has since been called Easter Island.

origins.name: Rokin
origins.en: We must discard the long-standing theory that this name is a derivation from Rak-in (a rak within the Dam, such as the Damrak outside the Dam). This part of the Amstel, now partially dammed for 2/3 of its length, originally had no embankments. The buildings on Kalverstraat ran right down to the water. When in the sixteenth century the facade along the water of the first part was moved back from the Dam, something had to give way, a quay was built here, which was designated as Ruck-in in 1559. A few years later this became the Rock-in. With later extension, the entire quay was given this name.

origins.name: Rollemanstraat
origins.en: The street name refers to the caravan park on site. Rolleman is slang for caravan resident.

origins.name: Rombout Hogerbeetsstraat
origins.en: Pensioner of Leiden (1561-1626), supporter of Hugo de Groot. Imprisoned in 1619, but released in 1625 after the death of Prince Maurice. The name of the street had previously been established as Eerste Hugo de Grootdwarsstraat (council decision, 1897).

origins.name: Romeinsarmsteeg
origins.en: To an old signboard on which a hand with a sword could be seen. On the arm you could recognize a sleeve of Roman clothing. Such a signboard could also be seen on a house on the Vijgendam until 1847. Before the seventeenth century, this was the Nieuwe Kruissteeg.

origins.name: Romerostraat
origins.en: Oscar Arnulfo Romero (1917-1980), archbishop of San Salvador, capital of El Salvador. Spoke for the voice of the opposition. On March 24, 1980, he was murdered on the steps in front of the cathedral by right-wing paramilitary forces.

origins.name: Rondeel
origins.en: A semicircular, usually stone, bastion that was part of the city wall at the beginning of the sixteenth century. A rondeau is lower and made of heavier masonry than the older wall towers. Due to its meaning and due to the first syllable of the word, the name refers to the round shape of the new building.

origins.name: Röntgenstraat
origins.en: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen (1845-1923), German physicist. Discovered x-rays (X-rays) in 1895, applied in medicine for making photographs of internal body parts. He won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901. The municipality of Watergraafsmeer named the street during its construction Wilhelminastraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1904).

origins.name: Roomolenstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a facade stone. In the seventeenth century the street was called Molensteeg, later Roomolensteeg and in 1884 it was changed by the municipal council to Roomolenstraat. Perhaps the alley led to a (red) mill, which stood here outside the fortress before 1600.

origins.name: Roompotstraat
origins.en: Current channel in the mouth of the Oosterschelde, along the coast of Walcheren.

origins.name: Roomtuintjes
origins.en: Old amusement park, formerly located on the Mauritskade, where Pieter Vlamingstraat now begins. Demolished between 1880 and 1884 for the construction of the Dapperbuurt.

origins.name: Rooseveltlaan
origins.en: Franklin Delano Roosevelt (1882-1945), president of the United States from 1932. Comes from a Dutch family that emigrated to America in 1649. He played a major role in the Allied victory in World War II, partly because he strongly opposed American neutrality. When the street was built, it was named Zuider Amstellaan (council decision, 1922).

origins.name: Roosje Vospad
origins.en: Socialist trade union leader and politician (1860-1932, married to M. Stel), fighter for universal suffrage. One of the first women to try to integrate her feminist views into a socialist position.

origins.name: Roosje Vosstraat
origins.en: Socialist trade union leader and politician (1860-1932, married to M. Stel), fighter for universal suffrage. One of the first women to try to integrate her feminist views into a socialist position.

origins.name: Rooswijck
origins.en: Eighteenth-century country house with later added towers, located between Santpoort and Velsen (North Holland).

origins.name: Rosa Luxemburgstraat
origins.en: German politician (1870-1919), representative of the radical-Marxist movement in the social democracy. During World War I imprisoned for anti-war agitation. In 1918 she was one of the leaders of the communist Spartacus League, which was soon transformed into the Communist Party of Germany. Killed by officers.

origins.name: Rosa Manusstraat
origins.en: Rosette Suzanne (Rosa) Manus (1881-1943), feminist and pacifist. She was the driving force behind the congresses of the League of Women for the Equal Suffrage Movement and devoted much of her work to the Peace Movement, also internationally. In 1941 she was arrested by the occupiers and in 1943 she died in the Ravensbrück concentration camp.

origins.name: Rosa Overbeekbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after Rosa Overbeek, a fictional character from the work of Theo Thijssen (1879-1943). She is the girlfriend of Kees the boy, who named bridge 123 after her.

origins.name: Roseboom
origins.en: Also known as 'The White rose tree'. Whale hunter, who sailed from Oostzanerwerf around 1726. The ship is named after its owner, shipowner Cornelis Roos (1691-1757).

origins.name: Rosendaalstraat
origins.en: Seventeenth-century inn on the Ringdijk (between Schagerlaan and Pauwenlaan), demolished around 1809.

origins.name: Rosmarijnsteeg
origins.en: Rosemary or Rosemary is an evergreen, fragrant shrub. The alley was originally called Raamsteeg, but is already mentioned under the current name in 1616. This name is probably derived from a facade stone of one of the corner houses, on which a rosemary was depicted. An old note has been found in which there is talk of the decorators, who lived here and who made flowers and other decorations for baptism and wedding parties, which may have been the reason for the facade stone and for the naming of the alley.

origins.name: Rossinistraat
origins.en: Gioacchino Rossini (1792-1868), Italian opera composer.

origins.name: Rostockbrug
origins.en: Rostock is a port city in northeastern Germany. The names in the Houthavens are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Rosy Wertheimstraat
origins.en: Composer (1888-1949). Her compositions show the influence of Strawinsky and Debussy, among others.

origins.name: Rotterdammerbrug
origins.en: To the city of Rotterdam

origins.name: Rousseaustraat
origins.en: Jean Jacques Rousseau (1711-1778), French philosopher of the Enlightenment. One of the pioneers of the French Revolution, writer on education and composer.

origins.name: Rozenburglaan
origins.en: Country house between Kruislaan and Betondorp, built in 1642 and demolished in 1914 for the expansion of the Nieuwe Oosterbegraafplaats. The outside was originally called 'Het Vischkaantje', but was later called 'Rozenburg' after one of the owners David Rutgers van Rozenburg.

origins.name: Rozengracht
origins.en: The flower. The Rozengracht was filled in in 1895.

origins.name: Rozenoordpad
origins.en: Former nursery on the Amstel, located between Zorgvlied and the Kalfje. Also the location of the boat connection between Ouderkerk and Amsterdam.

origins.name: Rozenstraat
origins.en: The flower. The Rozengracht was filled in in 1895.

origins.name: Rozijnenstraat
origins.en: The fruits, dried grapes, from southern Europe, Central Asia, California and Australia.

origins.name: Rubensstraat
origins.en: Petrus Paulus Rubens (1577-1640), South Dutch painter of biblical scenes and historical paintings. Known for his lush female figures. He was the teacher of Anthonie van Dijck.

origins.name: Rudi Bloemgartensingel
origins.en: Jewish resistance fighter (1920-1943), one of the nine people involved in the attack on the Amsterdam Population Register on March 27, 1943. Also involved in the attack on the railway at Sloterdijk and in the establishment of the inciting magazine 'Rattenkruid'.

origins.name: Rudi van Dantzigstraat
origins.en: Rudi van Dantzig was a Dutch choreographer, ballet dancer and writer. He was artistic director of Het Nationale Ballet for twenty years.

origins.name: Rudolf Agricolastraat
origins.en: Philosopher (1443-1485), his real name was Roelof Huisman. From the province of Groningen. Renowned humanist, professor in Heidelberg.

origins.name: Rudolf Dieselstraat
origins.en: German engineer (1858-1913), inventor of the diesel engine named after him.

origins.name: Rudolf Nurejevstraat
origins.en: Rudolf Nureyev was a Russian-Austrian ballet dancer and choreographer.

origins.name: Ruigoord
origins.en: Former island in the IJ, after the reclamation a rise in the Houtrakpolder, on which the village of the same name was established. (Nowadays largely demolished.)

origins.name: Ruijgoordweg
origins.en: Former island in the IJ, after the reclamation a rise in the Houtrakpolder, on which the village of the same name was established. (Nowadays largely demolished.)

origins.name: Ruimzicht
origins.en: Former farm on the Uitweg, demolished for the construction of garden city Osdorp.

origins.name: Ruisbeekhof
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Ruiseveenpad
origins.en: Named after a hamlet near Veenendaal (Utrecht).

origins.name: Ruisrietstraat
origins.en: Reed species, grows along water edges.

origins.name: Rumbeke
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of West Flanders.

origins.name: Rumphiusstraat
origins.en: Georgius Everhardus Rumphius (1627-1702), born in Germany. In 1652 he embarked on a ship of the VOC. From 1662 he began systematically researching the flora and fauna on the Indonesian island of Ambon.

origins.name: Runstraat
origins.en: Fine ground oak bark, used for tanning leather.

origins.name: Rupelmonde
origins.en: One of the first country houses built by the Amsterdam patricians in the seventeenth century in Loenen aan de Vecht. It is still built in the style of an Amsterdam canal house.

origins.name: Rusland
origins.en: The oldest spelling, as it appears in a deed from 1403, is 'Willem Ruusschentuin'. The name was then shortened through ''t Ruyssenlandt', ''t Russeland' and ''t Ruslant' to the now incomprehensible Rusland. The street is so wide because the left part was a small canal (the Raamsloot), which was dug in 1537, but was still filled in in the same century.

origins.name: Rustenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out in 1878 on the Rustenburgerpad, which recalls the former Rustenburg country house from 1620.

origins.name: Rustenburgerstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out in 1878 on the Rustenburgerpad, which recalls the former Rustenburg country house from 1620.

origins.name: Rusthofstraat
origins.en: Former manor house on the Weesperzijde, near the Fahrenheitsingel, originally called Voorzigt, changed to Rusthof in 1807 and demolished around 1820.

origins.name: Rutherfordstraat
origins.en: Ernest Rutherford (1871-1937), English natural and chemist. Gained fame in the field of radioactivity. Received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1908.

origins.name: Ruys de Beerenbrouckstraat
origins.en: Mr. Charles Joseph Marie Ruys de Beerenbrouck (1873-1936), Roman Catholic statesman. Minister of Justice and several times prime minister with the portfolio of Internal Affairs.

origins.name: Ruyschstraat
origins.en: Frederik Ruysch (1638-1731), professor in Amsterdam. Famous anatomist, surgeon and botanist. The street was previously called Derde Boerhaavestraat (council decision, 1882).

origins.name: Ruysdaelkade
origins.en: Seventeenth-century family of painters and engravers, of whom the most famous is Jacob Isaak Ruysdael (1628-1682), landscape painter. He was the teacher of Hobbema. The street already appears under this name in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1888.

origins.name: Ruysdaelstraat
origins.en: Seventeenth-century family of painters and engravers, of whom the most famous is Jacob Isaak Ruysdael (1628-1682), landscape painter. He was the teacher of Hobbema. The street already appears under this name in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1888.

origins.name: S. F. van Ossstraat
origins.en: S.F. van Oss (1868-1949), journalist, founder (1913) and editor-in-chief of the weekly magazine 'De Haagse Post'. Wrote weekly under the pseudonym Mr. Goeree d'Overflacque his humorous-satirical reflections.

origins.name: Saaftingestraat
origins.en: Region in the northeast of Zeelandic Flanders, in 1583 flooded for strategic reasons (the defense of Antwerp) and later not reclaimed.

origins.name: Saenredamstraat
origins.en: Pieter Jan Saenredam (1597-1665), painter. Painted among other things 'Face in the Sint Bavokerk' and 'The old town hall on the Dam'.

origins.name: Saffierstraat
origins.en: Hard blue gemstone.

origins.name: Sagittahof
origins.en: Constellation in the northern sky.

origins.name: Sallandstraat
origins.en: One of the three quarters of Overijssel, located between Gramsbergen and Deventer. The other quarters are Twente and Vollenhove.

origins.name: Saltetstraat
origins.en: Rudolph Hendrik Saltet (1853-1927), hygienist, professor in Amsterdam. Performed important work for public health.

origins.name: Salzmannhof
origins.en: Christiaan G. Salzmann (1744-1811), German pedagogue from the time of the Enlightenment.

origins.name: Sam de Wolffstraat
origins.en: Salomon de Wolff (1878-1960), economist and politician of Jewish descent. From 1909 to 1913 member of the Provincial States of North Holland, from 1930 to 1940 private lecturer at the University of Amsterdam. In 1943 he was arrested and deported to the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, from which he was allowed to go to Palestine (Israel).

origins.name: Sam van Houtenstraat
origins.en: Samuel van Houten (1837-1930), politician, initially liberal, later conservative. Minister of the Interior from 1894 to 1897. As a member of parliament, he submitted a proposal for the Children's Labor Act, the first social law, known as Van Houten's Children's Law (1874).

origins.name: Samosstraat
origins.en: Greek island in the east of the Aegean Sea.

origins.name: Sandenburch
origins.en: Former castle near Veere, built in the thirteenth or fourteenth century by a member of the old knightly family Van Sande. Lived for many years by the lords of Borssele. (Not to be confused with the still existing Sandenburg on the Langbroekerwetering.)

origins.name: Sanderijnstraat
origins.en: One of the main characters from the Abel play 'Lanseloet ende Sanderijn' (from around 1400).

origins.name: Sandhorst
origins.en: Lost medieval castle in Wassenaar. Destroyed in 1818 after repeated renovations.

origins.name: Sandinostraat
origins.en: Augusto Sandino (1895-1934), resistance leader in Nicaragua. Fought from 1926 to 1934 with his guerrilla group in the mountains of Nicaragua against the American troops and the presidents held in their thrall by them. Arrested and murdered by the National Guard.

origins.name: Sandwijk
origins.en: Name of a country house with a large garden on the Oosterweg in the Purmer. Nowadays, there is a farm located there, called Abcoude.

origins.name: Sanne Sanneshof
origins.en: Photographer (1937-1967). His central theme is 'the woman'. He was looking for a new language of images and found it in the combination of photo and film. When he was killed in a car accident at the age of thirty, he was a leading photographer in the Netherlands and was about to break through internationally.

origins.name: Santoriniweg
origins.en: Greek island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Sape Kuiperplantsoen
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1924-1943), born in Arnhem, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Sara Burgerhartstraat
origins.en: Named after the main character from the novella 'History of Miss Sara Burgerhart' from 1872.

origins.name: Sarah Vaughanstraat
origins.en: Sarah Lois Vaughan (1924-1990). Considered one of the most important American jazz singers in history. Known for her wide vocal range, expressive voice and strong vibrato.

origins.name: Sardiniëweg
origins.en: The Italian island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Sarphatikade
origins.en: Samuel Sarphati (1813-1866), Amsterdam doctor and pharmacist with many contacts in banking circles. Did much for the city. He made plans for the expansion of the city around Frederiksplein and outside the Singelgracht, among other things, to which he founded the Nederlandsche Bouwmaatschappij in 1864. Among the associations and buildings that came into being thanks to his efforts, we can mention: the Society for Agriculture (1848), the Association for Popular Industry (1852) with the Palace of Popular Industry built by it (1864), the Trade School, the National Mortgage Bank, the Amstel Hotel (1866).

origins.name: Sarphatipark
origins.en: Samuel Sarphati (1813-1866), Amsterdam doctor and pharmacist with many connections in banking circles, who did much for the city. Among other things he drew up plans to expand the city around the Frederiksplein and beyond the Singelgracht, and founded the Nederlandsche Bouwmaatschappij for this in 1864. Societies and buildings that came about through him include the Maatschappij voor Landbouw (1848), the Vereeniging voor Volksvlijt (1852) with its Paleis voor Volksvlijt (1864), the Handelsschool, the Nationale Hypotheekbank and the Amstel Hotel (1866).

origins.name: Sarphatistraat
origins.en: Samuel Sarphati (1813-1866), Amsterdam doctor and pharmacist with many connections in banking circles, who did much for the city. Among other things he drew up plans to expand the city around the Frederiksplein and beyond the Singelgracht, and founded the Nederlandsche Bouwmaatschappij for this in 1864. Societies and buildings that came about through him include the Maatschappij voor Landbouw (1848), the Vereeniging voor Volksvlijt (1852) with its Paleis voor Volksvlijt (1864), the Handelsschool, the Nationale Hypotheekbank and the Amstel Hotel (1866).

origins.name: Saskia van Uijlenburgkade
origins.en: Wife of Rembrandt van Rijn (1612-1642). She probably knew Rembrandt through her uncle Hendrick, who was an art dealer. In 1634 the couple got married, in 1641 son Titus was born. Buried in the Old Church.

origins.name: Sassenheimstraat
