origins.en: The South Holland village between Lisse and Warmond.

origins.name: Saturnusstraat
origins.en: The planet, one of the largest in our solar system.

origins.name: Sausalitolaan
origins.en: City on the Bay of San Francisco, where the pedestrian promenade is being renovated in the second decade of the twenty-first century.

origins.name: Savelsbos
origins.en: Nature reserve near Gronsveld (South Limburg), total 174 ha: a slope forest with a rare animal and plant world and a prehistoric flint workshop.

origins.name: Saxen-Weimarlaan
origins.en: The German royal family, related by marriage to the Dutch royal family Orange-Nassau.

origins.name: Saxenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: Former country house, later pottery factory, which stood here until 1879. The street has been passed down under this name from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Saxenburgerstraat
origins.en: Former country house, later pottery factory, which stood here until 1879. The street has been passed down under this name from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Scannerstraat
origins.en: Device with which a computer can read and store text and images. As a counterpart to the street names that remind of the former shipbuilding industry in Amsterdam-North, this naming refers to modern information technology.

origins.name: Schaafstraat
origins.en: Woodworking tools.

origins.name: Schaarbeekstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Schaarsbergenstraat
origins.en: Village on the edge of the National Park De Hoge Veluwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Schaepmanstraat
origins.en: Herman Johan A.M. Schaepman (1844-1903), Roman Catholic priest, statesman and poet, professor at the Rijsenburg Seminary. From 1880 to 1903 member of parliament (advocate for expansion of suffrage and social legislation). Editor of the daily newspaper 'De Tijd', later of 'Het Centrum'. As a poet a follower of Bilderdijk and Da Costa.

origins.name: Schagerlaan
origins.en: Robert van Schager, resident of the manor house 't Roode Hart, the only manor house on this lane that survived the flood of 1651.

origins.name: Schaikstraat
origins.en: Village, south of Ravenstein (North Brabant).

origins.name: Schakelstraat
origins.en: The connection, in this case of electrical current.

origins.name: Schalk Burgerstraat
origins.en: Willem Schalk Burger (1852-1918), one of the folk leaders of the young Republic of South Africa. Boer general in the Second Boer War (1899-1902). After Paul Kruger left for Europe, he was acting president of Transvaal.

origins.name: Schalkwijkpad
origins.en: Village in the province of Utrecht, on the Utrecht-Culemborg railway line.

origins.name: Schapensteeg
origins.en: Named after the former landowner Jacob Schaap. The alleyway appears under the name Jacob Schapensteeg from the oldest mention (from 1595). Only in the course of the seventeenth century does the name appear only as Schapensteeg.

origins.name: Scharenburg
origins.en: The port city of Scarborough on the English east coast, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Scharenslijperspad
origins.en: Originally a typical traveling profession. The name is related to the caravan world and refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Scharrebiersluis
origins.en: Scharrebier was traditionally the drink for ordinary workers. This 'thin' beer type was formerly sold on this collection bridge, because there was often a lot of working people present there

origins.name: Scharwouderstraat
origins.en: This 'thin' beer type was formerly sold on this pick-up bridge, because there was often a lot of working people present there.

origins.name: Scheepmakerskade
origins.en: An unofficial name for this bridge is Rapenburgerschutsluis. The origin of the name Rapenburg is shrouded in mystery.

origins.name: Scheepsbouwkade
origins.en: Reference to the NSM and later NDSM shipyard on the north side of the IJ, where ships were built between 1922 and 1978. Also see: NDSM Square.

origins.name: Scheepsbouwweg
origins.en: The name recalls the shipyard, and in particular the new construction shipyard, where many ships were built until the 1970s of this century.

origins.name: Scheepstimmermanstraat
origins.en: Occupational name for shipbuilding.

origins.name: Scheldeplein
origins.en: River originating in France, which flows into our country past Antwerp and then discharges into the sea via the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Scheldestraat
origins.en: River originating in France, which flows into our country past Antwerp and then discharges into the sea via the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Schellingwouderdijk
origins.en: Village. The dike is part of the Waterland sea dike.

origins.name: Schelluinenstraat
origins.en: The village northwest of Gorinchem (South Holland).

origins.name: Schelvisch Hoofd
origins.en: Named after the place where the Noordhollandse tram station was located. Also the end point of the North-South Holland coffee shop-Central Station ferry.

origins.name: Schepenbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Meerssen (Limburg).

origins.name: Schepenlaan
origins.en: The streets in this district are named after ship types and ship parts.

origins.name: Schermerstraat
origins.en: Between 1631 and 1635 more were drained in North Holland.

origins.name: Scherpenzeelstraat
origins.en: Village in the Gelderse Valley (Gelderland).

origins.name: Schielandplein
origins.en: Place in South Holland

origins.name: Schiemanstraat
origins.en: Occupational name at sea: the petty officer on board responsible for supervising the rigging for the mast.

origins.name: Schiermonnikoogstraat
origins.en: Wadden island (Friesland).

origins.name: Schierstins
origins.en: Fourteenth-century defensible tower-shaped building, located in Veenwouden (Friesland) and restored in 1962. The building was already in the possession of the gray or semi-monks of the abbey of Klaarkamp before 1439.

origins.name: Schillingdijk
origins.en: The currency of Austria.

origins.name: Schimmelstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Jan Schimmel (1825-1906), bank director, known as a novelist and playwright. He was also editor of 'De Gids'. These streets came into Amsterdam in 1896 with the names Van Speyckstraat and Van Speyckdwarsstraat established by Nieuwer-Amstel, but were renamed in 1922, after another Van Speyckstraat came within the municipal boundary due to the annexation of Sloten.

origins.name: Schinkelhavenkade
origins.en: The name recalls the old amusement park Schinkelhaven. The street was part of the Schinkelkade before 1922.

origins.name: Schinkelhavenstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the old amusement park Schinkelhaven. The street was part of the Schinkelkade before 1922.

origins.name: Schinkelkade
origins.en: A swing bridge is a short connecting piece between two canals. In this case Nieuwe Meer and Overtoom. It is assumed that the connecting piece owes its name to its shape: 'swing bridge' is synonymous with 'shin', the lower leg between the foot and the knee. The quay was previously called Nieuwer-Amstel Visserkade. The streets were respectively named Visserstraat, Alexanderstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1882) and Willemsparkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1883) by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, but were changed due to confusion with names already existing in Amsterdam in 1896.

origins.name: Schipbeekstraat
origins.en: Built in the fifteenth century and extended in later centuries, shipping canal on the border of Gelderland and Overijssel. Flows into the IJssel near Deventer.

origins.name: Schipluidenlaan
origins.en: Village in the Westland, south of Delft.

origins.name: Schippersgracht
origins.en: In this neighborhood, on the harbor side, the shipowners and sailors made up the majority of the population, which is why the canal and street got this name.

origins.name: Schippersstraat
origins.en: In this neighborhood, on the harbor side, the shipowners and sailors made up the majority of the population, which is why the canal and street got this name

origins.name: Schoenerstraat
origins.en: Small merchant ship with sharp bow and with two or more masts.

origins.name: Schoffelstraat
origins.en: Named after the hoe, a gardening tool.

origins.name: Schokkerjachtdijk
origins.en: Ship, a fishing vessel related to the hull. The name probably comes from the island of Schokland. Schokkers were known for their enormous seaworthiness.

origins.name: Schokkerspad
origins.en: Small fishing boat, originally from the Netherlands.

origins.name: Schoklandstraat
origins.en: Former island in the Zuiderzee, now incorporated into the Noordoostpolder.

origins.name: Schollenbrugpad
origins.en: To the extension that used to stand here, and which took its name from the old Schollenbrug in the Weesperzijde, which connected the Watergraafsmeer to the city. That bridge was previously called Schulpbrug, after the seventeenth-century inn the Schulp. This was on the other side of the bridge, so in the Watergraafsmeer (with a shell or shell in the facade).

origins.name: Schollenbrugstraat
origins.en: To the extension that used to stand here, and which took its name from the old Schollenbrug in the Weesperzijde, which connected the Watergraafsmeer to the city. That bridge was previously called Schulpbrug, after the seventeenth-century inn the Schulp. This was on the other side of the bridge, so in the Watergraafsmeer (with a shell or shell in the facade).

origins.name: Schonerwoerdstraat
origins.en: Village in the so-called Five Brothers Countries (South Holland).

origins.name: Schoolmeesterstraat
origins.en: Named after the pseudonym 'De Schoolmeester' of the Dutch poet Gerrit van de Linde (1808-1858).

origins.name: Schoolstraat
origins.en: To the old municipal school of Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Schooltuinpad
origins.en: Refers to the nearby school garden complex.

origins.name: Schoonboomstraat
origins.en: Former church village on Zuid-Beveland, drowned by a storm surge in 1532.

origins.name: Schoonhovendreef
origins.en: City on the Lek, on the border of Utrecht and South Holland.

origins.name: Schoorlstraat
origins.en: Village at the foot of the dunes, north of Alkmaar.

origins.name: Schopenhauerhof
origins.en: Arthur Schopenhauer (1778-1860), German philosopher. Denied the existence of a causal free will.

origins.name: Schorpioenstraat
origins.en: Constellation, sign of the Zodiac.

origins.name: Schotse Hooglanden
origins.en: The mountain, located in Scotland.

origins.name: Schotse Huizenpad
origins.en: The mountain, located in Scotland.

origins.name: Schoutensteeg
origins.en: Named after a former resident, Jan Arentsz Schouten. In the fifteenth century, the alley was therefore fully called Jan Arentszn Schoutensteeg. He was the alderman of Amsterdam from 1426 to 1430. Before that time, the name Willem Noirtsteeg was also used.

origins.name: Schouwstraat
origins.en: ''t Schouw' is a hamlet on the Noordhollandsch Kanaal, on the northern municipal border of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Schovenstraat
origins.en: Combined kernel stalks.

origins.name: Schubertstraat
origins.en: Franz Schubert (1797-1828), Austrian composer. Wrote symphonies, chamber music and songs, including: 'Die Forelle', 'Erlkönig' and the cycle 'Die Winterreise'.

origins.name: Schuitenhuisstraat
origins.en: In general, a shooting house is a boat shelter (now boat house). The name appears on a historical map from 1659 (by Stevijn and Van Broeckhuysen) in the vicinity of the inn 'De drie Baarsjes'.

origins.name: Schurenbergweg
origins.en: A hill near Hoensbroek (Limburg).

origins.name: Schutterweg
origins.en: The zodiac sign Sagittarius or Sagittarius in the Zodiac.

origins.name: Schweigmannstraat
origins.en: Antonius Petrus Paulus Schweigmann (1893-1945), resistance fighter, born in Leeuwarden, killed in Sandbostel (Germany).

origins.name: Science Park
origins.en: Campus for international knowledge institutes in the field of ICT, exact sciences and scientific research.

origins.name: Sean MacBridestraat
origins.en: Irish politician (1904-1988). After World War II, he was Minister of Foreign Affairs and actively involved in the creation of the Geneva Conventions and the European Convention for Human Rights. In 1961, he was one of the founders of Amnesty International. He received both the Soviet Peace Prize and the Nobel Peace Prize.

origins.name: Seifertplein
origins.en: Jaroslav Seifert (1901-1986), Czech writer. After the Russian invasion, his strongly anti-fascist and patriotic work could only be distributed underground. In 1984 he received the Nobel Prize for Literature.

origins.name: Seineweg
origins.en: River in France.

origins.name: Seinwachterstraat
origins.en: Signalman, who operates the signals in a signal box along the railway track.

origins.name: Seizoenenhof
origins.en: The name fits the adjacent district with names of the four seasons.

origins.name: Semarangstraat
origins.en: City on the island of Java (Indonesia).

origins.name: Senecastraat
origins.en: Roman philosopher and poet (4 BC-65 AD). Teacher of Nero, who later forced him to commit suicide.

origins.name: Senefelderstraat
origins.en: Aloys Senefelder (1771-1834), Austrian typographer. Inventor of lithography.

origins.name: Seranggracht
origins.en: River on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Serge Lifarsteeg
origins.en: Serge Lifar was a Russian-French dancer, choreographer, ballet director and author.

origins.name: Servaes Noutsstraat
origins.en: Michiel Servaes Nouts (1630-1693), the first bellringer of the Town Hall on the Dam.

origins.name: Servetsteeg
origins.en: This name already occurs here in the seventeenth century, but the original name Revet- or Ravetsteeg is also used until the eighteenth century. A Revet, Ravet or Rabat is a billiards hall. This billiards hall was located at the corner of the alley and the city wall. It can therefore be assumed that Servet is a corruption of Revet.

origins.name: Sextantweg
origins.en: The navigation tool, an angle measuring instrument for determining position at sea using the stars.

origins.name: Shackletonstraat
origins.en: Sir Ernest Henry Shackleton (1874-1922), English South Pole researcher. Reached the magnetic South Pole in 1909.

origins.name: Sibogastraat
origins.en: Siboga or Sibolga is a city on the west coast of Sumatra (Indonesia).

origins.name: Sibrandus Stratinghstraat
origins.en: Inventor and chemist (1785-1841). Was a professor in Groningen, where he developed and tested motorized vehicles. In 1834, he made possible, as the first person in the Netherlands, a test drive with a steam carriage. Probably also built the first electromagnetic vehicle in the world.

origins.name: Siciliëweg
origins.en: Italian island in the Mediterranean Sea.

origins.name: Siebren van der Baanhof
origins.en: Resistance hero (1894-1944). Keeper of the Reformed Church on the Keizersgracht, where he hid weapons and other things of the illegality. Upon discovery, by the occupiers in 1944, shot dead on the sidewalk in front of the building together with the pastor Ferwerda. Van der Baan was also active in the distribution of the illegal newspaper 'Trouw'.

origins.name: Sieg Vaz Diasstraat
origins.en: Journalist (1904-1943) and resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed on the Leusderheide.

origins.name: Sierenborch
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the French port city of Cherbourg, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Sierplein
origins.en: Before houses were built on this square and the square was given an official name, the square was popularly called Sierplein due to the decorative paving.

origins.name: Sieverdinkpad
origins.en: Name of an old farm near Winterswijk.

origins.name: Sijlhoff
origins.en: Former castle in Leiderdorp, first built around 1292, destroyed in 1420, rebuilt during the Spanish period and finally demolished in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Sijpestein
origins.en: Castle was already mentioned in 1288, which was destroyed and rebuilt several times. In 1911 the old foundations were exposed, after which the castle was rebuilt in its original style. It is located under Loosdrecht.

origins.name: Sijsjesbergweg
origins.en: Hill near Huizen (North Holland), north of the Table Mountain.

origins.name: Sijsjesstraat
origins.en: Songbird.

origins.name: Sikkelstraat
origins.en: Agricultural tools for cutting corn stalks.

origins.name: Silenestraat
origins.en: Plant, belonging to the daisy family, grows in dunes and along berms.

origins.name: Silodam
origins.en: The embankment in the IJ. Since the end of the nineteenth century, there has been a large grain silo here, which was later expanded with a second. Both silos are out of use and are being converted into houses.

origins.name: Silvoldestraat
origins.en: The Gelderland village on the Oude IJssel.

origins.name: Silvretta
origins.en: Mountain peak in Switzerland, 3411 meters high.

origins.name: Simon Carmiggeltstraat
origins.en: Simon Johannes Carmiggelt (1913-1987), writer and journalist, best known for his newspaper columns ('Kronkels'), which appeared under the pseudonym Kronkel in 'Het Parool'. In 1974 Carmiggelt received the P.C. Hooft Prize.

origins.name: Simon Stevinstraat
origins.en: Mathematician and engineer (1548-1620), head of Water Works and teacher of Prince Maurice. Inventor of the ten-part fractions and of the sailing cart. During the construction, the street was named Kerklaan by the Watergraafsmeer municipality (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1901).

origins.name: Simon van Gijnpad
origins.en: The Museum Mr. Simon van Gijn in Dordrecht. In 1925, the former 1729 residence of the banker and collector Simon van Gijn (1836-1922) was converted into a museum. In addition to the authentic interiors, the museum is known for its collection of national history prints and the collection of crafts and old toys.

origins.name: Simon van Woerdenstraat
origins.en: Simon van Woerden (1902-1998) designed the Bethel Church around 1958.

origins.name: Simone de Beauvoirstraat
origins.en: French writer (1908-1986), taught philosophy in Marseille, Rouen and Paris from 1931 to 1943. Her literary work is critical, sharp and imbued with her existentialist way of life.

origins.name: Simonshavenstraat
origins.en: Village on the South Holland island of Putten.

origins.name: Simonskerkestraat
origins.en: The village that drowned in 1484 on Schouwen-Duiveland (Zeeland).

origins.name: Simsonstraat
origins.en: The hero of the Israelites in the Old Testament (symbol of strength). Was stripped of his hair by his beloved Delilah, and therefore of his strength.

origins.name: Sinaasappelstraat
origins.en: Named after the orange, a citrus fruit.

origins.name: Sinderenstraat
origins.en: Neighborhood near Varsseveld (Gelderland).

origins.name: Singel
origins.en: A singel is a waterway or a road along the outer edge of the city. In Amsterdam, the Singel (the Amsterdammer speaks of the Singel) formed the city boundary in the second half of the fifteenth century, within which the walls with gates were built. At that time, that canal was called 't Singel or the Stedegracht (now Singel, Kloveniersburgwal and Geldersekade). The current Singel has retained the old name. However, in the seventeenth century, the city administration introduced the name Koningsgracht for this purpose, but that name could not be maintained (see also Koningsplein).

origins.name: Singerstraat
origins.en: The Singer Museum in Laren. The American painter W.H. Singer Jr. (1868-1943) came to Laren around 1900 and had a villa built in 1911. In 1956, a new wing of the building was converted into a museum. The basis of the collection is the collection of the Singer couple: nineteenth and twentieth-century works by mainly Dutch and French artists.

origins.name: Sinjeur Semeynsstraat
origins.en: To the book 'Sinjeur Semeyns' by H.J. mould

origins.name: Sint Agnietenstraat
origins.en: Here was formerly the Sint Augustinian Monastery, founded in 1397, destroyed in the great city fire in 1452 and rebuilt again. The still existing monastery church, the Sint Augustinian Chapel, dates from 1470 and housed the Athenaeum from 1632 to 1862.

origins.name: Sint Annendwarsstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a religious figurine, depicting Sint Anna.

origins.name: Sint Annenstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a religious figurine, depicting Sint Anna.

origins.name: Sint Antoniesbreestraat
origins.en: which in turn derives its name from the Sint Antoniesgasthuis or Leprosy House.

origins.name: Sint Antoniesluis
origins.en: Named after the Sint Antoniesdijk, the sea wall located outside the city until the seventeenth century, which in turn took its name from the Sint Antoniesgasthuis or Leprosy House. The Sint Antoniesluis was part of the Zwanenburgwal before 1976.

origins.name: Sint Jacobsdwarsstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a holy image, depicting the apostle James, who sat on the facade at one of the street corners. The Sint Jacob Chapel will not have been the namesake, as this chapel was located further north on the Nieuwendijk.

origins.name: Sint Jacobsstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a holy image, depicting the apostle James, who sat on the facade at one of the street corners. The Sint Jacob Chapel will not have been the namesake, as this chapel was located further north on the Nieuwendijk.

origins.name: Sint Jansstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a religious statue, depicting the apostle John, who sat on the facade at one of the street corners.

origins.name: Sint Jorisstraat
origins.en: To the Sint Joris guesthouse, which was located here, founded in the second half of the fourteenth century and demolished at the end of the sixteenth century for the expansion of the city.

origins.name: Sint Luciënsteeg
origins.en: The former Sint Lucian monastery that was moved to the complex of the Burgerweeshuis after 1578 (now Amsterdam Museum of History).

origins.name: Sint Nicolaasstraat
origins.en: Probably named after a small religious statue, which must have stood on the corner of the street on the facade.

origins.name: Sint Olofspoort
origins.en: The Sint Olofspoort was one of the oldest city gates and stood here from before 1380 to 1618. The gate got its name from the adjacent Sint Olofkapel, which still exists and is one of the oldest buildings preserved in Amsterdam. Foundation remains have been found from the gate. Sint Olofssteeg was called Oudezijds Wijde Kapelsteeg until 1914.

origins.name: Sint Olofssteeg
origins.en: The Sint Olofspoort was one of the oldest city gates and stood here from before 1380 to 1618. The gate got its name from the adjacent Sint Olof Chapel, which still exists and is one of the oldest buildings preserved in Amsterdam. Foundation remains have been found from the gate. The Sint Olofssteeg was called Oudezijds Wijde Kapelsteeg until 1914.

origins.name: Sint Pieterspoortsteeg
origins.en: The gate is a remnant of the Sint Pietersgasthuis, which already stood here in the second half of the fourteenth century. In 1578 the hospital was transferred to the Binnengasthuis and the buildings, with the exception of the gate, were demolished and rebuilt as a bank.

origins.name: Sint Willibrordusdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the church of that name, dedicated to Sint Willibrordus, the Anglo-Saxon preacher and archbishop from the seventh century, who completely Christianized the Dutch area. The church was demolished in 1970 due to structural failure. The street and the cross street were taken over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel in 1896 under the names Kerkstraat, Hoedemakerskade (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890 and 28-8-1891) and Eerste Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890).

origins.name: Sint Willibrordusstraat
origins.en: Named after the church of that name, dedicated to Sint Willibrordus, the Anglo-Saxon preacher and archbishop from the seventh century, who completely Christianized the Dutch area. The church was demolished in 1970 due to structural failure. The street and the cross street were taken over from the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel in 1896 under the names Kerkstraat, Hoedemakerskade (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890 and 28-8-1891) and Eerste Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890).

origins.name: Sint-Hubertpad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Luxembourg.

origins.name: Sint-Truidenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Siriusstraat
origins.en: One of the largest and brightest stars in the constellation The Great Dog.

origins.name: Sixhavenweg
origins.en: Baron Willem Six (1859-1919), from 1898 to 1919 chairman of the Royal Sailing and Rowing Association, a great promoter of the construction of the marina in Amsterdam North. Two months before the completion of the harbor, he died, after which the harbor was named after him.

origins.name: Sjai Agnonstraat
origins.en: Sjmoeël Joseef Agnon (1887-1970) was the first writer in Hebrew to win the Nobel Prize for Literature. He is known by the acronym Sjai as his first name.

origins.name: Skûtsjespad
origins.en: Traditional type of jolle. Sailing vessel for sea and river navigation with round bow, flat bottom and side sails.

origins.name: Slaakstraat
origins.en: Water between St. Philipsland and North Brabant, dammed in 1884.

origins.name: Slangenburg
origins.en: Fifteenth-century castle under Doetinchem, renovated in the seventeenth century under General Van Baer van Slangenburg.

origins.name: Slatuinenweg
origins.en: This is the remainder of the former Slatuinenpad, which ran from the Baarsjesweg to the Haarlemmerweg until 1927 and along willow groves (willow grove gardens). It was a popular walking path of the Amsterdamers.

origins.name: Slauerhoffstraat
origins.en: Jan Jacob Slauerhoff (1898-1936), doctor and poet. As a ship's doctor, he traveled around the world. His poetry therefore reveals a continuous restlessness.

origins.name: Sleewijkstraat
origins.en: The village of Sleeuwijk on the Merwede opposite Gorinchem (North Brabant).

origins.name: Slego
origins.en: The name is the Old Dutch rendering of the port town of Sligo, located on the northwest coast of Ireland.

origins.name: Sleutelbloemstraat
origins.en: Also known as primula. Plant that occurs in meadows and on old estates.

origins.name: Sleutelbrug
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the seventeenth-century brewery 'De Sleutel' that belonged to Gerrit Bicker and which was located on the site of the current Binnengasthuisterrein.

origins.name: Slibveldenweg
origins.en: The road ends just after the Wijsentkade in a rectangular piece of land where the 'Slibvel- den' were built in the late 1950s. In popular parlance, the path is known as the "Slibveldenweg"

origins.name: Slichtenhorststraat
origins.en: Neighbourhood and estate under Nijkerk (Gelderland).

origins.name: Sliedrechtstraat
origins.en: Location on the Beneden-Merwede, formerly known for its dredging companies and shipyards.

origins.name: Slijkstraat
origins.en: Named after the soil conditions in the sixteenth century. In Amsterdam-Centrum, several street names indicate the former swampy ground (see Nes-Niezel). Only the main streets were raised at the time (Zandstraat-Dijkstraat).

origins.name: Slijperweg
origins.en: Metalworker, who smooths the surface of metal objects.

origins.name: Slikkerveerstraat
origins.en: Village on IJsselmonde, at the confluence of Lek and Noord.

origins.name: Slimmeweg
origins.en: This is the former name of the Osdorperweg, as found on old maps of this area.

origins.name: Slingerbeekstraat
origins.en: River in the Gelderse Achterhoek. Flows into the Oude IJssel near Doetinchem.

origins.name: Slochterweg
origins.en: The original name of the section located here of the North Holland Canal, which connected the Buiksloter Meer with the Broeker Meer. Before this naming, the road formed parts of the Canal Dyke (until 1966 Landsmeer) and the Leeuwarderweg.

origins.name: Sloestraat
origins.en: Former tidal current between Walcheren and Zuid-Beveland, now completely reclaimed.

origins.name: Slootdorpstraat
origins.en: The village in the Wieringermeerpolder.

origins.name: Slootstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out in 1660 on a filled in ditch near the Former City Timberyard.

origins.name: Sloterdijkerbrug
origins.en: The old dike village, of which only the church and a small part remain today. It belonged to the municipality of Sloten, which was annexed to Amsterdam in 1921. The village was originally called Sloterdam and had a harbor and a lock in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Sloterdijkerweg
origins.en: The old dike village, of which only the church and a small part remain today. It belonged to the municipality of Sloten, which was annexed to Amsterdam in 1921. The village was originally called Sloterdam and had a harbor and a lock in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Sloterdijkstraat
origins.en: Opinions differ on the naming of this street. According to some, a house called Sloterdijk at the corner of the street is the namesake, others look for a direct connection with the village of Sloterdijk on which one had the view through the street.

origins.name: Sloterkade
origins.en: To the village of Sloten, which was the main village of the municipality of Sloten until 1-1-1921, to which also the village of Sloterdijk and the hamlet of Osdorp belonged. The municipality extended from the Haarlemmermeer to the North Sea Canal and from the Schinkel to Halfweg.

origins.name: Slotermeerlaan
origins.en: The name is derived from Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk, which was dredged back into the water after repeated dryings for the purpose of sand mining. This water is the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Sloterweg
origins.en: To the village of Sloten, which until 1-1-1921 was the main village of the municipality of Sloten, to which also the village of Sloterdijk and the hamlet of Osdorp belonged. The municipality extended from the Haarlemmermeer to the North Sea Canal and from the Schinkel to Halfweg. The Sloterweg originally ran to (or began at) the Schinkel. Due to the construction of the ring road, a part has disappeared and deteriorated (see also Rijnsburgstraat).

origins.name: Slufter
origins.en: Nature monument on the island of Texel. In the Slufter are the only ponds, which are still in open connection with the sea. Breeding ground for seabirds and storks.

origins.name: Sluispad
origins.en: The path runs along the sluice located here in the Gaasp.

origins.name: Sluisstraat
origins.en: Artificial dam. By opening and closing doors, the connection between two waters is regulated.

origins.name: Smaksteeg
origins.en: The name already appears in the sixteenth century and originates from a facade stone of a corner house. On it stood a taste, a kind of ship.

origins.name: Smalschipstraat
origins.en: Ship, flat-bottomed of Frisian origin with swords and a gaff-rigged mast. Very suitable for shallow waters. The narrow ship was used to load goods and unload larger ships.

origins.name: Smaragdplein
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the various workshops were used for the naming, in this case the forge of the shipyard.

origins.name: Smaragdstraat
origins.en: Gemstone with grass green color.

origins.name: Smederij
origins.en: These and other streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (ADM). As a reminder of that former purpose, the names of the various workshops were used for the naming, in this case the forge of the shipyard.

origins.name: Smederij Meisterbrug
origins.en: Family business in the Bellamy neighborhood, founded in 1909.

origins.name: Smitstraat
origins.en: Nicolaas Jacobus Smit, general in the First Boer War of Independence (1880-1881) of the Transvaal Boers, where he defeated the English at Ingogo. In 1883 negotiator for the Boers in London.

origins.name: Sneeuwbalstraat
origins.en: Named after the guelder rose (snowball bush), a shrub.

origins.name: Sneeuwbalweg
origins.en: Named after the guelder rose (snowball bush), a shrub.

origins.name: Snellerwaardgracht
origins.en: Village on the Hollandse IJssel (Utrecht). The original spelling is Snelrewaard.

origins.name: Snelleveldplein
origins.en: Neighborhood on the Waal near Waardenburg (Gelderland).

origins.name: Snelleveldstraat
origins.en: Neighborhood on the Waal near Waardenburg (Gelderland).

origins.name: Snelliusstraat
origins.en: Willebrord Snellius (1580-1626), mathematician and physicist. Leiden professor, founded the first European observatory.

origins.name: Snijdersbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Geulle (Limburg).

origins.name: Snodenhoekpark
origins.en: Neighbourhood under EIst in the Betuwe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Snoekjesbrug
origins.en: After a resident from the sixteenth century, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike depicted on the facade of his house. Originally, the name was therefore Snoeksgracht/steeg.

origins.name: Snoekjesgracht
origins.en: After a resident from the sixteenth century, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike depicted on the facade of his house. Originally, the name was therefore Snoeksgracht/steeg.

origins.name: Snoekjessteeg
origins.en: After a resident from the sixteenth century, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike depicted on the facade of his house. Originally, the name was therefore Snoeksgracht/steeg.

origins.name: Snorrenhoefstraat
origins.en: Neighborhood near Leusden (Utrecht).

origins.name: Socratesstraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher (469-399 BC), teacher of Plato. Was condemned as a freethinker to drink the cup of poison.

origins.name: Soembawastraat
origins.en: One of the Lesser Sunda Islands (Indonesia).

origins.name: Soendastraat
origins.en: Island group to which the main islands of Indonesia belong, divided into the Greater and Lesser Sundas. The Greater include Java, Sumatra, Kalimantan (Borneo) and Sulawesi (Celebes). The Lesser include Bali and the other series of islands east of Java. The Sundas are located in West Java.

origins.name: Soerabajastraat
origins.en: Port city on East Java (Indonesia).

origins.name: Soestdijkstraat
origins.en: Village, falls under the municipality of Soest. The royal palace Soestdijk is located in the municipality of Baarn.

origins.name: Soesterberghof
origins.en: Village, falls under the municipality of Soest. Especially known for the nearby military airfield.

origins.name: Soetendaal
origins.en: Former country house near Maarssen on the Vecht.

origins.name: Soewardistraat
origins.en: Soewardi Soerjaningrat (Jakarta 1889 - Jakarta 1959), later called himself Ki Hadjar Dewantoro. He was closely involved in the action of the multiracial Indian Party that sought an independent India. For this reason, he was exiled to the Netherlands (1913-1919). After his return, he was mainly engaged in educational work. In the first Indonesian cabinet, he was minister of education and culture (1945).

origins.name: Softwareweg
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Solebaystraat
origins.en: Location on the east coast of England. In the Battle of Solebay (1672), the Dutch-Zeeuw fleet under Admiral De Ruyter successfully fought against the English.

origins.name: Solitudobrug
origins.en: The name is based on former country estates along the Amstel and Watergraafsmeer.

origins.name: Solitudolaan
origins.en: Former country house near the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, which was located approximately at this location. It was already mentioned in 1730, and still existed in 1798.

origins.name: Solitudopad
origins.en: Former country house near the Amstel and the Weespertrekvaart, which was located approximately at this location. It was already mentioned in 1730, and still existed in 1798.

origins.name: Solostraat
origins.en: The largest river on the island of Java (Indonesia).

origins.name: Somerlustpad
origins.en: Former country house on Kruislaan, where the Nieuwe Ooster Cemetery is now located.

origins.name: Sommelsdijkstraat
origins.en: Village on the island of Overflakkee (South Holland).

origins.name: Sonderbuur
origins.en: Name of a demolished farm on the Haarlemmerweg near Halfweg.

origins.name: Sonneveld
origins.en: Medieval house of the Van Zonneveld family in Valkenburg (Limburg), demolished in 1789.

origins.name: Sontvaarderstraat
origins.en: A southerner is an inland ship that sails between the Netherlands and the Swedish south coast.

origins.name: Sophialaan
origins.en: Queen Sophia Frederika Mathilda of Württemberg (1817-1877), the first wife of King William III.

origins.name: Sophie Redmondplein
origins.en: Jeanne Sophie Everdine Redmond (1907-1955), first female doctor in Suriname. She fought for the position of the woman and the preservation of the heritage of Surinamese culture. Her nickname was Datra Foe potisma, doctor for the poor. She wrote plays, which were compiled in 1972.

origins.name: Spaanse Brabanderstraat
origins.en: Based on the novel by Gerbrand Adriaensz. Bredero,'Spaanschen Brabander' from 1617.

origins.name: Spaarndammerdijk
origins.en: The place Spaarndam, northeast of Haarlem. The name is derived from the dam in the Spaarne.

origins.name: Spaarndammerplantsoen
origins.en: The place Spaarndam, northeast of Haarlem. The name is derived from the dam in the Spaarne.

origins.name: Spaarndammerstraat
origins.en: The place Spaarndam, northeast of Haarlem. The name is derived from the dam in the Spaarne.

origins.name: Spaarndammertunnel
origins.en: The place Spaarndam, northeast of Haarlem. The name is derived from the dam in the Spaarne.

origins.name: Spaarnwouderdijk
origins.en: Named after the village of Spaarnwoude. The old Spaarnwouderdijk that came into Amsterdam in 1921 by annexation of the municipality of Sloten, has practically disappeared completely, so that name has been discontinued. At the same time, a newly built bicycle path has taken on the old name Spaarnwouderdijk.

origins.name: Spadinalaan
origins.en: Area in South Toronto on Lake Ontario. There has been a redevelopment process underway here since the beginning of the twenty-first century.

origins.name: Spahof
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Liège.

origins.name: Spakenburgstraat
origins.en: Village on the Eem Lake (Utrecht).

origins.name: Spaklerweg
origins.en: The Spakler family, founders and owners of the sugar factory (a family business). Coenraad Hendrik Spakler (born around 1732 in Westphalia) owned a sugar refinery on the Rozengracht.

origins.name: Spanderswoudstraat
origins.en: Nature monument. It is an old 's-Gravelandse country house with forest, wood walls and meadows.

origins.name: Spangenhof
origins.en: The former Spangen castle, between Schiedam and Overschie. Today, Spangen is a district of Rotterdam.

origins.name: Spankerenkade
origins.en: Village near Dieren (Gelderland).

origins.name: Sparrenweg
origins.en: Coniferous tree.

origins.name: Spechtstraat
origins.en: Name of a bird family.

origins.name: Speelmanstraat
origins.en: Willem Pieter Speelman (1919-1945), resistance fighter, born in Vlagtwedde, executed by firing squad in Halfweg.

origins.name: Speerdistelstraat
origins.en: Named after the spear thistle, a thistle.

origins.name: Speerstraat
origins.en: Attribute for throwing the spear, already practiced by the ancient Greeks.

origins.name: Spelderholt
origins.en: Nature monument northeast of Hoenderlo (Gelderland).

origins.name: Spengenpad
origins.en: Neighborhood near Kockengen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Sperwerlaan
origins.en: Predatory bird.

origins.name: Speuldestraat
origins.en: Neighborhood near Ermelo (Gelderland).

origins.name: Spicastraat
origins.en: Star in the zodiac sign Virgo.

origins.name: Spiegelgracht
origins.en: To a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers, who had soap factories. In 1564 Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' lived in the corner building of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel and in 1608 Pieter Lourens Spiegel. The intended house is still called Hertspiegel in 1738. The construction of the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat begins in 1665. Again, it is likely that a resident of the Spiegel family is the namesake.

origins.name: Spijkerkade
origins.en: The - usually metal - tool for wood connections.

origins.name: Spijtellaantje
origins.en: L.J. Spijdel (born 1844), who established a shipyard here in 1885. The lane came to be located due to the annexation of Sloten in Amsterdam and was so named in popular parlance. In 1949, the name was officially established.

origins.name: Spinaker
origins.en: A spinnaker is meant: a sail, which is deployed when a ship sails directly into the wind.

origins.name: Spinakerhof
origins.en: A spinnaker is meant: a sail, which is deployed when a ship sails directly into the wind.

origins.name: Spinhuissteeg
origins.en: To the nearby Spinhuis, a women's prison founded in 1596. From 1833 to 1941, the main police headquarters was located in this building.

origins.name: Spinozahof
origins.en: Benedictus Spinoza (Baruch d'Espinoza) (1632-1677), Jewish philosopher, who after being expelled from the Jewish community, lived by grinding eyeglass lenses. One of the leading thinkers of the seventeenth century, best known for his 'Ethics'. From 1874 to 1966, the Spinoza Clinic for Eye Patients stood on this street. A part of the street was previously called Andrieszkade, after the oldest known mayor of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Spinozastraat
origins.en: Benedictus Spinoza (Baruch d'Espinoza) (1632-1677), Jewish philosopher, who after being expelled from the Jewish community, lived by grinding eyeglass lenses. One of the leading thinkers of the seventeenth century, best known for his 'Ethics'. From 1874 to 1966, the Spinoza Clinic for Eye Patients stood on this street. A part of the street was previously called Andrieszkade, after the oldest known mayor of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Spitsbergenstraat
origins.en: Island group in the North Sea, mostly covered by a permanent ice cap. It now belongs to Norway. Spitsbergen was discovered in 1596 by Willem Barentsz, who had the settlement of Smeerenburg built there for whaling purposes.

origins.name: Spitskopstraat
origins.en: Mountain in South Africa where the Boers defeated the English in the First Boer War (1880-1881).

origins.name: Spooksteeg
origins.en: The origin of the name is unknown. Before 1800, the name is not mentioned on maps or in registers.

origins.name: Sporadenlaan
origins.en: Greek island group.

origins.name: Sportpark de Weeren
origins.en: A weir is an elongated plot of land between two boundary ditches. The ditch between two posts is also called a weir ditch. By council decision in 1971, part of the road was added to Buikslotermeerplein.

origins.name: Sportpark Kadoelen
origins.en: Name for the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was annexed to Amsterdam on August 1, 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) already appears in 1375. In 1429, there is talk of the lordship of Landsmeer and the lordship of Quadolen, which then had one lord together. Old maps indicate Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterlandse zeedijk (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1-8-1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed due to confusion with the Zuideinde (former Oostzaan).

origins.name: Sportpark Oostzanerwerf
origins.en: To the Oostzanerwerf district, where the sports park is located. The district derives its name from the municipality of Oostzaan, to which this area belonged until 1-8-1966.

origins.name: Sportpark Sloten
origins.en: To the village of Sloten, which until 1-1-1921 was the main village of the municipality of Sloten, to which also the village of Sloterdijk and the hamlet of Osdorp belonged. The municipality extended from the Haarlemmermeer to the North Sea Canal and from the Schinkel to Halfweg. The Sloterweg originally ran to (or began at) the Schinkel. Due to the construction of the ring road, a part has disappeared and deteriorated (see also Rijnsburgstraat).

origins.name: Sportpark Spieringhorn
origins.en: The former inland polder, which already existed before the poldering of the IJ.

origins.name: Sportparklaan
origins.en: Refers to the former sports park

origins.name: Sportstraat
origins.en: The street is located in the middle of streets whose names are derived from the Greek plays and from figures from antiquity who are generally known for their power.

origins.name: Spreeuwenpark
origins.en: Named after the starling, a bird.

origins.name: Spui
origins.en: Until the end of the fourteenth century, the water that formed the southern border of the city. This water was equipped with a lock when the Singel was dug, hence the name Spui. The Spui was filled in in 1882.

origins.name: Spuistraat
origins.en: Named after the Spui, where the street leads out. Before the filling in in 1867, this was the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal. This canal was dug around 1385, along the straight course of the street this can still be recognized.

origins.name: Spyridon Louisweg
origins.en: Greek athlete, won gold in the marathon at the Olympic Games in Athens in 1896.

origins.name: Srefidensiplein
origins.en: Srefidensi is an important concept in Surinamese history and means 'independence'. The word was invented by the Surinamese poet Henri Frans de Ziel, alias Trefossa (1916-1975). 'Srefi' means 'self' in Sranantongo and 'densi' something like 'do'. Trefossa also wrote the Surinamese national anthem

origins.name: Staalkade
origins.en: To the Staalhof around the corner on the Groenburgwal. The Staalhof was the seat of the Staalmeesters, a college that supervised the products of the linen industry in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The Staalkade first emerged around 1630 through the merger and bore the name Binnen-Amstel until 1913.

origins.name: Staalmeesterslaan
origins.en: One of Rembrandt's most famous paintings.

origins.name: Staalstraat
origins.en: To the Staalhof around the corner on the Groenburgwal. The Staalhof was the seat of the Staalmeesters, a college that supervised the products of the linen industry in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The Staalkade first arose around 1630 by embankment and bore the name Binnen-Amstel until 1913.

origins.name: Staatsliedenbrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after the neighborhood in which it is located, the Staatsliedenbuurt

origins.name: Stade de Colombes
origins.en: Stadium in Paris. Ajax won the quarter-finals of the European Cup for Champions on March 5, 1969 at this stadium.

origins.name: Stadhouderskade
origins.en: When this quay was to be named, it was two hundred years ago that stadtholder William III freed the country from the English, the French and the Münsterians. Although Amsterdam has never been very stadtholder-friendly, this was still a reason to name the stadtholders, namely William II (1626-1650) and William III (1650-1702), in addition to a Nassaukade and a Mauritskade.

origins.name: Stadionkade
origins.en: A stadium has been a playing field with eccentrically sloping seats since the time of the Greeks. The road runs along the place where the stadium stood during the inauguration in 1922 (at the current Amazonestraat). The Olympic Stadium (on the square) was built for the 1928 Olympic Games.

origins.name: Stadionplein
origins.en: A stadium has been a playing field with eccentrically sloping seats since the time of the Greeks. The road runs along the place where the stadium stood during the inauguration in 1922 (at the current Amazonestraat). The Olympic Stadium (on the square) was built for the 1928 Olympic Games.

origins.name: Stadionweg
origins.en: A stadium has been a playing field with eccentrically sloping seats since the time of the Greeks. The road runs along the place where the stadium stood during the inauguration in 1922 (at the current Amazonestraat). The Olympic Stadium (on the square) was built for the 1928 Olympic Games.

origins.name: Staghof
origins.en: The part of the rigging of a ship that must support the masts.

origins.name: Stammerlandweg
origins.en: The name recalls the Stammerlandpolder, an old polder name, now part of the Gemeenschapspolder.

origins.name: Stapels
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the French port town of Etaples, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Staringplein
origins.en: Antoni Christiaan Winand Staring (1767-1840), poet of nature poetry. Lived at De Wildenborch castle near Vorden.

origins.name: Staringstraat
origins.en: Antoni Christiaan Winand Staring (1767-1840), poet of nature poetry. Lived at De Wildenborch castle near Vorden.

origins.name: Starrenboschstraat
origins.en: The estate Starre-Bosch, which stood on Kruislaan from 1690 to around 1800, on the site of the current Oosterbegraafplaats.

origins.name: Statenjachtstraat
origins.en: The official name of the service vessel of the state colleges in the Seven Provinces.

origins.name: Stationsplein
origins.en: To the Central Station completed in 1889, designed by architect Pierre Cuypers. Despite the many objections of the municipal government and the Chamber of Commerce, construction of the station at this location was carried out by the then-government.

origins.name: Staverdenplein
origins.en: Neighborhood in the municipality of Ermelo (Gelderland). The castle of Staverden, built around 1905 on medieval foundations, is also known as Pauwenhof.

origins.name: Steelvlietplein
origins.en: As a result of a storm surge in 1530, a church village near Reimerswaal on Zuid-Beveland drowned.

origins.name: Steenbokstraat
origins.en: The constellation, also the sign of the Zodiac.

origins.name: Steenderenstraat
origins.en: Village north of Doesburg (Gelderland). The town of Bronkhorst is now also part of this municipality.

origins.name: Steengroevenpad
origins.en: Country house east of Winterswijk.

origins.name: Steenhouwerijbrug
origins.en: Named after the stonemasons who worked in the Stads Metseltuin on the Leidsegracht.

origins.name: Steenhouwerssteeg
origins.en: In 1557, the stonemason Jan Woutersz lived on the corner of the canal. Before that, this was the Schoolsteegje, because this was the exit of the O.Z.-school.

origins.name: Stekkenbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill northwest of Groesbeek (Gelderland).

origins.name: Stellendamstraat
origins.en: Fisherman's village on the island of Goeree-Overflakkee (South Holland).

origins.name: Stellingweg
origins.en: A stelling is a loop supported by supports around a high mill. From this loop the mill is watered and the sails are taken in. In 1976, for traffic technical reasons, part of the Stellingweg was renamed Molenaarsweg, while another part was added to Appelweg.

origins.name: Stenen Beer
origins.en: Named after defensive work in the Amsterdam position, located between Buitendijk and Couhornerhoek during the Batavian Republic. Demolished in 1825.

origins.name: Stenendokweg
origins.en: The dug docks of the shipyard, which are closed with sluice gates. They are mainly used at the repair yard.

origins.name: Stenghof
origins.en: A mast is an extension of the ship's mast.

origins.name: Stentorstraat
origins.en: A microscopic aquatic creature, can attach itself to a substrate, with its body stretching enormously in length, with a mouth funnel at the end.

origins.name: Stephensonstraat
origins.en: George Stephenson (1781-1848), English engineer, inventor of the locomotive (1814).

origins.name: Sterappelstraat
origins.en: Apple variety, originating around 1830 in southern the Netherlands or Belgium. The fruits are quite small, round and have a dark red color.

origins.name: Sterkenburg
origins.en: Old knight's manor town in Driebergen (Utrecht), of which only the heavy round tower remained after the demolition in 1848 and against which a new house was built.

origins.name: Sterrenplein
origins.en: The celestial bodies, namely fixed stars, planets and comets. The square is the center of the oldest part of the garden village of Oostzaan, where the streets are named after celestial bodies.

origins.name: Sterrenstraat
origins.en: The celestial bodies, namely fixed stars, planets and comets. The square is the center of the oldest part of the garden village of Oostzaan, where the streets are named after celestial bodies.

origins.name: Stettineiland
origins.en: Important historical Swedish and Prussian export port of wood. The city is now Polish and called Szczecin; Originally council decision spelled 'Stennin', this was later restored.

origins.name: Steve Bikoplein
origins.en: Steve Biko (1946-1977), killed in the nonviolent resistance against racial discrimination in South Africa. From 21-9-1904 to 1-2-1978 this was Pretoriusplein.

origins.name: Steven Vennecoolstraat
origins.en: Master builder (1659-1719), built among other things the Deutzenhofje on the Prinsengracht.

origins.name: Stichtstraat
origins.en: The name for the entire worldly area of the bishop of Utrecht, which ran from Bodegraven to the city of Groningen. Amstelland also belonged to it. later the term was narrowed down to the current province of Utrecht.

origins.name: Stieltjesstraat
origins.en: Thomas Jan Stieltjes (1856-1894), mathematician. Made contributions to mathematical analysis and number theory.

origins.name: Stierstraat
origins.en: The constellation, also a sign in the Zodiac.

origins.name: Stoel en Spreehof
origins.en: Teunis Stoel (1852-1912) and Marius Spree (1875-1925), who together operated the Plantage Schouwburg in the Plantage. They brought real folk pieces, such as works by Justus van Maurik.

origins.name: Stoelenmatterspad
origins.en: Originally a typical traveling profession. The name is related to the caravan world and refers to the caravan camp on site.

origins.name: Stokerkade
origins.en: Occupational name for lighting fires or ovens, and especially on locomotives and ships.

origins.name: Stolwijkstraat
origins.en: Village east of Gouda (South Holland).

origins.name: Stompetorenstraat
origins.en: Village in the Schermer, near Alkmaar (North Holland).

origins.name: Stoofsteeg
origins.en: Probably named so, because there were some one-room houses here, where needy people lived. The alley is mentioned in 1464 under the name Stovestege. Stove means room (compare the German 'Stube'). The alley was also previously known as Sint Jans Molenpad.

origins.name: Stoombootweg
origins.en: The road leads to the place on the Landsmeerdijk of the former station of the steamboat service on Amsterdam.

origins.name: Stoomgemaalstraat
origins.en: The mill, which drained the polder and replaced the windmill in the course of the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Stormsteeg
origins.en: Because this part of the city was on the outermost edge until the sixteenth century, people here were hit hard by storms. It is likely that the name of the alley was therefore created.

origins.name: Stormvloedkeringstraat
origins.en: Hydraulic construction that must counteract extreme high water floods.

origins.name: Stoutenburggracht
origins.en: Village south of Hoevelaken (Utrecht). It is named after the former castle that belonged to Van Oldebarneveldt.

origins.name: Strackéstraat
origins.en: Johan Ph. Stracke (1817-1892), sculptor. Made statues of Tollens (Rotterdam), Boerhaave (Leiden), Jan van Nassau (Utrecht) and in Amsterdam, among other things, sculptures on the facade of the Sint Jacobsgesticht in the Plantage Middenlaan. (Not to be confused with F. Stracke who made the bust of Prince Henry.)

origins.name: Stralsundbrug
origins.en: Stralsund is a German port city on the island of Rügen on the Baltic Sea. The names in the Houthavens are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Strandboulevard
origins.en: Refers to the important beach where this street runs along. The beach that is also the namesake of Strandeiland.

origins.name: Strandeilandlaan
origins.en: Name refers to the future Beach Island

origins.name: Strandvlietpad
origins.en: Named after the subway stop, where this path leads to. Strandvliet was the name of an old farm near Duivendrecht.

origins.name: Strawinskylaan
origins.en: Igor Strawinsky (1882-1971), American of Russian birth. Conductor and composer of operas and ballet music, including 'Le sacre du printemps'.

origins.name: Strawinskypad
origins.en: Igor Strawinsky (1882-1971), American of Russian birth. Conductor and composer of operas and ballet music, including 'Le sacre du printemps'.

origins.name: Streefkerkstraat
origins.en: Village in the Alblasserwaard near the Lek (South Holland).

origins.name: Strekkerweg
origins.en: Occupational name for someone who deforms metal, for example by means of a series of successive punch presses perpendicular to the direction of tension as in blacksmithing. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Stromarkt
origins.en: Named after the function that this square-shaped piece of street had in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Stromboliweg
origins.en: Volcanic island northeast of Sicily, part of the Lipari archipelago.

origins.name: Struisgrasstraat
origins.en: Grass species, which occurs all over the world.

origins.name: Stuurmankade
origins.en: Someone who controls a vessel.

origins.name: Stuyvesantstraat
origins.en: Peter Stuyvesant (1592-1672), colonial administrator, governor of Curaçao. The last director of the colony of New Netherlands, which had to be ceded to the English with the Treaty of Breda (1667). He stimulated trade in America and the West.

origins.name: Subangstraat
origins.en: Name of the Kuala Lumpur airport, Malaysia.

origins.name: Suikerdiefjestraat
origins.en: Small bird. One of the most famous birds of the Dutch Antilles.

origins.name: Suikerpeerpad
origins.en: Old Dutch pear variety. The path is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Suikerplein
origins.en: This square and the surrounding streets were laid out on the grounds of the former Westersuikerfabriek where many families used to live in the Spaarndammerbuurt neighborhood.

origins.name: Sumatrakade
origins.en: Island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Sumatraplantsoen
origins.en: Island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Sumatrastraat
origins.en: Island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Surinamekade
origins.en: Refers to the country of Suriname.

origins.name: Surinameplein
origins.en: Named after Suriname

origins.name: Surinamestraat
origins.en: Named after Suriname

origins.name: Suze Groenewegplantsoen
origins.en: Politician (1875-1940), teacher in Rotterdam. Since 1914 member of the party board of the SDAP. Member of the Provincial States of South Holland and of the municipal council of Rotterdam and the first female member of the House of Representatives (1918-1937). As a member of parliament, she has worked, among other things, for the possibility of also appointing women as mayors.

origins.name: Suze Robertsonstraat
origins.en: Painter (1856-1922) from the Breitner school. Primarily painted still lifes.

origins.name: Swammerdamstraat
origins.en: Jan Swammerdam (1637-1680), anatomist and physicist. Conducted important microscopic research, preserved in his 'Bible of Nature'.

origins.name: Taandwarsstraat
origins.en: Tannin is a yellowish-brown pigment, prepared from oak bark and used to make fishnets and sails durable. The tanneries, formerly spread throughout the city, were only allowed on the Realeneiland around 1623 due to fire danger.

origins.name: Taanstraat
origins.en: Tannin is a yellowish-brown pigment, prepared from oak bark and used to make fishnets and sails durable. The tanneries, formerly spread throughout the city, were only allowed on the Realeneiland around 1623 due to fire danger.

origins.name: Tafelbergweg
origins.en: Name of a hill near Blaricum (North Holland).

origins.name: Tagorestraat
origins.en: Rabindranath Tagore (1861-1941) was the first Indian writer to win the Nobel Prize for Literature.

origins.name: Talbotstraat
origins.en: William Henry Fox Talbot (1800-1877), English philosopher, Egyptologist, mathematician, linguist, physicist and photographer. Founder of modern photography. Experimented in the 1930s of the nineteenth century with photographic processes. Developed a negative process that made it possible to make more than one print of a negative.

origins.name: Talmastraat
origins.en: Aritius Sybrandus Talma (1864-1916), Reformed minister, later anti-revolutionary statesman. Leader of the Christian Songwriters' Association and director of the Patrimonium Housing Foundation. From 1908 to 1913 Minister of Agriculture. He played an important role in improving the poor conditions in the field of housing.

origins.name: Taman Sapituin
origins.en: Taman Sari means flower garden in Indonesian

origins.name: Tamariskhof
origins.en: Evergreen shrub with (light) pink flowers, which grows well on the coast.

origins.name: Tan Malakastraat
origins.en: Tan Malaka (Suliki 1894 - Kediri 1949). Tan Malaka obtained a teacher's certificate in Haarlem. During his stay in the Netherlands (1913-1919), he became more active in the Communist Party. After returning, he joined the Communist Party founded by Henk Sneevliet. The colonial authorities arrested him and exiled him from India. Back in the Netherlands, he was the first Indonesian to stand for a seat in the House of Representatives (1922). He was not elected and left for the Soviet Union. He then served as an agent of the Communist International (Komintern) in Southeast Asia until 1927 and led a hidden and persecuted existence.

origins.name: Tartaud-Kleinhof
origins.en: The theater actors Frits Tartaud (1857-1946), actor-director, director of the Rotterdam Theater, and his wife Alida Klein (1873-1938), a gifted tragedienne.

origins.name: Tasmanstraat
origins.en: Abel Jansz. Tasman (1603-1659), sailor and explorer. Discovered in 1642 and 1644 the island of Tasmania and New Zealand named after him.

origins.name: Teerketelsteeg
origins.en: This alley, which originally ended dead on the water where Koggestraat is now, ran behind the house 'de Teerketel' on the current Spuistraat. Tar was cooked and sold in the sixteenth century.

origins.name: Tefelenstraat
origins.en: Village on the Maas, northwest of Oss.

origins.name: Tegenhouderstraat
origins.en: The metalworker, who works together with the bricklayer. With a chisel, he holds the nail head against it when it is hammered through the bricklayer. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Teilingen
origins.en: Thirteenth-century castle, now a ruin located in Sassenheim (South Holland). Became famous through Jacoba of Bavaria, who lived and died there.

origins.name: Teixeira de Mattosstraat
origins.en: Named after the originally Portuguese-Jewish family that later established a bank at number 746 Prinsengracht. The bank went bankrupt in 1966.

origins.name: Tekkopstraat
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Woerden (Utrecht).

origins.name: Teleportboulevard
origins.en: The office area around the Sloterdijk station, of which this road forms a central axis, had the unofficial name Teleport when it was built. This is an American term adopted for an area of work with high-quality internal and external communication systems. The original intention to develop this area in this way has only been partially realized.

origins.name: Telescoophof
origins.en: A pair of binoculars for astronomical observations.

origins.name: Tempelhofstraat
origins.en: Name of the Berlin airport.

origins.name: Ten Katestraat
origins.en: Jan Jacob Lodewijk ten Kate (1819-1889), preacher-poet also provided translations of Goethe, Dante and Andersen. Originally widely read, but since the movement of the Eighty-Eighters has been pushed back.

origins.name: Tenderstraat
origins.en: The wagon behind the steam locomotive, on which coal and water are transported.

origins.name: Tenerifestraat
origins.en: Spanish island off the African coast. One of the Canary Islands.

origins.name: Teniersstraat
origins.en: David Teniers the Younger (1610-1690), South Dutch painter. Founded the Brussels Academy in 1663. Known for his tavern scenes and farmer's fairs.

origins.name: Ter Boede
origins.en: Originally a medieval castle near Koudekerke (Walcheren), now a stately country house from around 1740.

origins.name: Ter Gouwstraat
origins.en: Jan ter Gouw (1814-1894), teacher. Well-known historian of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Ter Haarstraat
origins.en: Bernard ter Haar (1806-1880), preacher-poet from the school of Tollens. Wrote religious and domestic poems. From 1854 professor in Utrecht.

origins.name: Ter Hooge
origins.en: Medieval castle near Koudekerke (Zeeland), significantly renovated in 1755 and partly rebuilt.

origins.name: Ter Kleef
origins.en: Former castle, built at the end of the fourteenth century, blown up in 1572 after the siege of Haarlem by the Spanish. Today, only a farm-like building, a tower and a pile of stones remain in Haarlem-Noord.

origins.name: Terheideweg
origins.en: Village south of The Hague. Known in national history for the naval battle of 1653 against the English, in which Admiral Maarten Harpertszoon Tromp died.

origins.name: Terletstraat
origins.en: Neighborhood on the Arnhem-Apeldoorn road.

origins.name: Termietergouw
origins.en: The farm 'de Termiet', where the road leads to it. (Termite comes from ter Miede, and ants are grasslands.)

origins.name: Termieterweg
origins.en: The farm 'de Termiet', where the road leads to it. (Termite comes from ter Miede, and ants are grasslands.)

origins.name: Termini
origins.en: Most important train station in Rome.

origins.name: Ternatestraat
origins.en: Island belonging to the Moluccas (Indonesia).

origins.name: Terpstraat
origins.en: Artificially raised residential hill, occurs under this name in Friesland. Terpen also occur in all kinds of shapes in other provinces under the name woerd, werd or wierd.

origins.name: Terschellingstraat
origins.en: Wadden island (Friesland).

origins.name: Tervurenpad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Teslastraat
origins.en: Nikola Tesla (1856-1943), Yugoslav engineer and physicist. In 1884 he emigrated to America. A member of Edison's team made numerous inventions in the field of alternating current and high-frequency technology. The unit of magnetic induction is named after him.

origins.name: Tesselschadestraat
origins.en: Maria Tesselschade Visscher (1594-1649), poet. She adorned the Muiderkring with her sister. Daughter of Roemer Visscher, who gave her this name at her birth, because he had just lost many of his ships at Texel.

origins.name: Tetje de Jongbrug
origins.en: Theodora (Tetje) de Jong (Uithoorn, May 2, 1918 - Drachten, January 21, 1999) was the first paid female police commissioner in the Netherlands. In 1954, the same year in which the first women joined the uniform service at the Amsterdam police, De Jong was appointed chief inspector. On January 1, 1964, De Jong was officially appointed police commissioner in Amsterdam. In 1977, De Jong received a Royal award due to her great significance for the Amsterdam police: she was appointed Officer of the Order of Orange-Nassau.

origins.name: Teugestraat
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Voorst (Gelderland).

origins.name: Texelplein
origins.en: Wadden island (North Holland).

origins.name: Texelweg
origins.en: Wadden island (North Holland).

origins.name: Teylerplein
origins.en: The oldest museum in the Netherlands: the Teylers Museum in Haarlem. The eighteenth-century merchant Pieter Teyler van der Hulst left his fortune to promote art and science. In 1784 the museum began with one room, where scientific instruments, extinct animals and drawings were exhibited. Over time, the collection has been expanded with paintings, coins and fossils, among other things.

origins.name: Th. J. Lammerslaan
origins.en: Theodorus Johannes Lammers (1890-1972), Amsterdam architect. Designer from the later period of the Amsterdam School, the man behind the Physiological Laboratory of the Vrije Universiteit on Valeriusplein.

origins.name: Th. K. van Lohuizenlaan
origins.en: Theodore Karel (1890-1956), architect and urban planner. He was at the basis of the General Expansion Plan for Amsterdam, which appeared in 1934. Worked closely with Cornelis van Eesteren.

origins.name: Th. Weeversweg
origins.en: Theo Weevers (1875-1952) professor of botany in Amsterdam. Founder of government care for nature conservation. Chairman of the State Committee on nature reserves and nature conservation.

origins.name: Theemsweg
origins.en: River in England.

origins.name: Theo Fransmanbrug
origins.en: Theo Frenchman, who was the first district chairman of Amsterdam-North from 1981 to 1990. He worked as such to find new destinations for the NDSM site after the closure of the shipyard.

origins.name: Theo Frenkelhof
origins.en: Theodorus Maurits Frenkel (1871-1956), actor, theater and film director, member of the famous theater family Bouwmeester. Directed about two hundred films in England, France and Germany. Between 1915 and 1922 he also directed a number of feature films in the Netherlands. Achieved international success with his adaptation of Heijermans' play 'Brand in De Jonge Jan', in which he also acted.

origins.name: Theo Mann-Bouwmeesterhof
origins.en: The actress Theodora Mann born Bouwmeester (1850-1939), sister of Louis Bouwmeester. She was one of the greatest tragedians. Her starring roles included Tosca, Lady Macbeth and Mary Stuart.

origins.name: Theo Thijssenhof
origins.en: Theodorus Thijssen (1879-1943), Amsterdam teacher and pedagogue. Wrote novellas and novels on the field of school and children's life, of which 'Kees the boy' is best known.

origins.name: Theo van Doesburgstraat
origins.en: Pseudonym of Christian E.M. Küpper (1883-1931), painter and designer of stained glass windows under the influence of Mondrian. Driving force of the 'Stijlgroep' (1917). As an architect, he worked with Rietveld.

origins.name: Theodoor van Hoytemastraat
origins.en: Painter (1863-1917), mainly painted animals, illustrator and lithographer.

origins.name: Theodorus Dobbestraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1901-1944), born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Dieren.

origins.name: Theodorus Majofskistraat
origins.en: Theodorus Johannes Majofski (1770-1836), Polish-born actor, ancestor of a famous acting family. In his time, he was one of the most important figures in Amsterdam theater.

origins.name: Theophile de Bockstraat
origins.en: Painter (1851-1904), best known for his nature scenes.

origins.name: Theophilusstraat
origins.en: A rhymed Marian legend from the fourteenth century.

origins.name: Thérèse Schwartzeplein
origins.en: Therèse van Duijl-Schwartze (1852-1918), portrait painter. At the request of the painter Lizzy Ansingh, the first name is included in full in the name, to make it clear that it was a woman.

origins.name: Thérèse Schwartzestraat
origins.en: Therèse van Duijl-Schwartze (1852-1918), portrait painter. At the request of the painter Lizzy Ansingh, the first name is included in full in the name, to make it clear that it was a woman.

origins.name: Theseusstraat
origins.en: In Greek mythology the hero of Attica, who defeated the minotaur with the help of Ariadne.

origins.name: Tholenstraat
origins.en: One of the Zeeuwse islands, separated by water from the Eendracht of North Brabant.

origins.name: Thomas à Kempisstraat
origins.en: Thomas van Kempen (1380-1471), philosopher, from Kempen in the land of Cleve. Author of the famous work 'On the imitation of Christ'.

origins.name: Thomas Hoodstraat
origins.en: English scholar, lived at the end of the sixteenth century. He taught astronomy and navigation in London among other things and published about the use of sea charts. In 1602 a translation of his work appeared in Amsterdam under the title 'Tgebruijck vande zeecaarte'.

origins.name: Thomas Prinslaan
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1885-1942), carried out sabotage at the Kromhout-Motorenfabriek where he worked, participated in the preparation of the February Strike in 1941. On November 19, 1942, he was executed in Soesterberg.

origins.name: Thomas R. Malthusstraat
origins.en: Thomas Robert Malthus (1766-1834), British historian and economist. In 1798 his pamphlet 'An Essay on the Principle of Population' appeared, in which he demonstrates that the population is increasing faster than economic growth. This would lead to overcrowding and social misery.

origins.name: Thomas van Aquinostraat
origins.en: Italian theologian and philosopher (1225-1274), one of the greatest of the scholastics, who tried to make the Church's teachings understandable to the mind.

origins.name: Thomas van Erpehof
origins.en: Professor of Oriental languages (1584-1624) at the University of Leiden, close friend of Hugo de Groot.

origins.name: Thorbeckeplein
origins.en: Jan Rudolf Thorbecke (1798-1872), liberal statesman and professor in Leiden. Prime Minister and several times Minister of the Interior. His most important act was the revision of the constitution in 1848. Originally this was a part of the Reguliersgracht. After the filling in of this part in 1874, the name Reguliersplein was born. In 1876, the statue of Thorbecke was unveiled here, made by the sculptor F. Leenhoff. This was the reason for giving the square its current name. (The statue bears the inscription Optimo civi cives = the citizens to the best citizen.)

origins.name: Thorn Prikkerstraat
origins.en: Named after Johan Thorn Prikker (1868-1932) who worked in the Symbolist, Impressionist and Art Nouveau style.

origins.name: Tichelstraat
origins.en: Named after the many tile and brick bakeries established here in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Tidorestraat
origins.en: Island belonging to the Moluccas (Indonesia).

origins.name: Tielstraat
origins.en: The city in the Betuwe on the Waal, center of fruit and vegetable cultivation.

origins.name: Tienenpad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Tiengemetenstraat
origins.en: The South Holland island in the Haringvliet.

origins.name: Tienraaikade
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Mierlo, east of Venray (Limburg).

origins.name: Tijl Uilenspiegelstraat
origins.en: Main character from a folk book from around 1500, who is seen as a personification of the Flemish folk character with his mischievous antics. The story was depicted in 1867 by Charles de Coster, and in a symphonic poem by Richard Strauss.

origins.name: Tijnmuiden
origins.en: The English port town of Tynemouth, near Newcastle, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Tilanusstraat
origins.en: Christiaan Bernhard Tilanus (1856-1943), professor of surgery in Amsterdam. Tilanus was born as the son of J.W. Tilanus, professor from 1867-1893 and grandson of the equally famous professor C.B. Tilanus (1828-1873). He was a specialist in bacteriology and later also in orthopedics. He soon saw the importance of first aid by laypeople in accidents. At his initiative, a brochure was distributed in 1893 that laid the foundation for the establishment of the first first aid association in the Netherlands, the 'Association for First Aid in Accidents', which later received the title of Royal. He also founded the Clinical School, the Training School for midwives and the Orthopaedic Association.

origins.name: Timo Smeehuijzenbrug
origins.en: Timo Smeehuijzen was a 20-year-old soldier who died in Afghanistan on June 15, 2007. Before that, he attended school at the nearby Fons Vitae high school, hence this location. This bridge is also a tribute to all other soldiers who died in Afghanistan.

origins.name: Timorplein
origins.en: Island belonging to the Lesser Sunda Islands in Indonesia. Half of the island was Portuguese territory.

origins.name: Timorstraat
origins.en: Island belonging to the Lesser Sunda Islands in Indonesia. Half of the island was Portuguese territory.

origins.name: Tintorettostraat
origins.en: Jacopo Robusti (1518-1594), calling himself Tintoretto, Italian painter. One of the main painters of the Venetian school.

origins.name: Tip Maruggstraat
origins.en: Silvio Alberto 'Tip' Marugg (Willemstad, 1923 - Willemstad 2006) was a writer and poet. After obtaining his Mulodiploma in 1942, he served in the military for five years. After that, he worked at Shell, where he discovered writing after working on the staff magazine Passaat. He debuted in 1958 with the novel Weekend Pilgrimage. For his third novel The morning is calling again from 1988 he was nominated for the AKO Literature Prize and in 1989 he received the Cola Debrot Prize. Island life played a major role in his books, which have been translated into several languages.

origins.name: Titiaanstraat
origins.en: Painter's name of Tiziano Vecellio (1477-1576), famous master of the Venetian school.

origins.name: Titus Brandsmabrug
origins.en: This bridge is named after Titus Brandsma (1881 - 1942). He was a Roman Catholic priest and professor of Theology in Nijmegen. As a spiritual advisor, he exerted influence in 1942 on the Catholic daily newspapers to avoid making propaganda for the NSB. The same year, he was deported to Dachau, where he died.

origins.name: Titus van Rijnstraat
origins.en: Son of Rembrandt van Rijn and Saskia van Uijlenburg (1641-1668). Modeled several times. After Rembrandt's death, he ran an art gallery with works by the painter with his stepmother Hendrikje Stoffels. Was buried in the Westerkerk.

origins.name: Tjalkstraat
origins.en: River sailing ship with flat bottom and round bow, gaff rigged.

origins.name: Tjepmapad
origins.en: Former country house near Vleuten (Utrecht), of which only the seventeenth-century gate building remains.

origins.name: Tjerk Hiddes de Vriesstraat
origins.en: Frisian admiral (1622-1666), died in the Second English War at Dunkirk.

origins.name: Tjeukemeerhof
origins.en: More, located in southern Friesland.

origins.name: Tjotterspad
origins.en: Inland waterway sailboat with low draft.

origins.name: Tobias M.C. Asserstraat
origins.en: Jurist (1838-1913). Known at home and abroad in the field of international private law. In 1862 he became a professor in Amsterdam, in 1893 a member of the Council of State. In 1911 he received the Nobel Peace Prize.

origins.name: Toetsenbordweg
origins.en: Street name in the category Information technology.

origins.name: Tofana
origins.en: Mountain peak in Italy, 3243 meters high.

origins.name: Tolbrugstraat
origins.en: To the toll booth at the corner of the current Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was collected since around 1780 until the annexation of this area in 1896. The toll was intended for the maintenance of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation, the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1886).

origins.name: Toldwarsstraat
origins.en: To the toll booth at the corner of the current Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was collected since around 1780 until the annexation of this area in 1896.
