The toll was intended for the maintenance of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation, the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1886).

origins.name: Tolhuisweg
origins.en: To the entertainment venue the Toll House, formerly a popular venue. Construction dates back to 1662, when a highway was built here and a toll was established. In the garden, the famous concerts were held from 1887 to 1912 by the then popular seventh regiment under the leadership of organist Joh. Zaagmans.

origins.name: Tolkamerstraat
origins.en: The village with border office near Lobith (Gelderland) on the Rhine. The Rhine is the busiest border crossing in the world here.

origins.name: Tollensstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Frederik Tollens (1780-1856), Rotterdam merchant, who became known as a folk poet.

origins.name: Tolsendestraat
origins.en: Former church village, south of Yerseke (Zeeland), flooded in 1530.

origins.name: Tolstraat
origins.en: To the toll booth at the corner of the current Tolstraat and the Amsteldijk. The toll was collected since around 1780 until the annexation of this area in 1896. The toll was intended for the maintenance of the Amsteldijk from this point to Ouderkerk. Before the annexation, the street was called Verversstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1886).

origins.name: Tom Schreursweg
origins.en: Cornelis Petrus Antonius Schreurs (1896-1956), already took the initiative in 1923 for radio sports broadcasts, in particular of international football matches.

origins.name: Tomatenstraat
origins.en: Named after the tomato, a fruit.

origins.name: Toministraat
origins.en: Port city on the island of Sulawesi (Celebes) in Indonesia.

origins.name: Tommaso Albinonistraat
origins.en: Italian composer (1671-1750), probably self-taught. Worked as a chamber musician of Ferdinando Carlo, Duke of Mantua. Johan Sebastian Bach used themes by Albinoni three times as a starting point for his own compositions. Albinoni wrote instrumental works and about fifty operas.

origins.name: Ton de Leeuwstraat
origins.en: Composer (1926-1996), was associated with the Sweelinck Conservatory in Amsterdam from 1959 to 1987, first as head professor of composition and from 1984 as artistic director. He dealt with the relationship between the East and the West in music. He received many awards, including the Prix d'Italia and the Matthijs Vermeulen Prize.

origins.name: Tondenpad
origins.en: Neighbourhood in the municipality of Brummen, west of Zutphen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Tongelaer
origins.en: Former castle from the fifteenth century, located under MilI, municipality of Beers (North Brabant). Only a square gate tower remains.

origins.name: Tongerenstraat
origins.en: Neighbourhood and estate west of Epe (Gelderland).

origins.name: Tonia Stieltjesplein
origins.en: Tonia Stieltjes (1881-1932) was born in the Czaar Peterstraat, as the daughter of an Afro-Surinamese born into slavery. She campaigned for the improvement of the working and living conditions of aid workers and is considered the first black trade unionist woman. She also lives on in the many portraits where she posed as a model.

origins.name: Top Naeffstraat
origins.en: Anthonetta van Rhijn born Naeff (1878-1953), novelist and theater critic. Wrote biographies of Willem Royaards and Sarah Bernhardt, among others.

origins.name: Top Rinckerstraat
origins.en: Friedrich Johannes Wilhelm Rincker (1877-1939), one of the top figures in Dutch cricket, played in 43 international matches.

origins.name: Topaasstraat
origins.en: A yellow gemstone.

origins.name: Topkapipad
origins.en: Topkapi Museum in Istanbul. One of the most beautifully preserved examples of worldly architecture in Istanbul. Originally the palace of the sultans. Opened as a museum since 1924. The collection consists of the most diverse objects that belonged to the Turkish court, including weapons, porcelain, jewelry, clothing and miniatures.

origins.name: Torensluis
origins.en: The name of this permanent bridge refers to the Jan Roodenpoortstoren, which used to stand next to the gate in the city wall here and was demolished in 1829. The base of the tower is still located on the side of this bridge.

origins.name: Torensteeg
origins.en: The alley leads to the place where once stood the Jan Roodenpoort tower next to the gate in the city wall. After the demolition of the city wall, this tower still existed until 1829. The base of the tower is still located on the side of the bridge, the Tower Lock.

origins.name: Torenven
origins.en: An old local name: a swamp near the tower.

origins.name: Torresstraat
origins.en: Luis Vaez de Torres (1728-1779), Spanish explorer. Discovered the Torresstraat, a sea island named after him, between Australia and New Guinea.

origins.name: Torricellistraat
origins.en: Evangelista Torricelli (1608-1647), Italian physicist, professor in Florence. Inventor of the Torricelli tube, a precursor to the mercury barometer. This street was named Dr. Leydsstraat by the former municipality of Watergraafsmeer (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1921).

origins.name: Tosaristraat
origins.en: Mountain village and plain in East Java. The highest place on the island. During the Dutch rule one of the most popular holiday destinations.

origins.name: Tosarituin
origins.en: Mountain village and plain in East Java. The highest place on the island. During the Dutch rule one of the most popular holiday destinations.

origins.name: Tourniairestraat
origins.en: Bachigaloupi Tourniaire (1850-1921), in his time a particularly beloved actor who excelled in comedic roles, and his son Oscar Tourniaire (1880-1939), who played many Shakespearean roles as an actor.

origins.name: Touwbaan
origins.en: The street was laid out on the site where in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the line railways of the Dutch East India Company lay.

origins.name: Touwbaanpark
origins.en: The street was laid out on the site where in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the line railways of the Dutch East India Company lay.

origins.name: Touwslagerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name from shipbuilding. The name reminds us of the many shipyards that were established here in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Transformatorweg
origins.en: Device for converting electrical current from one voltage to another

origins.name: Transvaalkade
origins.en: The country across the Vaal River. Formerly an independent Boer Republic and after the 1899-1902 war a province of the Union of South Africa. The street originated from the remainder of Lange Overamstelstraat (formerly named by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel) and Ringstraat (council decision, 1904), the quay was originally named Ringkade by Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Transvaalplein
origins.en: The country across the Vaal River. Formerly an independent Boer Republic and after the 1899-1902 war a province of the Union of South Africa. The street originated from the remainder of Lange Overamstelstraat (formerly named by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel) and Ringstraat (council decision, 1904), the quay was originally named Ringkade by Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Transvaalstraat
origins.en: The country across the Vaal River. Formerly an independent Boer Republic and after the 1899-1902 war a province of the Union of South Africa. The street originated from the remainder of Lange Overamstelstraat (formerly named by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel) and Ringstraat (council decision, 1904), the quay was originally named Ringkade by Nieuwer-Amstel.

origins.name: Treilerhof
origins.en: A trawler or trawler is a vessel for marine fishing, where fishing is done with a trawl or scraper net.

origins.name: Tretjakovlaan
origins.en: Named after the Tretyakov Museum in Moscow. Construction was completed in 1900. The collection is based on the art collection of Pavel Tretyakov, which he donated to Moscow in 1892. Famous for the unique collection of icons.

origins.name: Trianonpad
origins.en: The name of two small palaces in the park of Versailles. The Grand Trianon was built at the behest of Louis XIV (1687-1688) and the Petit Trianon at the behest of Louis XV (1762-1768).

origins.name: Trichtstraat
origins.en: Village on the Linge, northwest of Geldermalsen (Gelderland).

origins.name: Trijn Hullemanlaan
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1912-1941), involved in many illegal activities and member of the resistance group 'Krijn Breur'.

origins.name: Trimurtistraat
origins.en: Trimur: independence

origins.name: Troelstralaan
origins.en: Pieter Jelles Troelstra (1860-1930), lawyer and politician, and Frisian poet. Co-founder of the SDAP in 1894, member of the House of Representatives from 1897 to 1924.

origins.name: Troepiaalsingel
origins.en: Brightly colored bird. Usually flies in large flocks (troops), hence the name.

origins.name: Trompenburgstraat
origins.en: Former country house on the Amstel, named after the then owner: fleet commander Cornelis Tromp. After his death in 1691, mayor Nicolaas Witsen moved in there. At the beginning of the twentieth century, the Spijker automobile factory and the Nestelroy-Trompenburg paper factory settled here successively. The name of the street was originally Trompstraat (council decision, 1899).

origins.name: Trouringhstraat
origins.en: Title of a learned poem by Jacob Cats.

origins.name: Truus Wijsmullerbrug
origins.en: Geertruida Wijsmuller-Meyer (1896 - 1978) was already working to bring Jewish refugees from Central Europe to safety through the Netherlands before World War II. For example, she organized weekly transports of 500 children from Frankfurt, Vienna or Prague to England in 1938 and 1939 with the permission of Adolf Eichmann. In August 1939, she organized the evacuation of the Jewish population from Danzig in Poland After the outbreak of the war, she guided the transports to Marseille or Spain on a stopover to Palestine. She also provided food packages for Jewish children in Westerbork In addition, she managed to save 50 children from Westerbork from deportation to Poland.

origins.name: tt. Melaniaweg
origins.en: The turbinetanker Melania. This 330-meter-long and 250,000-ton tanker was delivered to Shell in 1969. The ship was built on the shipyard of the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM) in two parts and welded together after launching. Melania is the name of a shell (the trademark of Shell).

origins.name: tt. Melissaweg
origins.en: The turbine tanker Melissa. Built in 1965 by Van der Giessen-De Noord, first owned by N.V. Verenigde Tankkustvaart and then by P.A. van Es & Co. N.V..

origins.name: tt. Neveritaweg
origins.en: Turbine tanker, 110,000 tons. The last tanker built entirely by the Nederlandsche Dok en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij (NDSM), built in 1968 on behalf of Koninklijke Shell Groep. At that time the largest ever built supertanker in the Netherlands.

origins.name: tt. Vasumweg
origins.en: The turbine tanker Vasum, built in 1955 at the shipyard of the Dutch Dok- en Scheepsbouw Maatschappij on behalf of the Royal Shell Group. Vasum is the name of a shell (the trademark of Shell). The road was laid on the grounds of the former shipyard of the NDSM.

origins.name: Tugelaweg
origins.en: River in South Africa, the southern defensive line of the Boers in the war of 1899 to 1902, where fierce fighting took place against the English.

origins.name: Tuigerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name for the person who hoists and lowers ships. (The rigging of a ship includes all the ropework and steel wires for operating masts, winch equipment and davits.) The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Tuilstraat
origins.en: Village on the Waal opposite Zaltbommel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Tuimelaarstraat
origins.en: Dolphin, does not grow longer than 2.5 meters. It is dark, lives in groups and is distributed worldwide. The spinner dolphin is very agile and is often kept in dolphinariums.

origins.name: Tuin van Hera
origins.en: Greek goddess of marriage and childbirth. Fold and also sister of Zeus. Hera was also revered as the patroness of herds; The cow was one of the animals dedicated to her.

origins.name: Tuinbouwstraat
origins.en: The cultivation of vegetables, fruits and flowers.

origins.name: Tuinderijlaan
origins.en: Refers to community garden park De Bongerd.

origins.name: Tuinstraat
origins.en: Garden here has the meaning of shipyard or enclosed space. The street name is derived from the Stadstimmertuin (the City Shipyard), which was located here from 1612 to 1660 (near the Lijnbaansgracht) and where the street ran along.

origins.name: Tulastraat
origins.en: Tula, nicknamed Rigaud, was one of the leaders of the uprising of the enslaved people that broke out in Curaçao in August 1795. In September 1795 he was captured and executed.

origins.name: Turbinestraat
origins.en: Machine in which a screw-shaped rotor is brought into motion by fluid or steam, used among other things for generating electrical energy.

origins.name: Turbón
origins.en: Mountain peak in Spain, 2492 meters high.

origins.name: Turfdraagsterpad
origins.en: When this path still ran through to the (Old) Turfmarkt, the women who worked at the Turfmarkt lived in the houses along this path.

origins.name: Turfsteeg
origins.en: Named after the peat warehouse of the Oudezijds Huiszittenarmen (later the Arsenal), where the alley runs along.

origins.name: Turnerstraat
origins.en: Practitioner of gymnastics, one of the ancient Greek sports.

origins.name: Turnhoutplantsoen
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Tussen de Bogen
origins.en: Regarding the location between the railway viaducts. The spaces between these viaducts were called arches on site.

origins.name: Tussen Kadijken
origins.en: When a lot of land had been silted up outside the old sea wall (St. Antoniesdijk), a summer dike or canal was built. Originally, the new sea wall was spoken of, but that later fell out of use. With further raising of this new dike, the Laagte and the Hoogte van de Kadijk were spoken of. The Tussen Kadijken was called Korte Kerkstraat until 1943. This is indeed in the extension of the Plantage Kerklaan, but has never been connected to it.

origins.name: Tussen Meer
origins.en: Named after a former farm on the Uitweg near the Sloterpolder that was demolished in the 1950s for the construction of the Slotermeer district.

origins.name: Tussendek
origins.en: One of the decks of a ship.

origins.name: Tutein Noltheniusstraat
origins.en: Rudolf Peter Johannes Tutein Nolthenius (1851-1939), civil engineer. Designed plans for relocating the mouth of the Maas.

origins.name: Twee Koningskinderenstraat
origins.en: Named after the fairy tale 'The Twee Royal Children' by the Brothers Grimm.

origins.name: Tweede Anjeliersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Flower, belonging to the rose family.

origins.name: Tweede Atjehstraat
origins.en: The northern part of the Indonesian island of Sumatra. Especially known for the Atjeh War (1873-1904), to which the name of General Van Heutsz is associated.

origins.name: Tweede Bloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion from 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which the canal is named. On the fort stood the mill 'De Blom' from 1614 to 1878, which was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

origins.name: Tweede Boerhaavestraat
origins.en: Hermannus Boerhaave (1668-1738), professor of medicine in Leiden. Gained international fame. The street name Boerhaavestraat (first to fourth) has been changed quite often: established as Boerhaavestraat on 15-11-1876, changed to Eerste Boerhaavestraat on 15-11-1882. This change lapses again on 10-12-1884. On 13-10-1897 the street is extended with the same name and finally on 19-2-1908 the split into the current Eerste and Tweede Boerhaavestraat follows. For the Second, Third and Fourth Boerhaavestraat appointed in 1882, the names Deymanstraat, Ruyschstraat and Blasiusstraat were replaced.

origins.name: Tweede Boomdwarsstraat
origins.en: In this part of the Jordaan, streets are named after flowers, shrubs and trees. The street was also called Lindeboomstraat in the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Tweede Breeuwersstraat
origins.en: Occupational name. A brewer sealed the seams between the planks in a ship wall. In the Eerste Breeuwersstraat (formerly Breeuwersstraat), many brewers lived in the seventeenth century, who worked at the shipyards on the Prinsen- and Realeneiland. In 1895, the street running parallel to it was given the same name, making the addition Eerste and Tweede necessary.

origins.name: Tweede Ceramstraat
origins.en: Island in Indonesia.

origins.name: Tweede Coehoornstraat
origins.en: Menno baron van Coehoorn (1641-1704). Fortress builder, general engineer of the fortifications.

origins.name: Tweede Constantijn Huygensstraat
origins.en: Poet and prose writer (1596-1687), wrote among other things 'Hofwijck' and short poems. He was secretary of several successive stadholders. Before 1894 parts of these streets were called Eerste and Tweede Bilderdijkstraat (council decision, 1878 and 19-12-1883).

origins.name: Tweede Disteldwarsstraat
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Tweede Egelantiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the eglantine (sweet briar), a shrub.

origins.name: Tweede Goudsbloemdwarsstraat
origins.en: The flower, belonging to the family of the composites.

origins.name: Tweede Helmersstraat
origins.en: Jan Frederik Helmers (1767-1813), Amsterdam broker, who devoted himself to the arts. Wrote, among other things, 'De Hollandse Natie' (1813). The second part of the Eerste Helmersstraat was in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel until 1896 and was then called Hofdijkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890). The beginning of this street was originally a short side street of the Nassau quay and was called Sophiapark.

origins.name: Tweede Hugo de Grootstraat
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of International Law. Became involved in church disputes as leader of the Remonstrants and was imprisoned at Loevestein at the request of Prince Maurice. From there, he managed to escape in 1621 through a bookcase.

origins.name: Tweede Jacob van Campenstraat
origins.en: Master builder (1595-1659). Designer of the town hall on the Dam, now a royal palace. However, he was not allowed to complete the work. Van Campen also built the Heiligewegse gate in 1636 and a palace for Prince Frederick Henry in 1657 in Rijswijk. The division into Eerste and Tweede occurred after the intervening part of the street was sold to Heineken Brewery in 1930.

origins.name: Tweede Jan Steenstraat
origins.en: Painter (1626-1679), often painted domestic scenes: cheerful and cluttered interiors. This is how the expression 'a household of Jan Steen' was born.

origins.name: Tweede Jan van der Heijdenstraat
origins.en: Painter and technician (1637-1712), inventor of the snake fire hose and of a new model street lamp. Painter of portraits and cityscapes.

origins.name: Tweede Keucheniusstraat
origins.en: Levinus W.C. Keuchenius (1822-1893), anti-revolutionary statesman. Fierce opponent of the public school. From 1888 to 1890 Minister of Colonies.

origins.name: Tweede Kostverlorenkade
origins.en: To the Kostverloren Wetering, dug in 1413 to obtain a shorter waterway to the Haarlemmer and Leidse lakes. According to some, a reason for the name Kostverloren would be that this waterway, which has been a source of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609, has cost a lot of money in proceedings. The name Kostverloren occurs in various places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Tweede Laurierdwarsstraat
origins.en: The South European ornamental tree

origins.name: Tweede Leeghwaterstraat
origins.en: Jan Adriaansz Leeghwater (1575-1650), civil engineer. Worked as a supervisor and millwright on many drainage works, including the Beemster. Designer of the first plan for draining the Haarlemmermeer.

origins.name: Tweede Leliedwarsstraat
origins.en: The namesake of all these streets is the oldest, namely the Oude Leliestraat, which is already mentioned in 1560. This derives its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Tower lock). The name passed on after 1612 to the canal dug along its extension and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets located in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Tweede Lindendwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the linden (lime tree), a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Tweede Looiersdwarsstraat
origins.en: The tanneries and the leather trade, to which these and the nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal belt are named, were first located outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came within the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after those long-established businesses, starting with the Runstraat and the Huidenstraat. After 1658, the tanneries spread out to areas east of the Vijzelgracht, where we now find the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat. The Third Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision, 1898) for filling in. For the Drowned Nieuwe Looierssloot

origins.name: Tweede Marnixplantsoen
origins.en: Philip of Marnix, lord of Sint Aldegonde (1538-1598), friend and advisor of Prince William of Orange, author of the Union of the Nobles (1568). Possibly poet of the Wilhelmus. The Marnixstraat, formerly called Schans, was laid out after 1850 on the site where the city walls used to be, which were demolished between 1820 and 1840.

origins.name: Tweede Nassaustraat
origins.en: Named after our royal house of Orange-Nassau. The quay was referred to as Buitensingel before the naming in 1879.

origins.name: Tweede Oosterparkstraat
origins.en: Named after the nearby Oosterpark and originally (council decision, 1882) named Eerste, Tweede and Derde Parkstraat. The Eerste Oosterparkstraat previously bore the name Oetgenspad after Frans Hendriks Oetgens, a 16th-century mayor whose land a number of paths were laid out. The street name applied until 1895 until Linnaeusstraat. In the latter year, the street section along the park was named after the park.

origins.name: Tweede Passeerdersdwarsstraat
origins.en: Passing was the preparation and processing of Spanish leather. When this type of leather processing was banned in Amsterdam-Centrum in 1631, this passership settled here next to the already existing leather tanneries.

origins.name: Tweede Rozendwarsstraat
origins.en: Named after the rose, a flower.

origins.name: Tweede Schinkelstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the old amusement park Schinkelhaven. The street was part of the Schinkelkade before 1922.

origins.name: Tweede Sweelinckstraat
origins.en: Jan Pietersz Sweelinck (1562-1621), musician of great fame. Organist of the Old church. Wrote many compositions for the psalms and the love songs. Part of the Tweede Sweelinckstraat was in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1896 as Tweede Hoedemakersdwarsstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1890).

origins.name: Tweede Tuindwarsstraat
origins.en: Garden here has the meaning of shipyard or enclosed space. The street name is derived from the Stadstimmertuin (the City Shipyard), which was located here from 1612 to 1660 (near the Lijnbaansgracht) and where the street ran along.

origins.name: Tweede Van der Helststraat
origins.en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of civic guard and regents' group portraits.

origins.name: Tweede van Swindenstraat
origins.en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor in Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He was part of the Commission to determine the meter, after which he developed the metric system, which was introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

origins.name: Tweede Vogelstraat
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Tweede Weteringdwarsstraat
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed out of the Spui from the outside. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this here. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Sections have been transformed into walking areas (First and Tweede Weteringplantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat.

origins.name: Tweede Weteringplantsoen
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed out of the Spui from the outside. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this here. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Sections have been transformed into walking paths (First and Tweede Weteringplantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat.

origins.name: Tweede Wittenburgerdwarsstraat
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (next to Kattenburg and Oostenburg), built in the second half of the seventeenth century, from the beginning built with shipyards and houses. One of the first shipyards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. Very likely we must look here for the origin of the name Wittenburg.

origins.name: Tweelingenhof
origins.en: The sign of the zodiac.

origins.name: Twellostraat
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Voorst (Gelderland) on the old road Apeldoorn-Deventer. The village is surrounded by a number of estates.

origins.name: Twentestraat
origins.en: The eastern part of the province of Overijssel.

origins.name: Twikkel
origins.en: Castle in Delden (Overijssel), built in 1347, then renovated and expanded several times.

origins.name: Twiskestraat
origins.en: Twiske is the (West) Frisian word for 'between', it refers to the border ditch between the Waterland and the Zaanontginningen. The current recreation area near Oostzaan still bears this name.

origins.name: U.J. Klarenstraat
origins.en: Uilke Jan Klaren (1852-1947), founder of the playground work in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Ubbo Emmiushof
origins.en: Historian (1547-1625). The first rector magnificus of the University of Groningen.

origins.name: Uffizilaan
origins.en: Galleria degli Uffizi in Florence, museum. Most of the building was built between 1560 and 1580. The painting collection is based on the art collection of the de'Medici family. Contains works from the Florentine, Venetian and Dutch school.

origins.name: Uilenburgersteeg
origins.en: The island of Uilenburg, which together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken came to lie within the city in 1593. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known with certainty, but it is likely that the name comes from the swampy land located here, which was called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was created by the merger of the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

origins.name: Uilenburgerwerf
origins.en: The island of Uilenburg, which together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken came to lie within the city in 1593. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known with certainty, but it is likely that the name comes from the swampy land located here, which was called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was created by the merger of the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

origins.name: Uilengouw
origins.en: Owl is the nickname of the Zunderdorpers

origins.name: Uitdammerdijk
origins.en: The hamlet of Uitdam, located on the IJsselmeerdijk north of the municipal boundary. The road came under the name Waterlandse zeedijk in Amsterdam when the former municipality of Ransdorp was abolished in 1921. (Uitdam = outside dam, outside dike.)

origins.name: Uiterwaardenstraat
origins.en: The land along the rivers between the summer and winter dikes, which run underwater in winter.

origins.name: Uitgeeststraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland.

origins.name: Uithoornstraat
origins.en: The North Holland town of Uithoorn is named after this, because at the junction of this street on the Amstel River, the merchant ship of Uithoorn docked.

origins.name: Uitwegpad
origins.en: The Exit was for the construction of the western garden towns of Slotermeer and Osdorp a country road between Osdorperweg and Haarlemmerweg, parallel and west of the former Slotermeer (now Sloterplas). Along this road were a number of farms, which are named in another part of this district.

origins.name: Uiverbrug
origins.en: The Uiver is the name of the legendary KLM aircraft, which participated in the London to Melbourne air race in 1934 and won the first prize in the handicaps section of this race at the time. Like the Uiver, this bridge is also made of aluminum.

origins.name: Ukkelhof
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Uranusstraat
origins.en: The planet.

origins.name: Urkstraat
origins.en: Former island in the Zuiderzee, now located in the Noordoostpolder. The island was bought by Amsterdam in 1660 in connection with the control of the shipping route over the Zuiderzee.

origins.name: Utopia
origins.en: From 'ou topos', Ancient Greek for 'no place'. The concept was introduced in 1516 by the English humanist Thomas More, who in his book Utopia writes about a society of the same name, hypothetical with socialist and communist elements.

origins.name: Utrechtsedwarsstraat
origins.en: To the city of Utrecht. is the new route to Utrecht. The old road ran via Duivendrecht and Abcoude.

origins.name: Utrechtsestraat
origins.en: To the city of Utrecht. The street leads to the Frederiksplein, where the Utrecht Gate used to stand (demolished in 1860). The Nieuwe Utrechtseweg is the new main route to Utrecht. The old road ran via Duivendrecht and Abcoude.

origins.name: Vaalmuiden
origins.en: The English port city of Falmouth, on the south coast of Cornwall, according to a spelling as it appears on Dutch sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Vaalrivierstraat
origins.en: River (side river of the Orange River) that formed the border between Orange Free State and Transvaal. Known for the two Boer Wars of Freedom.

origins.name: Vaartstraat
origins.en: Channel.

origins.name: Valburgdreef
origins.en: Location in Gelderland, located near Nijmegen.

origins.name: Valckenierstraat
origins.en: Gillis Valckenier (1623-1680), nine times mayor of Amsterdam between 1665 and 1680. The street was laid out on the culverted section of the Nieuwe Lijnbaansgracht.

origins.name: Valentijnkade
origins.en: Francois Valentine (1666-1727), preacher and writer in the former Dutch East Indies. He wrote the standard work: Old and New East Indies. He also translated the Bible into Malay.

origins.name: Valeriusplein
origins.en: Adriaan Valerius (1575-1626), notary in Veere. Known for the collection of folk songs he established, still known today as 'Nederlandtsche Gedenckclanck'.

origins.name: Valeriusstraat
origins.en: Adriaan Valerius (1575-1626), notary in Veere. Known for the collection of folk songs he established, still known today as 'Nederlandtsche Gedenckclanck'.

origins.name: Valkenburgerstraat
origins.en: The island of Valkenburg or Marken, which came within the city around 1600. The origin of the name Valkenburg is unknown. It is possible that there was once a house with a facade stone or a shipyard with that name here. A facade stone with Valkenburg also occurs elsewhere (Nieuwendijk 62/68).

origins.name: Valkenisseweg
origins.en: Village that disappeared in January 1862 in a storm surge in the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Valkenstein
origins.en: Lost castle, which stood near Poortugaal on IJsselmonde (South Holland).

origins.name: Valkenweg
origins.en: The raptor. The beginning of the Valkenweg disappeared due to the construction of the IJ tunnel. The Valkenweg bridge was therefore renamed Adelaarsweg-pont (now Meeuwenlaan).

origins.name: Valkhof
origins.en: The Valkhof, located near the Waal Bridge in Nijmegen, was originally founded around 800 by Charlemagne. The castle was rebuilt by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa in 1155 and demolished in 1797, with the exception of the now still remaining Carolingian chapel and some wall remains.

origins.name: Valreep
origins.en: The opening in the obstacle of a ship, where the safety belt strap is attached. Originally, it is the name of a rope ladder (belt = rope).

origins.name: Valschermkade
origins.en: Dutch word for parachute.

origins.name: Valutaboulevard
origins.en: Currency is the general word for currency unit.

origins.name: Van 't Hofflaan
origins.en: Jacobus H. van 't Hoff (1852-1911), chemist. Professor in Amsterdam from 1878 to 1896, then in Berlin. Lay the foundation for stereochemistry. Won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901. This street was transferred from the municipality of Watergraafsmeer in 1921 under the name Koninginnelaan (council decision of Watergraafsneer, 1902).

origins.name: Van Abbestraat
origins.en: The Stedelijk Van Abbemuseum in Eindhoven. The art collector Henri van Abbe donated a museum for contemporary art to Eindhoven in 1936. The collection consisted mainly of works that Van Abbe himself had purchased. Over the years, the museum has built up an important collection with works by Picasso, Chagall, Mondrian and Appel, among others.

origins.name: Van Alphenstraat
origins.en: Hieronymus van Alphen (1746-1803), poet. Gained particular fame through his children's poetry.

origins.name: Van Baerlestraat
origins.en: Caspar van Baerle or Barlaeus (1584-1648), Reformed preacher, from 1632 professor at the Athenaeum. Renowned speaker and writer of Latin poems. Part of this street was originally called Houbrakenstraat (council decision, 1880) and another part Roelof Hartstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1893).

origins.name: Van Beuningenplein
origins.en: Coenraad van Beuningen (1622-1693), mayor of Amsterdam, statesman and envoy to various foreign courts.

origins.name: Van Beuningenstraat
origins.en: Coenraad van Beuningen (1622-1693), mayor of Amsterdam, statesman and envoy to various foreign courts.

origins.name: Van Bleiswijkstraat
origins.en: Pieter van Bleiswijk (1724-1790), statesman. From 1771 to 1787, he was the council pensionary of Holland. He joined the resistance against Stadhouder Willem V and was removed from office in 1787.

origins.name: Van Boetzelaerstraat
origins.en: Pieter Alexander baron van Boetzelaer (1759-1826), one of the mayors of Amsterdam from 1813 to 1824. After 1824, one mayor ruled in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Van Bommel-Van Dampad
origins.en: The Museum Van Bommel Van Dam in Venlo. In 1967, Maarten van Bommel and his wife Reina van Bommel-van Dam donated their art collection to the municipality of Venlo, which was housed in a museum named after the couple in 1971. The collection ranges from paintings and drawings by Dutch artists to wooden sculptures from Africa.

origins.name: Van Boshuizenstraat
origins.en: Koenraad van Boshuizen was bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland from 1515 to 1530.

origins.name: Van Bossestraat
origins.en: Peter Philip van Bosse (1809-1879), liberal statesman. Served as Minister of Finance and Colonies on several occasions. Advocated for free trade.

origins.name: Van Brakelstraat
origins.en: Jan van Brakel (1618-1690), naval officer under Admiral De Ruyter (Four-Day Naval Battle, voyage to Chatham).

origins.name: Van Breestraat
origins.en: Johannes Bernardus van Bree (1801-1857), composer, violinist, conductor and music educator. First conductor of the society Caecilia. Composed cantatas and masses.

origins.name: Van de Sande Bakhuijzenstraat
origins.en: The painter family Van de Sande Bakhuijzen, to which Hendrikus (1795-1860), representative of the romantic school, Julius (1835-1925), painter of cityscapes and landscapes and Gerardine (1826-1895), painter of flowers and fruit belong, among others.

origins.name: Van de Veldestraat
origins.en: The brothers Adriaen van de Velde (1636-1672), landscape painter, and Willem van de Velde (1633-1707), painter of seascapes.

origins.name: Van der Boechorststraat
origins.en: Lord Floris van der Boechorst, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland from 1340 to 1347.

origins.name: Van der Duijnstraat
origins.en: Adam F.J.A. Count van der Duijn van Maesdam (1771-1848). One of the trio (with Van Hogendorp and Van Limburg Stirum) who took charge of the government in 1813 and prepared for the restoration of the rule of the stadtholder's family.

origins.name: Van der Helstplein
origins.en: Bartholomeus van der Helst (1612-1670), painter of civic guard and regents' group portraits.

origins.name: Van der Hoopstraat
origins.en: Joan Cornelis van der Hoop (1742-1825), after the revolution of 1813 chairman of the provisional government of Amsterdam. In 1814 minister of the Navy.

origins.name: Van der Pekstraat
origins.en: Jan Ernst van der Pek (1865-1919), architect. Designed several blocks of workers' housing, mainly in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Van der Vijverstraat
origins.en: Cornelis van der Vijver (1789-1855), historian, in particular of old Amsterdam.

origins.name: Van Diemenkade
origins.en: Anthony van Diemen (1593-1645), Amsterdam merchant, who was governor-general of Dutch East Indies from 1636 to 1645. Together with Tasman, he discovered New Holland (Australia) and Van Diemen's Land. The street was laid out on the former Barentskade (council decision, 1878).

origins.name: Van Diemenstraat
origins.en: Anthony van Diemen (1593-1645), Amsterdam merchant, who was governor-general of Dutch East Indies from 1636 to 1645. Together with Tasman, he discovered New Holland (Australia) and Van Diemen's Land. The street was laid out on the former Barentskade (council decision, 1878).

origins.name: Van Eeghenlaan
origins.en: Christiaan Pieter van Eeghen (1816-1889), Amsterdam merchant, president-commissioner of the Nederlandsche Bank. Initiator of the construction of Vondelpark.

origins.name: Van Eeghenstraat
origins.en: Christiaan Pieter van Eeghen (1816-1889), Amsterdam merchant, president-commissioner of the Nederlandsche Bank. Initiator of the construction of Vondelpark.

origins.name: Van Effenstraat
origins.en: Justus van Effen (1684-1735), literary scholar. He supervised, among other things, the first Dutch translation of Defoe's 'Robinson Crusoe'.

origins.name: Van Gentstraat
origins.en: Willem J. baron van Gent (1626-1672), vice admiral. Rowed up the Thames in 1667 and captured the English admiral's ship (Chatham). Died in the Battle of Solebay in 1672. The street came to Amsterdam in 1921 under the name Piet Heinstraat (council decision of Sloten, 1910).

origins.name: Van Gilsestraat
origins.en: Maarten van Gilse (1918-1943), resistance fighter, born in Munich, executed in Amsterdam, and Jan Hendrik van Gilse (1912-1944), resistance fighter, born in Munich, executed in The Hague.

origins.name: Van Hallstraat
origins.en: Floris Adriaan van Hall (1791-1866), Amsterdam lawyer. As Minister of Finance in 1844 took drastic measures to reduce the enormous national debt. In 1848 leader of the conservative opposition.

origins.name: Van Hanxleden Houwertstraat
origins.en: Johan Coenraad H.F. van Hanxleden Houwert (1906-1945), resistance fighter, born in Medemblik, executed by firing squad in Limmen (North Holland).

origins.name: Van Heemskerckstraat
origins.en: Jacob van Heemskerck (1567-1607), sailor who was sent from Amsterdam in 1596 to search for a sea route to India 'around the north'. See also Barentszstraat. Heemskerck later became an admiral and died at Gibraltar against the Spanish. He is buried in the Old Church.

origins.name: Van Heenvlietlaan
origins.en: Jan van Heenvliet, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland 1396/1397.

origins.name: Van Helt Stocadestraat
origins.en: Nicolaas van Helt Stocade (1615-1669), painter, mainly of portraits.

origins.name: Van Hilligaertstraat
origins.en: Paulus van Hilligaert (1595-1640), painter.

origins.name: Van Hogendorpplein
origins.en: Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp (1762-1834), liberal statesman, pensioner of Rotterdam. Prepared with Van der Duyn van Maasdam and Van Limburg Stirum the restoration of Dutch independence after the fall of Napoleon. Chairman of the Constitutional Commission.

origins.name: Van Hogendorpstraat
origins.en: Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp (1762-1834), liberal statesman, pensioner of Rotterdam. Prepared with Van der Duyn van Maasdam and Van Limburg Stirum the restoration of Dutch independence after the fall of Napoleon. Chairman of the Constitutional Commission.

origins.name: Van Houweningenstraat
origins.en: Elsje van Houweningen, Hugo de Groot's valet, who helped him escape from Loevestein Castle by bookcase in 1621.

origins.name: Van Karnebeekstraat
origins.en: Mr. Abraham Pieter Cornelis van Karnebeek (1836-1925), statesman, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Vice-Chairman of the First Hague Peace Conference and Chairman of the Carnegie Foundation and Mr. Herman Adriaan van Karnebeek (1874-1942), statesman, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Chairman of the League of Nations Assembly and designer of the Belgian treaty.

origins.name: Van Kinsbergenstraat
origins.en: Jan Hendrik van Kinsbergen (1735-1819), admiral during the Battle of Doggersbank in 1781. Reorganized the navy.

origins.name: Van Koetsveldstraat
origins.en: Cornelis Eliza van Koetsveld (1807-1893), preacher and writer. His 'Religious and Moral Novellas' denounced the misery of emerging capitalism. His most famous novel is 'The Pasture of Mastland'.

origins.name: Van Leijenberghlaan
origins.en: Arent van Leyenbergh, around 1400 bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland.

origins.name: Van Limburg Stirumplein
origins.en: Leopold Count of Limburg Stirum (1758-1840), captain of the State army. In 1813 he took over the provisional government with Van Hogendorp and Van der Duyn van Maasdam and prepared the arrival of King William I.

origins.name: Van Limburg Stirumstraat
origins.en: Leopold Count of Limburg Stirum (1758-1840), captain of the State army. In 1813 he took over the provisional government with Van Hogendorp and Van der Duyn van Maasdam and prepared the arrival of King William I.

origins.name: Van Linschotenstraat
origins.en: Jan Huygen van Linschoten (1563-1611), well-known sailor and explorer. Wrote several travel stories about East and West Indies.

origins.name: Van Marumstraat
origins.en: Martinus van Marum (1750-1837), physician and mathematician. Developed an electroplating machine and wrote a dissertation on fluid movement in plants. Since 1784 director of the Teylers Foundation.

origins.name: Van Middellandtstraat
origins.en: Pieter van Middellandt, rear admiral, fought under Admiral De Ruyter at Etna in 1676. Died in the same year in the Battle of Palermo.

origins.name: Van Miereveldstraat
origins.en: Michiel J. van Miereveld (1567-1641), portrait painter.

origins.name: Van Mierlobrug
origins.en: Henricus Antonius Franciscus Maria Oliva (Hans) van Mierlo (Breda, August 18, 1931 - Amsterdam, March 11, 2010) Dutch journalist and politician. In 1966, together with Hans Gruijters, he was the main initiator of the establishment of the social liberal party Democrats '66. For this party, he served as political leader for two separate periods and was a member of both the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors. In the 1980s, he was also Minister of Defense in the Van Agt II and III cabinets and from 1994 to 1998, he was Minister of Foreign Affairs and Vice Prime Minister in the 'purple' Kok I cabinet, which was partly due to him.

origins.name: Van Moerkerkenstraat
origins.en: Pieter Hendrik van Moerkerken (1877-1951), literary critic and art critic. He was a professor at the Academy of Fine Arts in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Van Mourik Broekmanstraat
origins.en: Gerrit H. van Mourik Broekman (1875-1948), civil engineer. From 1900 professor in Santiago (Chile) and advisor to the Chilean government. From 1924 professor in Delft.

origins.name: Van Musschenbroekstraat
origins.en: Petrus van Musschenbroek (1692-1761), physicist, professor in London, Utrecht and Leiden. He showed the length increase of a heated rod.

origins.name: Van Neckstraat
origins.en: Jacob van Neck (1564-1638), Dutch admiral, who made two trips to the Moluccas for the Dutch East India Company, laying the foundations for Dutch trade in East India. After that, he was mayor of Amsterdam several times.

origins.name: Van Nijenrodeweg
origins.en: Gijsbrecht van Nijenrode, in 1357-1358 bailiff of Amstelland, Waterland and Gooiland. A part of the road was abandoned in 1986 due to the construction of the Beysterveld street.

origins.name: Van Noordtkade
origins.en: Olivier van Noordt (1558-1627), sailor and ship captain, who sailed around the world via the Strait of Magellan from 1598 to 1601. He later documented this journey.

origins.name: Van Noordtstraat
origins.en: Olivier van Noordt (1558-1627), sailor and ship captain, who sailed around the world via the Strait of Magellan from 1598 to 1601. He later documented this journey.

origins.name: Van Oldenbarneveldtplein
origins.en: Van Oldenbarneveldt (1547-1619), statesman, council pensionary of Holland. He gave the impetus for the establishment of the United East India Company. After many years of cooperation with Prince Maurice, he came into conflict and finally ended his life on the scaffold.

origins.name: Van Oldenbarneveldtstraat
origins.en: Van Oldenbarneveldt (1547-1619), statesman, council pensionary of Holland. He gave the impetus for the establishment of the United East India Company. After many years of cooperation with Prince Maurice, he came into conflict and finally ended his life on the scaffold.

origins.name: Van Ollefenstraat
origins.en: Daan van Ollefen (1824-1900) and Christina da Silva (1809-1881), a theatrical actors' couple. Mrs. Van Ollefen-da Silva was one of the three stars of the Leidseplein.

origins.name: Van Ostadestraat
origins.en: Adriaan van Ostade (1610-1685), painter of peasant life. The section between Amsteldijk and Sweelinckstraat used to be called Hoedemakersstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1883) and numbered from Amsteldijk, as Kuipersstraat and other nearby streets that were laid out before 1896 by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel are still numbered today. When this section was named in the Van Ostadestraat in 1904, it had to be renumbered.

origins.name: Van Rappardstraat
origins.en: Willem Louis C. Ridder van Rappard (1798-1862), statesman. In 1847 Minister of Finance.

origins.name: Van Reedestraat
origins.en: Hendrik Adriaan van Reede tot Drakenstein (1636-1693), from an aristocratic family in Utrecht, left in 1656 in service of the VOC for Asia. There he studied the tropical flora to improve the supply of medicines.

origins.name: Van Reenenstraat
origins.en: Mr. Gerlach Cornelis Joannes van Reenen (1818-1893), mayor from 1850 to 1853, then minister of the Interior until 1856, and then chairman of the House of Representatives for many years and member of the Council of State.

origins.name: Van Reigersbergenstraat
origins.en: Maria van Reigersbergen (1589-1643), wife of Hugo de Groot.

origins.name: Van Rensselaerstraat
origins.en: Kiliaen van Rensselaer (1580-1646), jeweler, member of the Amsterdam chamber of the West India Company. Founded the colony of Rensselaerswijk near New Amsterdam (New York).

origins.name: Van Riebeeckhavenweg
origins.en: Jan Anthonie van Riebeeck or Riebeek (1618-1708), founded the Cape Colony at Cape de Goede Hoop in 1652, when he was in service of the Dutch East India Company.

origins.name: Van Slingelandtplein
origins.en: Simon van Slingelandt (1666-1736), secretary of the Council of State from 1690 to 1725 and council pensionary from 1727 to 1736. Strived for improvement of the state structure. Wrote his political writings consisting of four parts.

origins.name: Van Slingelandtstraat
origins.en: Simon van Slingelandt (1666-1736), secretary of the Council of State from 1690 to 1725 and council pensionary from 1727 to 1736. Strived for improvement of the state structure. Wrote his political writings consisting of four parts.

origins.name: Van Speijkstraat
origins.en: Jan Carel Josephus van Speyk (1802-1831), an Amsterdam orphan boy, who became a naval officer. During the Belgian uprising in 1831, he had his ship flown into the air near Antwerp because he refused to surrender.

origins.name: Van Spilbergenstraat
origins.en: Joris van Spilbergen (1568-1620), sailor. Made a round-the-world voyage from 1614 to 1617.

origins.name: Van Suchtelen van de Haarestraat
origins.en: Mr. Anthon Hendrik Peter Karel van Suchtelen van de Haare (1869-1946), last mayor of the municipality of Sloten (1909-1921).

origins.name: Van Swindendwarsstraat
origins.en: Jean Henri van Swinden (1746-1823), philosopher, mathematician and physicist, professor in Franeker and from 1785 in Amsterdam. He was part of the Commission to determine the meter, after which he developed the metric system, which was introduced in the Netherlands in 1816.

origins.name: Van Tuyll van Serooskerkenplein
origins.en: Frederik W.C.H. baron van Tuyll van Serooskerken (1851-1924), the first chairman of the Dutch Olympic Committee.

origins.name: Van Tuyll van Serooskerkenweg
origins.en: Frederik W.C.H. baron van Tuyll van Serooskerken (1851-1924), the first chairman of the Dutch Olympic Committee.

origins.name: Van Walbeeckstraat
origins.en: Johannes van Walbeeck (1601-1649), sea captain of the West Indian Company. Leader of the expedition to conquer Curaçao (1634).

origins.name: Van Woustraat
origins.en: Geert van Wou (1460-1524), famous bellfounder from Kampen.

origins.name: Van Zeggelaarstraat
origins.en: Gerrit van Zeggelaar (1868-1934), writer and publicist. Gained fame through his publications and lectures on Waterland. The street was transferred from the municipality of Landsmeer on 1-8-1966 with the names Thorbeckestraat, Borgesiusstraat and Groen van Prinstererstraat.

origins.name: Vancouverstraat
origins.en: George Vancouver (1758-1790), English sailor. He was the first to sail around the island named after him (off the west coast of Canada).

origins.name: Varenweg
origins.en: Plant family, which reproduces by spores.

origins.name: Varikstraat
origins.en: Former municipality on the Waal, in the Tielerwaard (Gelderland). Now falls under the municipality of Neerijnen.

origins.name: Varkenssluis
origins.en: This bridge is named after the pig market, which was held here in the sixteenth century

origins.name: Vasco da Gamastraat
origins.en: Portuguese explorer (1469-1524), found the sea route around Cape of Good Hope in 1497.

origins.name: Vätternkade
origins.en: The second largest lake in Sweden, located in the south of the country.

origins.name: Vechtstraat
origins.en: The river that flows into the IJsselmeer near Muiden.

origins.name: Veelaan
origins.en: Named after the former livestock market.

origins.name: Veemarkt
origins.en: Named after the former livestock market.

origins.name: Veemkade
origins.en: Company that takes goods into custody and operates warehouses. The Dutch vemen grew out of the seventeenth-century daring carriers' guilds.

origins.name: Veenbesstraat
origins.en: Red, sometimes white currant, with a fresh taste. There are two types: the small bog currant and the cranberry. The first grows in upland bog areas, the second is common on Terschelling, after a barrel of cranberries washed ashore there in the mid-nineteenth century.

origins.name: Veenendaalplein
origins.en: Location in the Gelderse Valley (Utrecht).

origins.name: Veerstraat
origins.en: A ferry is a place where - and a boat with which - one is taken across a waterway.

origins.name: Veeteeltstraat
origins.en: The sector of the agricultural company that deals with the keeping (and breeding) of livestock.

origins.name: Vegastraat
origins.en: The star Vega or Wega in the constellation Lyra. One of the brightest stars in the northern sky.

origins.name: Velazquezstraat
origins.en: Diego Rodriguez de Silvary Velazquez (1599-1660). Spanish painter of historical works and portraits.

origins.name: Veldbiesstraat
origins.en: Grass species. Mainly found on the northern hemisphere.

origins.name: Veldhuizenstraat
origins.en: Village in the municipality of Vleuten-de Meern (Utrecht).

origins.name: Veldzicht
origins.en: Farm on the former Uitweg, demolished for the construction of the western garden towns. Before 1975, this street was called Heijningspad (council decision, 1958), which was withdrawn when the name of the Heining was given.

origins.name: Velserweg
origins.en: The North Holland municipality of Velsen, where the North Sea Canal was dug through the dunes. The road ran, until the excavation of the Van Riebeeckhaven, from Sloterdijk to the municipal border and had the names Middenweg (Grote IJpolder) and Frogerweg before the naming in 1938.

origins.name: Veluwelaan
origins.en: Part of the province of Gelderland between the Gelderse Valley and the Gelderse IJssel.

origins.name: Venetiëhof
origins.en: Italian port city, on which the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a scheduled service.

origins.name: Venetiëstraat
origins.en: Italian port city, on which the former KNSM (see KNSM-laan) maintained a scheduled service.

origins.name: Venhuizenstraat
origins.en: The village between Hoorn and Enkhuizen (North Holland).

origins.name: Vennepluimstraat
origins.en: Type of reed.

origins.name: Verbindingsdam
origins.en: Dam in Ertshaven

origins.name: Verbindingstraat
origins.en: The names express the function. The dam is the connection between the IJ island, which was built in 1898, and the Handelskade. The street was built even before the major annexation of 1896, to enable the residents of Nieuwer-Amstel, who lived here on the edge of Amsterdam, to reach their town hall on the Amsteldijk on their own territory.

origins.name: Verdistraat
origins.en: Giuseppe Verdi (1813-1901), Italian opera composer. Composed among others 'Aida', 'Rigoletto' and 'La Traviata'.

origins.name: Verfstraat
origins.en: Reference to the Vettewinkel paint factory, later Sigma, which was located on the Cruquiusterrein from 1934 to 2008.

origins.name: Verlengde Stellingweg
origins.en: A stelling is a loop supported by supports around a high mill. From this loop the mill is watered and the sails are taken in. In 1976, for traffic technical reasons, part of the Stellingweg was renamed Molenaarsweg, while another part was added to Appelweg.

origins.name: Verleunstraat
origins.en: Johannes Adrianus Jozef Verleun (1919-1944), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed in The Hague.

origins.name: Veronesestraat
origins.en: Paolo Cagliari, called Veronese (1528-1588), Italian painter of large decorative canvases.

origins.name: Vertrouwen
origins.en: Vertrouwen in achieving the stated goal.

origins.name: Verversstraat
origins.en: This occupational name reminds us of the linen industry, an important industry in Amsterdam in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The linen merchants were only allowed to settle between the Kloveniersburgwal and the Zwanenburgwal after 1593. The Groenburgwal was called Verversgracht at that time.

origins.name: Vervoorenstraat
origins.en: Louis Christiaan Vervooren (1895-1944), resistance fighter, born in Rotterdam, killed in Bruttig (Germany).

origins.name: Vespuccistraat
origins.en: Amerigo Vespucci (1451- 1512), Florentine explorer. He sailed and described the American coasts. It is likely that America was named after him and not after Columbus.

origins.name: Vianenstraat
origins.en: Fortified town on the Lek (South Holland).

origins.name: Victor Rutgersstraat
origins.en: Victor Henri Rutgers (1877-1945), resistance fighter, killed in the Bochum concentration camp (Germany). Rutgers was a lawyer and statesman, Minister of Education in 1925 and from 1928 professor at the Vrije Universiteit in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Victoria Welbystraat
origins.en: Victoria Welby (1837 – 1912) was a prominent British philosopher and linguist

origins.name: Victorieplein
origins.en: The square was named this in 1946 in connection with the victory of the Allied countries. Previously it was called Daniël Willinkplein, after the poet (1676-1722), known for his Amstellandse Arcadia. (council decision, 1922).

origins.name: Vier Heemskinderensluis
origins.en: This bridge is named after the facade stone with the Vier Heemskinderen on the corner building of the Herengracht and the Leidsegracht.

origins.name: Vier Heemskinderenstraat
origins.en: Named after the facade stone with the Vier Heemskinderen on the corner building of the Herengracht and the Leidsegracht.

origins.name: Vierde Vogelstraat
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Viermasterstraat
origins.en: A sailing ship, usually a barque, with four masts.

origins.name: Vierwindendwarsstraat
origins.en: This peculiar name is probably derived from a facade stone of a house or warehouse, which stood here on the Realeneiland. Such a stone gave the house on the Lindengracht the name of ''t huis in de vier blazende winden'.

origins.name: Vierwindenstraat
origins.en: This peculiar name is probably derived from a facade stone of a house or warehouse, which stood here on the Realeneiland. Such a stone gave the house on the Lindengracht the name of ''t huis in de vier blazende winden'.

origins.name: Vijfde Vogelstraat
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Vijgepeerpad
origins.en: Old Dutch pear variety. The path is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Vijverhoef
origins.en: Old knight's manor house under Breukelen on the Vecht, originally from 1670, demolished in 1812. Sung by Vondel. The current Vijverhof, on the same site, dates from 1867.

origins.name: Vijzelgracht
origins.en: The name is probably derived from the former inhabitants Cornelis Arents Vijselaar (around 1600) and Jan Vijselaar (around 1632). Vijzelstraat was then a short street and ran to the current Reguliersdwarsstraat. When the street was extended, the name also passed on to this extension. Until the eighteenth century, people spoke of Old and New Vijzelstraat. The Vijzelgracht, dug between 1660 and 1670, was filled in in 1934.

origins.name: Vijzelstraat
origins.en: The name is probably derived from the former inhabitants Cornelis Arents Vijselaar (around 1600) and Jan Vijselaar (around 1632). The Vijzelstraat was then a short street and ran to the current Reguliersdwarsstraat. When the street was extended, the name also passed on to this extension. Until the eighteenth century, people spoke of Old and New Vijzelstraat. The Vijzelgracht, dug between 1660 and 1670, was filled in 1934.

origins.name: Vikingpad
origins.en: Collective name for groups of adventurers, exiles, merchants, settlers from Denmark, Norway and Sweden, who made the coasts of 'Friesland' unsafe in particular in the ninth century.

origins.name: Vilvoordestraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Vincent van Goghstraat
origins.en: Vincent Willem van Gogh (1853-1890) painter and draughtsman. Initially worked in the Borinage and Drenthe, before leaving for France in 1886, where he produced most and most famous paintings. He has been of great significance for the development of painting.

origins.name: Vinkenstraat
origins.en: The strip south of the Haarlemmerdijk, between the current Binnen Oranjestraat and the Haarlemmerplein, was called the Rietvink in the sixteenth century after an old inn. The street laid out here in the seventeenth century was alternately called Rietstraat, Vinkenstraat and Middenstraat. Of these, the name Vinkenstraat finally remained. In 1566, the first public sermon was held for the Protestants on the Rietvink. Within the city, this was not yet allowed at that time.

origins.name: Violette Corneliushof
origins.en: Photographer (1919-1998). Became involved in the artist resistance during World War II. Worked for the illegal magazine 'De Vrije Kunstenaar' and later for the Persoonsbewijzen Centrale. After the war, she developed into an architecture photographer and eventually chose reportage photography.

origins.name: Violettenstraat
origins.en: An outdated name for the flower the violet.

origins.name: Virginiahof
origins.en: Virginia Dementricia, later Virginia Gaai (Aruba, 1842 - after 1867), was a slave and who rebelled against her owners in Aruba. She repeatedly violated the rules imposed on her and was punished with forced labor every time. In 1859 she tried to run away but failed and resulted in more heavy labor and a prison sentence. Shortly after her release, Virginia was arrested again and accused of 'street disorder and resistance to the police'. This time she received a life sentence. Her owner sold her in 1860. In 1863 slavery was abolished. The last thing known about her is that she gave birth to a son in Willemstad on June 2, 1867: Marcelino Martis Gaai.

origins.name: Virginiastraat
origins.en: Virginia Dementricia, later Virginia Gaai (Aruba, 1842 - after 1867), was a slave and who rebelled against her owners in Aruba. She repeatedly violated the rules imposed on her and was punished with forced labor every time. In 1859 she tried to run away but failed and resulted in more heavy labor and a prison sentence. Shortly after her release, Virginia was arrested again and accused of 'street disorder and resistance to the police'. This time she received a life sentence. Her owner sold her in 1860. In 1863 slavery was abolished. The last thing known about her is that she gave birth to a son in Willemstad on June 2, 1867: Marcelino Martis Gaai.

origins.name: Visseringstraat
origins.en: Simon Vissering (1818-1888), professor of political science in Leiden, Minister of Finance. He already campaigned in 1848 for IJmuiden as a new seaport.

origins.name: Viveportenstraat
origins.en: Kapeldorp on Terschelling, disappeared in the sixteenth century due to storm surges.

origins.name: Vlaardingenlaan
origins.en: City in South Holland, on the Nieuwe Maas.

origins.name: Vlaggemast
origins.en: The ship's mast to which the flag is attached.

origins.name: Vlakkerweg
origins.en: Occupational name for someone who flattens metal with a sledgehammer, that is, makes it smooth. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Vleutenstraat
origins.en: Location in Utrecht.

origins.name: Vliegtuigstraat
origins.en: The means of transport through the air, using surfaces (wings).

origins.name: Vlielandstraat
origins.en: Wadden island (Friesland).

origins.name: Vlierweg
origins.en: Plant, with white flowers and black berries.

origins.name: Vlietstraat
origins.en: Drainage channel.

origins.name: Vlimmerenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Vlothavenweg
origins.en: The nearby Vlothaven, dug in 1931, was originally shallow and part of the timber port intended for timber barges. Around 1960, the harbor was deepened and adapted for sea vessels.

origins.name: Vluchthavenbrug
origins.en: Probably named after that part of the harbor where small ships could dock in case of bad weather.

origins.name: VOC-kade
origins.en: The United East India Company (VOC), founded in 1602 for trade in East India. The management was in the hands of seventeen directors. From Batavia, the administrative Amsterdam-Centrum Asia, a network of trading settlements was established. In 1799 the state took over the company.

origins.name: Voetbalstraat
origins.en: Refers to the sports park that was here with football clubs

origins.name: Voetboogstraat
origins.en: The street was laid out on the shooting range of the Doelen der Voetboogschutters in 1649.

origins.name: Vogelenzangstraat
origins.en: Village in the dune area, on the edge of the Amsterdam waterworks dunes.

origins.name: Vogelkade
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Vogelplantsoen
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Vogelplein
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Volendammerweg
origins.en: Village southeast of Edam, known for its traditional clothing.

origins.name: Volewijkshof
origins.en: The peninsula north of the IJ, directly opposite the center of Amsterdam. As early as 1360, there was a gallows field here, where the bodies of executed people were hung and exhibited. After the arrival of the Batavian Republic in 1795, this practice was prohibited.

origins.name: Volharding
origins.en: Volharding in pursuit of the goal.

origins.name: Volkerakstraat
origins.en: Water between Overflakkee and North Brabant, which was closed off from Haringvliet and Hollands Diep (Hellegatsplein) by a dam in 1970.

origins.name: Voltaplein
origins.en: Alessandro Volta (1745-1827). Italian physicist, professor at Pavia. Made several inventions in the field of electricity. A unit of electrical voltage is named after him, the 'Volt'.

origins.name: Voltastraat
origins.en: Alessandro Volta (1745-1827). Italian physicist, professor at Pavia. Made several inventions in the field of electricity. A unit of electrical voltage is named after him, the 'Volt'.

origins.name: Von Guerickestraat
origins.en: Otto von Guericke (1602-1682), German physicist, inventor of the air pump and the electrostat machine. They are named after him the Maagdenburger (half) spheres, for demonstrating the effect of atmospheric pressure (Von Guericke was mayor of Magdeburg). The street was originally named Wolmaranstraat, established by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer (council decision, 1915). In 1922, all the streets in this neighborhood were given different names.

origins.name: Von Humboldtstraat
origins.en: Alexander baron von Humboldt (1769-1859), natural scientist and scientific explorer. Traveled South America and Siberia. Founder of climatology and plant geography.

origins.name: Von Liebigweg
origins.en: Justus von Liebig (1803-1873), German chemist. Researcher of artificial fertilization. He invented a method for the preparation of meat extract.

origins.name: Von Zesenstraat
origins.en: Philipp von Zesen (1619-1689), German historian. He wrote, among other things, 'Beschreibung der Stadt Amsterdam'.

origins.name: Vondelbrug
origins.en: Joost van den Vondel (1587-1679) was a poet who wrote many tragic plays, the most famous of which is 'Gijsbrecht van Aemstel'.

origins.name: Vondelkerkstraat
origins.en: The street was taken over by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under this name. A decision to name it by that municipality and the reason why has not been found. The Vondelkerk, built in 1873 under the architecture of Pierre Cuypers, is about a kilometer away from here and therefore cannot have been the reason for the naming of this street.

origins.name: Vondelpark
origins.en: Joost van den Vondel (1587-1679), poet. He wrote 24 tragedies, as well as poetry on heroes and heroic deeds. The part of the street that was in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1896 was first called Verlengde Vondelstraat. Under the leadership of C.P. van Eeghen, a number of Amsterdamers designed the plan for the construction of a Riding and Walking Park in 1864, and then carried it out according to a design by L.D. Zocher. The first part was opened in 1865. When a statue of Vondel was placed here in 1867, the park was renamed Vondelpark.

origins.name: Vondelstraat
origins.en: Joost van den Vondel (1587-1679), poet. He wrote 24 tragedies, as well as poetry on heroes and heroic deeds. The part of the street that was in the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel before 1896 was first called Verlengde Vondelstraat. Under the leadership of C.P. van Eeghen, a number of Amsterdamers designed the plan for the construction of a Riding and Walking Park in 1864, and then carried it out according to a design by L.D. Zocher. The first part was opened in 1865. When a statue of Vondel was placed here in 1867, the park was named Vondelpark.

origins.name: Voorburgstraat
origins.en: Village in South Holland, suburb of The Hague.

origins.name: Voordek
origins.en: One of the ship decks.

origins.name: Voordewind
origins.en: Ship term, in particular in sailing: the wind directly from behind. The term is also used figuratively a lot.

origins.name: Voorlandpad
origins.en: Former manor house on the Middenweg, built in 1689 as Meerenburg, renamed Voorland in 1722. The manor house was demolished in 1934 to make way for the Ajax stadium De Meer.

origins.name: Voormalige Stadstimmertuin
origins.en: From 1660 to 1899, the City Timberyards were located here (timber workshops and storage facilities for building materials). Today, this site is located on Van Reigersbergenstraat.

origins.name: Voornestraat
origins.en: The western part of the South Holland island of Voorne-Putten.

origins.name: Voorsteven
origins.en: The front part of the ship's hull.

origins.name: Voorthuizenstraat
origins.en: The village in the municipality of Barneveld (Gelderland).

origins.name: Vorselaarstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Vorticellaweg
origins.en: Microscopically small aquatic creature. Single-celled ciliate with a bell-shaped head and a contractile stalk.

origins.name: Vosmaerstraat
origins.en: Carel Vosmaer (1826-1888), writer and critic. Clerk at the Court of The Hague, then of the Supreme Court. Originally a classicist, later supported the movement of the Eighties. Wrote among other things 'Nanno', and a translation of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

origins.name: Vossenbesstraat
origins.en: Also known as red currant. Plant from the heath family, native to the Netherlands, and growing in dry soil. The foxberry is usually processed into compote due to its sour, slightly bitter taste.

origins.name: Vossiusstraat
origins.en: Gerardus Johannes Voss, calling himself Vossius (1577-1649), philologist and historian, professor successively in Heidelberg, Leiden and from 1631 together with Barlaeus at the Amsterdam Athenaeum. His textbook on rhetoric (1648) had a great influence.

origins.name: Vredeman de Vriesstraat
origins.en: Jan Vredeman de Vries (1527-1606), architect and painter, also worked in several foreign cities. Through his designs, books and engravings, he spread the Dutch Renaissance.

origins.name: Vredenburgerbrug
origins.en: Catholic nursing home Vredenburg was built, now converted into houses. Before the inn, there were successively

origins.name: Vredenburgersteeg
origins.en: In the seventeenth century a very well-known inn, which stood on the site where in 1835 the Roman Catholic nursing home Vredenburg was built. Now converted into houses. Before the inn, there was successively a brewery owned by mayor Kornelis Jacobsz and a saltworks. Hence the former names Cornelis Jacobsz Brouwersteeg and Zoutkoperssteeg. The name Rottenest also came up.

origins.name: Vredenhofpad
origins.en: Named after the adjacent Vredenhof cemetery on the Haarlemmerweg.

origins.name: Vredenhofweg
origins.en: Named after the adjacent Vredenhof cemetery on the Haarlemmerweg.

origins.name: Vredespleintje
origins.en: The name was chosen in 2016 by the residents and refers to the theme of 'peace' about which at least thirteen eighteenth and nineteenth-century writers named in the neighborhood have written. In the past, the square was the place for the Solidarity Festival, and in 2010 for the festival 'World Citizens of Amsterdam'.

origins.name: Vreelandplein
origins.en: Village on the Vecht (Utrecht). The castle of the same name was demolished in 1529 at the request of Charles V.

origins.name: Vreeswijkpad
origins.en: Utrecht town on the Lek, opposite Vianen. Now part of the municipality of Nieuwegein.

origins.name: Vriesseveem
origins.en: A veem is a company responsible for storing and delivering goods in and out of its warehouses. The veems each had their own license plate, after which they were named. These could be different colors and models of hats (e.g. Blue hats, Clogs). They also derived their name from the origin of the workers (e.g. Vriesseveem, Zeeuwse Veem).

origins.name: Vrijburg
origins.en: Former country house on the Haarlemmerweg.

origins.name: Vrije Geer
origins.en: Old name of part of the municipality of Sloten, a triangular area, that extended from the southeast corner of the Slotermeer to the Haarlemmermeer. The area was outside the jurisdiction (1100 rods) of Amsterdam. The inhabitants of the Vrije Geer were traditionally exempt from paying certain fines to the counts of Holland.

origins.name: Vrijheidslaan
origins.en: This lane, which originally was called Amstellaan, was changed to Stalinlaan after World War II, after the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, because the Soviet Union together with the Allies achieved our liberation. After the Russian intervention in the Hungarian uprising in 1956, the name was changed to Vrijheidslaan.

origins.name: Vrijzicht
origins.en: Former farm in the old municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Vrolikstraat
origins.en: Gerardus Vrolik (1775-1859) and his son Willem Vrolik (1801-1863), both professors of medicine in Amsterdam. They collected an extensive collection of anatomical preparations. The first part of this street is now called Wibautstraat.

origins.name: Vrouwenmantelstraat
origins.en: Plant, native to Europe, North and West Asia, North America and Greenland. Has been traditionally used, among other things, against severe menstrual pain and menopausal complaints.

origins.name: Vuurwerkerplantsoen
origins.en: A pyrotechnician is a profession or was a profession within the metal industry

origins.name: Vuurwerkerweg
origins.en: Occupational name, someone who works with the glowing metal in a forge.

origins.name: W.J. Bijleveldstraat
origins.en: Wolter Jan Bijleveld (1902-1945), resistance fighter, born in Makassar, died in Vaiklingen (Germany). He was head of the Connections and Intelligence Service of the Order Service (O.D.).

origins.name: W.J. Knoopstraat
origins.en: Lieutenant General (1811-1894), co-founder of the Dutch Red Cross.

origins.name: W.L. Penningstraat
origins.en: Willem Levinus Penning (1840-1924), poet under the pseudonym M. Coens.

origins.name: Waagdragerhof
origins.en: Weighingmen were responsible for weighing goods in the Waag. They carried the goods from the warehouses to the Waag to weigh them.

origins.name: Waaigat
origins.en: Old name for an opening in the canal wall. Wave holes were also there on Warmoesstraat and Rapenburgerstraat.

origins.name: Waalenburgsingel
origins.en: Polder on Texel (north of the village of De Waal). Meadow and swamp lands with extensive fauna and flora.

origins.name: Waalseilandbrug
origins.en: Named after the word 'waal' which means a piece of water surrounded by rows of poles in which ships could overwinter or be repaired

origins.name: Waalstraat
origins.en: Branch of the Rhine from Nijmegen to Gorinchem. Then flows together with the Maas, after which it is called the Merwede.

origins.name: Waddendijk
origins.en: Offshore shallow area, which dries up at low tide, especially in the Wadden Sea.

origins.name: Waddenweg
origins.en: Offshore shallow area, which dries up at low tide, especially in the Wadden Sea.

origins.name: Wagenaarstraat
origins.en: Jan Wagenaar (1709-1773), historian, city historian of Amsterdam, wrote among other things 'Fatherland History' (21 volumes) and a history of Amsterdam in three volumes.

origins.name: Wageningendreef
origins.en: Location in Gelderland.

origins.name: Wagenstraat
origins.en: The name recalls the car park - a place for cars that came from outside the city - near the Regulierspoort.

origins.name: Wakkerstraat
origins.en: Jacobus Philippus van Medenbach Wakker (1784-1860), notary and mayor of the municipality of Watergraafsmeer from 1817 to 1853. The street is named after him, because he lived there.

origins.name: Walborg
origins.en: Seventeenth-century country house, located on the Maas under Laak (Limburg). Today only a ruin remains.

origins.name: Walcherenstraat
origins.en: One of the Zeeuwse islands. Due to the poldering of the Sloe, now completely connected to Zuid-Beveland.

origins.name: Waldeck Pyrmontlaan
origins.en: A former German princely house. This family produced Queen Emma, the second wife of King William III and mother of Queen Wilhelmina.

origins.name: Waldenlaan
origins.en: 'Walden; or, Life in the Woods', philosophical and socially critical book by the American Henry Thoreau from 1854, which describes his Spartan living conditions in a self-built cottage in nature.

origins.name: Walenpleintje
origins.en: The square owes its name to the Old Walloon Church located here. This church is the old monastery church of the former monastery of the Pauls Brothers. The name had already existed unofficially for centuries. The naming took place on the occasion of the celebration of the fourth centenary of the Alteration of May 26, 1578.

origins.name: Wallestein
origins.en: Former seventeenth-century outside, under Loenersloot (Utrecht). Demolished in the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Wally Moespad
origins.en: Wally Moes (1856-1918), painter of genre scenes and portraits, also made etchings.

origins.name: Walraven van Hallweg
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1945), born in Amsterdam, executed in Haarlem.

origins.name: Walvisvaart
origins.en: The Oostzanerwerf was one of the centers of the whaling industry in the 17th and 18th centuries, where generations of commanders and crew members of whaling ships lived. There was also a lot of activity related to whaling.

origins.name: Wamberg
origins.en: Nobility house, whose oldest wing dates back to 1560. Expanded in 1769 and early twentieth century. Located on the Aa outside the village of Berlicum (North Brabant).

origins.name: Wamelplein
origins.en: Village in the Land of Maas and Waal, opposite Tiel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Wamelstraat
origins.en: Village in the Land of Maas and Waal, opposite Tiel (Gelderland).

origins.name: Wannepad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Liège.

origins.name: Wanningstraat
origins.en: Joannes Wanning, musician, born in Kampen, organist at Danzig (Germany/Poland). Lived at the end of the sixteenth century and beginning of the seventeenth century.

origins.name: Ward Bingleystraat
origins.en: Dutch actor of English birth (1757-1818). Often performed in national tragic plays.

origins.name: Waregemstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of West Flanders.

origins.name: Warmelo
origins.en: Fortified noble house under Diepenheim (Overijssel), originally sixteenth and seventeenth century. Restored in 1928. Property of Prince Bernhard and inhabited by his mother Princess Armgard.

origins.name: Warmoesstraat
