origins.en: The current Warmoesstraat had two names until the seventeenth century: Kerkstraat for the northern part up to the Oude Kerk, and Warmoesstraat for the southern part, probably after the radish or vegetable market held here. Later, the entire street was given this name. Finally, in the twentieth century, the part where the Krasnapolsky Hotel is located was added to the Dam.

origins.name: Warmondstraat
origins.en: Location in South Holland, north of Leiden.

origins.name: Warnsborn
origins.en: Former estate, now nature reserve located west of Arnhem.

origins.name: Watergangseweg
origins.en: Village on the North Holland Canal, under Landsmeer.

origins.name: Waterkeringweg
origins.en: Any natural or artificial barrier that holds back the water, such as a dam, dike or lock. The street is located on the former premises of the Municipal Waterworks, in a neighborhood where all streets begin with 'water'.

origins.name: Waterlandplein
origins.en: Waterland is in broad terms the area between Amsterdam, Zaandam, Purmerend and Monnickendam. In fact a large nature reserve.

origins.name: Waterlooplein
origins.en: Named after the Battle of Waterloo in 1815. The square was created in 1874 by filling in the Houtgracht and the Leprozengracht.

origins.name: Watermaalpad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Watermanstraat
origins.en: The constellation and zodiac sign.

origins.name: Waterpoortsteeg
origins.en: Reminiscent of the Waterpoort, formerly a small passage in the city wall as a connection to the Lastage, which was located outside the city at the time.

origins.name: Waterpoortweg
origins.en: Gate in a fence. Defensive work built over a moat. The street is located on the former site of the Municipal Waterworks, in a neighborhood where all streets begin with 'water'.

origins.name: Waterschapstraat
origins.en: A water board is a public legal body that manages the maintenance of flood defenses and the drainage of a certain area.

origins.name: Watervoort
origins.en: Simplified spelling of the Irish port city of Waterford, as it appears on sea charts from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

origins.name: Watteaustraat
origins.en: Jean Antoine Watteau (1684-1721), French painter, painted in Rococo style.

origins.name: Waverstraat
origins.en: River on the border of North Holland and Utrecht.

origins.name: Wedderborg
origins.en: The castle at Wedde (Groningen), originally built in 1362 and rebuilt in 1530 at the behest of Charles of Gelder. The remains of the old wall were exposed in 1957.

origins.name: Weegbreestraat
origins.en: Named after the plantain, a plant.

origins.name: Weegschaalhof
origins.en: The zodiac sign and constellation in the zodiac.

origins.name: Weenahof
origins.en: The Weena Castle, first mentioned in 1306. It was a water castle and was located at the mouth of the Rotte, within the current Rotterdam.

origins.name: Weerdestein
origins.en: Already mentioned in 1340 castle under Nederlangbroek (Utrecht), in 1548 knightly court town. Single square tower, surrounded by three moats, restored in 1870. The gate building dates from 1642.

origins.name: Weerslootpad
origins.en: Common name for canals in North Holland.

origins.name: Weesperplein
origins.en: The street runs in the direction of - and is therefore named after - the city of Weesp. At the end of the street was formerly the Weesperpoort, and along the extension, outside the Singelgracht, the Weesperpoort station (demolished 1939). The buildings along Weesperstraat were demolished between 1950 and 1960, after which it gained its current width.

origins.name: Weesperstraat
origins.en: The street runs in the direction of - and is therefore named after - the city of Weesp. At the end of the street was formerly the Weesperpoort, and along the extension, outside the Singelgracht, the Weesperpoort station (demolished 1939). The buildings along the Weesperstraat were demolished between 1950 and 1960, after which it gained its current width.

origins.name: Weesperzijde
origins.en: The Weesperzijde was already the main route to the direction of Weesp since the drying of the Watergraafsmeer. The name was given to distinguish it from the other side of the Amstel, which was formerly called the Utrechtsezijde (today Amsteldijk).

origins.name: Weidestraat
origins.en: Agricultural concept: the grassland on which livestock farming is carried out. By council decision in 1974, part of the Weidestraat was added to the Gaffelstraat and the Harkstraat.

origins.name: Weissenbruchstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Johannes Weissenbruch (1825-1903), landscape painter, pupil of Andreas Schelfhout.

origins.name: Weissensingel
origins.en: The lake, the Weissensee, located in Carinthia in Austria.

origins.name: Weissmanstraat
origins.en: Adriaan Willem Weissman (1858-1923), Amsterdam architect. Built the Stedelijk Museum (1895) among other things. Founder and first secretary of the Bond Heemschut.

origins.name: Weldam
origins.en: Stately, rising from the water, noble house near Markelo (Overijssel), built in 1644 using medieval masonry. Surrounded by a garden in eighteenth-century style.

origins.name: Welnastraat
origins.en: Former country house on the Amstel

origins.name: Welsumerstraat
origins.en: Welsumer is a less well-known chicken breed, bred from various other breeds and named after the village of Welsum (north of Deventer).

origins.name: Wembleylaan
origins.en: Stadium in London. Ajax won the final of the European Cup for Champions on June 2, 1971 at this stadium. Ajax-Panathinaikos (2-0).

origins.name: Wenslauerstraat
origins.en: This is probably the name of a landowner or construction company that built here. Before 1896, this street belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel under the same name.

origins.name: Werengouw
origins.en: A weir is an elongated plot of land between two boundary ditches. The ditch between two posts is also called a weir ditch. By council decision in 1971, part of the road was added to Buikslotermeerplein.

origins.name: Werfkade
origins.en: Refers to the shipyards that used to be here

origins.name: Werfstraat
origins.en: Refers to the shipyards that used to be here

origins.name: Werkendamstraat
origins.en: Village on the Merwede in the Land of Altena (North Brabant).

origins.name: Werkhovenstraat
origins.en: Village on the Kromme Rijn near Bunnik (Utrecht).

origins.name: Werktuigstraat
origins.en: Tools. The street name refers to the lost shipbuilding activity in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: Wervershoofstraat
origins.en: Village near Medemblik.

origins.name: Wessel Gansfortstraat
origins.en: Johan Wessel Gansfort (1419-1489), biblical humanist, professor in Heidelberg, returned to the Netherlands in 1479. Through his opposition to the indulgence trade and the infallibility of the Pope, he can be considered a precursor of the Reformation.

origins.name: Wessel Ilckenstraat
origins.en: Jazz musician (1923-1957), drummer. From 1950 onwards, he performed with his own formation. Until his death, he was undisputed the driving force of Dutch modern jazz. The annual Dutch jazz grand prize is named after him.

origins.name: Westbroekplein
origins.en: Village under Maartensdijk (Utrecht).

origins.name: Westbroekstraat
origins.en: Village under Maartensdijk (Utrecht).

origins.name: Westeinde
origins.en: Named after its location: west of the Utrechtsepoort. Also

origins.name: Westelijke Merwedekanaaldijk
origins.en: The Merwedekanaal, now the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal, dug between Amsterdam and Vreeswijk, was completed in 1892 after a long ordeal. This canal was against the wishes of Amsterdam and the Chamber of Commerce, which were in favor of a canal through the Gelderse valley.

origins.name: Westerdok
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerdoksdijk
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerdokskade
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerduinenstraat
origins.en: Nature monument on the island of Texel, between Den Hoorn and De Koog. The area includes dunes, gullies and heathlands.

origins.name: Westergasbrug
origins.en: This steel loading bridge is named after the former Westergasfabriek that operated here from 1885 to 1985

origins.name: Westerhoofd
origins.en: The western harbor head of the Coenhaven.

origins.name: Westerkade
origins.en: The quay is located on the west side of the Lijnbaansgracht. This is probably the reason for the naming.

origins.name: Westerkoggestraat
origins.en: Polder in West Friesland.

origins.name: Westerlengte
origins.en: The distance in degrees in a westerly direction, measured from the first meridian.

origins.name: Westermarkt
origins.en: When the square was built in 1616, it was named Keizersmarkt, but with the construction of the Westerkerk, completed in 1630, the square came to be known as Westermarkt in popular parlance and thus displaced the official name Keizersmarkt.

origins.name: Westerpark
origins.en: When it was built, the park was located in the western part of the then-city. The park was built on the site where the first station of the Hollandse Spoor stood from 1843 to 1878. The street was part of the Houtmankade before 1979.

origins.name: Westerstraat
origins.en: The name was given in 1861, when the Anjeliersgracht, as the street was previously called, was filled in. Why it became Westerstraat then is not clear.

origins.name: Westertoegang
origins.en: This bridge is located above the water that forms the western entrance to the IJ

origins.name: Westerwoldestraat
origins.en: Region in the southeastern part of the province of Groningen.

origins.name: Westhavenweg
origins.en: This harbor, dug about half in 1937, was initially called the Fordhaven, but soon gained the unofficial name Westhaven. After the harbor was extended by more than a kilometer to its current length in 1961, the name was also officially established, along with that of other harbors. The later built road therefore bore the name earlier than the harbor.

origins.name: Westlandgracht
origins.en: The area west of Delft, an internationally known horticultural area.

origins.name: Westmallepad
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Westpoortweg
origins.en: Business park and industrial area, near the western harbors of the city.

origins.name: Westrandweg
origins.en: Refers to the western side of Amsterdam

origins.name: Westwouderstraat
origins.en: The village of Westwoud, between Hoorn and Enkhuizen (North Holland).

origins.name: Westzaanstraat
origins.en: Village west of Zaandam (and west of the Zaan).

origins.name: Weteringlaan
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed out of the Spui from the outside. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this here. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Parts have been transformed into walking places (First and Second Wetering Plantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat.

origins.name: Weteringschans
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed out of the Spui from the outside. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this here. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Parts have been transformed into walking places (First and Second Wetering Plantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat.

origins.name: Weteringstraat
origins.en: The streets are located in the Weteringbuurt. The names remind us of the Wetering, which originally flowed out of the Spui from the outside. The Boerenwetering is still a remnant of this. The Schans was formerly the wall on the inside of the city wall. In the first half of the nineteenth century, the walls and embankments were demolished. Parts have been recreated in promenades (First and Second Weteringplantsoen) and a road has been built, which first went by the name of Schans in its full length, but was later renamed Marnixstraat, Weteringschans and Sarphatistraat. The Nieuwe Weteringstraat was built on the site that became available due to the demolition of the Flour and Bread Factory.

origins.name: Wethouder Abrahamspad
origins.en: Ephraim Joseph Abrahams (1875-1954), a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for 23 years, nine of which as a alderman (1919-1921 and 1927-1934).

origins.name: Wethouder de Roosplein
origins.en: Albertus de Roos (1900-1978), for 17 years a member of the Amsterdam City Council for Arts Affairs. In 1962 he took office in the Council of State.

origins.name: Wethouder De Roosplein
origins.en: Albertus de Roos (1900-1978), for 17 years a member of the Amsterdam City Council for Arts Affairs. In 1962 he took office in the Council of State.

origins.name: Wethouder De Vriesplantsoen
origins.en: Simon de Vries (1869-1961), a member of the municipal council for many years, of whom he was alderman from 1908 to 1918.

origins.name: Wethouder Den Hertogstraat
origins.en: Herman Johannes den Hertog (1872-1952), alderman of Amsterdam from 1914 to 1921.

origins.name: Wethouder Driessenstraat
origins.en: Bernard Herman Maria Driessen (1828-1896), alderman of Amsterdam from 1886 to 1891.

origins.name: Wethouder Ed. Polakstraat
origins.en: Eduard Polak (1880-1962), a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for 22 years, eight of which as a alderman (1923-1927 and 1929-1933).

origins.name: Wethouder Frankeweg
origins.en: Bernardus Cornelis Franke (1889-1953), well-known figure in the Amsterdam socialist movement. Wethouder for Labor Affairs from 1939 to 1941 and from 1945 to 1953. After his death, the Nieuweweg (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1904), where he lived for many years, was named after him. A plaque has also been inlaid there.

origins.name: Wethouder in 't Veldstraat
origins.en: Arie in 't Veld (1893-1976), alderman of Amsterdam from 1948 to 1962.

origins.name: Wethouder Insingerstraat
origins.en: Albrecht Fredrik Insinger (1788-1872) was a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for thirty years, seven of which as a alderman (1843-1850).

origins.name: Wethouder Ramstraat
origins.en: Bernard Ram (1894-1982), member of the Municipal Council from 1949 to 1962 and from 1953 to 1958 alderman for Labor Affairs, in which capacity he was confronted with the tram strike of 1953.

origins.name: Wethouder Seegersplein
origins.en: Leendert Seegers (1891-1970), with a break during the war years 1940-1945 for forty years a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for the CPN. From 1945 alderman, but in 1948 dismissed in connection with the discussion around the communist coup in Prague.

origins.name: Wethouder Serrurierstraat
origins.en: Louis Serrurier (1844-1916). During the 26 years he served on the Amsterdam municipal council, he was a alderman for fifteen years.

origins.name: Wethouder Steinmetzstraat
origins.en: Willem Steinmetz (1891-1968), a member of the Amsterdam municipal council for many years (1931-1962), of whom the last fourteen years as a alderman for municipal companies, among others.

origins.name: Wethouder Tabakstraat
origins.en: Johannes Tabak (1904-1978), alderman for Social Affairs from 1962 to 1968.

origins.name: Wethouder van Essenweg
origins.en: Pieter Hendrik van Essen (1902-1965), from 1931 to 1949 and from 1958 to 1965 alderman of the municipality of Haarlemmerliede and Spaarnwoude.

origins.name: Wethouder Van Wijckstraat
origins.en: Franciscus H.C. van Wijck (1901-1970), a member of the municipal council for 27 years and a alderman from 1945 to 1966, among others for the municipal companies.

origins.name: Wethouder Vospad
origins.en: Isidoor Henry Joseph Vos (1887-1943), a member of the municipal council for 22 years. During that period, he was a alderman from 1921 to 1928 and from 1933 to 1935.

origins.name: Wethouder Wierdelsstraat
origins.en: Ferdinandus J.A.M. Wierdels (1862-1935), municipal council member from 1919 to 1931 and alderman from 1919 to 1925.

origins.name: Wevelgemstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of West Flanders.

origins.name: WG-plein
origins.en: The former Wilhelmina-Gasthuis, colloquially referred to as the W.G. The square and surrounding streets were laid out after the closure and partial demolition of the hospital, which was founded in 1891 on and adjacent to the grounds of the old Pesthuis. In 1957, the W.G. became an academic hospital and in 1983 the last patients moved to the Academic Medical Center. However, part of the buildings have remained standing and have been renovated for residential functions and commercial spaces.

origins.name: Wiardi Beckmanstraat
origins.en: Herman Barnard Wiardi Beckman (1904-1945) was a Dutch politician and a resistance fighter during World War II. He was also a member of the House of Representatives on behalf of the Social Democratic Workers' Party.

origins.name: Wibauthof
origins.en: Florentinus Marinus Wibaut (1859-1936), socialist-democratic politician and statesman, from 1914 to 1927 and from 1929 to 1931 alderman. Of great significance for housing construction, social development and the theater life in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Wibautstraat
origins.en: Florentinus Marinus Wibaut (1859-1936), socialist-democratic politician and statesman, from 1914 to 1927 and from 1929 to 1931 alderman. Of great significance for housing construction, social development and the theater life in Amsterdam. The street was laid out after the closure of Weesperpoort station in 1939 on the route of the former railway line. The streets along the railway line that disappeared due to this naming were Miquelstraat, Spoorbaanstraat and the first part of Vrolikstraat.

origins.name: Wiborgeiland
origins.en: Swedish, Russian, Finnish and finally again Russian Baltic Sea port, which was important for the Amsterdam timber trade.

origins.name: Wichersstraat
origins.en: Mr. Hendrik Ludolf Wichers (1800-1853), statesman and lawyer. Was Minister of Justice in the De Kempenaer cabinet in 1849 and then a member of the Council of State.

origins.name: Wiegbrug
origins.en: This bascule bridge is named after the type of bridge it originally represented. A swing bridge is a roller bascule bridge.

origins.name: Wielewaalstraat
origins.en: Named after the golden oriole, a singing bird.

origins.name: Wielingenstraat
origins.en: The gully in the mouth of the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Wierdestraat
origins.en: Artificially raised residential hill, which occurs under this name in the province of Groningen. Occurs in Friesland under the name terp.

origins.name: Wieringerwaardstraat
origins.en: Polder in North Holland (northeast of Schagen), a piece of tidal flat area drained in 1610.

origins.name: Wigbolt Ripperdastraat
origins.en: Geuzenaanvoerder from Groningen, appointed governor of Haarlem by the Prince of Orange during the siege of 1672 to 1673. After the fall of the city, he was beheaded by the Spanish.

origins.name: Wijde Heisteeg
origins.en: The Heisteeg gets its name from a corner house that was called ''t Hayblok'. This house is already mentioned at the beginning of the sixteenth century. The street was laid out on land that came to the city in the middle of the fifteenth century. The Wijde Heisteeg dates back to the next city expansion.

origins.name: Wijde Kapelsteeg
origins.en: To the chapel 'ter Heilige Stede', later called Nieuwezijds Kapel. After the demolition of the original church in 1909, the current one was put into use in 1912. Previously there were even more Chapel Stops, but their names were changed due to confusion.

origins.name: Wijde Kerksteeg
origins.en: To the Old Church, where the steps lead up from Warmoesstraat, which was originally called Kerkstraat for part of it.

origins.name: Wijde Lombardsteeg
origins.en: To the nearby Lommerd or Bank van Lening, founded in the year 1614.

origins.name: Wijdenesserstraat
origins.en: To the village of Wijdenes, east of Hoorn (North Holland).

origins.name: Wijdesteeg
origins.en: The alley was already mentioned under this name in 1564. Compared to other alleys, this one was quite wide. Earlier, the alley was known by the names Witloossteeg (after a resident) and Houtmarktsteeg.

origins.name: Wijenburg
origins.en: Nobility house in Echteld (Gelderland) from the sixteenth century with a late medieval tower. Interior renovated in the eighteenth century, now restored. Named after the lords of Wije, lords of Echteld.

origins.name: Wijkergouw
origins.en: A gouw is a village road or village moat. A district can be a residential area, but also a side water. This may be the second meaning. The name 'De Weijcker' already appears here on a map from the seventeenth century (by Gerrit Drogeham).

origins.name: Wijmarkthof
origins.en: Name of the former land outside the dike along the Spaarndammerdijk near Sloterdijk, protected by a summer dike against the water of the former IJ.

origins.name: Wijnand Nuijenstraat
origins.en: Wijnand Jan Joseph Nuijen (1813-1839), painter from the romantic school. Painted seascapes, street and cityscapes. When it was discovered after the council decision was made that the first name was incorrect, the relevant alderman did not consider it worth changing the name.

origins.name: Wijngaardsstraatje
origins.en: The street already appeared under this name in 1430. It is likely that a inn located here at the time with a facade stone was the name giver.

origins.name: Wijnkersstraat
origins.en: Shiny, dark red to brown cherry.

origins.name: Wijnsilostraat
origins.en: Names refer to companies that were based here Wine trade Roders

origins.name: Wijsmullerstraat
origins.en: Jan Hillebrand Wijsmuller (1855-1925), landscape painter.

origins.name: Wijttenbachstraat
origins.en: Daniel Wijttenbach (1746-1820), professor of philosophy in Amsterdam, later professor of ancient languages in Leiden.

origins.name: Wilco Jiskootpad
origins.en: Willem Herbertus Jiskoot (1924-1945), resistance fighter, born in Amsterdam, executed by firing squad in Haarlem. He was a member of the main group of the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Wildeman
origins.en: Former grain mill on Amstelveenseweg, near Kalfjeslaan.

origins.name: Wildenborch
origins.en: Fortified castle from 1372, of which only a heavy gate tower remains. This tower is now the central part of the current building, which dates from 1782. Located under Vorden (Gelderland).

origins.name: Wildrijkstraat
origins.en: Nature reserve in the municipality of Zijpe. The area includes one of the few deciduous forests in the north of North Holland.

origins.name: Wilgenweg
origins.en: Named after the willow, a deciduous tree.

origins.name: Wilhelmina Bladergroenstraat
origins.en: Wilhelmina Johanna Bladergroen (1908-1983), psychologist and pedagogue, from 1967 to 1978 professor of child psychology of the deviant child at the University of Groningen. Initiator of the development of L.O.M. schools.

origins.name: Wilhelmina Druckerstraat
origins.en: Pioneer of the Dutch women's movement (1847-1925). Founded the Women's Suffrage Association with Aletta Jacobs in 1893.

origins.name: Wilhelminastraat
origins.en: Wilhelmina Helena Paulina Maria princess of Orange Nassau (1880-1962), daughter of King William III and Queen Emma. Queen of the Netherlands from 1898 to 1948.

origins.name: Wilhelmus Leemansstraat
origins.en: Hydrologist (1841-1929), chief inspector of the Dutch Water Authority. He had a stake in the construction of the Nieuwe Waterweg and the waterway from Zwolle to the North Sea (IJsselmeer). A pumping station is named after him in the Wieringermeerpolder.

origins.name: Willaertstraat
origins.en: Adriaen Willaert (1485-1562), South Dutch composer. Working in Venice since 1527, where he founded the so-called Venetian music school.

origins.name: Willebroekstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Willem Augustinstraat
origins.en: Skating legend (1923-2004). From 1941 he rode the Elfstedentocht every time (nine times)

origins.name: Willem Baerdesenstraat
origins.en: Willem Baerdesen (1528-1601), also written as Bardes or Bardesius, mayor of Amsterdam at the time of the Alteration in 1578.

origins.name: Willem Bartjenshof
origins.en: Schoolmaster (1569-1645), began his career in Amsterdam. Gained great fame through his notebooks, which have been reprinted repeatedly. Lived in Zwolle since 1618.

origins.name: Willem Beukelsstraat
origins.en: The fisherman from Biervliet, who improved the herring cakes (removing the intestines). Died in 1397. The street was called before 1922: Michiel Adr. de Ruijterstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1907).

origins.name: Willem de Zwijgerlaan
origins.en: Nickname of Prince Willem of Orange (1533-1584), also known as 'The Father of the Fatherland'. Son of Willem of Nassau and Juliana of Stolberg. Because he inherited the principality of Orange, he is the ancestor of the House of Orange-Nassau.

origins.name: Willem Fenengastraat
origins.en: Founder of the Amsterdam Dry Dock Company (1848-1930).

origins.name: Willem Frederik Hermansstraat
origins.en: Writer (1921-1995) and polemicist. Was lecturer in physical geography at the Rijksuniversiteit Groningen. His most famous novels include 'The dark chamber of Damocles' and 'Never sleep again'. Chaos and chance play a major role in his work. He established his name as a polemicist with his book 'Mandarins in sulfuric acid', in which he criticized the Dutch literary world. In 1977 he received the Grand Prize of the Dutch Letters.

origins.name: Willem Frogerstraat
origins.en: Willem Antonie Froger (1812-1883), civil engineer, designer of the North Sea Canal opened on 1-11-1876.

origins.name: Willem Gerresepad
origins.en: Willem Frederik Gerrese (1910-1943), resistance fighter, born in The Hague, executed in Leusden. He was affiliated with the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Willem Gertenbachstraat
origins.en: Willem Johannes Gertenbach (1904-1943), resistance fighter, born in Zandvoort, executed by firing squad in Leusden. As a printer, he had an important role in the production of the illegal newspaper 'Het Parool'.

origins.name: Willem Heselaarsstraat
origins.en: Prominent figure in the Roman Catholic labor movement in Amsterdam (1886-1960). Performed important work in the crisis of the 1930s in favor of workers in employment.

origins.name: Willem Kesstraat
origins.en: Visual artist (1856-1934). First conductor of the Concertgebouw Orchestra, founded in 1888, succeeded in 1895 by Willem Mengelberg.

origins.name: Willem Kloosstraat
origins.en: Poet (1858-1938), leading figure in the Movement of Eighty, founder and editor of 'De Nieuwe Gids'. As a critic, he made pioneering work, which made him of great importance for the development of Dutch literature.

origins.name: Willem Kraanstraat
origins.en: Wilhelmus Johannes Kraan (1909-1942), resistance fighter, municipal worker and one of the initiators of the February Strike of 1941. Born in Amsterdam, executed in Soest.

origins.name: Willem Kromhoutstraat
origins.en: Architect (1864-1910). Among his works are the Hotel Americain (1900).

origins.name: Willem Landréstraat
origins.en: Guillaume Louis Frédérick Landré (1874-1948), composer. Wrote operas and symphonies. Music critic for many years for various newspapers. His son Guillaume (1905-1968) was also a composer.

origins.name: Willem Leevendstraat
origins.en: Letter novel by Betje Wolff and Aagje Deken from 1785. The street was transferred from the former municipality of Sloten in 1921 under the name Prinses Julianastraat (council decision of Sloten, 1910).

origins.name: Willem Molengraaffstraat
origins.en: Jurist in the field of commercial law (1858-1931). Professor at Utrecht and reformer of Dutch maritime law.

origins.name: Willem Mollhof
origins.en: Church historian (1812-1879), professor at the municipal University of Amsterdam. Layed the foundation for modern church history.

origins.name: Willem Mulierhof
origins.en: Athlete, known as Pim Mulier (1865-1954). He is called the father of Dutch athletics and football. Founded the Dutch Football Association in 1889. In 1890 he rode the entire journey by skating alone along the eleven cities of Friesland. He gave the impetus to the famous eleven-city race, which was first organized in 1909.

origins.name: Willem Nakkenstraat
origins.en: Painter (1835-1926), mainly of cattle, sometimes also of figures.

origins.name: Willem Noorlanderkade
origins.en: Architect (1877-1940), designed the Ceintuur Theater on the Ceintuurbaan, completed in 1920. In the 1920s, he designed the residential complex between the Berberisstraat and the Mosveld in Amsterdam Noord, two villas on the Meeuwenlaan and residential blocks around the Andoornstraat.

origins.name: Willem Paaphof
origins.en: Writer and lawyer (1856-1923), co-founder of 'De Nieuwe Gids'.

origins.name: Willem Parelstraat
origins.en: High bootsman on the VOC shipyard in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Willem Passtoorsstraat
origins.en: Willem C.J. Passtoors (1856-1916), Amsterdam cigar dealer, who founded the Roman Catholic People's Federation in the Netherlands in 1888, and thus became the founder of the Roman Catholic Workers' Movement in our country. From 1901-1913 he was a member of the House of Representatives.

origins.name: Willem Pijperstraat
origins.en: Composer (1894-1947), teacher at the conservatories of Amsterdam and Rotterdam. As a lyric poet influenced by the French impressionists Franck and Debussy and by Mahler. Pijper wrote symphonies, choral works and stage music, among other things.

origins.name: Willem Roelofsstraat
origins.en: Landscape painter (1822-1892), representative of a new Dutch realism.

origins.name: Willem Royaardsstraat
origins.en: Willem Cornelis Royaards (1867-1929), actor and director. Led his own company for several years before becoming president of the Vereeniging Het Nederlandsch Toneel from 1920 to 1924.

origins.name: Willem Schermerhornstraat
origins.en: Politician and statesman (1894-1977) Prime Minister-President of the Netherlands after World War II, of the Schermerhorn/Drees cabinet (1945-1946). Before 1945 he belonged to the liberal democrats and led the Dutch People's Movement after 1945. Between 1946 and 1963 he was a member of the House of Representatives and the House of Lords for the Labour Party.

origins.name: Willem Schoutenstraat
origins.en: Sailor (1580-1625) made a round-the-world trip and discovered the later named islands in New Guinea.

origins.name: Willem Theunisse Blokstraat
origins.en: Master carpenter. Built ships.

origins.name: Willem van Hembyzestraat
origins.en: Leader of the Geuzen during the capture of Den Briel in 1572.

origins.name: Willem van Konijnenburgstraat
origins.en: Willem Adriaan van Konijnenburg (1868-1943), painter, engraver, lithographer, designer of glass and murals and writer about art. He initially painted realistically, later through contacts with Thorn Prikker, Derkinderen and Toorop his work became more stylized.

origins.name: Willem van Weldammelaan
origins.en: Governor of Amstelland and Waterland from 1392 to 1395.

origins.name: Willem Witsenstraat
origins.en: Painter (1860-1923) of Amsterdam cityscapes. Close relative of Breitner. The street was originally named Albert Hahnstraat (council decision, 1925).

origins.name: Willemsbrug
origins.en: This bascule bridge is named after King William I (1772-1843), who opened the nearby Willemspoort in 1840

origins.name: Willemskerkestraat
origins.en: In the sixteenth century, a village drowned in Zeelandic Flanders.

origins.name: Willemsparkweg
origins.en: This street leads to the former Willemspark, which was designed in 1881 as a connection to Vondelpark. That neighborhood still belonged to the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel at the time, which called this road Parkweg. However, the plans were changed in 1902, after which the current villa district around Emmaplein was created. Willemspark is named after King William I.

origins.name: Willemsstraat
origins.en: King William I (1772-1843). The Goudsbloemgracht was filled in in 1857. On the occasion of the inauguration of the new street created by this (which coincided with the then still widely known birthday of the previous king on August 24), a festival was organized and the filled in Goudsbloemgracht was renamed Willemstraat. The second s in the street name was added after 1909. Since 1918, the name has appeared with double s.

origins.name: Willeskopstraat
origins.en: Named after a village near Oudewater (Utrecht).

origins.name: William Barlowlaan
origins.en: English mathematician (1544-1625), published his famous work 'The navigator's supply' in 1597 and invented a nautical instrument that he called the 'compass of variation'.

origins.name: William Barlowsteiger
origins.en: English mathematician (1544-1625), published his famous work 'The navigator's supply' in 1597 and invented a nautical instrument that he called the 'compass of variation'.

origins.name: William Boothstraat
origins.en: English traveling preacher (1829-1914), originally Methodist. Founded the Salvation Army in 1878 and was its first general.

origins.name: Willinklaan
origins.en: Dirk Jan Willink (1888-1951), prominent figure in the Dutch athletics world. Played a particularly important role in the development of the synthetic tracks. Held numerous sports positions.

origins.name: Willy la Croixstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1906-1944), was involved in many illegal activities.

origins.name: Willy Mullenskade
origins.en: Cinema operator and filmmaker (1880-1952), in the early years of cinema he operated a traveling cinema together with his brother Albert, where he provided the films with commentary with his voice. He made many commissioned films in the Netherlands and India.

origins.name: Willy Pétillonstraat
origins.en: Youth book writer (1885-1948), debuted in 1908 with the boys' book 'The Adventures of a Bengal'. Then followed a large number of girls' books.

origins.name: Willy Sluiterstraat
origins.en: Painter and illustrator (1873-1949), chairman of Pulchri Studio in The Hague for many years.

origins.name: Wilmkebreekpad
origins.en: Named after a pond in North Holland, which was created by a levee breach in the years 1512 and 1518. Dried up in 1933, then flooded several times.

origins.name: Wilnisgracht
origins.en: The commuter village between Mijdrecht and Breukelen (Utrecht).

origins.name: Wiltzanghlaan
origins.en: Poem by Vondel. The first part of the street was previously designated as Zoutmanstraat by the municipality of Sloten (council decision of Sloten, 1910).

origins.name: Wim Ibobrug
origins.en: Wim Ibo (1918-2000) was a cabaretier and writer, who became especially known as a cabaret historian. His book 'And now the morality of this song' is generally considered the cabaret bible.

origins.name: Wim Noordhoekkade
origins.en: Photographer (1916-1995), best known for his special color photography.

origins.name: Wim van Estlaan
origins.en: Cyclist (1923 - 2003), first Dutchman to wear the yellow jersey as leader of the general classification in the Tour de France of 1951. Wim van Est's nicknames were: 'The Locomotive', 'Iron Willem', 'the Knob' and 'the Beul of the Heike'.

origins.name: Windjammerdijk
origins.en: Equipped sailing ship for the big voyage.

origins.name: Windrooskade
origins.en: Star-shaped figure indicating wind directions.

origins.name: Windroosplein
origins.en: Star-shaped figure indicating wind directions.

origins.name: Windtunnelkade
origins.en: In a wind tunnel, certain properties of aircraft are tested by artificially developed high wind speeds.

origins.name: Wingerdweg
origins.en: The climbing plant.

origins.name: Winkler Prinshof
origins.en: Anthony Winkler Prins (1817-1908), preacher and writer. Editor of the Winkler Prins encyclopedia named after him.

origins.name: Winterdijkstraat
origins.en: The outer river embankment, the bandijk, which limits the riverbed in winter and spring.

origins.name: Winterjanpad
origins.en: Old Dutch pear variety. The path is located on the former community garden complex De Bongerd.

origins.name: Winterstraat
origins.en: The season. The street came under the name Rijnstraat in 1966 from the former municipality of Weesperkarspel. (council decision of Weesperkarspel, 1964).

origins.name: Winthontstraat
origins.en: Named after the historic ship the Winthont, with which enslaved people were transported in the eighteenth century.

origins.name: Wismarbrug
origins.en: Wismar is a port city on the Baltic Sea in northeastern Germany near Rostock. The names in the Houthavens are named after places with which the Netherlands traded extensively in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

origins.name: Wisseloord
origins.en: Men's house in 's-Graveland.

origins.name: Wisseloordpad
origins.en: Men's house in 's-Graveland.

origins.name: Wisseloordplein
origins.en: Men's house in 's-Graveland.

origins.name: Wisselstraat
origins.en: The switch between two train tracks, which is operated with a lever and allows trains to switch from one track to another.

origins.name: Witbolstraat
origins.en: Grass species that occurs in Europe, Asia and North Africa.

origins.name: Withoedenveem
origins.en: A veem is a company that is responsible for storing and delivering goods in and out of its warehouses. The veems each had their own license plate, after which they were named. These could be different colors and models of hats (e.g. Withoeden, Cloche hats). They also derived their name from the origin of the workers (e.g. Vriesseveem, Zeeuwse Veem).

origins.name: Witte Boogbrug
origins.en: Named after her appearance, it is a white arch bridge

origins.name: Witte de Withplein
origins.en: Witte Cornelisz de With (1599-1658, vice-admiral of Holland and West Friesland. Fought under Tromp at Duins and at Terheide, among other places. Died in the battle at the Sont against the Swedes.

origins.name: Witte de Withstraat
origins.en: Witte Cornelisz de With (1599-1658, vice-admiral of Holland and West Friesland. Fought under Tromp at Duins and at Terheide, among other places. Died in the battle at the Sont against the Swedes.

origins.name: Witte Katbrug
origins.en: Named after the species

origins.name: Witte Klok
origins.en: Former farmhouse in the old municipality of Sloten.

origins.name: Wittenburgergracht
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (next to Kattenburg and Oostenburg), built in the second half of the seventeenth century, from the beginning built with shipyards and houses. One of the first shipyards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. Very likely we must look here for the origin of the name Wittenburg.

origins.name: Wittenburgerkade
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (next to Kattenburg and Oostenburg), built in the second half of the seventeenth century, from the beginning built with shipyards and houses. One of the first shipyards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. Very likely we must look here for the origin of the name Wittenburg.

origins.name: Wittgensteinlaan
origins.en: Ludwig Josef Johann Wittgenstein (1889-1951), British philosopher of Austrian descent. Eminently researched, he developed through mathematics into a renowned and influential logician and linguist.

origins.name: Wodanstraat
origins.en: Wodan was the supreme god of the Germans.

origins.name: Woestduinstraat
origins.en: Country estate under Bloemendaal. Known for the horse races, which were regularly held there at the beginning of the twentieth century and visited by many Amsterdamers.

origins.name: Wognumerpad
origins.en: Village in North Holland.

origins.name: Wognumerplantsoen
origins.en: Village in North Holland.

origins.name: Wognumerstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland.

origins.name: Woiskistraat
origins.en: Max Woiski sr. (Domburg (Suriname), 1911 - Hoogeveen 1981) was a well-known musician. In the 1930s, he performed in his own club La Cubana in Amsterdam's Leidsestraat under the name José Baretto. In the early stages of his career, he mainly played Latin American music; later also Surinamese music. His biggest hit was B.B. with R. (Brown beans with rice). In the 1960s he had his own production company MMP and moved to Mallorca where he bought a nightclub. In 2018 theater group Orkater together with the Bijlmer Parktheater staged the play Woiski vs. Woiski.

origins.name: Wolbrantskerkweg
origins.en: In 1421, the church village, which was located near the current town of Dubbeldam (South Holland), drowned.

origins.name: Wolderwijdpad
origins.en: One of the Veluwe edge lakes

origins.name: Wolter Brandligtstraat
origins.en: Resistance fighter (1901-1943), by profession writer. Born in Kampen, executed in Amsterdam.

origins.name: Woltera van Reesstraat
origins.en: Woltera Bertha Johanna Berns van Rees (1841-1926), director of the Burgerziekenhuis and wife of the founder of the hospital, Anton Wilhelm Cornelis Berns.

origins.name: Wolvenstraat
origins.en: A predator belonging to the dog breed. As with more streets in this neighborhood, the naming is related to the fur trade.

origins.name: Wormerveerstraat
origins.en: Location in the Zaanstreek. The street was known as Houtrijkkade (council decision, 1888) before 1913.

origins.name: Woubruggestraat
origins.en: Village near the Braassemermeer (South Holland).

origins.name: Woudrichemstraat
origins.en: Fortified town on the Maas in the Land of Altena (North Brabant)

origins.name: Woutertje Pietersestraat
origins.en: Named after the book 'The History of Woutertje Pieterse' by Eduard Douwes Dekker under his pseudonym Multatuli.

origins.name: Wouwermanstraat
origins.en: Philips Wouwerman de Oude (1619-1668), painter of horses and war scenes.

origins.name: Wyandottestraat
origins.en: Chicken breed of American origin. Wyandotte is a city in the North American state of Michigan.

origins.name: Zaagmolenstraat
origins.en: Named after the many sawmills, which stood here until the end of the nineteenth century.

origins.name: Zaaiersweg
origins.en: The farmer who sows the seed.

origins.name: Zaandammerplein
origins.en: The city of Zaandam, now forming the municipality of Zaanstad with a few other places.

origins.name: Zaandijkstraat
origins.en: The place in the Zaanstreek, now municipality of Zaanstad. From 30-3-1881 to 1913 this was the Eerste Spaarndammerdwarsstraat.

origins.name: Zaanhof
origins.en: The place in the Zaanstreek, now municipality of Zaanstad. From 30-3-1881 to 1913 this was the Eerste Spaarndammerdwarsstraat.

origins.name: Zaanstraat
origins.en: The Zaan River, the main artery of the Zaanstreek. The street first appears under the name Houtrijkkade (council decision, 1888).

origins.name: Zacharias Jansestraat
origins.en: Zeeuwish eyeglass grinder (1580-1620), inventor of the binoculars. The original name Paul Krugerstraat, established by the municipality of Watergraafsmeer (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1900), had to be changed after the annexation of 1921 due to confusion with the street of the same name in the Transvaalbuurt.

origins.name: Zakslootje
origins.en: An old street name, originally a dead-end ditch. No longer included in the street name database from 1875. Due to the need for address indication, this name was included in the street name database again in 1984.

origins.name: Zamenhofstraat
origins.en: Ludwig Lazer Zamenhof (1859-1917), Polish doctor and linguist. In 1887, under the pseudonym Dr. Esperanto, he compiled a auxiliary language, which has continued to exist as Esperanto. Before 1948, the street was called Plaatijzerweg (derived from the steel industry) established on 6-6-1917. However, this was later found to be an unattractive name.

origins.name: Zanddwarsstraat
origins.en: The piece of land over which Zandstraat and Zanddwarsstraat run was originally swampy. In 1593 it was raised. Presumably the origin of the name lies in this sand elevation. By council decision in 1982, Zandstraat, which formerly ran through Reguliersbreestraat, was shortened to the current Zuiderkerkhof.

origins.name: Zandhoek
origins.en: According to a decree of 1634, the sand market was allowed to be held on this corner of the Western Islands.

origins.name: Zandhoeksbrug
origins.en: This double pick-up bridge is named after the Zandhoek. According to a decree of 1634, the sand market was allowed to be held at this corner of the Western Islands..

origins.name: Zandpad
origins.en: As early as 1688, this path is mentioned as the sand path or Muntepad, belonging to Willem de Munt, goldsmith on the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal. It must have been a sandy dirt road at that time.

origins.name: Zandpad-Driemond
origins.en: This is the part of the old Weesper Zandpad, which is located in the village of Driemond. The rest of the Zandpad is now called Provincialeweg. The municipal council of Amsterdam changed the name Zandpad to Zandpad-Driemond due to confusion with the Zandpad in Oud-West.

origins.name: Zandstraat
origins.en: The piece of land over which the Zandstraat and the Zanddwarsstraat run was originally swampy. In 1593 it was raised. Presumably the origin of the name lies in this sand elevation. By council decision in 1982, the Zandstraat, which formerly ran through Reguliersbreestraat, was shortened to the current Zuiderkerkhof.

origins.name: Zandvoortstraat
origins.en: The seaside resort (North Holland).

origins.name: Zandzeggestraat
origins.en: Permanent, native plant from the sedge family. A dune and heath plant, which counteracts sand erosion.

origins.name: Zaventemweg
origins.en: Name of Brussels airport.

origins.name: Zeebergweg
origins.en: Adriaan van Zeebergh (1746-1824), statesman, from 1773 to 1787 pensionary of Haarlem. During the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War (1780-1784), he was one of the leaders of the resistance against Stadhouder Willem V. In 1787 he was removed from office.

origins.name: Zeeburgerdijk
origins.en: The fortress 'Seeburgh', which stood halfway through the seventeenth century at the end of the dike. The Zeeburgerdijk is a part of the original sea dike of the North Sea. Before the Watergraafsmeer was drained, this was the only connection in the direction of Naarden.

origins.name: Zeeburgerkade
origins.en: The fortress 'Seeburgh', which stood halfway through the seventeenth century at the end of the dike. The Zeeburgerdijk is a part of the original sea dike of the North Sea. Before the Watergraafsmeer was drained, this was the only connection in the direction of Naarden.

origins.name: Zeeburgerpad
origins.en: The fortress 'Seeburgh', which stood halfway through the seventeenth century at the end of the dike. The Zeeburgerdijk is a part of the original sea dike of the North Sea. Before the Watergraafsmeer was drained, this was the only connection in the direction of Naarden.

origins.name: Zeeburgerstraat
origins.en: The fortress 'Seeburgh', which stood halfway through the seventeenth century at the end of the dike. The Zeeburgerdijk is a part of the original sea dike of the North Sea. Before the Watergraafsmeer was drained, this was the only connection in the direction of Naarden.

origins.name: Zeedijk
origins.en: The name expresses the function. Since the founding of the city, this has been the sea wall and also the border of the first settlement on the side of IJ and Zuiderzee. The street still has the function of water dam, albeit as a sleeping wall.

origins.name: Zeelandstraat
origins.en: The province. Located in the middle of streets named after Zeelandish castles.

origins.name: Zeemagazijnkade
origins.en: Named after the VOC warehouse in Oostenburg.

origins.name: Zeevaart
origins.en: The practice of shipping at sea.

origins.name: Zeevaarthof
origins.en: The practice of shipping at sea.

origins.name: Zeilmakerstraat
origins.en: Occupational name from shipbuilding. The name reminds us of the many shipyards that were established here in earlier centuries.

origins.name: Zeilstraat
origins.en: The cloth on vessels, for the capture of wind.

origins.name: Zekeringstraat
origins.en: The stop in the electrical line, which is responsible for protecting the network from overload in the event of a short circuit.

origins.name: Zelzatestraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of East Flanders.

origins.name: Zennehof
origins.en: Channel in Belgium, near Brussels.

origins.name: Zenostraat
origins.en: Greek philosopher (342-270 BC), founder of the Stoic school.

origins.name: Zesde Vogelstraat
origins.en: Streets are named after birds in this neighborhood.

origins.name: Zieseniskade
origins.en: Johanna Cornelia Ziesenis-Wattier (1762-1827), one of the greatest Dutch actresses of her time. The quay was built on the old Gangpad.

origins.name: Zijkanaal H-weg
origins.en: The road over the dike along Zijkanaal H and formed by the reclamation of the Noorder IJpolder.

origins.name: Zilverberg
origins.en: Nature monument, consisting of forest and oak wood complexes. Located between Oosterbeek and Doorwerth.

origins.name: Zilvermeeuwpad
origins.en: Large, commonly occurring gull species.

origins.name: Zilverplevierstraat
origins.en: Sturdy bird with black beak and black-and-white plumage. The silver plover breeds in the far north, but is especially common in spring and autumn on the mudflat and in the Zeeland delta.

origins.name: Zilverschoonstraat
origins.en: The plant, belonging to the ranunculus family.

origins.name: Zlotylaan
origins.en: The currency of Poland.

origins.name: Zocherstraat
origins.en: Louis Paul Zocher (1820-1915), garden architect. Designer and builder of Vondelpark (1864).

origins.name: Zomerdijkstraat
origins.en: A summer dike is the low dike or quay directly along the riverbed, which in summer - so at low water level - limits the riverbed.

origins.name: Zomerstraat
origins.en: The season. Earlier, the street name was established on 29-11-1957 by the former municipality of Weesperkarspel as Geinstraat.

origins.name: Zonhovenstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Zonnebeke
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of West Flanders.

origins.name: Zonnehoekspad
origins.en: In the Netherlands, in summer the sun is much higher above the horizon than in winter. The angle that the rays of the sun make is also called the solar angle.

origins.name: Zonnehof
origins.en: The central body in the planetary system to which Earth belongs.

origins.name: Zonneplein
origins.en: The central body in the planetary system to which Earth belongs.

origins.name: Zonneweg
origins.en: The central body in the planetary system to which Earth belongs.

origins.name: Zonnewendebrug
origins.en: Zonnewendebrug is a bridge in Oostburg in the Centrum district of Amsterdam. When designing this bridge, attention was paid to light and shadow formation. The fence is 3D printed and has the effect that the perspective of the bridge changes throughout the day and when you walk over it. This bridge has bridge number 2106 which refers to the longest day of the year: the summer solstice.

origins.name: Zonzeelstraat
origins.en: A village that drowned in 1421 during the St. Elizabeth flood in the northwest part of North Brabant.

origins.name: Zoomstraat
origins.en: River in North Brabant, near Bergen op Zoom.

origins.name: Zorgwijkstraat
origins.en: Hofstede at the end of the Middenweg corner Oosterringdijk, built in 1696 and demolished in 1820 for the widening of the Middenweg.

origins.name: Zorgzaam
origins.en: The group of women, who regularly holds her silent march on Meiplein in Buenos Aires (Argentina). They want to know the truth about the fate of their men and children, who have disappeared under the general regime. In contrast to the weapons of violence and empty talk, they show in their collectivity and their persistence their struggle for truth, freedom and justice. Around this square, a number of streets are named after the virtues they represent.

origins.name: Zoutberg
origins.en: Farm on the western Ringsloot of the Purmer. Now gone.

origins.name: Zoutkeetsbrug
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, on both sides of this canal stood the salt chain, which were warehouses where coarse salt was processed for household use.

origins.name: Zoutkeetsgracht
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, on both sides of this canal stood the salt chain, which were warehouses where coarse salt was processed for household use.

origins.name: Zoutkeetsplein
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, on both sides of this canal stood the salt chain, which were warehouses where coarse salt was processed for household use.

origins.name: Zuid-Bevelandstraat
origins.en: The Zeeuwse island.

origins.name: Zuid-Hollandstraat
origins.en: The province. The surrounding streets are named after castles from this province.

origins.name: Zuideinde
origins.en: Acquired from the municipality of Oostzaan in 1966. The name indicates its location relative to the village of Oostzaan. In the part that also passed from the municipality of Landsmeer to Amsterdam at the same time, there was also a Zuideinde (relative to the village of Landsmeer), but due to confusion that road was later changed to Kadoelenweg.

origins.name: Zuidelijke Wandelweg
origins.en: Originally built as a walking path between the Amsteldijk and the Amstelveenseweg. Parallel to this, but still further outside the urban development of before 1940, ran the Buitenveldertse Wandelweg, which disappeared due to the construction of the garden city of Buitenveldert. The now still existing remnant of the Zuidelijke Wandelweg only has the name in common. The character of walking path has disappeared.

origins.name: Zuider IJdijk
origins.en: South side of the IJ

origins.name: Zuiderakerweg
origins.en: The location in the Akerpolder. The street was taken over in 1921 under the name Zuiderweg.

origins.name: Zuidergasfabriekbrug
origins.en: This bridge name refers to the Zuidergasfabriek, which stood here from 1909 to 1967.

origins.name: Zuiderkerkhof
origins.en: Named after the original function of this square. The gate that gave access to the old cemetery has now been restored and placed in the entrance from Sint Antoniesbreestraat to the square.

origins.name: Zuidermolenweg
origins.en: Old mill in the former Sloten (suyder Mole), mentioned on the map by Jan Dou from 1687.

origins.name: Zuiderzeepark
origins.en: Zuidzee, after closure in 1932 IJsselmeer.

origins.name: Zuiderzeeweg
origins.en: Zuidzee, after closure in 1932 IJsselmeer.

origins.name: Zuidewijn
origins.en: Ridderhuizinge in Vrijhoeve-Capelle (North Brabant). Partly sixteenth century, partly seventeenth century, renovated in 1763, consisting of two wings built perpendicular to each other with gabled facades.

origins.name: Zuidgorsstraat
origins.en: Nature reserve near Ellewoutsdijk (Zeeland), a landmass outside the dikes in the Westerschelde.

origins.name: Zuidplein
origins.en: The Zuidplein derives its name from its location near Station Zuid and its geographical location in the city. The square forms an important junction in Amsterdam Zuid and is connected to Noord and the Noordplein there via the metro line.

origins.name: Zuivelplein
origins.en: Livestock products (milk, butter and cheese).

origins.name: Zunderdorpergouw
origins.en: The county (village road) leads to the village of Zunderdorp, which has been part of the municipality of Amsterdam since 1-1-1921.

origins.name: Zus Braunstraat
origins.en: Swimmer, won gold in the 1928 Olympic Games in Amsterdam in the 100-meter backstroke.

origins.name: Zutendaalstraat
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Limburg.

origins.name: Zwaagstraat
origins.en: Village in North Holland, north of Hoorn.

origins.name: Zwaansvliet
origins.en: Men's house in the Beemster (North Holland). Before 1965, the street was part of the Kastelenstraat.

origins.name: Zwaardemakerstraat
origins.en: Hendrik Zwaardemaker (1857-1930), physiologist, professor in Utrecht. Known for his olfactory and taste studies.

origins.name: Zwaluwstraat
origins.en: Named after the swallow, a singing bird.

origins.name: Zwanebloemlaan
origins.en: Swamp plant with pink flowers. The name refers to the shape of the stampers, which resemble swans. Grows along canals, waterways and drainage channels, and is planted as an ornamental flower in ponds.

origins.name: Zwanenburgwal
origins.en: Shortly after the land (on which the street and quay were laid out) was drawn to the city just before 4:00 PM, there is talk of a house 'where Swanenburg hangs out', on the corner of Zwanenburgwal. This will therefore probably have been the name giver. Swanenburg was already a more common name at that time. Gerrit Barents Swanenburgh, for example, built the Muiderpoort, Weesperpoort and Utrechtsepoort in the seventeenth century. By council decision in 1976, a part of the Zwanenburgwal was named in Sint Antoniesluis. In order to build the Stopera, the Zwanenburgerstraat with adjacent buildings was relocated.

origins.name: Zwanenplein
origins.en: Named after the swan, a water bird.

origins.name: Zwarte Pad
origins.en: Fungus species. The black toad is black with irregular light brown spots on back and legs, or brown with black spots

origins.name: Zwartegouw
origins.en: This path was built around 1965, after the construction of the garden town Nieuwendam and the Sportpark de Weeren, for the convenience of access to the adjacent farms. In popular parlance, the path soon took on the name of 'Black path'.

origins.name: Zwenkgrasstraat
origins.en: Rare, native plant from the grass family with plume-shaped flowers.

origins.name: Achter Twiske
origins.en: Twiske is the (West) Frisian word for 'between'. It is unknown whether this refers to the location near the Twiske stream or perhaps to the eponymous peatland area.

origins.name: Achtergracht
origins.en: This canal was dug around 1660 behind the four main canals, hence the name. It connected the Reguliersgracht with the Amstel. In 1870, most of it was filled in.

origins.name: Adenhaven
origins.en: Port city in Yemen, on the Red Sea.

origins.name: Admiralengracht
origins.en: Collective name of the Dutch and Zeelandish admirals, after which the streets in the surrounding district are named.

origins.name: Afrikahaven
origins.en: World region. In Africa, deserts, steppes, savannas and rainforests occur. About two-fifths of Africa consists of desert area.

origins.name: Alaskahaven
origins.en: Alaska is the largest state of the United States, located in the most northwestern part of the North American mainland.

origins.name: Albardagracht
origins.en: Johan Willem Albarda (1879-1957), socialist-democratic politician and statesman. From 1939 to 1945 Minister of Water Affairs (from 1940 to 1945 in London).

origins.name: Amerikahaven
origins.en: The world region.

origins.name: Amstel
origins.en: The river to which Amsterdam owes its name and origin.

origins.name: Amstelkanaal
origins.en: Channel, dug around 1920 as part of Berlage's Plan Zuid. Connects the river of the same name with a five-branching canal system, including the Boerenwetering, the Noorder and the Zuider Amstelkanaal.

origins.name: Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal
origins.en: Pressurized canal with a length of 72 kilometers, connecting the IJ via Utrecht with the Waal near Tiel. Part of an important connection with the Ruhr area.

origins.name: Arendonksingel
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Ashaven
origins.en: Transportation goods that were and are shipped through the Amsterdam port

origins.name: Australiëhaven
origins.en: The world region.

origins.name: Aziëhaven
origins.en: The largest of the world regions.

origins.name: Barnegat
origins.en: Former sea arm of the IJ. The name is derived from 'barnen', an older form of the verb burn. This probably refers to the regular reed burning in the area.

origins.name: Beringhaven
origins.en: The Bering Street, a sea street between Asia and America. Discovered and named in 1741 after the Dane Vitus Bering.

origins.name: Beulingsloot
origins.en: One of the residents, Gerrit Jansz Beulinck, who lived here around 1660. He may have made this known with a signboard. In the sixteenth century, the names Leertouwers- and also Huidevettersstraat and -sloot appear here.

origins.name: Bickersgracht
origins.en: These streets are located on the Bickerseiland. This island was originally owned by Dr. Johan Bicker (1591-1653), shipbuilder and merchant, shipowner and mayor of Amsterdam, who bought it in 1631. The streets that were later laid out on this island automatically took the name of the founder. For the

origins.name: Bijleveldschesluis
origins.en: This name appeared in old archives, the exact meaning unknown.

origins.name: Bilderdijkgracht
origins.en: Willem Bilderdijk (1756-1831), poet and historian. Bilderdijk went against the complacent spirit of his time and was therefore a much-controversial figure. The name Bilderdijkstraat originally extended to Vondelstraat. (That part, from Jacob van Lennepkade, is now called Eerste Constantijn Huygensstraat. (council decision, 1894.) The Bilderdijkpark (park and street) was laid out on the grounds of the cemetery of the former Roman Catholic church 'De Liefde'.

origins.name: Blauwburgwal
origins.en: Probably named after the Blue Bridge. The canal was dug at the end of the sixteenth century. The current name first appears from 1614. Previously, the canal was referred to as the Blue Bridge canal outside Jan Roonpoort, or as the perpendicular city wall near the Blue Bridge. Most bridges were painted red at that time.

origins.name: Bloemgracht
origins.en: Many streets and canals in the Jordaan are named after flowers. In this expansion from 1612, the Bloemgracht is probably the oldest canal. The canal ran to the Bolwerk de Bloem (later called Rijkeroord), after which the canal is named. On the fort stood the mill 'De Blom' from 1614 to 1878, which was then moved to the Haarlemmerweg near the Nieuwpoortkade.

origins.name: Boerenwetering
origins.en: The name of the water, which originally ran from Kalfjeslaan to the current Koningsplein. Also formerly called Oude Wetering, in contrast to the Nieuwe Wetering (Kostverlorenvaart). The Weteringbuurt and the Weteringschans derive their name from this water.

origins.name: Bosporushaven
origins.en: The Sea of Marmara in Turkey, which forms part of the connection between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean Sea, separates Europe from Asia.

origins.name: Brantasgracht
origins.en: River in Indonesia, East Java, 257 km long.

origins.name: Broekermeerringsloot
origins.en: Ring-shaped ditch around the clay polder Broekermeer, which was built around 1628.

origins.name: Brouwersgracht
origins.en: To the many breweries that could be found in this neighborhood in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. The designation Binnen and Buiten is related to the location relative to the Haarlemmerdijk.

origins.name: Brusselsingel
origins.en: Capital of Belgium, located in the province of Brabant.

origins.name: Buiksloterkanaal
origins.en: Until 1921, Buiksloot was an independent municipality, after which it merged into Amsterdam. 'Ban' means both jurisdiction and legal authority. The Banne Buiksloot was traditionally one of the six bans (jurisdictions) into which the bailiwick of Waterland was divided. After the Batavian Revolution of 1795, the word continued to exist, but then only referred to the polder. It was not until 1936 that the Waterland bans were lifted

origins.name: Buiten-IJ
origins.en: Water east of the Oranjesluizen with connection to the Ijmeer and the Markermeer.

origins.name: Burgemeester Cramergracht
origins.en: Willem Daniël Cramer (1788-1856), mayor of Amsterdam from 1836 to 1841.

origins.name: Burgemeester van Tienhovengracht
origins.en: Gijsbert van Tienhoven (1841-1914), alderman from 1874 to 1880 and mayor of Amsterdam from 1880 to 1891, then minister.

origins.name: Cacaohaven
origins.en: The tropical product, raw material for chocolate, that is transhipped in the Amsterdam port.

origins.name: Carel Reynierszhaven
origins.en: Lived from 1604 to 1653. Established the first settlement of the Dutch East India Company on the coast of Coromandel (Dutch East Indies). From 1650 to 1653 he was governor-general of Dutch East Indies.

origins.name: Christoffel Plantijngracht
origins.en: South Dutch printer and lexicographer (1514-1589). His printing house and publishing house in Antwerp developed into one of the most famous in Europe (now a museum).

origins.name: Coenhaven
origins.en: Jan Pieterszn Coen (1587-1629). Governor-General of Dutch East Indies (1619-1623 and 1627-1629), founded Batavia that after the transfer of sovereignty regained its old name

origins.name: Cornelis Douweskanaal (Oost)
origins.en: Maritime, scientific and astronomical (1712-1773). Director of the Amsterdam Maritime School.

origins.name: Cornelis Douweskanaal (West)
origins.en: Maritime, scientific and astronomical (1712-1773). Director of the Amsterdam Maritime School.

origins.name: Da Costagracht
origins.en: Isaäc da Costa (1798-1860), Amsterdam lawyer, poet and prose writer of Portuguese-Jewish descent, who converted to Christianity.

origins.name: Damrak
origins.en: Rak is the old name for a straight stretch of navigable water. Here is therefore the rak or the waterway to the Dam, which narrowed on the west side in the course of the eighteenth century. The name of the water was passed on to it when the road or quay was built (in 1526). The houses on Warmoesstraat between Nieuwebrugsteeg and the Beurs are still called the houses 'aan 't Water'.

origins.name: De Boelegracht
origins.en: Gerrit de Boele, bailiff of Amstelland and Waterland (1354/55).

origins.name: De Leek
origins.en: De Leek is a lake in Amsterdam-North.

origins.name: De Rijpgracht
origins.en: Jan Cornelisz de Rijp (1570-1630), seafarer, sailed simultaneously with Heemskerk and Barentsz in search of a northern passage, but did not overwinter on Nova Zembla because he followed a route around Spitzbergen. When the street was built, it was named Willem Barentsstraat by the municipal council of the former municipality of Sloten (council decision, 1910).

origins.name: Dijksgracht
origins.en: The street was built at the end of the sixteenth century as a dike, after which the surrounding area (formerly a swamp) was drained.

origins.name: Distelhaven
origins.en: The plant. The Distelstraten, with the exception of the Distelweg, form a complex of emergency housing (Disteldorp) built in 1919, to meet the large demand for housing for the workers of the rapidly growing industry after World War I in the short term.

origins.name: Duivendrechtsevaart
origins.en: The village of Duivendrecht in the municipality of Ouder-Amstel. Duivendrecht comes from Doeve (a first name) and drecht (place where the ships are pulled overland). When Watergraafsmeer was still a lake, a ferry was maintained from where the village now lies, across to the other side, towards Oetewaal.

origins.name: Durgerdammergouw
origins.en: Named after the village that belonged to the then abolished municipality of Ransdorp until 1921. The name was created by distortion of the oldest name: IJdoringherdam = dam located at the corner of the IJ. (The outlying polder located here on the outside of the dike has retained the name IJdoorn.) The Durgerdammerdijk is the part of Waterlands sea wall to which Durgerdam is located.

origins.name: Egelantiersgracht
origins.en: Named after the eglantine (sweet briar), a shrub.

origins.name: Eilandsgracht
origins.en: In this district there used to be many tanneries, where the hides of elk, deer, bears, etc. were processed.

origins.name: Entrepotdok
origins.en: Named after the function. The dock was built in 1827, imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid. The warehouses have lost their function as a transhipment point, the upper floors of some have now been converted into houses (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Entrepotdoksluis
origins.en: Named after the function. The dock was built in 1827, imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid. The warehouses have lost their function as a transhipment point, the upper floors of some have now been converted into houses (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Entrepothaven
origins.en: Named after the function. The dock was built in 1827, imported goods had to be stored here until the import duties were paid. The warehouses have lost their function as a transhipment point. Some parts have now been converted into houses (Binnenkadijk).

origins.name: Erasmusgracht
origins.en: Desiderius Erasmus (1467-1536), humanist. Made fierce attacks on the abuses in the Roman Catholic Church. His best-known work is 'Praise of Folly'.

origins.name: Ertshaven
origins.en: The ore boats used to be unloaded at the quay.

origins.name: Fahrenheitsingel
origins.en: Gabriel Daniel Fahrenheit (1686-1736), German by birth, who settled in the Netherlands as a physicist. In 1715 he set the freezing point of the thermometer at 32 degrees and the boiling point at 212 degrees. The Fahrenheitstraat was originally called De Wetstraat (council decision of Watergraafsmeer, 1901).

origins.name: Gaasp
origins.en: The name comes from the Gaasp river

origins.name: Gaasperplas
origins.en: The name comes from the Gaasp stream. The Gaasperplas itself is an artificial lake up to 35 meters deep, created by sand mining for the construction of the Bijlmermeer.

origins.name: Geldersekade
origins.en: In the second expansion of the city on the east side, the current Geldersekade was the city moat. The inner wall (on the side of the Zeedijk) is therefore the oldest, built around 1500. The other side was outside the city until 1585. In the seventeenth century, that old side was partly called Cologne quay and further Gelderse kaai, also briefly London quay or English quay. The names originated because there were jetties here where ships docked that sailed to the Gelderland cities, to Cologne, London and other English harbors.

origins.name: Gerritsloot
origins.en: The origin of the name is unclear.

origins.name: Gevlewater
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the name of the bridges that cross over them

origins.name: Grimburgwal
origins.en: To the water the Grim, which from 1342 to around 1400 formed the southern boundary of the city (grim = muddy ditch).

origins.name: Groenburgwal
origins.en: The land between Kloveniersburgwal and Zwanenburgwal, where the linen windows stood and which was annexed to the city in 1593, was then the place of the dyeing houses. This canal was therefore originally called Verwersgracht. At the beginning of the seventeenth century, the name Groenburgwal was created, because there were special green dyeing houses here.

origins.name: Groote Braak
origins.en: The name refers to the breakthrough of the Spaarndammerdijk during a northwest storm in 1675. The water from the IJ then struck a 140-meter-wide hole with a depth of almost 10 meters in the water wall.

origins.name: Grote Die
origins.en: Literally: 'Big water', to distinguish it from the Kleine Die further along. The quay was at the level of the Nieuwendijk.

origins.name: Grote Haven
origins.en: Haven on the side channel to Nieuwendam.

origins.name: Haarlemmervaart
origins.en: Sailing to Haarlem

origins.name: Haveneilandschutsluis
origins.en: Named after the adjacent inner harbor that is connected to the IJmeer via a lock

origins.name: Havenkom A
origins.en: The name speaks for itself. The harbor bowls B and D are filled in.

origins.name: Havenkom C
origins.en: The name speaks for itself. The harbor bowls B and D are filled in.

origins.name: Heiligewegsluis
origins.en: After the Miracle of Amsterdam, the chapel 'Ter Heilige Stede' was founded between Rokin and Kalverstraat (later Nieuwezijds Kapel). For the benefit of the pilgrims, a road was then laid alongside the Heiligewegsevaart (later Overtoom) from Sloten to Kalverstraat, which was called the Heiligeweg. Our street is the remainder of that pilgrimage route. In old documents, Leidsestraat is also called Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Herengracht
origins.en: To the Lords Regulators of the city (The city was not previously governed, but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch, when it was widened in 1612 to the current canal, as the first of the three main canals. The part beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658. The Nieuwe Herengracht also belongs to that expansion.

origins.name: Het Nauw
origins.en: The narrow passage of the water between the Ransdorper Die and the Holysloter Die

origins.name: Het Slochter
origins.en: A slaughterhouse is another term for waterway.

origins.name: Hoekenesgracht
origins.en: Island in the former IJ. The word nes means spit of land.

origins.name: Hollandiagracht
origins.en: First Dutch film company that regularly produced and distributed films and documentaries. Filmfabriek Hollandia was founded in 1912 and expanded in 1913 with a theater company. In 1922, it went bankrupt.

origins.name: Holysloter Die
origins.en: A stream south of Broek in Waterland.

origins.name: Hoornsloot
origins.en: Probably named after the place Hoorn.

origins.name: Hornhaven
origins.en: Former island De Hoorn or Horn in the former IJ. After the construction of the North Sea Canal, the island could still be clearly recognized in the landscape in the Great IJpolder. Due to the extension of the Westhaven (around 1960), it was completely buried. 'Horn' means corner and was given to similar coastal formations as 'nes' and 'ham'. The full name of this horn was Zaanderhorn. It was a peninsula that belonged to the western part of Zaanden, the predecessor of Zaandam.

origins.name: Houthaven
origins.en: Built in 1873 and enlarged in 1878. for transport goods that are shipped via the Amsterdam harbor.

origins.name: Houthavengracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the name of the bridges that cross over them

origins.name: Houtveemkanaal
origins.en: To the adjacent wood pits.

origins.name: Hugo de Grootgracht
origins.en: Humanist (1584-1645), founder of International Law. Became involved in church disputes as leader of the Remonstrants and was imprisoned at Loevestein at the request of Prince Maurice. From there, he managed to escape in 1621 through a bookcase.

origins.name: IJhaven
origins.en: The IJ was formerly a branch of the North Sea. In the years 1865 to 1872 it was reclaimed by the construction of the North Sea Canal and in 1872 closed off from the North Sea by the IJdijk and the Orange Locks.

origins.name: IJmeer
origins.en: The IJmeer is a marginal lake in the Netherlands. It is located between the polder De Nes, Pampushaven, the Hollandse Brug and the mouth of the IJ at IJburg, divided between the provinces of North Holland and Flevoland.

origins.name: IJssloot
origins.en: The origin of this name is unknown.

origins.name: Jacob van Lennepkanaal
origins.en: Prose writer (1802-1868), mainly of historical novels, including 'The Rose of Dekama' and 'Ferdinand Huyck'.

origins.name: Jan Massensloot
origins.en: It is not known how this canal got its name.

origins.name: Jan van Riebeeckhaven
origins.en: Jan Anthonie van Riebeeck or Riebeek (1618-1708), founded the Cape Colony at Cape de Goede Hoop in 1652, when he was in service of the Dutch East India Company.

origins.name: Johan van Hasseltkanaal-Oost
origins.en: Lived from 1850 to 1916, was director of Public Works 1900-1907, before that director of the Waterworks. He had a major role in the organization of the ENTOS shipping exhibition in 1913. In 1900 Van Hasselt made a design for the development of Amsterdam-Noord, with residential areas planned and a canal. In 1919, an east and a west part of this channel was dug and named after him. When a road was built on the unexcavated part, that one was also named after him.

origins.name: Kadoelerbreek
origins.en: Name for the part of the municipality of Landsmeer that was annexed to Amsterdam on August 1, 1966. The name Kadoelen (or Quadolen) already appears in 1375. In 1429, there is talk of the lordship of Landsmeer and the lordship of Quadolen, which then had one lord together. Old maps indicate Kadoelen as a hamlet along the Waterlandse zeedijk (Landsmeerderdijk). The Kadoelenweg was taken over on 1-8-1966 under the name Zuideinde, but in 1970 that name was changed due to confusion with the Zuideinde (former Oostzaan).

origins.name: Kattenburgervaart
origins.en: A canal named after Kattenburg, the westernmost of the three Eastern Islands in Amsterdam

origins.name: Kattensloot
origins.en: This name is probably named after the species.

origins.name: Keizersgracht
origins.en: Named after Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms in 1489.

origins.name: Kinselmeer
origins.en: A lake north of Durgerdam.

origins.name: Kleine Wetering
origins.en: A weir is a dug watercourse. Named for its size as Kleine Wetering.

origins.name: Kloveniersburgwal
origins.en: The Kloveniersburgwal owes its name to a company of the civic guard called the kloveniers, after the firearm its men carried, the klover or culverin.

origins.name: Kolberggracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the name of the bridges that cross over them

origins.name: Koningsbergengracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the name of the bridges that cross over them

origins.name: Korte Prinsengracht
origins.en: To 'the princely title', which refers to that of the princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and in terms of the nature of the buildings, the simplest. During the enlargement of 1612, it was dug and built from Brouwersgracht to Leidsegracht. With the enlargement of 1658, this canal is also extended across the Amstel (up to the Entrepotdok). For the part on the Plantage, see also Plantage Westermanlaan - formerly Plantage Prinsenlaan. The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat.
