The name Prinsenmarkt for the current Noordermarkt did not find favor with the bourgeoisie.

origins.name: Kostverlorenvaart
origins.en: To the Kostverloren Wetering, dug in 1413 to obtain a shorter waterway to the Haarlemmer and Leidse lakes. According to some, a reason for the name Kostverloren would be that this waterway, which has been a source of contention between Amsterdam and Haarlem until 1609, has cost a lot of money in proceedings. The name Kostverloren occurs in various places in the Netherlands.

origins.name: Krom Boomssloot
origins.en: Named after the 16th-century shipbuilder Cornelis Pietersz. Boom. To connect his shipyard with the surrounding water with the Lastage, he had a canal and a cross-channel dug.

origins.name: Lamonggracht
origins.en: River on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Lauriergracht
origins.en: The South European ornamental tree

origins.name: Le Mairegracht
origins.en: Jacob le Maire (1585-1616), explorer. Discovered the sea route named after him at the southern tip of South America and the cape, which he called Cape Horn, to his hometown Hoorn. The Le Maire Street was projected and named in a different place on 20-11-1878, but that council decision was withdrawn on 19-8-1905.

origins.name: Leidsegracht
origins.en: The city of Leiden. All these streets date back to the great city expansion of 1658. The Leidsestraat got this name because it led to the Leidsepoort. It is part of the old Heiligeweg.

origins.name: Leliegracht
origins.en: The namesake of all these streets is the oldest, namely the Oude Leliestraat, which is already mentioned in 1560. This derives its name from the house 'In de witte lelye' on the Singel near the Jan Rodenpoortstoren (Tower lock). The name passed on after 1612 to the canal dug along its extension and finally to the Nieuwe Leliestraat and cross streets located in the Jordaan.

origins.name: Lijnbaansgracht
origins.en: The ropewalks of the rope-making works. The Linebaansteeg dates back to the fifteenth century, when the Singel was the outer canal. The rope-making works needed a fairly large area for the exercise of its business. That could only be found on the outside of the city. The Linebaan lay on the city side of the canal, so within the rampart. The Lijnbaansgracht walked around the entire city. It is now filled in in a number of places and has been given other names there, such as Leidseplein, Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen, Frederiksplein, Maarten Jansz. Kosterstraat, Valckenierstraat and Plantage Muidergracht.

origins.name: Looiersgracht
origins.en: The tanneries and the leather trade, to which these and the nearby streets in the Jordaan and the canal belt are named, were first located outside the city in the sixteenth century. When the area gradually came within the city and streets were laid out here, they were named after those long-established businesses, starting with the Runstraat and the Huidenstraat. After 1658, the tanneries spread out to areas east of the Vijzelgracht, where we now find the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and dwarsstraat. The Third Looiersdwarsstraat was the Oude Looierssloot (council decision, 1898) for filling in. For the Drowned Nieuwe Looierssloot,

origins.name: Lozingskanaal
origins.en: Channel that runs to Gemaal Zeeburg.

origins.name: Lübeckgracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the name of the bridges that cross over them

origins.name: Luiksingel
origins.en: Belgian city, located in the province of Liège.

origins.name: Machinetocht
origins.en: A canal in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

origins.name: Madagascarhaven
origins.en: African island, the fourth largest island in the world, located southeast of Africa

origins.name: Mainhaven
origins.en: Side river of the Rhine, to which the city of Mainz is located.

origins.name: Majanggracht
origins.en: River on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Marssloot
origins.en: A canal in Amsterdam-North, near the Kadoelen.

origins.name: Mauritiushaven
origins.en: Island located east of Madagascar, which was colonized by Dutch sailors from 1598 and later taken over by the French and the English, among others. It is named after stadtholder Prince Maurice, Count of Nassau.

origins.name: Mechelensingel
origins.en: Belgian town, located in the province of Antwerp.

origins.name: Mercuriushaven
origins.en: In Roman mythology the god of trade.

origins.name: Merdekagracht
origins.en: Merdeka means free or independent and already formed the forbidden battle cry of the nationalist movement during the colonial period. After the Proclamation of the Republic of Indonesia on August 17, 1945, it became the characteristic battle cry of the independence fighters.

origins.name: Minervahaven
origins.en: In Roman mythology the goddess of wisdom.

origins.name: Moezelhaven
origins.en: Side river that flows into the Rhine near Koblenz (Germany). Important river for the industries and mines in the Saar region.

origins.name: Neptunushaven
origins.en: In Roman mythology the god of the sea.

origins.name: Nieuwe Achtergracht
origins.en: This canal was dug around 1660 behind the four main canals, hence the name. It connected the Reguliersgracht with the Amstel. In 1870, most of it was filled in.

origins.name: Nieuwe Diep
origins.en: Due to a breakthrough of the Zuiderzee through the Diemerdijk in 1422, the new lake was formed under the lake the Bovendiep.

origins.name: Nieuwe Gouw
origins.en: Gouw is a Waterland term for road. The addition Nieuwe indicates that this road is slightly younger than the other Waterland roads. However, the road already appears on the map of Amstellandt and the surroundings of Covens from 1749. In 1957, the name was officially established again.

origins.name: Nieuwe Gouwsloot
origins.en: A county is a Waterland term for road.

origins.name: Nieuwe Herengracht
origins.en: To the Lords Regulators of the city (The city was not previously governed, but ruled). The canal already existed as a ditch, when it was widened in 1612 to the current canal, as the first of the three main canals. The part beyond the Leidsegracht belongs to the expansion of 1658. The Nieuwe Herengracht also belongs to that expansion.

origins.name: Nieuwe Houthaven
origins.en: Storage yard for the timber trade. Built in 1873 and enlarged in 1878.

origins.name: Nieuwe Keizersgracht
origins.en: Named after Emperor Maximilian, Archduke of Austria, who granted Amsterdam the privilege of bearing the imperial crown on its coat of arms in 1489.

origins.name: Nieuwe Meer
origins.en: The water surface was given this name to distinguish it from the Old Lake (see there). The Nieuwe Meer has been enlarged since the 1950s with part of the Riekerpolder and pumped to a depth of thirty meters for sand mining for the western garden towns.

origins.name: Nieuwe Prinsengracht
origins.en: To 'the princely title', which refers to that of the princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and in terms of the nature of the buildings, the simplest. During the enlargement of 1612, it was dug and built from Brouwersgracht to Leidsegracht. With the enlargement of 1658, this canal is also extended across the Amstel (up to the Entrepotdok). For the part on the Plantage, see also Plantage Westermanlaan - formerly Plantage Prinsenlaan. The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for the current Noordermarkt did not find favor with the bourgeoisie.

origins.name: Nieuwe Vaart
origins.en: Named after the Nieuwe Vaart dug around 1650 to the IJ and the Oosterdok.

origins.name: Noorder Amstelkanaal
origins.en: Channel that forms a connection between the Amstel and the Schinkel.

origins.name: Noordhollandsch Kanaal
origins.en: A canal that runs from Amsterdam-North, via Purmerend and Alkmaar to Den Helder.

origins.name: Noordzeekanaal
origins.en: The canal provides direct access to the North Sea from Amsterdam and was created by reclaiming the IJ and dredging the dunes near Velsen. The canal was dug to a design by Willem Antonie Froger and opened on November 1, 1876. The construction and operation of the canal and polders were carried out by the Canal Company, whose assets were taken over by the state after its dissolution in 1884. The road was part of the Basisweg and the Zuiderweg in the Grote IJpolder before the naming in 1978.

origins.name: Oesjesduiker
origins.en: The name of this diver comes from the signboard 't Osje, which was formerly attached to a butcher on the corner of the Oostenburgergracht

origins.name: Olympiakanaal
origins.en: The sacred place in ancient Greece where, in 776 BC, the Olympic Games were held for the first time.

origins.name: Onbekendegracht
origins.en: The Onbekendegracht originally gave the Former City Timberyard access to the Amstel. In a notarial deed, drawn up in 1800, the canal was called 'the Unknown or Amstelgragtje'.

origins.name: Oostelijk Marktkanaal
origins.en: Is located on the east side of the Centrale Markthallen.

origins.name: Oostenburgerdwarsvaart
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. The demolition of the streets and buildings began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was removed from public transport in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and declared abandoned in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abandoned in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oostenburgervaart
origins.en: Oostenburg was the most eastern of the three islands (next to Kattenburg and Wittenburg) that were annexed to the city with the enlargement of 1658. The demolition of the streets and buildings began in 1664. There were initially three streets from the canal, named Oostenburgervoorstraat, -middenstraat and -achterstraat according to their location. The Oostenburgerachterstraat was removed from public transport in the first half of the twentieth century due to the expansion of the Werkspoor company and declared abandoned in 1957. The Oostenburgermiddenstraat was abandoned in 1985. That is where Compagniestraat now runs.

origins.name: Oosterdok
origins.en: The Oosterdok was created by a seawall completed in 1832 on the east side of the city. The quay on and along this dyke was named Oosterdokskade and Oostelijke Handelskade.

origins.name: Oosterdoksdoorgang
origins.en: The water passage located between the name bearer Oosterdokskade.

origins.name: Oostertocht
origins.en: A tow is a connecting ditch between polder ditches and the polder canal.

origins.name: Oostertoegang
origins.en: Eastern access from the Oosterdok to the IJ

origins.name: Open Havenfront
origins.en: Former open waterfront. Filled in for the construction of Central Station.

origins.name: Oranjesluizen
origins.en: To the House of Orange-Nassau to which the royal family belongs. The first stone of the Oranjesluizen was laid by the then king William III, on April 29, 1870.

origins.name: Osdorpergracht
origins.en: To the neighborhood of Osdorp. On old maps, this neighborhood is mentioned as Oostdorp. In 1957, construction began on the garden city of Osdorp, which was practically completed in 1973. The Osdorperweg used to bear the names Herenstraat (in the village of Sloten) and Slimmeweg.

origins.name: Oude Houthaven
origins.en: Buried in 1876 for the purpose of bypassing and storing wood.

origins.name: Oudeschans
origins.en: A bastion is an earthen wall and as such the Oudeschans was built around 1516 for defense against the Gelders. The concept of bastion has long since been lost here, but water and quay have retained the name. The addition 'Old' will have been given, when in the next century a new bastion was built around the enlarged city.

origins.name: Oudezijds Achterburgwal
origins.en: Canal behind the Voorburgwal on the old side.

origins.name: Oudezijds Voorburgwal
origins.en: Before 1385 the Amstel divided the city into two almost equal halves, the old side (with the Oude Kerk) and the new side (with the Nieuwe Kerk). Each side was bounded by a burgwal, a town moat. When new burgwallen were dug behind them around 1385, the existing one became the Voorburgwal and the new one the Achterburgwal, on the old side and the new side alike. After the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal was filled in in 1867, it was renamed Spuistraat. The terms Oudezijds and Nieuwezijds date from the fifteenth century; before that people spoke of the Church side and the Windmill side.

origins.name: Papaverkanaal
origins.en: The plant, wild and cultivated. is also called buttercup.

origins.name: Passeerdersgracht
origins.en: Passing was the preparation and processing of Spanish leather. When this type of leather processing was banned in Amsterdam-Centrum in 1631, this passership settled here next to the already existing leather tanneries.

origins.name: Pereboomsloot
origins.en: The fruits of the pear tree.

origins.name: Pernaugracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the name of the bridges that cross over them

origins.name: Petroleumhaven
origins.en: To the port located here for unloading oil tankers and the areas for storing petroleum products. The port was put into use in 1888. The first part of the road was previously named Vlothavenweg (council decision, 1953).

origins.name: Pieter Postsingel
origins.en: Master builder (1608-1669), had a share in the construction of the town hall on the Dam. Other buildings: Mauritshuis and Huis ten Bosch in The Hague, town hall in Maastricht.

origins.name: Plantage Muidergracht
origins.en: The place Muiden. The former Muidergracht began at the Leprozengracht. Part of it was renamed Jonas Daniël Meijerplein after filling in, the second part was later renamed Hortusplantsoen. The part of the Plantage Muidergracht parallel to Sarphatistraat was called Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.

origins.name: Polygoongracht
origins.en: Film factory, founded in 1919 in Haarlem. Producer of commissioned films, documentaries and weekly cinema news bulletins.

origins.name: Postjeswetering
origins.en: To the former Postjeswetering. A post is a freshwater fish.

origins.name: Prinseneilandsgracht
origins.en: Probably named after the house 'The three Princes', which must have stood here in the seventeenth century. The house had busts of Prince William I, Prince Maurice and Prince Frederick Henry. However, it is not known where this house stood.

origins.name: Prinsengracht
origins.en: To 'the princely title', which refers to that of the princes of Orange. The canal is one of the three main canals, and in terms of the nature of the buildings, the simplest. During the enlargement of 1612, it was dug and built from Brouwersgracht to Leidsegracht. With the enlargement of 1658, this canal is also extended across the Amstel (up to the Entrepotdok). For the part on the Plantage, see also Plantage Westermanlaan - formerly Plantage Prinsenlaan. The first side street after the Brouwersgracht became the Prinsenstraat. The name Prinsenmarkt for the current Noordermarkt did not find favor with the bourgeoisie.

origins.name: Profiltigracht
origins.en: Film factory, founded in 1929 in The Hague. Producer of (commissioned) films, documentaries and cinema newsreels. First counterpart, later partner of Polygoon.

origins.name: Raamgracht
origins.en: The linen windows, where the painted linen was hung to dry, had to be set up outside the city. When the Kloveniersburgwal was still the city moat, these windows could be found at the height of the current Raamgracht. The nearby Verversstraat also still reminds us of this old Amsterdam industry.

origins.name: Ransdorper Die
origins.en: A stream north of Ransdorp.

origins.name: Rapenburgwal
origins.en: Originally the name of the island bounded by the IJ (now Oosterdok), Oudeschans, Rapenburgwal and Schippersgrachtje. The main street has taken the name of the island. The origin of the name is unknown (no explanation has been found for the Leiden Rapenburg either).

origins.name: Realengracht
origins.en: Reynier Reael, in 1633 alderman (schepen) of the city. He was the owner of the entire Realeneiland.

origins.name: Recht Boomssloot
origins.en: The 16th-century shipbuilder Cornelis Pietersz Boom. To connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the surrounding water, he had a canal and a cross-channel dug. These were then named after him.

origins.name: Reguliersgracht
origins.en: All these names remind us of the Reguliersklooster, which stood outside the then-city gate from 1394 to 1532, on the site where Utrechtsestraat and the Keizersgracht now intersect. The city gate, whose Mint Tower is a remnant, was formerly called the Regulierspoort. The Reguliersgracht ended there at that gate. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, parts of it were demolished. Before 1909, Regulierssteeg was called Watersteeg.

origins.name: Ringsloot
origins.en: Ring-shaped ditch.

origins.name: Ringvaart
origins.en: The water along which the path runs. A Ringvaart is the basin of a polder, into which excess water from the polder is discharged.

origins.name: Rokin
origins.en: We must discard the long-standing theory that this name is a derivation from Rak-in (a rak within the Dam, such as the Damrak outside the Dam). This part of the Amstel, now partially dammed for 2/3 of its length, originally had no embankments. The buildings on Kalverstraat ran right down to the water. When in the sixteenth century the facade along the water of the first part was moved back from the Dam, something had to give way, a quay was built here, which was designated as Ruck-in in 1559. A few years later this became the Rock-in. With later extension, the entire quay was given this name.

origins.name: Scharrebiersluis
origins.en: Scharrebier was traditionally the drink for ordinary workers. This 'thin' beer type was formerly sold on this collection bridge, because there was often a lot of working people present there

origins.name: Schellingwouderbreek
origins.en: Village Schellingwoude

origins.name: Schinkel
origins.en: A swing bridge is a short connecting piece between two canals. In this case Nieuwe Meer and Overtoom. It is assumed that the connecting piece owes its name to its shape: 'swing bridge' is synonymous with 'shin', the lower leg between the foot and the knee. The quay was previously called Nieuwer-Amstel Visserkade. The streets were respectively named Visserstraat, Alexanderstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1882) and Willemsparkstraat (council decision of Nieuwer-Amstel, 1883) by the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel, but were changed due to confusion with names already existing in Amsterdam in 1896.

origins.name: Schippersgracht
origins.en: In this neighborhood, on the harbor side, the shipowners and sailors made up the majority of the population, which is why the canal and street got this name.

origins.name: Seranggracht
origins.en: River on the Indonesian island of Java.

origins.name: Singel
origins.en: A singel is a waterway or a road along the outer edge of the city. In Amsterdam, the Singel (the Amsterdammer speaks of the Singel) formed the city boundary in the second half of the fifteenth century, within which the walls with gates were built. At that time, that canal was called 't Singel or the Stedegracht (now Singel, Kloveniersburgwal and Geldersekade). The current Singel has retained the old name. However, in the seventeenth century, the city administration introduced the name Koningsgracht for this purpose, but that name could not be maintained (see also Koningsplein).

origins.name: Singelgracht
origins.en: A singel is a waterway or road along the outer edge of the city. In Amsterdam, the Singel (the Amsterdammer speaks of the Singel) formed the city boundary in the second half of the fifteenth century, within which walls with gates were built. At that time, that canal was called 't Singel or the Stedegracht (now Singel, Kloveniersburgwal and Geldersekade). The current Singel has retained the old name. However, in the seventeenth century, the city administration introduced the name Koningsgracht for this purpose, but that name could not be maintained (see also Koningsplein).

origins.name: Sint Antoniesluis
origins.en: Named after the Sint Antoniesdijk, the sea wall located outside the city until the seventeenth century, which in turn took its name from the Sint Antoniesgasthuis or Leprosy House. The Sint Antoniesluis was part of the Zwanenburgwal before 1976.

origins.name: Sixhaven
origins.en: Baron Willem Six (1859-1919), from 1898 to 1919 chairman of the Royal Sailing and Rowing Association, a great promoter of the construction of the marina in Amsterdam North. Two months before the completion of the harbor, he died, after which the harbor was named after him.

origins.name: Sloterparkbadsingel
origins.en: The name is derived from Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk, which was dredged back into the water after repeated dryings for the purpose of sand mining. This water is the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Sloterplas
origins.en: The name is derived from Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk, which was dredged back into the water after repeated dryings for the purpose of sand mining. This water is the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Slotervaart
origins.en: The name is derived from Slotermeer, a lake between Sloten and Sloterdijk, which was dredged back into the water after repeated dryings for the purpose of sand mining. This water is the Sloterplas.

origins.name: Smallepadsgracht
origins.en: Ship, flat-bottomed of Frisian origin with swords and a gaff-rigged mast. Very suitable for shallow waters. The narrow ship was used to load goods and unload larger ships.

origins.name: Snellerwaardgracht
origins.en: Village on the Hollandse IJssel (Utrecht). The original spelling is Snelrewaard.

origins.name: Snoekjesgracht
origins.en: After a resident from the sixteenth century, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a pike depicted on the facade of his house. Originally, the name was therefore Snoeksgracht/steeg.

origins.name: Sonthaven
origins.en: The sea route between Denmark and Sweden, through which Amsterdam merchant ships have been sailing to the Baltic Sea since the fourteenth century. In 1658, the Dutch fleet under Jacob van Wassenaar defeated the Swedish fleet here at Obdam.

origins.name: Spiegelgracht
origins.en: To a well-known Amsterdam family, mostly manufacturers, who had soap factories. In 1564 Lourens Pieters 'in den Spiegel' lived in the corner building of the Oude Spiegelstraat on the Singel and in 1608 Pieter Lourens Spiegel. The intended house is still called Hertspiegel in 1738. The construction of the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat begins in 1665. Again, it is likely that a resident of the Spiegel family is the namesake.

origins.name: Spoorwegbassin
origins.en: The Spoorwegbassin is a harbor. A basin is a harbor basin.

origins.name: Stadiongracht
origins.en: Refers to the adjacent Olympic Stadium.

origins.name: Stoutenburggracht
origins.en: Village south of Hoevelaken (Utrecht). It is named after the former castle that belonged to Van Oldebarneveldt.

origins.name: Stralsundgracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the name of the bridges that cross over them

origins.name: Suezhaven
origins.en: Egyptian port town at the entrance - and namesake - of the Suez Canal opened in 1869.

origins.name: Syphonsluis
origins.en: Lock that works through the lever, a mechanism to pump water away.

origins.name: Texashaven
origins.en: Texas is one of the 50 states of the United States of America.

origins.name: Tolhuiskanaal
origins.en: To the entertainment venue the Toll House, formerly a popular venue. Construction dates back to 1662, when a highway was built here and a toll was established. In the garden, the famous concerts were held from 1887 to 1912 by the then popular seventh regiment under the leadership of organist Joh. Zaagmans.

origins.name: Twiske
origins.en: Twiske is the (West) Frisian word for 'between', it refers to the border ditch between the Waterland and the Zaanontginningen. The current recreation area near Oostzaan still bears this name.

origins.name: Uilenburgergracht
origins.en: The island of Uilenburg, which together with the islands of Rapenburg and Marken came to lie within the city in 1593. The origin of the name Uilenburg is not known with certainty, but it is likely that the name comes from the swampy land located here, which was called the Uylenbraeck in 1470. The Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat was created by the merger of the Uilenburgerstraat and the Batavierstraat.

origins.name: Uitdammer Die
origins.en: The hamlet of Uitdam, located on the IJsselmeerdijk north of the municipal boundary. The road came under the name Waterlandse zeedijk in Amsterdam when the former municipality of Ransdorp was abolished in 1921. (Uitdam = outside dam, outside dike.)

origins.name: Usselincxhaven
origins.en: Willem Usselincx (1567-1647), Flemish merchant and sailor, founder of the West Indian Company in 1621.

origins.name: Van Noordtgracht
origins.en: Olivier van Noordt (1558-1627), sailor and ship captain, who sailed around the world via the Strait of Magellan from 1598 to 1601. He later documented this journey.

origins.name: Vlothaven
origins.en: The nearby Vlothaven, dug in 1931, was originally shallow and part of the timber port intended for wooden barges. Around 1960, the port was deepened and adapted for sea vessels.

origins.name: Voorboezem
origins.en: A bay is an inland body of water without a fixed water level.

origins.name: Weersloot
origins.en: Common name for canals in North Holland.

origins.name: Weespertrekvaart
origins.en: The canal that connects Amsterdam with Weesp. A tow canal was used by barges. The tow canal was built in 1639, using several existing waterways.

origins.name: Westelijk Marktkanaal
origins.en: Was put into use in 1934 for freight transport from and to the Central Market Halls.

origins.name: Westerdok
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerdoksluis
origins.en: The causeway, built between 1830 and 1834, which formed the Nieuwe Waal into the Westerdok. When the railway was extended to Stationseiland at the end of the late 1880s of the nineteenth century, a section of the dock had to be filled in and the Westerdokskade was built. The Westerdokstraat was laid out and named in 1879, but disappeared in 1973 due to the widening of the Haarlemmer Houttuinen.

origins.name: Westerkanaal
origins.en: The canal is located on the west side of the city. This is probably the reason for the naming.

origins.name: Westerkanaalschutsluis
origins.en: This bascule bridge is named after the Westerkanaal, over which it lies, and because it is located in the western part of Amsterdam.

origins.name: Westertoegang
origins.en: The water that forms the western access to the IJ.

origins.name: Westhaven
origins.en: This harbor, dug about half in 1937, was initially called Fordhaven, but soon gained the unofficial name Westhaven. After the harbor was extended by more than a kilometer to its current length in 1961, the name was also officially established, along with that of other harbors. The later built road therefore bore the name earlier than the harbor.

origins.name: Westlandgracht
origins.en: The area west of Delft, an internationally known horticultural area.

origins.name: Weteringpoort
origins.en: This fixed bridge is named after the Weteringpoort, which stood nearby here from 1688 to 1841. The name recalls the Wetering, which used to enter the city from Kalfjeslaan here and flowed into the Spui. The current Boerenwetering is still a remnant here.

origins.name: Wismargracht
origins.en: The names of the canals refer to the name of the bridges that cross over them

origins.name: Wittenburgervaart
origins.en: One of the three eastern islands (next to Kattenburg and Oostenburg), built in the second half of the seventeenth century, from the beginning built with shipyards and houses. One of the first shipyards was that of Jan Witheyn (1610-1662), founded in 1657. Very likely we must look here for the origin of the name Wittenburg.

origins.name: Zanzibarhaven
origins.en: East African island in the Indian Ocean, which had several colonizers. Here, in 1818, under the rule of the Sultan of Oman, the Dutch monopoly on cloves was broken. Later it became British, and since 1964 it has been part of Tanzania.

origins.name: Zijkanaal I
origins.en: One of the ten side canals A to K. Was put into use in 1876 at the same time as the North Sea Canal.

origins.name: Zouthaven
origins.en: In the past, this location was the Zouthaven for the city.

origins.name: Zoutkeetsgracht
origins.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, on both sides of this canal stood the salt chain, warehouses where coarse salt was processed for household use.

origins.name: Zuider Amstelkanaal
origins.en: The southern part of the Amstelkanaal. Refers to the water the Amstel.

origins.name: Zwanenburgwal
origins.en: Shortly after the land (on which the street and quay were laid out) was drawn to the city just before 4:00 PM, there is talk of a house 'where Swanenburg hangs out', on the corner of Zwanenburgwal. This will therefore probably have been the name giver. Swanenburg was already a more common name at that time. Gerrit Barents Swanenburgh, for example, built the Muiderpoort, Weesperpoort and Utrechtsepoort in the seventeenth century. By council decision in 1976, a part of the Zwanenburgwal was named in Sint Antoniesluis. In order to build the Stopera, the Zwanenburgerstraat with adjacent buildings was relocated.
